records.jp: というか、いっつも一等賞じゃないか、こいつ。
records.en: Or should I say, alllways shooting for first place, ain't she.
records.assessment: He remarks that she is always the first-place arrival, not that she is continually aspiring or trying to win first place. The English turns an observed result into intention.
records.remedy: Use 'She's always first place, isn't she?'

highlights.text: shooting for first place

records.jp: シカト？
records.en: Ostracism?
records.assessment: The slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' denotes broader social exclusion and changes the immediate interpersonal act.
records.remedy: Use 'Ignoring me?'

highlights.text: Ostracism

records.jp: シカトですか。
records.en: Is this ostracism I see?
records.assessment: The repeated slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' again substitutes a different, broader social process.
records.remedy: Use 'Are you ignoring me?'

highlights.text: ostracism

records.jp: 「パンツ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Wear..."
records.assessment: The isolated noun is 'underwear' or 'panties,' setting up the following exchange. 'Wear' is not that noun and removes the joke's concrete object.
records.remedy: Use 'Underwear...' or 'Panties...'

highlights.text: Wear

records.jp: 「くどい」
records.en: Touko: "Be succint."
comments: Re: that monster above. -GHS
records.assessment: She calls him persistent or tiresome for repeating himself. The English orders him to be concise, changes the speech act, and misspells 'succinct.'
records.remedy: Use 'You're persistent' or 'Enough already.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Be succint."

records.jp: 「パンツ買ってくんない？」
records.en: Taichi: "Please buy what I wear?"
comments: See CCA0006 -GHS
records.assessment: He explicitly asks her to buy him underwear. The vague paraphrase 'what I wear' suppresses the concrete object that drives the exchange.
records.remedy: Use 'Won't you buy me some underwear?'

highlights.text: what I wear

records.jp: 「どーして私があなたのパンツを買わないといけないのっ！」
records.en: Touko: "Whyyy would I ever need to buy what you wear?!"
comments: Overreaction, he asks 'please', she uses a stronger 'ought' -GHS
records.assessment: She explicitly protests having to buy his underwear. The vague paraphrase removes the repeated noun and weakens the comic escalation.
records.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to buy your underwear?'

highlights.text: what you wear

records.jp: 冬子は親指をぐっとつかんで、ごきっと横に折った。
records.en: Youko grabs my thumb tightly, and harshly twists it along with my wrist.
comments: "goki~!" is http://www.aadayo.com/aa/asciiart5115.html, harsh movement to the side. -GHS
records.assessment: She grips his thumb and bends it sideways with a crack. The English turns this into twisting the thumb together with his wrist and loses the specified break-like motion.
records.remedy: Say that she bent his thumb sideways with a crack.

highlights.text: twists it along with my wrist

records.jp: 「あほーっ、折れたらどうするのだーっ！　自慰もままならないではないかーっ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Morooon, what if you'd broken iiit! I would never manage to console myself agaaain!"
comments: "Console myself" means masturbation, word and all but the euphemism works better in every instance (no really), so it's a running gag somehow. -GHS
records.assessment: He explicitly complains that he would not even be able to masturbate. 'Console myself' euphemizes away the sexual joke and its reason for mentioning the hand.
records.remedy: Use an explicit equivalent of 'I wouldn't even be able to masturbate.'

highlights.text: console myself

records.jp: 危うく手首を返したからよかったものの。
records.en: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.
comments: Should make sense, she IS getting weaker. -GHS
records.assessment: He says it was fortunate that he narrowly turned his wrist, which prevented worse injury. The English makes her the actor who barely managed to twist his wrist and reverses the protective causality.
records.remedy: Use 'It was a good thing I managed to turn my wrist in time.'

highlights.text: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.

records.jp: 「話しかけないで」
records.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me."
comments: Don't talk to me + don't approach me. It's thematically important so I'll keep it at least around here, see CCD2002 for the most obvious explanations. -GHS
records.assessment: She only tells him not to talk to her. The English adds a command to keep physically away.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't talk to me.'

highlights.text: Stay back and

records.jp: 「話しかけないで！」
records.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me!"
comments: PCP above
No denial of the existence of TV. Well, how damn convenient. -GHS
records.assessment: The repeated command again concerns speaking only. The English repeats an unsupported instruction to keep physically away.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't talk to me!'

highlights.text: Stay back and

records.jp: 話しかけないでと辛口に言われると、話しかけたくなる。
records.en: When I'm told in harsh tones not to approach or talk, I end up wanting to get close and talk.
comments: Frickin' contrarian. Remember that Touko subsists on a diet of bitterbugs. -GHS
records.assessment: Being sharply told not to speak makes him want to speak. The English twice adds physical approach and closeness that are absent from the source.
records.remedy: Keep both clauses about talking without adding movement or proximity.

highlights.text: not to approach or talk
get close and talk

records.jp: 話しかけると、また、話しかけないでと辛口に言われる。
records.en: I get close and talk to her, but once more she harshly tells me to stay away and not to talk to her.
comments: Mirrors strongly above. -GHS
records.assessment: He talks to her and is again sharply told not to. The English adds both moving close and being ordered to stay away.
records.remedy: Keep the exchange about speaking without adding physical-distance commands.

highlights.text: get close and talk to her
stay away and not to talk to her

records.jp: アンテナの組み立ては遅々として進んでいないように見えた。
records.en: The antenna assembly appeared to be only progressing laggingly.
records.assessment: The source says the assembly appears to be making little or no progress. The stacked adverbs and invented manner 'laggingly' produce unidiomatic English.
records.remedy: Say that the assembly appeared to be making very little progress.

highlights.text: only progressing laggingly

records.jp: 「朝から寝てるったぁどういう了見っすか」
records.en: Taichi: "Already this sleepy in the morning, really, what is the big idea!"
records.assessment: The source challenges her for actually sleeping there since morning. The English changes the completed or ongoing act of sleeping into merely feeling sleepy.
records.remedy: Ask what she is thinking, sleeping there since morning.

highlights.text: Already this sleepy in the morning

records.jp: よたよたと身をもたげた。
records.en: She rose herself with a wobble.
records.assessment: The source says she raises herself shakily. English 'rise' is intransitive here and cannot take the reflexive object used in the translation.
records.remedy: Use 'She raised herself shakily' or 'She rose unsteadily.'

highlights.text: rose herself

records.jp: まさか徹夜して泊まったんじゃなかろうな？
records.en: It can't be, she didn't pull an all-nighter and spend the night here?
records.assessment: The source is the narrator's worried supposition that she might have stayed all night. The English combines 'it can't be' with a negative question-like clause, obscuring whether he suspects or denies it.
records.remedy: Use a clear suspicion such as 'She didn't pull an all-nighter here, did she?'

highlights.text: It can't be, she didn't pull an all-nighter and spend the night here

records.jp: この黒須太一、そんな世の中にひとこともの申す！
records.en: This Kurosu Taichi here would like to push out a few words to the heart of that culture!
comments: See CCA0030, this is intentionally meta. -GHS
records.assessment: The source grandly says he has one thing to say to such a society. The English invents several words being physically pushed into the culture's heart and loses the setup for the single next-line declaration.
records.remedy: Say that he has one thing to say to such a world.

highlights.text: push out a few words to the heart of that culture

records.jp: 眼鏡を拭きながらあくびを噛み殺す。
records.en: She kills a yawn in her teeth while wiping her glasses.
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom means that she suppresses or stifles a yawn. The literal English image of killing it in her teeth is not idiomatic.
records.remedy: Say that she stifles a yawn while wiping her glasses.

highlights.text: kills a yawn in her teeth

records.jp: 先輩は眼鏡をかけ直す。
records.en: and Senpai wears back her glasses.
records.assessment: The source says she puts her glasses back on. English does not use 'wear back' for the completed action of replacing them.
records.remedy: Use 'puts her glasses back on.'

highlights.text: wears back her glasses

records.jp: 「部活に参加するんで、仕事ください」
records.en: Taichi: "I will be participating to club activities, ergo, a task please."
records.assessment: The source plainly says he is joining club activities and asks for work. The English uses the wrong preposition, an intrusive formal connector, and an articleless request.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical direct request for a task because he is participating in club activities.

highlights.text: participating to club activities, ergo, a task please

records.jp: 聞き耳を立てるが、いまいち聞こえない。
records.en: Even if I stand my ears at attention, I can't quite hear it all.
comments: As intentional as that thing in CCA0012. -GHS
records.assessment: The source uses the idiom of listening closely. The literal militarized image for his ears is not an English equivalent.
records.remedy: Say that he strains his ears or listens closely.

highlights.text: stand my ears at attention

records.jp: 『おつきあいする対象としては』
records.en: Misato: 『as a target of socialization』
records.assessment: The source considers him as a potential dating or romantic partner. The English replaces dating with the clinical and much broader process of socialization.
records.remedy: Refer to him as someone she might date or go out with.

highlights.text: target of socialization

records.jp: 「げんこーやってくださーい」
records.en: Misato: "Please do a scriiipt!"
records.assessment: The source asks him to write the script. 'Do a script' omits the specific act of writing and is not the natural collocation in this request.
records.remedy: Ask him to write the script.

highlights.text: do a scriiipt

records.jp: 「そうです。求められるものは、知性に感動、涙と真実。聞く者の耳朶を打ちどこまでも爽やかにさせる古き良き若者文化の再来を我が放送部の手でいや声で実現しようではありませんか！」
records.en: Misato: "Indeed. The demanded item impresses with its intelligence, it is tears as well as truth. Shall we not persistently strike the earlobe of listeners with the thoroughly refreshing good old youth culture resurrected by the hands, no, the voice of our Broadcast Club!"
comments: Technical, precise, slightly deranged and damn verbose - this was NVL until basically the fifth or sixth rewrite. Overliteral about the ears continues with "striking the earlobes", even funnier considering Mimi = ears. -GHS
records.assessment: The source lists intellect, emotion, tears, and truth as requirements, then imagines reviving a refreshing youth culture through the club's voices. The English turns the requirements into a single 'item,' splices independent clauses, and converts striking listeners' ears figuratively into persistently hitting their earlobes.
records.remedy: Present the four required qualities clearly, then preserve the rhetorical proposal to revive a refreshing youth culture through the club's voices.

highlights.text: The demanded item impresses with its intelligence, it is tears as well as truth
persistently strike the earlobe of listeners

records.jp: 「くっくっくっ……」
records.en: Misato: "Huh huh huh, hic..."
comments: Last one's a hiccup -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains only a suppressed or sinister laugh at this point. The English adds a hiccup that belongs to a different nearby beat.
records.remedy: Render the laughter without adding a hiccup.

highlights.text: hic

records.jp: もう滅茶苦茶だ。
records.en: She's wasted.
records.assessment: The source sums up the entire situation as a complete mess or beyond reason. The English narrows that judgment to her being intoxicated, losing the narrator's broader reaction.
records.remedy: Use a broader judgment such as 'This is a complete mess.'

highlights.text: She's wasted

records.jp: 座った目で言う。
records.en: She says, with eyes that look like they've been through glasses.
comments: Drunken eyes <-> "sitting" eyes, just a bad pun. -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes fixed, glazed, or dead-serious eyes. The English invents eyes that have physically passed through spectacles and does not convey her stare.
records.remedy: Describe her as speaking with fixed or glazed eyes.

highlights.text: eyes that look like they've been through glasses

records.jp: 「〆切は日曜日です」
records.en: Misato: "Cofferdam gets struck on Sunday."
comments: It's just a pretentious way of saying "deadline". Today you learned: Alpha is a kanji! -GHS
records.assessment: The source plainly sets Sunday as the manuscript deadline. The English substitutes an unrelated construction involving a cofferdam and being struck.
records.remedy: State that the deadline is Sunday.

highlights.text: Cofferdam gets struck on Sunday

records.jp: 「よろしい！」
records.en: Misato: "It is entrusted!"
comments: Bit weird, but she's wasted + other pun below. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is the superior's approving 'Good' or 'Very well.' The English instead declares that something has been entrusted, changing the speech act and adding an unspecified object.
records.remedy: Use an approving 'Good!' or 'Very well!'.

highlights.text: It is entrusted

records.jp: 「あかんだろ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Why you worthless...!"
records.assessment: The source is an exasperated objection that her behavior is unacceptable. The English turns it into an unfinished insult about her worth and loses the actual prohibition.
records.remedy: Use a direct objection such as 'You can't do that!'

highlights.text: Why you worthless

records.jp: あの真面目な先輩がお酒を……。
records.en: That serious Senpai, in vino veritas...
records.assessment: The source marvels that this normally serious senior is drinking alcohol. The English substitutes an added Latin proverb and never directly states the surprising action.
records.remedy: State that the serious senior is drinking.

highlights.text: in vino veritas

records.jp: 「ぺけくん、よろ子……」
records.en: Misato: "Peke-kun, entrustman..."
comments: Yoroshi, but since 子 (ko/child) is also shi, yoroko due to personification. -GHS
records.assessment: The drunken coinage personifies a feminine-sounding name built from the phrase meaning 'take care of it.' The English makes it a masculine 'man' and reduces the pun to abstract entrustment.
records.remedy: Use a name-like personification that preserves the request phrase and feminine ending.

highlights.text: entrustman

records.jp: 「もう、だっこして運んでいっちゃいますよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Really, you want me to carry you in my arms like a child now?"
comments: See CCD1001 -GHS
records.assessment: The source warns that he is about to pick her up and carry her away. The English instead asks whether she wants him to do it, shifting the decision and desire to her.
records.remedy: Warn that he will carry her in his arms if she remains there.

highlights.text: you want me to carry you

records.jp: 「ＺＺＺ……」
records.en: Senpai: "Kusuh, kusuh..."
comments: Foreign SFX. -GHS
records.assessment: The source presents conventional sleep notation rather than a giggle or voiced utterance. The English sound effect resembles quiet laughter and changes the audible beat.
records.remedy: Render a sleeping or snoring sound.

highlights.text: Kusuh, kusuh

records.jp: 「おっぱいとかおしりとか触っちゃうかもです？」
records.en: Taichi: "When I might cop a feel of your boobs or your butt or something?"
records.assessment: The source continues a warning that he might touch her while carrying her. The English opens with 'When' and leaves the clause without a governing main statement.
records.remedy: Use a complete warning beginning 'I might...'

highlights.text: When I might cop a feel

records.jp: 「どうかしてるのは俺だっつーの！」
records.en: Taichi: "No, the question is, have you gone mad, BOY!"
comments: ...which is why the point is that HE is going into the girlishness, not imitating Misato's speech at all. Therefore, it's a pronouns thing (watashi vs. ore). That last thing is North Kanto/Tohou. Wait, Tohoku still hasn't changed name to Tohou? What are they waiting for? Think of all the tourists going to literal Bullet Hell! What could possibly go wrong! -GHS
records.assessment: The source snaps that the narrator himself is the one acting crazy. The English addresses a boy and asks whether that other person has gone mad, reversing person, subject, and speech act.
records.remedy: Make the narrator correct himself: 'I'm the one who's crazy!'

highlights.text: have you gone mad, BOY

records.jp: 自分の側頭部を殴った。
records.en: I struck at my temporal lobe.
comments: PCP CCA0015
records.assessment: The source says he strikes the side of his head or temple. A temporal lobe is an internal brain region and cannot name the visible place he hits.
records.remedy: Use 'the side of my head' or 'my temple.'

highlights.text: temporal lobe

records.jp: 仕方ない人だなあ。
records.en: Helpless people aren't we.
comments: Either works. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls the senior a hopeless or troublesome person. The English changes singular third person into a plural judgment that includes the narrator.
records.remedy: Use a singular judgment such as 'What a hopeless person.'

highlights.text: Helpless people aren't we

records.jp: とりあえず先輩の上体を起こす。
records.en: First thing, raise Senpai's upper body.
records.assessment: The source narrates the narrator lifting her upper body. The English drops the subject and finite verb, making the action read as an instruction.
records.remedy: Use a finite first-person narrative sentence.

highlights.text: First thing, raise Senpai's upper body

records.jp: くってり。
records.en: Plump!
comments: Soff'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a limp slumping or flopping sound as her body gives way. 'Plump' describes fullness of shape and does not convey that motion.
records.remedy: Use a limp flop or slump sound.

highlights.text: Plump

records.jp: 首がうなだれた。
records.en: Her necks limps to one side.
comments: How much stuff does he do to sleeping people anyway? He certainly pesters sleepy Touko lots. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says her head or neck droops. The English pluralizes a single neck, mismatches the verb, and adds a direction not present in the source.
records.remedy: Say that her head droops.

highlights.text: Her necks limps to one side

records.jp: 胸元で潰れる、ふたつの風船的感覚。
records.en: squish the pit of her stomach, and had a twin balloonlike sensation.
records.assessment: The source describes two balloonlike sensations compressing against the narrator's chest. The English relocates the contact to the pit of her stomach and leaves the clause without a coherent subject.
records.remedy: Describe the two soft, balloonlike sensations pressing against his chest.

highlights.text: squish the pit of her stomach

records.jp: 背中のあたりをごそごそとまさぐる。
records.en: Tamper with a rustle around the middle of the upper back.
records.assessment: The source narrates him fumbling or groping around her back. The English uses an imperative-like bare verb, substitutes 'tamper,' and turns the rustling manner into an object.
records.remedy: Say that he feels around her back with a rustle.

highlights.text: Tamper with a rustle around the middle of the upper back

records.jp: 外す（所要時間０．５秒）。
records.en: Undone (time required: 0,5").
comments: Self-destruct button? Well, that he knows all sorts of embarrassing sexual techniques shouldn't be surprising for a first time reader, all things considered, but it's really uncommon for this kind of character to be able to quickly undo bra hooks. It's of course because he's worn bras. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives a duration of 0.5 seconds. The English uses a decimal comma and an inch mark, which conventionally communicates a measurement rather than elapsed seconds.
records.remedy: Write '0.5 seconds.'

records.jp: ブラそのものをずらして、前止めの隙間から、するするするーっと抜き出す。
records.en: Shift the bra itself, and from the gap of the frontal stoppers, and carefully, caaarefully, move to slip it out.
comments: It seems to have no shoulder straps, same will be in CCD1001. Odd for someone with boobs that size... -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to the gap at the front fastening or clasp. 'Frontal stoppers' is not an English garment term, and the repeated conjunctions leave the extraction action syntactically tangled.
records.remedy: Refer to the front clasp and describe slipping the garment out in one clear action.

highlights.text: frontal stoppers

records.jp: 人肌のそれを、己の鼻先に添える。
records.en: Accompany its skin-induced warmth to the tip of one's nose.
comments: Purple. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the narrator brings the still body-warm garment to the tip of his nose. The English makes warmth the object of 'accompany,' shifts into generic 'one,' and obscures the physical action.
records.remedy: Say that he holds the body-warm garment to the tip of his nose.

highlights.text: Accompany its skin-induced warmth to the tip of one's nose

records.jp: けっこうずっしり。
records.en: Heavy with measure,
records.assessment: The source says she is fairly or satisfyingly heavy. 'With measure' is a literal abstraction that does not modify weight naturally in English.
records.remedy: Say that she is fairly heavy.

highlights.text: Heavy with measure

records.jp: でもほどよく乗ったふたつの感触がたまらない。
records.en: but the double sensation adequately riding on my back is unbearable.
records.assessment: The source positively savors the feel of the two soft forms resting against him. The English's 'adequately riding' is malformed, while unqualified 'unbearable' can reverse the positive reaction into discomfort.
records.remedy: Describe the two pleasant sensations resting against his back as irresistible.

highlights.text: double sensation adequately riding on my back is unbearable

records.jp: シャツ一枚を隔てて生胸。
records.en: because behind a single layer of shirt, it is now raw.
records.assessment: The source explicitly notes bare breasts separated from him by only a shirt. The English drops the body part and uses 'raw,' which does not communicate uncovered skin in this construction.
records.remedy: Name the bare breasts through the single layer of shirt.

highlights.text: it is now raw

records.jp: 背中に弾む感触があまりにも素晴らしくて、無意味に学校中を巡ってしまった。
records.en: The feeling bouncing on my back unbearably wonderful, I ended up pointlessly doing the rounds of the school grounds.
records.assessment: The source states that the bouncing sensation is so wonderful that he tours the school needlessly. The English omits the finite verb from the causal clause.
records.remedy: Insert a finite predicate, such as 'The feeling ... was so wonderful that...'

highlights.text: The feeling bouncing on my back unbearably wonderful

records.jp: 保健室に人はいない。
records.en: there's no people in the infirmary.
comments: Gunjou having an infirmary but no nurse on duty's par for the course. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says nobody is in the infirmary. The plural complement requires 'there are no people' or the singular alternative 'there's nobody.'
records.remedy: Use a grammatical existential construction.

highlights.text: there's no people

records.jp: ぶちゅう
records.en: Prezy-kiss!
comments: This is written Buchuu, which is a hideous combination of President and kiss. See CCA0029 for "payoff", such as it is. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is the sound of a conspicuously wet kiss. The invented 'Prezy' element has no source basis and makes the sound's action obscure.
records.remedy: Use a recognizable wet-kiss sound effect.

highlights.text: Prezy-kiss

records.jp: ようやっと、一日のはじまりだ。
records.en: The beginning of this day was all narrow dodges.
records.assessment: The source says that, at long last, his day is beginning. The English invents past narrow escapes or evasions and loses the temporal sense of finally starting.
records.remedy: Say that at last the day can begin.

highlights.text: The beginning of this day was all narrow dodges

records.jp: 夜が暑苦しくないのが、田舎のいいとこだ。
records.en: One good thing of countryside is that the evenings are not sticky damp hot.
records.assessment: The source naturally observes that country nights are not oppressively hot. The English omits the article before 'countryside' and stacks adjectives into an ungrammatical temperature phrase.
records.remedy: Say that one good thing about the countryside is that nights are not stiflingly hot.

highlights.text: good thing of countryside
sticky damp hot

records.jp: 窓から滑り込む風はほどよく冷たく、肌に優しい。
records.en: The wind that slips through the window is cold with moderation, and gentle on the skin.
records.assessment: The source describes the breeze as pleasantly or moderately cool. 'Cold with moderation' is a literal abstract construction rather than an English temperature description.
records.remedy: Use 'pleasantly cool' or 'moderately cool.'

highlights.text: cold with moderation

records.jp: 日記はもちろん、原稿も書かないと。
records.en: The diary, of course, but I also got to do the script.
records.assessment: The source says he also has to write the broadcast script. 'Do the script' is an imprecise collocation that omits the named act of writing.
records.remedy: Say that he has to write the script.

highlights.text: do the script

records.jp: 「……ふーむ」
records.en: Taichi: "...uh huh."
records.assessment: The source is a thoughtful 'Hmm' while he considers what to write. 'Uh huh' conventionally signals agreement or acknowledgment and changes the speech function.
records.remedy: Use a pondering interjection such as 'Hmm.'

highlights.text: uh huh

records.jp: 難。
records.en: {}DIFFICULT.
records.assessment: The source is a terse declaration that the task is difficult. The English preserves the word but leaks empty control or formatting braces into visible text.
records.remedy: Remove the stray braces.

records.jp: 一進一退の攻防。
records.en: Offense and defense in an advance and retreat.
records.assessment: The source figuratively describes a back-and-forth struggle that makes no progress. The word-for-word military nouns do not form that idiom in English.
records.remedy: Use a natural image of a back-and-forth struggle.

highlights.text: Offense and defense in an advance and retreat

records.jp: 一時間後、机に突っ伏す。
records.en: One hour later, I fall prostate on the desk.
records.assessment: The source says he slumps face down onto the desk. 'Prostate' names a gland; the intended posture word is 'prostrate,' and even that needs the desk relation stated clearly.
records.remedy: Say that he slumps face down over the desk.

highlights.text: prostate

records.jp: ちょっと微妙なおもしろみを加えようとして、おかしくなった。
records.en: I went to add too much subtle funny on it, and it just got weird.
comments: I'd wonder if the first revisions of Tanaka's stuff are readable at all, but given CCZAS is likely not edited very thoroughly, I don't have to doubt much. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says a slight attempt to add an uncertain bit of humor made the draft strange. The English treats 'funny' as a mass noun and uses the wrong preposition.
records.remedy: Say that trying to add a subtle bit of humor made it strange.

highlights.text: too much subtle funny on it

records.jp: そしてまたその二人同士が友好的な関係を築いていたとき。
records.en:
And furthermore, in the while the two fellows
were building a most amicable relationship.
comments: 'Toki'(time/occasion) is written in kana this time when he used kanji so far: he's going into sexual delusions. Or is it? This "building" is the same used by Misato in CCA0015B; it means the same as Taichi's growing of hearts. The next line, however... -GHS
records.assessment: The source sets another occasion when the two friends had formed a friendly relationship. 'In the while' is not a grammatical temporal connector in English.
records.remedy: Use 'when the two had formed a friendly relationship.'

highlights.text: in the while

records.jp: そう。
records.en: Hence.
comments: Just being pretentious for tonal consistency. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is an affirming transition equivalent to 'Yes' or 'That's right.' 'Hence' asserts a logical consequence that the one-word source does not encode.
records.remedy: Use an affirmative transition.

highlights.text: Hence

records.jp: そして私の手には、彼女の身につけていた胸布が残された。
records.en:
And so in my hand it remained, that
chestcloth that so much learned of her flesh.
comments: Same as the 'groincloth', direct reference. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the garment she had been wearing remained in his hand. The English invents the garment having learned from her flesh and attaches the relative clause ungrammatically.
records.remedy: State plainly that the garment she wore remains in his hand.

highlights.text: that so much learned of her flesh

records.jp: 芸術の都ロンドンに生まれていればスターダム確実の文才がほとばしった。
records.en: a surge of authentic literary talent that if I had been born in that capital of the fine arts London, stardoming would've been the foregone.
comments: I strongly suspect this should be Paris... except in England, between the '30s and 1949, at an Oxford pub called The Eagle and Child... Engine doesn't accept the accented e in eclat, so the machine translator that I only edit stuff from defaulted to sorta-engrish. Still works because, once again, this is about ridiculing the half-educated who'd think this stuff is impressive instead of pretentious and laughable. -GHS
records.assessment: The source boasts that stardom would have been assured had he been born in London. The English invents the verb 'stardoming' and leaves 'foregone' without the noun needed for the idiom.
records.remedy: Say that stardom would have been a foregone conclusion.

highlights.text: stardoming would've been the foregone

records.jp: いやあ、ただ小難しい言葉を使うだけで、気取れるものだなあ。
records.en: Naaah, 'tis just a put on airs mine, I'm just using tortuous verbiage here!
comments: Sarcastically making self-disparaging remarks, which instead are honest, see below. IMO it's too blunt, but I'm sort of biased in that regard. -GHS
records.assessment: The source admits that merely using difficult words makes it easy to sound pretentious. The English phrase has no grammatical subject-predicate structure and mangles the idiom 'put on airs.'
records.remedy: Use a grammatical admission that difficult words alone let him sound pretentious.

highlights.text: 'tis just a put on airs mine

records.jp: タームとかトートロジーとかアイロニーとか、そういう専門用語も決して平易な日本語に訳すことなくバンバン使っていかないとな。
records.en: Weltanschaaung, countenancing, intratextuality: those are the kind of technical terms that I got to use like bullets in a machine gun without translation into plain language.
comments: Same SFX as Miki used about Kiri.　Original terms (term, tautology, irony) would make this way sillier than intended; could've used Japanese VN terms like imouto, but that would make this way more meta than intended as well. See CCX0001: this would be the mud water that covers the sewage. And yet, after all this, I could only say that it's the exact opposite. -GHS
records.assessment: The source specifically lists 'term,' 'tautology,' and 'irony' as jargon he should deploy untranslated. The English replaces all three examples, misspells one substitute, and includes a nontechnical ordinary word.
records.remedy: Preserve the source's three example terms.

highlights.text: Weltanschaaung, countenancing, intratextuality

records.jp: 俄然やる気になって、再びペンを取った。
records.en: Inspiration struck in a sudden, and once again I took to the pen.
records.assessment: The source says he suddenly becomes motivated and takes up his pen again. English requires 'all of a sudden' or a direct adverb, and 'inspiration struck' shifts motivation toward receiving an idea.
records.remedy: Say that he suddenly felt motivated and picked up the pen again.

highlights.text: Inspiration struck in a sudden

records.jp: まだ気温もそう高くない午前中。
records.en: Mid-morning, when the temperature is still not so high,
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 午前中 means during the morning, not specifically mid-morning. 'When the temperature is still not so high' is also a calqued comparative construction.
records.remedy: Use 'It is morning, and the temperature has not climbed very high yet.'

highlights.text: Mid-morning, when the temperature is still not so high,

records.jp: 早朝だ。
records.en: It's mid-morning.
records.assessment: 早朝 explicitly means early morning. The English says 'mid-morning,' contradicting the stated time.
records.remedy: Use 'It is early morning.'

highlights.text: It's mid-morning.

records.jp: 「さて」
records.en: Taichi: "Then,"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: さて is a complete discourse marker such as 'Well, then.' The English ends the fragment with a comma and no following clause.
records.remedy: Use 'Well, then.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then,"

records.jp: 機材を持って屋上に来る。
records.en: I had come to the rooftop carrying equipment,
records.assessment: The narration is in the present sequence and forms one action with the following encounter. 'I had come' introduces an unsupported past-perfect frame and leaves the line hanging on a comma.
records.remedy: Use 'I come up to the roof carrying equipment...'

highlights.text: I had come to the rooftop carrying equipment,

records.jp: 「太一……か」
records.en: Tomoki: "Taichi... right."
records.assessment: 太一……か is recognition: 'Taichi... is that you?' or 'Oh... Taichi.' 'Taichi... right' instead sounds as though the speaker is recalling the name.
records.remedy: Use 'Taichi...?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Taichi... right."

records.jp: ぎょっとしている。
records.en: Seemed startled.
records.assessment: The Japanese gives a complete observation that Tomoki looks startled. 'Seemed startled' omits the subject and shifts the observation into an English fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'He looks startled.'

highlights.text: Seemed startled.

records.jp: 「……そんなわけ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...that'd be, well."
comments: Going with indecisive, if only because he's easily convinced below. ...which makes his betrayal odd, I know. -GHS
records.assessment: そんなわけ is the beginning of a denial such as 'No way' before the line trails off. 'That'd be, well' is neither grammatical nor a denial.
records.remedy: Use '...As if I would.' or an equivalently interrupted denial.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...that'd be, well."

records.jp: 「先輩、気にしてるみたいだぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "Senpai seems very worried you know."
records.assessment: The source says Senpai seems concerned. 'Very worried' adds degree, and 'you know' adds a conversational tag absent from the line.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai seems concerned about you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Senpai seems very worried you know."

records.jp: 「そーとーストレスかかってるみたいだ」
records.en: Taichi: "She seems to be taking in adequate amounts of stress."
records.assessment: 相当ストレスかかってる says she is under considerable stress. 'Taking in adequate amounts of stress' makes stress an intake meeting a sufficient quota.
records.remedy: Use 'She seems to be under a lot of stress.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "She seems to be taking in adequate amounts of stress."

records.jp: 「一人で無茶してるのも、そのせいだ」
records.en: Taichi: "If she's acting so madly on her own, that's gotta be the cause."
records.assessment: 一人で無茶してる means she is pushing herself recklessly on her own. 'Acting so madly' recasts overexertion as insanity.
records.remedy: Use 'That is why she is pushing herself so hard on her own.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If she's acting so madly on her own, that's gotta be the cause."

records.jp: 「無茶って言うかさ……」
records.en: Tomoki: "Mad you call it..."
records.assessment: 無茶って言うか is a hesitant qualification, 'Reckless, or rather...' 'Mad you call it' is broken inversion and repeats the earlier mistranslation of 無茶 as madness.
records.remedy: Use 'Reckless... or maybe...'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Mad you call it..."

records.jp: 「……まあ、おまえたちの問題だと思うけど……正直、おまえの手が借りられないのはきつい」
records.en: Taichi: "...well, it's only a problem between you guys, but... honestly, not even wanting your help, that's harsh."
comments: On both of them. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker says that although it is the siblings' problem, not being able to borrow Tomoki's help is hard. 'Not even wanting your help' makes the speaker refuse assistance and reverses the relation.
records.remedy: Use '...I know this is between you two, but honestly, it is hard not having your help.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...well, it's only a problem between you guys, but... honestly, not even wanting your help, that's harsh."

records.jp: 「それに……こういうのって、俺たちには大切だと思うぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "Because... what we're doing here, I think it's important for us."
records.assessment: それに adds a further reason: 'Besides...' 'Because' instead subordinates the sentence as an explanation of the preceding line and loses the additive relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Besides, I think this kind of thing matters to us.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because... what we're doing here, I think it's important for us."

records.jp: 「いや、こうやって作業進めておけばぺけくんすごいです大感動です濡れちゃいますブチューッ……みたいな」
records.en: Taichi: "'Wow, the work has progressed this much, Peke-kun sugoi!, Prezy super deeply moved, Prezy sooo wet, kissy-kissy!'... or words to that effect. That is my goal."
comments: PCP CCA0029
records.assessment: The imagined praise addresses ぺけくん, Peke-kun. 'Prezy' substitutes an unrelated name, leaves すごい untranslated as 'sugoi,' and adds the explanatory sentence 'That is my goal.'
records.remedy: Preserve the imagined quote with Peke-kun and translate its Japanese praise directly, without the added explanation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Wow, the work has progressed this much, Peke-kun sugoi!, Prezy super deeply moved, Prezy sooo wet, kissy-kissy!'... or words to that effect. That is my goal."

records.jp: 「ブチューはないだろう」
records.en: Tomoki: "Prezy-kiss ain't happening though."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: ブチュー is the exaggerated kissing sound just used in the imagined quote. 'Prezy-kiss' adds the unrelated name again and changes the objection's target.
records.remedy: Use 'The smooching is not happening.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Prezy-kiss ain't happening though."

records.jp: 「そうそう」
records.en: Taichi: "Yeppy yep."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: そうそう is an ordinary agreement, 'Right, exactly.' 'Yeppy yep' invents a childish verbal tic.
records.remedy: Use 'Right, right.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yeppy yep."

records.jp: 「お、サンキュ」
records.en: Taichi: "Oh, thank ye."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: サンキュ is a casual loanword 'Thanks.' 'Thank ye' adds an archaic or dialectal second-person form.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh, thanks.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Oh, thank ye."

records.jp: 缶ジュース。
records.en: Canned juice.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 缶ジュース is a canned soft drink in this context. 'Canned juice' is a literal Japanism that can incorrectly imply fruit juice in English.
records.remedy: Use 'A canned drink.'

highlights.text: Canned juice.

records.jp: 「……どうして部活なん？」
records.en: Tomoki: "...why activities now?"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: どうして部活なん asks why the subject is club activities. 'Why activities now?' omits 'club' and adds a temporal 'now' not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use '...Why club activities?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...why activities now?"

records.jp: 「おまえと……姉さんに関わることだけど、いいか？」
records.en: Taichi: "It's about... you and your nee-san, however. Can I?"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 姉さん is the older sister under discussion. Leaving 'nee-san' untranslated is unnecessary, while 'however. Can I?' breaks the permission question into unnatural English.
records.remedy: Use 'It concerns you and your sister... Is that okay?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's about... you and your nee-san, however. Can I?"

records.jp: 少しこわごわと、質問を押し出す。
records.en: With a little nervousness I push out the question.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 質問を押し出す describes forcing the question out despite nervousness. 'Push out the question' is a literal collocation rather than natural English.
records.remedy: Use 'A little apprehensively, I force the question out.'

highlights.text: With a little nervousness I push out the question.

records.jp: 「どうしておまえは関東の人間なのにたまに『～なん？』とか『そうやん』とかのエセ関西弁をまじえるんだ？」
records.en: Taichi: "How come you're from Kanto but you drop in some fake-Kansai accent in your sentences?"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: エセ関西弁 is fake Kansai dialect. Calling it an 'accent' narrows the feature to pronunciation even though the quoted examples are grammatical endings.
records.remedy: Use 'Why do you sometimes mix fake Kansai dialect into your speech even though you're from Kantō?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "How come you're from Kanto but you drop in some fake-Kansai accent in your sentences?"

records.jp: 「最高に姉貴と関係ない質問だよ！！」
records.en: Tomoki: "That's the single most unrelated question to Aneki!!!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 姉貴 means the speaker's older sister, but 'Aneki' is left untranslated. 'Unrelated question to' is also the wrong English preposition.
records.remedy: Use 'That question has absolutely nothing to do with my sister!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That's the single most unrelated question to Aneki!!!"

records.jp: 「まーまー、待ちたまえよ。ロマンは一日にして成らずだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Waiiit, waiiit, gladden me with holding on! Romance wasn't built in a day!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 待ちたまえ means 'wait' or 'hold on.' 'Gladden me with holding on' is an unrelated and unidiomatic command that breaks the Rome/romance proverb joke.
records.remedy: Use 'Now, now, wait. Romance wasn't built in a day.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Waiiit, waiiit, gladden me with holding on! Romance wasn't built in a day!"

records.jp: 「気を抜いてくれてありがとう太一くん」
records.en: Tomoki: "Thank you for making me waste some time, Taichi-kun."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: Tomoki sarcastically thanks Taichi for letting him lower his guard after presenting the question as serious. 'Making me waste some time' changes relaxed vigilance into lost time.
records.remedy: Use 'Thanks for letting me drop my guard, Taichi-kun.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Thank you for making me waste some time, Taichi-kun."

records.jp: 「そうシニックになるな」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't become so cynical!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source tells him not to be so cynical. 'Don't become so cynical' recasts a present attitude as a future change of state.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't be so cynical.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't become so cynical!"

records.jp: 「生きる糧があるならそういうのもいいけどさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "But once you have food to live, that'd be good to have, though."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 生きる糧 is figurative sustenance or a reason that sustains life. 'Food to live' literalizes the expression and leaves the comparison incoherent.
records.remedy: Use 'If it gives you something to live for, I suppose that's fine.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "But once you have food to live, that'd be good to have, though."

records.jp: 「青春群像グラフティー」
records.en: Taichi: "Vitelloni Graffitea."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source names a 'youth ensemble graffiti' ideal, setting up the following sound-based tea joke. 'Vitelloni' imports an unbound foreign title and replaces the ensemble-youth phrase.
records.remedy: Preserve the youth-ensemble-graffiti phrase while enabling the following sound joke.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Vitelloni Graffitea."

records.jp: 「それで……それだけで？」
records.en: Tomoki: "With this... just with this thing?"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source asks skeptically whether that is all. 'With this thing' adds an object and changes the follow-up into a question about means.
records.remedy: Use 'And... that's all?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "With this... just with this thing?"

records.jp: 「することがあるのはいいもんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, if you have something to do yourself that's fine too."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source says it is good simply to have something to do. 'Something to do yourself that's fine too' introduces a contrast and second-person subject absent from the statement.
records.remedy: Use 'It's good to have something to do.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if you have something to do yourself that's fine too."

records.jp: 「……あるじゃん。別に。物資探すとか、さ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...to do, hmmm. Not really. Looking for goods and materials, maybe."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: Tomoki says there are other things to do, such as searching for supplies. 'Not really' denies that existence and reverses his point.
records.remedy: Use 'There are other things to do, though. Like searching for supplies.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...to do, hmmm. Not really. Looking for goods and materials, maybe."

records.jp: 「そーかー？」
records.en: Taichi: "Dooon't you nooow?"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: そーかー is a questioning 'Really?' or 'Is that so?' 'Don't you now?' reverses the polarity and treats the prior line as a denial.
records.remedy: Use 'Really?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Dooon't you nooow?"

records.jp: 「どうしてそんな楽しそうなんだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Why're you looking like you're having fun now."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source asks why he is having so much fun. 'Looking like' makes it merely an appearance, and 'now' adds a temporal contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'Why are you having so much fun?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Why're you looking like you're having fun now."

records.jp: 友貴は腕で目元をぬぐった。
records.en: Tomoki wiped his undereye with his arm.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 目元 is the eye area and the action uses the arm to wipe it. 'His undereye' is not an idiomatic count noun for that area.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki wipes his eyes with his arm.'

highlights.text: Tomoki wiped his undereye with his arm.

records.jp: 「とっとと頼む」
records.en: Taichi: "Then help you whelp!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: とっとと頼む means 'Hurry up; I'm counting on you' or 'Get to it.' 'Then help you whelp' has the wrong object, adds an insult, and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'Then hurry up and help me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then help you whelp!"

records.jp: 「ばか、内心泣いてるっての。号泣だっての。泣き感動路線だっての」
records.en: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source says he is crying and sobbing inwardly and calls it a tearjerker route. The English inserts 'baka' twice and leaves 'utsuge' untranslated.
records.remedy: Use natural English for the internal sobbing and tearjerker-route joke without added Japanese insults.

highlights.text: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"

records.jp: 「男同士でジメジメしたって寒いだけだ、そーいうイベントは貴様のねーちゃんと起こすわい」
records.en: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The narrator says he will trigger that sentimental event with Tomoki's sister instead. 'Go trigger that event' orders Tomoki to do it, reversing the agent; 'nee-chan' is also left untranslated.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll save that kind of event for your sister.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"

records.jp: 「さあ、そうと決まったらとっとと働け！　放送予定日は明日じゃい」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast's scheduled for tomorrow ya know."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: そうと決まったら means 'now that that's settled.' 'If that's your decision' assigns the decision specifically to Tomoki, and 'you whelp' adds an insult absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use 'Now that that's settled, get to work! The broadcast is tomorrow.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast's scheduled for tomorrow ya know."

records.jp: 校舎に戻る足を止め、友貴。
records.en: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki stops on his way back into the school building. 'A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops' turns the route into a body part and is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'On his way back into the school building, Tomoki stops.'

highlights.text: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.

records.jp: 「……てっきり姉貴と仲直りしろとか言うのかなって思ってた、姉貴を手伝えよ弟だろって」
records.en: Tomoki: "...I thought you would tell me to put things right with Aneki, for sure, that a younger brother should help his Aneki."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 姉貴 is left untranslated twice as 'Aneki,' and the reported expectations are assembled as a run-on rather than two parallel things Taichi might say.
records.remedy: Use '...I was sure you'd tell me to make up with my sister, or say that as her brother I ought to help her.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...I thought you would tell me to put things right with Aneki, for sure, that a younger brother should help his Aneki."

records.jp: 「いや、姉弟喧嘩なんてごくまっとうな人生じゃん。止めんよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 止めんよ means the speaker will not interfere with or stop the siblings' quarrel. 'Don'tcha stop' changes the first-person decision into an imperative telling Tomoki to continue.
records.remedy: Use 'No. A sibling quarrel is a perfectly normal part of life. I won't interfere.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."

records.jp: 「要するに俺様を手伝えということだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 'The greatness that is I' uses the wrong pronoun case and awkwardly expands 俺様.
records.remedy: Use 'In short, you're here to help the great me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."

records.jp: 胸を張る。
records.en: Puff that chest with pride!
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 胸を張る is the narrator's present action of throwing out his chest. 'Puff that chest with pride!' changes it into an imperative addressed to someone else.
records.remedy: Use 'I puff out my chest.'

highlights.text: Puff that chest with pride!

records.jp: 「……おまえ大物」
records.en: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: おまえ大物 is an impressed or incredulous judgment that the addressee is really something. 'What're you a VIP' is not grammatical and treats 大物 as a literal status question.
records.remedy: Use '...You really are something.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."

records.jp: 「適応係数８０オーバーのオーバーロードですから」
records.en: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source says the speaker is an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient above eighty. The English makes him ruler 'of all those' above eighty, adding a hierarchy and other people.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient over eighty.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."

records.jp: 「……そのオーバーロードとも、これからも普通に友達してやるよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source promises to keep treating even this self-styled Overlord as an ordinary friend. 'This Overlord's normal friend' turns 'ordinary' into a property of the friend and muddles the continuing relationship.
records.remedy: Use '...Even with an Overlord like that, I'll go on being your friend like normal.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."

records.jp: 「そういうの、嫌いじゃないから」
records.en: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: そういうの refers to that kind of behavior or attitude. 'That of you' is ungrammatical and changes the demonstrative into a property possessed by the addressee.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't dislike that kind of thing.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."

records.jp: 「キライジャナイカラ……ププ！」
records.en: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The line mockingly repeats the immediately preceding sentiment. 'That of you' remains ungrammatical even inside the imitation and obscures the exact callback.
records.remedy: Mock the established English line while preserving its wording, for example 'I don't disliiike that kind of thiiing...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"

records.jp: そう言った友貴は、一瞬で人類の限界まで赤面しきっていた。
records.en: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 'Reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind' is an over-literal and syntactically congested rendering of the hyperbole that he blushed to the human limit.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki had instantly turned as red as humanly possible.'

highlights.text: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.

records.jp: 「でも、これでちっとは進捗すんな」
records.en: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: ちっとは進捗する says this will produce at least a little progress. 'We're a little on the way' is not idiomatic English and turns the progress into physical position.
records.remedy: Use 'Still, this should move things along a little.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."

records.jp: 楽しい部活ごっこ。
records.en: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: 部活ごっこ is playing or pretending at club activities. 'Pretend-a-club-activities' is not a coherent English compound.
records.remedy: Use 'Our fun little game of pretending to be a club.'

highlights.text: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.

records.jp: 大切な思い出となりえる。
records.en: They may become precious memories.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The singular activity just named could become a precious memory. 'They may become' supplies a plural subject with no stable antecedent.
records.remedy: Use 'It could become a precious memory.'

highlights.text: They may become precious memories.

records.jp: ありがとうと、思うため。
records.en: For the sake of thinking... thank you.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The source expresses the purpose of someday being able to think or say 'thank you.' 'For the sake of thinking... thank you' does not form a grammatical English relation between purpose and quoted thought.
records.remedy: Use 'So that I can think: thank you.'

highlights.text: For the sake of thinking... thank you.

records.jp: 俺は戦っているんだと思う。
records.en: I will be fighting.
comments: CP CCA0029
Assuming this is an older revision for hopefully obvious reasons. -GHS
records.assessment: 俺は戦っているんだと思う is a present reflective claim: 'I think this is what I'm fighting for.' The English changes it to future tense and omits the governing 'I think.'
records.remedy: Use 'I think that is what I am fighting for.'

highlights.text: I will be fighting.

records.jp: 最古の記憶は。
records.en:
These are the recollections
of that which is so far gone.
comments: CP CCA0001
records.assessment: 最古 marks the earliest or oldest memory. The rendering replaces the superlative with mere remoteness, changes a singular fragment into plural recollections, and supplies an object not present in the Japanese.
records.remedy: Retain the singular earliest-memory fragment and its superlative force.

highlights.text:
These are the recollections
of that which is so far gone.

records.jp: 日付さえおぼろげな、遠い霞のなか。
records.en:
The date alone vague and indistinct,
laying at the heart of a dim distant haze.
comments: CP CCA0001
records.assessment: さえ is scalar and additive: even the date is hazy. 'The date alone' instead suggests that only the date is vague. 'At the heart of' is added, and 'laying' is ungrammatical in this intransitive construction.
records.remedy: Express that even the date is vague within a distant haze, without the added center metaphor.

highlights.text:
The date alone vague and indistinct,
laying at the heart of a dim distant haze.

records.jp: 枠に切り取られた散在する瞬きに目を奪われる。
records.en:
a scattering of twinkles cut off by
the frame that absconds with my sight.
comments: CP CCA0001
records.assessment: The scattered glints, cut out by the frame, capture the observer's gaze. The English instead makes the frame the agent that 'absconds' with sight, changing the source's attachment and using an inapplicable English verb.
records.remedy: Make the framed, scattered glints the object that captures the gaze.

highlights.text:
a scattering of twinkles cut off by
the frame that absconds with my sight.

records.jp: 俺たち一年生が進級し、幸せな三年生が引退して。
records.en:
Among us the freshmen are being promoted,
while the happy third years are retiring.
comments: CP CCB0001
records.assessment: The source narrates the first-years advancing a grade and the third-years retiring as linked completed transitions. "Among us the freshmen are being promoted" is ungrammatical and changes the sequence to present progressive actions.
records.remedy: Use "We first-years moved up a grade, and the happy third-years retired.".

highlights.text:

while the happy third years are retiring.

records.jp: 彼女は……どうせ呼べばすぐにやってくる。
records.en: Her... after all, she'll turn up quick if called.
comments: CP CCB0001
records.assessment: The source's topic is "she": if called, she will come right away anyway. "Her" uses the object form as the subject, and "turn up quick" is grammatically nonstandard here.
records.remedy: Use "She... would come right away if we called her, anyway.".

highlights.text: Her... after all, she'll turn up quick if called.

records.jp: 支払った代価は安くない。
records.en: there was no cheap price to pay.
comments: CP CCB0001
records.assessment: The source says the price paid to gather seven people was not small. "There was no cheap price to pay" is an unnatural negative construction that fails to state clearly that a steep price was actually paid.
records.remedy: Use "the price we paid was not small.".

highlights.text: there was no cheap price to pay.

records.jp: 学院には内緒のオチャメ。
records.en: a mischief kept away from the Institute.
comments: CP CCB0001
records.assessment: The source calls it a bit of mischief kept secret from the academy. "A mischief kept away from the Institute" changes secrecy into physical separation and uses an unnatural count noun.
records.remedy: Use "a little mischief kept secret from the academy.".

highlights.text: a mischief kept away from the Institute.

records.jp: 公になれば、ちょっとした騒ぎになる。

If this was turned public, it

records.en: On the very downbeat of the sneeze, the launched glob of mucus fired onto to my uniform with a nuzzle velocity superior to even that of the Shinkansen (no, seriously).
comments: CP CCA00013
records.assessment: The Japanese technical term is muzzle velocity; the highlighted phrase is a word-substitution error.

highlights.text: nuzzle velocity

records.jp: 粘着力の強い液体は、弾丸に引っ張られてむさ苦しい桜庭の鼻腔から引きずり出され、普通なら切れてしまう接続部を主人のしぶとさを彷彿とさせる粘度で保持し、橋の完成と相成った。
records.en: This mightily adhesive fluid was drawn by the fired bullet and dragged from Sakuraba's nasal cavity, and this connection that normally would break had a viscosity strongly reminiscent of the stubbornness of the head of a house that made it hold, thus completing the bridge.
comments: PCP CCA0013
See CCA0002. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to the weapon's owner or master, not the head of a household.

highlights.text: head of a house

records.jp: 「おい……はなぢる野郎」
records.en: Taichi: "Hey... Dung-headed Cumnose."
comments: Still see CCA00013. Also, this is the most obvious representation of Taichi's true ultramarine, which has nothing to do with murder. -GHS
records.assessment: The English coins a compound insult whose imagery is not present in the Japanese insult.

highlights.text: Dung-headed Cumnose

records.jp: 極度の弛緩によるものか。
records.en: I wouldn't know if it's because of the extreme mental strain,
comments: CP CCA00013
records.assessment: The Japanese denotes relaxation or slackening; the English gives the opposite state.

highlights.text: mental strain

records.jp: 桜庭はぽややんとしていた。
records.en: but Sakuraba looked really satisfied.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes a dazed or spaced-out condition, not satisfaction.

highlights.text: really satisfied

records.jp: 「可愛い俺様を、泣き寝入りさせたままにしておくようなハンカチじゃないんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Leaving the most adorable Greatness That Is I crying himself to sleep is not worth a handkerchief."
comments: PCP CCA0013
records.assessment: The Japanese says the item is not worth leaving a handkerchief behind for; the English garbles the comparison and its predicate.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Leaving the most adorable Greatness That Is I crying himself to sleep is not worth a handkerchief."

records.jp: 桜庭の体がびくんと震えた。
records.en: Sakuraba's body shook as if tipsy.
comments: 微醺... if only because the next sentence would then imply he's drunk on snot. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese gives a brief involuntary jerk or flinch; the highlighted intoxication comparison is unsupported.

highlights.text: as if tipsy

records.jp: ヤツも得物をっ！
records.en: The girl has has special weapon too!
comments: Yes, despite him NOT having one. -GHS
records.assessment: The duplicated verb makes the English sentence ungrammatical.

highlights.text: has has

records.jp: 「今助けてやるからな美希！」
records.en: Taichi: "That's because I've come to rescue you, Miki!"
records.assessment: The Japanese promises an imminent rescue; the English instead gives the rescue as the reason for a prior arrival.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That's because I've come to rescue you, Miki!"

records.jp: 霧が腰を落とす。
records.en: Kiri slacks off her hips.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes lowering the hips into a stance; the highlighted phrase does not convey that motion.

highlights.text: slacks off her hips

records.jp: 「こちらは武装していない。そちらも無意味な虚勢はやめたまえ」
records.en: Taichi: "I sport weaponlessness on my side. So gladden me by ceasing meaningless bluffs on yours."
comments: Specified, as this all but reads "I can kick your ass with Karate and you got nothing!" Cross conversation complete. Nice job, moron! -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese ending is a commanding speech-form marker, not the lexical verb in the highlight.

highlights.text: gladden

records.jp: たまえ、とか言ってる俺はどこまでも格好いい。
records.en: When use words like 'gladden' I am in all respects cool.
comments: This is to distract the reader, but not incorrectly so: he's not doing this on purpose, and this is evidence of that. Also why I had to specify it all around. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese explicitly comments on the preceding imperative ending; the English substitutes an unrelated lexical word and breaks the metalinguistic reference.

highlights.text: gladden

records.jp: 純愛貴族の異名は伊達ではなかった。
records.en: My nickname of The Aristocrat of Pure Love is no dandyism.
comments: See CCC3004, that 'pure' seems added here. Unchanged in all versions. -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom means that something is not merely for show; the highlighted noun is not its meaning here.

highlights.text: dandyism

records.jp: 「ブリキロボがあれほど欲しがっていた心を狙っているっ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "You're aiming for a heart with the intensity of the desire the Tin Robot had?!"
comments: Hum. The reference to Oz seems obvious, but the Tin Man from Oz is called ブリキ男 (Buriki Otoko) not ブリキロボ (Buriki Robo). May be a conflation/censorship that also indicates Micheal Jackson is connected, see CCD4003. ...I can't even believe I wrote that. GIS "Buriki Robo" to see the design, it's common. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese compares the target to the heart longed for by the Tin Man; the English changes who or what possesses the intensity and weakens the allusive relation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You're aiming for a heart with the intensity of the desire the Tin Robot had?!"

records.jp: 泣きそう。
records.en: It's to cry.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes someone as on the verge of tears; the English predicate is ungrammatical and does not express imminence.

highlights.text: It's to cry.

records.jp: 自分がするのはつらかった。
records.en: when I'm the one subjected to it, it's heartreanding.
comments: See CCC4012. Odd... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to performing the action oneself; the English reverses agency and says the speaker is subjected to it.

highlights.text: when I'm the one subjected to it, it's heartreanding.

records.jp: 「舐めさせていただきたく、姫君」
records.en: Taichi: "I would be most grateful to be granted permission to lick, Princess-kun."
records.assessment: The Japanese form means princess or lady and contains no masculine -kun suffix.

highlights.text: Princess-kun

records.jp: でもなかった。
records.en: I mean there wasn't.
comments: 亡かった -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese negates the preceding claim that nobody was present; the English repeats that claim instead of reversing it.

highlights.text: I mean there wasn't.

records.jp: 「……食い物ありませんか？」
records.en: Taichi: "...without any food, are you?"
comments: Sarcastic, as this can come right after Taichi gives her food in the Kiri route. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese asks whether any food is available; the English changes it into a malformed negative tag question.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...without any food, are you?"

records.jp: 「……燃えてきた」
records.en: Taichi: "...I was burnt."
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom means becoming fired up or enthusiastic; the English literalizes it as having been burned.

highlights.text: burnt

records.jp: 「いい保存食になるらしい」
records.en: Taichi: "Seems she got good at making preserved food."
comments: See CCC0003A. Well, she probably needs lots of preservatives (hee hee) -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says sweets make useful preserved or emergency provisions; the English instead says a person became skilled at making preserved food.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Seems she got good at making preserved food."

records.jp: 「同棲」
records.en: Miki: "Sharing the house."
records.assessment: The Japanese uses a term for cohabiting as a couple; the generic phrase 'sharing the house' removes the relationship-specific premise of the exchange.

highlights.text: Miki: "Sharing the house."

records.jp: 「同棲」
records.en: Kiri: "Sharing the house."
comments: PCpshew
records.assessment: The repeated Japanese term means romantic cohabitation; the generic English phrase again erases the running distinction.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Sharing the house."

records.jp: 「違う。同棲とは違う」
records.en: Taichi: "Wrong. Sharing the house is wrong."
comments: Just that bit suspiciously overstrong. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese denies that the described arrangement counts as romantic cohabitation; the English instead declares house-sharing itself wrong.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wrong. Sharing the house is wrong."

records.jp: 「姉弟みたいなものと言えばいえるけど……俺はそう思ってない」
records.en: Taichi: "I could sort of say if I could that we're sort of like siblings, but... I don't really think that."
records.assessment: The Japanese specifies an older-sister and younger-brother relationship; the generic English term loses that asymmetry.

highlights.text: siblings

records.jp: 「ミリオンは夢のまた夢」
records.en: Miki: "The million would be a dream within a dream."
records.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation but does not close it.

highlights.text: Miki: "The million would be a dream within a dream."

records.jp: なんとか食えるだろう。成長期だし。
records.en: I gotta eat something. It's my growth period.
comments: He's just growing progressively chuunier... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the speaker should somehow be able to eat or finish the available amount; the English only states a generic need to eat something.

highlights.text: I gotta eat something. It's my growth period.

records.jp: そうかもしれんが。
records.en: So she says, but is she now?
records.assessment: The Japanese concedes that the preceding claim may be true before qualifying it; the English recasts the clause as skepticism about what someone says.

highlights.text: So she says, but is she now?

records.jp: 「言ったよ」
records.en: Taichi: "'Cause I said 'em."
records.assessment: The Japanese means 'I did say that'; the English adds an unsupported causal connector and an unclear plural object.

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Cause I said 'em."

records.jp: 人気のない廊下に佇む二人。俺の咀嚼、曜子ちゃんの腹の虫、サンドイッチを取り出す紙袋の音。渾然一体となって和音を作る。
records.en: The two of us loiter in a low-traffic corridor. Sounds audible are my chewing, Youko-chan's belly bug and the sandwiches being taken out of a paper bag. They work harmoniously to create a chord.
comments: "Impopular" corridor, not deserted, nothing else. Odd. Belly bug this time. More harmonics-oriented musical terms. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom refers to a rumbling stomach; the literalized English phrase denotes no corresponding sound or bodily event.

highlights.text: belly bug

records.jp: 左側に掲げる。
records.en: I float it to the left.
comments: See CCC3019A -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the object is held up to one side; it does not float.

highlights.text: float it

records.jp: 「……いい、帰ってひきこもるから」
records.en: Youko: "...'s fine. Going home to hikikomori."
comments: See CCB0007. Twice it's enemy action, there's a subtle Tomoki going on here. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese uses a verb meaning to go home and shut oneself away; the English turns the noun label into an ungrammatical destination.

highlights.text: Going home to hikikomori

records.jp: たいらげた。
records.en: I ate up my fill.
comments: Not all of them since he hands lots over in a second, going with him being just full. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the food was completely finished; the English instead emphasizes satiety.

highlights.text: ate up my fill

records.jp: 食物ごとき、自力でいくらでも調達できる人だけどなぁ。
records.en: But as far as food goes, she's someone who can just make as much as she wants, inn'she.
records.assessment: The Japanese says she can procure as much food as needed, not necessarily make it.

highlights.text: make as much as she wants

records.jp: ゆるゆると身をよじる。
records.en: Slowly-slow I spiral into the flesh.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes her slowly twisting or writhing; the English changes the subject to the narrator and introduces movement into flesh.

highlights.text: Slowly-slow I spiral into the flesh.

records.jp: 頬がひきつるほどうまい。
records.en: Delicious enough to want to suck on the cheeks.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the taste is so good that the speaker's cheeks twitch; the English instead describes wanting to suck on cheeks.

highlights.text: Delicious enough to want to suck on the cheeks.

records.jp: 「と、自虐ネタはここまでにして」
records.en: Taichi: "And, the jokes tending towards the masochistic end here."
comments: See CCA0011C -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese term means self-deprecating or self-mocking; it does not mean masochistic here.

highlights.text: masochistic

records.jp: 来ていると思ったのに。
records.en: But I thought she was coming.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the speaker expected the person already to be present or to have come; the progressive English changes that state.

highlights.text: was coming

records.jp: 胸騒ぎがした。
records.en: I felt vaguely at unease.
records.assessment: The Japanese expresses a premonitory unease; the English is malformed and weakens the bodily apprehension.

highlights.text: I felt vaguely at unease.

records.jp: いつもと違う行動を取らないでくれ。
records.en: Never take actions different from the always.
records.assessment: The Japanese asks the person not to act differently from usual; the English phrase 'different from the always' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: Never take actions different from the always.

records.jp: はじまって三日目の『いつも』。
records.en: The beginning of the third day of The Always.
records.assessment: The Japanese frames this as the third day of a newly established routine; the English instead calls it the beginning of the third day of an entity named 'The Always.'

highlights.text: The beginning of the third day of The Always.

records.jp: 何をするにでもだ。
records.en: But to do what?
records.assessment: The Japanese says the location works for doing anything, not that the narrator is asking what the pair will do.

highlights.text: But to do what?

records.jp: 「どこが濡れるってーっ？」
records.en: Miki: "Were am I getting you weeet?"
records.assessment: The English uses 'Were' where the question requires 'Where.'

highlights.text: Were

records.jp: 「なんかオジサンっぽい」
records.en: Kiri: "Why like an old lech now..."
records.assessment: The Japanese says the remark sounds like an older man's; the English adds lechery and an unsupported interrogative framing.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Why like an old lech now..."

records.jp: 「心はおじさんなの、てりゃー！」
records.en: Miki: "I have the heart of an old lech, TEH'RYAAA!"
comments: Because she's older now. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the speaker is an older man at heart; the highlighted sexual characterization is added.

highlights.text: old lech

records.jp: 「くらえー！！」
records.en: Kiri: "Drink thiiis!!!"
records.assessment: The Japanese battle cry means 'Take this,' not an instruction to drink.

highlights.text: Drink thiiis

records.jp: 「うわー……なーんて、くらわないもーん」
records.en: Miki: "Waaah... buuut, I ain't gonna driiink!"
records.assessment: The Japanese replies that the attack will not land; rendering the repeated verb as drinking breaks the exchange.

highlights.text: driiink

records.jp: 「髪の長さが違う分、ハンデいるもん」
records.en: Miki: "The length of my hear is different, so I gotta have a handicap!"
records.assessment: The English has 'hear' where the Japanese and sentence require 'hair.'

highlights.text: hear

records.jp: 「狩猟解禁！？」
records.en: Miki: "They rescinded the hunting prohibition?!
records.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation but does not close it.

highlights.text: Miki: "They rescinded the hunting prohibition?!

records.jp: 「あははははっ、転んだー！」
records.en: Miki: "Ahahahahah, you feeell!"
records.assessment: The Japanese says the other person fell; the highlighted spelling produces 'feel' instead.

highlights.text: feeell

records.jp: 「水浸しにしてやるっ」
records.en: Kiri: "I'll plunge you down!"
records.assessment: The Japanese threat is to drench the other person; 'plunge you down' describes a different action.

highlights.text: Kiri: "I'll plunge you down!"

records.jp: 「だめー！　濡れたら髪がワカメになるー！」
records.en: Miki: "Nooo! If you wet my hear it'll turn into Wakame seaweed!"
comments: This line MT translated by my ATM machine's awesome DRM management DLC content. -GHS Shaft
records.assessment: The English has 'hear' where the Japanese and sentence require 'hair.'

highlights.text: hear

records.jp: 「ああ、ちょっと様子見に……ちょっとこっち」
records.en: Tomoki: "Ahhh, I came to see at how things are things a bit... c'mere a bit."
comments: It sort of sounds like he wants to tell him something, but he's just leading him away from the infirmary so their talking won't wake her up. Siscon. -GHS
records.assessment: The duplicated words make the English clause ungrammatical.

highlights.text: things are things

records.jp: 「生命維持活動部。そっちはなんとか」
records.en: Tomoki: "Life Maintenance and Improvement Club! That's going somehow."
records.assessment: The club name in Japanese contains life-maintenance activities; 'Improvement' is not present.

highlights.text: and Improvement

records.jp: 「隠し事があると見た」
records.en: Taichi: "Then what I saw is a secret."
comments: WE JUST DIDN'T WANT TO TELL YOU ABOUT DEMONIC RAPTURE KEICHI -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese means that the speaker judges the other person to be hiding something; the English instead treats what was seen as itself a secret.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then what I saw is a secret."

records.jp: 「ないと見た」
records.en: Tomoki: "You saw nothing."
records.assessment: The reply echoes the prior construction to deny that there is a secret; 'You saw nothing' changes both the proposition and the verbal joke.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "You saw nothing."

records.jp: 「いや、童貞関係ないから」
records.en: Taichi: "No, virginity's unrelated."
records.assessment: The Japanese source labels this line as Tomoki's dialogue; the English assigns it to Taichi.

highlights.text: Taichi

records.jp: ……んなバカな。
records.en: ...dumm'ass I am.
comments: BTW, the joke is gone from at least the Reprint and PS2 edition. And since the 360 engine is anti-furries(tm) and prints the English right *next* to the Japanese text, the joke bombs flat right then and there. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese rejects the preceding idea as absurd; the English instead calls the narrator a fool.

highlights.text: ...dumm'ass I am.

records.jp: 「怪我でもしたのか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Are there injuries anywhere?"
records.assessment: The Japanese asks whether a person was hurt; the English turns this into an impersonal question about injuries anywhere.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Are there injuries anywhere?"

records.jp: 「そう……怪我、したんだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Yeah... injury, there's that."
comments: Of course it's referring to Misato... or is it? She got injured in her flight; see CCD1001 - Tomoki also got injured by helping her avoid a similar injury. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese confirms that someone was injured; the English fragment does not state that event.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Yeah... injury, there's that."

records.jp: 「……怪我というより、心の病気の方だったか」
records.en: Taichi: "...perhaps, rather than injury, I should have called it a disease of the heart."
records.assessment: The Japanese phrase refers to a psychological or mental illness; the highlighted calque suggests a cardiac or romantic condition.

highlights.text: disease of the heart

records.jp: 眼鏡で巨乳の養護教師（男口調であることが多い）が必要な空間である。
records.en: A space that demands a teacher nurse with glasses and big boobs (oftentimes with the verbal expressions of a man, like saying 'sugee' instead of 'sugoi').
comments: Specified due to of course. Not 養護教諭, which is used below. Unsure of the difference, perhaps fetishism, training, gender... typo? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese parenthesis only notes a masculine manner of speaking; the highlighted example is translator-added explanation.

highlights.text: like saying 'sugee' instead of 'sugoi'

records.jp: 眼鏡で巨乳の養護教師がいない保健室など、ネタの乗っていない中トロのようなものだ。
records.en: An infirmary with no teacher nurse with glasses and big boobs is like medium-fatty tuna served without any condiments at all.
comments: Or a tuna that doesn't fit into the joke...? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese food comparison concerns the topping or featured ingredient, not condiments, so the English changes the analogy.

highlights.text: condiments

records.jp: 中には白衣があった。
records.en: Inside there was a white robe.
records.assessment: In this clinical context the Japanese denotes a white medical or lab coat, not a robe.

highlights.text: white robe

records.jp: 『下も』
records.en: Nurse Youko: 『Below too.』
records.assessment: The Japanese elliptically instructs the person to remove clothing from the lower half as well; the highlighted English does not communicate that instruction.

highlights.text: Below too
