records.assessment: Kiri says this differs from scenarios where there is an identifiable cause. The English stacks two locative 'in' phrases and does not state the contrast clearly.

highlights.text: it is different in how there is a reason in that

records.jp: 「夢から覚めたみたいに」
records.en: Kiri: "This will be like waking up from a dream."
comments: This might as well be a direct quote from C.S. Lewis. More importantly, Taichi does a lot of dreaming... like right now. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri makes an atemporal comparison to waking from a dream. The English invents a future event and an explicit subject.

highlights.text: This will be like

records.jp: 「いがみあってばかりで、こわいだけなのに……」
records.en: Kiri: "If all is quarreling, then everything is scary..."
records.assessment: Kiri says people do nothing but quarrel and that this is merely frightening. The English changes the statement into an ungrammatical conditional.

highlights.text: If all is quarreling, then everything is scary

records.jp: 沈みかけていた表情にさっと色がさす。
records.en: Color sprung quickly in that face that had sunk into depression.
records.assessment: The Japanese metaphor says color returns to her expression as it is sinking. The English diagnoses the face as having sunk into depression and uses past perfect.

highlights.text: face that had sunk into depression

records.jp: ゆるゆる座る。ピザには手をつけない。
records.en: She slowly sits down. She does not lay hand on the pizza.
comments: Japanese pizza, *shudder* -GHS
records.assessment: The English singular count noun requires a determiner or possessive: 'lay a hand on.'

highlights.text: lay hand on the pizza

records.jp: 感情の揺り戻し。
records.en: It's emotional swingback.
records.assessment: 感情の揺り戻し means an emotional rebound or backlash. 'Swingback' is a nonstandard calque.

highlights.text: emotional swingback

records.jp: 「挙げ句の果てに流刑地に送られたっと」
records.en: Taichi: "And to top it all of, you were sent to the penal colony."
comments: On the moon of Rura Penthe? -GHS
records.assessment: The fixed phrase is 'to top it all off.'

highlights.text: top it all of

records.jp: 「けど悪意はない。いじめも。見てみろよ」
records.en: Taichi: "But there's no malice. Bullying neither. Look around!"
records.assessment: The Japanese adds that there is no bullying either. The English uses an isolated noun with a negative additive adverb but no predicate.

highlights.text: Bullying neither.

records.jp: 自力で食事を取れる者が、ぽつぽつと食事をしている。
records.en: Those who could eat by their own strength were eating, bit by bit.
comments: The rest are oddly unmentioned... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says people able to feed themselves eat here and there around the room. The English literalizes independent ability as physical strength and makes ぽつぽつ modify the incremental manner of eating.

highlights.text: by their own strength were eating, bit by bit

records.jp: 会話もない。
records.en: Conversations neither.
records.assessment: The Japanese adds that there is no conversation either. The English lacks a predicate.

highlights.text: Conversations neither.

records.jp: 「未熟なのに人と繋がると、齟齬は起きる」
records.en: Taichi: "When people become connected despite being inexperienced, discordances occur."
comments: Literally "shelves of 'insert' kanji topped by a stop kanji, plus Abe Lincoln's Hat or five mouths". Kanjis are weird. -GHS
records.assessment: 齟齬 means frictions, mismatches, or misunderstandings. The rare plural 'discordances' is a technical calque rather than natural English for interpersonal conflict.

highlights.text: discordances

records.jp: 「だから人は、完璧になったら一人で事足りるべきだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore, if people become perfect, they ought be satisfied with solitude."
comments: Which is Taichi's problem: humans don't become perfect, see CCA0017A, CCD1001B. -GHS
records.assessment: Standard English requires the infinitive marker: 'ought to be.'

highlights.text: ought be

records.jp: 「男性恐怖症でもあるのか」
records.en: Taichi: "You've also androphobia?"
comments: Bit of anthophobia and we're all set. -GHS
records.assessment: The English question is missing the verb 'got' or 'have.'

highlights.text: You've also androphobia?

records.jp: 容易に敵意になるし、平時においては萎縮を招く。
records.en: It easily becomes hostility, and generates withering in times of peace.
records.assessment: The Japanese says this awareness makes her shrink back or become timid in ordinary situations. The English turns that emotional inhibition into plant-like withering and misreads 平時 as peacetime.

highlights.text: generates withering in times of peace

records.jp: 「いや、喜んでどうする……」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm happy and I shouldn't be..."
records.assessment: 喜んでどうする is Taichi rebuking himself: 'Why am I celebrating?' The English states a condition of happiness and a separate normative prohibition.

highlights.text: I'm happy and I shouldn't be

records.jp: 「チャンネルが違うというか……交差しないというか……」
records.en: Taichi: "I could say the Channel is different... or should I say there is no way to make yourselves Cross..."
comments: Oh, but look at this, gentle reader, Tanaka's blatant about the stuff; there's nooothing hidden aaanywhere at aaall. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese tentatively says that their channels do not intersect. The English introduces a second-person reflexive object, turns the relation into inability, and uses 'Cross' as an ungrammatical infinitive.

highlights.text: there is no way to make yourselves Cross

records.jp: 「相手の法則にのっとって接触すれば、会話は成立するさ」
records.en: Taichi: "If you contact the other party while conforming to their rules, you can construct conversations."
records.assessment: 会話は成立する means communication or conversation can take place. English speakers do not normally 'construct conversations' in this sense.

highlights.text: construct conversations

records.jp: 「観察力があれば。そうだな……たとえば」
records.en: Taichi: "Powers of observation are needed. Right, then... for example."
comments: He's also stating laterally what's needed to understand Cross Channel. Damn but Tanaka must have been laughing himself silly at writing this stuff. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese answers conditionally, 'if you have powers of observation.' The English replaces the condition with a general assertion of necessity.

highlights.text: Powers of observation are needed.

records.jp: 手近な席に座っている暗そうな眼鏡の女子のもとに。
records.en: Sitting in a seat at hand was a girl with glasses and mood dark. I approach her.
comments: Ambiguous. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese describes a gloomy-looking girl with glasses. 'With ... mood dark' is not an English attributive construction.

highlights.text: a girl with glasses and mood dark

records.jp: 実は彼女と俺は、交易をしているのだ。
records.en: Her and I will, in fact, be trading.
comments: And next he'll show you how to pull a rabbit from the top hat? Curious way to put it, 's all. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that she and Taichi actually have an established trading relationship. The English uses an object pronoun as subject and changes the standing arrangement into a future transaction.

highlights.text: Her and I will, in fact, be trading.

records.jp: 半径３０センチの距離。これが彼女の聖域だ。
records.en: That is her sanctuary: a radius of 30 centimeters of distance.
comments: Vs. a math folder... or seven? other people. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese states a thirty-centimeter radius. The English redundantly attaches 'of distance' and produces an unnatural measure phrase.

highlights.text: a radius of 30 centimeters of distance

records.jp: 思案し、少女は弁当箱を掲げる。俺に。
records.en: She ponders, then the girl sets out the lunchbox. Towards me.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the girl holds up or presents her lunchbox to Taichi. 'Sets out' instead suggests placing or arranging it, while the detached direction fragment obscures the action.

highlights.text: sets out the lunchbox. Towards me.

records.jp: 卵焼きをひとつもらった。
records.en: I took one fried egg,
comments: Grrr, have to translate it as the same term in CCD2002 just doesn't work untranslated -GHS
records.assessment: 卵焼き here is tamagoyaki, a rolled omelet, not a fried egg.

highlights.text: fried egg

records.jp: はむはむと食べはじめる。
records.en: Munch, munch she begins to eat down.
records.assessment: The Japanese simply says she begins munching. 'Eat down' is not idiomatic for beginning to eat the offered food.

highlights.text: begins to eat down

records.jp: 「物々交換が基本なんだ。あのこ」
records.en: Taichi: "Bartering is foundation. For her."
comments: See CCC0031B. Specific term 'foundation' -GHS
records.assessment: The English omits the article in 'is the foundation/basis' and strands the qualifier 'for her' as a fragment.

highlights.text: Bartering is foundation. For her.

records.jp: 「サヴァン症候群的な面もある。単純計算が異常にできる。あと数百年先のカレンダーの日にちと曜日をぴたりと即答する」
records.en: Taichi: "She has similar symptoms to a Savant syndrome as well, an abnormal ability to make simple calculations. Ask her about what day of the week it will be on a date several centuries ahead, receive an immediate exact reply."
comments: As long as it's September 1998, that's easy! This is more hints that basic math is needed here, thankfully no more. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says she also has savant-syndrome-like aspects. The English treats the syndrome as a countable symptom and uses the ungrammatical collocation 'symptoms to.'

highlights.text: similar symptoms to a Savant syndrome

records.jp: 「……そんなのいやです」
records.en: Kiri: "...that is not right."
records.assessment: Kiri says she does not want or cannot bear that kind of existence. The English recasts her aversion as a moral judgment that it is incorrect.

highlights.text: that is not right

records.jp: 「悪意はないのかもしれないけれど、わたしはそんなのはいやです」
records.en: Kiri: "There might not be malice or anything, but, that is not right to me."
comments: This is what Kiri can't accept. In a sense, she wants to push a certain shape of things on people. But that's no more necessary than it is necessary for Cross Channel to quote the Bible every other sentence to be a ZOMGS BIBLE GEAMS soon 2 be published by Will subsidiary Willdom Tree -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that even if there is no malice, she still hates or rejects such a state. The English turns her emotional refusal into a claim about correctness.

highlights.text: that is not right to me

records.jp: 「だって……人がいるのに……一人一人が絶海の孤島みたいで……閉じてて……」
records.en: Kiri: "Because... when people exist... to still exist one by one as if solitary islands on distant seas... closed off..."
comments: Tomoki's island, or Yusa's? See above, Gunjou the Island Prison, though laterally it's also the Cross World in a more psychological reading. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that even with people present, each person is closed off like an isolated island. The English repeats 'exist' in an ungoverned infinitive and does not form a complete clause.

highlights.text: when people exist... to still exist one by one

records.jp: 「いやなんです……」
records.en: Kiri: "That is just not right..."
records.assessment: The Japanese repeats Kiri's personal 'I don't like it.' The English again substitutes an impersonal judgment that it is wrong.

highlights.text: That is just not right

records.en: Kiri: "...eh?'
records.assessment: The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.

records.jp: 「お、お兄チャマが起きそう」
records.en: Taichi: "Oh, looks like Onii-chama's waking up."
comments: OHAIOOOOOO, TAKE IMOTO-SAN TO THE CULTURAL FESTIVAL -GHS
records.assessment: The deliberately childish distortion of 'older brother' is left as an unexplained Japanese kinship form rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Onii-chama

records.jp: 「いいなあ豊」
records.en: Taichi: "Nice, eh, Yutaka."
records.assessment: いいなあ豊 means that Yutaka is lucky or fortunate. The English instead reads as Taichi telling Yutaka that something is nice.

highlights.text: Nice, eh, Yutaka.

records.jp: が、それ以上文句を言う様子はなかった。
records.en: but outside of that, there didn't seem to be any further complaints.
comments: See Tomoki with regards to Taichi, but not with his sister. More reading key. -GHS
records.assessment: それ以上 means beyond that or any further, not spatially 'outside of that.'

highlights.text: outside of that

records.jp: かわりに別のことに興味を引かれたようだ。
records.en: Instead, he seems to have been caught into a different interest.
records.assessment: The Japanese says something else caught his interest. 'Caught into an interest' is not an English construction.

highlights.text: caught into a different interest

records.jp: 「ＯＫ、事情はわかった……で、縁談はまとまったのか？」
records.en: Shinkawa: "O.K., I get the situation... marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?"
comments: He's as good as Taichi at this stuff. -GHS
records.assessment: 縁談はまとまった asks whether the marriage arrangement has been settled. The English invents submission and does not idiomatically express an arrangement being finalized.

highlights.text: marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?

records.jp: 「しませんっ！！」
records.en: Kiri: "It is not!!!"
records.assessment: Kiri says that she will not do it, in context rejecting the proposed marriage. The English substitutes an impersonal statement that something is not.

highlights.text: It is not!!!

records.jp: 一人で弁当を広げた。
records.en: Alone, I unfolded and spreaded out my packed lunch.
records.assessment: The past tense of 'spread' is 'spread,' not 'spreaded.'

highlights.text: spreaded out

records.jp: 既視感が、俺の意識を過去昔へと連れ去った。
records.en: Paramnesia kidnapped my awareness to the distant past.
comments: It's also a fancy world for Deja Vu. Also. -GHS
records.assessment: 既視感 is a sense of déjà vu. 'Paramnesia' is a broader clinical term, and awareness is not idiomatically 'kidnapped' into memory.

highlights.text: Paramnesia kidnapped my awareness

records.jp: 夏も終わりかけていた。
records.en: Summer was also in its ending,
records.assessment: The Japanese says summer was drawing to an end. 'In its ending' is not idiomatic English.

highlights.text: Summer was also in its ending

records.jp: 最後の命を振り絞っていると知れる。
records.en: Straining their voice to make it known that they are summoning the last of their life force.
records.assessment: The narrator can tell that the cicadas are wringing out the last of their lives. The English turns this inference into the cicadas' purpose and changes expending their remaining life into summoning a life force.

highlights.text: to make it known that they are summoning the last of their life force

records.en: Kiri: "...Kurosu... senpai?"
records.assessment: The Japanese school-status address is left as an unexplained honorific rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: senpai

records.jp: 知っていた。
records.en: She knew.
comments: This line makes literally little sense: knew what? of course she damn well knew Yutaka had died. That Yutaka had fallen from the rooftop it should be easily understood. The point here is that she knows THE EXACT SPOT. And Taichi recognizes this all the way from here. This is why he sounds so worried in CCC3023. -GHS
records.assessment: The first-person narrator says that he knew. The English changes the subject to Kiri.

highlights.text: She knew.

records.jp: 世間は群青の危険な少年少女たちのことなど、どうでも良かった。
records.en: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.
comments: Which is why Kiri repeatedly assaulting Taichi with what may be a still relatively nasty BB gun is frowned upon, but not necessarily cause her particular trouble. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the wider world did not care about Gunjou's dangerous boys and girls. The English instead says the students and their surroundings could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

highlights.text: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

records.jp: 珍しく興奮していた。
records.en: There was a rare excitement here.
comments: Hers, and his sexual one due to it being the way he dodges emotional impact. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri was unusually agitated. The English removes her as subject and turns her state into an unidentified excitement in a place.

highlights.text: There was a rare excitement here.

records.jp: ありがちな問いかけ。
records.en: An usual question to ask,
records.assessment: 'Usual' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

highlights.text: An usual question

records.jp: 「……ずっと、つらい思いをしてきたんです」
records.en: Kiri: "...always, he was always feeling bitter."
records.assessment: Kiri says Yutaka had been suffering or enduring painful experiences. 'Feeling bitter' instead suggests resentment.

highlights.text: feeling bitter

records.jp: 「本当にずっとつらかった？」
records.en: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"
records.assessment: The question asks whether it was truly painful or hard the entire time. 'Bitter' changes suffering into resentment.

highlights.text: bitter?

records.jp: 「……先輩と友達になってからは……笑うように……」
records.en: Kiri: "...since he became friends with you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling..."
records.assessment: The Japanese address is left as an unexplained honorific, and 笑うように means he began or came to smile after becoming friends with Taichi, not merely that he seemed to be smiling.

highlights.text: you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling

records.jp: 「受けた苦しみを、ちっとも取り戻してないっ」
records.en: Kiri: "He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!"
comments: She possibly just means all that had happened at their previous school that got them sent there. But if she does have the insight that she's alleged to have, she does know, deep down, already. That's why she's easily convinced. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that none of the suffering inflicted on him had been made up for or restored to him. The English instead says that he personally failed to recover from anguish.

highlights.text: He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!

records.jp: 「じゃあ霧ちんは、豊の人生が取るに足らないものだったと思ってるわけか」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore, Kiri-chin, you think that the life Yutaka was living had no value, do you?"
comments: That's a much odder question. What does he care whether she thinks Yutaka had a worthless life? Part troll, part him wanting to know if she's over him. -GHS
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「……と言ってはみたものの、悲しいのは理屈じゃないものな」
records.en: Taichi: "...so I might say, however, sadness is not something rational."
records.assessment: と言ってはみたものの means 'that said' or 'although I say that.' The English sequence does not form the intended concessive relation idiomatically.

highlights.text: so I might say, however

records.jp: 俺も迷っていた。
records.en: I was puzzled, too,
records.assessment: 迷っていた means Taichi was uncertain or conflicted over what to do with Kiri, not that he failed to understand something.

highlights.text: puzzled

records.jp: 視界を埋めた純白が、巨大な入道雲と理解できるまでの刹那。
records.en: An instant passed before I could understand that the pure white my vision was buried in was an enormous cluster of cumulonimbus.
records.assessment: 入道雲 refers to one enormous towering cumulonimbus cloud. 'Cumulonimbus' is being used as a mass/category noun after 'cluster of' rather than naming that cloud.

highlights.text: an enormous cluster of cumulonimbus

records.jp: 万感こもごも含んだ意味に、霧には聞こえたのだろう。
records.en: Kiri must have heard thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other.
comments: See CCX0001: he's serious. And Kiri can tell, even if she can't do so rationally any more than Taichi can. He thinks he's manipulating her; he's actually asking her to cry in his stead. But he doesn't understand this yet. -GHS
records.assessment: 万感こもごも means the words carried a whole mixture or flood of emotions. The English literalizes 万 as an exact count and turns simultaneous mixed feeling into a temporal sequence.

highlights.text: thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other

records.jp: 「ゆたにぃが……死んじゃった……死んで……」
records.en: Kiri: "Yuta-nii... he died... he's dead..."
records.assessment: Kiri's intimate childish form for her older brother is left as an unexplained Japanese suffix construction.

highlights.text: Yuta-nii

records.jp: 嗚咽。
records.en: A wail of tears.
records.assessment: 嗚咽 means sobbing. Tears do not themselves wail, and the English changes the physical action into an abstract sound.

highlights.text: A wail of tears.

records.jp: ゆたにぃ。
records.en: 'Yuta-nii'.
comments: ゆ。 -GHS
records.assessment: The intimate older-brother address is reproduced in Japanese morphology without an English representation.

highlights.text: Yuta-nii

records.jp: 大好きな、お兄ちゃんだったわけだ。
records.en: He was her beloved onii-chan, that's what he was.
records.assessment: お兄ちゃん identifies her beloved older brother in an affectionate register. The English leaves the kinship term and suffix untranslated.

highlights.text: onii-chan

records.jp: 豊の葬式で見た二人の顔には、軽い安堵があった。
records.en: The face I saw on those two at Yutaka's funeral was that of faint relief.
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to the expressions on both parents' faces. The English combines plural 'those two' with one face.

highlights.text: The face I saw on those two

records.jp: いろんなつらい目に遭っても、二人で支え合ってきたんだろう。
records.en: Whatever hardship their eyes met, the two would have supported each other.
records.assessment: つらい目に遭う is an idiom meaning to undergo hardships. The English incorrectly makes their literal eyes encounter hardship.

highlights.text: Whatever hardship their eyes met

records.jp: 霧は半分なのだ。
records.en: Kiri is only an half, yes.
records.assessment: 'Half' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

highlights.text: an half

records.jp: ただ霧は、望んでそうなった。
records.en: Except Kiri seemed to have wished for that.
comments: In case someone didn't see CCC0000 as rape... -GHS
records.assessment: 望んでそうなった says that Kiri became that way because she wanted or chose it. The English misreads そうなった as evidential 'seemed' and reduces the deliberate result to a past wish.

highlights.text: seemed to have wished for that

records.jp: が、いずれ悲しみが薄れれば、あるべきはずのもう半分を求めるだろう。
records.en: But should someday the sadness grow faint, she will be searching for that half that she expects to be there, that must be there.
comments: The error Taichi makes here is to think that is a good thing. It isn't. Other people can't cry your own tears any more than a human taking punishment can take away another human's sin. -GHS
records.assessment: The inverted conditional places 'someday' between the modal and subject in a non-English order.

highlights.text: should someday the sadness grow faint

records.jp: 一心同体だった二人。
records.en: They were alter egos.
records.assessment: 一心同体 describes two people united in mind and body or functioning as one. 'Alter egos' means alternative selves or personae and does not express their mutual unity.

highlights.text: alter egos

records.jp: 霧に罪はない。
records.en: Kiri has no sin,
comments: See CCA0021 -GHS
records.assessment: 罪はない here means Kiri is not at fault or is innocent. 'Has no sin' imposes an unnatural religious formulation.

highlights.text: has no sin

records.jp: 背中に手をまわす。
records.en: Hands move on her back.
comments: Impersonal -GHS
records.assessment: The first-person narrator says he puts an arm or his hands around her back. The English removes him as agent and describes unidentified hands moving on her.

highlights.text: Hands move on her back.

records.jp: 少しずつ、情緒は沈静化していく。
records.en: Little by little, her emotions were transforming into calmness.
records.assessment: The Japanese says her emotions gradually settle down. The English changes the state into a transformation toward an abstract noun and unnecessarily shifts into past progressive.

highlights.text: were transforming into calmness

records.jp: その頃には、俺はすっかり霧を抱きしめていた。
records.en: By then, I had completely hugged Kiri.
records.assessment: すっかり here means that by then he was fully holding her in an embrace. 'Completely hugged' incorrectly modifies the completed act by degree.

highlights.text: completely hugged Kiri

records.jp: 「霧……寂しい？」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri... lonely?'
comments: There we go. -GHS
records.assessment: The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kiri... lonely?'

records.jp: 「……黒須先輩？」
records.en: Kiri: "...Kurosu-senpai?"
records.assessment: The surname-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kurosu-senpai

records.jp: 見下ろせば小さな面差し。
records.en: If I look down those small features of hers,
records.assessment: The Japanese is a descriptive fragment centered on the small face below him. The English creates an unfinished conditional and lacks the required preposition 'at' after 'look down.'

highlights.text: If I look down those small features of hers,

records.jp: 深みをたたえた黒曜石がふたつ、表面を薄い塩水で濡らす。
records.en: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.
comments: 黒曜石, AKA "see CCC0000 again". -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese likens her two deep eyes to obsidian and says a thin layer of salt water wets their surfaces. The English adds sadness, then makes the stones actively moisten her whole face, reversing what is wetting what.

highlights.text: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.

records.jp: 「豊は幸せだったと思うよ。霧もいたし、イヤなことは忘れてたし」
records.en: Taichi: "I think Yutaka was happy, you know. Because you were there too, Kiri, so he could forget about the bad things."
records.assessment: The Japanese lists Kiri's presence and his having forgotten unpleasant things as parallel reasons. The English makes her presence the cause that enabled his forgetting.

highlights.text: Because you were there too, Kiri, so he could forget about the bad things.

records.jp: 「最期まで、幸せだったって、俺は思ってる」
records.en: Taichi: "He was happy until his last, that's what I believe."
comments: IOW, he also sorts of blames Kiri for this. But given he's trying to (erroneously) make her into his Alter Ego, this resentment appears minor compared to the flurry in which he's trying to rescue Kiri from him even after he died. -GHS
records.assessment: 最期まで means until the end or his final moment. 'Until his last' requires a following noun in English.

highlights.text: until his last

records.jp: 顔を近づける。
records.en: I bring her face close.
records.assessment: The narrator brings his own face closer to Kiri. The English makes him move her face instead.

highlights.text: I bring her face close

records.jp: 強く抱きしめた。
records.en: I hugged her with strength.
records.assessment: 強く抱きしめた means held or embraced her tightly. 'Hugged with strength' is not idiomatic English.

highlights.text: hugged her with strength

records.jp: 霧の息が詰まった。
records.en: Kiri breathing grew labored.
records.assessment: 霧の息が詰まった says Kiri's breath caught or stopped. The English instead says her ongoing breathing became difficult and also omits the possessive apostrophe.

highlights.text: Kiri breathing grew labored.

records.jp: フェンスに押しつけて、唇を吸い続ける。
records.en: Pushing her against the fence, I continue to suck her lips.
records.assessment: In this context 唇を吸う describes continuing the kiss. 'Suck her lips' is distractingly anatomical and nonidiomatic in English.

highlights.text: suck her lips

records.en: Kiri: "...don't... get it..."
records.assessment: わからない here is 'I don't know' in answer to whether she is lonely. 'Don't get it' instead suggests failure to understand the question.

highlights.text: don't... get it

records.jp: 今度は歯茎の内側に、侵略していく。
records.en: This time I go invade the inside of the teethridge.
records.assessment: 歯茎 means the gums. 'Teethridge' is not the standard anatomical term and is presented as a closed compound not recognized in English.

highlights.text: teethridge

records.jp: 俺は薄笑いを浮かべていたんだと思う。きっと。
records.en: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.
comments: And this is what sends her over the edge. After all, unprovoked as it was, he stopped when she asked. That's very odd rape there. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator retrospectively thinks he must have been wearing a faint smile. The English switches to present progressive and sets tentative 'I think' against an independent assertion of certainty.

highlights.text: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.

records.jp: 衝撃が、ゆっくりと嫌悪に覆われていく様を、俺は見ていた。
records.en: I could see how the the shock was slowing being covered up by disgust.
comments: Which is odd; shouldn't it be anger? -GHS
records.assessment: The article is duplicated, and the adverb modifying 'being covered' must be 'slowly,' not 'slowing.'

highlights.text: the the
slowing being

records.jp: 俺の脇を通り過ぎて。
records.en: Passing right underarm.
comments: And Taichi the martial arts trained multiple murderer und ebul serial rapist just lets her go. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says she passes by Taichi's side. 'Underarm' names the armpit or a throwing style and lacks the possessive needed even for a literal body reference.

highlights.text: Passing right underarm.

records.jp: 軋む扉。締まる扉。
records.en: The door creaks.
records.assessment: The source presents two beats: the door creaks, then the door closes. The English omits the closing beat entirely.

highlights.text: The door creaks.

records.jp: なるほど確かにこれはマズイ。
records.en: I see, it's certain, this is very bad.
comments: See CCC3025 now. Specific wording seen in reference to Youko. -GHS
records.assessment: なるほど確かに means roughly 'I see—this really is bad.' The English strings two discourse markers and two finite clauses together with commas.

highlights.text: I see, it's certain, this is very bad.

records.jp: 部活にもあまり顔を出さなくなった。
records.en: She nearly stopped showing face at club.
records.assessment: The idiom is 'show her face,' and the club requires a determiner in this construction.

highlights.text: stopped showing face at club

records.jp: そして今。
records.en: And then, the present.
records.assessment: そして今 locates the narrative at 'and now.' Adding 'then' points to a different temporal relation.

highlights.text: And then, the present.

records.jp: 霧の言ったとおり、世界はあっさりとサッパリした。
records.en: As Kiri had said, the world became clean and tidy so easily.
comments: See CCC3007 -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the world was simply and thoroughly emptied or cleared out. 'Clean and tidy' domesticates this into neatness and misses the disappearance being described.

highlights.text: the world became clean and tidy

records.jp: 人間なんて簡単に『なくなる』んだと、俺も思い知った。
records.en: And I realized as well that humans could just simply Pass Away.
records.assessment: The quoted なくなる means disappear or cease to exist. 'Pass away' narrows it to a euphemism for death and the arbitrary capitalization supplies emphasis not in the source.

highlights.text: Pass Away

records.jp: アダムとイブとは言わないけど、せめてもう少し完璧な人間が生き残れば良かったのにな。
records.en: I wouldn't say it should be like Adam and Eve, but it'd have been good if at least humans just a little bit more perfect had survived.
comments: We're about 5 chapters too late for them. -GHS
records.assessment: The English needs a quantified plural such as 'some humans' or a comparative noun phrase such as 'slightly more perfect people.'

highlights.text: at least humans just a little bit more perfect had survived

records.jp: そして現代。
records.en: And then, this generation.
comments: This sinful generation that shan't get any sign but that of Jonas, who lived in the whale. Which then inspired Pinocchio which then brings us to dolls becoming alive and Cross Channel. Strange journey. -GHS
records.assessment: 現代 means the present day or modern era, not one biological generation.

highlights.text: this generation

records.jp: 俺たちは、健全ささえ失いかけている。
records.en: We were losing even the soundness of mind.
records.assessment: The Japanese speaks about the narrator's current era and says 'we are even beginning to lose' soundness or health. The past progressive incorrectly places the condition in an earlier period.

highlights.text: We were losing

records.jp: こんな傷だらけの人間をとりわけて、神様はいったいどうする気なんだろう。
records.en: What could God possibly be thinking of doing by spreading around these humans so chock full of wounds?
comments: This question may be the drive behind Jintai. -GHS
records.assessment: とりわけて means singling out or selecting these wounded humans. The English instead says God distributes them spatially.

highlights.text: by spreading around these humans

records.jp: こんな……どす黒い感情を抱えた俺を。
records.en: Like me... so engorged in wicked feelings as I am.
comments: See CCZAS: it's not his sight that brought these people in, it's God. -GHS
records.assessment: A person can be engorged with something, not 'in' it, and the bodily image is not a natural rendering of harboring dark emotions.

highlights.text: engorged in wicked feelings

records.jp: どうせ世界は回っているのだと思った。
records.en: I thought that the world was revolving anyhow,
records.assessment: The Japanese thought is that the world keeps turning no matter what. 'Was revolving anyhow' sounds like uncertain physical rotation and misses the concessive idiom.

highlights.text: the world was revolving anyhow

records.jp: 取り返しはきくのだと。
records.en: and that it was possible to take back what was done.
comments: Given 取り返しがつかない is the far more common term, and has the meaning of absolute irredeemability, its positive opposite is what is meant here. Seems particularly appropriate considering that, no, it can't be done. -GHS
records.assessment: 取り返しはきく means the damage can be undone or things can be set right. It does not mean retrieving an action already performed.

highlights.text: take back what was done

records.jp: 発展性のない世界にあるのは、可能性という娯楽だけ。
records.en:
A world in which advancement has no
consequence is a world that only has the
the amusement of the potential.
records.assessment: 発展性のない世界 is a world with no potential for development, in which possibility itself is the only amusement. The English instead says advancement has no consequence, duplicates 'the,' and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
A world in which advancement has no
consequence is a world that only has the
the amusement of the potential.

records.jp: 俺はその悦楽を、思い描いてしまった。
records.en: That was a pleasure I had well envisioned.
records.assessment: 思い描いてしまった says he ended up imagining that pleasure. 'Had well envisioned' introduces an unsupported past-perfect relation and uses 'well' as an unnatural aspect marker.

highlights.text: I had well envisioned

records.jp: 「霧ちん、そこは新川豊が死んだ場所だよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri-chin, that's the spot where Shinkawa Yutaka died you know."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「悪意はなくなったかわりに……密度もなくなって……」
records.en: Kiri: "In exchange for malice being gone... its density is also gone..."
records.assessment: Kiri says that with malice gone, the density of the world or human existence has also vanished. The pronoun 'its' instead makes density a property of malice.

highlights.text: its density is also gone

records.jp: 「先輩はどうして、生きてるんですか？」
records.en: Kiri: "Senpai, how come you are alive?"
records.assessment: The status-based Japanese address is left unexplained instead of represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 心臓に楔が打ち込まれた。
records.en: It was a wedge being driven through my physical heart.
comments: No, moron, the undead is Sakuraba, and he's not a vampire! Though the concept of Emotional Vampirism certainly is part of Kiri's problem with Taichi... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese presents the impact as a wedge driven into his heart. The English's 'was ... being driven' has no clear temporal anchor and 'through' changes penetration into traversal.

highlights.text: It was a wedge being driven through my physical heart.

records.jp: アイロニカルな構図。
records.en: What an ironical composition.
comments: He's flustered and he's about to start acting like an ass to escape from what is happening. -GHS
records.assessment: アイロニカルな構図 means an ironic setup or situation. 'Ironical composition' is not idiomatic for the described reversal.

highlights.text: ironical composition

records.jp: 「自分に生きる資格があると思っているんですか？」
records.en: Kiri: "Do you think you have the qualifications to live inside of yourself?"
comments: See CCC0045A -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri asks whether he believes he has the right or qualification to live. The English invents the idea of living inside oneself.

highlights.text: the qualifications to live inside of yourself

records.jp: 的確な比喩だと思った。
records.en: How the word uses that kanji from my last name. I found that to be an accurate metaphor.
comments: ;_; -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese only says the narrator considers 'black' an apt metaphor. The English inserts an explicit explanation about the kanji in his surname.

highlights.text: How the word uses that kanji from my last name.

records.jp: 「あなたは人を傷つけるものです。決して相容れない」
records.en: Kiri: "You are something that hurts people. Completely incompatible."
comments: Now she's calling him human antimatter. This is a comedy scene. -GHS
records.assessment: 決して相容れない says he and people can never coexist or be compatible. The English omits both sides of the relation and leaves an adjective as a sentence fragment without a subject or verb.

highlights.text: Completely incompatible.

records.jp: 「どうしてあなたの適応係数が８０を越えているのか、昔は不思議でした。けどそれはまったくおかしなことじゃない。あなたの中のヒトの部分は、文字通り二割ほどしかない」
records.en: Kiri: "The reason why your Conformity Coefficient crosses over 80 has been inexplicable to me for a long time. But that is absolutely nothing strange. Because the part inside you that is human is literally less than twenty percent and no more."
comments: Now here's a nice oddity. 80 is written in Western numerals, 20 isn't; this puts an emphasis on the 8 rather than the 20. Since the real number of his humanity isn't 20 but 16, we have 8 and 1+6=7. This is very intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: 二割ほど means roughly twenty percent. 'Less than ... and no more' is redundant and incorrectly replaces approximation with an upper bound.

highlights.text: literally less than twenty percent and no more

records.jp: 今までたくわえられ佐倉霧という様式を覆す、鮮烈なイメージを構築していく。
records.en: she goes to construct vivid images, overturning the pattern thus far preserved within the name Sakura Kiri.
comments: With words, not her figure. IOW, she's become like he is in his moments of ass-talking exposition to avoid talking about his real feelings, see CCX0001. This is not her becoming Supersecure, this is her falling apart. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says her torrent of words constructs a vivid image that overturns the accumulated model of the person called Sakura Kiri. The English instead says a pattern is preserved inside her name and fails to express the reversal coherently.

highlights.text: she goes to construct vivid images, overturning the pattern thus far preserved within the name Sakura Kiri.

records.jp: 言葉のナイフが、俺の精神を刺そうとしていた。
records.en: The knife that were those words were trying to stab at my very essence.
comments: See CCC0014, CCC3004. Well, the knives are metaphorical, surely no other weapon is. -GHS
records.assessment: The English uses two incompatible finite verbs and fails subject-verb agreement.

highlights.text: The knife that were those words were trying

records.jp: 佐倉霧の切り札となって！
records.en:
>                                              trump card
Became Sakura Kiri's kiri-fuda!
comments: Wordplay so transparent and awful can't have a reaction expected from the reader except cringing. More than with all the crap above, readers here are presumed to read this as Taichi ridiculing Kiri and not taking anything she's saying seriously, where context and character analysis demonstrates that the real reason is a typical, incompetent attempt to break a tense mood he can't manage. All mixed with how Kiri's attack is hypocritical and nonsensical. Expected audience reaction remains the same: a cringing WTF. Furries elicit the same reaction, therefore, there it goes. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese exclamation says the once-dull weapon becomes Sakura Kiri's trump card, with the ordinary word 切り札 carrying the prose. The English exposes raw layout markup, reverses the clause order, and inserts unexplained romanized 'kiri-fuda.'

highlights.text:
>                                              trump card
Became Sakura Kiri's kiri-fuda!

records.jp: 「あなたの欺瞞は、怪物の分際で怪物に徹さないところです」
records.en: Kiri: "Your deceit is that you do not pour your heart and soul into the monster you are, despite your place in society being that of a monster."
comments: She's all but telling him that he should be more of a Rapist Protagonist! -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says his fraud is that, despite being a monster, he refuses to commit fully to being one. The English invents a monster's 'place in society' and substitutes pouring heart and soul into an identity.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Your deceit is that you do not pour your heart and soul into the monster you are, despite your place in society being that of a monster."

records.jp: 「人と怪物との間に共感が芽生えて、仲良く幸せに暮らせると思っているんですか？　あなたが人並みの幸せを手に出来ると？」
records.en: Kiri: "Did you think that empathy could sprout between person and monster, and that you could have a happy life in harmony with others? That you would be able to lay hands on the happiness of the ordinary person?"
records.assessment: 幸せを手に出来る means attain or obtain happiness. 'Lay hands on happiness' carries an unintended sense of seizing a physical target.

highlights.text: lay hands on the happiness

records.jp: 「ありえない」
records.en: Kiri: "It will not be."
records.assessment: Kiri states that the imagined outcome is impossible. The English turns impossibility into a prediction that it will not occur.

highlights.text: It will not be

records.jp: 「体を食い破って出てくる寄生虫に、愛を抱く人がいないのと一緒です。もしいたとしてもそれは狂人でしょう」
records.en: Kiri: "It is the same as no one would hug with love the parasite that comes out of their body, having devoured its way through it. Should one like that ever even exist, they would be madmen."
comments: We're still talking about the Christian God, who would do that. Indeed the idea that the guy upstairs would be a madman to accept even murderers as long as they bend their knee is a very typical question. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says no one would feel love for such a parasite. The English changes the feeling into a physical embrace.

highlights.text: hug with love the parasite

records.jp: 「傷つけて楽しむため、あなたの目はいつも私たちに注がれている。それもひと思いにではなく、ゆっくりと時間をかけて嬲り尽くそうとしている」
records.en: Kiri: "Your eyes are always focused on us, so that you can enjoy the hurting. And it's not something done instantly, you slowly take the time to perform that bullish sexual 'teasing' of yours all the way to the end."
comments: (3P) just doesn't fit in this tone, however, it's still extremely odd that the big great Wounding And Hurting thing she'd bring up would be teasing, written with an oddly sexualized kanji. This continues to underline that the scene is not intended to be taken fully seriously. Neither Taichi's apparent contempt nor Kiri's apparent venom are the true character intent. And then it brings back to the question of Yusa: was it the same there? -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri accuses him of slowly tormenting people to exhaustion. The English invents both a bovine quality and a specifically sexual form of teasing.

highlights.text: bullish sexual 'teasing'

records.jp: 「では何者なんですか？　何者でもないあなたこそ、世界から消えるべきだった。わたしはそう思います」
records.en: Kiri: "Then who or what are you? You are neither who nor what, that is what you are, just something that ought to have disappeared from the world. That is what I think."
comments: And three days of him not being an annoying prick to her later... "I wanna be your sex slave! Go on, all the teasing you like!" Not poor writing, but a reading key. -GHS
records.assessment: 何者でもない means he is nobody or nothing. The paired interrogative pronouns do not form an idiomatic English predicate.

highlights.text: You are neither who nor what

records.jp: 「あなたは掛け値なしの精神異常者。狂人の中の狂人」
records.en: Kiri: "You are, without exaggeration, a psychotic, a deviant of the soul. A madman among madmen."
comments: It's just increasingly ridiculous and mad. This is all on the basis of an ex-post facto rationalization of Taichi kissing her (due to his automatic repetition of a previous pattern) after having witnessed him together with Taichi on the rooftop the day Yutaka jumped. In no way is this to be taken seriously. -GHS
records.assessment: 掛け値なしの精神異常者 supplies one characterization, an unqualified mentally abnormal or deranged person. The English expands it into two diagnoses and adds the metaphysical phrase 'deviant of the soul.'

highlights.text: a psychotic, a deviant of the soul

records.jp: 「……狂える者たちの頂点です」
records.en: Kiri: "...the crowning jewel of all that go mad."
comments: This even sounds stupid, if you think about it. -GHS
records.assessment: 頂点 is the apex or pinnacle. 'Crowning jewel' is laudatory and ornamental, changing the force of the condemnation.

highlights.text: crowning jewel

records.jp: 「そしてもう一つ。わたしたちに手を出そうとは思わないことです」
records.en: Kiri: "And then one more. Do not even think of wanting to lay your hands on us in any sense."
records.assessment: The source warns him not to think of making a move on them. The nested 'think of wanting to' is not natural English.

highlights.text: think of wanting to lay your hands

records.jp: 「もし先輩が生贄を求めてわたしたちに近づくことがあれば……」
records.en: Kiri: "Should you approach us in search for a sacrificial lamb, Senpai..."
records.assessment: The fixed phrase is 'in search of,' not 'in search for.'

highlights.text: in search for

records.jp: つかつかと靴音を立てて、脇を通り過ぎる。
records.en: With the sound of determined footstep, she passes right underarm.
comments: PCP CCC3008
records.assessment: Kiri strides past the narrator's side. The English calques the body-part expression and says she passes beneath an armpit.

highlights.text: passes right underarm

records.jp: 軋む扉。締まる扉。
records.en: The door creaks.
records.assessment: The source presents two successive beats: the door creaks and then closes. The English omits the closing beat.

highlights.text: The door creaks.

records.jp: 俺は一人になった。
records.en: I became alone.
records.assessment: The Japanese says he was left alone or found himself alone. 'Became alone' is not idiomatic for that change of situation.

highlights.text: I became alone.

records.jp: 言葉を反芻して、噛みしめる。
records.en: I ruminate over the word, and try biting into it.
records.assessment: The narrator turns the word over and absorbs its meaning. The English renders the idiom as a literal attempt to bite a word.

highlights.text: try biting into it

records.jp: 苦み。
records.en: Bitter.
records.assessment: 苦み is the noun 'bitterness' or 'a bitter taste.' The English supplies an adjective without anything for it to modify.

highlights.text: Bitter.

records.jp: 脳がある種の神経伝達物質を分泌し、その味が味覚を司る神経に直接乗って錯覚を起こす。
records.en:
The brain secretes a certain type of
neurotransmitter, and its flavor rides directly
to the nerves that govern the taste, creating
the illusion.
comments: He's even going into synesthesia! -GHS
records.assessment: The English preserves intrusive engine line breaks and uses the awkward phrase 'the nerves that govern the taste' where English requires the nerves governing taste or the gustatory nerves.

highlights.text:
The brain secretes a certain type of
neurotransmitter, and its flavor rides directly
to the nerves that govern the taste, creating
the illusion.

records.jp: いみじくも、自分を表するときの言葉と同じ。
records.en:
So exquisite that it's the exact same word
I use to represent myself.
comments: Now see CCD0022A. Odd he'd contradict himself there, if he really agrees he's a monster. But as the end of the script truly shows, he doesn't believe he's a monster. He wishes he were, because that'd make things sooo simple. -GHS
records.assessment: いみじくも means aptly or quite appropriately here, not exquisitely. The English also preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text: So exquisite

records.jp: ささった無数の切片が、苦痛を生み続ける。
records.en: The countless slices that had been cut into it continue to produce agony.
records.assessment: 切片 here are fragments or slivers lodged in the heart. The English turns them into slices that themselves had been cut into the heart, changing both object and action.

highlights.text: slices that had been cut into it

records.jp: 膝立ちになる。
records.en: I fall to my knees.
records.assessment: 膝立ちになる means he rises or moves into an upright kneeling posture. 'Fall to my knees' describes a collapse in the opposite direction.

highlights.text: I fall to my knees.

records.jp: 立ちくらみがした。
records.en: I became dizzy from vertigo.
records.assessment: 立ちくらみ is a head rush or momentary dizziness on changing posture. The English adds a diagnosis of vertigo and redundantly says dizziness came from dizziness.

highlights.text: dizzy from vertigo

records.jp: 表面に細かな傷をつけただけだ。
records.en: It just left thin gashes on the surface.
records.assessment: 細かな傷 are small, superficial scratches or wounds. 'Gashes' denotes deep cuts and contradicts the point that the damage is only on the surface.

highlights.text: thin gashes

records.jp: かつて俺が受けてきた『攻撃』は、こんなものではない。
records.en: The... Attack that I took in my beginnings was nothing like this.
comments: And here's the real problem: he has a very skewed perspective on the topic. An attack that completely shatters the rationality, takes away color from the hair and more being the standard would make the above look small. But the body has evidence... -GHS
records.assessment: かつて means in the past or once. It does not specifically locate the attacks in his beginnings or childhood.

highlights.text: in my beginnings

records.jp: 適度な攻撃は、適度な緊張感を呼ぶ。
records.en: A moderate attack that invokes a moderate strain.
records.assessment: The English turns the main predicate into a relative clause and leaves the sentence without a finite verb governing its subject.

highlights.text: A moderate attack that invokes a moderate strain.

records.jp: その場に横になる。
records.en: I end up laying down on that spot.
comments: See CCC3004. This is the same thing that Yutaka does. Taichi has narcolepsy attacks when overstimulated just like him! -GHS
records.assessment: The intransitive present participle is 'lying down'; 'laying' requires an object.

highlights.text: laying down

records.jp: 「いっそ楽にしてくれよ～っと♪」
records.en: Taichi: "Please release me from my pleee～asure!♪"
comments: Seems to be a play on いっそひと思いに殺しておくれ -GHS
records.assessment: 楽にしてくれ asks to be put out of his misery or relieved of suffering. The English chooses 'pleasure,' reversing pain relief into release from enjoyment.

highlights.text: release me from my pleee～asure

records.jp: 意識浮上。
records.en: Consciousness rises to surface.
records.assessment: The countable noun phrase requires an article: 'rises to the surface.'

highlights.text: rises to surface

records.jp: 腹具合から、三時間ってとこか。
records.en: From the stomach's condition, this is three o'clock.
comments: Ah, yes, Three O'Clock, that damn Irishman who manned the conn on the Los Angeles (pronounced "los angles") class nuclear submarine USS what was its name-GHS
records.assessment: Judging from the condition of his stomach, he estimates that he had been asleep for about three hours. The English instead identifies a clock time.

highlights.text: this is three o'clock

records.jp: ……キャパが少なくてどうも。
records.en: ...thank you, my low capacity.
comments: There's http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%95%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA hmmm, but if it's more like it's http://detail.chiebukuro.yahoo.co.jp/qa/question_detail/q1111321236 - which, given CCD1001, means it can be left unspecified. It means his rationality. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator ruefully blames his limited mental capacity. The English invents an expression of thanks and addresses the capacity as if it were a benefactor.

highlights.text: thank you, my low capacity

records.jp: 至福。
records.en: Beatitude.
records.assessment: 至福 means bliss or supreme happiness. 'Beatitude' has a marked theological and formal sense not present here.

highlights.text: Beatitude.

records.jp: 「……びっくりしましたよ。倒れてたから」
records.en: Miki: "...I was surprised. I found you knocked unconscious."
records.assessment: 倒れてた says he was lying collapsed or had fallen down. The English adds that someone knocked him out, implying both an assailant and unconsciousness.

highlights.text: knocked unconscious

records.jp: 「でも、そういう時の先輩が、一番いいですね」
records.en: Miki: "But when you're like that, Senpai, you're at the best."
records.assessment: The Japanese status address is left unexplained, and the idiom is 'at your best,' not 'at the best.'

highlights.text: Senpai, you're at the best

records.jp: 「面白おかしく、毎日がお祭り騒ぎみたいで」
records.en: Miki: "When you're hilarious and funny, when you're like the revelry of a festival every day."
comments: See CCC3004. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says life is fun and amusing, as if every day were a festival. The English makes Taichi himself 'the revelry,' repeats an unfinished 'when' clause, and lacks a main predicate.

highlights.text: When you're hilarious and funny, when you're like the revelry of a festival every day.

records.jp: 「ちょっとばかり、寂しくなりすぎですよね」
records.en: Miki: "This became just a little too lonely, didn't it."
records.assessment: The Japanese comments on how excessively lonely things have become. Deictic 'this' and simple past 'became' do not naturally express the continuing situation.

highlights.text: This became just a little too lonely

records.jp: 「いくらなんでも６０億から８人はないだろう」
records.en: Taichi: "Whatever you do, you can't go from six billion to eight people."
comments: 6[+0 the time loop]+8=14=7x2. -GHS
records.assessment: いくらなんでも means 'no matter how you look at it' or 'even so.' It does not refer to an action the listener might perform.

highlights.text: Whatever you do

records.jp: 「種の存続に影響ありですね」
records.en: Miki: "It has effects on the survival of the species doesn't it."
records.assessment: The count noun is more naturally singular here, and the tag question requires punctuation separating it from the statement.

highlights.text: It has effects on the survival of the species doesn't it.

records.jp: 尻に手を伸ばす。
records.en: I extend my hands towards her butt.
records.assessment: The Japanese says he reaches one hand toward her rear. The English changes the physical detail to both hands.

highlights.text: my hands

records.jp: 「霧ちんが持ってろって」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin told me to keep it."
comments: See CCC3016, it's a lie. But wait for it... -GHS
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese form of address is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「霧ちん、専守防衛なのに軍備拡張しすぎなんじゃないかなあ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri-chin might have a policy of non-aggressive defense, but aren't you wondering if she's going too far in the expansion of armaments?"
comments: See CCB2015 -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi himself asks whether Kiri's military expansion is excessive even for a purely defensive policy. The English asks Miki whether she is wondering about it, shifting the experiencer; it also leaves the diminutive address untranslated.

highlights.text: aren't you wondering if she's going too far

records.jp: 衣服数枚隔てて、キューティーデルタゾーンだぞ。
records.en: The Kyute Delta Zone was there, separated by several layers of clothes.
records.assessment: キューティー supplies 'cutie' or 'cutie delta.' 'Kyute' is neither an English word nor a consistent romanization.

highlights.text: Kyute Delta Zone

records.jp: 「そんなことするとー、こっちもそれなりの対外政策を実施しますよ」
records.en: Miki: "If you're going to do that, then we shall enforce our Moderate foreign policy!"
records.assessment: それなりの means a commensurate or appropriate response, not a politically moderate policy. The arbitrary capital letter further turns the phrase into an invented proper label.

highlights.text: our Moderate foreign policy

records.jp: 「詭弁を弄されるか。ならば」
records.en: Miki: "Quibbling via sophistry are we. Well then!"
records.assessment: 詭弁を弄する means resort to sophistry. 'Quibbling via sophistry' is redundant and the inverted tag construction lacks question punctuation.

highlights.text: Quibbling via sophistry are we.

records.jp: ホームラン級のシチュだぞ。
records.en: A home-run level 'chewation, yeah.
records.assessment: シチュ is a colloquial shortening of 'situation.' The English invents an opaque pseudo-word beginning with an unmatched quotation mark.

highlights.text: 'chewation

records.jp: 耳に棒が突っ込まれた。
records.en: A rod is thrust into the ear.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes the earpick being thrust into Taichi's ear. The generic definite article distances the body part from its owner unnaturally.

highlights.text: the ear

records.jp: 「オーノーッッッ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "OOO NOOhhh?!" (oh nooo?!)
comments: English. -GHS
records.assessment: The source already writes the English exclamation 'oh no' phonetically in Japanese. The translation first obscures it and then inserts an editorial parenthetical into the spoken line.

highlights.text: (oh nooo?!)

records.jp: 「ペイン！　ペイン！」
records.en: Taichi: "PEIN! PEIN!" (pain! pain!)
comments: should i just use furrygana -GHS
records.assessment: The source is the English word 'pain' repeated in katakana. The translation leaves a misspelled transliteration and then adds a parenthetical gloss inside the dialogue instead of simply rendering the English cry.

highlights.text: Taichi: "PEIN! PEIN!" (pain! pain!)

records.jp: これは耳拷問、無意味に略せばみみごーではないか。
records.en: this is Ear Torture, or if one wants to nonsensically abbreviate it, ExtraTerrestrial.
comments: Because ET get it get it get it well here's the explanation anyway. Original: 耳拷問 mimigoumon, ear torture vs. みみご mimigo, which is Fukuoka-ben (I guess?) for 'earwax'. Fits perhaps TOO well thematically now, given CCZAS. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator nonsensically abbreviates 耳拷問, 'ear torture,' as みみごー to set up the following sound play. 'Extraterrestrial' has no relation to either component and replaces the joke with unrelated content.

highlights.text: ExtraTerrestrial

records.jp: 沖縄料理風の悲鳴を発し、俺は実をよじる。
records.en: Emitting the name of the pig's ear dish in Okinawan cuisine in a literally ear-piercing scream, I make pun of the truth in ways untranslatable.
comments: hee hee -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator emits 'Mimigaa,' evoking the Okinawan pig-ear dish mimigā, and writhes. The English converts the narration into translator commentary about untranslatability and omits the physical action entirely.

highlights.text: Emitting the name of the pig's ear dish in Okinawan cuisine in a literally ear-piercing scream, I make pun of the truth in ways untranslatable.

records.jp: 美希は正座を崩した。
records.en: Miki collapsed her seiza.
records.assessment: 正座を崩す means she relaxes or breaks out of the formal kneeling posture. A person cannot 'collapse' a posture as a transitive object in this way.

highlights.text: collapsed her seiza

records.jp: 太ももが顔を挟んだ。
records.en: Thighs squeeze across my face.
records.assessment: Her thighs clamp or squeeze his face between them. 'Across' describes extension over a surface, not pressure from both sides.

highlights.text: squeeze across my face

records.jp: 俺は宇宙（コスモ）を感じていた。
records.en: I was feeling the space (as in cosmos).
records.assessment: The parenthetical reading コスモ already specifies that 宇宙 is to be read 'cosmos.' The English inserts an editorial explanation into the narration instead of rendering the intended word.

highlights.text: (as in cosmos)

records.jp: 少女の太ももに包まれて。
records.en: I am engulfed by a girl's loins.
records.assessment: 太もも means thighs. 'Loins' refers to a different anatomical region and sexualizes the image beyond the explicit source wording.

highlights.text: a girl's loins

records.jp: 交互に舞い降りて、俺を翻弄。
records.en: They dance in succession through me, and toss me about.
records.assessment: Pain and pleasure descend on him alternately and buffet or toy with him. The English changes alternating descent into movement 'through' him and does not clearly preserve the alternation.

highlights.text: dance in succession through me

records.jp: 「これより攻撃にうつります」
records.en: Miki: "Moving ever onwards to the attack!"
records.assessment: これより攻撃にうつります announces that she is now commencing or switching to an attack. 'Ever onwards' invents continued forward progress.

highlights.text: Moving ever onwards to the attack!

records.jp: 「行けー、行けー、スクランブルだー、耳かきだ～♪」
records.en: Miki: "Go～, let's go～, it's a scra～mble, to our earpi～cks♪"
comments: According to http://www6.ocn.ne.jp/~rejina/cc/motoneta.html it's the opening to this http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grendizer but I honestly don't hear it. Though, damn, that doesn't sound like the actress is faking that tone deafness... -GHS
records.assessment: 耳かきだ announces ear cleaning or the earpick attack. The English changes it to movement toward plural earpicks.

highlights.text: to our earpi～cks

records.jp: その瞬間、苦痛が快楽を越えた。
records.en: That instant, agony had exceeded pleasure.
records.assessment: The Japanese marks the moment at which pain exceeds pleasure. Past perfect incorrectly presents the crossing as already complete relative to another past event.

highlights.text: had exceeded

records.jp: 「そ、それは耳垢じゃなくて脳ではないのかだーーーーーーーーーーっ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "Th-, that isn't earwax that is just my braaaaaaaaaaain!?!"
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether the object might be his brain rather than earwax. The English turns the horrified possibility into a definite assertion.

highlights.text: that isn't earwax that is just my braaaaaaaaaaain

records.jp: おお美希よ、どうかその子をはがさないでおくれ。
records.en: Oh great Miki you are, somehow find it in you to not peel off that poor thing, please!
records.assessment: The Japanese mock-pleads, 'O Miki, please don't peel the little thing off.' The English adds praise and 'somehow find it in you,' while its vocative word order is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Oh great Miki you are, somehow find it in you to not peel off that poor thing, please!

records.jp: 耳を意味する悲鳴を（略）。
records.en: A scream that means 'nooo' in Japanese but in English sounds lik(snip).
comments: ...ear. Expanded. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator parenthetically abbreviates a scream that sounds like the word for 'ear.' The English substitutes a malformed editorial explanation ending in '(snip)' rather than a complete narrative rendering.

highlights.text: A scream that means 'nooo' in Japanese but in English sounds lik(snip).

records.jp: めりめりと音を立ててはがれていく！！
records.en: It's being flayed off with a scrubscrub-like sound!!!
records.assessment: めりめり is a tearing, ripping, or peeling sound. 'Scrub' describes rubbing a surface and changes the imagined action.

highlights.text: scrubscrub-like sound

records.jp: 「ロボトミー反対っ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Lobotomies ostracized!!!"
records.assessment: ロボトミー反対 is a protest against lobotomy: 'No lobotomies' or 'Down with lobotomy.' The English says plural operations themselves have been socially excluded.

highlights.text: Lobotomies ostracized!!!

records.jp: べりいっ
records.en: ~veryh~
comments: I think this one shortened the lifespan of the universe by a few billion years -GHS
records.assessment: べりいっ is the climactic ripping or peeling sound. The English turns it into a decorated near-English word unrelated to that sound.

highlights.text: ~veryh~

records.jp: 俺はオルガスムスを迎えた誘惑熟女のように、びくっと痙攣した。
records.en: I convulsed spastically in manners similar to a seductive cougar meeting orgasm.
comments: Possible reference, naturally, remains unknown. Possibly porn videos? -GHS
records.assessment: The simile compares his spasm to a seductive mature woman reaching orgasm. 'In manners' has the wrong number and collocation, while a person does not idiomatically 'meet orgasm.'

highlights.text: in manners similar to a seductive cougar meeting orgasm

records.jp: 「ひ、膝枕と太ももも堪能したし、こ、このあたりで」
records.en: Taichi: "La-, lap pillow and thighs I have had my fill off, s-, so from this onwards..."
records.assessment: The phrase requires 'fill of,' not 'off.' More importantly, このあたりで asks to stop around here; 'from this onwards' indicates continuation and leaves the request unstated.

highlights.text: I have had my fill off, s-, so from this onwards

records.jp: 幸せの隙を突かれて、ひっくり返された。
records.en: In a gap of happiness I was thrust, then overturned.
comments: The gap, and himself. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says his momentary distraction in happiness is exploited and he is flipped over. The English turns the opening into a location, makes Taichi the object of 'thrust,' and obscures who exploits the opening.

highlights.text: In a gap of happiness I was thrust, then overturned.

records.jp: それなりの対外政策……恐るべし！
records.en: The moderate foreign policy... is frightening!
records.assessment: それなりの means a proportionate or corresponding response, not a politically moderate policy.

highlights.text: moderate foreign policy

records.jp: 処女貫通悶絶二穴責めから解放されたのは、十分後だった。
records.en: I was freed from the swooningly agonizing Dual Hole Virginity Piercing torture an adequate ten minutes later.
comments: 悶絶 fainting-level agony/lesbian couples? I don't think that's what 'lesbian bed death' means. -GHS
records.assessment: 十分後 means ten minutes later. The English misreads the homograph 十分 as the adjective 'adequate' and attaches that unrelated sense to the duration.

highlights.text: an adequate ten minutes later

records.jp: 人生で最も長い十分だったと言えよう。
records.en: The most extremely long ten minutes of my life, I could say.
comments: They'd be about 90 minutes. -GHS
records.assessment: A superlative and an absolute intensifier cannot both modify 'long' this way; the source simply calls them the longest ten minutes of his life.

highlights.text: most extremely long

records.jp: 「わたしの耳かきで喜んでくれたのは、せんぱいがはじめてです」
records.en: Miki: "You are the very first to be delighted by my earpick, Senpai!"
comments: Earpick, not her earpicking: above she says it's "been so long". That may well refer to her having done it to him before; if so, she also knows that Kiri's about to get it pretty much in the same way, so this would be her pre-venge. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains unexplained instead of being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: いや、決して喜んではいないが。
records.en: No, this is in no way delighting!
records.assessment: The narrator corrects the preceding claim by saying he was certainly not pleased. The English shifts to a present continuous construction in which an event is 'delighting' without an object.

highlights.text: this is in no way delighting!

records.jp: 「むしろ俺の強力な煩悩力があったおかげで、耐えられたと言うべきか」
records.en: Taichi: "Rather should I say, that it is thanks to the powerful strength of my worldly desires that I withstood this."
comments: Given the meta above, I can only conclude that he managed to stick to his 'problem' because, well, it's not literally on his brain. -GHS
records.assessment: The inversion and comma leave the clause malformed, while 'powerful strength' redundantly doubles the same quality.

highlights.text: Rather should I say, that it is thanks to the powerful strength

records.jp: 笑い飛ばした。
records.en: I laughed at her.
records.assessment: 笑い飛ばした means he laughed the matter off. The English instead makes Miki the target of ridicule.

highlights.text: I laughed at her.

records.jp: 「ところで君は霧ちんを捜しているのではないかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "By the way, weren't you looking for Kiri-chin or something?"
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese form remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「ああ、ご存じですか？　なんか見つからなくて」
records.en: Miki: "Ahhh, she was around? I didn't really find her."
records.assessment: ご存じですか asks whether Taichi knows where she is or knows anything about it. The English instead infers that Miki has asked whether Kiri had been present.

highlights.text: she was around?

records.jp: 「……ま、今日はそっとしておいてあげたら？」
records.en: Taichi: "...well, how about leaving it at that for today?"
records.assessment: そっとしておく means leaving Kiri alone and not disturbing her. 'Leave it at that' means stop discussing or doing an unspecified matter and loses the person being spared.

highlights.text: leaving it at that

records.jp: 「というか霧っちになにかエロいことしましたね？」
records.en: Miki: "Or should I say, did you do something pervy to Kiricchi?"
comments: I still can't wrap my head around the idea that 'ero' is an i adjectives. IT DOES NOT MAKE SEEEEE-GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese nickname is carried over without an English representation.

highlights.text: Kiricchi

records.jp: しようとしたことは確かだが。
records.en: Well, it's true that I was going to do it.
records.assessment: しようとした says he actually tried or attempted it. 'Was going to' can mean mere intention and weakens the completed attempt.

highlights.text: I was going to do it

records.jp: 「しようとしたけど、きついこと言われて引き下がった」
records.en: Miki: "You were going to, but you were told something harsh and were stopped."
comments: Meaning she knows he'd stop when asked. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi admits in the first person that he tried but backed down after being told something harsh. The English labels Miki as speaker and changes the confession into her second-person account of his behavior.

highlights.text: Miki: "You were going to, but you were told something harsh and were stopped."

records.jp: 「まあ事実だしねぇ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, the truth isn't it."
records.assessment: The intended colloquial statement requires a subject and tag punctuation, such as 'Well, it's true, isn't it?'

highlights.text: Well, the truth isn't it.

records.jp: 「先輩は……優しいモードの時は、好きですよ？」
records.en: Miki: "Senpai... when you're in Nice Guy mode, I love you, you know?"
comments: See CCA0009A. Still no hint that she's aware of a "crazy ass murderer mode". -GHS
records.assessment: The status address is left unexplained, and 優しいモード means his gentle or kind mode. 'Nice Guy' carries a distinct modern social stereotype not supplied by the source.

highlights.text: Senpai
Nice Guy mode

records.jp: 「誉め殺しのつもりか。百戦錬磨のこの俺、たやすくはだまされないぞ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Do you want to kill me with faint praise? I am a veteran of a hundred battles, it is no easy thing to deceive me!"
comments: Rather than 'damning' with. More literal for more purple. And of course, he's being perfectly deceived. -GHS
records.assessment: 誉め殺し means praising someone extravagantly to death or buttering them up, not faint praise. The English chooses nearly the opposite degree of praise.

highlights.text: kill me with faint praise

records.jp: 「めっちゃニヤけてるんですけど」
records.en: Miki: "But you're totally an effeminate fop with a catty grin."
comments: Grinning like a cat + to be girly. Because cats are girls? Ah, that'd explain women, as well as cat ladies, and if we add nekomimi-desu, we have catgirls as well. It's all clear now! -GHS-nyan
records.assessment: Miki simply points out that he is grinning broadly. The English invents gendered and class-coded insults and attributes cattiness absent from the source.

highlights.text: an effeminate fop with a catty grin

records.jp: ああ、俺の正直者！
records.en: Ahhh, my real identity!
comments: Meaning the above should be the pun. -GHS
records.assessment: 俺の正直者 jokingly praises his own honest reaction or face for betraying him. It does not reveal an abstract 'real identity.'

highlights.text: my real identity

records.jp: 「なぜ怒られながら求婚されるのだろう……」
records.en: Miki: "Why a marriage proposal in the middle of being angry even..."
comments: ...but does Miki actually 'get' Taichi? -GHS
records.assessment: 怒られながら means while she is being yelled at or angrily proposed to. 'Being angry' instead makes Miki herself the one experiencing anger.

highlights.text: in the middle of being angry

records.jp: 「霧ちんがいいって言ったら」
records.en: Miki: "If Kiri-chin says it's OK."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「……そういうところがダメなんですってば」
records.en: Miki: "...that part of you is completely rotten I keep telling you."
records.assessment: ダメ says that this trait is what is wrong with him or why he is hopeless. 'Completely rotten' adds a much harsher moral judgment.

highlights.text: completely rotten

records.jp: 蝋燭に火を。
records.en: Fire in the candle.
comments: Fire! Fire! Fire! Fire! Fire! -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator lights the candle. 'Fire in the candle' is a static, unidiomatic noun phrase and does not express the action.

highlights.text: Fire in the candle.

records.jp: 今日起きたことを記していく。
records.en: I go record all that has happened today,
records.assessment: The progressive Japanese aspect does not license the nonidiomatic English sequence 'go record' without 'and' or an infinitive.

highlights.text: I go record

records.jp: 可能な限り克明に。
records.en: detailed within the limits of the possible.
records.assessment: 可能な限り克明に means in as much detail as possible. The English uses an adjective without a governing noun and literalizes the limit phrase.

highlights.text: detailed within the limits of the possible

records.jp: 無人の街を足蹴にしていく。
records.en: Nonchalantly walking around this uninhabited city.
records.assessment: 街を足蹴にしていく evokes her treading or kicking her way across the deserted city. 'Nonchalantly walking around' removes the forceful physical image and adds an attitude.

highlights.text: Nonchalantly walking around

records.jp: 前触れなく、背筋が冷え切った。
records.en: Without harbinger, my spine growing frozen.
records.assessment: The English lacks a finite main verb, and 'without harbinger' is not an idiomatic rendering of 'without warning.'

highlights.text: Without harbinger, my spine growing frozen.

records.jp: ぞわぞわと、脊髄を撫で上げられる感覚。
records.en: It's a hustling, bustling sensation that crawls up the spinal cord.
records.assessment: ぞわぞわ describes an eerie crawling or prickling sensation. 'Hustling, bustling' suggests busy cheerful activity and reverses the affect.

highlights.text: a hustling, bustling sensation

records.jp: 忍び寄る恐怖。
records.en: Fear creeping close like a ninja up to an enemy.
comments: Visuals. See CCB2011. Guess who it is! -GHS
records.assessment: 忍び寄る is an ordinary verb meaning to creep or steal closer. The English manufactures an explicit ninja simile and enemy absent from the source.

highlights.text: like a ninja up to an enemy

records.jp: 嘘のように、悪寒は霧消してしまった。
records.en: Incredibly enough, the chill vanished in the fog.
comments: Can literally be read "it's almost a lie: the chill erased Kiri". Left odd. -GHS
records.assessment: 霧消 is a lexicalized word meaning dissipate or vanish completely. The English literalizes its characters as disappearance inside fog.

highlights.text: vanished in the fog

records.jp: 部屋の生ぬるさが戻り、じんわりと身を包む。
records.en: The room returning to half-hearted lukewarmth, I begin to dress myself.
records.assessment: The lukewarm air of the room returns and gently envelops his body. The English calls the warmth 'half-hearted' and changes the room's enveloping action into Taichi beginning to dress himself.

highlights.text: The room returning to half-hearted lukewarmth, I begin to dress myself.

records.jp: 今の……は。
records.en: And now... I,
records.assessment: 今の……は is a broken question meaning 'What was that just now?' The English instead begins a first-person clause and leaves it unfinished.

highlights.text: And now... I,

records.jp: こっちだな。
records.en: It's here, isn't it.
records.assessment: こっちだな identifies the direction, 'this way,' rather than a location already reached.

highlights.text: It's here

records.jp: とと……自転車発見。
records.en: Then, then... bicycle discovery.
comments: Also "father" and "anglefish", but, uhm not seeing it. More importantly, bad feeling -> Youko's presence? -> bicycle use. Notice he can use a bike, unlike a car. This is, of course, extremely thematically important. -GHS
records.assessment: とと marks a small stumble or self-interruption before noticing a bicycle. It is not two occurrences of temporal 'then,' and 'bicycle discovery' is not idiomatic narration.

highlights.text: Then, then... bicycle discovery.

records.jp: 深呼吸する。
records.en: Take a deep breath,
records.assessment: The first-person narrator says that he takes a deep breath. The English changes the narration into an imperative addressed to an unspecified listener.

highlights.text: Take a deep breath,

records.jp: 目を閉じて、ぐっと目蓋で眼球を圧迫する。
records.en: close the eyes, and impose strong pressure on the eyeballs with the eyelids.
records.assessment: The narrator closes his own eyes and presses on them. The English continues as an imperative and uses generic 'the eyes' rather than preserving the first-person action.

highlights.text: close the eyes

records.jp: なんてことはない。
records.en: The thing itself doesn't happen.
comments: Is he wearing night vision goggles? He totally is, is he. -GHS
records.assessment: なんてことはない means it is nothing special or no great feat. The English instead denies that an unspecified event occurs.

highlights.text: The thing itself doesn't happen.

records.jp: 猫の目―――
records.en: The fickleness of cat's eyes---
comments: Whoops, non-literal meaning ga aru... or should I say gairu. -GHS
records.assessment: 猫の目 here names cat-like eyes or night vision in the immediate sensory description. The English imports the separate idiom of circumstances changing as quickly as a cat's eyes.

highlights.text: The fickleness of cat's eyes

records.jp: 自分が別の者になりそうな感覚でもある。
records.en: There is also the sensation of having become someone else.
comments: And that's exactly all the hints you get, really. -GHS
records.assessment: なりそう expresses the feeling that he is on the verge of becoming someone else. The English presents the transformation as already complete.

highlights.text: having become someone else

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんの目、本気だ。
records.en: Youko-chan has seriousness in her eyes.
records.assessment: The affectionate address is left untranslated, and the Japanese says the look in her eyes is serious or that she means it. English does not naturally say someone 'has seriousness' in the eyes.

highlights.text: Youko-chan has seriousness in her eyes.

records.jp: 握られていた両端の片方だけをはなすと、挟まれていた石つぶてが遠心力をまとってリリースされた。
records.en: When one of the two ends now held in one hand is released, the stone laid between them is released, clad in centrifugal force,
comments: It's technically not real, but http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrifugal_force is close enough. Plus this is all an intentional ascientific troll anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: She releases one of the two ends she had been gripping, sending the cradled stone flying under centrifugal force. The English redundantly repeats 'released,' calls force clothing the stone, and makes the hand/end relation difficult to parse.

highlights.text: When one of the two ends now held in one hand is released, the stone laid between them is released, clad in centrifugal force,

records.jp: どうすることもできないタイミングだった。
records.en: and with a timing that made it impossible for me to do anything about it.
records.assessment: The timing leaves Kiri, the target, unable to react. The English instead says the observing narrator was unable to intervene.

highlights.text: impossible for me to do anything

records.jp: 行動の起こり、意識が向いた瞬間を突かれると、人は瞬時に対処できない。
records.en: When their consciousness actively focuses even for an instant on the originating action, a person cannot react instantaneously.
comments: Reflexes are faster than rational thought I guess. -GHS
