records.assessment: The Japanese says a person cannot react instantly when attacked at the very onset of an action, the moment attention turns toward it. The English makes consciousness focus on an 'originating action' and obscures the attack exploiting that transition.

highlights.text: When their consciousness actively focuses even for an instant on the originating action, a person cannot react instantaneously.

records.jp: すとんとうずくまる霧。
records.en: Thump, and Kiri squats down.
records.assessment: うずくまる describes hunching, crouching, or collapsing in pain. 'Squats down' suggests a controlled posture rather than the impact's effect.

highlights.text: Kiri squats down

records.jp: 紐に挟んだ石を振り回して投げつける。
records.en: It's throwing a stone held with a belt at someone.
records.assessment: The source describes whirling and hurling a stone cradled in the sling's cord. The English omits the whirling action and changes the cord or strap into a belt.

highlights.text: throwing a stone held with a belt at someone

records.jp: 圧搾空気も火薬もガスも使わない推進力は、紐の長さと回転数でしかない。
records.en:
A propulsive power that use neither compressed
air nor gunpowder nor gas, but exclusively
length of string and speed of revolution.
comments: Compressed air, interesting he'd mention those. They have CA guns in the Club... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says its propulsion uses neither compressed air, powder, nor gas: only cord length and rotation speed. The English has subject-verb disagreement, lacks a finite predicate after 'but exclusively,' and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
A propulsive power that use neither compressed
air nor gunpowder nor gas, but exclusively
length of string and speed of revolution.

records.jp: 空気摩擦さえ考慮された銃弾。
records.en: The bullet only takes air friction into account,
records.assessment: The Japanese describes bullets designed with even air resistance taken into account. The English makes the bullet itself perform the calculation and misplaces 'only,' suggesting air friction is the sole factor considered.

highlights.text: The bullet only takes air friction into account

records.jp: 微細な数字の極地にある砲身。
records.en:
its gun barrel exists at the extremes of
detailed numbers.
comments: Assuming because it's the calculations required to account for friction and trajectory. According to a changed line in CCC3002 from the console version (not kept due to censorship metareferences), this should be what it means. It's an odd way of putting it, the term literally means "polar region". It's also there in the interview in the Materials Book: maybe it was in popular use in those years. -GHS
records.assessment: The barrel represents the culmination of minute numerical precision. The English turns precision into an abstract location where a barrel exists and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
its gun barrel exists at the extremes of
detailed numbers.

records.jp: 人を殺すため続けられた研鑽。
records.en:
Hers is a continued diligent research in how
to kill people.
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to the generations of refinement continued for the purpose of killing people in firearms generally. The English assigns that research personally to Youko and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text: Hers is a continued diligent research

records.jp: 生まれながらにして祝福を受けた遺伝子に導かれた、見た目はいたいけな少女に過ぎない彼女の内部筋肉は、成人男子さえ凌駕する。
records.en:
Under her figure that never transcends that of a
helpless girl lie internal muscles that surpass
even those of an adult man, descended from genes
blessed from birth.
comments: A 17 (18) year old girl with the speed and strength of an adult male. Totally plausible. Why, it's almost as believable as bullet-train-speed sneezes, brain cell mitosis, Kierkegaard writing Wittgenstein's Tractatus, ridiculously cute marmosets having 'fearsome' and "crafty" (are they brains???) muscles, the generation of Comic Force Fields, cat's eyes in humans, magically fogging-up glasses, the summoning of a sword from beyond time and space, martial arts masters providing random commentary, and boooy we haven't even started. Super Ninja! -GHS
records.assessment: Her internally developed musculature, guided by exceptional inborn genes, surpasses an adult man's despite her harmless-looking figure. The English instead says the muscles descended from genes and attaches that phrase after the comparison, while preserving intrusive line breaks.

highlights.text:
Under her figure that never transcends that of a
helpless girl lie internal muscles that surpass
even those of an adult man, descended from genes
blessed from birth.

records.jp: 俊敏さ、バネ、機動力。
records.en: it's in sharpness, in springiness and in mobility.
comments: All-surpassing Hyper Super, Mega Future... -GHS
records.assessment: 俊敏さ means agility or quickness. 'Sharpness' describes an edge or mental acuity rather than bodily speed.

highlights.text: sharpness

records.jp: 会得の難しい投石を、手足の延長線上として使いこなす。
records.en:
The slingshot of stone throwing, so hard to
master, she manages as if it were an extension
of her limbs.
comments: She's literally tossing stones at someone who is glass, and can't even shatter her... -GHS
records.assessment: 投石 here is the difficult art of using a sling, the belt-like weapon just described. A slingshot is a different Y-shaped weapon, and the English preserves intrusive line breaks.

highlights.text: The slingshot of stone throwing

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんの最初の一撃からは無警戒だったはずなのに、よく命を守り通したと。
records.en: Though Youko-chan's first attack must have caught her unaware, she managed to preserve her life through it.
comments: More like, Youko couldn't kill Kiri despite being an invisible ghost. In other words, Youko's completely incompetent and/or likely is no more capable of killing someone than she was at the Mansion. -GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 「太一を、殺そうとしたから」
records.en: Youko: "Because you want to kill Taichi."
records.assessment: Youko says Kiri tried to kill Taichi. The English changes the attempted act into a current desire.

highlights.text: you want to kill Taichi

records.jp: 「太一を殺す練習をしていたから」
records.en: Youko: "Because you are practicing to kill Taichi."
records.assessment: The Japanese says she had been practicing how to kill Taichi. English requires 'practicing killing' or 'practicing how to kill,' and the present progressive loses the prior activity.

highlights.text: you are practicing to kill Taichi

records.jp: この世からなくしてしまった。
records.en: They simply and completely vanish from the world.
comments: Like all of humanity...? See the new CCD0022A: this line comes right before she fails to kill anyone at the Mansion. Or anyone here: she didn't remove Sakuraba when he annoyed Taichi, nor Misato when she did the same, nor Touko when she became too sticky. And while he might've forgotten, there's no way no how that Youko forgot about Yutaka! This makes little sense outside the Youko Is Taichi's Censor Filter, and even then... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Youko made those unwanted things disappear from the world. The English changes her completed causation into a present-tense spontaneous vanishing.

highlights.text: They simply and completely vanish

records.jp: 献身的どころの話じゃない。
records.en: I'm absolutely not talking about devotion,
records.assessment: 献身的どころの話じゃない means her behavior goes far beyond what can merely be called devotion. The English instead denies that the topic is devotion at all.

highlights.text: I'm absolutely not talking about devotion

records.jp: ほとんど利己的なまでの、好意。
records.en: this is favoritism, and very nearly self-conveniently so.
comments: 利己 = convenient - self. 己 <-> 乙. -GHS
records.assessment: 好意 is affection or goodwill that is almost selfish in its intensity. 'Favoritism' changes the emotion into unfair preferential treatment, while 'self-conveniently' is not an English adjective complement.

highlights.text: this is favoritism, and very nearly self-conveniently so

records.jp: 眼前で膨れあがる破壊力、霧は恐怖に射竦められる。
records.en: As the destructive force swells out in front of her eyes, Kiri is bound down by fear.
comments: See CCB0006, same thing Kiri did to Taichi. -GHS
records.assessment: 射竦められる means Kiri is transfixed or frozen by fear. 'Bound down' suggests physical restraint and is not idiomatic here.

highlights.text: bound down by fear

records.jp: 威力は若干落ちる。
records.en: Her might has decreased somewhat.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the projectile's power would be slightly lower when released after one rotation. The English assigns power to Youko personally and presents a completed decrease.

highlights.text: Her might has decreased somewhat.

records.jp: おかげで霧の足も、深刻な傷を受けずに済んだ。
records.en: Consequently, Kiri's leg did not take a serious wound.
comments: This reads as if Youko's strength has decreased in general, not that she's doing lots of spins because she can't kill Kiri with one spin. -GHS
records.assessment: English says a body part did not suffer or sustain a serious injury, not that it 'took' one.

highlights.text: did not take a serious wound

records.jp: 回転数は高く鋭く保持されて。
records.en: The number of revolutions is maintained sharp and high.
records.assessment: A rotation rate can be held high and fast, but a number of revolutions cannot idiomatically be 'sharp.'

highlights.text: The number of revolutions is maintained sharp and high.

records.jp: 「いいじゃないか、別に」
records.en: Taichi: "Nah, I don't think so, not really."
records.assessment: Taichi accepts the risk and says it is fine if Kiri might harm him. The English instead denies Youko's claim that harm may occur.

highlights.text: Nah, I don't think so, not really

records.jp: 「好きにさせよう」
records.en: Taichi: "Lemme do what I wanna do."
records.assessment: Taichi says they should let Kiri do as she pleases. The English instead asks permission for Taichi himself to act freely.

highlights.text: Lemme do what I wanna do

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃん」
records.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan!"
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 強く名を呼ぶ。
records.en: I call her name with strength,
records.assessment: 強く名を呼ぶ means call her name firmly or sharply. English does not normally modify calling a name with 'with strength.'

highlights.text: call her name with strength

records.jp: 「取るの」
records.en: Youko: "Removing."
records.assessment: 取るの expresses Youko's resolve to remove or take Kiri: 'I'm removing her/it.' The English omits the object and finite subject-auxiliary structure.

highlights.text: Removing.

records.jp: 「取らなくていい」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm fine without removing."
records.assessment: Taichi tells Youko she does not have to remove Kiri. The English makes Taichi the person who would do the removing and reframes the instruction as his personal comfort.

highlights.text: I'm fine without removing.

records.jp: 命が助かった安堵と、俺に仲裁されたことへの違和。
records.en: A physical discomfort towards the combination between the relief of her life being saved and the idea of my intercession.
comments: 違和<->違和感, which is the exact specific word that is used by Taichi to define Nanaka and Youko. Very odd she would feel that herself, isn't it? Now look closely at CCC3019A. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri feels emotional unease or dissonance at being saved through the narrator's intervention. The English changes this to bodily discomfort.

highlights.text: A physical discomfort

records.jp: そのことが、結果として俺を傷つけるとも考えず。
records.en: And she'll do that without ever thinking if the result would hurt me.
records.assessment: The complement after 'thinking' is whether the result would hurt him, not an if-clause.

highlights.text: without ever thinking if

records.jp: 「……いつだってそうだ。自分の気持ちだけを押しつけて」
records.en: Taichi: "...always, always like that. Always pushing onto others what are just your feelings."
records.assessment: The relative pronoun 'what' takes singular agreement here: 'what is just your feeling,' or the sentence should be recast with plural 'feelings.'

highlights.text: what are just your feelings

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんが手首をひねった。
records.en: Youko-chan twisted her wrist.
comments: So she CAN do this with a single revolution? Or rather, none at all. -GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: その顔面の前にてのひらを置く。
records.en: I cover that face with the palm of my hand.
comments: ...he blocks her view. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator places his palm in front of Kiri's face to shield it. The English says he covers her face directly.

highlights.text: I cover that face

records.jp: 次の瞬間、激痛とともに石がおさまった。
records.en: The next instant, a stone was delivered together with intense pain.
comments: He could just smack his own hand with the slingshot. That's why she would just twist her wrist, not spin the slingshot. -GHS
records.assessment: The stone comes to rest in or against the protecting palm with a burst of pain. 'Was delivered together with' treats pain as a second delivered object and obscures the interception.

highlights.text: a stone was delivered together with intense pain

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんが青ざめる。
records.en: Youko-chan turns pale.
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: こればかりは、本気で。
records.en: She's only ever serious about this kind of stuff.
comments: Since he's all but using her betrayal as leverage... -GHS
records.assessment: こればかりは、本気で intensifies the narrator's own reaction: this, at least, genuinely displeased him. The English assigns habitual seriousness to Youko.

highlights.text: She's only ever serious about this kind of stuff.

records.jp: 「大切だと言う。愛してると言う。好意を押しつける」
records.en: Taichi: "You're precious, you tell me. I love you, you tell me. You keep pushing your favoritism on me."
records.assessment: Taichi accuses Youko of imposing her affection on him. Favoritism is preferential treatment and does not mean affection.

highlights.text: pushing your favoritism on me

records.jp: しどろもどろ。
records.en: Disoriented.
records.assessment: しどろもどろ means faltering or incoherent in speech. 'Disoriented' instead describes loss of bearings or general confusion.

highlights.text: Disoriented.

records.jp: 「死への抵抗感を、忘れるから」
records.en: Youko: "There's this forgetting the reluctance to die."
comments: There's no way she can know this outside of being unreset... whether at the hokora or being a ghost like Nanaka. -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says Taichi sometimes forgets his aversion to death. The English removes him as the subject and creates an existential nominalization rather than a finite statement.

highlights.text: There's this forgetting the reluctance to die.

records.jp: 確かに、そういう面が俺にはある。
records.en: That's also that aspect of me, certainly.
records.assessment: The Japanese acknowledges that he indeed has such a side to him. The double demonstrative is not an idiomatic English predicate.

highlights.text: That's also that aspect of me

records.jp: 「全力で身を守る。そのかわり、君も手を引け」
records.en: Taichi: "I shall defend my body with all my strength. In exchange, you will withdraw and your hands will be tied."
comments: Figurative and literal seem to work both -GHS
records.assessment: 手を引け simply tells Youko to back off in exchange. The English adds that her hands will be physically or figuratively tied and turns the imperative into a future prediction.

highlights.text: you will withdraw and your hands will be tied

records.jp: 「佐倉霧の武器を渡して」
records.en: Youko: "Hand me over Sakura Kiri's weapons."
comments: She seems to ask that of him... -GHS
records.assessment: The phrasal verb requires the recipient after the object: 'Hand Sakura Kiri's weapons over to me,' or simply 'Hand me her weapons.'

highlights.text: Hand me over Sakura Kiri's weapons.

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんが拾う。
records.en: Youko-chan picks them up.
comments: But Taichi's in front of her... and has a convenient big bag that'd totally fit a crossbow (or whatever the thing actually is) inside. -GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 「武装は禁止。もし武器を保有したら敵意があると見なすから」
records.en: Youko: "Weapons are forbidden. Should you posses or retain any weapon, it shall be seen as hostile intent."
records.assessment: The verb is misspelled; it should be 'possess.'

highlights.text: posses

records.jp: 気配がすっと消える。
records.en: Her presence is immediately erased.
records.assessment: Her presence smoothly vanishes. 'Erased' implies an external agent deliberately deleting it, while すっと describes the manner rather than merely immediacy.

highlights.text: immediately erased

records.jp: 「どうして」
records.en: Kiri: "What reason."
comments: See CCD3003, to better contrast with a 'naze' -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri asks 'Why?' The English noun fragment is not a grammatical question.

highlights.text: What reason.

records.jp: 感情がもつれて、怒鳴りつけたいのを必死で抑えている。
records.en: Emotions growing complicated, that she's holding back a desperate desire to scream.
records.assessment: The English begins with a participial phrase and then attaches a that-clause without any finite main verb, leaving the sentence incomplete.

highlights.text: Emotions growing complicated, that she's holding back a desperate desire to scream.

records.jp: そんなくぐもった声だった。
records.en: And with that mumbling voice,
records.assessment: The Japanese concludes that this is what her muffled voice sounds like. The English instead begins an unfinished adjunct describing an action performed with the voice.

highlights.text: And with that mumbling voice,

records.jp: 「どうしてって……言われてもなぁ」
records.en: Taichi: "The reason you ask... don't got one."
records.assessment: Taichi says it is difficult to answer when asked why, then gives his reason in the next line. The English asserts that he has no reason at all.

highlights.text: don't got one

records.jp: 「ま、そうだよな。納得はいかんわな」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, that's how it goes. You're not gonna accept this anyway."
records.assessment: そうだよな acknowledges that her reaction makes sense. 'That's how it goes' instead gives a fatalistic generalization.

highlights.text: that's how it goes

records.jp: 「嫌っていた相手に助けられるというのは」
records.en: Taichi: "It's what being rescued by someone you don't like is about."
records.assessment: Taichi describes being rescued by someone Kiri hated. 'Don't like' substantially weakens that hostility.

highlights.text: someone you don't like

records.jp: 「まいったな、どーも」
records.en: Taichi: "Aw shucks, thank ye."
records.assessment: Taichi says the situation is troublesome or that she has him at a loss. The English thanks Kiri in an invented rustic dialect.

highlights.text: Aw shucks, thank ye

records.jp: 「こんな状況で、何も変わらないあなたはっ」
records.en: Kiri: "Even when things are like this, you did not change at ALL!"
records.assessment: Kiri accuses him of remaining unchanged in the current situation. The simple past frames this as a completed failure to change rather than a continuing state.

highlights.text: you did not change

records.jp: 突如として、声を荒げかける。
records.en: All of a sudden, her voice raises.
records.assessment: 声を荒げかける says she begins or nearly starts to raise her voice harshly. The English presents the raising as fully occurring and uses the intransitive voice for an intentional vocal action.

highlights.text: her voice raises

records.jp: 空気が澱む。
records.en: Mood stagnates.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the atmosphere turns stagnant or heavy. The English omits the article and uses a bare abstract 'mood' as if it were a substance.

highlights.text: Mood stagnates.

records.jp: 憎悪が混入しているのだ。
records.en: Hatred is being mixed in it,
records.assessment: The pronoun has no clear antecedent after 'mood,' and English requires hatred to be mixed 'into' something or present within it.

highlights.text: Hatred is being mixed in it

records.jp: 「俺が一番危険だと思ったんだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "You think I'm the number one most dangerous, right?"
records.assessment: 'Number one' and the superlative 'most dangerous' redundantly mark the same ranking.

highlights.text: number one most dangerous

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃんか」
records.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan, right?"
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 「あ、あなたたちは同類です……だから一緒で」
records.en: Kiri: "Y-, you two are of the same kind... therefore, you are as each other."
comments: Let's just keep piling on the suspicions, shall we. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says the two are the same kind and therefore belong together. 'Are as each other' is not an English comparative or predicate.

highlights.text: therefore, you are as each other

records.jp: 黙っていると、
records.en: I stay silent.
records.assessment: The Japanese is a subordinate temporal condition: when he remains silent, she asks again. Ending it as an independent sentence loses the trigger relation.

highlights.text: I stay silent.

records.jp: 「わたしがあなたのことを敵視していたのは……知ってるはずなのに……」
records.en: Kiri: "I see you as an enemy... and I believe you know that, but..."
records.assessment: Kiri refers to having regarded him as an enemy before he saved her. The English shifts that stance into the present.

highlights.text: I see you as an enemy

records.jp: 「いやいや、漫画とかだとこうやって仲間を増やしていくんですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Now, now, in a manga for example this is how you'd expand your Nakama!"
comments: Manga term for manga mentions. -GHS
records.assessment: 仲間 is an ordinary word for companions or allies in this line. The English leaves it romanized and capitalized as unexplained fandom terminology.

highlights.text: Nakama

records.jp: そういうルールを自分に課していたらしい霧が、自ら怒声を発した。
records.en: Having yet seemingly self-imposed this rule, Kiri still fired off these harsh words.
comments: Wow, Kiri's a forum troll too? She already has the blue hair, now she only needs clothes at least a century off date and to be someone's obvious mary sue... -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri, who apparently imposed that rule on herself, now raises an angry shout. The English misplaces 'yet' and 'seemingly,' then reduces the vocal outburst to unspecified harsh words.

highlights.text: Having yet seemingly self-imposed this rule, Kiri still fired off these harsh words.

records.jp: 唇を噛んだ。
records.en: She bit her lips.
records.assessment: The English idiom and the singular Japanese body part call for 'bit her lip.'

highlights.text: bit her lips

records.jp: 構わず言う。
records.en: Uncaring, I said,
records.assessment: 構わず means he continues without heeding her interruption. 'Uncaring' characterizes him as generally callous instead of describing the immediate conversational action.

highlights.text: Uncaring

records.jp: 「ばかにして……いつも」
records.en: Kiri: "Making people look stupid... always."
records.assessment: Kiri accuses Taichi of always making fun of or treating her like a fool. The English changes the object to people generally and describes causing them to appear unintelligent.

highlights.text: Making people look stupid

records.jp: 「これが俺のアイデンティティなんだよ。他の接し方はない」
records.en: Taichi: "This is my eye-dentity indeed. Other ways to deal with things I haven't."
comments: It's all about the eyes. OK, it's probably more about love (ai), but that doesn't exist, much like women. -GHS
records.assessment: アイデンティティ is simply the loanword 'identity.' The English invents an 'eye-dentity' pun absent from the source, then leaves the following sentence in non-English object-first order.

highlights.text: Taichi: "This is my eye-dentity indeed. Other ways to deal with things I haven't."

records.jp: 「でだ、霧ちん」
records.en: Taichi: "Ann'now, Kiri-chin."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: とりあえず、だ。
records.en: First thing, this.
records.assessment: とりあえず marks 'for now' or 'first things first.' The English leaves a demonstrative without any predicate or referent.

highlights.text: First thing, this.

records.jp: 「この怪我、ちょっと手当してくれないかな」
records.en: Taichi: "Shouldn't you give me some treatment for this injury now."
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether she could treat the injury. 'Shouldn't you' changes the request into a reproach asserting obligation.

highlights.text: Shouldn't you give me some treatment

records.jp: さっきから、指先をしたたる血を意識していた。
records.en: I've been aware for a while now of the blood trickling down my fingertips.
records.assessment: The blood is dripping from his fingertips, not traveling down their length.

highlights.text: blood trickling down my fingertips

records.jp: 「それにこの怪我、君を助けてできたものだし」
records.en: Taichi: "Besides this injury was what allowed me to save you."
records.assessment: He incurred the injury while saving her. The English reverses the causal relation and says the injury enabled the rescue.

highlights.text: this injury was what allowed me to save you

records.jp: 「だって、それは黒須先輩が勝手に……」
records.en: Kiri: "But that's just what you decided to do all on your own, Kurosu-senpai..."
comments: Watch that honorific, someone'll think that you actually like the guy. -GHS
records.assessment: The surname-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kurosu-senpai

records.jp: キッパリと。
records.en: Flat and clear.
records.assessment: キッパリと means firmly or flatly as an adverb describing how he speaks. The English supplies two adjectives without a noun.

highlights.text: Flat and clear.

records.jp: 「借りは作りたくないですから」
records.en: Kiri: "Because I do not want to come into debt."
comments: Payback seems foundation. -GHS
records.assessment: 借りを作る means owe someone a favor or incur a debt. 'Come into debt' is not the English collocation.

highlights.text: come into debt

records.jp: 「けど……手当するようなものなんて……」
records.en: Kiri: "But... this medical help thing, really..."
records.assessment: Kiri says she has nothing with which to treat the wound. The English omits the lack of supplies and substitutes a vague comment about medical help.

highlights.text: this medical help thing, really

records.jp: 「でも……他に」
records.en: Kiri: "But... there's more."
records.assessment: Kiri is trying to say there is no other treatment or nothing else she can use. 'There's more' states the opposite.

highlights.text: there's more

records.jp: 「こんなとき美希ちんだったら、ぺろぺろと舐めて癒してくれるのに」
records.en: Taichi: "If it was Miki-chan in this situation, you'll be healing her by going all licky-licky with your tongue wouldn't you!"
records.assessment: Taichi says that if Miki were here, she would lick his wound better. The English leaves the nickname suffix unexplained and instead says Kiri will heal Miki, reversing healer and patient.

highlights.text: Taichi: "If it was Miki-chan in this situation, you'll be healing her by going all licky-licky with your tongue wouldn't you!"

records.jp: 「傷口がいたむ……いたた、こりゃきついな」
records.en: Taichi: "Wound gape painy... owChCh, this hurrrts!"
comments: Now he's just ridiculing her. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the wound aches. The English creates an unintelligible string of nouns and a nonword rather than a clause.

highlights.text: Wound gape painy

records.jp: 「あなたに借りは作りたくないですから」
records.en: Kiri: "Because I do not want to come into debt with you."
records.assessment: The idiom is to owe him a favor or be indebted to him, not 'come into debt with' him.

highlights.text: come into debt with you

records.jp: おずおずと、舌先が傷口に触れた。
records.en: With the nervousness of diffidence, the tip of her tongue touches the gash.
comments: See CCC3022. Spoilers spoilers! -GHS
records.assessment: The phrase redundantly nominalizes two near-synonyms and lacks an idiomatic relation to the action; おずおずと simply means timidly.

highlights.text: With the nervousness of diffidence

records.jp: それにねっとりとしている。
records.en: And furthermore, soggy.
records.assessment: ねっとり describes a sticky, viscous, or clinging wetness. 'Soggy' means saturated and structurally softened by water.

highlights.text: soggy

records.jp: 優しく傷口をなぞる。
records.en: She gently traces the gash of the wound.
records.assessment: The source says she traces the wound gently. 'Gash of the wound' redundantly makes one type of wound a component of another.

highlights.text: gash of the wound

records.jp: 下腹部が熱っぽくなる。
records.en: The lower abdomen grows feverishly hot.
records.assessment: 'Feverishly' describes frantic action. A body part grows feverish or becomes hot.

highlights.text: grows feverishly hot

records.jp: 「いいよ、霧」
records.en: Taichi: "Very good, Kiri."
records.assessment: いいよ tells Kiri that it feels good. The English instead praises her performance as if issuing an evaluation.

highlights.text: Very good, Kiri.

records.jp: 時折、舌を離して熱いため息をつく。
records.en: On occasion, she distances her tongue and breathes a hot sigh.
records.assessment: She occasionally pulls or lifts her tongue away. A person does not idiomatically 'distance' a body part in this construction.

highlights.text: distances her tongue

records.jp: 「指先の方も、キレイにして」
records.en: Taichi: "The fingertips, too, make them clean."
records.assessment: Taichi tells her to clean his fingertips too. The English makes the fingertips a left-dislocated subject and uses an unexplained plural object 'them.'

highlights.text: The fingertips, too, make them clean.

records.jp: ねろねろと舌が蛇行し、てのひらをおりていく。
records.en: With salivation noises her tongue crawls serpentine, descending on the palm of the hand.
records.assessment: The tongue travels down his palm. 'Descending on' suggests alighting upon it rather than moving along its surface.

highlights.text: descending on the palm

records.jp: 「血は取れた？」
records.en: Taichi: "Did you remove the blood?
records.assessment: The spoken line opens with a quotation mark but has no closing quotation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Did you remove the blood?

records.jp: 指先を出すと、霧はこわごわと唇を這わせた。
records.en: Kiri timidly, nervously makes her lips crawl on the offered fingertips.
records.assessment: She timidly runs or presses her lips over the offered fingertips. 'Makes her lips crawl' personifies them as an independent creature and uses the wrong preposition.

highlights.text: makes her lips crawl on

records.jp: いけない、な。
records.en: That... it ought not be.
comments: He wants to stick his duck inside her. Why a duck? Because you must eat it, that's why! Don't you know Panese? That's the language of people who eat too much pan. Duck pan. -GHS
records.assessment: The construction requires 'ought not to be'; the source more directly says the situation is bad or must stop.

highlights.text: it ought not be

records.jp: やがて霧は舌を離す。
records.en: Before long Kiri distances her tongue.
records.assessment: The Japanese says she finally pulls her tongue away. English does not naturally use 'distance' transitively for this body movement.

highlights.text: distances her tongue

records.jp: 血も止まっていた。
records.en: The blood had been stopped as well.
records.assessment: The bleeding had stopped. The English makes blood itself a passively stopped substance and implies an unstated agent.

highlights.text: The blood had been stopped

records.jp: 「……曜子ちゃんの言ったこと、本気だと思う」
records.en: Taichi: "...what Youko-chan said, I think she's serious."
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 「俺だって、みんなをどうこうしようなんて思ってない」
records.en: Taichi: "Me, I don't really think want to do much to anyone."
records.assessment: The English has two competing finite predicates and needs either 'don't really want' or 'don't really think I want.'

highlights.text: I don't really think want

records.jp: 「霧が言うように、ろくでなしではあるけど……仲間を傷つけるつもりはないよ」
records.en: Taichi: "As you said, Kiri, although I might be a ne'er-do-well... I have no intention of hurting my Nakama... my friends."
records.assessment: 仲間 is directly translatable as companions or friends here. The English first leaves it as capitalized Japanese fandom terminology and then adds an in-line gloss.

highlights.text: my Nakama... my friends

records.jp: 「それどころか、怪我したみみ先輩にかわってアンテナを組み立てているところだ」
records.en: Taichi: "On the contrary, I'm assembling the antenna in place of Mimi-senpai, who got hurt."
records.assessment: The name-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Mimi-senpai

records.jp: 「……人なんて、もういない」
records.en: Kiri: "...but people... there's none anymore."
records.assessment: The plural antecedent requires 'there are none' or 'there isn't anyone.'

highlights.text: people... there's none

records.jp: 「何もかも通じなくなって……誰が生きているって言うんですか」
records.en: Kiri: "Nothing but nothing seems to be conveyed... are you saying someone is still alive?"
comments: ...but she could still mean "I can't find anything good about the people around me", i.e. that everybody is metaphorically gone, not literally so. Regardless, it's only these two lines, as the first can well be metaphorical. -GHS
records.assessment: 何もかも通じなくなって says every means of communication has stopped working or getting through. The English double negative phrase is malformed and 'conveyed' lacks a message or recipient.

highlights.text: Nothing but nothing seems to be conveyed

records.jp: 俺には、甘美な響きさえともなう。
records.en: To me, that comes with nothing but a distinctively sweet sound.
records.assessment: さえ says the phrase carries even a sweet resonance for him, as an unexpected additional quality. 'Nothing but' says sweetness is its sole quality and reverses the scalar relation.

highlights.text: nothing but a distinctively sweet sound

records.jp: 「……合宿……つまらなかったな」
records.en: Taichi: "...that training camp... wasn't that pointless."
comments: Odd change of topic. -GHS
records.assessment: つまらなかった says the camp was boring, dull, or worthless. The English inserts negation and turns the judgment into its opposite.

highlights.text: wasn't that pointless

records.jp: 「無理矢理セッティングして、苦労して７人集めて、なだめすかしたり嘘ついたりして……」
records.en: Taichi: "Forcing the setting against will, gathering seven people with so much hardship, with soothing and coaxing, with blatant lies..."
records.assessment: He forcibly arranged the camp and struggled to gather seven people. The English nominalization lacks whose will was opposed and does not form an idiomatic action.

highlights.text: Forcing the setting against will

records.jp: 霧は異質なものでも見る目つきを、俺に投げかけている。
records.en: Kiri threw a look at me that said she was yet discerning something heterogeneous.
records.assessment: Kiri looks at him as though he were something alien or abnormal. The English uses a technical adjective for mixed composition, adds 'yet,' and makes her look report an ongoing act of discernment.

highlights.text: a look at me that said she was yet discerning something heterogeneous

records.jp: 「仲直りさせる機会を作るため、合宿に人を集めたって言うんですか？」
records.en: Kiri: "Are you saying that you intended to create a chance for reconciliation by assembling the people at the training camp?"
records.assessment: He gathered people for the camp. 'Assemble' can be intransitive for people, but 'assembling the people' treats them like objects or equipment being put together.

highlights.text: assembling the people

records.jp: 瞳をしばたく。
records.en: Pupils twinkle.
records.assessment: 瞳をしばたく means she blinks her eyes in surprise. The English instead says the pupils emit sparkling light.

highlights.text: Pupils twinkle.

records.jp: 一文内に指示代名詞を四回も使うという、近代日本語表現の目指す美学にてらしあわせるとすこぶる不格好な慣用語を用いて、俺は話をそらす。
records.en: By inserting demonstrative pronouns four times in a sentence I construct an idiom that is extremely unshapely and clumsy when contrasted with the aesthetic sense that is the goal of modern Japanese expression, and with it I change subject.
comments: Something is very wrong here. What has Japanese got to do with anything when this is in English??? HELP! -GHS
records.assessment: He changes the subject of the conversation. English requires the article 'the' and more naturally calls it changing the topic.

highlights.text: change subject

records.jp: 「立派じゃないけど、仲良きことは美しきかな、だ」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm not upstanding, but I can still think about what a beautiful thing it is to get along well, can't I."
comments: The problem is that he doesn't like good relationships to change... or relationships to change at all. -GHS
records.assessment: 仲良きことは美しきかな is a recognizable fixed literary quotation meaning roughly 'how beautiful it is to live in harmony.' The English dissolves it into generic explanation, omits its quoted aphoristic form, and adds a tag question.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm not upstanding, but I can still think about what a beautiful thing it is to get along well, can't I."

records.jp: 「さわらにゃわからん、と」
records.en: Taichi: "If I donn'touch I can't know, duh."
records.assessment: The words are incorrectly fused and the auxiliary is misspelled; the phrase should be 'don't touch.'

highlights.text: donn'touch

records.jp: 「他には？」
records.en: Taichi: "The other?"
records.assessment: 他には asks whether she is hurt anywhere else or has any other injuries. 'The other' presupposes a specific second item that has not been named.

highlights.text: The other?

records.jp: 「はだけて」
records.en: Taichi: "Strip."
records.assessment: Taichi tells Kiri to uncover the injured shoulder. 'Strip' instructs her to remove her clothing generally and greatly broadens the command.

highlights.text: Strip.

records.jp: 肩を抱いて、後ずさる。
records.en: Covering her shoulders, she steps back.
records.assessment: 肩を抱いて says she clutches or holds the injured shoulder as she retreats. 'Covering her shoulders' changes the protective physical action and makes the body part plural.

highlights.text: Covering her shoulders

records.jp: 「いろんな接触をして境界線を調整していくのが、人付き合いってやつだろ？　違うのか？」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm adapting the boundary lines as I perform all kinds of contacts. Isn't that what with socializing is? Am I wrong?"
records.assessment: Taichi describes social interaction as mutually adjusting boundaries through many kinds of contact. The English makes him alone adapt the boundaries and produces the ungrammatical question 'what with socializing is.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm adapting the boundary lines as I perform all kinds of contacts. Isn't that what with socializing is? Am I wrong?"

records.jp: 「霧ちんは生真面目に受け取りすぎだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri-chin, you just take things just way, way too seriously."
comments: In short. But so does Miki. -GHS
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 軽く揉んだら、痛がった。
records.en: There was pain even when I went over it lightly.
comments: 揉 -GHS
records.assessment: He lightly massages or squeezes the shoulder and she shows pain. 'Went over it' omits the tactile examination and can mean merely reviewing something.

highlights.text: went over it lightly

records.jp: 「……こっちはまずい箇所に当たったな」
records.en: Taichi: "...I touched the bad spot have I."
records.assessment: Taichi observes that the projectile struck this injury in a bad spot. The English instead attributes the pain to where he just touched her.

highlights.text: I touched the bad spot

records.jp: 「どのくらい痛い？」
records.en: Taichi: "How much pain?"
records.assessment: English asks 'How bad does it hurt?' or 'How much does it hurt?' The bare noun phrase is not a natural question here.

highlights.text: How much pain?

records.jp: 「……ほとんど……腕も動きます……」
records.en: Kiri: "...I can just about... still move the arm..."
records.assessment: Kiri says it hardly hurts and offers her ability to move the arm as evidence. 'Just about' instead says she can barely move it.

highlights.text: I can just about... still move the arm

records.jp: 「……先輩が、力を入れすぎるんです」
records.en: Kiri: "...you just put too much strength into it, Senpai."
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「そんな入れてないよ」
records.en: Taichi: "I didn't put any of the sort."
records.assessment: Taichi says he did not use that much force. The English denies using any unspecified thing and is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: I didn't put any of the sort

records.jp: 「……男の人は、みんな力強いじゃないですか……島先輩とかだって、あんな細いのに一人でモニター持ち上げるし」
records.en: Kiri: "...men are all so strong aren't they... Shima-senpai, for example, he's so slender yet he can lift one of those monitors on his own."
comments: Says the girl who can fire a crossbow WITH ONE HAND. And once again, Super Ninja with her supra-male muscles can't take this thing? -GHS
records.assessment: The surname-plus-status address remains in Japanese morphology rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Shima-senpai

records.jp: 「……あいつは元バスケ部で……走れないだけで筋力はそのままだから」
records.en: Taichi: "...that guy's ex-basketball club, that's why... he can't run, that's it, his physical strength remains."
records.assessment: He is a former basketball-club member; he merely cannot run now, while his muscular strength remains. The English calls the person a club and makes the club history sound like the reason he cannot run.

highlights.text: that guy's ex-basketball club, that's why... he can't run, that's it

records.jp: 放送部で腕相撲したら、最下位になるんじゃないか。
records.en: If the Broadcast Club had an arm wrestling competition, wouldn't she fall dead last rank?
comments: ...despite surviving two direct stone strikes by an allegedly trained killer without an issue, having a nearly superhumanly powerful kick, and later in Miki's route she'll keep toe-to-toe with Taichi repeatedly. -GHS
records.assessment: English says 'come in dead last' or 'rank last,' not 'fall dead last rank.'

highlights.text: fall dead last rank

records.jp: 立ち上がる。
records.en: I start going.
comments: Lit. "I stand up", but in the water level thing above, Taichi was standing, Kiri was kneeling, and he is not even hinted to have kneeled when he checked her wound. Going with a lateral meaning, but I suspect error. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator stands up. The English instead says he begins to depart or move.

highlights.text: I start going

records.jp: 不承不承、ついてくる。
records.en: Unwillingly and grudgingly she comes with.
records.assessment: The phrasal construction requires an object or adverb: 'comes with me' or 'comes along.'

highlights.text: she comes with

records.jp: 「一人になったら曜子ちゃんに襲われるかもよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "I think Youko-chan'll attack if you're on your own, don't you?"
records.assessment: The affectionate address is left unexplained. Taichi warns that Youko might attack Kiri if she is alone; the English adds 'I think' and a tag asking Kiri to agree with her own possible attack.

highlights.text: I think Youko-chan'll attack if you're on your own, don't you?

records.jp: 俺は火炎放射器の一つさえも持っていない、ひ弱な現代ボウイだ。
records.en: Not a single flamethrower I own, wimpish modern Bowie that I am.
comments: Hum. ボウイ is certainly not an alternate spelling for "boy" that I can find, as in, at all. And the correct ボーイ has been used, so it's intentional. Unchanged in the console versions.暴威 ("violent tyranny") doesn't seem to quite fit.

Splitting the difference and going with David Bowie, for which this IS the correct transliteration. We had Michael Jackson and his zombies, we might have Ground Control to Major Tom as well. I know, Space Oddity wasn't about aliens... but 2001 ASO, to which it is inspired, was. And that's about the following century, the evolution of mankind, and lots more related themes. Plus it's Taichi and he'd totally bring that up when it's only this vaguely related, because he's precisely the kind of half-educated twit who would. -GHS
records.assessment: 現代ボウイ is a stylized 'modern boy.' 'Bowie' turns it into the unrelated surname of the musician David Bowie.

highlights.text: modern Bowie

records.jp: 拳だけ、あればいい。
records.en: Not as long as I have the Fist.
comments: Running punches are particularly effective. Eat it, vid boi! -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says fists are all he needs. The English begins with negation, producing a fragment that means he does not need something only while he has one abstract 'Fist.'

highlights.text: Not as long as I have the Fist.

records.jp: 空手の亜種としてのそしり・中傷・訴訟。
records.en: Calumny - slander - lawsuits place it as a subspecies of Karate.
records.assessment: The mock school has endured accusations, abuse, and lawsuits over being a karate offshoot. The English makes those three things actively classify it as one and uses punctuation in place of a grammatical list.

highlights.text: Calumny - slander - lawsuits place it as a subspecies of Karate.

records.jp: 幾人もの戦友が、道を離れていった。
records.en:
>                                Nakama
Countless Comrade-in-Arms had abandoned the Way.
comments: Some shonen is certainly chuuni, but is all chuuni automatically shonen? I suppose it depends on whether anybody cries if we put all shonen and chuuni inside a forest and set it on fire; in that case, we toss said criers on the fire as well. Problems solved! All of them! -GHS
records.assessment: The source says many comrades left the path. The English exposes raw annotation layout and unexplained 'Nakama,' then combines plural 'countless' with singular 'Comrade-in-Arms.'

highlights.text:
>                                Nakama
Countless Comrade-in-Arms had abandoned the Way.

records.jp: だが人類が地球から根絶されようとしている今、ついに本懐の刻は訪れたのだ！
records.en: However, in this present where humanity is about to be exterminated from the Earth, at last has the time of my long-cherished desire come!
comments: Hmmm... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says 'now, when humanity is about to be eradicated.' English does not use 'this present' as a temporal location in this construction.

highlights.text: in this present where

records.jp: いない。
records.en: Unpresent,
records.assessment: いない simply means the person is not there. 'Unpresent' is an extremely rare adjective and cannot stand naturally as this locative fragment.

highlights.text: Unpresent

records.jp: トイレ……にはいない。
records.en: Toilet... in it is unpresent.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the person is not in the bathroom. 'Unpresent' is not a locative predicate for a person, and the inverted prepositional construction is malformed.

highlights.text: in it is unpresent

records.jp: 浴槽……にはいない。
records.en: Bathtub... in it is unpresent.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the person is not in the bath. 'Unpresent' is not a locative predicate for a person, and the inverted prepositional construction is malformed.

highlights.text: in it is unpresent

records.jp: 一階の物置部屋……いない。
records.en: First floor storage room... unpresent.
records.assessment: The person is not in the storage room. 'Unpresent' is an unnatural substitute for 'not there.'

highlights.text: unpresent

records.jp: 睦美さんの寝室……いない。
records.en: Mutsumi-san's bedroom... unpresent.
comments: So her bedroom is on the ground floor. -GHS
records.assessment: The honorific is left unexplained, and 'unpresent' does not naturally say that the person is absent from the bedroom.

highlights.text: Mutsumi-san's bedroom... unpresent.

records.jp: ごめんなさい睦美さん。
records.en: Apologies, Mutsumi-san.
records.assessment: The Japanese honorific remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Mutsumi-san

records.jp: 俺の部屋……の隣。
records.en: to my room's... closest room.
comments: Effect -GHS
records.assessment: The room is directly next to his, not merely whichever other room happens to be closest.

highlights.text: closest room

records.jp: おねえちゃん部屋。
records.en: Onee-chan's room.
comments: See CCC0033B, it's definitely Youko's. -GHS
records.assessment: The kinship term and affectionate suffix are left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Onee-chan's room

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんが、家を出ていって以来になる。
records.en: Ever since Youko-chan left the house.
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 室内に飛び込むと同時に、演舞！
records.en: I catapult myself into the room and at the same time, I dance!
records.assessment: 演舞 here is a stylized martial-arts demonstration or kata as he bursts into the room. Calling it simply a dance removes the mock-combat action.

highlights.text: I dance!

records.jp: ホコリが舞う。
records.en: Dust and pride fluttering and dancing.
comments: 誇り still -GHS
records.assessment: The source says only that dust rises or swirls. The English invents pride as a second thing fluttering in the room.

highlights.text: and pride

records.jp: ホコリの中で暴れたせいか、喉が渇いた。
records.en: Perhaps because of my boastful struggle in the middle of dust, my throat was parched.
comments: And 誇り again! And of course he's parched, after working in there for an hour or so. -GHS
records.assessment: 暴れた says he thrashed or rampaged around in the dust. The English adds boasting and recasts the comic physical movement as a struggle.

highlights.text: boastful struggle

records.jp: 「そこでおまえの家に来てみたら、トマトがあるじゃないか」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Therefore I came to your house, because aren't there tomatoes here."
comments: Seems like he expected to find tomatoes there, see CCC0035A. -GHS
records.assessment: He came to the house and found tomatoes there. The English combines 'therefore,' 'because,' and an embedded question into a contradictory causal sentence.

highlights.text: Therefore I came to your house, because aren't there tomatoes here.

records.jp: 「友貴に食料はいらないと言ってしまった」
records.en: Sakuraba: "I seem to have told Tomoki that I would not need food."
comments: Therefore, he knows Tomoki would be bringing food to Taichi, at least, including tomatoes; so the ones in CCC0035A et al should be from him. -GHS
records.assessment: 言ってしまった says he regrettably or inadvertently ended up telling Tomoki he needed no food. 'Seem to have' instead makes him uncertain whether he said it.

highlights.text: I seem to have told Tomoki

records.jp: 「そういうわけで、今日から厄介になる」
records.en: Sakuraba: "And with that being like that, I shall be in your care from now."
records.assessment: そういうわけで means 'for that reason' or 'so.' The English expands it into a nonidiomatic nested demonstrative phrase.

highlights.text: with that being like that

records.jp: 「ホワイ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "Naze?!"
comments: TL Note: WHYYYYYY -GHS
records.assessment: The source writes the English word 'why' in katakana. The translation perversely replaces it with the romanized Japanese word 'naze' instead of rendering the intended English exclamation.

highlights.text: Naze?!

records.jp: 「以上の理由をもちまして、本日より桜庭浩は黒須太一の家に住まうことになった」
records.en: Sakuraba: "And because of all the aforementioned reasons, it came to be that from that day Sakuraba Hiroshi was to live together with Kurosu Taichi."
comments: Narration??? -GHS
records.assessment: Sakuraba grandly declares that as of today he will live at Taichi's house. The English changes the spoken present decision into retrospective narration about 'that day.'

highlights.text: it came to be that from that day Sakuraba Hiroshi was to live

records.jp: 「誰が言葉の意味がわからんと言ったか！　スペペッ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Who said that words don't have understandable meaning! NerNeeer!"
comments: See CCB2009, same source (uncertain). Well, we're still post-Babel. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks who said he failed to understand the meaning of Sakuraba's words. The English instead asserts that words in general lack understandable meaning.

highlights.text: Who said that words don't have understandable meaning!

records.jp: 「部屋を貸してくれ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Please rent me a room."
records.assessment: 部屋を貸してくれ asks Taichi to let him use or stay in a room. 'Rent me a room' implies a rental transaction and is not the natural ditransitive construction.

highlights.text: rent me a room

records.jp: 「いいだろう」
records.en: Taichi: "Ain't it nice."
records.assessment: いいだろう means 'Fine' or 'All right' as Taichi agrees. The English changes acceptance into a question asking whether something is nice.

highlights.text: Ain't it nice.

records.jp: おぼっちゃまである桜庭に道理を説いても仕方がない。
records.en: Preaching the truth of reason to Sakuraba the Obocchama is pointless.
comments: See CCC0003B. Nope, still serious. As for Obocchama, well, if you can't tell from context what that means you're way beyond screwed. -GHS
records.assessment: The class-marked term for a sheltered rich young master is left as unexplained romanized Japanese.

highlights.text: Obocchama

records.jp: 「庶民の家なんてこんなもんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's a commonfolk's residence so that's how it is."
records.assessment: 'Common folk' is a plural collective expression and does not take the singular possessive form 'a commonfolk's.'

highlights.text: a commonfolk's residence

records.jp: 「感覚的には倍以上なんだが……存外、オレの部屋も狭いらしい」
records.en: Sakuraba: "On first look it look like it should be at least twice, but... seems my room is unexpectedly small."
comments: Here it is, one of the most important reading keys in the VN, and it's again assigned to Sakuraba. His room is 16 tatami, which he certainly knew beforehand; but Taichi told him that a 1.5 tatami room is actually 8, as a troll. By trusting Taichi, and concluding that his 16 tatami room is more like 3-4 tatami, he proves that Taichi cannot be taken literally without the math no longer adding up. Most damning is how specific this is: Taichi's 8 is an open lie and troll, while there's no reason to doubt Sakuraba's 1+6=7. 8 is a lie, and 7 is the truth. -GHS
records.assessment: The third-person singular subject requires 'it looks like.'

highlights.text: it look like

records.jp: 無意識に代名詞を切り替えて問う。
records.en: An inquiry with an unconsciously inserted slur.
comments: Made fit by modification. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator notes unconsciously switching his second-person pronoun to the rough 貴様. The English turns that pronoun choice into an inserted slur and omits the actual switch.

highlights.text: An inquiry with an unconsciously inserted slur.

records.jp: ちなみに俺は甲斐性ある睦美さんのおかげで、月二万円をもらっている。
records.en: Incidentally, with obligations to the resourceful Mutsumi-san, I receive about 20,000 yen monthly.
comments: ~$200. Who knows how much they're paying her for keeping mr. 84% here (plus her second unclear but frankly suspicious job), and that's excluding all the money that the guy likely had before he wasted it all on bad market calls. -GHS
records.assessment: Thanks to capable, providing Mutsumi, Taichi receives twenty thousand yen monthly. The English invents obligations owed to her and leaves the honorific untranslated.

highlights.text: with obligations to the resourceful Mutsumi-san

records.jp: なかなかの水準だ。
records.en: The waterline of my living standard's not bad at all.
comments: Can't leave out a literal reference, see CCC3012A. Sorta mixed metaphor, but fits the tone of the scene anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: 水準 means level or standard. The English literalizes the word's characters as a physical waterline.

highlights.text: The waterline of my living standard

records.jp: 「リ、リアリー？」
records.en: Taichi: "RI-, RIARII?" (re-, really?)
records.assessment: The source writes the English 'really?' phonetically in katakana. The translation leaves a Japanese-accent transliteration and inserts an editorial parenthetical gloss instead of rendering the intended English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "RI-, RIARII?" (re-, really?)

records.jp: 「イエス」
records.en: Sakuraba: "IESU." (yes)
comments: Yes, "イエス" can be read Jesus. -GHS
records.assessment: The source writes the English 'yes' phonetically in katakana. The translation leaves a romanized Japanese pronunciation and inserts an editorial gloss instead of the intended English answer.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "IESU." (yes)

records.jp: 「どこの芸能人の息子だ貴様は！」
records.en: Taichi: "What entertainer are you the son of, you bastard!
comments: See CCB2002. HOLY SHIT SAKURABA IS THE BELLY BUG -GHS
records.assessment: The spoken line opens with a quotation mark but has no closing quotation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "What entertainer are you the son of, you bastard!

records.jp: 「第一、オレは芸能人じゃない」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Number one, I am not an entertainer."
comments: Not an entertainer's SON. Then again, that's true: he's not comic relief, he's Mr. Exposition. -GHS
records.assessment: 第一 is the discourse marker 'first of all,' not a numbered ranking label.

highlights.text: Number one

records.jp: 「オレはオレだ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "As far as I go, I am I."
comments: Just for sillies -GHS
records.assessment: オレはオレだ means 'I am who I am.' The English adds a scope phrase and leaves the complement in an unidiomatic nominative form.

highlights.text: As far as I go, I am I.

records.jp: 常軌を逸している。
records.en: That's derailing from the proper course.
comments: See CCB0005. Interesting. -GHS
records.assessment: 常軌を逸している is an idiom meaning abnormal, outrageous, or beyond all reason. The English literalizes it as a vehicle leaving a route.

highlights.text: derailing from the proper course

records.jp: チャリチャリ音がする。
records.en: There's a jingle-jingle of a sound.
comments: There's a bicycle-bicycle sound... see CCA0002. ~yes~ -GHS
records.assessment: The construction redundantly nominalizes the onomatopoeia; the coins simply jingle.

highlights.text: a jingle-jingle of a sound

records.jp: 「はは、おぼっちゃまも貧乏な時があるようだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Hahah, looks like Obocchama has moments of poverty too, then."
records.assessment: The class-marked term for a sheltered rich young master is left as unexplained romanized Japanese.

highlights.text: Obocchama

records.jp: ガッ、と腕を交差させた。
records.en: thump, arms are crossed,
comments: Not with each other, it seems. -GHS
records.assessment: The two men cross or clasp their arms in a forceful gesture. The passive construction omits both participants and leaves the action detached from them.

highlights.text: arms are crossed

records.jp: 「そういや、おまえには小銭を何度か貸したよな」
records.en: Taichi: "Say hey, haven't I lent you coin so many times now."
records.assessment: He lent Sakuraba small change several times. 'Coin' needs plural or a determiner, and 'so many' exaggerates 何度か.

highlights.text: lent you coin so many times

records.jp: 「律儀なやつめ。けどまあ記念に返されておくか」
records.en: Taichi: "Damn the man of integrity you are. But well, let's say it's returned in memoriam."
records.assessment: Taichi decides to accept the repayment as a memento or keepsake. 'In memoriam' commemorates someone who has died and introduces death absent from the joke.

highlights.text: returned in memoriam

records.jp: せせらぎの如く笑いあう。
records.en: We snicker together as if babbling brooklets.
records.assessment: They laugh together like the sound of a stream. 'Snicker' implies suppressed or mocking laughter, and the comparison lacks an article before 'babbling brooklets.'

highlights.text: snicker together as if babbling brooklets

records.jp: 十万円金貨が十五枚入っていた。
records.en: Inside there were fifteen gold coins, ten thousand yen each.
records.assessment: The Japanese specifies fifteen gold coins worth 100,000 yen each. The English renders them as 10,000 yen each, reducing the denomination by a factor of ten.

highlights.text: ten thousand yen each

records.jp: よく見たら十万円金貨だけではなかった。
records.en: Looking closely, they weren't only ten thousand yen gold coins.
records.assessment: 十万円金貨 means one-hundred-thousand-yen gold coins. The English again lowers the denomination by a factor of ten.

highlights.text: ten thousand yen gold coins

records.jp: まさか桜庭の中では……十万円は大金ではない……ではない……ではない……？（エコー）
records.en: Could it be that, when it comes to money, inside Sakuraba's head... 100,000 yen are not much... not much.. not much...? (echo)
comments: See CCZDXC -GHS
records.assessment: A monetary amount is treated as singular in English: '100,000 yen is not much.'

highlights.text: 100,000 yen are not much

records.jp: 「はっ？」
records.en: Taichi: "But?"
records.assessment: The Japanese is a startled 'Huh?' The English supplies an adversative conjunction and implies a contrast that is not present.

highlights.text: But?

records.jp: 人類滅亡前、まだ金が意味のある時代に一度でもせびっていたら。
records.en: If, before the Fall of Mankind, in the times when money still had significance, I had only just once extorted him some money...
comments: Going with that specific meaning for obvious reasons -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator regrets not wheedling or begging some money from him earlier. 'Extorted' implies coercive criminal extraction and substantially changes the imagined act.

highlights.text: extorted him some money

records.jp: 神はいじわるであらせられる！
records.en: God exists as my personal bully!
records.assessment: The elevated comic line says God is cruel or spiteful. The English turns this into an ontological claim that God exists specifically as Taichi's personal bully.

highlights.text: God exists as my personal bully!

records.jp: 後悔しまくりの俺だった。
records.en: That was the earnest regret spree of mine.
comments: Ostracismfest returns! Ah, wait, it was never there... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he was drowning in or consumed by regret. The English piles nouns into a nonidiomatic possessive phrase and adds 'earnest.'

highlights.text: the earnest regret spree of mine

records.jp: 「もういい……寝てくれ……」
records.en: Taichi: "I had enough... let me sleep..."
comments: See CCB0006 -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi tells Sakuraba to go to sleep. The English instead asks Sakuraba to allow Taichi to sleep.

highlights.text: let me sleep

records.jp: まあヤツのことだ。
records.en: Well, that guy's himself.
records.assessment: まあヤツのことだ means 'knowing him' or 'given what he is like.' The English possessive-reflexive predicate does not express that reasoning.

highlights.text: Well, that guy's himself.

records.jp: 放浪癖があるからな。
records.en: He's got vagabondism after all.
records.assessment: 放浪癖 is a habit or tendency to wander. 'Vagabondism' is a marked ideological or social label rather than a natural description of that habit.

highlights.text: vagabondism

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃん？」
records.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan?"
comments: Odd that Youko doesn't go kill Kiri when Taichi decides not to follow her, isn't it. -GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: こっちの家には入らないよう言ってあったのに。
records.en: And in my house, when she was told not to come in.
records.assessment: The narrator notes that he had told her not to enter this house, yet she is here. The English starts two subordinate phrases, omits him as the person who told her, and has no main clause.

highlights.text: And in my house, when she was told not to come in.

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんは……まるで……あの時の彼女みたいだ……。
records.en: Youko-chan is... just like... like she was at that time...
comments: A rapist and a cowardly manipulator then. Hum, what character are those words usually (and erroneously) associated with out there...? -GHS
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 抱きついてきた。
records.en: I was being embraced.
records.assessment: She suddenly clings to or embraces him. The passive progressive turns the bounded action into an ongoing state and suppresses her as agent.

highlights.text: I was being embraced.

records.jp: だが彼女はすぐに身を離す。
records.en: She, however, quickly distances her body.
records.assessment: She immediately pulls away. English does not naturally describe this as transitively 'distancing her body.'

highlights.text: distances her body

records.jp: 「……口元に、トマトのかけら」
records.en: Youko: "...on the lips, piece of tomato."
comments: See CCC0000. Admittedly, this might be the only real line in the whole thing, but... remember CCC0035A, still odd he has no problem with the red of tomatoes and this might be important. -GHS
records.assessment: The line needs articles and a finite relation: there is a piece of tomato on his lips.

highlights.text: on the lips, piece of tomato

records.jp: 彼女の頭部が、俺に合わさってきた。
records.en: Her head became one with me.
comments: Just sound weird. -GHS
records.assessment: She brings her face or head toward his. The English instead claims their bodies merge into one entity.

highlights.text: Her head became one with me.

records.jp: 唇の端を、舌がかすめた。
records.en: Her tongue latches on the edge of the lips.
records.assessment: Her tongue briefly grazes or brushes the corner of his lips. 'Latches on' describes gripping and remaining attached, changing the action's duration and force.

highlights.text: latches on

records.jp: 到達する前に、両肩を抱いて引きはがす。
records.en: Before she reaches, I grab and push her off from the shoulders.
records.assessment: The source specifies before she reaches his lips. The English omits the destination and leaves 'reaches' without an object.

highlights.text: Before she reaches

records.jp: こんな不安定になって。
records.en: for things to become so unstable.
comments: See CCA0003. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator finds it rare for Youko herself to become this emotionally unstable. The English assigns instability to generic 'things.'

highlights.text: for things to become so unstable

records.jp: 「睦美さんとの約束だったはずだ」
records.en: Taichi: "As follows from the promise we made with Mutsumi-san."
records.assessment: It was a promise they made to Mutsumi. The English uses an unsupported logical formula, says the promise was 'with' her, and leaves the honorific untranslated.

highlights.text: As follows from the promise we made with Mutsumi-san.

records.jp: 「キミにも、守ってもらう」
records.en: Taichi: "And I will have you keep them, too."
records.assessment: Taichi will make Youko keep that one promise. The plural pronoun lacks a plural antecedent.

highlights.text: keep them

records.jp: 声をあらげて叫ぶ。
records.en: The voice raises until a shout.
records.assessment: Taichi raises his voice and shouts. The English makes an abstract voice raise itself through a graded process.

highlights.text: The voice raises until a shout.

records.jp: 「キミとは他人である、俺が自分の意志と責任で決める」
records.en: Taichi: "You are someone else. I decide with my own volition what is my responsibility."
comments: Important that it be left literal, since she of course doesn't agree that they're different people. -GHS
records.assessment: Because Youko is a separate person from him, Taichi says he will decide by his own will and bear responsibility for that decision. The English instead makes 'what is my responsibility' the object he decides.

highlights.text: I decide with my own volition what is my responsibility.

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんは出ていく。
records.en: Youko-chan leaves,
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 表情の乏しいマスクはすべらかで、落胆も失意も張りつかない。
records.en: Her mask of scant expressions is smooth, that neither discouragement nor disappointment stick to it.
records.assessment: The relative clause cannot attach after a comma with 'that' in this form; it requires coordination or a nonrestrictive 'so ... that' construction.

highlights.text: is smooth, that neither

records.jp: 俺は追いつめられたままの姿勢で、冷蔵庫に背を当てたまま、ずるずると床にうずくまった。
records.en: Still in the posture into which I was chased, my back slid onto the front of the refrigerator to the floor, until I was nearly sitting.
records.assessment: With his back still pressed to the refrigerator in the cornered posture, he slides down until he crouches on the floor. The English says his back slides onto the refrigerator's front and ends with the weaker, inaccurate 'nearly sitting.'

highlights.text: Still in the posture into which I was chased, my back slid onto the front of the refrigerator to the floor, until I was nearly sitting.

records.jp: 世界が揺り戻されるまで、あと三日ほど。
records.en: There remain three days to the swingback of the world.
comments: Including this day. Uh, for those who can't do basic math, which I suspect is most of you. -GHS
records.assessment: 揺り戻される describes the world being reset, rolled back, or snapping back. 'Swingback' is not a natural noun for this event.

highlights.text: swingback

records.jp: 舞台は未来。
records.en: Setting is futuristic.
records.assessment: The count noun requires an article or possessive: 'The setting is futuristic' or 'Its setting is the future.'

highlights.text: Setting is futuristic.

records.jp: 主人公は何度死のうが主人公であり、パーティーが全滅してゲームオーバーにならない限り、危機的な破滅は起こらない。
records.en:
The protagonist can die as many times as he wants,
but he's the main character; within the limit of
the party not being entirely eliminated, causing
a game over, no complete failure will occur.
records.assessment: The protagonist remains the protagonist however many times he dies; the source does not grant him a desire or choice to die. The rest of the sentence has a malformed 'within the limit of' condition and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text: The protagonist can die as many times as he wants

records.jp: 主人公のみならず、キャラクターが死ぬと、それは厳然たる死なのである。
records.en:
Not just when the main character dies, but if
any character dies, that death is the final kind.
records.assessment: 厳然たる死 means an uncompromisingly real or irrevocable death. 'The final kind' is vague and does not state what distinguishes it; intrusive engine line breaks remain.

highlights.text: that death is the final kind

records.jp: 直前のセーブデータ時の主人公が、そこではポンと精製される。
records.en:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.
records.assessment: The facility produces the protagonist as he existed at the most recent save data. The English places the restored state immediately before that save, shifting the checkpoint backward.

highlights.text:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.

records.jp: セーブ以降の、死んだ主人公の固有時間は、まったく省みられない。
records.en:
The protagonist's eigentime after the save and
before death was never ever re-examinable.
comments: Let's start throwing in semi-credible mathematical spatial concepts... not that this doesn't fit in the big giant troll this all is, since he's literally pointing a giant spotlight on how people's memories should be erased but aren't. -GHS
records.assessment: The dead protagonist's own elapsed experience after the save is not considered or honored at all. 'Re-examinable' means capable of later inspection and changes disregard into technical impossibility; intrusive line breaks remain.

highlights.text: was never ever re-examinable

records.jp: けど鮮烈な死のイメージがつきまとい、俺は憑かれたように遊び続けた。
records.en:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.
comments: Taichi likes to chase beautiful images, however difficult they are to obtain, even in videogames... except he conveniently forgets to mention how the game came with a complete walkthrough, doesn't he now. -GHS
records.assessment: The vivid image of death haunts or follows him, while he continues playing as if possessed. The English instead makes him voluntarily pursue that image and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.

records.jp: 「……げんなりだ」
records.en: Taichi: "...so dejecting."
records.assessment: げんなり describes being weary, disgusted, or thoroughly put off. 'Dejecting' is an unnatural participial adjective for his state.

highlights.text: so dejecting

records.jp: してみると俺は何人目なのだろうか。
records.en: If that's how it is then, I am which number of myself now?
records.assessment: He wonders which iteration or number he is. The interrogative phrase cannot serve as the predicate after 'I am' in this word order.

highlights.text: I am which number of myself now?

records.jp: でも部活があるしな。
records.en: But I have club don't I.
records.assessment: The club activity requires a determiner or complement, and the tag question requires punctuation.

highlights.text: I have club don't I.

records.jp: 先輩の図面。
records.en: With Senpai's blueprints.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 先輩を信じるのだ。
records.en: Senpai believes it.
records.assessment: The narrator exhorts himself to trust his senior. The English instead makes the senior the person who believes something and leaves the title untranslated.

highlights.text: Senpai believes it.

records.jp: 炎天下での作業が続く。
records.en: Fatigue duty continues under the scorching sun.
records.assessment: This is continued work under the blazing sun. 'Fatigue duty' specifically denotes noncombat manual labor assigned to soldiers, often as routine or punishment, which the source does not establish.

highlights.text: Fatigue duty

records.jp: 俺は日射には滅法強い。
records.en: I am extraordinarily resistant to sunstroke,
records.assessment: 日射 means solar radiation or exposure to sunlight. 'Sunstroke' is a medical condition, not the environmental stimulus to which his white hair supposedly makes him resistant.

highlights.text: resistant to sunstroke

records.jp: そんなわけで真夏日だが、作業は進む。
records.en: Today may be a Manatsubi, with its temperature likely above 30 Celsius, but work continues.
comments: THIS IS EDUTAINMENT BITCHES AND YOU! WILL! LEEEEEARRRRRNNNN!!!asdsafdfdaskldies -GHS
records.assessment: 真夏日 is a hot summer day, technically one reaching thirty degrees Celsius. The English leaves the term romanized and inserts an explanatory aside into the prose instead of rendering it.

highlights.text: a Manatsubi, with its temperature likely above 30 Celsius

records.jp: 「こう暑いと、海にでも行きたくなるけど」
records.en: Taichi: "But with this heat I actually wanted to go to the beach."
records.assessment: He says the current heat makes him want to go to the beach. The past tense moves the desire out of the present conversation.

highlights.text: I actually wanted to go

records.jp: 「楽しかったな。美希には悪いけど」
records.en: Taichi: "That was so fun! Too bad about Miki, though."
records.assessment: Taichi says he feels bad for Miki while recalling that it was fun. 'Too bad about Miki' sounds dismissive and can mean her misfortune is merely unfortunate.

highlights.text: Too bad about Miki

records.jp: 「その……支倉先輩が……」
records.en: Kiri: "It's... Hasekura-senpai, she..."
records.assessment: The surname-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Hasekura-senpai

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃんが……監視してる？」
records.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan... she's monitoring you?"
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 声が震える。
records.en: Voice shakes.
records.assessment: Kiri's voice trembles. The English omits both the possessor and the article required for a count noun.

highlights.text: Voice shakes.

records.jp: 未成熟ながら、美しいガラス細工みたいな女の子だったのに。
records.en: Because she was immature an immature girl, and yet so like a beautiful glass sculpture.
records.assessment: The adjective and noun phrase are accidentally duplicated around a missing conjunction or comma.

highlights.text: she was immature an immature girl

records.jp: こんな……中途半端な有様は、どういうことだ。
records.en: But what to do with something this... half-baked.
comments: "I know! Let's give 'er another half!" -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator asks how Kiri came to be left in this damaged, incomplete state. The English turns her into an object he must decide what to do with and uses 'half-baked,' which means poorly planned.

highlights.text: what to do with something this... half-baked

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんを恨む気持ちがある。
records.en: I feel resentment towards Youko-chan.
records.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: ああ、俺はまた沈んでいるなと思う。
records.en: Ahhh, don't sink down again, you.
records.assessment: The narrator observes that he himself is sinking again emotionally. The English converts that realization into a second-person command not to sink.

highlights.text: don't sink down again, you

records.jp: テンション高めに保っていられる時はいい。
records.en: I prefer times where the tension can be kept high.
records.assessment: テンション here means his energy, spirits, or excited mood. The English false friend 'tension' suggests stress or strain and changes the psychological state.

highlights.text: the tension can be kept high

records.jp: そうでない時、俺の心は沈んでいく。
records.en: In times where it can't, my heart sinks.
records.assessment: When he cannot keep his spirits high, his heart sinks. The English uses the false friend 'tension,' assigns ability to an unexplained 'it,' and uses 'where' for time.

highlights.text: In times where it can't

records.jp: 光のあたたかさを忘れさせ、ただ個体で生きるものにする場所。
records.en: A place that makes you forget all the light, that swallows whole all that desires but to live as an Individual.
comments: Sounds like the Nietzscheian abyss, the one that stares back. -GHS
records.assessment: The abyss makes him forget the warmth of light and reduces a being to living as a mere isolated organism. The English omits warmth, introduces a consuming entity, and changes the organism into 'all that desires' to live.

highlights.text: A place that makes you forget all the light, that swallows whole all that desires but to live as an Individual.

records.jp: 長くいれば、凍った心もやがて退化し、純粋な生きる意志。
records.en: Being there for long eventually makes this frozen heart degenerate into a pure volition to live.
comments: Will to Power. -GHS
records.assessment: After long enough, even the frozen heart atrophies, leaving only a pure will to live. The English says the heart itself transforms into that will, changing subtraction into metamorphosis.

highlights.text: makes this frozen heart degenerate into a pure volition to live

records.jp: 先輩から引き継いだ泣き言を、下級生にそのままぶつけた。
records.en: I thrust, unaltered, the complaints I inherited from a Senpai onto an underclassman.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: a Senpai

records.jp: 霧に脚立の上で作業させることによって、パンチランド建国という幸運も期待している自分がいた。
records.en: Because there also exist the expectation within myself that via making Kiri work on top of the stepladder the blessed event that is the Foundation of Panchiraland will occur.
comments: See CCB0005 -GHS
records.assessment: The clause has singular 'expectation' with plural agreement and wraps the narrator's private hope in an unnatural existential-locative construction.

highlights.text: there also exist the expectation within myself

records.jp: 「パンチラはいい……」
records.en: Taichi: "Panchira's nice..."
records.assessment: パンチラ means a glimpse of underwear and is directly relevant to the coined 'Panchiraland' joke. Leaving it romanized makes the joke inaccessible in English.

highlights.text: Panchira

records.jp: 「パンチラと聞こえたのですけど」
records.en: Kiri: "I heard 'panchira' however."
records.assessment: Kiri explicitly says she heard the word for a glimpse of underwear. The untranslated romanization withholds the content of her accusation.

highlights.text: panchira

records.jp: 「言ってないよそんなこと」
records.en: Taichi: "I haven't said such things."
comments: Intentional -GHS
records.assessment: He denies the just-completed utterance: 'I didn't say that.' Present perfect is unnatural with this specific immediate past event.

highlights.text: I haven't said

records.jp: 「借りは返しきっておきたいですし、手伝います」
records.en: Kiri: "As I want to return what I borrowed in full, I will help."
