comments: Like with the end of Touko's route, this makes zero sense if one hasn't gone to help her. Flat-out plot hole in this case. OTOH... she doesn't believe her debt cleared; of course, she doesn't understand the concept of 'repayment' any more than she understands forgiveness. -GHS
records.assessment: 借り refers to an obligation or favor owed, not a physical borrowed item she can return. She wants to repay her debt fully.

highlights.text: return what I borrowed in full

records.jp: 俺の言動を遮って、強い語調で。
records.en: She intercepts my speech and conduct with strong tone.
records.assessment: Kiri cuts off his words and actions with a forceful tone. 'Intercepts conduct' is not idiomatic, and 'tone' requires an article.

highlights.text: intercepts my speech and conduct with strong tone

records.jp: 「和解するつもりは、まったくありませんから」
records.en: Kiri: "I have absolutely not a shred of intention to reconciliate."
comments: This is where readers should laugh. Deeere dere dere (that's the laugh for when tsunderes go deredere) -GHS
records.assessment: The negation is misplaced after 'have,' and the normal English verb is 'reconcile,' not the rare and distracting 'reconciliate.'

highlights.text: I have absolutely not a shred of intention to reconciliate.

records.jp: 先輩が来た。
records.en: Senpai had come.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「あ、先輩」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, Senpai."
records.assessment: The direct status address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「２２世紀を生きる萌えっ娘であるなら、ゆあーん、とか、ゆよーん、くらいは―――」
records.en: Taichi: "For the Moekko of the 22nd Century ought be doing the Yuahhn, or the Yuyohhn and---"
comments: Fetishist technical term again. See below. -GHS
records.assessment: The subject is introduced by 'for' but followed by a finite modal, leaving the sentence ungrammatical; the coined Japanese label for a cute archetypal girl is left unexplained.

highlights.text: For the Moekko of the 22nd Century ought be doing

records.jp: 「詩人の中原中也じゃないですか。パクりですか」
records.en: Misato: "Is that not just poetry from Nakahara Chuya? Are you plagiarizing?"
comments: CP http://www.nakaharachuya.com/poems.htm English translation. Well, the above two words were. -GHS
records.assessment: The sounds quote a poem by the poet Nakahara Chūya. English needs 'poetry by,' and the Japanese name is not normalized to standard Hepburn.

highlights.text: poetry from Nakahara Chuya

records.jp: 「中原好きなんです」
records.en: Misato: "So you like Nakahara it seems."
comments: i think he prefers nakadashi -ghs
records.assessment: Misato says that she likes Nakahara Chūya. The English assigns that preference to Taichi and does not normalize the name to standard Hepburn.

highlights.text: So you like Nakahara it seems.

records.jp: 「い、いや、温故知新といいますか王政復古といいますか……古きをたずねて新しきをしるみたいなっ」
records.en: Taichi: "N-, nah, it is called learning from the past, or maybe the restoration of Imperial rule... it is an inquiry of the past to truly understand the future, or the like!"
comments: Thus spake Confucius (no, really, it's his). -GHS
records.assessment: 温故知新 means gaining new knowledge or insight by studying the old. 'The future' is not stated and narrows 'new' to a temporal era.

highlights.text: to truly understand the future

records.jp: 「とりあえず……退院おめでとうです」
records.en: Taichi: "Anyway... congratulations on your quick dehospitalization."
records.assessment: 退院 is discharge from the hospital. 'Dehospitalization' is an institutional process term and not an idiomatic congratulation to a patient.

highlights.text: dehospitalization

records.jp: 俺も先輩の美乳をじっと見つめた。
records.en: I, also, fixedly stared at Senpai's beautiful boobs.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai's

records.jp: 不満げな顔。
records.en: She had dissatisfaction on her face.
records.assessment: The natural English construction is that she looked dissatisfied; a face does not idiomatically 'have dissatisfaction on' it.

highlights.text: had dissatisfaction on her face

records.jp: 「健全かつ健康そのものの俺は、前向きに生きていたいんです」
records.en: Taichi: "The perfect picture of health and furthermore wholesomeness that am I naught desires but to live in optimistic proactivity!"
records.assessment: The mock-grandiose sentence still requires a grammatical subject and verb. 'That am I' has inverted agreement, 'naught desires' has no valid subject, and 'live in optimistic proactivity' is not an English collocation.

highlights.text: that am I naught desires but to live in optimistic proactivity

records.jp: 「そしていずれは、酸いも甘いも噛み分けたヤングアダルトへと変態していくのです」
records.en: Taichi: "And then shall I, at last, pervert my awful nature into that of a Young Adult that is experienced in the ways of the world, having tasted its bitter and its sweet!"
comments: This is the "innocent" meaning of the word hentai. -GHS
records.assessment: 変態する means transform or metamorphose, while enabling the following misunderstanding of 'pervert.' The English makes Taichi actively corrupt an already 'awful nature,' adding moral content and losing the intended transformation.

highlights.text: pervert my awful nature into

records.jp: いいなあ先輩は。
records.en: Ain't that nice, Senpai.
records.assessment: The narrator thinks his senior has it good because she can touch her own chest freely. The English addresses her with an untranslated title and asks generically whether something is nice.

highlights.text: Ain't that nice, Senpai.

records.jp: 自分のおっぱい揉み放題だもんなぁ。
records.en: You can go over your own boobs as muuuch as you liiike.
records.assessment: 揉み放題 says she can squeeze or fondle them as much as she likes. 'Go over' means inspect or review and removes the tactile joke.

highlights.text: go over your own boobs

records.jp: 「違います！」
records.en: Taichi: "Not like that!"
records.assessment: Misato protests 'That's not what I mean' after clutching her chest. The English labels Taichi as the speaker, reversing the dialogue role.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Not like that!"

records.jp: アンテナの反対側、霧が息を落とす。
records.en: On the other side of the antenna, Kiri lets a sigh drop to her feet.
comments: Oh, she's on the other side of the antenna here, too. -GHS
records.assessment: 霧が息を落とす means Kiri lets out or lowers a breath. The English turns the sigh into a physical object falling to the floor.

highlights.text: lets a sigh drop to her feet

records.jp: 「あ、そうだ。質問したいこといっぱいなんですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, right. We are chock full of questions we would like to ask!"
records.assessment: Taichi says he personally has a great many questions. The English changes the speaker to an unspecified plural group.

highlights.text: We are chock full of questions we would like to ask!

records.jp: 「終わったら、こっちもお願いします、部長先輩」
records.en: Kiri: "Once that is done, there is thing I would like to ask, President-senpai."
comments: Seems to be antenna related. Seems... -GHS
records.assessment: The count noun requires an article, and the hybrid office-title-plus-Japanese-honorific address is left unexplained rather than represented naturally in English.

highlights.text: there is thing I would like to ask, President-senpai

records.jp: 「え、でも桜庭君が手伝ってくれるとは限らないですし……」
records.en: Misato: "Eh, but Sakuraba-kun is not necessarily going to help out..."
records.assessment: The Japanese personal suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Sakuraba-kun

records.jp: 「手伝えって言えば手伝いますよ、たぶん」
records.en: Taichi: "If he is told to help he will absolutely help! Maybe."
records.assessment: Taichi says Sakuraba will help if asked, probably. The English first adds absolute certainty and then immediately contradicts it with 'maybe.'

highlights.text: he will absolutely help! Maybe.

records.jp: 先輩の本音はわかっている。
records.en: I understood Senpai's real intentions.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai's

records.jp: 部活は、自分一人の逃避だったんだ。
records.en: Club was something for her own flight alone.
records.assessment: The club was a private form of escape or escapism for her. 'Her own flight' suggests physical travel, while 'alone' attaches ambiguously.

highlights.text: something for her own flight alone

records.jp: ずっと、時間がかかるならそれでよかった。
records.en: She was happy from the start that this would take time,
records.assessment: She was content as long as the work would keep taking a very long time. The English says she was happy from the beginning that it would take time, weakening the indefinite duration and changing the condition into a settled forecast.

highlights.text: She was happy from the start that this would take time,

records.jp: 無尽蔵に没頭していられるように。
records.en: that there existed something in inexhaustible supply she could devote herself to.
comments: Odd that he wouldn't use something like "sink" or "immerse" here, given the "aridity" above. -GHS
records.assessment: The source expresses the purpose of keeping her absorbed without end. The English invents a separate inexhaustible supply of something and makes that the object of devotion.

highlights.text: something in inexhaustible supply she could devote herself to

records.jp: 「ねえ先輩、これって、完成してＳＯＳ発信したらそれで終わりなんですかね？」
records.en: Taichi: "Say, Senpai, when we finish here and we send the SOS, is that the end of this?"
comments: See CCA0030, he's doing the same thing. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 逃避とともに終わる。
records.en: The flight ends together with this.
records.assessment: The escape or escapism ends when the work does. 'Flight' misleadingly suggests physical movement or aviation.

highlights.text: The flight ends

records.jp: だからこの人は、一人で作業していたんだ。
records.en: That is why this girl here is doing this work alone.
records.assessment: The narrator concludes that this is why the woman had been working alone. The English calls her a girl and changes the retrospective explanation to present progressive.

highlights.text: this girl here is doing this work alone

records.jp: 「ＦＭ電波だけでなく、ハンディ無線機も使うんですよね？」
records.en: Taichi: "FM radios are not the only one, there are also hand-held transceivers in use, right?"
comments: See CCB0018. http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%88%E3%83%A9%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B7%E3%83%BC%E3%83%90%E3%83%BC_%28%E7%84%A1%E7%B7%9A%E6%A9%9F%29 they seem indeed more widespread than expected in Japan. Should perhaps connect to Wacchi. -GHS
records.assessment: FM radio waves or broadcasting are supplemented by handheld transceivers. The English changes the medium into plural receiver devices and combines plural 'radios' with singular 'one.'

highlights.text: FM radios are not the only one

records.jp: 先輩の顔に、赤みがさしていく。
records.en: A tinge of redness on Senpai's face.
records.assessment: The Japanese status title remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai's

records.jp: 「三人でやれば、一日で終わるかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "If we do it with people three, we'll finish in a day maybe?"
comments: screw it *chug* -GHS
records.assessment: English places the numeral before the noun: 'with three people' or 'if the three of us do it.'

highlights.text: with people three

records.jp: 「うーむ。メカニカルに詳しい美少女がいれば」
records.en: Taichi: "Uh-huh. If only there was a beautiful girl experienced with the mechanical."
records.assessment: メカニカルに詳しい means knowledgeable about mechanical things. 'The mechanical' cannot stand as this abstract object after 'experienced with.'

highlights.text: experienced with the mechanical

records.jp: 「霧ちーん、いるー？」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chiiin, you heeere?"
records.assessment: The elongated diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chiiin

records.jp: 「と言いますか、メンツに加えられようとしているわたし……」
records.en: Miki: "What you are saying is that you want me added to the personnel..."
records.assessment: Miki observes that she is being maneuvered into joining the group. The English changes this to Taichi consciously wanting her added.

highlights.text: you want me added

records.jp: ちらりと相棒に視線をやる。
records.en: She gives a fleeting gaze to her accomplice.
records.assessment: 相棒 means partner or companion. 'Accomplice' specifically implies cooperation in wrongdoing.

highlights.text: accomplice

records.jp: 「霧ちんもいるし」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin's here too."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「霧ちん、じゃあアレはどうするの？」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin, what do we do with 'that' then?"
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: はじっこで震える二人をよそに、美希と霧はにゃーにゃー鳴いている。
records.en: Standing away from the corner in which the two of us shook and trembled, while Miki and Kiri were meowing with nyans and meows.
records.assessment: The two frightened observers tremble in a corner while Miki and Kiri meow at each other. The English begins with a dangling 'standing away,' then adds a 'while' clause without any governing main predicate.

highlights.text: Standing away from the corner in which the two of us shook and trembled, while Miki and Kiri were meowing with nyans and meows.

records.jp: 「なるほど……そんなことがありましたか」
records.en: Miki: "I see... so is that what there was?"
records.assessment: Miki acknowledges and understands what happened. The English turns the statement into an ungrammatical question about what existed.

highlights.text: so is that what there was?

records.jp: 納得していた。
records.en: They understood each other.
records.assessment: 納得していた says Miki appeared convinced or had understood the explanation. The English invents mutual understanding by an unspecified plural pair.

highlights.text: They understood each other.

records.jp: 最近の若者は、マイ言語まで創りあげてしまうのかよ！
records.en: Are the youngsters these days so creative they would construct a Selflanguage!?
comments: * Taichian for one's own personal language. Yeah, hypocrite much? Still, post-Babel. -GHS
records.assessment: マイ言語 jokingly means a private language of their own. 'Selflanguage' is an opaque nonword and needs a space or idiomatic compound.

highlights.text: construct a Selflanguage

records.jp: 「じゃあさ、じゃあさ、建国しても軍隊も持たないみたいなことになっちゃうんだね」
records.en: Miki: "So then, so then, in the end if we do our nation-founding we'd have to do without an army, that's what happened."
comments: They're not having the real conversation now, however... are they? This might just be further hints to ensure the reader understands that the above doesn't need to be understood to be understood and wooo I'm going cross-eyed. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki describes the prospective consequence: it would be like founding a country without an army. The English says this outcome already happened.

highlights.text: that's what happened

records.jp: 「美希ちんもナイフとか持ってたろ？　あれは捨てた方がいいかな」
records.en: Taichi: "You have a knife too, Miki-chin, right? I'd throw that away if I were you."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Miki-chin

records.jp: 「ナイフなんて持ってたんだ？」
records.en: Kiri: "Why do you even have a knife?"
comments: See CCC3010. Liar liar. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri merely asks in surprise whether Miki had a knife. The English adds a demand for the reason and the emphatic judgment 'even.'

highlights.text: Why do you even have a knife?

records.jp: 「……うーん、まあ霧ちんに渡したりしなければいいんでない？」
records.en: Taichi: "...oookay, so, well, if you don't give it over to Kiri you should be OK I guess?"
records.assessment: The diminutive address 霧ちん is reduced to the bare name, removing the marked familiarity.

highlights.text: Kiri

records.jp: 「いやー、しかし霧ちんとせんぱいが和解とは……世も末ですね」
records.en: Miki: "But ooooh, Kiri-chin and Senpai have made up... it's the end of the world it is."
comments: Cough? -GHS
records.assessment: Both Japanese forms of address are carried over rather than represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin and Senpai

records.jp: 「和解したわけでは」
records.en: Kiri: "Well, made up, it's that..."
records.assessment: Kiri starts to deny that they have reconciled. The English is ungrammatical and does not express that negation.

highlights.text: Well, made up, it's that...

records.jp: 「……だそうで」
records.en: Taichi: "...we totally did."
records.assessment: Taichi reports Kiri's unfinished denial with 'so she says.' The English instead makes him affirm that they reconciled, reversing both content and attribution.

highlights.text: we totally did

records.jp: 「先輩、ちとこちらに」
records.en: Miki: "Senpai, this way for a bit."
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 手を引かれ、アンテナから離れていく。
records.en: Pulling my hand, she moves us away from the antenna,
records.assessment: Miki takes Taichi by the hand and leads him away. The dangling participle makes her pull Taichi's hand as though it were her own action object and the vague 'moves us' obscures who leads whom.

highlights.text: Pulling my hand, she moves us

records.jp: 会話が霧たちに届かない位置。
records.en: to a position where we can't be heard by Kiri or Senpai.
records.assessment: 霧たち means Kiri and the others, not an alternative between Kiri and an untranslated senior title.

highlights.text: Kiri or Senpai

records.jp: 「先輩の方は、それでいいんですか？」
records.en: Miki: "Senpai, on your part, are you OK with this?"
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「確かに霧ちんは、先輩のことちょっぴりその……苦手みたいで……」
records.en: Miki: "Of course Kiri-chin sees you just a bit... as not entirely nice, Senpai..."
records.assessment: 苦手 means Kiri is uncomfortable with or has trouble dealing with him, not that she judges him 'not entirely nice'; both Japanese address forms also remain untranslated.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin sees you just a bit... as not entirely nice, Senpai

records.jp: 「嫌ってたよ。はっきり言って」
records.en: Taichi: "She hates me. Just say that plainly."
records.assessment: 嫌ってた is retrospective: she hated or had disliked him. The English changes it to an unqualified present state.

highlights.text: She hates me

records.jp: 苦笑い。
records.en: Bitter smile.
records.assessment: 苦笑い is a wry or awkward smile, not necessarily an expression of bitterness.

highlights.text: Bitter smile

records.jp: 「霧っち、人間不信なんですよ。で、こういう無秩序な状況になったら、先輩みたいな人のそばにいるのは危険だって言うです」
records.en: Miki: "Kiricchi doesn't trust humans, that's why. And with things have gotten this chaotic, she says it's dangerous to stay next to people like you, Senpai."
records.assessment: The clause is missing a conjunction or finite framing, and the two marked Japanese address forms remain untranslated.

highlights.text: with things have gotten this chaotic

records.jp: いやー、良い眼力だ、霧ちん。
records.en: Wooow, nice insight, Kiri-chin.
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「だから……そのぅ……先輩のことをですね」
records.en: Miki: "That's why... well... her and you, Senpai."
records.assessment: Miki hesitantly raises Kiri's view of Taichi. The English is a sentence fragment with an object pronoun, gives no coherent proposition, and retains the Japanese title.

highlights.text: her and you, Senpai

records.jp: 「仮想敵国にしていたと」
records.en: Taichi: "On how she sees me as a hypothetical enemy government."
comments: Sarcastic comment on how that part's obviously important, but also see CCC3007 - solitary islands isn't quite countries, but it's close enough. -GHS
records.assessment: 仮想敵国 is a hypothetical enemy state or nation, not an enemy government.

highlights.text: hypothetical enemy government

records.jp: 「理由は……霧ちんも言ってくれないんですけど、いつ頃からかそうなって」
records.en: Miki: "The reason... Kiri-chin never told me, but, it's been like this for some time."
comments: But how long has Miki been pushing Kiri against him...? After all, in your typical Settei, the Hero of Justice must confront the Evil Villain... -GHS
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「……そんな霧ちんと、うまくやっていけそうですか？」
records.en: Miki: "...can you get along with Kiri-chin when she's like this?"
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「うん、俺が霧ちんとうまくやる約束で、曜子ちゃんから手を引いてもらったんで」
records.en: Taichi: "Yes, I promised to play nice with Kiri-chin, that's why I got Youko-chan to hold back."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「支倉先輩って……先輩を傷つけると？」
records.en: Miki: "Hasekura-senpai... did she hurt you, Senpai?"
comments: The conversation sort of derails here. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese status suffix remains untranslated, and the same sentence repeats its title as bare 'Senpai.'

highlights.text: Hasekura-senpai

records.jp: 「そうだね。俺ヒロイン」
records.en: Taichi: "Isn't that true. And me's heroine."
comments: If she's the hero, he's the heroine. So the villain... -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi jokes that he is the heroine. The English uses an ungrammatical possessive construction and fails to state that equation.

highlights.text: And me's heroine

records.jp: 「……これでいい目見たこと一度もないです」
records.en: Taichi: "...that I've never seen as something lucky not once."
records.assessment: Taichi says his feminine face has never once done him any good. The English is an ungrammatical relative fragment and does not convey that lack of benefit.

highlights.text: that I've never seen as something lucky not once

records.jp: 「怯えられたり押し倒されたり混乱されたり」
records.en: Taichi: "I get frightened and I get pushed down and I get all confused."
comments: Of course he could be talking about Youko, see CCC0000, but... -GHS
records.assessment: Other people are frightened by him or confused, while he is knocked down. The English assigns all three reactions to Taichi himself.

highlights.text: I get frightened and I get pushed down and I get all confused

records.jp: 「糧だから」
records.en: Taichi: "Because it's provisions."
records.assessment: 糧 is sustenance or nourishment in the figurative comparison. 'Provisions' suggests a stock of supplies rather than something psychologically necessary.

highlights.text: provisions

records.jp: 「食い物が嫌いだけど食わないと死ぬって状況」
records.en: Taichi: "You might hate the food but if you don't eat, thing is, you'll be dying."
comments: See Touko. -GHS
records.assessment: The construction is ungrammatical, and the general consequence 'you die' is changed into a future progressive event.

highlights.text: if you don't eat, thing is, you'll be dying

records.jp: 「心の中でいろいろありまして、食う方に流れたわけだ」
records.en: Taichi: "There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat."
comments: See CCA0018B. What's for eating... -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that various things happened in his heart and he consequently came down on the side of eating. The English makes plural things flow somewhere according to methods of eating.

highlights.text: There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat

records.jp: 「人が俺に対してよからぬことを考えるのは、顔のせいだと思った。わけもわからず気になったのは、目だな」
records.en: Taichi: "I thought that it was the face to blame for why people don't think good of me. And I don't understand why, but my eyes keep bothering me."
comments: See CCA0021. These are indeed Mystic Eyes. Also CCD2002 - witches! And Miki's a witch... -GHS
records.assessment: The first clause is ungrammatical, while the second should say that what inexplicably bothered him was other people's eyes or gaze; the English instead suggests his own eyes are physically troubling him.

highlights.text: people don't think good of me. And I don't understand why, but my eyes keep bothering me

records.jp: 「目が他人と違う気がして……いや、顔の造作も普通じゃないような気がして……」
records.en: Taichi: "It feels like my eyes are different from that of others... no, it also feels like my facial features aren't normal..."
comments: What were they talking about again...? Sometimes Tanaka just seems to get lost. -GHS
records.assessment: The plural 'eyes' cannot be compared with the singular pronoun 'that'; the number must agree.

highlights.text: my eyes are different from that of others

records.jp: 「小ぎれいですよ。いわゆるハンサムではないですが」
records.en: Miki: "They're trim and pretty. Not what you would call 'handsome' however."
records.assessment: Miki describes Taichi's face as neat or pretty. The plural pronoun instead points back to his eyes.

highlights.text: They're trim and pretty

records.jp: 「ははあ、ソレが先輩の心の傷ってやつですか」
records.en: Miki: "Hah-ah... is that the wound on your heart, Senpai?"
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「んー、こんなのはオマケのオマケみたいなもので、本当は……」
records.en: Taichi: "Mmmmh, this is sort of the cherry on top of the cherry on top, in truth..."
comments: Yes, it totally is. -GHS
records.assessment: オマケのオマケ calls this a mere extra on top of an extra, minimizing its importance. 'Cherry on top' normally presents a positive culminating bonus and reverses that force.

highlights.text: the cherry on top of the cherry on top

records.jp: こらこら、と自分を諫める。
records.en: Come on!, come on!, I remonstrate myself.
comments: No talking about the truth. -GHS
records.assessment: The verb requires 'with' before its object in this sense, and the source is simply self-admonition.

highlights.text: I remonstrate myself

records.jp: 「とにかく取り引きなんで、曜子ちゃんに手を引いてもらうために霧は無力でいなければならないわけです」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, on to proper business. For purposes of getting Youko-chan to withdraw, it is absolutely imperative that Kiri remain free of offensive power."
comments: Suddenly formal. -GHS
records.assessment: とにかく取り引きなんで means that this is, in any case, a deal or bargain. The English instead announces a transition to business and retains a Japanese diminutive address later in the sentence.

highlights.text: Well, on to proper business

records.jp: 「ということで霧ちん借ります」
records.en: Taichi: "And therefore, I shall be borrowing Kiri-chin."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
records.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
comments: CP CCCA0028
records.assessment: The generic noun requires an article and should not be capitalized as an unexplained proper name.

highlights.text: coming to Club

records.jp: 冬子がいたら、そう言ってやろうと思っていたのだ。
records.en: If Youko had been among us, that's what I thought I would be telling her.
records.assessment: The Japanese says what he intended to tell Touko. The English substitutes Youko, changing the referenced person in the reflection.

highlights.text: If Youko had been among us

records.jp: 強襲、郵便局。
records.en: I go postal.
comments: I assert that this is a literal translation. -GHS
records.assessment: 強襲、郵便局 jokingly frames the post office visit as a raid or assault. The English imports an unrelated idiom for workplace violence.

highlights.text: I go postal

records.jp: 帰りは、これみよがしに交番の前を通ってくる。
records.en: On the way back, I ostentatiously pass back and forth in front of the kouban.
comments: Bored policeman 1: "Oh, it's one of those weirdos." -GHS
records.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

highlights.text: kouban

records.jp: ついでに交番も強襲しておく。
records.en: While I'm there, I also assault the kouban.
comments: Bored policeman 2: "If he's not doing anything, just leave him do his thing, less trouble." (Console version censors this, but saying "I'll intrude on the kouban" is even more explicit!) -GHS
records.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

highlights.text: kouban

records.jp: 「ほー、これが交番の内部かー」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, so thiiis is what the inside of a Kouban looks like."
comments: Bored policeman 1: "Yes indeed, yes indeed. Yeah, he's harmless." -GHS
records.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked and unnecessarily capitalized Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

highlights.text: Kouban

records.jp: 「いけね」
records.en: Taichi: "Cut it out now."
comments: Bored policeman 2: "Good evening to you too, I guess." Bored policeman 1: "...all kinds around here, all kinds..." -GHS
records.assessment: いけね is Taichi's realization, 'Oops' or 'Oh, right.' The English turns it into a command directed at someone else.

highlights.text: Cut it out now

records.jp: 「さてと……」
records.en: Taichi: "And then now..."
records.assessment: さてと is a transition such as 'Well, then.' The English phrase is not idiomatic.

highlights.text: And then now

records.jp: 方々に。
records.en: This way, and that way.
records.assessment: 方々に means he writes to various people or destinations. The English substitutes vague directions and loses the postcard recipients.

highlights.text: This way, and that way

records.jp: 慌ただしい夜である。
records.en: A busy night we will have here.
comments: He just dumps 'em in the post, doesn't he. And it's like 5PM anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator states that it is a hectic night. The English changes this to an awkward future forecast.

highlights.text: A busy night we will have here

records.jp: 楽しい部活ごっこ。
records.en: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The improvised compound has mismatched articles and number and is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: pretend-a-club-activities

records.jp: 大切な思い出となりえる。
records.en: They may become precious memories.
comments: CP CCA0029
records.assessment: The singular activity or experience could become a precious memory. The English invents a plural antecedent and plural memories.

highlights.text: They may become precious memories

records.jp: そんな可能性があったことを、日記に残しておこうと思った。
records.en: I thought I would leave behind, in the diary, that a possibility like this exists.
records.assessment: The diary is to record that such a possibility had existed. The English changes the retrospective possibility into an ongoing present fact.

highlights.text: a possibility like this exists

records.jp: 「いきなり使われるわたし……」
records.en: Miki: "Just exploited out of the blue I am..."
records.assessment: The inverted subject and verb order is not grammatical English and does not reproduce an established marked speech pattern here.

highlights.text: Just exploited out of the blue I am

records.jp: 「肩揉んでください」
records.en: Taichi: "Backrub, please."
records.assessment: 肩揉んで asks for a shoulder massage. A backrub changes the body part.

highlights.text: Backrub

records.jp: 「そんなこと強要したらだめですー」
records.en: Misato: "Coercing that kind of things is not acceptable!"
records.assessment: The demonstrative and noun disagree in number; this must be 'that kind of thing' or 'those kinds of things.'

highlights.text: that kind of things

records.jp: 軽く見えてヘビィな一撃だった。
records.en: It looks light but that fist was heavy.
comments: It's likely one of the many less-than-common transliterating, but like it happens several times, "heavy" is written with ヘビ(snake)+ィ instead of more common ways. Let's leave it at a "hmmm". -GHS
records.assessment: The narration retrospectively says that the blow only looked light but was heavy. The English shifts the first half into present tense and invents a fist as the subject.

highlights.text: It looks light but that fist was heavy

records.jp: 「……ズボンおろしの刑に処します」
records.en: Miki: "...sentenced to the removal of trousers."
comments: ZUBOOOOOOON? -GHS
records.assessment: The passive sentence fragment is missing both its subject and the auxiliary 'is.'

highlights.text: sentenced to the removal of trousers

records.jp: 「ちょっと山辺さん、パンツもおりてますよっ」
records.en: Misato: "Wait Yamanobe-san, you are taking off his underwear too!"
records.assessment: The Japanese address suffix remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Yamanobe-san

records.jp: 「言ってることぺけくんっぽいですよ……」
records.en: Misato: "Those are very Peke-kun-ish things you say..."
records.assessment: The Japanese personal suffix is embedded in an improvised English adjective rather than represented naturally.

highlights.text: Peke-kun-ish

records.jp: 「師匠と弟子っすから」
records.en: Misato: "We are teacher and pupil, that is why."
records.assessment: The authoritative source identifies Miki as the speaker. The English labels the line as Misato's, reversing the dialogue role.

highlights.text: Misato: "We are teacher and pupil, that is why."

records.jp: 「霧ちん霧ちん、ほらほら、なんか見えてるよ？」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin Kiri-chin, c'mon c'mon, do you see it?"
records.assessment: The repeated diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「なんかかぶせといてよー！　気になるー！」
records.en: Kiri: "Cover that up with something, reallyyy! It's making me siiick!"
records.assessment: 気になる says it is bothering or distracting her. The English intensifies this into physical disgust or nausea.

highlights.text: It's making me siiick

records.jp: 騒がしくて目を覚ました。
records.en: The loud noises made me awake.
records.assessment: The natural construction is 'woke me up'; 'made me awake' is not idiomatic here.

highlights.text: made me awake

records.jp: 「美希がやったんじゃない、責任取ってしまってきてよ！」
records.en: Kiri: "Didn't you do this, Miki! Take responsibility now!"
records.assessment: Kiri tells Miki to take responsibility and put it away. The English omits the required action and leaves only a generic demand for responsibility.

highlights.text: Take responsibility now

records.jp: 「むりむり、物理的に無理！　処女ですし。ここは年長者の部長先輩が」
records.en: Miki: "Impossible impossible, physically impossible! I am a virgin! This is something for our senior President-senpai!"
records.assessment: The address redundantly combines an English status adjective and office title with an untranslated Japanese suffix.

highlights.text: senior President-senpai

records.jp: 「……先輩も未経験なんですか？」
records.en: Miki: "...Senpai is also inexperienced then?"
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「乙女には、あの物体は手厳しすぎます！」
records.en: Miki: "To us maidens, that bodily part is waaay to hard to handle!"
records.assessment: The intensifier before an adjective is 'too,' not 'to.'

highlights.text: waaay to hard

records.jp: 騒がしいなあ。
records.en: Boisterously noisy aren't they.
comments: Three girls are a crowd. -GHS
records.assessment: The sentence lacks a finite main clause and does not grammatically render the narrator's simple observation that they are noisy.

highlights.text: Boisterously noisy aren't they

records.jp: 風が肌に突き刺さるほどに感じられた。風邪かな。
records.en: A sense as if the wind is piercing directly through to the skin. Did I get a fever?
records.assessment: The first sentence is a verbless fragment, while 風邪 means a cold, not a fever.

highlights.text: A sense as if the wind is piercing directly through to the skin. Did I get a fever?

records.jp: 三人の目線が、一斉にこっちを向いた。
records.en: In unison, the sights of the three turned towards me.
records.assessment: The three people's gazes turn toward him. 'Sights' denotes views or optical devices and cannot idiomatically perform this action.

highlights.text: the sights of the three turned towards me

records.jp: 「どうしました、お嬢さんがた、フッ」
records.en: Taichi: "What has happened, my three Ojou-sama?"
comments: Moved the "fu!" down here -GHS
records.assessment: お嬢さんがた is an address to the young ladies. The English carries over a different Japanese title and adds the explicit numeral three.

highlights.text: my three Ojou-sama

records.jp: 耳をつんざく悲鳴×３。
records.en: Ear-pearcing scream x 3.
records.assessment: 'Piercing' is misspelled.

highlights.text: Ear-pearcing

records.jp: 「どうしたというのです、娘さん？」
records.en: Taichi: "What has happened, nee-san?"
comments: See CCA0016 -GHS
records.assessment: 娘さん is a playful 'miss' or 'young lady,' not the untranslated kinship address nee-san.

highlights.text: nee-san

records.jp: 「こ、こないでくださーい！　近寄らないで、いやー、気持ち悪いーっ！！」
records.en: Misato: "Do-, don't come near pleeease! Don't get any close, noooo, disgustiiing!!!"
records.assessment: The comparative adverb is required: 'Don't get any closer.'

highlights.text: Don't get any close

records.jp: 拒絶されてる。
records.en: I was rejected.
records.assessment: The narration observes the rejection in progress: 'I'm being rejected.' The English shifts it into a completed past event.

highlights.text: I was rejected

records.jp: 俺またまた、拒絶されちゃってる。
records.en: Again and again I was completely rejected.
comments: See CCA0010. Not necessarily a comedy scene for him. -GHS
records.assessment: またまた marks yet another present recurrence, not repeated rejection within a completed past episode.

highlights.text: Again and again I was completely rejected

records.jp: 人にキモがられる運命。
records.en: To be treated as disgust itself is my lot in life.
records.assessment: The narrator says his fate is for people to find him creepy or disgusting. The English instead makes him an abstraction called 'disgust itself.'

highlights.text: To be treated as disgust itself

records.jp: むきになって追いかける。
records.en: The chase turns frantic and desperate.
records.assessment: Taichi gets worked up and chases them. The English makes the chase itself change state and omits his emotional reaction.

highlights.text: The chase turns frantic and desperate

records.jp: 泣きそうだった。
records.en: It was to cry.
records.assessment: The narrator says he felt close to tears. The English is ungrammatical and gives the emotion no experiencer.

highlights.text: It was to cry

records.jp: 「全然そんなこと責めてないですー！　あー、きちゃだめー！　きあーっ！」
records.en: Miki: "That is not the thing at fault at all! AHHH, don't get neaaar! Keyaaaah!"
records.assessment: Miki says they are not criticizing his white hair. The English instead claims that an unspecified thing is not at fault.

highlights.text: That is not the thing at fault at all

records.jp: 「ちょ、やだ、やだやだやだやだっ、やだーーーーーーーーーーっ！」
records.en: Kiri: "Wa, you don't, don'tdon'tdon'tdon't, you dooooOOOOOON'T!"
records.assessment: Kiri repeatedly says that she does not want this. The English changes her first-person refusal into an incoherent second-person statement.

highlights.text: Wa, you don't, don'tdon'tdon'tdon't, you dooooOOOOOON'T

records.jp: 「そんなにいやかー！」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't-ed so muuuch!"
comments: I'm learning so many new verbs. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether she hates it that much. The English uses a nonexistent inflection and expresses no intelligible question.

highlights.text: Don't-ed so muuuch

records.jp: 目標を切り替える。
records.en: I foggedly change target.
comments: KIRIkaeru -GHS
records.assessment: 'Foggedly' is not an established adverb and does not express that Taichi redirects his pursuit to a new target.

highlights.text: foggedly change target

records.jp: 「おらおら、手が届きそうだ霧さんよぉ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Oh yes oh YES, you are within reach Kiri-saaan!"
comments: Hokuto no Taichi now??? -GHS
records.assessment: The elongated Japanese address suffix remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-saaan

records.jp: 「あー、霧ちんが陵辱されるー！」
records.en: Miki: "Ahhh, Kiri-chin is being rape assaulteeed!"
comments: That's a nukige term if I've ever read one, so here's a high class reference to the masterpiece that is http://vndb.org/v1292. (Yes, it's the same term.) -GHS
records.assessment: The phrase combines a noun and verb into an ungrammatical passive, while the diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin is being rape assaulteeed

records.jp: 「でも霧ちんが……霧ちんがー！」
records.en: Miki: "But Kiri-chin will... Kiri-chiiin!"
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「そんなっ、このままじゃ霧ちんの貞操が……」
records.en: Miki: "But if this continues Kiri-chin's chastity will be..."
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin's

records.jp: 「佐倉さんの犠牲を無駄にしないためにも、逃げましょう！」
records.en: Misato: "Let us escape, so that Sakura-san's sacrifice will not have been in vain!"
comments: Although Kiri has no problem, it's Misato the first to want to run. After all, she knows Taichi's not going to do anything, does she. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese personal suffix remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Sakura-san's

records.jp: 「霧ちん……ごめん……きみのこと忘れないっ」
records.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin... sorry... I shall never forget you!"
records.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Kiri-chin

records.jp: 「ちょっと嘘でしょう！？　先輩！　美希ー！　ひとでなしーっ！」
records.en: Kiri: "Wait, are you kidding?! Senpai! Mikiii! You aren't humaaan!"
comments: Her sorta-catchphrase it seems. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: Senpai

records.jp: 「観念するんだな佐倉霧……いや……愛奴隷・佐倉霧！」
records.en: Taichi: "Resigned to your fate, are you, Sakura Kiri... no... Love Slave Sakura Kiri!"
records.assessment: The source is an imperative telling Kiri to resign herself. The English turns it into a malformed question about whether she already has.

highlights.text: Resigned to your fate, are you

records.jp: キレた霧に蹴倒された。
records.en: Kiboshlessly kickdowned by Kiri.
comments: This one's just poetic license through and through. Also, not zubaaan'd... ah, the CG has him with pants so it's inconsistent. NOW he notices! -GHS
records.assessment: The phrase uses a nonexistent adverb and a nonexistent past participle, and it omits that Kiri had snapped before kicking Taichi down.

highlights.text: Kiboshlessly kickdowned by Kiri

records.jp: こんな悲しいことがあるだろうか。
records.en: Is this sorrowful thing the truth then?
records.assessment: The narrator asks whether anything could be sadder than this. The English instead asks whether an unspecified sad thing is true.

highlights.text: Is this sorrowful thing the truth then

records.jp: 人間の価値は外見なのか。
records.en: Is the value of a human in the looks?
records.assessment: English asks whether human worth lies 'in looks' or 'in appearance,' without the definite article.

highlights.text: in the looks

records.jp: 普段は可愛いとか言ってくれたのも……全部嘘なのか。
records.en: I'm always being called 'cute' and 'adorable' and all that... are they all lies, then?
comments: This is also unserious of him; he always has a problem being called 'cute', as that's not manly. -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to their ordinary assurances that he was cute. The English makes the action continuously passive and adds a second quoted adjective.

highlights.text: I'm always being called 'cute' and 'adorable' and all that

records.jp: 白い髪。独特な虹彩を持つ瞳。鼻も少し曲がってるかも。
records.en: White hair. Pupils with a peculiar iris. Nose maybe a little crooked.
records.assessment: The source describes eyes with distinctive irises. The English reverses the anatomical relationship, making multiple pupils possess one iris.

highlights.text: Pupils with a peculiar iris

records.jp: マイケルのように、整形しろとでも。
records.en: Like Michael, there's still plastic surgery, but...
comments: I think the reason this is being drilled in so hard (by this thing's standards) is because of the irony of Taichi being already de-facto albino. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks rhetorically whether he is expected to get plastic surgery like Michael. The English turns that challenge into a statement that surgery remains available and omits the implied demand.

highlights.text: Like Michael, there's still plastic surgery, but

records.jp: 俺は物語の主人公のように皆に愛される存在を目指しているだけなのになぁ。
records.en: But I got no aim except to be a being loved by everyone, like the hero of a tale, nothing else!
comments: ...impossible goals... -GHS
records.assessment: The piled constructions 'got no aim except' and 'be a being loved' are not grammatical natural English for his aspiration to become someone everyone loves.

highlights.text: I got no aim except to be a being loved by everyone

records.jp: 「おおう」
records.en: Taichi: "CoOoOovEeEr... diIiIsguiIiIse..."
comments: 覆う oou. Of course it's "sob". Of course... -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains only a sobbing exclamation. The English invents the words 'cover' and 'disguise' and a prolonged performance not present in the line.

highlights.text: CoOoOovEeEr... diIiIsguiIiIse...

records.jp: 世界はどこまでも残酷だった。
records.en: The world was harshness, anywhere, anytime.
records.assessment: The source says the world was endlessly cruel. The English equates the world with the abstract noun 'harshness' and adds a temporal 'anytime.'

highlights.text: The world was harshness, anywhere, anytime

records.jp: チ○ポ出てた。
records.en: My p0n00 was out.
comments: Wall of text justifying why references to Fate/Stay Night doujins are every bit as perfectly appropriate as ones to Kagetsu Tohya doujins. -GHS
records.assessment: The source uses a conventionally censored vulgar noun. The opaque alphanumeric invention neither supplies an English obscenity nor reproduces a recognizable English censorship convention.

highlights.text: p0n00

records.jp: しかも精神的に虐げられたせいで、ギンギンになっているではないか。マゾだから。
records.en: And furthermore, didn't it grow all twangy in ecstasy because I was being emotionally oppressed! Of course, I'm a masochist.
comments: And finally, the real monster is out. The scene above is actually the real reason why Taichi gets rejected: too much blatant sex drive. There's no other monster. -GHS
records.assessment: ギンギン describes being fully erect. 'Twangy' is the wrong physical quality, while 'in ecstasy' adds an emotional state not stated.

highlights.text: twangy in ecstasy

records.jp: ズボンとパンツは。
records.en: Trousers and undies where...
records.assessment: The sentence fragment is missing its predicate, and 'where' is a spelling error for 'were.'

highlights.text: Trousers and undies where...

records.jp: 倒れていた箇所。
records.en: That's the spot I was collapsed in.
records.assessment: A person lies or had fallen 'at' a spot; 'was collapsed in' is not an idiomatic locative construction here.

highlights.text: the spot I was collapsed in

records.jp: 身につける。
records.en: I wear them back.
records.assessment: English says that he puts the clothes back on; 'wear' cannot take 'back' to express the act of dressing.

highlights.text: I wear them back

records.jp: 「にしても、どうして下半身脱いでたのかな……俺」
records.en: Taichi: "Even then, why did you go and strip off the lower half of the body... me."
comments: He does that on the TOP half multiple times, such as CCA0002. He certainly believes he does that unconsciously, see CCB2010, CCA0017A. One of the rare times when readers are explicitly shown how wrong he can get with his self-diagnosis. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks himself why he had been naked from the waist down. The English addresses a second person, treats the body as a detachable object, then appends 'me' without grammatical function.

highlights.text: why did you go and strip off the lower half of the body... me

records.jp: 二人は機材を抱えていた。
records.en: The two were bringing in equipment.
records.assessment: The two are holding or carrying the equipment when seen. The English imposes a progressive past delivery action.

highlights.text: were bringing in equipment

records.jp: 「とりあえずこれどうする？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Anyway, how's this for now?"
records.assessment: Tomoki asks what they should do with the equipment. The English instead solicits an evaluation of how something is at present.

highlights.text: how's this for now

records.jp: 「使われる……いいように使われる……」
records.en: Tomoki: "I'm being exploited... just exploited as convenient..."
comments: See Miki above... -GHS
records.assessment: The passive phrase requires an adverbial construction such as 'used however it suits him'; 'as convenient' has no grammatical complement.

highlights.text: just exploited as convenient

records.jp: 「合宿で使ったやつがあったかな？」
records.en: Tomoki: "The ones we used for training camp, don't we got those?"
comments: So they don't rob them from the cars? How did Misato forget? Maybe it's just a minor plot hole, but given how the bread in the cafeteria goes from "discarded by Sakuraba" to "never brought in in the first place"... -GHS
records.assessment: The auxiliary requires the base verb 'have,' while the source tentatively recalls that they may have had the equipment rather than asserting present possession.

highlights.text: don't we got those

records.jp: 「あとテントがいる。機材が熱でやられるし、雨振ったらあれだし」
records.en: Taichi: "Next we need a tent. The heat'll damage the equipment, and it'll get washed down if it rains."
records.assessment: The concern is that rain would get at or damage the equipment. 'Washed down' suggests deliberate rinsing or being swept away.

highlights.text: it'll get washed down if it rains

records.jp: 「テントならここに三つあるけどな」
records.en: Sakuraba: "But if tents we need, there are three right here."
records.assessment: The fronted conditional noun phrase is ungrammatical English; the source simply says that, if they need a tent, there are three here.

highlights.text: if tents we need, there are three right here

records.jp: 「なんだってジョン？　どこにだい？」
records.en: Taichi: "What did you say, John? Where they are?"
comments: Unsure of the reference if any... unless he means "a" john? Maybe it's still John Lennon, see CCA0027. -GHS
records.assessment: The direct question requires subject-verb inversion: 'Where are they?'

highlights.text: Where they are?

records.jp: わざとらしく問いかける。
records.en: I forced out the question.
records.assessment: わざとらしく means he asks in a deliberately affected or theatrical manner. The English instead says he had difficulty producing the words.

highlights.text: I forced out the question

records.jp: 「ぷぷっ……ふ、普段はたたんでしまってある」
records.en: Tomoki: "Pffft... no-, normally they are always folded."
records.assessment: 'Normally' and 'always' redundantly assert two different frequencies; the source says they are normally kept folded away.

highlights.text: normally they are always folded

records.jp: 芋蔓式に受ける。
records.en: We make 'em one after another.
records.assessment: 芋蔓式に受ける says the linked jokes keep landing or making them laugh in succession. The English says only that they produce unspecified objects one after another.

highlights.text: We make 'em one after another

records.jp: 「で、高さに個人差があったりな」
records.en: Sakuraba: "And, there's an individual difference in height."
records.assessment: The varying heights entail differences among individuals, requiring the plural 'individual differences.'

highlights.text: an individual difference

records.jp: 互いの肩を叩きながら、腹を抱えた。
records.en: We slap our shoulder reciprocally as we hold our sides in laughter.
records.assessment: They slap one another's shoulders. The English gives the group a single shared shoulder and uses an adverb that does not repair the missing reciprocal object.

highlights.text: We slap our shoulder reciprocally

records.jp: 「バイオ技術を応用したテントだな」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Our tents are applied biotechnology."
records.assessment: The joke calls it a tent that applies biotechnology. The English instead equates the tents with the abstract technology in an ungrammatical passive construction.

highlights.text: Our tents are applied biotechnology

records.jp: 「とりあえず、ちゃんとしたテントだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Anyway, we need a proper tent don't we."
records.assessment: The tag question requires a comma before it.

highlights.text: we need a proper tent don't we

records.jp: 話を元に戻す。
records.en: The conversation returns to its origin.
records.assessment: The conversation returns to the original subject, not to a spatial or causal 'origin.'

highlights.text: returns to its origin

records.jp: 「あー……そういや去年の部費の使用予定にあったよな。あれって買ったのかな？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Ahhh... didn't we have some some club budget reserved just for that last year. Did we even buy it after all?"
comments: Their first response still isn't "let's go to Atomic GS and pilfer some". Interesting. -GHS
records.assessment: The word 'some' is duplicated, and the sentence also needs a question mark before the following question.

highlights.text: some some club budget

records.jp: 「すまん……それ俺のせいで流れたんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Sorry... that was flushed away and I'm to blame."
records.assessment: The purchase plan fell through because of Taichi. The English uses a literal image of something being washed or flushed away.

highlights.text: that was flushed away

records.jp: 「……新川豊の件だな」
records.en: Sakuraba: "...the Shinkawa Yutaka accident."
records.assessment: 件 identifies the Shinkawa Yutaka matter or incident without specifying an accident. The English adds that unsupported causal category.

highlights.text: the Shinkawa Yutaka accident

records.jp: 「おまえは一人でやり遂げる男だと、俺は信じている」
records.en: Sakuraba: "You are a man that can get things done on his own, I believe that."
comments: Probably some of the most touching words of encouragement Taichi will ever get in his life. No, he's not talking about the antenna. The penis jokes were before. -GHS
records.assessment: Standard English uses 'who' for a person in this relative clause.

highlights.text: a man that can get things done

records.jp: 「一人でやらせる気なのかよ！」
records.en: Taichi: "You're just trying to get me to do this stuff on my own don't you!"
records.assessment: The tag question requires a comma before 'don't you.'

highlights.text: You're just trying to get me to do this stuff on my own don't you

records.jp: 「というかなんのためにハガキを出したんだよ俺は！」
records.en: Taichi: "Do I even need to say why I sent those postcards dammit!"
records.assessment: Taichi protests, 'Then what did I send the postcards for?' The English instead says that the reason is obvious and need not be stated, reversing the rhetorical complaint.

highlights.text: Do I even need to say why I sent those postcards

records.jp: 「僕はテントか……一人で持てるのか？」
records.en: Tomoki: "I'll get a tent then... but do I got to bring it alone?"
comments: Source unsaid, but assumed Atomic. No mention of whether they'll pay for it, of course. -GHS
records.assessment: The auxiliary requires the base form: 'do I have to bring it.'

highlights.text: do I got to bring it

records.jp: そもそも勝手に放送局作ってしまうことがすでに犯罪である。
records.en: In the first place, just up and making a broadcast channel would already be a crime.
comments: Though if Student Council President Mizum-- Club President Misato could get approval for 84% Taichi to join, the odds she doesn't have a license for this already are close to zero. It's to stare in disbelief at how easily everything fits. -GHS
records.assessment: 放送局 is a broadcasting station. A broadcast channel is a frequency or service rather than the illicit physical operation they are establishing.

highlights.text: making a broadcast channel

records.jp: 「マニュアル車って方が簡単だぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "Manual transmission cars are simple yannow."
comments: See CCA0011C, CCA0018B. And this is why Taichi can't drive. Though it doesn't matter, since he can ride a bike, even if he doesn't make much of a big deal about it. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi specifically claims that manual-transmission cars are easier. The English drops the comparison, which is essential to the misleading advice.

highlights.text: Manual transmission cars are simple

records.jp: 「職員用の駐車場ですぐ見つかると思う。ペダル二つの方はダメだぞ。あれは素人が動かすとかなり危険だからな」
records.en: Taichi: "I think you'll find some quick if you look in the faculty members parking lot. Just don't get the ones with two pedals, 'K. Those are fairly dangerous for an amateur to operate, so you know."
comments: It only looks like he's trolling him, because he truly believes this. And so... does he truly believe his lavatory is 8 tatami mats? Because he seems to truly believe there's 8 people around here. -GHS
records.assessment: 'Quick' cannot modify 'find' in this position, and the plural possessive 'members' requires an apostrophe; the natural sense is that he should quickly find one in the faculty parking lot.

highlights.text: you'll find some quick if you look in the faculty members parking lot

records.jp: 「友貴、桜庭も連れて行けよ。でテントとバッテリー両方な」
records.en: Taichi: "Tomoki, take Sakuraba with you. You both get tent and batteries."
records.assessment: The singular count noun requires an article: 'get a tent and batteries.'

highlights.text: get tent and batteries

records.jp: 桜庭はスタンドアローンで使うと泣きをみるしょっぱい男だった。
records.en: Sakuraba was the kind of overspicy guy who will just make a mess of things when used stand-alone.
comments: "He fails at everything" + "that's why he loves curry bread without loving curry*" + "he's too hard to use". *=curry is Christianity, so being too obvious about it won't work. -GHS
records.assessment: しょっぱい figuratively calls him a feeble or lousy man when operated alone. 'Overspicy' is an opaque literal invention, and the present description is needlessly shifted into future 'will.'

highlights.text: the kind of overspicy guy who will just make a mess of things when used stand-alone

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんの弁当があるわけだが……例によって二人分だな。
records.en: Youko-chan's bento's there but... it's for two, as her usual.
records.assessment: The Japanese suffix and food term remain untranslated, while 'as her usual' is ungrammatical; the sense is that, as usual, the lunch contains two portions.

highlights.text: Youko-chan's bento's there but... it's for two, as her usual

records.jp: 誰かと食うか。
records.en: Who should I eat this with.
records.assessment: The source tentatively considers eating with someone, not choosing a particular 'who,' and the direct question requires a question mark.

highlights.text: Who should I eat this with.

records.jp: 二年教室……不在。
records.en: Second year room... uninhabited.
records.assessment: 不在 says the person is absent. 'Uninhabited' implies that the room is not occupied or lived in at all.

highlights.text: uninhabited

records.jp: ……お嬢様だから自分でポストとか確認しないのかもしれない。
records.en: ...being an ojou-sama then she wouldn't check the post on her own perhaps.
comments: But she'll check a frickin' arrow letter, see CCB0022. Admittedly, that one might have been fired right into her bedroom as she was sleeping. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese social title remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

highlights.text: ojou-sama

records.jp: あとで様子、見に行ってみるか。
records.en: I should just go see how's things later on.
records.assessment: The embedded clause requires declarative order and number: 'go see how things are.'

highlights.text: go see how's things

records.jp: 次は、と。
records.en: Next then.
records.assessment: 次は、と is a clipped transition to the next place or item. 'Next then' is an unidiomatic fragment that does not express that transition naturally.

highlights.text: Next then.

records.jp: こういうのを同一性があると言うな。
records.en: It can be said that there is identity, can't it.
comments: I suspect it should be unclear whether this is rhetorical or not. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese asserts that this is what one calls sameness or identity. The English changes the assertion into an uncertain tag question.

highlights.text: It can be said that there is identity, can't it.

records.jp: どこで食べよう。
records.en: So where to go eating.
comments: Possible choice removed here, see main script flow file -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese is a complete deliberative question about where to eat. 'So where to go eating' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: So where to go eating.

records.jp: 今日は握り飯だった。
records.en: Today we have rice balls.
comments: Secret Sources in Japan(R) say that this specific type is the Rice Ball Onigiri, which are Onigiri made with 100% rice balls. Quite rare! -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says that today's lunch was rice balls. 'Today we have' invents a plural subject and presents the meal rather than identifying what he brought or had.

highlights.text: Today we have rice balls.

records.jp: 「いただきます」
records.en: Taichi: "Thank you for the food."
records.assessment: いただきます is the conventional pre-meal expression. 'Thank you for the food' is a literalized explanation rather than a natural equivalent in this spoken context.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Thank you for the food."

records.jp: 「ああ、そうか。ごめん」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, right, that. Sorry.
comments: Androphobia, germophobia, germanicalphobia? Some of this don't sound germane. -GHS
records.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation mark but never closes it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, right, that. Sorry.

records.jp: 「食べたまえ。二人分ある」
records.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with eating. There's enough for two."
records.assessment: 食べたまえ is a lightly grandiose command to eat. 'Gladden me with eating' invents a request to please the speaker and is not idiomatic English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gladden me with eating. There's enough for two."

records.jp: 「つまむ程度かまわないだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "You think she'd mind as long as it's snacking?"
comments: The foodsnatching king makes another pupil! -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that Miki surely will not mind Kiri having just a bite. The English conditional construction is malformed and does not clearly state whose permission is at issue.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You think she'd mind as long as it's snacking?"

records.jp: 「刃物とか武器になりそうなものには触れるなよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Cutlery and that sort could be seen as weapon so hands off."
records.assessment: Taichi prohibits touching blades or anything else that could serve as a weapon. The English narrows this to cutlery, says it could merely be seen as a weapon, and is missing an article.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cutlery and that sort could be seen as weapon so hands off."

records.jp: 「おかしいですよ、ゼッタイ」
records.en: Kiri: "That is weird, very much so."
comments: Oh, this isn't the start of it. -GHS
records.assessment: ゼッタイ emphatically means 'definitely' or 'absolutely.' 'Very much so' is an unnatural degree phrase attached to 'weird.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "That is weird, very much so."

records.jp: 「根本的なデキが違うんだろう」
records.en: Taichi: "Her fundamental capacity of doing seems just different."
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko is fundamentally made differently or has a different natural caliber. 'Her fundamental capacity of doing' is malformed and does not convey that comparison.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Her fundamental capacity of doing seems just different."

records.jp: 何をやっても瞬時でコツを掴む。
records.en: Whatever she does, she catches the trick in an instant.
records.assessment: コツを掴む means to get the knack or hang of something. 'Catches the trick' is a literal calque.

highlights.text: Whatever she does, she catches the trick in an instant.

records.jp: 「あー、受けてたね。なんか長期休みごとに、どっかの外国とか行って現地の軍事インストラクター雇って」
records.en: Taichi: "Yep, she did indeed. Every lengthy vacation period she goes to some foreign country and hires a local military instructor."
comments: This is a stream of bullshit so long it's amazing anyone *ever* read it with a straight face. He's borderline brainwashing Kiri with his chuuni. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi describes what Youko used to do on each long vacation. The English switches the repeated past activity into the simple present.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yep, she did indeed. Every lengthy vacation period she goes to some foreign country and hires a local military instructor."

records.jp: 「格闘なんてやってたんですか？」
records.en: Kiri: "What kind of martial art do you practice?"
records.assessment: Kiri asks in surprise whether Taichi practiced fighting at all. The English presupposes that he does and asks him to identify a discipline.

highlights.text: What kind of martial art do you practice?

records.jp: 「……あ、ごめん……ついカッとなって……」
records.en: Taichi: "...ah, sorry... I just fired in a rage accidentally..."
records.assessment: カッとなって means that Taichi lost his temper in the heat of the moment. 'Fired in a rage accidentally' describes no intelligible English action.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...ah, sorry... I just fired in a rage accidentally..."

records.jp: 霧は三メートルも逃げて、戦闘態勢を取っていた。
records.en: Kiri escapes to three meters away, and went into combat readiness.
comments: See CCA0008. Youko and Taichi aren't the only ones cross-training. OTOH, see CC0032: Youko manages only two meters. So Kiri and Miki both keep him at 3 meters, and Youko at 2... 8? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese narrates two coordinated past actions: Kiri retreated a full three meters and assumed a fighting stance. The English mixes present and past and uses the unidiomatic 'escapes to three meters away.'

highlights.text: Kiri escapes to three meters away, and went into combat readiness.

records.jp: 空手のパクりと言われると、我を忘れてしまう俺でもあった。
records.en: There is also a me that forgets hisself when he is called a Karate plagiarist.
comments: See CCC3016, but in general, he plagiarizes (and misreads) just about everything so it's just a detail. More importantly, see CCC0026. -GHS
records.assessment: The first-person narrator says that even he loses himself when accused of copying karate. The English shifts him into third person and uses the nonstandard reflexive 'hisself.'

highlights.text: There is also a me that forgets hisself when he is called a Karate plagiarist.

records.jp: 「言わないけど、たぶん銃器も使える」
records.en: Taichi: "I can't really say, but maybe she can even use firearms."
records.assessment: Taichi says that Youko does not talk about it but can probably use firearms. The English instead makes Taichi say that he cannot disclose the claim.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I can't really say, but maybe she can even use firearms."

records.jp: 「格闘というか、組み討ちになったら一瞬で殺されるんじゃないかな。いろんなワザ持ってるし、こないだすごく高価なナイフ買ってたし」
records.en: Taichi: "In hand-to-hand, if it comes to grappling, I think you might just get killed in an instant. She has knowledge of lots of techniques, and lately, she purchased this really expensive knife."
comments: Kinda odd he also happens to have a weird, expensive, foreign knife that apparently she bought, see CCC4010. Consider Miki lied about having received it from Kiri, and her word on whether she has one at all is contradictory at best. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he would probably be killed instantly if grappling with Youko. The English changes the endangered first-person speaker into a generic 'you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "In hand-to-hand, if it comes to grappling, I think you might just get killed in an instant. She has knowledge of lots of techniques, and lately, she purchased this really expensive knife."

records.jp: 「……そんな……いくらなんでも殺すなんて……」
records.en: Kiri: "...but then... no matter how you put it, it's all about the killing..."
records.assessment: Kiri protests that surely Youko would not actually kill someone. The English instead says that, however the matter is framed, it is all about killing.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...but then... no matter how you put it, it's all about the killing..."

records.jp: 「命を助けられて、何もできなくなった以上、こういう状況は仕方ありません」
records.en: Kiri: "My life was saved, so I cannot do anything anymore, nor do anything to change this situation."
records.assessment: Kiri says that because Taichi saved her life and she can no longer act against him, the present situation cannot be helped. The English turns the latter point into a vague inability to change the situation and obscures the causal sequence.

highlights.text: Kiri: "My life was saved, so I cannot do anything anymore, nor do anything to change this situation."

records.jp: 「か、からかって！」
records.en: Kiri: "Mo-, mocker!"
records.assessment: Kiri accuses Taichi of teasing her. 'Mo-, mocker!' changes the accusation into an unnatural noun of address.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Mo-, mocker!"

records.jp: 「……先輩には、確かにそんな部分があると思います」
records.en: Kiri: "...I think, Senpai, that there is certainly a part that acts like that in you."
records.assessment: Kiri says that Taichi certainly has such a side to him. 'A part that acts like that in you' is an ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...I think, Senpai, that there is certainly a part that acts like that in you."

records.jp: 「だめ。彼女は自分を持ってない」
records.en: Taichi: "Not happening. She can't hold herself down."
comments: Though given the Alter Ego thing, not to mention the possible identity, something like "she's not her own person" would also work. -GHS
records.assessment: 自分を持ってない means that she has no self or identity of her own. 'Can't hold herself down' instead describes failed restraint.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Not happening. She can't hold herself down."

records.jp: 「逃げてるんだよ。昔からそうだ」
records.en: Taichi: "I want to run away from her. Been like that for a long time."
records.assessment: Taichi says that she is running away and always has. The English makes Taichi the one who wants to run away from her.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I want to run away from her. Been like that for a long time."

records.jp: 「……これで精一杯なんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "...this is all that can be done."
comments: Could be referring to how Youko can never replace all people, or how he can't stop using people for amusement. Leaving ambiguous -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is already doing the best he can. The English removes him as the agent and says only that this is all that can be done.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...this is all that can be done."

records.jp: 「強く言ってあるから平気だと思うけど、俺が目を離してるときに霧ちんになにかする可能性もあるし」
records.en: Taichi: "I told her firmly so I think we'll be alright, but there's the possibility that she'll do something should you get away from my sight, Kiri-chin."
records.assessment: The danger is what Youko might do to Kiri while Taichi takes his eyes off her. The English instead makes Kiri move out of his sight.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I told her firmly so I think we'll be alright, but there's the possibility that she'll do something should you get away from my sight, Kiri-chin."

records.jp: 「俺にバレずに霧ちんをくびちょんぱしちゃうとかね」
records.en: Taichi: "And without I becoming aware, poor Kiri-chin could get completely neckchopped."
comments: Trying to be funny again. くびちょんぱ kubichonpa (decapitation) is not to be confused with くびちょんば kubichonba (baker's dozen). -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that Youko might chop Kiri's head off without his noticing. The English uses a passive construction with the invented verb 'neckchopped' and loses the actor.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And without I becoming aware, poor Kiri-chin could get completely neckchopped."

records.jp: がくがく震える。
records.en: Trembling with a clatter.
records.assessment: がくがく describes Kiri trembling violently. 'With a clatter' wrongly presents the mimetic expression as an external sound.

highlights.text: Trembling with a clatter.

records.jp: 「自分の命のため、俺のそばにいないといけない……ってことでいいじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "For the sake of your life, thou must stay by my side... ain't that a nice thing to say?"
records.assessment: Taichi says that needing to stay beside him to protect her life is a perfectly good justification. The English changes this into 'a nice thing to say' and adds unsupported mock-archaic and eye-dialect speech.

highlights.text: Taichi: "For the sake of your life, thou must stay by my side... ain't that a nice thing to say?"

records.jp: 「…………馬鹿にしてますっ」
records.en: Kiri: "......you are making me look stupid!"
records.assessment: 馬鹿にする means to make fun of or treat someone like a fool. 'Making me look stupid' instead means causing other people to view her badly.

highlights.text: Kiri: "......you are making me look stupid!"

records.jp: 「……こわいお人だ……敵さえも味方に……」
records.en: Miki: "...scary guy him... even enemies he makes allies..."
records.assessment: Miki calls him a frightening man who even turns enemies into allies. The English is a string of malformed fragments with unstable pronouns.

highlights.text: Miki: "...scary guy him... even enemies he makes allies..."

records.jp: 「これが三顧の礼だ」
records.en: Taichi: "I just asked very politely."
comments: This term has a whole historical lesson behind it... but that seems excessive here. -GHS
records.assessment: 三顧の礼 invokes an elaborate, repeated, respectful solicitation. 'I just asked very politely' discards both the allusive force and the exaggeration.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I just asked very politely."

records.en: Kiri: "...didn't..."
records.assessment: Kiri's elliptical 違う rejects his account as wrong. The isolated past-tense 'didn't' has no subject or complement.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...didn't..."

records.jp: 「あー、なんか食べてるー、この大量の食料はどうするのー？」
records.en: Miki: "Ahhh, why are you even eeeating, what will we do with this huge bag of foood?"
records.assessment: Miki asks why they have already started eating and what she is to do with all the food she brought. 'Why are you even eating' changes the temporal complaint and is grammatically awkward.

highlights.text: Miki: "Ahhh, why are you even eeeating, what will we do with this huge bag of foood?"

records.jp: 「うーむ。お菓子を昼飯がわりにするのは……つらそうだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Uh-huh. Using junk food in the stead of a proper lunch... that looks nasty."
records.assessment: Taichi says that substituting snacks for lunch looks difficult or unpleasant. 'Looks nasty' suggests disgust, and 'in the stead' is malformed in this construction.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uh-huh. Using junk food in the stead of a proper lunch... that looks nasty."

records.jp: 「健康にも悪い」
records.en: Taichi: "Terrible for the health, too."
records.assessment: The ordinary expression is 'bad for your health.' 'Bad for the health' uses an unsupported definite article.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Terrible for the health, too."

records.jp: むくれた。
records.en: Sullen.
records.assessment: The Japanese narrates that Miki sulked. 'Sullen' is an adjective fragment and does not state the action or change of state.

highlights.text: Sullen.

records.jp: 「太ってもお菓子大好き」
records.en: Miki: "I'll still fatteningly love sweets!"
comments: fu-tottemo. And I spared the pun with Taichi, which I'm sure is there. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says that she loves sweets even if she gets fat. 'Fatteningly love' is not English and fails to express the concession.

highlights.text: Miki: "I'll still fatteningly love sweets!"

records.jp: 「内心気にしてるんじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "But inside yourself this annoys you, doesn't it?"
records.assessment: Taichi observes that she really does care about getting fat deep down. The English says that something annoys her internally, which is not the same claim.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But inside yourself this annoys you, doesn't it?"

records.jp: 「あああ、手料理だぁぁぁぁ～」
records.en: Miki: "Aaah, it's handmade coooo～king!"
records.assessment: 手料理 means homemade food or cooking. 'Handmade cooking' is an unnatural literal compound.

highlights.text: Miki: "Aaah, it's handmade coooo～king!"

records.jp: ひし、とおにぎりを持った手にすがりつく。
records.en: Hug!, she clings to the hand that's holding the onigiri.
records.assessment: The mimetic ひし conveys that Miki clings tightly. The inserted exclamation 'Hug!' names a different action.

highlights.text: Hug!, she clings to the hand that's holding the onigiri.

records.jp: 「……女の子なのに不安な食生活だな。いつもこうなの？」
records.en: Taichi: "...for being girls your eating habits seem unstable. Is it always like this?"
records.assessment: Taichi calls their diet worrying or precarious. 'Eating habits seem unstable' is an unnatural collocation and does not convey his concern cleanly.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...for being girls your eating habits seem unstable. Is it always like this?"

records.jp: 「涙出そう」
records.en: Miki: "Feels I'm crying!"
comments: See CCC4009. And compare Taichi. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says that she feels as though she is about to cry. 'Feels I'm crying' is malformed and changes an imminent reaction into an ongoing one.

highlights.text: Miki: "Feels I'm crying!"

records.jp: 「生きてるっていいね」
records.en: Kiri: "We're living it up here."
records.assessment: Kiri says that being alive is good. 'Living it up' instead means enjoying oneself extravagantly and loses the statement about life itself.

highlights.text: We're living it up here.

records.jp: 美希と霧が、口を『＊』状にしながらトマトを食べる様を横目に見ながら、俺は水筒で喉を潤した。
records.en: While looking sidelong at Miki and Kiri's mouths go 『＊』-shaped via tomato eating, I quench my thirst with my canteen.
comments: See CCC4009. Miki and Kiri's mouths become like Taichi's asshole??????what??????? -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator watches the two eat with puckered mouths while taking a drink. 'Mouths go ... via tomato eating' is a calque, and the sentence inconsistently switches to present tense.

highlights.text: While looking sidelong at Miki and Kiri's mouths go 『＊』-shaped via tomato eating, I quench my thirst with my canteen.

records.jp: じっくり見られちゃってる！！
records.en: We're being calmly looked aaat!!!
records.assessment: The Japanese says that she is giving them a long, intent look. 'We're being calmly looked at' is unidiomatic and misreads じっくり as calmness.

highlights.text: We're being calmly looked aaat!!!

records.jp: 俺に気取られるように姿を見せているってことは……当てつけなんだろうな。
records.en: Her showing herself to me is the same as suspecting me... this is an insinuation.
records.assessment: Taichi infers that Youko is deliberately showing herself where he can notice as a spiteful display directed at him. The English instead introduces suspicion and an insinuation.

highlights.text: is the same as suspecting me... this is an insinuation

records.jp: 霧も見たらしい。
records.en: Seems Kiri has seen.
records.assessment: The line means that Kiri seems to have spotted her too. 'Seems Kiri has seen' omits the object and the necessary complementizer.

highlights.text: Seems Kiri has seen.

records.jp: 「平気だ、俺のそばにいるんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You're fine, you're by my side."
comments: I suspect he just played footsie. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi reassures Kiri and tells her to stay by his side. The English changes the instruction into a statement that she is already beside him.

highlights.text: you're by my side

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんの姿はない。
records.en: Youko-chan's figure is not there.
comments: How does Taichi know Miki can't see her, when he could see her just a split second ago? And this is not necessarily where Kiri points. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko is no longer there. 'Her figure is not there' is a literal and unnatural way to report her absence.

highlights.text: Youko-chan's figure is not there.

records.jp: 「……え？　なにもないけど、どったの？」
records.en: Miki: "...eh? There's nothing there, whass'it?"
comments: That's not necessarily the doorway. -GHS
records.assessment: どったの is a casual 'what's wrong?' The invented contraction 'whass'it?' instead asks what an object is.

highlights.text: Miki: "...eh? There's nothing there, whass'it?"

records.jp: 反射的に肩を抱く。
records.en: Reflexively I hold her shoulders.
comments: Is he? Miki says nothing. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi reflexively puts an arm around Kiri's shoulders. 'Hold her shoulders' suggests gripping them with his hands rather than the enclosing gesture.

highlights.text: Reflexively I hold her shoulders.

records.jp: これは滅茶苦茶珍しいことです。
