records.en: That is something unreasonably rare.
records.assessment: The Japanese calls the reaction extraordinarily rare. 'Unreasonably rare' wrongly evaluates the rarity as irrational.

highlights.text: That is something unreasonably rare.

records.jp: 愛おしい反面と、壊してしまいたいという欲求。
records.en: Lovability on one side, on the other, the want to destroy.
comments: Vs. desire -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator feels tenderness or affection on one side and an urge to destroy on the other. 'Lovability' describes a quality in Kiri rather than his feeling toward her.

highlights.text: Lovability on one side, on the other, the want to destroy.

records.jp: 「霧ちん、気をつけろよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri-chin, pay attention!"
records.assessment: 気をつけろ warns Kiri to be careful or watch out. 'Pay attention' suggests attending to information rather than danger.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kiri-chin, pay attention!"

records.jp: 「危害はないとしても、嫌がらせをしてくる可能性がある」
records.en: Taichi: "Even if harm doesn't come, there is still the possibility of harassment."
records.assessment: Taichi says that even if Youko does not physically harm Kiri, she may harass her. The English removes both actor and target and uses the unnatural phrase 'harm doesn't come.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Even if harm doesn't come, there is still the possibility of harassment."

records.jp: 「えーと……かなり陰湿だと思うよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Uhmmm... something fairly malicious, of the wet and private kind I think."
comments: Given Taichi and the circumstances, reading that as "wet vagina" is definitely expected. -GHS
records.assessment: 陰湿 means insidious, underhanded, or malicious. The English invents 'of the wet and private kind,' which has no support in the Japanese.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uhmmm... something fairly malicious, of the wet and private kind I think."

records.jp: 「……あなたと一緒じゃないですか」
records.en: Kiri: "...is that that not the same as what you do?"
records.assessment: The English repeats 'that' and produces a malformed question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...is that that not the same as what you do?"

records.jp: あああ、同性に寝取られた。
records.en: Ahhhh, same-sex netorare'd!
records.assessment: The Japanese makes a comic remark about being romantically supplanted by someone of the same sex. Turning the noun into the nonce verb 'netorare'd' leaves the idea untranslated.

highlights.text: Ahhhh, same-sex netorare'd!

records.jp: 美希がいました。
records.en: Miki graced us with her presence.
comments: oddly formal -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese simply and pointedly says that Miki was there. 'Graced us with her presence' adds an ironic social judgment.

highlights.text: Miki graced us with her presence.

records.jp: なぜ黙りこくるんだ。
records.en: Mysteriously, she keeps silent.
records.assessment: The narrator asks why Miki has fallen completely silent. The English changes the question into a statement that her silence is mysterious.

highlights.text: Mysteriously, she keeps silent.

records.jp: 「敵地で発見されぬよう行動する時などに用います」
records.en: Miki: "It's used to remain undiscovered during mobilizations in hostile territory."
comments: Metal Gear Solid was released September 3, 1998. Juuust in time. See CCD0008B for why it's certainly the reference. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says that the box is used when operating without discovery in hostile territory. 'Mobilizations' denotes organizing or deploying forces, not covert action.

highlights.text: Miki: "It's used to remain undiscovered during mobilizations in hostile territory."

records.jp: 「ミキハウスを見たら普通のヤングアダルトは『いい子供服あるかい？』って具合にダンディーに中をのぞきこみたくなるに決まっている」
records.en: Taichi: "On sight of the Miki House, a normal Young Adult will dandy up and with a, 'could there be some quality children's clothing inside?', decide to peek into it."
comments: http://www.mikihouse.co.jp/en/ and the arcana is solved. Please note that they don't ship internationally even though their site is in English (I think it's Japanese for "use a forwarding service"). Ah, wait, there's a USA site now: http://mikihouse-usa.com/ -GHS
records.assessment: The English sentence is syntactically broken: a normal young adult does not 'dandy up,' and the nested question and infinitive never form a coherent clause.

highlights.text: Taichi: "On sight of the Miki House, a normal Young Adult will dandy up and with a, 'could there be some quality children's clothing inside?', decide to peek into it."

records.jp: 「……うう、わたしの身につけているものくらいしかお売り出来ないですね」
records.en: Miki: "...ngh, and it's impossible to sell something that I've already worn, isn't it."
comments: I think we're switching from the box to the clothes. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says that all she could sell would be what she is currently wearing. The English says that selling something already worn is impossible, reversing the proposition.

highlights.text: Miki: "...ngh, and it's impossible to sell something that I've already worn, isn't it."

records.jp: 「どうしてそんな突然リアルな顔をして言うんですか？」
records.en: Miki: "Why are you saying this making this very Real Serious face all of a sudden?"
comments: The Rial is also a currency. -GHS
records.assessment: The English duplicates 'making this' and adds inconsistent capitalization to an otherwise ordinary reference to a suddenly serious face.

highlights.text: Miki: "Why are you saying this making this very Real Serious face all of a sudden?"

records.jp: 「リアル世代だからだ。だがそんなことはどうでもいい」
records.en: Taichi: "Because it's a Real-Life Generation. But, that is inconsequential."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is of the 'real generation.' The English makes an unspecified thing into 'a Real-Life Generation' and leaves the joke grammatically incoherent.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because it's a Real-Life Generation. But, that is inconsequential."

records.jp: 「買った。即決」
records.en: Taichi: "Bought. Impulse buy."
comments: See CCA0007. Has this guy ever had money...? -GHS
records.assessment: 即決 here means that the decision or deal is made immediately. 'Impulse buy' instead describes an unplanned consumer decision.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Bought. Impulse buy."

records.jp: 「十万円金貨だ。美希は知るまいが」
records.en: Taichi: "Ten thousand yen gold coins. You likely don't know about them, Miki."
records.assessment: 十万円金貨 identifies 100,000-yen gold coins. The English calls them 10,000-yen coins, an order-of-magnitude error.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ten thousand yen gold coins. You likely don't know about them, Miki."

records.jp: 「そこいらじゃ使えないが、まあ正式な通貨だぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "That they're not, but, well, they're still officially currency."
comments: I suspect banks would have relatively little issue exchanging a gold coin, but indeed I don't think shops would accept them. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that the coins cannot be used around here but are nonetheless legal tender. The English answers only that they are not spendable and omits the local limitation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That they're not, but, well, they're still officially currency."

records.jp: 「さあ、即決した。入金も済んだ。次はそっちの番だ」
records.en: Taichi: "That was an impulse buy after all. So, the money due was given. Next it's your end of the bargain."
records.assessment: Taichi says that the immediate deal is concluded and payment completed. 'That was an impulse buy' misreads 即決, and 'the money due was given' is an unnatural passive.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That was an impulse buy after all. So, the money due was given. Next it's your end of the bargain."

records.jp: 「もし約束を違えるのであれば……『たいへん悪い』という評価をつけるぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "Supposing you were to alter the deal... I would give you a rating of 'Very Negative'!"
comments: Not the translation, but dammit, it's Star Wars meets Ebay, and I can't pass that up. Or think of a midichlorians joke, dammit. -GHS
records.assessment: 約束を違える means to break the promise. 'Alter the deal' permits modification rather than expressing breach.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Supposing you were to alter the deal... I would give you a rating of 'Very Negative'!"

records.jp: 「女の子にとって、その噂はピンチ中のピンチです」
records.en: Miki: "But for a girl, to have that on her shoulders is to be in a pinch among pinches!"
records.assessment: Miki says that such a reputation would be the worst possible crisis for a girl. 'A pinch among pinches' is a literal calque, and 'have that on her shoulders' does not identify the damaging rumor.

highlights.text: Miki: "But for a girl, to have that on her shoulders is to be in a pinch among pinches!"

records.jp: 「なら脱ぎたまえ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ergo gladden me with stripping."
records.assessment: なら脱ぎたまえ is a direct, pompous command to strip. 'Gladden me with stripping' invents a motive of pleasing the speaker and is not idiomatic.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ergo gladden me with stripping."

records.jp: 「ＯＫＯＫ、いいよいいよ！　やっぱなし！」
records.en: Taichi: "Okieh okieh, 's enough, 's enough! I don't really want you to!"
comments: See CCA0030. -GHS
records.assessment: やっぱなし means that Taichi calls the plan off after all. 'I don't really want you to' describes his desire rather than retracting the demand.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Okieh okieh, 's enough, 's enough! I don't really want you to!"

records.jp: 冬子を拾ってきますか。
records.en: shall I not go recover Touko?
comments: formal for some reason -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi proposes going to pick Touko up. 'Recover Touko' treats her as a lost object or a rescue target.

highlights.text: shall I not go recover Touko?

records.jp: 職員室から鍵をあさり、合う車を探す。
records.en: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.
records.assessment: The Japanese gives a single present narrative sequence of rummaging for keys and finding the matching car. The English arbitrarily mixes past and present.

highlights.text: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.

records.jp: 駐車場は惨劇になっていた。
records.en: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.
records.assessment: The parking lot is described metaphorically as a scene of disaster. 'A tragedy had taken place' asserts an actual tragic event.

highlights.text: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.

records.jp: まるで暴走車が、当て逃げを繰り返したみたいに。
records.en: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.
comments: 暴走. Remember it... -GHS
records.assessment: The comparison is to a runaway or rampaging car repeatedly striking vehicles and fleeing. The English substitutes a 'rampant driver' and the formal criminal phrase 'performed hit-and-runs.'

highlights.text: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.

records.jp: フロントに放射状にヒビが。
records.en: cracks in that front radiator...
records.assessment: フロント here refers to the front glass or windshield bearing radiating cracks. A radiator does not take radial visible cracking in the described list, and the Japanese does not name one.

highlights.text: cracks in that front radiator...

records.jp: 「やっぱ素人にミッションは無理か、ククク」
records.en: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"
comments: Mission OR transmission, see CCA0003 - amateurs rejected! -GHS
records.assessment: ミッション is Japanese automotive shorthand for a manual transmission, with a joke about an amateur handling it. Leaving it as English 'mission' loses the automotive meaning.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"

records.jp: キーの合った車に乗り込む。
records.en: I get on the car that fits the key.
comments: The whole scene was massacred in the PS2 version because they removed him actually getting on a car and driving. Taichi, there, is apparently somehow driving his own self, and is utterly surreal idea. -GHS
records.assessment: One gets into a car, not 'on the car.'

highlights.text: I get on the car that fits the key.

records.jp: 男だから当然ミッションだ。
records.en: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,
records.assessment: Taichi says that because he is a man, naturally the car is a manual transmission. The English uses the unrelated word 'mission' and leaves the sentence dangling into the punch line.

highlights.text: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,

records.jp: ちょっと龍馬入ってる。
records.en: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.
comments: I can only suspect it's also a reference to [龍馬/竜馬]のつまずき, "even the best horse stumbles". -GHS
records.assessment: 龍馬 refers to Ryoma and explains Taichi's imitation of the distinctive ぜよ speech. The English translates the name's characters as a generic 'war horse' and invents a battle description.

highlights.text: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.

records.jp: タイヤ止めを乗り越えて背後の樹木をへし折ってしまったぞ。
records.en: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.
comments: I think it's just part of the parking space, only specifically intended to prevent, well, the above. -GHS
records.assessment: The car crosses the wheel stop and snaps the tree behind it. The English changes the tree into shrubbery and merely says that the car breaks into it.

highlights.text: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.

records.jp: こんなミス、百万回に一度もない。超レアイベントだ。
records.en: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.
records.assessment: Taichi says that this mistake would not happen even once in a million times and calls it hyper-rare. 'Isn't a one in a million' normally denies that it is rare and contradicts the next sentence.

highlights.text: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.

records.jp: 高そうな車なのに……すまん、今は亡き榊原教諭。
records.en: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.
records.assessment: 今は亡き is the conventional 'late' for a deceased person, and 教諭 is a teacher. 'Currently-Deceased Professor' is an unnatural, comic bureaucratic construction not present in the Japanese.

highlights.text: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.

records.jp: がくん、と車が急加速する。
records.en: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.
comments: Although automatic cars crawl forwards when not in brake, he likely had the accelerator down. -GHS
records.assessment: がくん describes the car lurching as it accelerates. 'Boom' introduces an explosive sound.

highlights.text: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.

records.jp: 横一列に並んでいた車の鼻先をかすめながら、バンパーをもぎっていく。
records.en: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.
records.assessment: The car clips the noses of vehicles lined in a single row and tears off their bumpers as it goes. The English changes the row to plural rows and leaves a single bumper without a clear owner.

highlights.text: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.

records.jp: やべー、校長のフェラーリもひどいことに。
records.en: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.
comments: Shinkawa's catchphrase... PS2 version talks about "that expensive war horse". ...then again, since this likely happens only in his mind... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator observes that the principal's Ferrari is now in terrible condition too. The English explicitly makes him the agent and describes an intentionally 'nasty' act.

highlights.text: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.

records.jp: ま、いっか。こんな危険な学校でフェラる方が悪い。
records.en: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.
comments: ※フェラる＝太一語。二つの意味が。①フェラーリのオーナーになること。②（全略）
I guess it now sounds more like 'fucking' than 'fellatio', but, eh, who gives a blowjob. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese pun blames the person who brings or drives a Ferrari at such a dangerous school. The English turns the pun into an unrelated claim that sexual activity at school is improper.

highlights.text: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.

records.jp: 「くじけずＧＯ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Undauntedly GO!"
records.assessment: くじけずＧＯ is an exhortation not to give up and to go. 'Undauntedly GO' uses an unnatural adverb.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Undauntedly GO!"

records.jp: せいぜいが放水車で破壊されるが関の山。
records.en: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.
comments: Term's relatively generic, but: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%A0%B4%E5%A3%8A%E6%A9%9F%E6%95%91%E9%9B%A3%E6%B6%88%E9%98%B2%E8%BB%8A <- guessing. It sounds like a movie reference, no idea. Some of those fire engines that I see GISing around look like they could just trample on cars, too. -GHS
records.assessment: The car's best prospect is to end up destroyed by a water-cannon truck. 'Water cannon fire engines' conflates vehicle types and changes the singular car into plural 'they.'

highlights.text: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.

records.jp: 地面に『の』の字を書きながら待っていると、奥からするすると車が走ってきた。
records.en: I pass the time by embarrassedly spiraling my finger in the ground in the shape of the 'no' hiragana, until a car came smoothly riding out from the back.
comments: Unsure how popular that is to do these days, I actually haven't seen it done that often, so specified a bit. See CCX0001. -GHS
records.assessment: Drawing の on the ground conventionally depicts dejection or sulking in this context. The English labels the gesture embarrassment and adds a spiraling motion not stated by the source.

highlights.text: I pass the time by embarrassedly spiraling my finger in the ground in the shape of the 'no' hiragana, until a car came smoothly riding out from the back.

records.jp: 淀みのない運転で、目の前に停車。
records.en: Driving without hesitation, it stops right in front of me.
records.assessment: Youko drives smoothly and stops before Taichi. 'Driving without hesitation, it stops' attaches the human action of driving to the car.

highlights.text: Driving without hesitation, it stops right in front of me.

records.jp: 「乗って」
records.en: Youko: "Get on."
records.assessment: The command for entering a car is 'Get in,' not 'Get on.'

highlights.text: Youko: "Get on."

records.jp: 「……桐原城ですお世話になります」
records.en: Taichi: "...castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose."
comments: Well and formal. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi gives the destination, Kirihara Castle, and courteously thanks her for the ride. 'Castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose' reverses the name and turns the thanks into a request.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose."

records.jp: 連れて行ってもらった。
records.en: I was being taken there.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that she took him there. 'I was being taken' uses an incomplete progressive passive and suppresses the driver.

highlights.text: I was being taken there.

records.jp: 大きすぎて陽光を遮り、一面の闇にしか見えない。
records.en: So enormously huge that it intercepts the sunlight, and I can't see anything besides silhouetted darkness.
comments: Hmmm... -GHS
records.assessment: The house blocks the sunlight and looks like a single expanse of darkness. 'Silhouetted darkness' is contradictory, and the English adds a claim that the narrator can see nothing else.

highlights.text: So enormously huge that it intercepts the sunlight, and I can't see anything besides silhouetted darkness.

records.jp: 俺は夜目がきくが、なぜかまったく見えない。
records.en: I have sharp night eyes, but for some reason I absolutely can't see.
comments: According to CCC4015, it's just the inside that's this dark. And us readers can see perfectly fine, can't we? And he used the exact kanji for "darkness" that, in CCX0001, says he can see through. What's perplexing is only the level of blatancy in this troll. -GHS
records.assessment: 夜目がきく means to see well in darkness. 'Have sharp night eyes' is a literal and unnatural compound.

highlights.text: I have sharp night eyes, but for some reason I absolutely can't see.

records.jp: これではいくら夜目がきいても、視界は確保できない。
records.en: With things like this, no matter how sharp my night vision, I can't be certain of what I see.
comments: The experiment extends afterwards, too. Theory: he's not outside of school, he's not seeing anything because there's nothing to see, Touko's not dead but in the infirmary passed out due to lack of food, Taichi's hallucinating everything including her death... and also it avoids having to have BGs of the inside of the mansion, so there's a tech troll as well. See CCC3018, end. -GHS
records.assessment: Even excellent night vision cannot secure any visibility in total darkness. The English instead says that he cannot be certain about what he does see.

highlights.text: With things like this, no matter how sharp my night vision, I can't be certain of what I see.

records.jp: なんかゾンビが出そうな屋敷だなあ。
records.en: This is the kind of a mansion where you'd just see some zombies popping out, isn't it.
comments: As long as it's not Chris's blood, we'll be safe. See CCB2010. -GHS
records.assessment: 'The kind of a mansion' incorrectly combines the definite construction 'the kind of' with an indefinite article.

highlights.text: This is the kind of a mansion where you'd just see some zombies popping out, isn't it.

records.jp: ……曜子ちゃんについてきてもらえばよかった。
records.en: ...it'd have been better if I had come with Youko-chan.
records.assessment: Taichi wishes that he had asked Youko to come along with him. 'If I had come with Youko' reverses who would be accompanying whom.

highlights.text: ...it'd have been better if I had come with Youko-chan.

records.jp: 眠り姫を思わせて、気高い。
records.en: A nobility that reminded me of Sleeping Beauty.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the sight evokes Sleeping Beauty and is noble. The English turns the predicate into the fragment 'A nobility.'

highlights.text: A nobility that reminded me of Sleeping Beauty.

records.jp: 群青の冬子は一人だった。
records.en: Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou was alone.
records.assessment: 群青 is the institution or group name Gunjou in this construction. 'Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou' translates the same name twice and invents an epithet.

highlights.text: Touko the Ultramarine of Gunjou was alone.

records.jp: 適応係数調査試験で弾かれて、ここに来た。
records.en: Plucked off by the Conformity Coefficient Test, she came here.
records.assessment: The test rejected or screened Touko out. 'Plucked off' describes removal by picking and is not the social or evaluative rejection expressed here.

highlights.text: Plucked off by the Conformity Coefficient Test, she came here.

records.jp: 適応係数は百分比で表される。
records.en: The Conformity Coefficient is represented with a percentage.
records.assessment: A value is expressed 'as a percentage,' not 'with a percentage.'

highlights.text: The Conformity Coefficient is represented with a percentage.

records.jp: 群青では、高からず低からず。
records.en: In Gunjou, neither the highest nor the lowest.
records.assessment: Her value is neither high nor low within Gunjou. 'Neither the highest nor the lowest' merely denies the two extreme ranks and allows a value that is still high or low.

highlights.text: In Gunjou, neither the highest nor the lowest.

records.jp: 学校に来ても制服を拒み、内にこもって人を拒み。
records.en: She came to school but refused the uniform, she segregates herself inside and rejects the people.
comments: Inside the classroom, not inside herself... though there's not much difference. And of course, when she says "people grew thin until they disappeared", she doesn't mean that everybody has physically disappeared; just that they've dumped her and left alone. -GHS
records.assessment: She shut herself away and rejected people. 'Segregates herself inside' is unidiomatic, changes tense, and does not express withdrawal into herself or her room.

highlights.text: She came to school but refused the uniform, she segregates herself inside and rejects the people.

records.jp: どこにも属さず誰にもへつらわず。
records.en: Belonging nowhere, being nice to no one.
records.assessment: へつらう means to flatter, fawn, or curry favor. 'Being nice to no one' wrongly turns refusal to abase herself into a lack of ordinary kindness.

highlights.text: Belonging nowhere, being nice to no one.

records.jp: そして今、冬子は寝台の上で小ぎれいに手を組んでいる。
records.en: And now, Touko is laying on top of her bed, her hands neatly overlapped.
records.assessment: A person lies on a bed; 'is laying' is transitive and requires an object.

highlights.text: And now, Touko is laying on top of her bed, her hands neatly overlapped.

records.jp: 自分でそうしたのだろうか。
records.en: She probably did that on her own.
records.assessment: The narrator wonders whether she arranged herself that way. The English turns the question into a probability assertion.

highlights.text: She probably did that on her own.

records.jp: 眠るように去ったのだろうか。
records.en: She probably passed as if sleeping.
comments: Notice how he never actually checks the corpse for a pulse. Now notice how he never even THINKS to check the corpse for a pulse. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator wonders whether she departed as if falling asleep. The English asserts probability and uses the incomplete verb 'passed' instead of preserving the question.

highlights.text: She probably passed as if sleeping.

records.jp: けど悲しささえ圧倒的な尊厳に塗りかえられて。
records.en: But even the sadness is varnished with an overwhelming sense of dignity.
records.assessment: Overwhelming dignity overwrites even the sadness. 'Varnished with' merely coats sadness and reverses which element transforms the other.

highlights.text: But even the sadness is varnished with an overwhelming sense of dignity.

records.jp: 俺は感動し、佇んだ。
records.en: Moved, I stand still.
comments: Oh, another one of those that work so well in English. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrative reports that he was moved and stood there. The English unexpectedly switches to present tense.

highlights.text: Moved, I stand still.

records.jp: それはわからない。
records.en: I have no idea of what.
records.assessment: He does not know which of the preceding causes applies. 'I have no idea of what' is incomplete and does not point back to the alternatives.

highlights.text: I have no idea of what.

records.jp: 暴く気もない。
records.en: Finding out, unthinkable.
records.assessment: Taichi has no intention of uncovering the cause. 'Finding out, unthinkable' changes lack of intent into a moral or conceptual impossibility.

highlights.text: Finding out, unthinkable.

records.jp: その事実が脳裏に呼び覚まされたのは、屋敷を出る直前だった。
records.en: That fact woke up in my mind just before I left the mansion.
records.assessment: The fact came back to mind. It did not literally 'wake up in' his mind.

highlights.text: That fact woke up in my mind just before I left the mansion.

records.jp: 汚されたように感じた。
records.en: It felt as if she was being dirtied.
records.assessment: He feels as if the sacred moment or its dignity has been defiled. The English instead says that Touko herself is being dirtied.

highlights.text: It felt as if she was being dirtied.

records.jp: 冬子を突き放したのだろう。
records.en: To get away from Touko, that's why.
records.assessment: Together with the preceding line, this asks why he had pushed Touko away. The English turns the second half into the answer 'To get away from Touko, that's why.'

highlights.text: To get away from Touko, that's why.

records.jp: さておき部活だ。
records.en: All that aside, to club.
comments: See CCA0005A, CCA0030. This sentence may not be unrelated at all. -GHS
records.assessment: さておき部活だ is 'Anyway, time for club activities.' 'To club' is an ungrammatical destination fragment.

highlights.text: All that aside, to club.

records.jp: ナチュラルに女子トイレに入る俺。
records.en: Entering all natural in the girls' toilet.
records.assessment: The narrator casually walks into the girls' restroom. 'Entering all natural' is not grammatical English and misuses 'all-natural.'

highlights.text: Entering all natural in the girls' toilet.

records.jp: 鏡を見る。
records.en: I look at the mirror.
records.assessment: One looks in a mirror, not 'at the mirror,' when describing seeing one's reflection.

highlights.text: I look at the mirror.

records.jp: 独特の模様を持つ瞳。
records.en: Pupils with a peculiar pattern.
comments: PCP CCC3018
records.assessment: 瞳 refers to the eyes or irises here. The English narrows it incorrectly to the pupils.

highlights.text: Pupils with a peculiar pattern.

records.jp: どちらかと言うと鷲鼻。
records.en: If I wanted to call it something, an aquiline nose.
records.assessment: どちらかと言うと means 'if anything' or 'rather,' classifying the nose as aquiline. 'If I wanted to call it something' incorrectly makes the label a matter of willingness.

highlights.text: If I wanted to call it something, an aquiline nose.

records.jp: 自分の目からだと、そう見える。
records.en: So I see, from my own eyes.
comments: See CCA0021. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese means 'at least, that is how it looks to me.' 'So I see, from my own eyes' is an unnatural literalization.

highlights.text: So I see, from my own eyes.

records.jp: 整っている、と言う人もいる。
records.en: Well-ordered, some people would say.
comments: See CCB2009. This is almost certainly intended as a comparison to Touko, given what's about to happen. -GHS
records.assessment: A face described as 整っている is well-proportioned or handsome. 'Well-ordered' applies organizational arrangement rather than facial appearance.

highlights.text: Well-ordered, some people would say.

records.jp: だから『あんなコト』になるわけだし。
records.en: That is why I end up as 'that thing', yes.
comments: Supposing him being used as a doll. -GHS
records.assessment: He says that this appearance is why 'that sort of thing' happens to him. The English instead says that he ends up becoming an object called 'that thing.'

highlights.text: That is why I end up as 'that thing', yes.

records.jp: この顔は、どことなく異質で、おどろおどろしい。
records.en: my face is somehow heterogeneous, making it eerie and terrifying.
comments: This is pure groundless self-conviction, however. As well as a pretext. -GHS
records.assessment: The face seems somehow alien and macabre or sinister. 'Heterogeneous' suggests mixed composition, and the added causal 'making it' is not in the source.

highlights.text: my face is somehow heterogeneous, making it eerie and terrifying.

records.jp: 屍蝋めいて、人とは思えない。
records.en: It looks like adipocere, and doesn't remind of a person.
records.assessment: The face looks like adipocere and does not look human. 'Doesn't remind of a person' is ungrammatical and weakens visual resemblance into recollection.

highlights.text: It looks like adipocere, and doesn't remind of a person.

records.jp: ……人形だ。
records.en: ...but a doll's.
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies it as a doll. The English possessive fragment 'a doll's' leaves the possessed noun missing.

highlights.text: ...but a doll's.

records.jp: 美もあろうが、ぎょっとする不気味さ……闇を含有している。
records.en: There may be beauty there, but there's also a startling ghastliness... it contains the darkness of despair.
comments: Going with darkness both lateral and literal. Once more, see CCX0001: lateral darkness should be what he can see through. -GHS
records.assessment: The image contains darkness. The qualifier 'of despair' is not present in the Japanese.

highlights.text: There may be beauty there, but there's also a startling ghastliness... it contains the darkness of despair.

records.jp: そして俺もまた、同じ暗がりに寄り添ってしまう。
records.en: And I, myself, also crawl up and cuddle with that same dark.
comments: Still different kanji. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he too draws close to or nestles against the same darkness. 'Crawl up and cuddle' adds a physically crawling, cute register.

highlights.text: And I, myself, also crawl up and cuddle with that same dark.

records.jp: けど俺は……普通がいい。
records.en: Except me... I like the normal.
records.assessment: Taichi says that he wants normality or wants to be normal. 'I like the normal' is ungrammatical and changes desire for a state into a preference.

highlights.text: Except me... I like the normal.

records.jp: 押し込めるほどに、闇は凝縮してしまわないか。
records.en: Doesn't the darkness just condense the more it is squeezed into a prison?
comments: This is a strong denunciation of his own pseudonihilism, whether he knows it or not. Notice the lack of trite whining about Light Needing Darkness To Be Seen. There's no Great Balance crap here; this is about the inevitable failure of pretending there is no darkness within the human being. -GHS
records.assessment: The more darkness is suppressed or confined, the more it condenses. 'Squeezed into a prison' invents a concrete prison metaphor.

highlights.text: Doesn't the darkness just condense the more it is squeezed into a prison?

records.jp: 常闇から生まれてくるもの。
records.en: Things shall be born from this everlasting darkness.
comments: See CCA0021 -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese is a noun phrase, 'that which is born from perpetual darkness,' leading into the next question. The English makes it a future assertion that multiple things shall be born.

highlights.text: Things shall be born from this everlasting darkness.

records.jp: 黒々とした人の髪が羨ましい。羨ましくてたまらない。
records.en: There's envy in that hair of people so very black. Unendurable envy.
comments: "I envy black hair" + "I AM DARKNESS AND MY HAIR IS JEALOUS!!!" -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi intensely envies people's jet-black hair. The English places envy inside the hair itself.

highlights.text: There's envy in that hair of people so very black. Unendurable envy.

records.jp: 染めようかとも思った。
records.en: I did intend to dye,
comments: The implication is that he hasn't... -GHS
records.assessment: He considered dyeing his hair. 'Did intend to dye' asserts a formed intention and leaves its object missing.

highlights.text: I did intend to dye,

records.jp: 黒毛に透けたくすんだ灰色を見るたび、意識してしまう。
records.en: Whenever I look at that ashen that desires to be seen through the black hair, I realize:
records.assessment: He sees dull gray showing through the dyed black hair and is made conscious of the disguise. The English personifies 'ashen' as desiring to be seen through the black.

highlights.text: Whenever I look at that ashen that desires to be seen through the black hair, I realize:

records.jp: 今の俺が、まさにお飾りであるようにだ。
records.en: and that I am, right then, nothing more than something decorated.
comments: ...and that he didn't. Regardless, notice the metaphor: he is white, but dyes himself black - and dislikes the white that still comes through to knock. He's not horrible, but wants to be... and largely because it's easier, see some of his rants in CCX0001 where he explicitly says he wants to be alone so he won't have to improve or admit his inadequacies, which are right around his major breakdown there. -GHS
records.assessment: お飾り means that Taichi himself is now a mere ornament or figurehead. 'Something decorated' describes an object bearing decoration, not a person reduced to ornamental status.

highlights.text: and that I am, right then, nothing more than something decorated.

records.jp: 冬子の件を、俺はあまりにも良いものと感じすぎている。
records.en: The matter of Touko is making me feel like I'm far too excessively good.
comments: Not because he's giddy, but because he's pining for her in the only way he knows of, really: self-bashing. This is the white peeking through. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi feels that he is viewing the matter as far too beautiful or good. The English says that the matter makes him feel that he himself is excessively good.

highlights.text: The matter of Touko is making me feel like I'm far too excessively good.

records.jp: 迷うことなく、足が向いた。
records.en: Unhesitating, I quickly moved there.
records.assessment: His feet turn toward the sound without hesitation. 'Unhesitating' dangles without a noun, and 'quickly' is not stated.

highlights.text: Unhesitating, I quickly moved there.

records.jp: 体調が思わしくなさそうだ。
records.en: Physical conditions don't seem favorable.
comments: Taichi is *seriously* worried about her. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Kiri does not look well. 'Physical conditions don't seem favorable' is an impersonal plural calque.

highlights.text: Physical conditions don't seem favorable.

records.jp: これで、逃げられないね、霧。
records.en: There'll be no escape this way, dear Kiri.
records.assessment: Taichi says that Kiri cannot escape now. The intimate address 'dear Kiri' is an unsupported addition.

highlights.text: There'll be no escape this way, dear Kiri.

records.jp: 平静さを取り戻していく。
records.en: Serenity is being recovered.
comments: A load of bull. All he's doing is shutting down his brain and acting automatically. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi is regaining his composure. The passive 'Serenity is being recovered' removes the experiencer and turns a mental state into an object.

highlights.text: Serenity is being recovered.

records.jp: きっと瞳孔も変化しているだろう。
records.en: I'm certain that there's even a change in the pupillary.
records.assessment: His pupils must be changing too. 'The pupillary' incorrectly uses an adjective as a noun.

highlights.text: I'm certain that there's even a change in the pupillary.

records.jp: 敏感に反応してしまう。
records.en: Very sensitive responsive.
comments: This is the only thing he can see of her, can he? -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi reacts sensitively to the movement. 'Very sensitive responsive' is ungrammatical and omits both the reacting subject and action.

highlights.text: Very sensitive responsive.

records.jp: 「……あの……生理の……終わりが重くて……」
records.en: Kiri: "...uhm... my things... the ending is hard..."
records.assessment: Kiri says that the end of her menstrual period is heavy. 'My things ... the ending is hard' obscures menstruation and mistranslates heavy bleeding as difficulty.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...uhm... my things... the ending is hard..."

records.jp: 「どんな風に重いの？」
records.en: Taichi: "What kind of 'hard' you mean?"
comments: He's verifying that she feels bad because of something. See CCC0000. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks in what way the menstrual symptoms are heavy. The English again substitutes 'hard' and uses the malformed question 'What kind ... you mean?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "What kind of 'hard' you mean?"

records.jp: 「全体的に不安定で……サイクルがさだまらなくて……」
records.en: Kiri: "A sense of insecurity throughout... the cycles aren't settled..."
records.assessment: Kiri says that her cycle is unstable and irregular overall. 'A sense of insecurity' describes an emotion, not menstrual irregularity.

highlights.text: Kiri: "A sense of insecurity throughout... the cycles aren't settled..."

records.jp: 「ああ、それは君の年ごろだったらだいたいそうさ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, you are of that age now, therefore sometimes that happens."
records.assessment: Taichi says that this is generally normal at her age. The English weakens frequency to something that only happens sometimes and makes age the cause.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, you are of that age now, therefore sometimes that happens."

records.jp: 「成長途中で、ホルモンバランスが未成熟なせいだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's the immature balance of hormones as you're on the way to growing to adulthood to blame."
records.assessment: The cause is an immature hormonal balance while she is still growing. 'The immature balance of hormones ... to blame' is an awkward nominal stack.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's the immature balance of hormones as you're on the way to growing to adulthood to blame."

records.jp: 「特に霧は体つきが華奢で、成長が遅れているようだから」
records.en: Taichi: "Especially because your body figure is delicate, Kiri, so your growth to adulthood seems to lag behind."
comments: Just like Yusa's. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri has a slight build and appears late in developing. The English uses 'body figure' and the doubled causal frame 'especially because ... so.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Especially because your body figure is delicate, Kiri, so your growth to adulthood seems to lag behind."

records.jp: 普通になる。普通の女に。
records.en: it will become normal. A normal female.
comments: This is not good thing, considering Tomoki and Sakuraba are "normal", which is what World Aphasic Miyuki looked like. -GHS
records.assessment: The metaphor says that she will become an ordinary woman. Calling her 'a normal female' is a dehumanizing biological label unsupported by the Japanese register.

highlights.text: it will become normal. A normal female.

records.jp: 「うん、で？」
records.en: Taichi: "Yes, therefore?"
records.assessment: うん、で means 'Yes, and?' or 'Go on.' 'Therefore?' incorrectly asks for a conclusion.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yes, therefore?"

records.jp: 「ふぅん。で、その残血というのは……」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh. Then, there's residual blood..."
records.assessment: Taichi asks what Kiri means by 'remaining blood.' The English turns this into a declarative statement that residual blood exists.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh. Then, there's residual blood..."

records.jp: 「……なにを……しようと……？」
records.en: Kiri: "...what are you... doing...?"
records.assessment: Kiri asks what he intends or is about to do. 'What are you doing?' asks about a present ongoing action.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...what are you... doing...?"

records.jp: 今まで浮かんでいた薄笑いを、すっと消した。
records.en: The faint smile that I was making up until now vanished, suddenly.
records.assessment: Taichi deliberately wipes the faint smile from his face. The English makes the smile vanish on its own.

highlights.text: The faint smile that I was making up until now vanished, suddenly.

records.jp: 葛藤と呼ぶべきものはある。
records.en: There is something here that ought be called 'conflicted',
records.assessment: The noun is an internal conflict. The English says something should be called the adjective 'conflicted.'

highlights.text: There is something here that ought be called 'conflicted',

records.jp: だが抵抗する理性は、はりぼてにも劣る。
records.en: however, the opposition of rationality is less than papier mache.
records.assessment: His reason, which should resist the impulse, is flimsier than a papier-mache prop. 'The opposition of rationality' instead suggests opposition directed against reason.

highlights.text: however, the opposition of rationality is less than papier mache.

records.jp: 役不足もいいところだ。
records.en: At best it could be said to be the dissatisfaction with one's lot in life.
comments: See CCX0001. People who do this obtain only archery targets, which is why he's a pin cushion for Kiri. -GHS
records.assessment: In context, 役不足もいいところ says that his reason is utterly unequal to its assigned task. The English gives an unrelated dictionary-like notion of dissatisfaction with one's lot.

highlights.text: At best it could be said to be the dissatisfaction with one's lot in life.

records.jp: うかつに触れたら、指紋がついてしまいそうだったからだ。
records.en: Because if it is touched thoughtlessly, I may just leave fingerprints.
records.assessment: Taichi explains that he refrained because he might leave fingerprints if he carelessly touched her. The English uses a passive condition and leaves the touching actor unspecified.

highlights.text: Because if it is touched thoughtlessly, I may just leave fingerprints.

records.jp: 「その股ぐらから垂れているのが、そうなのかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "that's what's trickling down from the area between the legs, isn't it?
comments: See CCC0000 -GHS
records.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation mark but does not close it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "that's what's trickling down from the area between the legs, isn't it?

records.jp: 緊張で感覚が麻痺しているらしい。
records.en: Her senses seem to be paralized by mental strain.
comments: See CCC3019A. Is it just Taichi that's imagining stuff? -GHS
records.assessment: 'Paralized' is misspelled; the standard form is 'paralyzed.'

highlights.text: Her senses seem to be paralized by mental strain.

records.jp: 一滴の生み出す、刹那の造形。
records.en: An instant of a shape created by a single drop.
comments: Just google the term. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese calls the milk crown a fleeting form created by one drop. 'An instant of a shape' is not a valid English noun phrase for a momentary shape.

highlights.text: An instant of a shape created by a single drop.

records.jp: ガラス細工の霧もまた、砕ける一瞬がもっとも。
records.en: Even more for the glasswork that is Kiri, that like it would pulverize in an instant. Appropriate.
comments: The time loop is the image of the Broadcast Club at moment of shattering. This may be read as nasty, but if it exists at that moment of shattering, then it won't vanish completely. People can't be still pictures, however, as he knows from Touko - and as he's restated just last script, seeing Touko being repeated is something horrible. Whether she's dead or just sitting day after day, week after week, in her classroom, refusing everything, until she's so debilitated she has to be cared for by a doctor. -GHS
records.assessment: The thought says that for glasswork Kiri too, the instant when she shatters is the most—, trailing into the next line. The English is ungrammatical and substitutes 'appropriate' for the superlative もっとも.

highlights.text: Even more for the glasswork that is Kiri, that like it would pulverize in an instant. Appropriate.

records.jp: もっとも―――
records.en: Appropriate---
records.assessment: もっとも continues the interrupted superlative, 'the most—.' 'Appropriate' is a different word and breaks the deliberate repetition.

highlights.text: Appropriate---

records.jp: 太ももに触れる。
records.en: Touch on the thighs.
comments: I object to the use of the kanji 太 to describe Kiri's thighs. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi touches Kiri's thigh. 'Touch on the thighs' omits the actor and changes the singular body part to plural.

highlights.text: Touch on the thighs.

records.jp: ぐいと体内に押し込む。
records.en: Squeeze and they would push inside the body.
comments: Toss a rock at it, nothing. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi presses his fingertips firmly into her body. The English changes the actual action into a hypothetical result, 'would push,' and leaves the agent unclear.

highlights.text: Squeeze and they would push inside the body.

records.jp: 血に触れる。
records.en: Touch on the blood.
records.assessment: The narrator touches the blood. 'Touch on the blood' is an agentless noun fragment.

highlights.text: Touch on the blood.

records.jp: どろりとしていて、まるで精液だ。
records.en: Muddy, and gooey, just like semen.
records.assessment: The blood is thick and gooey. 'Muddy' adds dirt or sediment not present in どろり.

highlights.text: Muddy, and gooey, just like semen.

records.jp: 「一匹はどこかに歩いていって、野良犬に食い殺される。苦しみは少ないかもしれない。ただ生きてきた意義は、老い先短いだろう野良犬の一食」
records.en: Taichi: "One strolled off somewhere, and got eaten by a stray dog. He may not have suffered much, but who knows. Just, that the meaning of his life was to be a single day's meal for a stray dog with only a few years left."
comments: Five cats, plus the mother and dog = 7 -GHS
records.assessment: The kitten's life's meaning is reduced to one meal for the dog. The English changes one meal into 'a single day's meal.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "One strolled off somewhere, and got eaten by a stray dog. He may not have suffered much, but who knows. Just, that the meaning of his life was to be a single day's meal for a stray dog with only a few years left."

records.jp: ひどい汗。
records.en: Horribly sweaty,
records.assessment: The Japanese notes an awful amount of sweat. 'Horribly sweaty' is an adjective fragment with no subject.

highlights.text: Horribly sweaty,

records.jp: 霧の視点は指先に結ばれている。
records.en: Kiri's sight focuses tight on the fingertips.
records.assessment: Kiri's gaze is fixed on his fingertips. 'Sight focuses tight' is an unnatural collocation.

highlights.text: Kiri's sight focuses tight on the fingertips.

records.jp: 「……車に轢かれて死ぬんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "...it got struck by a car and died!"
comments: See CCC3003, same kanji. Hmmm, is this the truth of the Hasekura Massacre? -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi narrates the remaining kitten's fate in the story's present: it gets run over and dies. The English shifts to past tense.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...it got struck by a car and died!"

records.jp: 「子猫だったら一瞬でぺたんこだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Being a kitten, it got flattened in a second."
records.assessment: He says that a kitten would be flattened instantly. The English presents this hypothetical consequence as a completed past event.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Being a kitten, it got flattened in a second."

records.jp: 「そんな死なんだぜ？」
records.en: Taichi: "What the hell is up with a death like that?!"
records.assessment: Taichi states that this is the kind of death it is. The English turns the observation into the angry question 'What the hell is up with a death like that?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "What the hell is up with a death like that?!"

records.jp: 「そんなことが、今までどれだけ繰り返されたんだ？」
records.en: Taichi: "And how many times has this repeated, over and over up, until this moment?"
records.assessment: 'Repeated, over and over up, until' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And how many times has this repeated, over and over up, until this moment?"

records.jp: 「……舐めて。そら……そう、いい子だね」
records.en: Taichi: "...lick. C'mon... like that, nice girl aren't you."
comments: See CCC3012A. He's replaying that same scene. -GHS
records.assessment: The praise requires punctuation around the address or tag. 'Nice girl aren't you' is malformed as written.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...lick. C'mon... like that, nice girl aren't you."

records.jp: 「世の中は苦痛とかさ、不幸とか、そういうもので満ちてて……」
records.en: Taichi: "Society is agony, it's sorrow, it's full of those things..."
records.assessment: The world is filled with pain, misfortune, and such things. The English substitutes society and makes society itself equal to agony and sorrow before saying it is full of them.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Society is agony, it's sorrow, it's full of those things..."

records.jp: 「すごく不安になるんだよな」
records.en: Taichi: "There is so much to be in anxiety about."
records.assessment: Those conditions make Taichi terribly anxious. 'There is so much to be in anxiety about' removes the direct causal feeling and is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There is so much to be in anxiety about."

records.jp: 「だから繋がりたい。一刻もはやく、一時でも長く」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore, the desire to connect. As quickly as possible, that to bear even the length of an hour is impossible."
comments: Yeah, well, he rhymed 'yaku' with 'nagaku', so he started it. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi wants to connect as soon as possible and for as long as possible, even a moment longer. The English instead says that bearing even an hour is impossible.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore, the desire to connect. As quickly as possible, that to bear even the length of an hour is impossible."

records.jp: 「本当の孤独もしらない、普通に生きるための心もすでに手に入れてる」
records.en: Taichi: "The heart and the mind to live normally are just put into their hands, so that they don't know true loneliness."
comments: MY EXISTENCE IS! DARKNESS!!! damn my white hair!!! It is crawling in the skin, such wounds don't seem to heal? ing -GHS
records.assessment: The people both do not know true loneliness and already possess the heart needed to live normally. The English makes the second fact a means or cause so that they do not know loneliness.

highlights.text: Taichi: "The heart and the mind to live normally are just put into their hands, so that they don't know true loneliness."

records.jp: 「遠い世界であるうちはいいんだけど……近寄ってきて、俺たちを食い物にしようとするだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "They can stay in this distant world fine, but... wouldn't they come close, and they try to make prey of us, use us as food?"
comments: Now the "normal" people are the one who come in and try to break the "deviant" ones... then again, see Yutaka's death: no one cared. In fact, Kiri's parents were more relieved than Taichi, Yutaka's own victim. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says they draw near and try to prey on people like Taichi. 'Wouldn't they come close, and they try' mixes a hypothetical question with a finite assertion.

highlights.text: Taichi: "They can stay in this distant world fine, but... wouldn't they come close, and they try to make prey of us, use us as food?"

records.jp: 顔を近づけて言う。
records.en: So I say as my head comes closer.
records.assessment: Taichi brings his face close, not merely his head as an anatomical object.

highlights.text: So I say as my head comes closer.

records.jp: 「自分で言ってたろ。世界が恐いって」
records.en: Taichi: "You've said it yourself. The world is frightening."
comments: See CCC3007 -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri herself said that the world scares her. 'The world is frightening' changes her personal fear into an objective description.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You've said it yourself. The world is frightening."

records.jp: 「俺たちのためのいいものなんて、何一つ残ってない」
records.en: Taichi: "Good things left behind for our sake, not one."
records.assessment: Not one good thing for people like them remains. The English is a verb-less inversion, 'Good things left behind ... not one.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Good things left behind for our sake, not one."

records.jp: 「でも、生きたいじゃないか……なあ？」
records.en: Taichi: "But you still want to live don't you... well?"
records.assessment: Taichi says 'But we want to live, don't we?' The English changes the inclusive plural into singular 'you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But you still want to live don't you... well?"

records.jp: 重い経血。
records.en: Hard menstrual blooding,
comments: Should relate to the term she used to define her menses. LOL PS2 version at this point speaking of Taichi being "like a vampire", when it's avoided every single reference to Kiri's menstruation so far. -GHS
records.assessment: 重い経血 means heavy menstrual blood or bleeding. 'Hard menstrual blooding' uses the wrong adjective and a nonexistent noun.

highlights.text: Hard menstrual blooding,

records.jp: 舌を当てた。
records.en: Tongue contacted.
records.assessment: Taichi applies his tongue. 'Tongue contacted' lacks an article, actor, and object and makes contact sound intransitive.

highlights.text: Tongue contacted.

records.jp: 哀れなほど震える下肢を、両腕で抱え込む。
records.en: Lower limbs tremble, pitifully, so I embrace them with both arms.
records.assessment: Taichi wraps both arms around her pitifully trembling legs. The English makes the trembling legs the opening subject, then uses 'so' as though their trembling causes his action.

highlights.text: Lower limbs tremble, pitifully, so I embrace them with both arms.

records.jp: 脚をつたって、付け根に達する。
records.en: Following along the leg, I reach their root.
records.assessment: He follows her leg to the groin. 'Their root' gives a plural pronoun an unclear antecedent and literalizes 付け根.

highlights.text: Following along the leg, I reach their root.

records.jp: 下着はもうダメになっていた。
records.en: Underwear were already a mess.
records.assessment: 'Underwear' is singular or mass in this construction and requires 'was,' not 'were.'

highlights.text: Underwear were already a mess.

records.jp: それは本格的に憎悪するための下準備。
records.en: That is the preliminary preparation for the full-scale hatred.
records.assessment: The natural phrase is preparation for full-blown hatred. 'The preliminary preparation for the full-scale hatred' is redundant and misuses the definite article.

highlights.text: That is the preliminary preparation for the full-scale hatred.

records.jp: 憎めばいいさ。
records.en: Hatred's no problem, you know.
records.assessment: Taichi tells Kiri that she may go ahead and hate him. 'Hatred's no problem' removes the hating subject, the hated object, and the permission.

highlights.text: Hatred's no problem, you know.

records.jp: どうせ俺たち固有の尊厳は、週末とともに全部なかったことにされるんだからな。
records.en: Because whatever happens, our personal dignity will made to be no more along with everything else at the end of the week.
comments: I tried 'eigendignity', but then I woke up and my pillow was gone, and I'm still too puzzled at how things could get mixed in this way to use it. Anyway, this pisses him off sooo much. -GHS
records.assessment: Their individual dignity will be erased as though it never existed at week's end. The English adds 'whatever happens' and has the ungrammatical auxiliary 'will made.'

highlights.text: Because whatever happens, our personal dignity will made to be no more along with everything else at the end of the week.

records.jp: 上体を傾けて、壁に押しつけていく。
records.en: She inclines her upper body, pushing into the wall.
comments: Now see CCC3012B. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi leans Kiri's upper body and presses her against the wall. The English makes Kiri independently incline and push herself.

highlights.text: She inclines her upper body, pushing into the wall.

records.jp: ののしる言葉が嬌声のよう。
records.en: Words of abuse are like flirting.
records.assessment: 嬌声 is an erotic cry or moan. 'Flirting' is social behavior and not a kind of voice.

highlights.text: Words of abuse are like flirting.

records.jp: 俺は下半身を露出させ、密着していく。
records.en: I expose her lower half, and put myself in close contact to it.
records.assessment: Taichi exposes his own lower body. The English says that he exposes Kiri's lower half.

highlights.text: I expose her lower half, and put myself in close contact to it.

records.jp: 缶が回転しながら飛んでいる。
records.en: Cans were flying in, spinning.
records.assessment: The line observes one can spinning through the air; the following units separately count two. The English prematurely changes this unit to plural 'Cans.'

highlights.text: Cans were flying in, spinning.

records.jp: その光景はひどくスローモーに見えた。
records.en: An event that I saw in terrifying slow-motion.
records.assessment: The scene appears extremely slow, not terrifying. ひどく modifies degree here, while the English turns it into emotional terror.

highlights.text: An event that I saw in terrifying slow-motion.

records.jp: 缶は飛ばない。誰かが投げた。誰が？　今考える必要はない。投げる。意図。意図を持って投げた。目的は？　缶を投げることによって期待できる効果。投げた缶が効果を発揮。
records.en: Cans do not fly. Somebody threw it.
comments: HACK splits as in the console version. This is too busy for a single screen after all. -GHS
records.assessment: After noting that cans do not fly and someone threw them, the Japanese continues through a rapid chain of questions about actor, intent, purpose, and expected effect. The English omits nearly the entire unit.

highlights.text: Cans do not fly. Somebody threw it.

records.jp: 炸裂？　投擲する武器？　手榴弾等。狭い室内。破壊力増。死？　死。死。範囲攻撃。回避不可能。位置関係。俺は確実に死。俺は死。確定。
records.en: Explosion? Thrown ordinance? Hand grenade type. Confined space. Destructive power multiplier.
comments: HACK same, split -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese continues after destructive power through death, range, impossibility of evasion, relative positions, and repeated certainty that Taichi will die. The English stops after the first five fragments and omits the rest.

highlights.text: Explosion? Thrown ordinance? Hand grenade type. Confined space. Destructive power multiplier.

records.jp: 霧の耳を押さえるようにして、頭部を抱きかかえた。
records.en: To pin down Kiri's ears I hugged her head.
comments: That would save her from the flashbang entirely. Well, except for the actual explosion which would bounce off the wall and tear them to shred even if it's a flashbang. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi cradles Kiri's head while covering her ears. 'Pin down Kiri's ears' suggests restraining or crushing them rather than shielding them.

highlights.text: To pin down Kiri's ears I hugged her head.

records.jp: 可愛いな、霧は。
records.en: Cute inn'she, Kiri.
records.assessment: The English tag 'inn'she' is nonstandard eye dialect unsupported by the Japanese and is grammatically malformed.

highlights.text: Cute inn'she, Kiri.

records.jp: そしてソレは弾けた。
records.en: And then the things exploded. Both simultaneously.
comments: YOU FOOL -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese singular ソレ says that it burst or detonated. The English changes it to plural things and adds that both exploded simultaneously.

highlights.text: And then the things exploded. Both simultaneously.

records.jp: 眼が灼かれた。
records.en: Eyes were burning.
comments: ...but his eyes were closed, and he wasn't looking at the damn thing... -GHS
records.assessment: His eyes have been seared by the flash. 'Were burning' describes an ongoing sensation rather than damage inflicted on them.

highlights.text: Eyes were burning.

records.jp: 耳が麻痺した。
records.en: Hearing was dimmed.
records.assessment: His ears or hearing have gone numb. 'Hearing was dimmed' uses a visual metaphor and suggests only reduced volume.

highlights.text: Hearing was dimmed.

records.jp: 違和感をおぼえる。
records.en: I learn of this sense of physical discomfort.
comments: Specific term. Kiri, being held tight, couldn't see or feel anything... even if the explosion should've killed them both. See CCC3012A, it was the same but less obvious there. -GHS
records.assessment: 違和感をおぼえる means that Taichi notices or feels that something is off. 'I learn of this sense of physical discomfort' is a literal and inaccurate construction.

highlights.text: I learn of this sense of physical discomfort.

records.jp: やっと舌がまわるようになった。
records.en: My tongue had barely gotten capable of functioning.
records.assessment: At last his tongue starts working again. 'Had barely gotten capable' means only just or with difficulty, not finally after impairment.

highlights.text: My tongue had barely gotten capable of functioning.

records.jp: 「フラッシュ……爆弾？」
records.en: taichi: "Flash... a bomb?"
records.assessment: The speaker label is incorrectly lowercased as 'taichi.'

highlights.text: taichi: "Flash... a bomb?"

records.jp: どこかで見た缶だと思ったら。
records.en: I was thinking I had seen that thing somewhere.
records.assessment: Taichi realizes that this explains why the cans looked familiar. The English reports only that he had been thinking he saw the thing somewhere and loses the realization.

highlights.text: I was thinking I had seen that thing somewhere.

records.jp: 「……昔の……アレかぁ」
records.en: Taichi: "...that was... from that time."
records.assessment: 昔のアレ refers to that thing or incident from long ago. 'From that time' identifies only a time and omits the remembered referent.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...that was... from that time."

records.jp: 可愛らしく、微笑した。
records.en: She made an adorable smile.
records.assessment: She smiles charmingly. 'Made an adorable smile' is a literal and unnatural collocation.

highlights.text: She made an adorable smile.

records.jp: 彼女との思い出話は、こんなものばかりだ。
records.en: Reminiscing with her is always like this.
records.assessment: His memories involving Youko are all stories like this. 'Reminiscing with her' describes a joint act of recollection, not the content of memories.

highlights.text: Reminiscing with her is always like this.

records.jp: 「理性は……取り戻せた？」
records.en: Youko: "Rationality... returned yet?"
records.assessment: Youko asks whether he has regained his reason. 'Rationality returned yet?' omits the subject and auxiliary.

highlights.text: Youko: "Rationality... returned yet?"

records.jp: そう、俺の危機だから助けてくれたわけじゃない。
records.en: no, this is not about rescuing me from emergency at all.
records.assessment: He realizes that Youko did not save him because he was in danger. The English impersonalizes the rescuer and uses the malformed phrase 'from emergency.'

highlights.text: no, this is not about rescuing me from emergency at all.

records.jp: 「……必要よ」
records.en: Youko: "...do need!"
records.assessment: Youko says 'I need you.' The English 'do need' omits both the subject and the needed object.

highlights.text: Youko: "...do need!"

records.jp: 「俺は半分なんかじゃないよ」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm not half of anything!"
records.assessment: Taichi rejects being merely one half of Youko's proposed whole. 'I'm not half of anything' denies a broader and different relation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm not half of anything!"

records.jp: 抵抗は……しなかった。
records.en: Resistance... I hadn't any.
comments: See CCC0000. Might's well CP the entire script. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he did not resist. 'Resistance I hadn't any' is ungrammatical pseudo-archaic inversion.

highlights.text: Resistance... I hadn't any.

records.jp: 「……少し汗くさかった」
records.en: Youko: "...I smelled some sweat."
comments: So did he smell her. Which is continuously absurd: flashbangs, as explosives, shouldn't be odorless. -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says that Taichi or his uniform smelled a little sweaty. 'I smelled some sweat' instead says that Youko perceived an odor, not that he emitted it.

highlights.text: Youko: "...I smelled some sweat."

records.jp: 無表情に呆れる。
records.en: Expressionless disgust.
records.assessment: Youko is exasperated without changing expression. 'Expressionless disgust' is a noun fragment and makes the reaction stronger and different.

highlights.text: Expressionless disgust.

records.jp: 「……ばっちぃ」
records.en: Youko: "...pigpen."
comments: It's just a kiddy word for 'dirty', but there's nothing quite equivalent. This half-reminder of CCA0009, half-Peanuts reference should do. -GHS
records.assessment: ばっちぃ means dirty or gross. 'Pigpen' calls someone a dirty place or character instead of giving the adjective.

highlights.text: Youko: "...pigpen."

records.jp: 「じゃー離れてくれていいよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Welll, then it's fine if we stay apart!"
records.assessment: Taichi says that she may let go of him, referring to immediate physical contact. The English changes this into the plural future state 'we stay apart.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Welll, then it's fine if we stay apart!"

records.jp: 無表情に悲しげになる。
records.en: Expressionless saddening.
records.assessment: Youko becomes or looks sad while remaining expressionless. 'Expressionless saddening' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text: Expressionless saddening.

records.jp: 「だいたい冬子だって毎日同じ服着てたじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "And anyway, doesn't Touko wear the same clothes every day now?"
comments: And his first thought remains to Touko. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that Touko too used to wear the same clothes every day. The English puts her action in the present and adds 'now.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And anyway, doesn't Touko wear the same clothes every day now?"

records.jp: 「……憎しみにとらわれていて、太一にとって危険だもの」
records.en: Youko: "...she is a prisoner of hatred, she is something dangerous to Taichi."
records.assessment: Youko says that Kiri is dangerous to Taichi. 'She is something dangerous' is ungrammatical and needlessly dehumanizing.

highlights.text: Youko: "...she is a prisoner of hatred, she is something dangerous to Taichi."

records.jp: 「なにをいまさら」
records.en: Kiri: "Why even at this point."
records.assessment: なにをいまさら dismisses the objection as too late now. 'Why even at this point' is an incomplete question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Why even at this point."

records.jp: 「どう言い訳していいものかわからないけど……」
records.en: Taichi: "I have no I idea how I could possibly explain this, but..."
records.assessment: The English contains the duplicated phrase 'no I idea.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I have no I idea how I could possibly explain this, but..."

records.jp: 応援団なみの謝りっぷりだと自画自賛。
records.en: A quality of apology on par with a cheering squad, if I may boast.
records.assessment: Taichi praises his own apology as being delivered like a cheering squad. 'A quality of apology' is an unnatural nominal calque.

highlights.text: A quality of apology on par with a cheering squad, if I may boast.

records.jp: 「なんですか、それ……なんなんですか、あなたは？」
records.en: Kiri: "Just what was that... what, just what are you?"
comments: ...not "what are you two"... -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri asks what the just-delivered apology is. 'What was that' incorrectly shifts the immediate question into past tense.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Just what was that... what, just what are you?"

records.jp: 乱れた胸元を抱えて、歩み去る。
records.en: Holding down the disheveled pit of her stomach, she walks away.
records.assessment: 胸元 is her disheveled chest, neckline, or front of her clothes. 'Pit of her stomach' identifies a different body area.

highlights.text: Holding down the disheveled pit of her stomach, she walks away.

records.jp: 黙殺。
records.en: Killer silence.
comments: Visuals -GHS
records.assessment: 黙殺 means that Kiri completely ignores him. 'Killer silence' is a literal wordplay invention and does not state the deliberate ignoring.

highlights.text: Killer silence.

records.jp: 「……太一……のめりこみすぎ」
records.en: Youko: "...Taichi... got completely absorbed in that."
comments: Likely in love. -GHS
records.assessment: Youko directly tells Taichi that he got too carried away. The English refers to him in third person and adds 'in that' as an external summary.

highlights.text: Youko: "...Taichi... got completely absorbed in that."

records.jp: 追いかけようとすると、背後から声がかかった。
records.en: As I go to follow her, I am called from behind.
records.assessment: Taichi tries or starts to pursue Kiri when a voice stops him. 'As I go to follow her' treats the pursuit as already underway.

highlights.text: As I go to follow her, I am called from behind.

records.jp: 「日記の情報量を増やすためにも、いろいろするべきだ」
records.en: Taichi: "And for the sake of increasing the amount of information in the diaries, I ought do all kind of things."
comments: Objection! Why would he increase the amount of information in the diaries if his eigentime is then meaningless? Conversely, if he can increase the amount of information in the diaries, how is his eigentime meaningless? -GHS
records.assessment: The phrase requires 'all kinds of things,' not singular 'all kind of things.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And for the sake of increasing the amount of information in the diaries, I ought do all kind of things."

records.jp: 「それだけで動いているなら確かに……けど太一のは違う」
records.en: Youko: "If this happened just because of that certainly... but Taichi is wrong here."
records.assessment: Youko says that if increasing the diary's information is Taichi's sole motive, his claim would be valid, but his actual motive is different. The English instead says an event happened for that reason and that Taichi himself is wrong.

highlights.text: Youko: "If this happened just because of that certainly... but Taichi is wrong here."

records.jp: 「死ぬまで、君とだけ向かいあって暮らせとでも？」
records.en: Taichi: "You say I should be living opposite of you alone, until death?"
comments: Opposite as in face to face... or as in opposed, ambiguous. See CCC3030, which clarifies this somewhat. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether he is supposed to live facing only Youko until death. 'Living opposite of you alone' suggests opposition or a house across from hers and misplaces 'only.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You say I should be living opposite of you alone, until death?"

records.jp: 「小さな輪の中で、ずっと……」
records.en: Taichi: "Inside a tiny circle of friends, forever..."
comments: Extremely ambiguous too. It's likely about cutting off oneself from others emotionally, not simply away from the rest. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says only 'inside a small circle.' Adding 'of friends' fixes the circle's membership without support.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Inside a tiny circle of friends, forever..."

records.jp: 「……普通で何が悪いんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "...what's wrong with the normal now."
records.assessment: Taichi asks what is wrong with being normal. 'What's wrong with the normal now' is ungrammatical and treats normality as a definite object.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...what's wrong with the normal now."

records.jp: 「彼女たちは、一時の玩具にしかならないのに」
records.en: Youko: "For those girls cannot possibly become more than temporary playthings."
records.assessment: The declarative sentence is incorrectly introduced by the dangling conjunction 'For.'

highlights.text: Youko: "For those girls cannot possibly become more than temporary playthings."

records.jp: さっきのように。
records.en: Just like it was long ago.
records.assessment: さっき means just now or a moment ago. 'Long ago' places the comparison in the distant past.

highlights.text: Just like it was long ago.

records.jp: 「今週は好きにさせてもらうよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Let me do whatever I like this week."
records.assessment: Taichi asserts that he will do as he likes this week. 'Let me do' changes the declaration into a request for permission.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Let me do whatever I like this week."

records.jp: 「もう今日は帰っていいから」
records.en: Taichi: "You should just go home for the day."
records.assessment: Taichi says that Youko may go home now, dismissing her. 'Should go home' changes permission or dismissal into advice or obligation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You should just go home for the day."

records.jp: 「固有の私の願望は、次週のそれとは別物で」
records.en: Youko: "The desire of my eigenself is... going to be different next week."
comments: Starting after this reset she'll put a chastity belt on Taichi. The problem, of course, is that if these characters are fixed (see CCC0045A), how are their eigenselves different? More importantly, see CCC4022. Youko had no care for eigentime, says Miki. I suspect that, much like the change in CCC3030, this is an intentional contradiction. -GHS
records.assessment: Her present individual desire is a different thing from next week's. 'Is going to be different next week' makes one continuing desire change over time, and 'eigenself' is unsupported jargon.

highlights.text: Youko: "The desire of my eigenself is... going to be different next week."

records.jp: 「私たちは毎週、滅びてる」
records.en: Youko: "Every week we are destroyed."
records.assessment: 滅びる means that each weekly self perishes or ceases to exist. Passive 'are destroyed' introduces an outside destructive agent.

highlights.text: Youko: "Every week we are destroyed."

records.jp: 「個別の滅び。つまり」
records.en: Youko: "Our proprietary is destroyed. In other words,"
records.assessment: 個別の滅び means individual extinction or each person's perishing. 'Our proprietary is destroyed' mistakes an adjective about individuality for commercial ownership and is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Youko: "Our proprietary is destroyed. In other words,"

records.jp: 「他の週にいる私がどうなろうと、知ったことではないけれど……」
records.en: Youko: "What the myselves that live in other weeks will do is something that I do not know, however..."
comments: This sounds, however, like she isn't unreset now... not that it ever mattered, whether she exists or not. -GHS
records.assessment: 知ったことではない means that she does not care what happens to versions of herself in other weeks. The English instead says that she does not know what they will do.

highlights.text: Youko: "What the myselves that live in other weeks will do is something that I do not know, however..."

records.jp: 「さようなら、になるの」
records.en: Youko: "This will become... farewell."
comments: See endings of Sendback. She still views the world as purely materialistic. She wants what she wants, and she wants it forever, and here. No pattern like that exists in the history of the world. -GHS
records.assessment: This will be goodbye. 'Become farewell' is a literal and unnatural predicate.

highlights.text: Youko: "This will become... farewell."

records.jp: 踵を返す。
records.en: She turns away.
records.assessment: 踵を返す is to turn on one's heel. 'Turns away' omits the abrupt physical motion.

highlights.text: She turns away.

records.jp: 背中で語る。
records.en: She speaks from her back.
records.assessment: She speaks with her back turned, not literally 'from her back.'

highlights.text: She speaks from her back.

records.jp: 言葉は重い石となって、胃に落ち込んだ。
records.en: Words that are heavy as stones, that drop straight down to the stomach.
records.assessment: The Japanese is one past-tense metaphor in which the words become a heavy stone and sink into his stomach. The English uses two malformed present-tense relative fragments.

highlights.text: Words that are heavy as stones, that drop straight down to the stomach.

records.jp: 廊下を歩む姿が、芥子粒大になって消えるまで、見送った。
records.en: I watched until the image of her walking down the corridor turned the size of an ant and vanished.
comments: 1) she lets him do that, since she can Kill Her Presence 2) HOW ****ING LONG IS THIS CORRIDOR??? -GHS
records.assessment: 芥子粒 means a mustard seed, emphasizing a tiny distant speck. The English changes it to an ant.

highlights.text: I watched until the image of her walking down the corridor turned the size of an ant and vanished.

records.jp: 二人の線が交錯することは、ないように思えた。
records.en: The lines of these two people seemed like they would never know mixing.
comments: Vs. crossing -GHS
records.assessment: It seemed that the two people's lines would never intersect. 'Would never know mixing' is ungrammatical and changes a geometric crossing into generic mixture.

highlights.text: The lines of these two people seemed like they would never know mixing.

records.jp: なんのために。
records.en: For some purpose.
records.assessment: The narrator asks himself, 'For what?' The English changes this uncertainty into the assertion 'For some purpose.'

highlights.text: For some purpose.

records.jp: 先輩と美希がいた。
records.en: Senpai and Kiri were there.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Senpai and Miki were there. The English substitutes Kiri for Miki.

highlights.text: Senpai and Kiri were there.

records.jp: 友貴たちはまだ戻ってないらしい。
records.en: Tomoki and the other don't seem to have come back yet.
comments: Sakuraba ergo "the other" -GHS
records.assessment: The plural phrase requires 'the others,' not singular 'the other.'

highlights.text: Tomoki and the other don't seem to have come back yet.

records.jp: 「あ、桐原せむぱいはどうでした？」
records.en: Miki: "Ah, how wHas Kirihara-semhpai?"
comments: Bit munched. Don't see the pun, if there's one. -GHS
records.assessment: The English question is corrupted by the string 'how wHas' and the speaker-title string is also misspelled.

highlights.text: Miki: "Ah, how wHas Kirihara-semhpai?"

records.jp: 「俺もだ」
records.en: Taichi: "As I did as well."
records.assessment: 俺もだ is simply 'Me too.' 'As I did as well' has no clear antecedent for 'did.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "As I did as well."

records.jp: 二人で笑う。
records.en: We laugh in a duo.
records.assessment: The two laugh together. 'Laugh in a duo' is an unnatural literal expression.

highlights.text: We laugh in a duo.

records.jp: 「わたくし、先ほどまでみみ先輩と抱き合って半泣きでガタガタ震えていたので、その分進捗遅いです」
records.en: Miki: "This one has been, until recently, tightly hugging Mimi-senpai while half-crying and shaking with rattle and clatter both, and due to that progress has slowed."
comments: Suddenly Taichi-sh. Hum, has she heard any explosion at all? -GHS
records.assessment: Miki was trembling violently. 'Shaking with rattle and clatter both' treats mimetic Japanese as literal external noises.

highlights.text: Miki: "This one has been, until recently, tightly hugging Mimi-senpai while half-crying and shaking with rattle and clatter both, and due to that progress has slowed."

records.jp: 「あれはなんだったのか……正直、トイレに行きたいのですけどこわくて校内に入れません」
records.en: Miki: "But what was that...? Honestly, I wanted to go to the toilet but I was scared and didn't go inside the building."
comments: TL: "I know this happened in the toilet." -GHS
records.assessment: Miki currently needs to use the restroom but is too afraid to enter the building. The English shifts both desire and refusal into the past.

highlights.text: Miki: "But what was that...? Honestly, I wanted to go to the toilet but I was scared and didn't go inside the building."

records.jp: 「うわぁ……悩ましい……」
records.en: Miki: "Bwaaah... disturbing..."
records.assessment: 悩ましい means that Taichi's offer poses a tempting or difficult choice. 'Disturbing' says only that it upsets her.

highlights.text: Miki: "Bwaaah... disturbing..."

records.jp: 「……欠陥商品ですね」
records.en: Miki: "...defective product wasn't it."
records.assessment: Miki calls it a defective product in the present. 'Defective product wasn't it' changes tense and omits the necessary article.

highlights.text: Miki: "...defective product wasn't it."

records.jp: 「テロする人いませんからね」
records.en: Taichi: "There are no more people who would do terror attacks, that is why."
records.assessment: The natural expression is 'people who would commit terrorist attacks.' 'Do terror attacks' uses the wrong verb and article pattern.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There are no more people who would do terror attacks, that is why."

records.jp: 「……つうことで、俺もちょっくら」
records.en: Taichi: "...and in passing, I too, just got to..."
