records.assessment: Taichi says that he too will just be off for a moment. 'And in passing, I too, just got to' uses the wrong transition and tense and never completes its construction.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...and in passing, I too, just got to..."

records.jp: 落ち着いた声音。
records.en: In a calmer tone of voice.
comments: ...was she ever in a panic? See CCA0016. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese describes a calm voice, not one calmer than a previous comparison point.

highlights.text: In a calmer tone of voice.

records.jp: 「いえ、なんでもありません。どちらに？」
records.en: Misato: "No, it is nothing. What are you doing?"
records.assessment: どちらに asks where Taichi is going. 'What are you doing?' asks about his activity rather than destination.

highlights.text: Misato: "No, it is nothing. What are you doing?"

records.jp: 「はあ、霧ちんをちょっと探してきます」
records.en: Taichi: "Sigh, I am trying to search for Kiri-chin."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he will go look for Kiri. 'I am trying to search' changes the prospective action into an awkward ongoing attempt.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sigh, I am trying to search for Kiri-chin."

records.jp: 霧の気配をたどる。
records.en: I follow up on Kiri's presence.
records.assessment: He follows or traces signs of Kiri's presence. 'Follow up on' means to take subsequent action on a matter, not track someone.

highlights.text: I follow up on Kiri's presence.

records.jp: とりあえず話しかける。
records.en: First, get close and talk to her.
comments: Touko. -GHS
records.assessment: For now Taichi calls out to Kiri. The English adds approaching her and changes the narration into an imperative-like infinitive.

highlights.text: First, get close and talk to her.

records.jp: わからない自分が、うとましい。
records.en: And this me who doesn't get it is... unpleasant.
records.assessment: Taichi finds the part of himself that does not know what it wants hateful or repellent. The English merely calls that self 'unpleasant,' removing his self-directed aversion.

highlights.text: And this me who doesn't get it is... unpleasant.

records.jp: 「怒り？」
records.en: Kiri: "Angry?"
records.assessment: 怒り is the noun 'anger.' The English supplies the adjective 'Angry?'

highlights.text: Kiri: "Angry?"

records.jp: 「まいったな」
records.en: Taichi: "Fine, I give up."
records.assessment: まいったな expresses being troubled or at a loss about the situation, not a decision to surrender the project.

highlights.text: Fine, I give up.

records.jp: 知られていた。
records.en: She had known.
records.assessment: The immediate realization is that she knew. The past perfect 'had known' unnecessarily places that knowledge before a different past reference point.

highlights.text: She had known.

records.jp: いけない。
records.en: That cannot be.
records.assessment: いけない here is Taichi's alarmed 'This is bad.' 'That cannot be' instead denies possibility.

highlights.text: That cannot be.

records.jp: 「けど、あなたから関わってきた」
records.en: Kiri: "But... there was involvement from you."
records.assessment: Kiri says that Taichi was the one who approached and involved himself with her. 'There was involvement from you' turns the deliberate action into an impersonal event.

highlights.text: Kiri: "But... there was involvement from you."

records.jp: 霧の双眼には、確信があった。
records.en: Kiri's eyes had confidence in them.
records.assessment: 確信 means firm conviction that her conclusion is true. 'Confidence' ordinarily describes self-assurance.

highlights.text: Kiri's eyes had confidence in them.

records.jp: 「人間の普通なんてどうだっていいんです。あなたはそういうものなんです」
records.en: Kiri: "The normal of people is inconsequential. Because of the kind of thing you are."
records.assessment: Kiri says that human normality is irrelevant and that this is simply the kind of being Taichi is. The English turns the second assertion into a causal fragment beginning 'Because.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "The normal of people is inconsequential. Because of the kind of thing you are."

records.jp: 「……人間の心を食べる、怪物なんです」
records.en: Kiri: "...you devour human hearts, beast that you are."
records.assessment: Kiri explicitly calls Taichi a monster that devours human hearts. 'Beast' loses the unnatural or monstrous being identified by 怪物.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...you devour human hearts, beast that you are."

records.jp: 「あのさ……俺と豊はダチだったんだよ。殺す理由がない」
records.en: Taichi: "Say now... me and Yutaka were buds, weren't we. Got no reason to kill him."
records.assessment: Taichi asserts that Yutaka and he were friends and therefore he had no motive. 'Me and Yutaka were buds, weren't we' is ungrammatical and converts the assertion into a tag question.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Say now... me and Yutaka were buds, weren't we. Got no reason to kill him."

records.jp: 「動機なんて不要です」
records.en: Kiri: "No such thing as a motive needed."
comments: Correction: seven times over. -GHS
records.assessment: The English omits the verb from 'No such thing as a motive needed.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "No such thing as a motive needed."

records.jp: 「餓えに理由なんてない」
records.en: Kiri: "Hunger is the only reason."
records.assessment: Kiri says that hunger has no reason; it operates without a rationale. 'Hunger is the only reason' does the opposite by making hunger the sufficient motive.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Hunger is the only reason."

records.jp: 「じゃあさ、どうしてわざわざ豊を獲物にしないといけなかったわけ？　仮に俺が怪物くんで、他人が獲物だとしても、男よりかは女の子の方がいいような気がするんだけど？」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, why would I go out of my way to intentionally pick Yutaka as game? Let's say that I'm a beast, and that I see other people as game, there's that thing how I prefer girls to men, noticed that?"
comments: He's trying to AVOID having to tell her that her brother was a rapist. Acts, not words. With the ironic consequence that he is wrong to do *this*, not what he'll do later on! -GHS
records.assessment: The English explanation is syntactically broken around 'there's that thing how,' and 'noticed that?' adds a direct challenge not in the Japanese.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then, why would I go out of my way to intentionally pick Yutaka as game? Let's say that I'm a beast, and that I see other people as game, there's that thing how I prefer girls to men, noticed that?"

records.jp: 「あれはだからさー……そのー」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm telling you that's not true... welll,"
comments: 3xl -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi begins to explain the nature of that look or behavior. The English instead flatly denies Kiri's claim as 'that's not true.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm telling you that's not true... welll,"

records.jp: 「……ありませんよ。けど、異質なものくらいはわかります」
records.en: Kiri: "...I do not! But, I understand as far as saying that it is something heterogeneous."
comments: IOW, she's saying it's not Taichi's sexual urges... which are things she knows absolutely nothing about. The girl doesn't even masturbate! Her annoyance at sexual harassment, much like everything, may just be an erroneous reaction to internal movements she doesn't understand. Her hate for Taichi is certainly nothing of the sort. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that she can at least recognize something alien or abnormal. 'I understand as far as saying that it is something heterogeneous' is not intelligible English.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...I do not! But, I understand as far as saying that it is something heterogeneous."

records.jp: そうか、この子。
records.en: She does, this girl here.
records.assessment: Taichi realizes something about this girl's perceptiveness. 'She does' supplies an assertion with no stable antecedent.

highlights.text: She does, this girl here.

records.jp: その目で見るなら、世界が恐いというのもうなずける。
records.en: If seen with eyes like that, I can nod in assent: the world is frightening.
records.assessment: Seen through Kiri's eyes, Taichi can understand why she finds the world frightening. 'If seen with eyes like that' dangles, and 'nod in assent' misstates understanding as agreement.

highlights.text: If seen with eyes like that, I can nod in assent: the world is frightening.

records.jp: 「それが悔しい……」
records.en: Kiri: "That is regrettable..."
records.assessment: 悔しい describes the mortification or frustration of having lowered her guard. 'Regrettable' is detached and much weaker.

highlights.text: Kiri: "That is regrettable..."

records.jp: 「それであなたの正体がわかりました」
records.en: Kiri: "that is how I understood your true shape."
records.assessment: 正体 is Taichi's true nature or identity. 'True shape' literalizes the characters and suggests physical form.

highlights.text: Kiri: "that is how I understood your true shape."

records.jp: 霧は窓の外に手を垂らした。
records.en: Kiri sank her hand outside of the window,
comments: Third floor at Suicidal Psychopath High (see the rooftop), and the window has no bars and is not locked. It's so damn blatant I'm not even sure this isn't a plot hole. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri lowers or dangles her hand outside the window. 'Sank her hand' describes submersion or downward penetration.

highlights.text: Kiri sank her hand outside of the window,

records.jp: 引き上げる。
records.en: dragging up,
records.assessment: Kiri pulls the hidden object up. The English gerund 'dragging up' has no subject and attaches awkwardly to her unfinished dialogue.

highlights.text: dragging up,

records.jp: 二つ目……つまり美希の分だったわけだ。
records.en: A second one... in other words, Miki also had one for herself.
records.assessment: The second weapon had evidently been intended as Miki's share. 'Miki also had one for herself' instead asserts prior possession and personal use.

highlights.text: A second one... in other words, Miki also had one for herself.

records.jp: 尊く、自分さえ保っていてくれるなら。
records.en: If I can just maintain my most sacred of selves.
comments: (He's not referring to split personalities here, just his behaviors.) -GHS
records.assessment: The reflection concerns people preserving their own noble selves. The English makes Taichi preserve 'my most sacred of selves,' shifting both possessor and construction.

highlights.text: If I can just maintain my most sacred of selves.

records.jp: 人は人を求めるものだけど。
records.en: People are the one thing people seek, however,
records.assessment: The Japanese says that people seek other people. 'People are the one thing people seek' adds exclusivity.

highlights.text: People are the one thing people seek, however,

records.jp: 自己を相手に仮託したら、おしまいだ。
records.en: if the partner is just used a pretext for the self, it's all over.
comments: Meaning the other side seems to become all-important, but it's just projecting the self on them. See CCC3012A for the most described example on Youko. -GHS
records.assessment: Projecting or entrusting the self onto another person is ruinous. The English instead says that the partner is used as a pretext for the self.

highlights.text: if the partner is just used a pretext for the self, it's all over.

records.jp: そうなる前に、距離を取るしかないじゃないか。
records.en: But before that happens, wouldn't you inevitably keep your distance?
comments: Youko is the easiest example again, though this deals more with isolation in general. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that before reaching that point, he has no choice but to keep his distance. The English turns necessity into a generalized rhetorical question addressed to 'you.'

highlights.text: But before that happens, wouldn't you inevitably keep your distance?

records.jp: 霧が練習していた、木との距離と重なる。
records.en: This distance and the distance with the tree Kiri practiced with overlap.
records.assessment: The distance matches the distance to the tree at which Kiri practiced. 'The distance with the tree ... overlap' is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: This distance and the distance with the tree Kiri practiced with overlap.

records.jp: 「だって、どっちにしろ世界はもう終わりなんですから」
records.en: Kiri: "Because either way the world has already ended."
records.assessment: Kiri says that the world will end anyway. The English says that it has already ended.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Because either way the world has already ended."

records.jp: 「君の嫌いな人はいないのに」
records.en: Taichi: "But the people you hate aren't anymore."
records.assessment: Taichi says that none of the people Kiri hates are present. 'The people you hate aren't anymore' omits the predicate required to express their absence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But the people you hate aren't anymore."

records.jp: 「……いなければいいというものじゃないです」
records.en: Kiri: "...this was never about wishing them to be gone."
comments: Meaning they're not necessarily gone... -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that their absence alone does not make matters right. The English changes this into a denial that she wished them gone.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...this was never about wishing them to be gone."

records.jp: 結晶化し、小さな霧を取り巻く文目となって、彩る。
records.en: It crystallizes, and becomes a tiny design that surrounds Kiri, coloring her.
comments: Is that you, 綾? -GHS
records.assessment: The crystallized intent becomes a pattern surrounding little Kiri and adorns her. The English makes the design itself tiny rather than Kiri.

highlights.text: It crystallizes, and becomes a tiny design that surrounds Kiri, coloring her.

records.jp: 思い出さえあれば、その輝かしい宝石さえあれば―――
records.en: If there's even just memories, if there's even just those shining jewels---
records.assessment: 'Memories' is plural and requires 'there are,' not 'there's.'

highlights.text: If there's even just memories, if there's even just those shining jewels---

records.jp: ……俺は、本当に人の気持ちをエサにして生きる怪物かも知れない。
records.en: ...I might just be a beast that makes food of people's feelings, I don't know.
records.assessment: Taichi may be a monster that feeds on human feelings. 'A beast that makes food of people's feelings' is a literal and unnatural construction.

highlights.text: ...I might just be a beast that makes food of people's feelings, I don't know.

records.jp: 人を殺すことが恐い。
records.en: Murder is frightening.
records.assessment: Kiri is afraid of killing a person. 'Murder is frightening' converts her personal fear of committing the act into a general observation.

highlights.text: Murder is frightening.

records.jp: 死んでやろうかとも思う。
records.en: And also the thought, shouldn't you just die you bastard?
comments: 死んでやろう -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi considers letting himself die or letting Kiri kill him. The English turns this into a second-person insult telling someone else to die.

highlights.text: And also the thought, shouldn't you just die you bastard?

records.jp: 「……豊の脚のことを責めたり……いろいろです」
records.en: Kiri: "...by picking on Yutaka's legs maybe... there's so many ways!"
comments: Soooooooo obviously reaching. Does she really think Yutaka'd kill himself on being teased? How stupid and weak does she think he is?! See CCA0011C: Yutaka's legs are the last of his problems, he'll happily make fun of them in a way that Taichi just can't do about his hair, see CCA3022. And so, if that's what she thinks he did, it stands that she'd do the same to him. Since he can't stand it, that may be what getting shot with the crossbow means. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri accuses Taichi of attacking Yutaka over his injured leg or condition. 'Picking on Yutaka's legs' changes the singular issue and trivializes the accusation.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...by picking on Yutaka's legs maybe... there's so many ways!"

records.jp: 変わらず、手は震えている。
records.en: Her hand was shaking, unchangingly.
records.assessment: Her hand continues to tremble. 'Was shaking, unchangingly' is an unnatural literalization of 変わらず.

highlights.text: Her hand was shaking, unchangingly.

records.jp: 殺す前に、自分がまいってしまいそうだった。
records.en: It seemed the self would give up just before murder.
comments: He's talking about her... or is he? -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri looks close to collapsing before she can kill him. 'The self would give up just before murder' loses Kiri as subject and misreads まいる.

highlights.text: It seemed the self would give up just before murder.

records.jp: 黙殺。
records.en: Killer silence.
comments: CP CCC3022 -GHS
records.assessment: 黙殺 again means that Kiri ignores the suggestion completely. 'Killer silence' does not express the intentional refusal to respond.

highlights.text: Killer silence.

records.jp: 「大富豪ってやつだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Those guys were multi-billionaires."
records.assessment: 大富豪 means an immensely wealthy family or magnates. 'Multi-billionaires' asserts a specific modern wealth threshold absent from the source.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Those guys were multi-billionaires."

records.jp: 「そこに住み込みで働く、母親の遠縁にあたる管理人夫妻にね」
records.en: Taichi: "I was a live-in worker there, for a manager and his wife who were distant relatives of mother's."
records.assessment: The live-in workers were the caretaker couple, distant relatives of Taichi's mother, who took him in. The English wrongly makes Taichi the worker.

highlights.text: I was a live-in worker there

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃんはそこの末娘だった」
records.en: Taichi: "Youko-chan was the youngest girl there."
records.assessment: 曜子 is the household's youngest daughter. 'Youngest girl there' loses the family relationship and could refer to age among staff or guests.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Youko-chan was the youngest girl there."

records.jp: 孤高の君―――
records.en: You who stand above---
comments: CP CCC0000
records.assessment: 孤高の君 is the private epithet Taichi gives the aloof, solitary girl. 'You who stand above' turns it into direct address and fails to function as a title.

highlights.text: You who stand above---

records.jp: 言葉をかわしたことはない。
records.en: There had never been exchange of words.
comments: Specific, she DID talk to him before. -GHS
records.assessment: The two had never exchanged words. 'There had never been exchange of words' omits an article and both participants.

highlights.text: There had never been exchange of words.

records.jp: ときおり俺は彼女らに招かれ、甘い飲み物を振る舞われた。
records.en:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.
comments: Possibly before he was made a full-on doll. -GHS
records.assessment: 彼女ら refers to the women or ladies of the household in this context. 'Girls' changes their age and register.

highlights.text:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.

records.jp: 毎月頭には大量の書物・衣類・嗜好品が届いた。
records.en:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.
comments: The wealth is the Hasekura equivalent of the power plant in Kamisaka. This idea of "rich cutoffs from the world" keeps returning here. -GHS
records.assessment: 嗜好品 means luxury or indulgence goods. 'Luxury food and consumables' splits it into unsupported categories.

highlights.text:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.

records.jp: ある頃からか、俺はご婦人がたに気に入られるようになった。
records.en:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.
comments: Origins of gerontophilia? -GHS
records.assessment: ある頃からか means 'from some point on.' 'Ever since somewhen' uses a nonstandard word and malformed time expression.

highlights.text:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.

records.jp: また俺の白い髪と、間近で見るとわかる不思議な模様を描く瞳も、彼女たちを退屈させなかった。
records.en:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.
comments: He claims he had white hair before the killing of the Shinkawas, contradicting CCX0001 and CCC0011C, but consistent with CCA0013 where he misdreamed Sakuraba's hair. -GHS
records.assessment: The unusual pattern is in Taichi's eyes or irises, not specifically drawn on his pupils. The English repeats the narrower anatomical error.

highlights.text:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.

records.jp: でもつきあった。
records.en: But I kept company.
records.assessment: Taichi nevertheless kept the ladies company. 'I kept company' normally requires the person accompanied.

highlights.text: But I kept company.

records.jp: 砂糖菓子めいて甘やかな人々に対し、逆らうという選択肢はなかった。
records.en:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.
comments: See CCC0000. The "choice" part is important, once this becomes a VN. -GHS
records.assessment: He had no option to resist the cloyingly sweet people. 'Against those people ... a choice labeled opposition did not exist' is a rigid and ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.

records.jp: こうして幼い子供らに馬乗りにされ髪引かれる玩具業務から離れた俺は、新しい仕事として人形業務に就くことになった。
records.en:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.
comments: Damn double meaning. Of horseplay, of course. -GHS
records.assessment: Small children rode astride him and pulled his hair as part of his toy role. 'The job of letting' them do it implies voluntary permission.

highlights.text:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.

records.jp: そんな俺を、彼女……孤高の君はひややかな視線で見ていた。
records.en:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.
records.assessment: The solitary girl regarded Taichi with a cold gaze. The English begins 'I was like that when,' shifts the epithet into direct address, and never forms a coherent subject-predicate relation.

highlights.text:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.

records.jp: 末娘。
records.en: youngest of the girls there.
records.assessment: 末娘 identifies Youko as the youngest daughter. 'Youngest of the girls there' omits the family relation.

highlights.text: youngest of the girls there.

records.jp: 一度、掃除の人夫として駆り出されたことがある。
records.en:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.
records.assessment: Taichi was once pressed into service as cleaning labor. 'Was tossed out when I was working as a cleaning man' instead says that he was ejected or dismissed.

highlights.text:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.

records.jp: 使用人さんたちにまじって参加した。
records.en: when I was mingling with the servitude.
comments: Another term censored in the PS2 version alone. It's such a hack job that it ended up with two -san honorifics in a row. Wonder if they just had a list of "no no" words and did a quick search and replace weeks before shipping. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi joins the household servants in the cleaning. 'Mingling with the servitude' uses an abstract condition of bondage instead of the people.

highlights.text: when I was mingling with the servitude.

records.jp: けど、蠱惑的だった。
records.en: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.
comments: Same description as Machiko-sensei, see CCA0007. -GHS
records.assessment: 蠱惑的 calls the voice bewitching or seductively captivating. 'Captivating as magic' turns the quality into a simile and loses its alluring register.

highlights.text: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.

records.jp: なるほど確かに一人だけ異質な者が、異世界にはいたのだ。
records.en:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.
comments: Latches on to above. This is the literal SF term... and of course, the closest to the literal truth of Cross Channel (in part). -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi realizes that one anomalous person existed alone within that otherworld. The English adds that she is 'always alone,' shifts to present tense, and says she dwells in a parallel world.

highlights.text:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.

records.jp: 綺麗な衣装を着て、女の子の言葉遣いでお茶の相手をしている時、支倉曜子について問いかけたことがある。
records.en:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.
records.assessment: Taichi wears beautiful clothes while speaking in girlish language. 'Gaudy dress' adds a negative judgment not present in 綺麗.

highlights.text:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.

records.jp: 末の息子のそのまた娘と。
records.en:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.
records.assessment: Youko is the daughter of the youngest son. The English adds another generation, making her the daughter of the son of the Head's son.

highlights.text:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.

records.jp: 若旦那とうら若き使用人との秘められた恋物語と、その顛末。
records.en:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.
comments: Since these are half-quotes anyway. Hmmm, with Taichi that's just six people. -GHS
records.assessment: 顛末 is the course and outcome of the secret relationship. 'Those are the facts' neither describes the outcome nor completes the preceding story phrase.

highlights.text:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.

records.jp: 腫れ物だった。
records.en: She was a tumor.
comments: See KCOP0003: "It's not a tumor." -GHS
records.assessment: 腫れ物 figuratively means a sore spot or untouchable person whom everyone handles warily. 'She was a tumor' literalizes the image into a medical growth.

highlights.text: She was a tumor.

records.jp: 彼女の実父である若旦那なる人物は、海外に留学してしまったそうだ。
records.en:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.
records.assessment: The narrator reports that her father had gone abroad to study. 'Seemed to be studying abroad' makes the study contemporaneous rather than the departure a past fact.

highlights.text:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.

records.jp: けれど知恵と技術と真実は、そこにはなかった。
records.en: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.
records.assessment: The ladies offered neither wisdom, technical skill, nor truth. 'Art' is too broad for 技術 here, and 'there weren't' is inverted ungrammatically.

highlights.text: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.

records.jp: 好ましくは思っていたけど、仲良くなりたいと願いはしなかった。
records.en:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.
comments: OTOH, he does understand that if she wanted to contact anyone, she'd have done it at this point, not when it's convenient for her. And she wouldn't have fallen in pseudo-love with him in the horror of the idea of mistreated him. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi thought well of Youko or found her likable. 'Desirable' introduces a stronger sexualized evaluation.

highlights.text:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.

records.jp: 独力で生きるものと、力に。
records.en:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.
records.assessment: He is drawn to beings that live by their own power and to that power itself. 'By that strength' makes the strength an agent or means acting on him.

highlights.text:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.

records.jp: 領土は減ったり増えたりする。
records.en:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.
comments: MORE than the sanctuary desired is also problematic! -GHS
records.assessment: Personal territory shrinks and expands as boundaries shift. 'Maybe decreases, maybe increases' changes the general dynamic into uncertainty.

highlights.text:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.

records.jp: 一般的な価値観では、豪壮なる千の軍隊より、一人の英雄が好まれる。
records.en:
In the general sense of values it's the lone hero
that is beloved, more than the thousand of armies
and their splendor.
comments: ...but heroes always have their own nakamas... -GHS
records.assessment: Conventional values favor one hero over a magnificent army of a thousand. 'The thousand of armies' instead denotes an ungrammatical plurality of many armies.

highlights.text:
In the general sense of values it's the lone hero
that is beloved, more than the thousand of armies
and their splendor.

records.jp: 一人で生きたいのか、群れて生きたいのか。
records.en:
Do they want to leave alone, or do they want to
live in the flock then?
records.assessment: The contrast is between living alone and living in a group. The typo 'leave alone' changes living by oneself into departing alone.

highlights.text:
Do they want to leave alone, or do they want to
live in the flock then?

records.jp: あるいは少女の完璧さへの嫉妬から。
records.en:
Or, perhaps, because of jealousy for her
perfection.
comments: Contrast CCC3022 -GHS
records.assessment: One feels jealousy 'of' or 'over' another's perfection. 'Jealousy for her perfection' suggests jealousy on its behalf.

highlights.text:
Or, perhaps, because of jealousy for her
perfection.

records.jp: 書物の内容は高度過ぎてほとんどわからなかった。
records.en:
The subjects of the book were extremely advanced,
and I just about didn't understand them,
comments: See also CCC3013. He just likes to chase difficult stuff if he's fascinated. -GHS
records.assessment: The books' content was so advanced that Taichi understood almost none of it. 'Just about didn't understand' can imply that he narrowly avoided failing to understand and is unidiomatic here.

highlights.text:
The subjects of the book were extremely advanced,
and I just about didn't understand them,

records.jp: 図書室では何百回となく出会い、すれ違った。
records.en:
We met in the library so many hundreds of times,
just passing by each other, never meeting.
comments: See CCD5001. -GHS
records.assessment: They encountered and passed one another hundreds of times. The English first says they met and then contradicts it with 'never meeting.'

highlights.text:
We met in the library so many hundreds of times,
just passing by each other, never meeting.

records.jp: 一度の会話もない空間を、俺たちは共有し続けた。
records.en:
We co-owned that air that never once we filled
with conversation.
comments: See CCA0006. SYMBOLISM. -GHS
records.assessment: They continued to share a space in which they never once spoke. 'Co-owned that air that never once we filled' is a strained and ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text:
We co-owned that air that never once we filled
with conversation.

records.jp: これは人類最初の楽園からしてそうだから、避けようのない摂理と考えられる。
records.en:
It has been like this ever since the original Eden
of mankind, therefore, I believe it to be a divine
providence from which there is no escape.
comments: This is one of the most important themes in the entire VN. Notice how he's talking about the Biblical Eden as if it was absolute fact. That's an odd thing for something that shouldn't have a mythological backstory... -GHS
records.assessment: Because collapse attended humanity's first paradise too, the narrator treats it as an unavoidable law or principle. 'Divine providence' adds divine intention.

highlights.text:
It has been like this ever since the original Eden
of mankind, therefore, I believe it to be a divine
providence from which there is no escape.

records.jp: 支倉のかわりに入ってきたのは、新興の人物とその親類縁者だった。
records.en:
Instead of the Hasekuras, new relatives that
were on the rise settled in.
comments: Possibly just a wealth thing, but also possibly just a popularity thing. This could just be a branch family coming in after the old head is arrested/killed in the kind of badass knife fight either japanese yakuza tend to have or that I just made up on the spot. It also follows the decadence of the mafia, seen also in the West, from old/traditional families with some interest for the appearance of decorum to far openly murderous thugs.

This is further metaphorized in the form of a dog that only ever attacks the Triple Secret Mister Exposition. Because Cross Channel. Oh, on the rise = SHINkou, like Shinkawa. I don't know why all the foreshadowing since it's all said five minutes later, maybe the reveal of who Yutaka is was to come later? Wonder if this script had to originally be part of the beginning of the route. -GHS
records.assessment: An upstart or newly wealthy man and his relatives replace the Hasekuras. The English omits the central man and says only that new relatives settled in.

highlights.text:
Instead of the Hasekuras, new relatives that
were on the rise settled in.

records.jp: 粗暴な人々であった。
records.en: We met wild, rude, violent people.
comments: To go meta, this represents your standard true love and weird fetish eroge got gradually flanked, perhaps in a sense replaced, by dark nukige. Cross Channel could be said to be a spiritual sequel to one, or perhaps, of a bad end route. And that's why it's in truth the sequel to Classroom of Atonement: Bad End. ~fin~ -GHS
records.assessment: The newcomers were a brutish lot. 'We met ... people' invents an encounter and makes the narrator's group the subject.

highlights.text: We met wild, rude, violent people.

records.jp: 事件である。
records.en: A matter for investigation,
records.assessment: The Japanese states simply that it was a criminal incident. 'A matter for investigation' adds a procedural consequence that the next lines specifically complicate.

highlights.text: A matter for investigation,

records.jp: 屋敷の一室は、もとは夜会に用いられていたホールだった。
records.en:
One of the room of the mansion was, originally,
used for evening parties.
records.assessment: The singular subject requires 'One of the rooms,' not 'One of the room.'

highlights.text:
One of the room of the mansion was, originally,
used for evening parties.

records.jp: ありとあらゆる方法で肉体をはけ口にされ、従属させられた。
records.en:
She was made subordinate to every single possible
method for a body to be used as an outlet for
others.
records.assessment: The woman's body was used as an outlet in every conceivable way and she was subjugated. The English says that she was made subordinate to methods, assigning the domination to an abstraction.

highlights.text:
She was made subordinate to every single possible
method for a body to be used as an outlet for
others.

records.jp: 妻を助けようと警察に連絡を取った。
records.en: he contacted the police so to rescue his wife.
records.assessment: The purpose clause should be 'so as to rescue' or 'to rescue,' not 'so to rescue.'

highlights.text: he contacted the police so to rescue his wife.

records.jp: 別に買収されてもいなかっただろう。
records.en:
I don't even think there was much in the way of
bribes.
records.assessment: The police probably had not been bribed at all. 'Not much in the way of bribes' allows some bribery and changes a binary denial into an amount.

highlights.text:
I don't even think there was much in the way of
bribes.

records.jp: 屋敷のネットで調べてみた。
records.en: I investigated the mansion on the 'net.
comments: This should be '92-'94 at best, so it should still work. I didn't start until '94-'95 and I remember when the Geocities Look was just barely getting started... hell I remember when Yahoo looked like a good idea, when you'd get banned from IRC for daring to criticize Windows 95, and AOLamer was only about to become a thing (today the term is "GameFAQs level", not that I believe all adjectives to "Internet discussion" to be anything but completely redundant). -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi investigates using the mansion's network or internet connection. 'Investigated the mansion on the net' says that the mansion itself was the research subject.

highlights.text: I investigated the mansion on the 'net.

records.jp: 警察のこうした対応によって看過された犯罪は、数限りなくあった。
records.en:
Crimes without number were being overlooked with
the complicity of the policy.
records.assessment: Countless crimes were overlooked because of this kind of police response. The English says 'policy' rather than police and upgrades nonintervention to active complicity.

highlights.text:
Crimes without number were being overlooked with
the complicity of the policy.

records.jp: 民間の権利意識が肥大化すると、おいそれと介入できなくなるのだった。
records.en:
The sense of entitlement in the population was so
bloated that intervention at a moment's notice
became impossible.
comments: See CCA0003. Indeed it is near its end. -GHS
records.assessment: 肥大化する権利意識 describes an expanding consciousness or assertion of civil rights. 'Bloated sense of entitlement' recasts rights awareness as selfish undeserved privilege.

highlights.text:
The sense of entitlement in the population was so
bloated that intervention at a moment's notice
became impossible.

records.jp: 些細なミスを、親の仇のように責める人間が増えるのだ。
records.en:
An increasing number of humans would persecute
tiny little errors as if they were offenses
against their own family.
comments: Humans is still colder. See every single online community there ever was and ever will be. This was bad in the '90s, insufferable in 2003, and is as of writing beyond what I would consider my worst predictions (and they were bad, lemme tell ya). This is only at the beginning stages, asw ell. -GHS
records.assessment: 親の仇のように means blaming a small mistake with the intensity reserved for one's parent's killer. 'Offenses against their own family' loses that specific comparison.

highlights.text:
An increasing number of humans would persecute
tiny little errors as if they were offenses
against their own family.

records.jp: 怠慢ではあろうが。
records.en: Negligence will result, but,
records.assessment: The inaction may itself be negligence. 'Negligence will result' instead makes negligence a future consequence.

highlights.text: Negligence will result, but,

records.jp: 誠実さは必要だろうが。
records.en: I've got to be sincere here:
records.assessment: The narrator concedes that institutional sincerity or integrity is necessary. 'I've got to be sincere here' makes it a promise about his own speech and incorrectly introduces the next sentence.

highlights.text: I've got to be sincere here:

records.jp: 自分を助けるのは、自分の有能さだ。
records.en: what can save yourself is your own power.
comments: See CCC0000. -GHS
records.assessment: What saves oneself is one's own competence. The English switches between 'yourself' and 'your' and broadens competence to power.

highlights.text: what can save yourself is your own power.

records.jp: 大きな実害を被らない限りにおいて、他人の不手際や浅い見識に腹を立てるということは。
records.en:
Getting angry about other people's clumsiness
or shallow opinions, the point where there is
no infliction of serious harm at least,
records.assessment: Together with the next line, this says that anger at harmless mistakes or shallow judgment entrusts part of one's heart to others. The English fragment never establishes the limiting condition or main relation.

highlights.text:
Getting angry about other people's clumsiness
or shallow opinions, the point where there is
no infliction of serious harm at least,

records.jp: 人の限界に起因する、理不尽で不完全なルールに身を置くことでもある。
records.en:
is also for one to invest themselves in the absurd
and imperfect rules generated by people's
limitations.
records.assessment: Being normal means placing oneself within irrational, imperfect rules born of human limits. 'Invest themselves in' suggests commitment of resources or belief rather than living under the rules.

highlights.text:
is also for one to invest themselves in the absurd
and imperfect rules generated by people's
limitations.

records.jp: ……優しいゆりかごであるはずがない。
records.en:
...there is no expectation that the cradle
will be gentle.
comments: The concept of the real world as nothing but the cradle for mankind in the next one, so very Christian. -GHS
records.assessment: The social order cannot possibly be a gentle cradle. 'There is no expectation that' weakens the categorical judgment into a prediction about expectations.

highlights.text:
...there is no expectation that the cradle
will be gentle.

records.jp: 粗暴なことが日常と化しやすい。
records.en:
Violence is easily made into the ordinary
of a life.
records.assessment: Brutality readily becomes everyday routine. 'The ordinary of a life' is not grammatical English.

highlights.text:
Violence is easily made into the ordinary
of a life.

records.jp: たちむかうには、強固な自我。
records.en:
What was needed to to fight against this were
a firm ego,
comments: Moved a bit from below -GHS
records.assessment: The English duplicates 'to' and mismatches singular 'ego' with plural 'were.'

highlights.text:
What was needed to to fight against this were
a firm ego,

records.jp: 妻は慰みものにさせられ、妊娠させられたり堕胎させられたりした。
records.en:
As the wife became tool of amusement, she was
made pregnant, then to abort the child.
records.assessment: The paired たり forms describe repeated or varied forced pregnancies and abortions. The English reduces this to one pregnancy followed by one abortion.

highlights.text:
As the wife became tool of amusement, she was
made pregnant, then to abort the child.

records.jp: 徐々に心も沈む。
records.en: And gradually hearts sink as well.
records.assessment: The woman's heart gradually sinks. The English pluralizes this into unspecified 'hearts.'

highlights.text: And gradually hearts sink as well.

records.jp: 夫は最後の手段に出た。
records.en: The husband fell on the last resort,
records.assessment: The husband resorts to his last option. 'Fell on the last resort' uses the wrong phrasal verb.

highlights.text: The husband fell on the last resort,

records.jp: 妻が輪姦されている脇で。
records.en: right next to her wife who was being gang-raped.
records.assessment: The husband is killed beside his own wife. 'Her wife' gives the wife a female possessor and severs the marital relation.

highlights.text: right next to her wife who was being gang-raped.

records.jp: 幼児性愛者だった。両刀とサドという二つのオプションをつけていた。
records.en:
He was a pedophile. He came with the optionals
'bisexual' and 'sadist' installed.
comments: http://d.hatena.ne.jp/keyword/%CE%BE%C5%E1 also, it continues the car metaphor, so it's even more hints as to who it should be. -GHS
records.assessment: 両刀 and サド are presented as two added options, bisexuality and sadism. 'Optionals' is not the English plural noun for optional features.

highlights.text:
He was a pedophile. He came with the optionals
'bisexual' and 'sadist' installed.

records.jp: 今度はお茶ではなく、Ｓの欲望の相手をした。
records.en:
This time I was no tea ceremony companion, but
for S and his desires.
comments: Specific term -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi is made to service S's desires rather than serve as a tea companion. 'But for S and his desires' omits the action and leaves the contrast incomplete.

highlights.text:
This time I was no tea ceremony companion, but
for S and his desires.

records.jp: 女児のような俺を、ノンケの男に相手させた。
records.en:
I, who looked like a little girl, was made into
his straight male partner.
comments: It's possible he's just ordered around by Shinkawa's dad to hurt and humiliate others, not necessarily rape 'em. This is possibly where he learned all his sexual harassment techniques. -GHS
records.assessment: S makes straight men engage with the cross-dressed Taichi. 'His straight male partner' makes Taichi the partner of S and collapses the other men into a possessive modifier.

highlights.text:
I, who looked like a little girl, was made into
his straight male partner.

records.jp: 冗談半分でやる者が大半だった。
records.en:
People who liked to half-jest were more than
the half there.
comments: Visuals. ...wait, so if you half-jest twice... -GHS
records.assessment: Most participants did it half as a joke. The English instead describes people who liked to half-jest and then compares their number to a half.

highlights.text:
People who liked to half-jest were more than
the half there.

records.jp: たまに覚醒してしまう者もいたが。
records.en:
Occasionally, there were people who grew
disillusioned, but,
records.assessment: 覚醒 means that some participants awakened to or discovered a new appetite. 'Grew disillusioned' means they lost belief or enthusiasm, the opposite direction.

highlights.text:
Occasionally, there were people who grew
disillusioned, but,

records.jp: 小学校のいじめとかでも、似たようなことが起こる。
records.en:
What happened there was something similar
to elementary school bullying.
comments: Against the ones who grew disillusioned. See Yusa. And Family Project, parts of Kana, parts of Yume Miru Kusuri... boy Tanaka likes this one. That's why I'm fairly sure it hits close to home to him. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator generalizes that similar behavior occurs in elementary-school bullying. The English changes this to a comparison with a specific past event.

highlights.text:
What happened there was something similar
to elementary school bullying.

records.jp: 集団の中では、かなりの高確率でこういうことは発生する。
records.en:
Inside of a group, there is a fairly high chance
that this sort of things would happen.
comments: Pretty much 1:1, see once more every online community ever. And "online" is only there because in online communities it's easier to see. -GHS
records.assessment: 'This sort of things' mismatches singular 'sort' and plural 'things.'

highlights.text:
Inside of a group, there is a fairly high chance
that this sort of things would happen.

records.jp: 学校ではいじめっ子としてならしていた……らしい。
records.en: It seemed at school he was a bully... of sorts.
comments: Since this is a metaphor for a normal life, as well as the Eden, this is about elementary school bullying. Literally. -GHS
records.assessment: The boy was reputed or notorious as a bully at school. 'A bully of sorts' weakens the established reputation into uncertainty about whether he qualified.

highlights.text: It seemed at school he was a bully... of sorts.

records.jp: 乱交の雰囲気に圧倒されていたのも束の間、俺を見て嘲笑った。
records.en:
In the brief moment of being overwhelmed by
the promiscuity in the air, he looked at me
and sneered in ridicule.
records.assessment: After only a brief spell of being overwhelmed, the boy sees Taichi and sneers. 'In the brief moment ... he looked' makes the reaction simultaneous rather than subsequent.

highlights.text:
In the brief moment of being overwhelmed by
the promiscuity in the air, he looked at me
and sneered in ridicule.

records.jp: 早熟な精通と重なっていたせいもあるだろうか。
records.en:
Perhaps it's also the accumulation of all
this precocious knowledge to blame.
records.assessment: 早熟な精通 refers to precocious sexual maturation or first ejaculation. 'Accumulation of all this precocious knowledge' misreads 精通 as expertise and invents accumulation.

highlights.text:
Perhaps it's also the accumulation of all
this precocious knowledge to blame.

records.jp: 落ち着いた……わけではなかった。
records.en: Calming down... was not the cause.
records.assessment: The stillness does not mean that Kiri has calmed down. 'Was not the cause' treats calming as a cause rather than a rejected interpretation.

highlights.text: Calming down... was not the cause.

records.jp: 愕然とした表情で、俺を見ている。
records.en: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.
records.assessment: 愕然 describes a stunned or shocked expression. 'Terror' identifies fear rather than shocked disbelief.

highlights.text: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.

records.jp: 「……な、なにを言って……？」
records.en: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"
records.assessment: Kiri asks what Taichi is saying now. 'What did you say?' asks for repetition of a completed utterance.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"

records.jp: 張り裂けそうな声。
records.en: Her voice seems to be bursting open.
records.assessment: Her voice sounds ready to split or tear. 'Bursting open' is an unnatural physical description of a voice.

highlights.text: Her voice seems to be bursting open.

records.jp: 「そんな話、聞いたこともない！　ずっと暮らしてきて、そんな話があったなんて。ありえない……考えられない―――」
records.en: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"
comments: Already from the voice it's obvious she suspects. -GHS
records.assessment: Kiri says that despite living together all that time, she never heard that such a story existed. The English specifically says that Yutaka never told her, assigning the silence to him.

highlights.text: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"

records.jp: ぴたりと霧は口をつぐんだ。
records.en: Kiri's lips closed tight on the spot.
records.assessment: ぴたり conveys that Kiri stops speaking abruptly. 'On the spot' instead describes location or immediacy of action.

highlights.text: Kiri's lips closed tight on the spot.

records.jp: 名探偵になった気分だ。
records.en: It felt she had become a detective, and a great one.
records.assessment: Taichi feels like a great detective. The English says that Kiri has become one.

highlights.text: It felt she had become a detective, and a great one.

records.jp: 「謎はとけまくってんだよ、霧ちん」
records.en: Taichi: "So you have unraveled the mystery, Kiri-chin."
comments: He's still being an ass. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi boasts that the mystery is unraveling all over or practically solving itself. The English credits Kiri with unraveling it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "So you have unraveled the mystery, Kiri-chin."

records.jp: 「あと俺、あいつがどうして脚を怪我したのか知ってる」
records.en: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."
records.assessment: Taichi knows how Yutaka injured his leg. 'Why that guy's leg is injured' asks for a present condition rather than the cause of the injury event.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."

records.jp: 「俺も女装させられてたし……向こうもわからなかったみたいだけど」
records.en: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."
records.assessment: Because Taichi was cross-dressed, Yutaka apparently did not recognize him either. 'There wasn't any recognizing from him' is ungrammatical and obscures the object of recognition.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."

records.jp: 「豊も俺も、あれで心が壊れないはずないんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."
records.assessment: The paired negative requires 'neither for Yutaka nor for me,' not 'nor for me nor for Yutaka.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."

records.jp: 感情のうねりは打ち寄せた波、俺を湿らせて引き返していく。
records.en: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.
records.assessment: The wave had already broken and was withdrawing. The English shifts from past perfect to present progressive within the same completed observation.

highlights.text: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.

records.jp: アタックしてきたのは、おまえの方なんだからな。
records.en: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.
records.assessment: The speaker says that the addressee was the one who came at or attacked him first. The English assigns the attack to a third-person woman and turns the reason into her general disposition.

highlights.text: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.

records.jp: 「苦しんでいるのなら、見逃してやろうと思った」
records.en: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."
comments: See CCC3007, it's possible he was already aware then. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker recounts his earlier thought that he would let the matter go if the other person was suffering too. 'I'll let it go' changes that embedded past intention into a present promise.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."

records.jp: 「あの日……わたしに質問した……幸せかって……？」
records.en: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"
records.assessment: The quoted question asks the speaker whether the speaker was happy. The English instead asks whether an absent male was happy.

highlights.text: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"

records.jp: 「よく覚えてるな」
records.en: Taichi: "You remember that, good."
records.assessment: 'You remember that, good' is an ungrammatical splice and does not cleanly express the approving reaction to the addressee's recollection.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You remember that, good."

records.jp: ありがちな問いかけ。
records.en: An usual question to ask,
comments: CP CCC3008
records.assessment: The English article is wrong: 'usual' begins with a consonant sound and requires 'a,' not 'an.'

highlights.text: An usual question to ask,

records.jp: 意味はまったく逆だった。
records.en: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.
comments: CP CCC3008
records.assessment: The source describes the question as difficult to answer; the intensifier 'damnably' adds an unsupported profane register.

highlights.text: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.

records.jp: 「……つらい思いをしてきたんです！」
records.en: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"
comments: PCP CCC3008
records.assessment: 辛い目に遭ってきた refers to undergoing painful or harsh experiences. 'Had been feeling bitter' changes external suffering into an internal resentful attitude.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"

records.jp: 「親族に邪険にされて……荒れて……」
records.en: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."
comments: Possibly referring to how they looked relieved at the funeral... possibly referring to the story in CCC3025. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the person was badly treated by relatives and consequently became wild or troubled. 'Relatives were cruel, and so rough' leaves the result without its subject and makes 'rough' appear to modify the relatives.

highlights.text: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."

records.jp: 「本当にずっとつらかった？」
records.en: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"
comments: CP CCC3008
records.assessment: The source again refers to experiencing painful or harsh treatment. 'Feeling so bitter' substitutes resentment for suffering.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"

records.jp: 「そりゃそうだろうさ。昔しでかしたことを綺麗さっぱり忘れれば、心もスッキリサッパリだ。いくらだって幸せになれるさ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"
comments: This is why forgetting's not removing the past, and why Taichi's attempt to have his way with the time loop can't work. -GHS
records.assessment: The source concludes that once those memories are gone, the person can become as happy as can be. 'How so very happy could he become' is an ungrammatical question and loses the stated causal conclusion.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"

records.jp: 「おまえが見たとおり、あの時の屋上ですべて話した」
records.en: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."
records.assessment: The speaker says that he told the other person everything on the rooftop at that time. 'That moment we talked about everything' removes the specified location and changes a one-way disclosure into mutual conversation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."

records.jp: 「許すも許さないもない。犯した罪は永遠にそのままだ。触れることなんてできない。変質させることもだ。俺もそこを責める気はなかった」
records.en: Taichi: "There's no forgiving nor condemning. Sins perpetrated remain like that in eternity. There's no putting your hands on them in any way. Neither there is changing them. I didn't feel like there was blame then."
comments: And... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he never intended to blame the other person for the fixed facts. 'I didn't feel like there was blame then' removes both the narrator's agency and the object of blame; the preceding 'Neither there is changing them' is also ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's no forgiving nor condemning. Sins perpetrated remain like that in eternity. There's no putting your hands on them in any way. Neither there is changing them. I didn't feel like there was blame then."

records.jp: その脇にしゃがみ込む。
records.en: She squats cradling her knees on the spot.
records.assessment: The narrator crouches beside the seated person. 'She squats cradling her knees' assigns the movement and posture to the other person.

highlights.text: She squats cradling her knees on the spot.

records.jp: 俺の顔には、憫笑が刻まれている。
records.en: A smile of pity engraves on my face.
comments: But is it an insincere one? -GHS
records.assessment: A pitying smile is etched on the person's face. 'A smile engraves' incorrectly makes the smile the agent of engraving and leaves the construction incomplete.

highlights.text: A smile of pity engraves on my face.

records.jp: 耳元に囁く。
records.en: I whisper in her ears,
records.assessment: The narrator whispers at one ear. The English plural 'ears' changes the concrete gesture.

highlights.text: I whisper in her ears,

records.jp: 霧の内部で糸が切れるのがわかった。
records.en: And so I knew that a string inside Kiri had been cut,
records.assessment: The metaphorical string snapped or broke. 'Had been cut' implies an external cutting agent and changes the event into an earlier past-perfect action.

highlights.text: And so I knew that a string inside Kiri had been cut,

records.jp: 決してもう繋がるまい。
records.en: and may never be reconnected again.
comments: The one that binds her to Yutaka. This is a GOOD THING FOR HER. -GHS
records.assessment: きっと二度と繋がらない expresses the speaker's firm expectation that it will surely never reconnect. 'May never' weakens this to possibility.

highlights.text: and may never be reconnected again.

records.jp: 涙はストレスを体外に流すのだという説がある。
records.en: A theory says that tears are the stress that flows outside of the body.
records.assessment: The theory says tears flush accumulated stress out of the body. 'Tears were built up stress' identifies the tears themselves as stress and loses the expulsion relation.

highlights.text: A theory says that tears are the stress that flows outside of the body.

records.jp: 霧は泣けない。
records.en: Kiri is not crying.
records.assessment: The narrator observes that the person cannot cry. 'Is not crying' states only the current absence of tears and omits the inability.

highlights.text: Kiri is not crying.

records.jp: ……深く絶望が沈殿してしまって。
records.en: ...a very deep despair is precipitating.
records.assessment: The source says despair has already settled or accumulated deep within the heart. 'Is precipitating' presents an ongoing process and uses an unnatural chemical-process verb for the emotional state.

highlights.text: ...a very deep despair is precipitating.

records.jp: 「どうして……言わなかったんですか」
records.en: Kiri: "How come... he never said anything?'
records.assessment: The speaker asks why the addressee did not tell her. The English says instead that a third-person man never said anything.

highlights.text: Kiri: "How come... he never said anything?'

records.jp: 「霧があまりにも豊のこと、慕ってたから」
records.en: Taichi: "Because you adore Yutaka too much, Kiri."
records.assessment: The source refers to how much the person used to adore or dote on another person. The present-tense 'adore' removes that retrospective framing.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because you adore Yutaka too much, Kiri."

records.jp: 霧には理解できていない。
records.en: For Kiri that is impossible to understand.
records.assessment: The speaker says she does not understand. 'It is impossible to understand' escalates her personal non-understanding into a categorical claim of impossibility.

highlights.text: For Kiri that is impossible to understand.

records.jp: 「脆いくせに攻撃的で」
records.en: Taichi: "Aggressiveness in spite of tender-heartedness."
records.assessment: The source contrasts fragility with aggression. 'Tender-heartedness' replaces vulnerability or fragility with kindness and sympathy.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Aggressiveness in spite of tender-heartedness."

records.jp: 「恨んでなんかない」
records.en: Taichi: "I had no grudge whatsoever."
records.assessment: The source says the person does not harbor resentment, a current continuing state. 'Had no grudge' relocates it to a completed past state.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I had no grudge whatsoever."

records.jp: 「子供の倫理観に、全能的なものを期待する方が悪い」
records.en: Taichi: "It is a bad thing for children's ethical values to include an expectation of omnipotence."
comments: Not in the children themselves, but for the children to expect this from others. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says it is wrong to expect omnipotence or perfect ethics from a child. The English instead makes children themselves possess values that expect omnipotence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is a bad thing for children's ethical values to include an expectation of omnipotence."

records.jp: 「おかげで蹴られたり嫌われたり大変だったぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's gonna be a mess if there's rejection or hatred because of that."
comments: Like how Youko rejected him the moment he followed her orders... or how Kiri expected Yutaka to be perfect. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker says that because of this he had a hard time being rejected or hated. The English turns it into a future hypothetical mess if rejection or hatred happens and obscures who suffers it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's gonna be a mess if there's rejection or hatred because of that."

records.jp: 霧の中で、精神状態が応急処置されるのがわかる。
records.en: I understand that, inside Kiri, her mental condition is taking emergency measures.
records.assessment: The narrator assesses the other person's mental state as being patched up by an emergency measure. The English makes the mental condition itself take emergency measures.

highlights.text: I understand that, inside Kiri, her mental condition is taking emergency measures.

records.jp: 「どうかしたいの？」
records.en: Taichi: "Was anything wrong?"
records.assessment: The question asks whether the speaker should do something about the situation or whether the addressee wants action taken. 'Was anything wrong?' asks only whether a problem existed.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Was anything wrong?"

records.jp: 「あやまったら、許してくれますか」
records.en: Kiri: "If I apologize, will you forgive?"
records.assessment: The plea asks the addressee to forgive the speaker. 'Please forgive' omits the required object and leaves the English incomplete.

highlights.text: Kiri: "If I apologize, will you forgive?"

records.jp: 霧の頭に手を置く。
records.en: I place my hands on Kiri's head.
records.assessment: The source specifies one hand. The English changes it to plural 'hands.'

highlights.text: I place my hands on Kiri's head.

records.jp: どうせあと一日だけの世界。
records.en: Because after all, this is a world of only one day.
comments: He spoiled iiit -GHS
records.assessment: The source imagines a world with only one day remaining. 'A world of only one day' instead describes a world whose entire duration or extent is one day.

highlights.text: Because after all, this is a world of only one day.

records.jp: ほつれて果てよう。
records.en: Let's become frayed until it ends.
records.assessment: The world unravels or frays and then ends. 'Frayed until it ends' changes the sequence into a process continuing up to an independently defined endpoint.

highlights.text: Let's become frayed until it ends.

records.jp: 「……それで……許されるのなら」
records.en: Kiri: "...if you... give forgiveness."
comments: See CCC3019B. That's how we know she is serious. -GHS
records.assessment: The conditional means that the speaker will do it if that earns the addressee's forgiveness. 'If you give forgiveness' is unidiomatic and does not specify whom or what is forgiven.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...if you... give forgiveness."

records.jp: 「どっかのランプの精みたく、願い事は三つまでとか言わないよね？」
records.en: Taichi: "Like to the Genie of the Lamp, I might have three desires that I could ask, you know?"
comments: And the reason Kiri's hair is so blue-ish is, therefore, because it's reference to Aladdin. But unfortunately, Tanaka couldn't get Robin Williams to play her part. And something precious was lost forever. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker confirms that the offer is not limited to three wishes like a lamp genie. 'I might have three desires' turns the addressee's limit into uncertainty about how many desires the speaker has.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Like to the Genie of the Lamp, I might have three desires that I could ask, you know?"

records.jp: 弱気になっちゃってまあ。
records.en: She got all weak-kneed dinn'she.
records.assessment: The eye-dialect spelling in 'dinn'she' is not grammatical standard English and adds an accent not represented by the source.

highlights.text: She got all weak-kneed dinn'she.

records.jp: 「俺はマニアだから、霧のＵＳＥＤ制服をよこしなさいとか要求するかもよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "I am a fetishist, therefore could I even firmly demand you to hand over your 『CHUUKO * USED』 uniform or the like, right Kiri?"
comments: It's Jagranese anyway(tm). -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker threatens that she may demand the addressee's used uniform. The English asks permission to demand it, and the inserted gloss 'CHUUKO * USED' is unsupported authorial commentary.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I am a fetishist, therefore could I even firmly demand you to hand over your 『CHUUKO * USED』 uniform or the like, right Kiri?"

records.jp: 「身につけている下着と着画もダゾ」
records.en: Taichi: "And even the underwear your are using, with a picture proving it's actually been worn o-f-c-o-u-r-s-e."
comments: See CCC0003A, CCC3019B again. -GHS
records.assessment: 'Your are using' substitutes the possessive 'your' for the required pronoun 'you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And even the underwear your are using, with a picture proving it's actually been worn o-f-c-o-u-r-s-e."

records.jp: 「……そんなもの、欲しがる……」
records.en: Kiri: "...if that's the sort of thing... you want..."
records.assessment: The source is a direct incredulous question asking whether the addressee wants such a thing. 'If you wish for...' leaves the conditional fragment without a result and loses the question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...if that's the sort of thing... you want..."

records.jp: まさか本当にそんなものが持てるとは。
records.en: No way, seriously, to have come into that, it's...
records.assessment: 'No way for the conversation to have come into that' is not an idiomatic or syntactically complete way to say the conversation could not possibly reach that point.

highlights.text: No way, seriously, to have come into that, it's...

records.jp: 「生きてみるものだ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's something to live on for."
records.assessment: 生きてみるものだ remarks that living on can bring unexpected experiences or that life is worth trying. 'Something to live on for' invents a specific object that gives life purpose.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's something to live on for."

records.jp: 俺は性急に次のステップを目指した。
records.en: I impatiently set my sights on the next step.
records.assessment: 性急に means hastily or impetuously. 'Impatiently' instead attributes irritation at delay.

highlights.text: I impatiently set my sights on the next step.

records.jp: 「じ、じゃあ、Ｈなことを強要しようかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "We-, well, maybe I ought to force you to some perverted stuff?"
records.assessment: The source says the speaker will not force sexual acts on the addressee. 'Force you to some perverted stuff' is an ungrammatical and imprecise rendering of forcing an action on someone.

highlights.text: Taichi: "We-, well, maybe I ought to force you to some perverted stuff?"

records.jp: 「……どのくらい……えっちなことを？」
records.en: Kiri: "...what level... of perverted?"
records.assessment: The question asks what kind of sexual behavior or how sexual it would be. 'What level of perverted?' lacks a noun or predicative construction and substitutes moral deviance for sexuality.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...what level... of perverted?"

records.jp: 「肉肉しい感じで、かな」
records.en: Taichi: "Something that would make us into a gut-to-gut, maybe."
comments: nikunikushii 肉肉しい "meat meatful" = 憎々しい "detestable", see below. -GHS
records.assessment: 肉肉しい is a pun on something fleshy or meaty. 'Gut-to-gut' replaces the meat wordplay with a different body-part idiom.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Something that would make us into a gut-to-gut, maybe."

records.jp: 「き、霧が俺を憎々しく思っていたことにかけてねっ」
records.en: Taichi: "Th-, that means there's how you really had a gut feeling that made you hate my guts, I sweeear!"
comments: ugh the pun -GHS
records.assessment: The English sentence about a gut feeling and hating one's guts is syntactically tangled and fails to express the compact reaction to the strained pun.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Th-, that means there's how you really had a gut feeling that made you hate my guts, I sweeear!"

records.jp: 強引すぎた。
records.en: That was too pushy.
records.assessment: 強引すぎた judges the preceding wordplay or line as too forced. 'I was being too pushy' instead describes coercive interpersonal behavior.

highlights.text: That was too pushy.

records.jp: 「わたしを……その……抱くんですか？」
records.en: Kiri: "Was I... is that like... 'embracing'?"
comments: Another euphemism for youguessedit. though going by Youko, she might mean "I was enveloped in anger". -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker asks whether the addressee is going to sleep with or embrace her. 'Was I... is that like embracing?' changes the subject and tense and does not form the intended question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Was I... is that like... 'embracing'?"

records.jp: 抱くに決まっていた。
records.en: I had decided on embracing (sex),
comments: Let's avoid turning this into ANOTHER running gag FFS. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator states that of course he meant or intended to sleep beside her. 'Had decided' turns that immediate intention into a prior settled decision.

highlights.text: I had decided on embracing (sex),

records.jp: 教壇に立たせる。
records.en: I make her take the teacher's stand.
comments: It's the wooden elevated platform on which the teacher's desk lies, see BG, but the expression is also literally "to be a teacher". -GHS
records.assessment: 教壇 is the classroom platform or podium. 'Teacher's stand' is not the normal English term and suggests a piece of furniture.

highlights.text: I make her take the teacher's stand.

records.jp: 「してほしいこと？」
records.en: Kiri: "Something you want?"
records.assessment: The question asks whether there is something the addressee wants the speaker to do. 'Something you want?' omits both the requested action and who would perform it.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Something you want?"

records.jp: 含んだまま応じる。
records.en: Agreement with the mouth full.
records.assessment: The source says the person responds with her mouth full, without specifying agreement. 'Agreement with mouth full' invents the content of the response and is a sentence fragment.

highlights.text: Agreement with the mouth full.

records.jp: トロトロに濡れていた。
records.en: Stickily syrupily wetted.
comments: More implied, but the Touko connections yet continue. -GHS
records.assessment: 'Stickily syrupily wetted' is not grammatical idiomatic English for being drenched or coated in a thick, sticky fluid.

highlights.text: Stickily syrupily wetted.

records.jp: 窓際に手をつかせる。
records.en: I lead her hands to the window.
records.assessment: The narrator makes the other person brace or place her hands against the window area. 'Lead her hands to the window' describes guiding detached hands toward it and loses the bracing action.

highlights.text: I lead her hands to the window.

records.jp: なんだＵＦＯか？　アダムスキーか。
records.en: Could it be a UFO? Where's Adamski?
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Adamski -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese asks whether the object is an Adamski-type flying saucer. It does not ask for the location of a person named Adamski.
records.remedy: Could it be a UFO? An Adamski type?

highlights.text: Where's Adamski?

records.jp: 「シスコンがこうじて帰宅した」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Siscon grew troubled and went home."
records.assessment: The Japanese says Tomoki's sister complex intensified or got the better of him, causing him to go home. The English turns 'siscon' into an entity that became troubled and loses the causal sense.
records.remedy: His sister complex got the better of him, so he went home.

highlights.text: Siscon grew troubled

records.jp: 「それにそんな暴れてると、見えるぞ霧ちん」
records.en: Taichi: "By the way, if you act all that flustered they'll notice, Kiri-chin."
comments: She's still not wearing any panties. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese warns Kiri that if she keeps thrashing about, what is under her skirt will become visible. The English instead says unspecified people will notice her agitation, removing the concrete warning and joke.
records.remedy: And if you keep thrashing around like that, we'll see them, Kiri-chin.

highlights.text: they'll notice

records.jp: 嬉しそうに、先輩は目尻を下げた。
records.en: The corners of Senpai's lowered, seemingly in happiness.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the corners of her eyes lowered in a pleased expression. The English omits the possessed noun after 'Senpai's', leaving both the image and sentence incomplete.
records.remedy: Senpai's eyes softened happily.

highlights.text: The corners of Senpai's lowered, seemingly in happiness.

records.jp: やっぱり無理してるのかな。
records.en: I knew it, this is just forced, is it?
records.assessment: The Japanese wonders whether Kiri is, as suspected, pushing herself too hard. The English makes an unspecified situation 'forced' and drops Kiri as the person overexerting herself.
records.remedy: Maybe she really is pushing herself too hard.

highlights.text: this is just forced

records.jp: 「座りたまへ」
records.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with sitting."
comments: He actually says tamaHe instead of tamae, so I'm going with the usual tweaks made with this kind of tongue slips and therefore "gladden me with sHi-GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese is an affected, old-fashioned command to sit. It does not say that sitting will gladden the speaker; that motive is invented.
records.remedy: Pray, have a seat.

highlights.text: Gladden me with sitting.

records.jp: 「……わかりません」
records.en: Kiri: "...I do not understand."
records.assessment: In response to whether she dislikes the prospect, the Japanese means that she does not know how she feels. 'I do not understand' instead presents a failure to comprehend the question or situation.
records.remedy: ...I don't know.

highlights.text: I do not understand.

records.jp: 「それに、わたしはこれを償いだと思ってます」
records.en: Kiri: "And, I think of this as a compensation."
comments: See CCD1001. It can't work, either direction. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies the act as atonement or making amends. 'Compensation' suggests payment or recompense and weakens the explicitly moral, guilt-bound sense.
records.remedy: And I think of this as atonement.

highlights.text: a compensation

records.jp: たった一日、あるかないかの人生だ。
records.en: It's a life of a single solitary day, that may not even be life.
comments: Spoiled iiit. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the life may not even amount to a full day. The English instead questions whether the span qualifies as life at all, changing the object of uncertainty.
records.remedy: It would be a life of a single day, if even that.

highlights.text: that may not even be life

records.jp: どうか幾度でも、幸せな時をと願う。
records.en: I beg for there to be happy times often and in so many ways,
records.assessment: The Japanese wishes for happy times however many cycles are repeated. The English turns repeated iterations into frequency and variety within unspecified time, losing the loop-bound relation.
records.remedy: I pray that, however many times it takes, there will be happy days.

highlights.text: often and in so many ways

records.jp: 「ええと、特に決まってはいないので、今からでも」
records.en: Misato: "Uhmmm, I did not decide a specific time, but it is hereafter."
comments: Should be around 10, then, as usual. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says no particular start time was fixed and that they could begin even now. The English's 'it is hereafter' does not communicate the offer to start immediately.
records.remedy: Um, we didn't set a particular time, so we could start now.

highlights.text: but it is hereafter

records.jp: 「えっ、私ですか？　だめですよ、だめだめ、無理です、噛みますっ」
records.en: Misato: "Eh, should I? No way, noway-noway, out of the question, I would swallow my tongue!"
comments: Not, necessarily saying she'd bite her tongue and die rather than do it but... interesting that she has no problem doing intraschool DJ, see CCD1001. Of course, this is the position as protagonist, it has nothing to do with being DJ at the antenna. -GHS
records.assessment: Here 噛む means stumbling over one's words or biting one's tongue while speaking. 'Swallow my tongue' conventionally means becoming speechless and is not the same speaking failure.
records.remedy: I'd stumble over every other word!

highlights.text: I would swallow my tongue!

records.jp: 腰を引く。
records.en: I pull her hips.
records.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri draws her hips or body back in resistance. The English instead makes the narrator pull her hips, reversing both the actor and the movement.
records.remedy: She drew back.

highlights.text: I pull her hips.

records.jp: でも俺は人が良かった。
records.en: But I'm glad to be a person.
records.assessment: In the contrast with a life of solitude, the Japanese says the narrator wanted or preferred other people. The English instead says he is pleased with his own status as a person, changing the object of the preference.
records.remedy: But I wanted other people.

highlights.text: I'm glad to be a person.

records.jp: ……顔さえ忘れそうだ。
records.en: ...I seem to have even forgotten their faces.
comments: MEMORY HUNTER. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says he feels he might even forget their faces, expressing an impending possibility. The English says the forgetting appears already to have happened.
records.remedy: ...I feel like I might even forget their faces.

highlights.text: I seem to have even forgotten their faces.

records.jp: 「いつもみたいに冗談で流して、友達づきあいしていけばよかったんです」
records.en: Taichi: "I wish I had just flowed into some joke like always, and just kept being a friend to him."
records.assessment: The Japanese says he should have laughed or brushed the matter off as a joke and continued the friendship. The English calques the verb into an unintelligible motion and does not convey dismissing the matter.
records.remedy: I should have laughed it off like I always did and stayed friends with him.

highlights.text: flowed into some joke

records.jp: 「……向き合った者同士でいられたはずなんです」
records.en: Taichi: "...it has to be between two people who are opposite but equal to each other."
comments: The difference between Taichi/Tomoki and Taichi/Yutaka, or Tomoki/Taichi and Tomoki/Misato. Also see CCC3022: this is the meaning of that "living opposite of you", and why Taichi can't do it. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that, despite hurting and being hurt, they should have been able to remain two people who faced or engaged with each other. It does not characterize them as opposite or equal; those relations replace the source's continued mutual engagement.
records.remedy: ...we still should have been able to remain two people who faced each other.

highlights.text: opposite but equal to each other

records.jp: 「……自分がこわくなりました」
records.en: Taichi: "...I had become horrifying."
records.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator became afraid of himself. The English instead says that he became an object of horror, changing the experiencer and proposition.
records.remedy: ...I became afraid of myself.

highlights.text: I had become horrifying.

records.jp: 「けど自殺はできません。自決だけは」
records.en: Taichi: "But I could not kill myself. That is self-determination!"
comments: 自決 "self-determination" is used in the blatant concept, but also literally means suicide. For a pseudo-Nietzscheian like Taichi, it's definitely an odd term to bring up, especially if he meant it just as a flat synonym. -GHS
records.assessment: Here 自決 means taking one's own life, reinforcing the preceding statement that he cannot commit suicide. It does not mean self-determination, and the English invents an affirmative exclamation.
records.remedy: But I couldn't kill myself. Suicide was the one thing I couldn't do.

highlights.text: That is self-determination!

records.jp: 「そんな俺と、いつもつきあってくれてる仲間のみんなには、いわゆる感謝というものをしてなくもないです」
records.en: Taichi: "And that is the kind of person I am, I haven't but never given something that could be called gratitude to all the people who are always around me."
