comments: Remembering how Higurashi had people's cross-dimension memories as nothing but unspecified Settei, though Umineko redefines this in a certain metasense, I'm once more reminded that Ryukishi doesn't seem to have understood what this part actually means, religiously speaking. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese concedes that the world may never advance even the tiniest bit. The English reverses this into the world advancing a little.
records.remedy: Even if the world never advances another inch

highlights.text: The world might be advancing just this little

records.jp: 「……はぁ……なんつうか、またその話が本当ならまた生き返るんだろうけど」
records.en: Taichi: "...sigh... why even, because if that thing you said's true then I'll just be reborn again."
records.assessment: The Japanese filler means 'how should I put it' or 'well,' not a question asking why.
records.remedy: how should I put this

highlights.text: why even

records.jp: 「……霧ちんが悪意ノイローゼになったのもありますけど、あっという間にキレかけてましたよね？」
records.en: Miki: "...Kiri-chin can also end up being neurotically malicious, did you see how she just snapped in the blink of an eye?"
records.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri developed a neurosis or fixation concerning others' malice. The English instead describes Kiri herself as malicious.
records.remedy: Kiri-chin also became neurotic about people's malice

highlights.text: can also end up being neurotically malicious

records.jp: 「これ、霧ちんがいつだか先輩を責めるときに使った言葉です」
records.en: Miki: "Those are the words that Kiri-chin sometimes uses when she wants to torment you, Senpai."
comments: And they are wrong applied to Taichi. Or rather, they apply to everyone. Because the more one pretends to be a person... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to words Kiri used on one unspecified occasion when accusing or reproaching him. The English changes that to a recurring habit and strengthens reproach into torment.
records.remedy: used once when she was accusing you

highlights.text: sometimes uses when she wants to torment you

records.jp: 「あ、そういう展開になったことがあるですよ」
records.en: Miki: "Ah, when things have unfolded that way, of course."
comments: See CCC3009. She was looking then... and likely as well when they had sex. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says there was a loop in which events unfolded that way. The English makes it a conditional-like fragment and adds 'of course.'
records.remedy: There was a time things unfolded that way.

highlights.text: when things have unfolded that way, of course

records.jp: 「でも、そんなことをしている時は、ただ無邪気なままの自分でいられて……先輩とばかやったり……みんなと部活したり……」
records.en: Miki: "But, while I'm doing all that, I must be the normal innocent myself... playing the fool with Senpai... doing club activities with everyone..."
records.assessment: The Japanese says those activities let her remain her ordinary innocent self. The English changes that enabling relation into an obligation.
records.remedy: I can just remain my usual innocent self

highlights.text: I must be the normal innocent myself

records.jp: 「それはもう……今のわたしとは違う人ですから……」
records.en: Miki: "That's already... because I, as I am now, am already a different person..."
comments: Ah, now we get to the real point of attrition of resetting vs. not resetting (though it's still not in the deepest reading). You stop being yourself whether you become someone else during sleep or not. Merely adding information is change. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the person after a future reset would no longer be the present her. The English says the present self is already a different person, reversing the temporal comparison.
records.remedy: because whoever comes after that won't be the me I am now

highlights.text: because I, as I am now, am already a different person

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃんとかもっと別物だぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "But Youko-chan, to say, she's way something else."
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom says Youko is on an entirely different level. The English is syntactically malformed and does not state the comparison clearly.
records.remedy: Youko-chan is on a whole different level.

highlights.text: But Youko-chan, to say, she's way something else.

records.jp: 「あの人は……完璧に近いものではありますけど……まとまっただけの人間そのものじゃないですか」
records.en: Miki: "That person's... she's something close to completeness, yet... she's just not a congruous human in the literal sense of the word, isn't she?"
comments: This is what Taichi thinks. She's still tossing his words back at him. She might not even quite understand them. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese characterizes her as nearly perfect but still simply a well-integrated human being. The English negates her being a coherent human and substantially reverses the claim.
records.remedy: she's close to perfect, but isn't she still just a thoroughly put-together human being?

highlights.text: she's just not a congruous human in the literal sense of the word

records.jp: 「いらんわい！」
records.en: Taichi: "Don'want it, no!"
comments: girly... -GHS
records.assessment: The dialogue contains an unmistakable missing letter and spacing error.
records.remedy: Don't want

highlights.text: Don'want

records.jp: 「具はいくら」
records.en: Miki: "Got some garnishes."
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies the rice-ball filling as salmon roe. The English neither identifies the ingredient nor correctly expresses a filling.
records.remedy: The filling is salmon roe.

highlights.text: Got some garnishes.

records.jp: 「少しは疑問に思ってくださいよ」
records.en: Miki: "You have questions, so please think about them a little."
records.assessment: She tells him to show at least some doubt about the situation. The English instead asserts that he already has questions and asks him to ponder them.
records.remedy: At least question this a little!

highlights.text: You have questions, so please think about them a little.

records.jp: 「……んー、なんとか暴走がおさまっていたっぽいのと……あと」
records.en: Miki: "...hmmm, somehow or other the rampancy seems to have quieted... after that."
comments: Once again, he never was rampant. He only tried to lure in Kiri, and that was pure self-defense. Either Miki doesn't understand, or Taichi going rampant means nothing what it seems. ...unless she's not referring to him, but the alternative would be Kiri. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese trails into an additional reason: his rampage seemed to have subsided, and besides that.... The English turns the connector into temporal sequence and drops the unfinished second reason.
records.remedy: and besides that...

highlights.text: after that

records.jp: 顔が赤い。
records.en: And face goes red.
records.assessment: The English omits the determiner or possessor required to identify whose face reddens.
records.remedy: Her face goes red.

highlights.text: And face goes red.

records.jp: 「なんかな、そういうのを好きになってくれるヤツもいるってのは、ありがたいことだよな」
records.en: Taichi: "Really, that I'd still become someone that someone else could fall in love with, got some thankfulness for that."
records.assessment: The Japanese expresses gratitude that someone can love that aspect or version of him. The English adds a transformation into becoming a lovable person.
records.remedy: there are people who can love that side of me

highlights.text: I'd still become someone that someone else could fall in love with

records.jp: 整った造作が、わずかに位置を変えて、見事に疑問を表現した。
records.en: Well-ordered facial features just barely modify their position, as a possibility is magnificently expressed in the form of question:
comments: Might as well be talking Youko and be that the end of it. This is possibly what Youko felt about Taichi back then, and Miki's may be the same as Youko's as far as Onigiri ultramarines go. -GHS
records.assessment: The facial shift beautifully expresses a question or puzzlement, not a possibility.
records.remedy: beautifully expressed a question

highlights.text: a possibility is magnificently expressed

records.jp: 「……で、霧ちんはどうだった？」
records.en: Taichi: "...so, what does Kiri-chin do?"
comments: present as it's multiple events -GHS
records.assessment: He asks how Kiri reacted on those occasions, not what she generally does in the present.
records.remedy: how did Kiri-chin react?

highlights.text: what does Kiri-chin do?

records.jp: 「……まー、相応の対応を受けました」
records.en: Miki: "...ohhh, she is met with suitable measures."
comments: Might not be the horrible thing that seems obvious. After all, she's talking about how KIRI reacts. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says she herself received the response or treatment one would expect. The English changes the recipient to Kiri and shifts the event into the present passive.
records.remedy: I got the response you'd expect.

highlights.text: she is met with suitable measures

records.jp: 「俺も似たようなものだなあ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's sort of how I was, then."
comments: Meaning he accepts that Youko doesn't really care about him. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says he is much the same now; the English incorrectly relegates the comparison to the past.
records.remedy: how I am, too

highlights.text: how I was

records.jp: 「帰ります。先輩はそこの金庫にあるわたしの想像を絶するレベルのＨな本でひとりえっちでもしててください」
records.en: Miki: "I'm going home. Senpai, please open that safe over there and use those porn books of levels by me unimaginable to have self-sex."
comments: See CCB2009. Nice to remind us of one of the most blatant metaphors for Taichi not being the monster he seems to be. -GHS
records.assessment: Although the underlying propositions are present, the English construction is grammatically incoherent and does not yield a usable instruction.
records.remedy: use the unimaginably filthy porn books in that safe to take care of yourself

highlights.text: use those porn books of levels by me unimaginable to have self-sex

records.jp: 知ってる！
records.en: She knew it!
records.assessment: The narrator exclaims that Miki knows about his hidden books. The English instead says that some female subject knew an unspecified fact, reversing the deixis and subject.
records.remedy: You knew about them!

highlights.text: She knew it!

records.jp: 「くす……だってぇ、普段のセクハラのイメージしかないんですから」
records.en: Miki: "Heh... but, this only gives me that image of normal everyday sexual harassment, that's why!"
records.assessment: She says her usual image of him is nothing but sexual harassment. The English instead says the present situation gives her that image.
records.remedy: because my usual image of you is nothing but sexual harassment

highlights.text: this only gives me that image of normal everyday sexual harassment

records.jp: 鼻を噛まれた。
records.en: Nose was bit.
records.assessment: The passive construction omits the possessor and uses the wrong participle.
records.remedy: My nose was bitten.

highlights.text: Nose was bit.

records.jp: ……勃った。
records.en: ...I erected.
records.assessment: The Japanese says he got an erection. The English's transitive verb makes the narrator erect an unspecified object and does not express the bodily event.
records.remedy: ...I got hard.

highlights.text: I erected.

records.jp: 制服をキッチリ着こなした美希がいた。
records.en: A Miki punctually wearing her uniform was among us.
records.assessment: The Japanese presents Miki neatly and properly dressed in her uniform. The English substitutes punctuality and adds an unsupported group in which she is present.
records.remedy: There stood Miki, neatly dressed in her uniform.

highlights.text: punctually wearing her uniform was among us

records.jp: 「うむー」
records.en: Taichi: Yeppp'."
comments: 3xp like a triple futanari and her three penises. -GHS
records.assessment: The dialogue has mismatched apostrophe and quotation punctuation.
records.remedy: Taichi: "Yeppp."

highlights.text: Taichi: Yeppp'."

records.jp: 「え、どうやって？」
records.en: Miki: "Eh, but how'd you do it?
records.assessment: The dialogue line lacks its closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Miki: "Eh, but how'd you do it?"

highlights.text: Miki: "Eh, but how'd you do it?

records.jp: 「俺も部活に行こうっと」
records.en: Taichi: "I also want to go to Club."
records.assessment: The Japanese expresses an immediate decision to go to the club, not merely a desire.
records.remedy: I'll head to the club too.

highlights.text: I also want to go to Club.

records.jp: 「そうですか」
records.en: Miki: "So you are."
records.assessment: The response means 'I see' or resigned acknowledgment, not an assertion about what the addressee is.
records.remedy: I see.

highlights.text: So you are.

records.jp: 「それぞれの先輩は、同一人物じゃないんですよ？」
records.en: Miki: "Ever one of you, Senpai is... not the exact same person, you know?"
comments: Which once again brings us to the loop not being anything of the sort. If Taichi's different every time despite the reset, either the reset is fake, or he's more than memories and molecules - which amounts to the same thing. The parallels with Yusa who was only shown his surface (but was that all she saw?) continue. -GHS
records.assessment: The English contains a typo and a broken agreement structure that obscures the reference to each weekly version of him.
records.remedy: Every version of you, Senpai, is

highlights.text: Ever one of you, Senpai is

records.jp: 「まあ甘えたかったら、いつでもその時々の黒須太一を頼ってくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, if you want to be fawned on, you can always depend on the occasional Kurosu Taichi!"
records.assessment: He tells her to rely on whichever Kurosu Taichi exists in a given loop whenever she wants comfort or indulgence. 'Be fawned on' reverses the social action, and 'occasional' misstates the loop-specific identity.
records.remedy: if you ever want someone to lean on, rely on whichever Kurosu Taichi is there that week

highlights.text: if you want to be fawned on, you can always depend on the occasional Kurosu Taichi

records.jp: 屋上で霧を助けた時の動き。
records.en: but also in her movements when she rescued Miki on the rooftop.
records.assessment: The Japanese says Miki rescued Kiri on the rooftop. The English replaces the rescued person with Miki herself.
records.remedy: when she rescued Kiri on the rooftop

highlights.text: when she rescued Miki on the rooftop

records.jp: 助け船を出す。
records.en: I launch a lifeboat.
records.assessment: The idiom means that he throws her a conversational lifeline or comes to her aid. The English renders a literal nautical action.
records.remedy: I throw her a lifeline.

highlights.text: I launch a lifeboat.

records.jp: 「俺は目だけはいいからわかるんだけどね」
records.en: Taichi: "All that's good of me are my eyes, so I understood this."
comments: Interesting he'd praise his eyes now, of all things... -GHS
records.assessment: He says his eyesight or powers of observation are good, not that his eyes are the only good thing about him.
records.remedy: I've got good eyes, so I could tell.

highlights.text: All that's good of me are my eyes

records.jp: 「あれは打算する者の動きではなかった」
records.en: Taichi: "Those where not the motions of a calculating self-interested person."
comments: She outgrew her problem, IOW. The problem is, without someone else rubbing her face in it, she doesn't know. This is the same thing with Taichi and HIS problem! -GHS
records.assessment: The line uses the adverb 'where' in place of the past-tense verb 'were.'
records.remedy: Those were not

highlights.text: Those where not

records.jp: 「あとこれ、日記。しっかり祠におさめておいてくれよ」
records.en: Taichi: "And then, here, the diary. Be sure to offer it to the inside of that hokora."
records.assessment: He asks her to store or place the diary securely in the shrine. The English's 'offer it to the inside' changes the action into a malformed ritual offering.
records.remedy: make sure you put it safely inside the shrine

highlights.text: offer it to the inside of that hokora

records.jp: 受けとる手が弱々しい。
records.en: A slender, frail, feminine hands receives it.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the hand receiving it is weak or unsteady. The English has number disagreement and adds unsupported physical descriptors.
records.remedy: The hand that takes it looks weak.

highlights.text: A slender, frail, feminine hands receives it.

records.jp: この挨拶は気に入った。
records.en: That farewell I found suitable.
comments: Hapchew! Did I get a cold? -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he liked the farewell, not merely that he judged it suitable.
records.remedy: I liked that farewell.

highlights.text: found suitable

records.jp: 自己犠牲は、ひるがえせば全て自分のための行いとも言えるのだから。
records.en: it's because if one tries to take their self-sacrifices back, they'll all become acts that can be said to have been merely performed for the sake of the self.
comments: Except, even with the loop, the past can't be taken back. The only way to make this work is for some future event to make these nothing but the expectable stumbling of an infant trying to learn to walk. This would still require Christian philosophy to really work. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that, viewed from the reverse side, every act of self-sacrifice can be considered an act for oneself. It does not describe retracting prior sacrifices.
records.remedy: looked at another way, every act of self-sacrifice can be called an act for oneself

highlights.text: if one tries to take their self-sacrifices back

records.jp: 見里先輩を……姉を恨むあまり。
records.en: Too much resentment for Mimi-senpai... her Aneki.
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies Mimi-senpai as Tomoki's elder sister. The English uses a female possessor and leaves the kinship term untranslated.
records.remedy: his older sister

highlights.text: her Aneki

records.jp: 邪魔したんだ。
records.en: This was just in the way.
records.assessment: The Japanese says Tomoki interfered or tried to obstruct what his sister was doing. The English instead makes an unspecified object merely be in the way.
records.remedy: He tried to stop her.

highlights.text: This was just in the way.

records.assessment: Nanaka agrees with Taichi's advice. The English instead turns the response into a skeptical question.
records.remedy: You're right.

highlights.text: Is it now.

records.jp: 手を合わされる。
records.en: She joined my hand with hers.
records.assessment: Nanaka presses her own palms together in a pleading gesture. The English instead makes her take and join Taichi's hand.
records.remedy: She presses her palms together.

highlights.text: She joined my hand with hers.

records.jp: 見ればフレンドリーな幽霊。
records.en: From the look of it, this a friendly specter.
comments: CTRL+SHIFT+F-> Find what: Nanaka / Replace with: Casper -> Replace in Files -> OK -GHS
records.assessment: The English noun phrase lacks the finite verb 'is.'
records.remedy: this is a friendly specter

highlights.text: this a friendly specter

records.jp: 俺に危害を加えてくることはあるまい。
records.en: It doesn't seem like she's going to inflict me harm.
records.assessment: The verb 'inflict' requires the harm as its direct object and the recipient after 'on.'
records.remedy: inflict harm on me

highlights.text: inflict me harm

records.jp: 親指を鳴らした。
records.en: I creaked my thumb.
comments: The base joint, you know, with the rest of the hand. It's hard to explain without pictures of lolis, though a bit easier with normal pictures. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator snaps his thumb or fingers. 'Creaked' describes a prolonged friction sound and does not express the gesture.
records.remedy: I snap my fingers.

highlights.text: I creaked my thumb.

records.jp: 俺にとっては、昨日の今日。
records.en: For me, it was yesterday like today.
comments: This is like the first time that he's acknowledged that the day before was 'that' Sunday 6/9. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom says this comes immediately after what happened yesterday. The English compares yesterday to today and is semantically incoherent.
records.remedy: for me, it had only happened yesterday

highlights.text: it was yesterday like today

records.jp: 七香はいなくなっていた。
records.en: Nanaka wasn't anymore.
records.assessment: The Japanese says Nanaka was gone. The English leaves the negative copula without the complement identifying what no longer held.
records.remedy: Nanaka was gone.

highlights.text: Nanaka wasn't anymore.

records.jp: 「あれ？　ななかー？」
records.en: Nanaka: "Eh? Nanakaaa?"
records.assessment: The narrator is calling for Nanaka after she vanishes. The English labels Nanaka as the speaker, making her call her own name.
records.remedy: Taichi: "Huh? Nanaka?"

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Eh? Nanakaaa?"

records.jp: 軽い気持ちで観音開きの扉をあけた。
records.en: Without taking things too seriously, I opened the hinged doors.
records.assessment: The Japanese specifically describes a pair of double doors opening from the center. Merely calling them hinged omits the distinguishing structure.
records.remedy: the double doors

highlights.text: the hinged doors

records.jp: 変哲のない学生ノートの束だ。
records.en: Student's notebooks of no unusuality.
comments: CP CCC0007
records.assessment: The English uses an unsupported singular possessive and the non-idiomatic abstraction 'no unusuality' for ordinary school notebooks.
records.remedy: A stack of perfectly ordinary school notebooks.

highlights.text: Student's notebooks of no unusuality.

records.jp: 他に何かからくりがあればともかく。
records.en: Even if there's some other trick, regardless,
comments: This is why I'm a lolroffle hyperliteral translator, because if I had to adapt this to what it actually means, the above would be simply "COUGH HINT HINT COUGH" -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese qualifies the conclusion with 'unless there is some other trick.' The English uses 'even if' and 'regardless,' reversing the exception into irrelevance.
records.remedy: Unless there's some other trick to it, anyway.

highlights.text: Even if there's some other trick, regardless,

records.jp: どのノートを見ても、脳天気ではあるけど……。
records.en: Looking at all these notebook, there's all this optimism in there, but...
comments: Remember the 'bad' ones are missing. -GHS
records.assessment: The plural demonstrative requires the plural noun 'notebooks.'
records.remedy: all these notebooks

highlights.text: all these notebook

records.jp: 「なんか全部、絶望的なあがきみたいだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Just, all of it, it all seems like of a hopeless struggle."
records.assessment: The construction incorrectly combines 'seems like' with an additional 'of.'
records.remedy: it all seems like a hopeless struggle

highlights.text: it all seems like of a hopeless struggle

records.jp: あの子も、知っていた？
records.en: Do I... know her?
records.assessment: The narrator wonders whether Nanaka also knew about the loop and shrine. The English instead asks whether he is acquainted with her.
records.remedy: Did she know too?

highlights.text: Do I... know her?

records.jp: 万が一に俺が忘れたとしても……曜子ちゃんなら自力で真実までたどり着くだろう。
records.en: Thousand will give you one that I even if I forget... Youko-chan can eventually reach the truth on her own power alone, definitely.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that even in the unlikely event that the narrator forgets, Youko can reach the truth herself. The English is grammatically incoherent and fails to convey the conditional.
records.remedy: Even if by some chance I forget... Youko-chan will reach the truth on her own.

highlights.text: Thousand will give you one that I even if I forget...

records.jp: ノートを見れば、今俺が考えた程度の結論には、瞬時に到達できるはずだ。
records.en: If she looks at the notebooks, she could likely reach in a single instant a final word of the same level as the one I, as I presently am, just thought up.
comments: CP CCC0008B
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to a conclusion at the same level as the one he reached, not a final utterance or final word.
records.remedy: the same sort of conclusion

highlights.text: a final word

records.jp: とりあえず俺がすべきこと。
records.en: For the time being,
comments: PCP CCC0008B
Moved some stuff below. -GHS
records.assessment: The source introduces a list as 'What I should do for now.' The English omits the obligation and leaves only a temporal connector.
records.remedy: What I should do for now:

highlights.text: For the time being,

records.jp: 「き、昨日の夜にわかってたことだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Y-, you didn't get that part yesterday night?"
comments: Indeed. That's because she's faking it, or, at least, taking the 98 game as seriously as Taichi is, meaning the difference between fake and real is borderline irrelevant. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi reminds her that she already knew this last night. The English instead asks whether she failed to understand some unspecified part.
records.remedy: You already knew that last night, didn't you?

highlights.text: you didn't get that part yesterday night?

records.jp: 「朝おきて、お母さんとかいなくて、ごはんもなくて……そんでみんなまでいなくなってたらって考えたら……」
records.en: Miki: "I woke up this morning, and mother wasn't there, and there wasn't to eat... and that's why I started thinking, what if everybody else is gone too, and..."
comments: Keeping "gohan" as breakfast, but she could literally mean that there was no rice in her breakfast. Her mother simply goes to work earlier than she goes to school, which would be normal given they have a commute, and Miki is either expected to buy something at Tasaki on the tab, cook something up herself, or has breakfast that doesn't involve rice - Taichi's never has. See CCA0004: that's another reason Miki's tab is brought up. Nothing in here that demands the end of mankind. -GHS
records.assessment: The construction omits the required subject or object for the absence of food.
records.remedy: there was nothing to eat

highlights.text: there wasn't to eat

records.jp: 人が一生を懸命に、後悔なく生きる様にも似て。
records.en: People doing their absolute hardest in life live in ways that resemble having no regrets.
records.assessment: The Japanese likens their compressed week to the way people strive to live a whole lifetime without regret. The English makes people themselves resemble a state of having no regrets and obscures the comparison.
records.remedy: Like people striving to live an entire lifetime without regrets.

highlights.text: People doing their absolute hardest in life live in ways that resemble having no regrets.

records.jp: 「痴漢じゃない！」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm not molester!"
records.assessment: The singular count noun requires an article.
records.remedy: I'm not a molester!

highlights.text: I'm not molester!

records.jp: ダッシュ！
records.en: Dassh'u!
comments: CP CCC0011C
records.assessment: The source uses the ordinary loanword 'dash' as an action cry. The English introduces pseudo-Japanese romanization rather than translating or preserving the English loanword.
records.remedy: Dash!

highlights.text: Dassh'u!

records.jp: 部室類は、廊下側にも窓がはめ込まれている。
records.en: Our club room has windows inlaid in the wall towards the corridor,
records.assessment: The Japanese generalizes that club rooms of this type have corridor-facing windows. The English narrows the plural class to one possessive room.
records.remedy: The club rooms have windows

highlights.text: Our club room has windows

records.jp: 「気になってさ。特に意味はないよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "It just bothered me. Doesn't have to have meaning."
comments: See CCA0029. Interesting progress. The problem with this is another: this is Monday. That thing's been draping off for how long now? And it didn't matter before. The reason would be simple: the Club Room isn't being used that much anymore, and it's been a while since it has been in use serious enough to need the camouflage. And the same is simply true now. -GHS
records.assessment: Tomoki states that fixing it has no special meaning. The English instead says meaningfulness is not required, leaving open that it may have meaning.
records.remedy: There isn't any special meaning to it.

highlights.text: Doesn't have to have meaning.

records.jp: 「なにがなにやら……」
records.en: Tomoki: "Something happened who knows what..."
comments: Careful on the progress: "there's no one" could be in the club room. This one could be "yeah, there's nobody here". -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom means he has no idea what is going on. The English combines an assertion and embedded question without a grammatical relation.
records.remedy: I have no idea what's going on...

highlights.text: Something happened who knows what...

records.jp: 友貴は、みみ先輩を恨んでいるんだったな。
records.en: Tomoki was bearing a grudge on Mimi-senpai,
records.assessment: The idiomatic preposition is 'against,' not 'on.'
records.remedy: a grudge against Mimi-senpai

highlights.text: a grudge on Mimi-senpai

records.jp: 苗字が違うのは、いろいろ事情があるらしい。
records.en: As to why their last name is different, there seem to circumstances of all sorts.
records.assessment: The existential construction is missing the verb 'be.'
records.remedy: there seem to be all sorts of circumstances

highlights.text: there seem to circumstances

records.jp: 「ああ、午後から動くよ。学校にはちょっと様子見に来ただけだし」
records.en: Tomoki: "Yeah, I'll be getting to work after noon. I just came to school to see how's things a bit."
records.assessment: The embedded clause requires statement word order and plural agreement.
records.remedy: to see how things are

highlights.text: to see how's things

records.jp: 気を静めないと。
records.en: For if I can't calm myself...
records.assessment: The narrator tells himself that he must calm down. The English creates an unfinished conditional about being unable to do so and adds a causal connector.
records.remedy: I have to calm myself down.

highlights.text: For if I can't calm myself...

records.jp: 「なあ友貴」
records.en: Tomoki: "Say, Tomoki."
records.assessment: Taichi addresses Tomoki. The English labels Tomoki as the speaker, making him address himself by name.
records.remedy: Taichi: "Hey, Tomoki."

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Say, Tomoki."

records.jp: 「マンガとかじゃ、そーいう諍いからいろいろ崩壊したりするんだけど」
records.en: Taichi: "With manga and the like we've had quarrels that have led to all sorts of downfalls, though."
records.assessment: Taichi says that in manga, quarrels like this can make all sorts of things fall apart. The English says the speakers themselves have had such ruinous quarrels.
records.remedy: in manga, quarrels like that can make everything fall apart

highlights.text: we've had quarrels that have led to all sorts of downfalls

records.jp: 教室の隅にダンボール箱が転がっている。
records.en: In the corner of the classroom lays a cardboard box.
records.assessment: The intransitive description requires 'lies,' not the transitive verb 'lays.'
records.remedy: lies a cardboard box

highlights.text: lays a cardboard box

records.jp: 動物化する俺。
records.en: I animalize.
comments: Hegel/Kojev and more postmodernism stuff maybe? whatever it's not MK3 for odd reasons. Anyway, if this is him turning into an animal, a beast, then the above are the signs. And it's all perfectly innocent, in the end. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he becomes animalistic. 'Animalize' is normally transitive and means to turn something into an animal.
records.remedy: I turn into an animal.

highlights.text: I animalize.

records.jp: どうしてカメラを、持ってこなかったんだ……俺は？
records.en: How come a camera you didn't bring with... myself?
records.assessment: The narrator asks himself why he did not bring a camera. The English shifts to second person, strands the object, and appends a contradictory reflexive.
records.remedy: Why didn't I bring a camera... with me?

highlights.text: How come a camera you didn't bring with... myself?

records.jp: どうして！　今！　この場で！　カメラを持てない！
records.en: WHY! RIGHT NOW! RIGHT HERE! YOU HAVE NO CAMERA!
comments: The secret of CCC4001 is revealed. It's totally pics of Kiri adjusting a cameltoe taken from the Miki House. Unreset Miki would eventually find this occasion. Once more, the role reversal is attempted. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator angrily asks why he himself does not have a camera here and now. The English directs the statement at a second person.
records.remedy: WHY DON'T I HAVE A CAMERA!

highlights.text: YOU HAVE NO CAMERA!

records.jp: モノローグを力強く区切り、猛省の嵐に身を置く。
records.en: Vigorously punctuating a monologue, I lay my self whole into the thunderstorm of deep soul-searching.
records.assessment: The reflexive is incorrectly split and the verb/preposition construction is non-idiomatic.
records.remedy: I throw my whole self into

highlights.text: I lay my self whole into

records.jp: 霧のハレンチは、それだけでは終わらない。
records.en: And Kiri's shamelessness does not have end with that alone.
records.assessment: The English uses 'have end' instead of the required verb phrase 'end' and attaches an unnatural qualifier.
records.remedy: does not end there

highlights.text: does not have end with that alone

records.jp: スカートがするっと落ちた。
records.en: The skirt falls with a smooth sound.
records.assessment: The adverb describes the skirt slipping smoothly down, not the quality of a sound.
records.remedy: slips smoothly down

highlights.text: falls with a smooth sound

records.jp: なんと下着をずりおろした！
records.en: What a sliding down of underwear we had!
records.assessment: The narration exclaims that Kiri pulled her underwear down. The English removes her agency and invents a shared event involving 'we.'
records.remedy: She actually pulled her underwear down!

highlights.text: What a sliding down of underwear we had!

records.jp: 何気ない少女の痴態。
records.en: The unconcerned silliness of a girl.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes an unselfconscious indecent display or compromising posture. 'Silliness' removes the erotic impropriety that drives the reaction.
records.remedy: A girl's casual indecent display.

highlights.text: The unconcerned silliness of a girl.

records.jp: 汚れた、ではなく漏れた、というところにくるモンがあった。
records.en: Summing up this pwecious situation as being not filthied, but leaking.
comments: This is actually another Biblical thing. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says something about her choice of 'leaked' rather than 'stained' strongly affected or aroused him. The English instead calls the situation precious and does not state its effect on him.
records.remedy: Something about her saying 'leaked,' not 'stained,' really got to me.

highlights.text: Summing up this pwecious situation as being not filthied, but leaking.

records.jp: 霧が窓際によりかかると同時に、
records.en: Simultaneously with Kiri going to lean over the window,
records.assessment: Kiri leans against or rests by the window. 'Lean over the window' suggests bending across or outside it.
records.remedy: lean against the window

highlights.text: lean over the window

records.jp: 「あ、黒須……先輩！」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, Kurosu... senpai!"
records.assessment: Kiri recognizes and addresses Kurosu-senpai. The English labels Taichi as the speaker, making him address himself.
records.remedy: Kiri: "Ah, Kurosu... senpai!"

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, Kurosu... senpai!"

records.jp: パニクっとるパニクっとる。
records.en: Gooo panic, gooo panic!
records.assessment: The narrator gleefully observes that she is panicking. The English turns the observation into an instruction encouraging panic.
records.remedy: She's panicking, she's panicking.

highlights.text: Gooo panic, gooo panic!

records.jp: 「霧のぱんつ」
records.en: Taichi: "Kiri no Panties."
comments: Kiri's panties + Kiri nopan[tsu]. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese possessive particle is left untranslated inside an otherwise English line.
records.remedy: Kiri's panties.

highlights.text: Kiri no Panties.

records.jp: おたおた。逃げ腰。
records.en: Shocked speechless. Get ready to flee.
records.assessment: The Japanese depicts her flustered and already shrinking back or poised to escape. The English substitutes speechlessness and an imperative to prepare.
records.remedy: She flails, edging backward to flee.

highlights.text: Shocked speechless. Get ready to flee.

records.jp: 「……可憐なヘアもな」
records.en: Taichi: "...and your touchingly sweet hair too."
records.assessment: In context the euphemistic ヘア refers to the delicate pubic hair he glimpsed. The English can only naturally be read as praising the hair on her head.
records.remedy: your delicate little patch of hair

highlights.text: your touchingly sweet hair

records.jp: 「朝からいいものが見られた。ありがとう、霧っち」
records.en: Taichi: "It's just morning and you're already showing me the good stuff. Thank your, Kiricchi."
records.assessment: The object pronoun has an extraneous final letter.
records.remedy: Thank you

highlights.text: Thank your

records.jp: 「それでうち解けたところで相談なんだけど……昼飯でも一緒にどうかなって」
records.en: Taichi: "But in case you wish to have a personal consultation about that... how about we also have lunch together, maybe."
records.assessment: Taichi jokes that now they have broken the ice, he has a proposal: lunch together. The English invents a consultation that Kiri might request about the incident.
records.remedy: Now that we've broken the ice, I wanted to ask if you'd have lunch with me.

highlights.text: in case you wish to have a personal consultation about that

records.jp: 泣きはらしたな。
records.en: She really weeped her heart out.
comments: This is the consequences of her Reset. -GHS
records.assessment: The past tense of 'weep' is 'wept.'
records.remedy: wept

highlights.text: weeped

records.jp: かなりアンダーなテンションだ。
records.en: Spirits seems kind of under.
records.assessment: The subject and verb disagree, and 'under' does not idiomatically mean low or depressed spirits.
records.remedy: Her spirits are extremely low.

highlights.text: Spirits seems kind of under.

records.jp: 「不安っす」
records.en: Miki: "Me's uneasy."
records.assessment: The first-person subject requires 'I'm,' not object-form 'me' plus a possessive contraction.
records.remedy: I'm uneasy.

highlights.text: Me's uneasy.

records.jp: 「景気づけをしてやろう」
records.en: Taichi: "I'll put some Seaman's Spirit onto ya!"
records.assessment: Taichi says he will cheer her up or give her a morale boost. The English invents a sailor-like substance applied to her.
records.remedy: I'll give you a little morale boost.

highlights.text: put some Seaman's Spirit onto ya

records.jp: あっさり揉めた。
records.en: Quickly and lightly I went over it.
comments: I'll never translate 揉 plainly will I. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he easily manages to grope or knead her breast. 'Went over it' removes the sexual physical action.
records.remedy: I managed to grope it with ease.

highlights.text: I went over it.

records.jp: まったいらな少年のような胸に、ブラは必要ないのだ。
records.en: But that plumb boylike chest needs no bra.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes her chest as completely flat and boyish. 'Plumb' means exactly, vertically aligned, or measured depth and does not mean flat.
records.remedy: that perfectly flat, boyish chest

highlights.text: that plumb boylike chest

records.jp: きっとこいつには、他に行く場所なんてありはしないんだ。
records.en: That this gal hasn't got any other place to go other than here, for sure.
records.assessment: The source is a complete assertion. The English begins with a subordinating 'that' and never supplies a governing clause.
records.remedy: I'm sure this girl has nowhere else to go.

highlights.text: That this gal hasn't got any other place to go other than here, for sure.

records.jp: ただそれだけの行動に、無数のメッセージがこもっていそうだ。
records.en: Yet, that mere behavior seems to seclude a countless number of messages.
comments: Same exact term as above, obviously intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says the tiny action seems to contain countless messages. 'Seclude' means isolate a person or thing from others and cannot express semantic containment.
records.remedy: seems to contain countless messages

highlights.text: seems to seclude a countless number of messages

records.jp: 「むにっ」
records.en: Taichi: "Boobnyah!"
comments: AKA touch on the boobs. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a comic sound accompanying another cheek pinch. The English explicitly invents a breast reference absent from the Japanese and immediate action.
records.remedy: Squish!

highlights.text: Boobnyah!

records.jp: 「そーゆーのを世間は馬鹿にするじゃない！」
records.en: Touko: "And isn't that the reason why the world would see me as stupid!"
comments: ...but there's no one else... -GHS
records.assessment: Touko says society mocks or calls people like that stupid. The English narrows the target to Touko personally and makes the issue how she appears.
records.remedy: that's exactly the sort of person society calls stupid

highlights.text: the world would see me as stupid

records.jp: 「だから、闘うんだろ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, struggle on!"
comments: See CCC4007? -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that is why she has to fight. The English turns the statement of necessity into a cheer or command to continue.
records.remedy: That's why you fight, isn't it?

highlights.text: Well then, struggle on!

records.jp: 「ですわ言葉のおばさん予備軍」
records.en: Taichi: "Usage of shan't tied to likelihood of being predestined to becoming an old bag."
comments: You a newspaper article now? Notice the complete and total nonsequitur. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi mocks her feminine ですわ-style speech as marking her for the ranks of future middle-aged women. The English substitutes the unrelated contraction 'shan't' and becomes grammatically incoherent.
records.remedy: You're in the future-old-lady brigade with that 'desu wa' speech.

highlights.text: Usage of shan't tied to likelihood of being predestined to becoming an old bag.

records.jp: 「ぬぁんですってーっ！？」
records.en: Touko: "WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID?!?"
comments: CP CCB004C
records.assessment: The shouted question uses an impossible contraction and the past form 'said' after the auxiliary.
records.remedy: WHAAAT DID YOU SAAAAY?!

highlights.text: WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID?!?

records.jp: ノートにあった着火のススメに則って、冬子を活気づけるか。
records.en: Can I revitalize Touko by igniting her, as is recommended in the notebooks?
records.assessment: The narrator resolves to enliven Touko by provoking her, following the notebook's recommendation. The English turns that decision into a question about whether he is able to do it.
records.remedy: I'll fire Touko up, following the notebook's recommendation.

highlights.text: Can I revitalize Touko

records.jp: ……かどうかはともかく、頑張れ。
records.en: ...or maybe it won't, regardless, she'll do her best.
records.assessment: The narrator inwardly tells Touko to hang in there. The English instead predicts that she will do her best.
records.remedy: whether that's true or not, hang in there.

highlights.text: she'll do her best

records.jp: 「そうです。何も起こらなければ、ここは……」
records.en: Misato: "Right then. If nothing goes wrong, because us being here..."
comments: "It's dangerous because we could jump" + "it's forbidden", see below (and the multiple times Misato jumps). -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese begins a conditional statement that if nothing had happened, this place or project would have proceeded. The English inserts 'because,' uses an object pronoun as a subject, and fails to convey the clause.
records.remedy: Yes. If nothing had happened, this place would have...

highlights.text: If nothing goes wrong, because us being here...

records.jp: 傷ついてさえいないのだから、俺は。
records.en: because I don't hurt in the slightest, I don't.
records.assessment: The narrator says he is not even emotionally hurt. 'I don't hurt' instead normally means he does not feel physical pain or does not harm others.
records.remedy: I'm not even hurt in the slightest.

highlights.text: I don't hurt in the slightest

records.jp: 「まあ、そのせいで屋上に行くのが禁止になったわけですから」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, because of 'that' coming to the rooftop had become forbidden."
comments: This is explicitly about Yutaka now. Though admittedly since it's Misato that can just be her adherence to rules talking, so the actual disappearance of mankind remains more than a little ambiguous still. -GHS
records.assessment: The adverbial phrase is incorrectly made the subject of 'had become,' leaving the causal sentence malformed.
records.remedy: because of that, going to the rooftop had been forbidden

highlights.text: because of 'that' coming to the rooftop had become forbidden

records.jp: 「……今さら手伝いましょうかってのも、虫の良い話なんでしょうね」
records.en: Taichi: "...even if I said wanted to help after all, that would be simply selfishness talking, would it."
