records.remedy: she's often at home

highlights.text: she's often found home

records.jp: 「あ、こうなってるのかー」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, so that's how it happens then!"
comments: He may still be talking about her work at the antenna, trying to distract her. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi pretends to inspect how the antenna is physically put together. The English instead refers to how an unspecified event happens.
records.remedy: so this is how it's put together

highlights.text: so that's how it happens then

records.jp: 「いえ、超冷静ですー」
records.en: Taichi: "No, hyper awake I aaam!"
records.assessment: Taichi says he is extremely calm or clearheaded, denying that he is befuddled. Being awake only denies sleep and does not convey composure.
records.remedy: perfectly clearheaded

highlights.text: hyper awake

records.jp: だからといって、事故を見逃すってのは……。
records.en: But letting the incident just happen because of that...
records.assessment: He considers knowingly allowing an accident to occur. Calling it an 'incident' removes the unintended-danger sense central to the ethical hesitation.
records.remedy: letting the accident happen

highlights.text: letting the incident just happen

records.jp: 手を払われる。
records.en: A swat of her hands.
comments: PCP CCA0014A
HACK SFX -GHS
records.assessment: Touko swats the narrator's offered hand away. The English instead presents an action involving her own plural hands without an object.
records.remedy: She swats my hand away.

highlights.text: A swat of her hands.

records.jp: よたよたと歩いていく。
records.en: Walking in a widdle and with a waddle.
comments: Like drunk Misato. -GHS
records.assessment: Touko totters unsteadily from weakness. The English invents baby-talk and a side-to-side waddling gait.
records.remedy: She totters away unsteadily.

highlights.text: in a widdle and with a waddle

records.jp: 「自分しか自分の心配をしてくれる人間がいないのは、つらいだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you... it's painful, right?"
comments: CP CCA0014A
This older revision had a comma missing. -GHS
records.assessment: The English has number disagreement and a broken nested noun phrase, obscuring the statement that only she worries about herself.
records.remedy: It's painful when the only person who worries about you is yourself

highlights.text: Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you

records.jp: 「顔色悪いな。生理か？」
records.en: Taichi: "Your face looks off-color. Menses?"
comments: CP CCA0014A
Yup, here he's gotta be really worried. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi crudely asks whether she is on her period. The isolated clinical plural noun is not a natural spoken question and changes the register.
records.remedy: On your period?

highlights.text: Menses?

records.jp: 「……あんまいい死に方できないな、俺」
records.en: Taichi: "...that ain't a really good way to die, me."
comments: PCP CCA0014A
Maybe older revision, maybe it just changed. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator reflects that at this rate he cannot expect to die well. The English instead comments on an unspecified current manner of dying and appends a dislocated 'me.'
records.remedy: I'm not going to die a very good death, am I?

highlights.text: that ain't a really good way to die, me

records.jp: 拾う。
records.en: recovered.
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: The narrator picks the fallen paper bag up. The English uses a passive-like result with no actor or object movement.
records.remedy: I pick it up.

highlights.text: recovered.

records.jp: そっぽを向く。
records.en: Uncooperative.
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: The Japanese gives the visible action of turning her face away. The English substitutes a judgment of her disposition.
records.remedy: She turns away.

highlights.text: Uncooperative.

records.jp: 「こんなことになったからって、幸せっぽくても、いいじゃん？」
records.en: Taichi: "And because of all that's happened here, can't you just sort of be happy, or something?"
records.assessment: Taichi says that even though this situation has occurred, it should be permissible for her to appear happy. The English makes the situation a cause and directly demands happiness.
records.remedy: Even with everything that's happened, it's okay to look a little happy, isn't it?

highlights.text: because of all that's happened here, can't you just sort of be happy

records.jp: 攻撃したあと、へたりこんでいた。
records.en: Right after this strike, Touko collapses sitting on to the floor.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The construction combines incompatible motion and posture verbs and uses 'on to' incorrectly.
records.remedy: sinks down onto the floor

highlights.text: collapses sitting on to the floor

records.jp: 目頭を押さえて、青い顔をしている。
records.en: Holding her eyes shut, her face almost colorless.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko presses the inner corners of her eyes while pale and faint. The English instead says she closes and holds both eyes shut.
records.remedy: Pressing the inner corners of her eyes

highlights.text: Holding her eyes shut

records.jp: 「こんな状況なんだぞ。休戦だ休戦」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't try it when you're like this. Truce, we're in a truce."
comments: PCP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi points to the extraordinary situation they all share and declares a truce. The English adds a command not to attempt an unspecified act in her present condition.
records.remedy: We're in a situation like this. Truce, truce.

highlights.text: Don't try it when you're like this.

records.jp: ぞっとする。
records.en: She's shivering.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The narrator himself shudders at the possibility of blindness. The English transfers the reaction to Touko.
records.remedy: I shudder.

highlights.text: She's shivering.

records.jp: 「気持ち悪い。ふらふらする……吐きそう」
records.en: Touko: "I feel nauseous. I feel dizzy... like to throw up."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko feels as though she is about to vomit. 'Like to' normally expresses preference or desire.
records.remedy: like I'm going to throw up

highlights.text: like to throw up

records.jp: 促す。
records.en: Urgently.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator urges her to lie down. The English supplies only an adverb, omitting both actor and action.
records.remedy: I urge her.

highlights.text: Urgently.

records.jp: 仮にそうでも、重篤な疾患や臓器におよぶ大怪我よりはマシだ。
records.en: Assuming it is for the moment, anything is preferable to serious illnesses or external damage that reaches internal organs.
comments: PCP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The narrator says that even if it is blindness, that is better than a grave disease or organ-threatening injury. The English adds a temporary assumption and claims anything at all is preferable.
records.remedy: Even if it is blindness, that's better than a grave illness or an injury reaching her organs.

highlights.text: Assuming it is for the moment, anything is preferable

records.jp: 「目に劇薬を浴びたとか」
records.en: Taichi: "Did you get some powerful medicine or something poisonous on the eyes?"
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: 劇薬 here is a caustic or highly toxic chemical splashed into the eyes. The English misleadingly offers ordinary strong medicine as one alternative.
records.remedy: some caustic chemical

highlights.text: some powerful medicine or something poisonous

records.jp: 「ちょっと見えるようになってきた」
records.en: Touko: "I think I'm starting to see something now."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko says her vision is beginning to return a little. The English instead says an unspecified object is becoming visible.
records.remedy: starting to see a little again

highlights.text: starting to see something

records.jp: 「そういう症状が出ることがあるんだ。気持ち悪いのもそのせいだ」
records.en: Taichi: "The symptoms seem to be all there. It should also cause your feeling of nausea, you know."
comments: PCP CCB0015B
Just a な at the end... -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi explains that anemia can produce symptoms like temporary darkness and that it also caused the nausea. The English instead says all diagnostic symptoms appear present.
records.remedy: Anemia can cause symptoms like that. It's also why you feel nauseous.

highlights.text: The symptoms seem to be all there.

records.jp: 無理して、嚥下した。
records.en: Deglutition, even if forcefully.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese says she forces herself to swallow. The English replaces the action with a technical noun fragment and uses a concessive 'even if' rather than describing effort.
records.remedy: She forces herself to swallow.

highlights.text: Deglutition, even if forcefully.

records.jp: 直に口をつけて、
records.en: she puts it to the mouth,
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The mouth is hers, so the phrase requires a possessive determiner.
records.remedy: puts it directly to her mouth

highlights.text: puts it to the mouth

records.jp: 喉が隆起して、水分を摂取する。旺盛に。
records.en: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko's throat works visibly as she drinks eagerly. The English is a verbless fragment, substitutes water passage for her drinking, and strands the manner adverb.
records.remedy: Her throat bobs as she drinks deeply.

highlights.text: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.

records.jp: 「……水分くらい補給してるわけ？」
records.en: Taichi: "...you're not replenishing your fluids regularly?"
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether she is at least taking in fluids. The English presupposes failure and adds a requirement of regularity.
records.remedy: You're at least keeping hydrated, right?

highlights.text: you're not replenishing your fluids regularly?

records.jp: 「帰る途中で転んで、坂の下に全部落ちた」
records.en: Touko: "They fell on the way home, and rolled all the way to the bottom of a hill."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko says she fell on the way home, causing all the drinks to tumble down the hill. The English makes the supplies fall by themselves and omits her fall.
records.remedy: I fell on the way home, and they all rolled to the bottom of the hill.

highlights.text: They fell on the way home

records.jp: 「不器用ちゃんか、おまえは」
records.en: Touko: "Clumsy-chan I'm gonna call ya."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi teases Touko for being clumsy. The English labels Touko as the speaker, making her give herself the nickname.
records.remedy: Taichi: "You're Clumsy-chan, aren't you?"

highlights.text: Touko: "Clumsy-chan I'm gonna call ya."

records.jp: 「はー、桐原先生、そりゃ呆けすぎですぜ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, Kirihara-sensei, you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!"
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi calls her excessively foolish or absentminded, with a possible boke joke. The English overexplains a comedy role and repeats the subject and verb ungrammatically.
records.remedy: you're taking the boke act way too far!

highlights.text: you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!

records.jp: 「人がいなくなったら、そんな価値観は消える」
records.en: Taichi: "If there's no people anymore, then the recognition of values like that disappears."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi says social values like concern for appearances disappear when other people are gone. The English says only people's recognition of those still-existing values disappears.
records.remedy: values like that disappear

highlights.text: the recognition of values like that disappears

records.jp: それは純粋な個としての人。
records.en: That is a person existing in pure Individuality.
records.assessment: The passage identifies what is demanded as a human being reduced to or acting as a pure individual. The English makes the previously named strength itself equal a person and uses an abstract capitalized noun unnaturally.
records.remedy: What is demanded is the human being as a pure individual.

highlights.text: That is a person existing in pure Individuality.

records.jp: 冬子にそれがあるとは思えない。
records.en: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The narrator says he cannot believe Touko possesses that strength to live as a pure individual. The English instead refers back to plural previously scorned desires.
records.remedy: I don't think Touko has that strength.

highlights.text: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.

records.jp: 冬子の凄絶な弱さを。
records.en: Touko's violent weakness,
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese describes the extremity or terrible intensity of Touko's weakness. 'Violent weakness' is internally contradictory and suggests aggression.
records.remedy: the terrible extremity of Touko's weakness

highlights.text: Touko's violent weakness

records.jp: 「世界は人を塗りつぶした。俺たちだけが、『互い』だ」
records.en: Taichi: "This world has painted out all people. We alone are... reciprocal."
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the two survivors are each other's only counterpart. 'Reciprocal' is an adjective and cannot denote the other person here.
records.remedy: We're the only ones each other has.

highlights.text: We alone are... reciprocal.

records.jp: 関わったのだ。望んで。
records.en: There was involvement. A wish for it.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The narrator says that he became involved because he wanted to. The English removes the actor and severs his desire from the action.
records.remedy: I got involved because I wanted to.

highlights.text: There was involvement. A wish for it.

records.jp: 冬子ルートとも言うべき流れに乗って、際まで行って、そこで全てが崩壊したとしても。
records.en: Even if I ride this flow that ought be called the Touko Route, even if I go all the way to the edge, even if nothing is there but Downfall...
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese supposes that everything may collapse at the endpoint. The English instead describes Downfall as the only thing located there.
records.remedy: even if everything falls apart when I get there

highlights.text: even if nothing is there but Downfall

records.jp: 敏感に冬子が反応した。
records.en: Touko's response is sensible.
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: The Japanese says Touko reacts sensitively or sharply to his unfinished suggestion. 'Sensible' means reasonable and changes the description.
records.remedy: Touko reacts sharply.

highlights.text: Touko's response is sensible.

records.jp: 「……どうしても、何？」
records.en: Taichi: "...whatever I do, what?"
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Touko follows up on Taichi's unfinished conditional. The English assigns her question to Taichi and also changes the conditional subject.
records.remedy: Touko: "...if it's absolutely what?"

highlights.text: Taichi: "...whatever I do, what?"

records.jp: 「どうして、人は滅びたんだと思う？」
records.en: Taichi: "What do you think annihilated humanity?"
comments: CP CCB0015B
records.assessment: Taichi asks why she thinks humanity perished. The English instead asks her to identify an agent or cause that annihilated it.
records.remedy: Why do you think humanity perished?

highlights.text: What do you think annihilated humanity?

records.jp: 何をするにでもだ。
records.en: But to do what?
comments: CP CCC0039
records.assessment: The Japanese concludes that the school is convenient no matter what the pair intend to do. The English turns this into a question about their activity.
records.remedy: Whatever they plan to do.

highlights.text: But to do what?

records.jp: 「水浸しにしてやるっ」
records.en: Kiri: "I'll plunge you down!"
comments: CP CCC0039
records.assessment: Kiri threatens to soak or drench Miki with water. The English instead says she will force Miki downward.
records.remedy: I'll soak you!

highlights.text: I'll plunge you down!

records.jp: 「だめー！　濡れたら髪がワカメになるー！」
records.en: Miki: "Nooo! If you wet my hear it'll turn into Wakame seaweed!"
comments: CP CCC0039
records.assessment: The English contains a typo that changes 'hair' to the verb 'hear.'
records.remedy: my hair

highlights.text: my hear

records.jp: そして……彼女たちと打算的に交流しようとする行為が、途端にむなしく思えてきた。
records.en: And then... I came to think that the act of calculating self-interested interaction with these girls would become instantaneously fruitless.
comments: See CCC4024. The parallels with Miki continue. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says his calculating attempt to interact with the girls suddenly felt empty. The English recasts this as a prediction that the interaction will later become fruitless.
records.remedy: suddenly seemed utterly empty

highlights.text: would become instantaneously fruitless

records.jp: 「俺はただ……見たいだけなのに」
records.en: Taichi: "Because I just... only want to see it."
comments: TAICHY LIKES TO WATCH guessing The Dream. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says only that he wants to watch. The English adds a causal connector and replaces the girls with an unspecified object.
records.remedy: I only... want to watch them.

highlights.text: Because I just... only want to see it.

records.jp: 当たり前のように、人のそばにあるものを。
records.en: that people who exist right next to each other, as if their presence were natural,
records.assessment: The Japanese names what ordinarily exists beside people as the object he wants to remember. The English turns it into an unfinished relative clause about nearby people.
records.remedy: the things that are naturally there beside people;

highlights.text: that people who exist right next to each other, as if their presence were natural,

records.jp: 人を心地よくさせるふれあいを。
records.en: will have with others an exchange of touches that is pleasant for their heart.
comments: Either he doesn't actually believe this, or what Youko does is much different from merely being there. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese refers broadly to comforting human contact or interaction. The English narrows it to an exchange of physical touches and supplies a future construction absent from the source.
records.remedy: the human contact that brings comfort.

highlights.text: will have with others an exchange of touches that is pleasant for their heart.

records.jp: 不思議世界でありながら、もどかしい現実でもある今に対する、憤りだ。
records.en: The resentment for this frustratingly slow reality that still exists in this inexplicable world.
records.assessment: The present is simultaneously a mysterious world and a frustrating reality. The English instead places a supposedly slow reality inside the world and adds continued existence.
records.remedy: this present, at once a mysterious world and a frustrating reality

highlights.text: this frustratingly slow reality that still exists in this inexplicable world

records.jp: せいぜい三日か四日。
records.en: Three days at most, at best four.
records.assessment: The Japanese estimates no more than three or four days. Calling three the maximum and then allowing four is internally contradictory.
records.remedy: Three days, maybe four at most.

highlights.text: Three days at most, at best four.

records.jp: グラグラと煮えたぎる感情のうねりが、怒りのそれと似て体を熱くした。
records.en: The friction of my emotions shaking into a boiling that heats my body in ways that yet resemble anger.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes a roiling, boiling surge of emotion. The English invents friction and turns the imagery into an incoherent transformation.
records.remedy: The roiling surge of boiling emotion

highlights.text: The friction of my emotions shaking into a boiling

records.jp: いつまでも―――
records.en: However long it takes---
records.assessment: The Japanese fragment means 'forever' or 'endlessly.' The English turns duration into a concession about completing a task.
records.remedy: Forever---

highlights.text: However long it takes---

records.jp: そんな白々しいもののため。
records.en: For the sake of these shamelessly transparent things.
comments: The vague undertone of lie... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator calls the ideals hollow, insincere, or brazenly false. 'Transparent' suggests that they are clear or obvious rather than counterfeit.
records.remedy: those hollow, insincere things

highlights.text: these shamelessly transparent things

records.jp: けど八方美人に進めてきた俺は、何も得られないまま時間を浪費してしまった。
records.en: But having progressed to the role of all-appealing histrion, I have wasted time while obtaining nothing.
comments: Damn, that nearly isn't in the dictionary. -GHS
records.assessment: 八方美人 means trying to please everyone. The English invents a theatrical role and does not convey his indiscriminate people-pleasing.
records.remedy: trying to please everyone

highlights.text: the role of all-appealing histrion

records.jp: 正門前にしゃがみこみ、夕刻前一足先に途方に暮れる。
records.en: Squatting down in front of the main gate, face through knees, stumped hopelessly just a few steps ahead of the evening hour.
records.assessment: The Japanese says he crouches before the main gate; it does not say that his face is between or through his knees.
records.remedy: Squatting in front of the main gate,

highlights.text: face through knees,

records.jp: 「……手伝うことはある？」
records.en: Youko: "...something you need help with?
records.assessment: The dialogue line is missing its closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Youko: "...something you need help with?"

highlights.text: Youko: "...something you need help with?

records.jp: 流しかけたのに、つい問いかけてしまう。
records.en: And even though I had just deflected it, I accidentally asked a question,
records.assessment: He had only started to brush her offer aside before asking his question. The English says the deflection had already been completed.
records.remedy: Though I had been about to brush it off

highlights.text: even though I had just deflected it

records.jp: 「ねえ……どうやったら、みんなでうまくできるのかな」
records.en: Taichi: "Say... I'm wondering how can I do it, how can I make things go well with everyone I mean."
records.assessment: Taichi wonders how everyone can get along together. The English makes him the explicit agent who must make the situation work.
records.remedy: how can all of us make things work together?

highlights.text: how can I do it, how can I make things go well with everyone I mean

records.jp: 「仲良くケンカして、放送用台本をみんなでチェックして、協力してトラブルに対処して……」
records.en: Taichi: "Having friendly fights, making an air check of the broadcast scenario with everybody, coping with our troubles via collaboration...
records.assessment: The Japanese says everyone checks the broadcast script together. 'Air check' denotes recording or monitoring a broadcast, and 'scenario' is not the script here.
records.remedy: checking the broadcast script together

highlights.text: making an air check of the broadcast scenario with everybody

records.jp: 「なんの冗談なんだよ、こりゃあ」
records.en: Taichi: "The hell of a joke is even this!"
records.assessment: The Japanese asks what kind of joke the situation is. The English is ungrammatical and does not form that question.
records.remedy: What kind of joke is this?

highlights.text: The hell of a joke is even this!

records.jp: 「……隠したから」
records.en: Youko: "...hidden."
records.assessment: Youko says that she hid the notebooks. The English omits both her action and the object, leaving only a participle.
records.remedy: ...because I hid them.

highlights.text: ...hidden.

records.jp: 「……もう、そろそろ理解してくれてもいいと思う」
records.en: Youko: "...and now, if you would please give me your understanding on this, it would be about time I think."
records.assessment: Youko says it is about time Taichi understood the fact she has stated. The English asks him to grant her his understanding or agreement.
records.remedy: I think it's about time you understood.

highlights.text: if you would please give me your understanding on this

records.jp: 深々と息を吐き出した。
records.en: A spat out my deep, deep breath,
records.assessment: The narrator lets out a deep breath. The English has an invalid subject and suggests spitting rather than exhaling.
records.remedy: I let out a long, deep breath,

highlights.text: A spat out my deep, deep breath,

records.jp: 「ＡとＢのどちらかを選ばないといけないとする。どっちを選ぶ？」
records.en: Youko: "You must absolutely and necessarily choose between A and B. Which do you choose?"
records.assessment: The Japanese only posits that one must choose A or B. The doubled intensifier is not present in the source.
records.remedy: choose between A and B

highlights.text: absolutely and necessarily

records.jp: 「ごはんのおかずを何から食べるのか」
records.en: Youko: "Which side dish of rice will we begin eating from?"
records.assessment: The Japanese asks which of the dishes served with a meal one eats first. The English incorrectly makes the side dish belong to rice.
records.remedy: Which side dish do we eat first?

highlights.text: Which side dish of rice

records.en: Taichi: "Observation... into being...?"
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether someone observed a world. The English instead repeats an abstract phrase about observation coming into being.
records.remedy: You... observed it?

highlights.text: Observation... into being...?

records.jp: 「当然世界は、永遠の時を繰り返しているのではない」
records.en: Youko: "The natural world is not repeating the same time over and over eternally."
records.assessment: 当然 is the sentence adverb 'of course,' not an adjective making this a 'natural world.'
records.remedy: Of course, the world

highlights.text: The natural world

records.jp: 時空が乱れて、先に進めなくなることが……終焉であることだって。
records.en: Space-time falls into disarray and ceases to progress onwards... that is its demise.
comments: No, if space-time is still continuous, then it is simply progressing forwards in a different shape. An advancement in shapes not understood isn't a collapse. This may be intentional, however. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator realizes that spacetime becoming disordered and unable to advance could itself count as an ending. The English removes this modal realization and asserts it as a settled definition.
records.remedy: that, too, could be an ending.

highlights.text: that is its demise.

records.jp: 「空間的に記録された情報に従って、分解された粒子が収束、月曜朝の状態に戻る」
records.en: Youko: "Following the recorded spatial information, the disassembled particles reorganize and return to the aspect of Monday."
comments: Recorded where? On the hard drive, for starters... -GHS
records.assessment: The particles return specifically to their Monday-morning state. 'Aspect of Monday' omits morning and does not express restoration of a state.
records.remedy: return to their state on Monday morning

highlights.text: return to the aspect of Monday

records.jp: 「君は一繋がり説だって言ったけど、でも俺には前者の方もそれっぽく聞こえる。どっちが正しいか、今のところは判断できないんじゃあ……」
records.en: Taichi: "You say that it's the single thread theory, but to my ears the first one sounds more like it. We can't discern which is correct at this point in time, you know..."
comments: Juuust a bit desperate. Interesting emphasis on the 'hearing'. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says the first theory also sounds plausible. The English says it sounds more correct than the continuous-world theory.
records.remedy: the first theory sounds plausible too

highlights.text: the first one sounds more like it

records.jp: 「……だったらまずは、今ある理論を適用するしかない」
records.en: Youko: "...therefore, to start with we have no choice but to adopt one of the theories we have now."
comments: "I dunno, but science says this, so it's gotta be one of these". Magnificently human. -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says they must begin by applying current theory. The English adds a choice among multiple theories, which is not stated.
records.remedy: start by applying the theory currently available to us

highlights.text: adopt one of the theories we have now

records.jp: 「理解者、でしょう？」
records.en: Youko: "Someone who understands, don't we?"
comments: Supposing it's in reference to above, "the person capable of understanding you". It's very funny considering she is possibly the only person who understands Taichi even worse than he does himself. Even if it were to refer to the theories, this incoherent quasi-scientific mess of an explanation shows she's basically clueless about the situation at hand. She is the real Dumbass Comic Relief, while Sakuraba is actually Mr. Exposition. Troll Channel continues... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese offers 'someone who understands you' as what is needed. The English uses a mismatched question tag and leaves the proposition incomplete.
records.remedy: Someone who understands you, right?

highlights.text: Someone who understands, don't we?

records.jp: 「他の誰も、あなたのことを理解してはくれない」
records.en: Youko: "No one else will give you understanding of what you are."
records.assessment: Youko says nobody else will understand Taichi. The English instead describes giving him an abstract understanding of what he is.
records.remedy: No one else will understand you.

highlights.text: give you understanding of what you are

records.jp: 病を心に秘めていても、人を傷つけることも知らない。
records.en: Even hiding the disease in the heart it's still possible to not know you are hurting someone.
comments: Could easily refer to both: Yusa hides her illness inside, as well, and by refusing his help when she's bullied (as is unclear, but very possible, see CCA0013), she's been hurting him as well. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that despite the illness hidden in her heart, Yusa did not even know how to hurt people. The English turns this into a general claim about unknowingly inflicting current harm.
records.remedy: Even with the sickness hidden in her heart, she didn't know how to hurt anyone.

highlights.text: Even hiding the disease in the heart it's still possible to not know you are hurting someone.

records.jp: 好意でも悪意でもない。
records.en: Neither favoritism nor malice there.
records.assessment: The gaze contains neither affection nor malice. 'Favoritism' means preferential treatment and does not denote positive feeling.
records.remedy: Neither affection nor malice.

highlights.text: Neither favoritism nor malice there.

records.jp: 熱烈なる食欲が、自分に注がれるのだ。
records.en: Boiling hot hunger is poured inside the self.
records.assessment: The fierce appetite is directed at the person being watched. The English instead describes hunger being poured inside that person's self.
records.remedy: is fixed intently upon you

highlights.text: is poured inside the self

records.jp: うずくまり、嘔吐にえずく少女を見下ろしながら、俺はそのくだらない結末にうんざりしていた。
records.en: I was looking down on a squatting little girl disgustingly vomiting her guts out, a conclusion of inferior quality that I grew bored of.
comments: "I AM A FEROCIOUS LION! FEAR ME LAMB, FOR I WILL DEVOUR YOU! I CANNOT STOP, FOR THESE OF MINE ARE BUT INSTINCwhat, you say no? Really really seriously no? Oh well, fine, I'm 'bored', yeah, that's what I am, you would've tasted sour anyway so harrumph." This is not the behavior of a ferocious creature, this is the behavior of a rabbit that's dressing up as a lion and doing a really bad job of it. ...or the behavior of someone who booted up Kana: Imouto thinking DURR I GET TO PORK MAI IMOUTO, and the very second scene of the story...

BTW, there's some odd stuff in this sentence. 嘔吐にえずく can almost be written 嘔吐に嘔吐く (there's a づ instead of a　ず, but the pronunciation is very close) -  pukingly due to puking? えずい (ezui) is Tousa-ben for "disgusting", ezuku is adverb. Emphasized puking for this. Also kudaroshi (looking down, same lateral meaning present as in English) and kudaranai (worthless) technically use the same kanji. Used look down/inferior. What odd puns, and odder placements as well. I can hardly put this down to Taichi's usual Distract With Bad Jokes behavior. -GHS
records.assessment: The girl crouches and retches while the narrator is disgusted or weary specifically with the pathetic ending. The English exaggerates the vomiting and makes the girl's action itself disgusting.
records.remedy: the girl crouched and retching, sick of how pathetic an ending it was

highlights.text: a squatting little girl disgustingly vomiting her guts out, a conclusion of inferior quality that I grew bored of

records.jp: 「いれば傷つけるだけ」
records.en: Youko: "If they are here you will only wound."
records.assessment: Youko says that merely having the others around means Taichi will hurt them. The English omits the object of 'wound' and leaves the thought incomplete.
records.remedy: If they're around, you'll only hurt them.

highlights.text: If they are here you will only wound.

records.jp: 「でもできたら、そんなことは……ない……そうはしたくない……」
records.en: Taichi: "But I if I could, I would... never... I don't want to do that..."
records.assessment: Taichi haltingly says that, if possible, he does not want things to be that way. The English is ungrammatical and introduces an unfinished action he 'would' perform.
records.remedy: But if I can help it, I don't... want things to be that way...

highlights.text: But I if I could, I would... never...

records.jp: 「私だけがいればいい」
records.en: Youko: "It would be best if only I were to be."
comments: Going by CCC0021, especially, this is another possible admission that she's a split personality. This is meant very literally: if he gives in to her truly and fully, he'd disappear. He'd be nothing but a phantom, like she is. But he'd have to give up the antenna, or anything equivalent as well. -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says that she is the only person Taichi needs. The English omits the complement and leaves 'be' without a completed meaning.
records.remedy: All you need is me.

highlights.text: It would be best if only I were to be.

records.jp: 「私だったら、太一とうまくやれるから」
records.en: Youko: "Because I alone can go make this go well for you, Taichi."
comments: "You could get lucky mah man" + "split personality blah blah blah codfish". -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says that she can get along successfully with Taichi. The English makes her manage an unspecified situation on his behalf instead.
records.remedy: Because I can make things work with you, Taichi.

highlights.text: I alone can go make this go well for you

records.jp: 「うまくやれるって……言うんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You say... you'd make things go well for me, right."
records.assessment: Taichi repeats Youko's claim that the two of them can get along. The English again turns it into her arranging favorable circumstances for him.
records.remedy: You say... we can make it work?

highlights.text: make things go well for me

records.jp: しかし俺の頭からは、曜日感覚は消えかけていた。
records.en: However, from the top in my head the sense for weekdays had almost vanished.
comments: And finally tossing around that 'week' with Youko pays off. -GHS
records.assessment: The sense of weekdays is disappearing from the narrator's mind. The English adds 'top' and forms an incoherent prepositional phrase.
records.remedy: from my mind

highlights.text: from the top in my head

records.en: Youko: "...g'mo."
comments: PCP CCA0004
Heh. See CCC4001. No complaints for the same level of awful greeting? Then again, they're same years. -GHS
records.assessment: ちわ is a casual contraction of a general greeting, not specifically 'good morning.'
records.remedy: ...hey.

records.jp: 「どうしました、おそろいで」
records.en: Misato: "What happened, you are here together."
comments: Harmless term, but as it is all too often the case: http://ejje.weblio.jp/content/%E3%81%8A%E6%8F%83%E3%81%84 look at 'em odd specific meanings. -GHS
records.assessment: Misato asks what brings the pair there together. The English asks what happened and joins it to a statement with a comma.
records.remedy: What brings the two of you here?

highlights.text: What happened, you are here together.

records.jp: 俺は柔らかな先輩が、かたい地面に吸い寄せられ、砕ける瞬間を見た。
records.en: I saw the instant that my fluffy tender sweet Senpai was attracted by the hard ground and shattered.
comments: Pulling Power? See CCX0001. With the above this makes perfect sense: he's remembered how he's killed everyone, and here he is, starting with a replay of Yutaka's death. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese contrasts the physically soft senior with the hard ground. 'Fluffy' and 'sweet' add sentimental characterization absent from the source.
records.remedy: my soft senpai

highlights.text: my fluffy tender sweet Senpai

records.jp: 途中、何度か胃液を戻した気がする。
records.en: On the way, it felt like my gastric juices had returned to the world so many times.
records.assessment: The narrator thinks he vomited stomach acid several times. The English euphemism about returning it to the world obscures the physical action.
records.remedy: I'd brought up stomach acid several times

highlights.text: my gastric juices had returned to the world

records.jp: ただ赤色の光景ばかりがまばゆいのだ。
records.en: Just, that this scene the color of red is dazzingly beautiful.
records.assessment: The red scene is dazzling or glaring to the narrator. The English adds aesthetic beauty, reversing the aversive context, and also misspells 'dazzling.'
records.remedy: is all that dazzles my eyes

highlights.text: is dazzingly beautiful

records.jp: ノイズを挟まないことにはピュアな赤が意識を浸食してしまう。
records.en: With there is no noise, no interference interposed, the pure red completely erodes my consciousness.
comments: See CCA0016A. This should be the explanation for all the Noise events. Therefore, the distortions he sees are these protections. Of course, since his memory is shot to pieces, moments of high stress seem to make him recall other moments of high stress, and the more moments of stress he has, the more becoming stressed would weigh him down. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese states that without noise as a buffer, pure red erodes consciousness. The English conditional is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Unless some noise is interposed

highlights.text: With there is no noise, no interference interposed

records.jp: 上の問いはまったく意味を持たない。
records.en:
Did she become aware of that shameful sexual
playact that I have inflicted on Youko-chan?
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the question above has no meaning. The English replaces it with an unrelated question about whether someone noticed a sexual act.
records.remedy: The question above has no meaning at all.

highlights.text:
Did she become aware of that shameful sexual
playact that I have inflicted on Youko-chan?

records.jp: 事態を理解できていなかったのかも知れない。
records.en: Sakuraba did not pose resistance.
records.assessment: The Japanese speculates that Sakuraba may not have understood what was happening. The English substitutes a statement about offering no resistance.
records.remedy: Perhaps Sakuraba didn't understand what was happening.

highlights.text: Sakuraba did not pose resistance.

records.jp: 美希がどの程度の戦力を持っているかを調べる。第一に設定されるシークエンスだ。
records.en:
However, Miki's threat level is an unknown
variable, and therefore caution was required.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes investigating the extent of Miki's fighting strength as the first planned sequence. The English replaces the investigation and ordering with a generic warning about caution.
records.remedy: The first sequence was to determine how much fighting strength Miki had.

highlights.text:
However, Miki's threat level is an unknown
variable, and therefore caution was required.

records.jp: 屋上のモップバケツにたくわえられた水は、赤黒かった。
records.en:
He had died.
The corpse had been moved and been
concealed in the prefab.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the water stored in the rooftop mop bucket was dark red. The English invents a death, a moved corpse, and concealment in a prefabricated structure.
records.remedy: The water in the rooftop mop bucket was dark red.

highlights.text:
He had died.
The corpse had been moved and been
concealed in the prefab.

records.jp: 日が暮れていた。
records.en: The sun was sinking, the day growing dark.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the sun had already set or night had fallen. The English presents sunset as still in progress.
records.remedy: The sun had set.

highlights.text: The sun was sinking, the day growing dark.

records.jp: ずっと、惚けていたのだろうか？
records.en: Haven't I just been playing dumb all along?
comments: Oh dear, I'm not touching this one... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator wonders whether he had been dazed or absent-minded the whole time. 'Playing dumb' implies deliberate pretence.
records.remedy: Had I been out of it this whole time?

highlights.text: playing dumb all along

records.jp: ああ、すごい夕日だ。
records.en: Ahhh, what an amazing twilight.
comments: If this is Sunday, then it's not evening; this is the time loop coming. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator reacts specifically to the sunset. 'Twilight' denotes the broader period or light and changes the object of the exclamation.
records.remedy: what an incredible sunset

highlights.text: what an amazing twilight

records.jp: 澄んだ大気ごしに見える、朱を基調とした濃淡のあわい。
records.en: I can see through the crisp clear atmosphere a pale shade with vermilion at its key component.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes gradations of color centered on vermilion. The English reduces them to one pale shade and calls vermilion a component.
records.remedy: gradations of color centered on vermilion

highlights.text: a pale shade with vermilion at its key component

records.jp: ＊戮機械みたいで。
records.en: Like a ****ing machine.
comments: 殺戮 slaughter, adapted to just killing machine because "slaughter machine" sounds off. -GHS
records.assessment: The partially censored Japanese means a slaughter or killing machine. The English reads as an obscenity modifying 'machine' and loses the lethal compound.
records.remedy: Like a sl***hter machine.

highlights.text: Like a ****ing machine.

records.jp: 生き残ったみんなに『大丈夫だよ』と言ったら……誰だっけな……拾ったナイフを、俺に向けて。
records.en: And then I said, "It's all right!" to all the survivors... and someone, who was it... turned one of the discarded knives towards me.
comments: From below it seems Miki. Understandably so, given Kiri died. -GHS
records.assessment: The person turns a knife they picked up toward the narrator. The Japanese does not say it was discarded.
records.remedy: a knife they'd picked up

highlights.text: one of the discarded knives

records.jp: それで、俺つい＊しちゃって。
records.en: And that is why I unconsciously ****ed.
comments: This is of course contradictory, but that's obviously intentional. The real tone of this scene seems to remain firmly humoristic. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says he ended up performing the censored action on that person. The English omits the object and leaves the transitive action incomplete.
records.remedy: I went and ****ed them.

highlights.text: I unconsciously ****ed.

records.jp: ＊してから＊したんだっけ？
records.en: You're xxxxed, therefore you ****?
comments: Funny fact: in the PS2 version, the words aren't censored (on the 360 they are). And the kanji being replaced isn't always the one for kill! Here, for example, the original sentence is 壊してから殺したんだっけ "you're wrecked, therefore you kill". This makes way more sense than messing about with "kill before you're killed", especially given the new stuff above. I'm changing the * to x, but "luckily" wreck and kill are both 4 letters. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator asks whether one censored action happened after another and then questions the order. The English changes the person, tense, and relation into a general implication.
records.remedy: Did I **** them after they ****ed someone?

highlights.text: You're xxxxed, therefore you ****?

records.jp: 言いたいことは山ほどあった。
records.en: The size of the amount of things I wanted to tell were a mountain,
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom says he had a mountain of things to say. The English is grammatically malformed and literalizes the quantity twice.
records.remedy: There was a mountain of things I wanted to say,

highlights.text: The size of the amount of things I wanted to tell were a mountain,

records.jp: 世界には『８人』しかいないのに。
records.en: When in the world there is nothing but 『8 people』...
comments: PCP CCB0022
records.assessment: The Japanese is a concessive fragment: this happened even though only eight people exist in the world. The English uses a temporal 'when' construction and mismatches number.
records.remedy: Even though there are only eight people in the world...

highlights.text: When in the world there is nothing but 『8 people』...

records.jp: みみ先輩は破壊された尖塔の足下にいた。
records.en: Mimi-senpai stood underfoot the demolished spire.
comments: PCP CCB0022
records.assessment: Mimi is at the foot of the destroyed tower. 'Underfoot' would place the tower beneath her, and the source does not say she stood.
records.remedy: was at the foot of the destroyed spire

highlights.text: stood underfoot the demolished spire

records.jp: 殴られた友貴の口元が、不自然に歪んだ。
records.en: Tomoki's face, punched, distorted unnaturally.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes Tomoki's mouth twisting unnaturally after the blow. The English expands the affected feature to his whole face.
records.remedy: Tomoki's mouth twisted unnaturally after the punch.

highlights.text: Tomoki's face, punched, distorted unnaturally.

records.jp: 殺傷力を有した霧だった。
records.en: Kiri was endowed with offensive abilities.
comments: PCP CCD0022A
records.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri possessed lethal or injuring force. 'Offensive abilities' weakens the explicit capacity to cause bodily harm.
records.remedy: lethal force

highlights.text: offensive abilities

records.jp: 違う。
records.en: A mistake.
comments: See CCB0022. Three routes on, and nothing at all's changed. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator interjects 'No' or 'That's wrong' to reject the preceding account. The English labels an unspecified thing as a mistake instead.
records.remedy: No.

highlights.text: A mistake.

records.jp: 違う違う違う。
records.en: A mistake, a mistake, a mistake.
records.assessment: The repeated Japanese directly rejects the account: 'No, no, no.' Repeating the noun 'mistake' changes the voice and syntax.
records.remedy: No, no, no.

highlights.text: A mistake, a mistake, a mistake.

records.jp: 「太一は、よく生きたと思う」
records.en: Youko: "Taichi has lived well and long I think."
comments: What the hell is he doing in the classroom now? -GHS
records.assessment: Youko says Taichi lived well or fought hard to live. The English adds longevity, which the source does not state.
records.remedy: lived well

highlights.text: lived well and long

records.jp: 女装してるんだから。
records.en: It's cross-dressed in women's clothing.
records.assessment: The narrator explains that he looks girlish because he is cross-dressing. The English assigns the action to an unspecified 'it.'
records.remedy: Because I'm dressed as a girl.

highlights.text: It's cross-dressed in women's clothing.

records.jp: そして夜ごとに僕たちは、引き立てられた。
records.en: And every night her, and this still innocent boy I was, were patronized.
comments: I didn't manage to do much with CCD0022A, and before that new script, it had been a while since the last boku. Oddly, here it's bokutachi, while the new '22A is bokura. Slightly manlier in the latter sense. As for this, it seems to be a very nice way of saying "raped"... or is it? -GHS
records.assessment: The two children were led or dragged out night after night. 'Patronized' means treated condescendingly or supported as a customer and does not convey that action.
records.remedy: were taken out before them

highlights.text: were patronized

records.jp: 児童虐待もいいところだ。
records.en: At best one could call it child abuse,
records.assessment: The Japanese says this was child abuse in the extreme or nothing short of child abuse. 'At best' weakens and potentially reverses that force.
records.remedy: It was nothing short of child abuse,

highlights.text: At best one could call it child abuse,

records.jp: 誓いだけで、充分、生きる力にはなった。
records.en: Just with this vow alone we came to have strength live, plenty of it.
records.assessment: The English omits the infinitive marker required to express strength to live.
records.remedy: strength to live

highlights.text: strength live

records.jp: 不可能を可能にする方程式が必要だった。
records.en: An equation was needed to make this impossible into possible.
comments: See CCD0021, "cold equation". More interesting, see CCA0006. A formula tames Taichi's penis... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese invokes making the impossible possible. The English inserts 'this' and uses an ungrammatical transformation construction.
records.remedy: make the impossible possible

highlights.text: make this impossible into possible

records.jp: 時間をかけ、道具を用意し、訓練し、観察し、変更し、検討し、保留し、購入し、改良し、調査し、決定し、撤回し、キスをした。
records.en: We took our time, and the implements we prepared, practiced, surveyed, amended, observed, deferred, purchased, improved, investigated, determined, retracted, kissed.
comments: Yes, it does sound like he did all that to the implements. Leaving it ambiguous. Interesting is that they apparently buy weapons and traps off what I suppose to be the 'net AND NO ONE NOTICES. Not even the police! That's one mother of They Just Didn't Care. Also, this may be where Taichi's interest in Wacchi comes from: studying the habits of those in the mansion. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese lists a sequence of actions performed by the pair. The English makes 'implements' the object of much of the list and does not preserve the parallel verbs.
records.remedy: We took our time, prepared tools, trained, observed, modified, considered, postponed, purchased, improved, investigated, decided, withdrew, and kissed.

highlights.text: We took our time, and the implements we prepared, practiced, surveyed, amended, observed, deferred, purchased, improved, investigated, determined, retracted, kissed.

records.jp: 僕らは一心同体で、姉弟で、繋がったものだった。
records.en: We were one thing, connected, as siblings and as alter egos.
records.assessment: 一心同体 says the siblings were of one heart and body. 'Alter egos' describes secondary selves or extremely close counterparts and changes the bodily unity claimed here.
records.remedy: one in body and soul

highlights.text: as alter egos

records.jp: 先週の日曜日、合宿からの帰り道からこっち、一度たりとも来たことはなかったのに。
records.en: When I have not come here not once since last week's Sunday, on the way back from the training camp.
comments: The problem is that this contradicts the entire route! The question isn't whether some strange change happened: the questions are when, and more importantly, what its exact nature is. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says he has not come once since last Sunday. The English uses a double negative and an unsupported temporal 'when' clause.
records.remedy: I haven't come here once

highlights.text: When I have not come here not once

records.jp: 殺戮してしまった世界から。
records.en: from this world that has been slaughtered.
records.assessment: The narrator wants to escape the world in which he committed a massacre. The English makes the world itself the victim of slaughter and removes his agency.
records.remedy: this world where I committed slaughter

highlights.text: this world that has been slaughtered

records.jp: そんな俺の目が、とらえたもの。
records.en: And those eyes I had seized something.
comments: I can't stop thinking of CCC3005, of course. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese introduces what the narrator's eyes caught. The English instead says that he had seized something and leaves 'those eyes' without a grammatical role.
records.remedy: What my eyes caught then.

highlights.text: And those eyes I had seized something.

records.jp: ある一点を超えた疑問は、脳内で瞬時に有機的結合を果たした。
records.en: Having crossed a certain point, one doubt intracerebrally achieved instantaneous organic combination:
comments: Seems to be a really pretentious (AKA trollish) way of saying "a question formed in my mind". -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator's accumulated questions suddenly connect into an integrated realization in his mind. The English turns one doubt into the agent of an incoherent medical-sounding process.
records.remedy: the questions suddenly connected into a coherent whole in my mind

highlights.text: one doubt intracerebrally achieved instantaneous organic combination

records.jp: そして俺は、誰かと恋仲になったり、よりを戻したり、和解したりしながら……一定の確率で、全員が結束する幸福な結末を求めた。
records.en: And then, while I would be having a love relationship, or a return to good terms, or a reconciliation with someone... I sought, with constant probability, the blissful result that is the unity of all of us.
records.assessment: 一定の確率 means that there was a certain chance of this outcome, not that the probability was constant over time.
records.remedy: with some probability

highlights.text: with constant probability

records.jp: あるはずのないハッピーエンド。
records.en: The happy ending should not be expected to exist.
records.assessment: The Japanese calls it a happy ending that cannot exist. The English weakens impossibility into a recommendation not to expect it.
records.remedy: A happy ending that cannot exist.

highlights.text: should not be expected to exist

records.jp: 「こんなオチしかねぇのかよ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Just this fucking punchline!"
comments: No triple exclamation marks for tone. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether this is the only ending available. The English removes the question and adds explicit profanity absent from the Japanese.
records.remedy: Is this the only kind of ending there is?!

highlights.text: Just this fucking punchline!

records.jp: 「どれだけ間違えれば気が済むんだよ！」
records.en: Taichi: "How long do I have to keep making mistakes before you're satisfied!"
comments: An impersonal 'you'. But since he's accusing her of being the cause of this, it should work either way. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks how many mistakes he himself must make before he is satisfied. The English makes Nanaka the person demanding satisfaction.
records.remedy: before I'm satisfied?!

highlights.text: before you're satisfied!

records.jp: 「答えろよ、おまえは知ってるんだろ？　すごい力ある何者か、なんだろ？」

Remember how they installed Psychopath High in this super-rich place to "compensate" for its wealth? -GHS

highlights.text: That's 'affairs'.
