highlights.text: it is necessary to do all over again

records.jp: 便利なリセットは、週末にしかない仕様だ。
records.en: The specifications of our convenient reset put it outside of choice at the weekend.
records.assessment: The convenient reset is designed to be available only on the weekend. The English says that it is outside the available choices at the weekend, implying the opposite.
records.remedy: is only available on the weekend

highlights.text: put it outside of choice at the weekend

records.jp: 時間をかけて生きる癖をつけないといけない。
records.en: It is indispensable to grow into the habit, however bad, of living while expending time.
comments: This has nothing to do with wasting it, best seen in the ending. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he must get used to taking time to live. The English calls the habit bad and recasts living patiently as expending time.
records.remedy: get into the habit of taking time to live

highlights.text: habit, however bad, of living while expending time

records.jp: 蝉も鳴かない世界だが、どこかに誰かがいる。
records.en: Even in this world where not even the cicadas cry somewhere, someone, must be among us.
comments: Renewing the idea that his messages also don't literally cross the barrier between worlds. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese contrasts a world where even cicadas are silent with the fact that somebody exists somewhere. The English misattaches 'somewhere' to the cicadas and produces an ungrammatical claim that somebody must be among the narrator's group.
records.remedy: Though not even cicadas sing in this world, somebody is out there somewhere.

highlights.text: where not even the cicadas cry somewhere, someone, must be among us

records.jp: あまりにも健全で、あたたかくて、胸がほんの少しだけ締めつけられたのだった。
records.en: so excessively wholesome in its warmth the what is inside the chest tightened, only just a little.
records.assessment: The wholesome warmth makes Taichi's chest tighten slightly. The English substitutes an ungrammatical unidentified thing inside the chest.
records.remedy: my chest tightened

highlights.text: the what is inside the chest tightened

records.jp: 部屋に変化が乏しいのも、いけない。
records.en: And how things that change in the room are rare is very very bad.
comments: Low external stimulus -> madness. Except he was already sort of mad, wasn't he. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the room's lack of variation or stimulus is also harmful. The English uses an ungrammatical relative construction that obscures the simple absence of change.
records.remedy: the lack of change in the room

highlights.text: how things that change in the room are rare

records.en: Tacihi: "...crap."
records.assessment: The speaker label transposes letters in Taichi's name.
records.remedy: Taichi:

highlights.text: Tacihi:

records.jp: ひたすら、きつい。
records.en: Determinately harsh.
records.assessment: Taichi says that the experience is simply or relentlessly brutal. 'Determinately' is not the meaning of the adverb and does not form an idiomatic English description.
records.remedy: Relentlessly brutal.

highlights.text: Determinately harsh.

records.jp: 白い部屋に吊して、放置するだけでいい。
records.en: Just hanging in some blank white room, and leaving things as is would be enough.
comments: Hmmm, doesn't google to padded cells, oddly enough. But it should mean "without stimuli". Odd "hanging". -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says torture needs only to hang a person in a blank white room and leave them there. The English omits the person being subjected to the treatment and turns the action into an unattached gerund.
records.remedy: Just hang someone in a blank white room

highlights.text: Just hanging in some blank white room

records.jp: 変化のない時間が、そいつをじわじわと傷つけ続ける。
records.en: These hours devoid of change must be what continues to gradually wound.
comments: Particularly ambiguous that he'd talk about her given how much HE is hurt by these unchanging hours. -GHS
records.assessment: The unchanging passage of time continues gradually injuring that person. The English omits the object being wounded and leaves the predicate incomplete.
records.remedy: The unchanging time will keep wearing that person down.

highlights.text: These hours devoid of change must be what continues to gradually wound.

records.jp: 意識しないくても、視線が向いてしまう。
records.en: Even devoid of consciousness as it is, my gaze still turns to face it.
records.assessment: Taichi says that his gaze turns there even when he does not consciously intend it. The English instead describes him or his gaze as literally unconscious.
records.remedy: Even when I try not to think about it

highlights.text: Even devoid of consciousness as it is

records.jp: 「腹減ったよ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Tummy's empty, you..."
records.assessment: Taichi weakly says that he is hungry. The English adds an unexplained second-person address and uses an incomplete idiom.
records.remedy: I'm hungry...

highlights.text: Tummy's empty, you...

records.jp: そして俺は食事をさせてもらった。
records.en: And then I was made to eat.
records.assessment: Taichi says that Youko lets him eat or feeds him. The English instead says that he is forced to eat.
records.remedy: She let me eat.

highlights.text: I was made to eat.

records.jp: こんな人だって、他者には違いない。
records.en:
This person that should be me, after all,
is no different from a stranger.
comments: Seems to be referring to himself in third person. Or to her, since it might just be the same thing. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi checks his impulse to surrender by recognizing that even someone like Youko is still another person. The English instead identifies the person as Taichi himself and calls him a stranger.
records.remedy: Even someone like her is still another person.

highlights.text:
This person that should be me, after all,
is no different from a stranger.

records.jp: 今の俺を、放棄することはできない。
records.en: The myself of now is incapable of resignation.
records.assessment: Taichi says that he cannot abandon his present self. The English makes the present self the agent and says that it cannot resign.
records.remedy: I cannot abandon the person I am now.

highlights.text: The myself of now is incapable of resignation.

records.jp: いろんな思い出を、心に秘めた……爆弾のような俺だ。
records.en:
this myself who hid all kinds of memories in
his heart... this myself so like a bomb.
records.assessment: The first-person narrator says that he conceals memories in his own heart. The English abruptly changes the possessive to third person.
records.remedy: my heart

highlights.text: his heart

records.jp: 「ごちそうさま。戻ってよし」
records.en: Taichi: "A most delicious meal. You may take your leave."
records.assessment: The fixed post-meal phrase thanks the provider for the food. The English instead evaluates the food as especially delicious.
records.remedy: Thanks for the meal.

highlights.text: A most delicious meal.

records.jp: 冷たく、言い放つ。
records.en: I release... cold words.
comments: PCP above
THIS is where he changes. The rest below is just formality. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi delivers the command coldly. The English uses the nonidiomatic action of releasing words and inserts an unsupported hesitation.
records.remedy: I say coldly.

highlights.text: I release... cold words.

records.jp: 当然、ギンギンになっている。
records.en: Naturally, 'it' is becoming ecstatic.
records.assessment: The Japanese explicitly describes a fully rigid erection. The English substitutes emotional ecstasy and changes the state into an ongoing transition.
records.remedy: I'm completely hard

highlights.text: 'it' is becoming ecstatic

records.jp: 去勢されないための虚勢。
records.en: Bravado to avoid this enervation.
records.assessment: The sentence says his bravado is meant to keep him from being castrated, playing on the similar Japanese terms. 'Enervation' means weakening and loses both the concrete threat and the wordplay.
records.remedy: castration

highlights.text: enervation

records.jp: 可能な限りさめた視線を向ける。
records.en: I turn a gaze at her that at cold to the very limit of the possible.
records.assessment: The phrase is grammatically malformed and obscures Taichi's effort to make his gaze as cold as possible.
records.remedy: as cold as I possibly can

highlights.text: that at cold to the very limit of the possible

records.jp: 顔が寄る。
records.en: Her face drops in.
records.assessment: Youko brings her face closer to Taichi's. The English uses 'drops in,' an idiom for making a brief visit, and does not convey the approach.
records.remedy: Her face comes closer.

highlights.text: Her face drops in.

records.jp: 口内を好き放題される。
records.en: She indulges of my oral cavity as she pleases.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko does whatever she wants inside Taichi's mouth. The English is ungrammatical and incorrectly makes his oral cavity something she indulges in or of.
records.remedy: She does whatever she wants inside my mouth.

highlights.text: She indulges of my oral cavity as she pleases.

records.jp: せめて、油断させないと。
records.en: At the very least I must not let my guard be lowered.
records.assessment: Taichi says that he must make Youko lower her guard. The English reverses both the person whose guard is involved and whether it should be lowered.
records.remedy: I have to make her lower her guard.

highlights.text: I must not let my guard be lowered.

records.jp: 虚を突かれた。
records.en: It is thrust in a hollow.
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom says that Taichi is caught off guard. The English translates its components literally into an unrelated physical action.
records.remedy: She catches me off guard.

highlights.text: It is thrust in a hollow.

records.jp: 彼女の舌の味が、よくわかる。
records.en: The flavor of the girl's tongue is one I know well.
records.assessment: Taichi says that he can distinctly taste Youko's tongue in the present moment. The English instead claims prior familiarity with its flavor.
records.remedy: I can taste her tongue clearly

highlights.text: one I know well

records.jp: 自身をコントロールできない。
records.en: I cannot control that by myself.
records.assessment: Taichi says that he cannot control himself. The English makes an unspecified external object the thing he cannot control alone.
records.remedy: I cannot control myself.

highlights.text: I cannot control that by myself.

records.jp: 寂しげなそれを、自覚してしまう。
records.en: I can feel the loneliness of this so very much.
records.assessment: Taichi realizes that his own exhalation sounds lonely. The English refers vaguely to the loneliness of 'this' and omits the breath he is judging.
records.remedy: I realize how lonely that breath sounds.

highlights.text: I can feel the loneliness of this so very much.

records.jp: 虚ろにさまよっていたらしい。
records.en: Seems I have just meandered about in hollowness.
comments: So hollowly is a word. Hmmm, not gonna use that. -GHS
records.assessment: While physically confined, Taichi realizes that he had apparently been drifting in a vacant daze. The English depicts him meandering about and substitutes the abstract location 'hollowness.'
records.remedy: apparently drifted in a vacant daze

highlights.text: meandered about in hollowness

records.jp: だが口ではそう言っていても、体は正直だった。
records.en: But while the mouth said so, the body had evidence.
comments: See CCA0012. And around it runs, one more time. He's gotten better with curry, but the "time loop" of this room is making him forget once again. He'll have to drop the bomb. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese idiom says that despite Taichi's words, his body honestly revealed his reaction. The English substitutes the unrelated claim that his body possessed evidence.
records.remedy: my body was honest

highlights.text: the body had evidence

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんを見た瞬間、全身の肌が泡立つ。
records.en: The instant I saw Youko-chan, the skin throughout my body bubbled,
records.assessment: Taichi breaks out in gooseflesh the moment he sees Youko. The English literally makes his skin bubble.
records.remedy: gooseflesh rose all over my body

highlights.text: the skin throughout my body bubbled

records.jp: 彼女が脇にしゃがみこむ。
records.en: She squatted underarm.
records.assessment: Youko crouches beside Taichi. The English mistakes the ordinary word for 'beside' as an anatomical underarm location.
records.remedy: She crouches beside me.

highlights.text: She squatted underarm.

records.jp: 僕は……緊張している。
records.en: Just a little boy, I... was nervous.
comments: He's about to be raped. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says only that the first-person speaker is nervous in the present. The English invents his being a little boy and changes the state to the past.
records.remedy: I... am nervous.

highlights.text: Just a little boy, I... was nervous.

records.jp: 「一心同体になるの」
records.en: Youko: "That we will become alter egos."
records.assessment: The Japanese expression means that the two will become one in body and soul. Alter egos are alternate selves and do not convey that union.
records.remedy: one in body and soul

highlights.text: alter egos

records.jp: 確か、はじめて彼女と……。
records.en: Definitely, the very first time me and her...
records.assessment: Here the adverb marks uncertain recollection, meaning 'if I remember correctly.' The English instead asserts certainty.
records.remedy: If I remember correctly

highlights.text: Definitely

records.jp: 監禁されてたんだ。
records.en: Being confined.
records.assessment: The Japanese is a complete past-progressive statement that the speaker was being held captive. The English is an unattached gerund fragment and omits the subject.
records.remedy: I was being held captive.

highlights.text: Being confined.

records.jp: 「脱出……脱出しないと、な」
records.en: Taichi: "Escape... if I don't escape, well."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he has to escape. The English turns that necessity into an unfinished conditional clause.
records.remedy: Escape... I have to escape.

highlights.text: Escape... if I don't escape, well.

records.jp: たった数日で？
records.en: With this number of days elapsed?
records.assessment: The Japanese asks whether this happened in only a few days. The English replaces both the small number and the emphatic 'only' with an unspecified quantity.
records.remedy: In only a few days?

highlights.text: With this number of days elapsed?

records.jp: 見てしまう。
records.en: I ended up seeing that.
records.assessment: In context, the Japanese describes Taichi finding himself looking toward the doorknob. The English instead claims that he saw an unspecified thing.
records.remedy: I find myself looking over there.

highlights.text: I ended up seeing that.

records.jp: 変化。性欲。空腹。
records.en: Mutation. Libido. Hunger.
records.assessment: The Japanese noun means change or variation in the otherwise unchanging confinement. 'Mutation' incorrectly implies a biological transformation.
records.remedy: Change.

highlights.text: Mutation.

records.jp: 一通り済むと、彼女の指先は、下腹部を撫でた。
records.en: The ending, as typical, is her fingers caressing my lower half.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that once the usual routine is finished, her fingertips stroke his lower abdomen. The English recasts the temporal clause as a typical ending and changes the body part to his entire lower half.
records.remedy: Once the usual routine is over, her fingertips stroke my lower abdomen.

highlights.text: The ending, as typical, is her fingers caressing my lower half.

records.jp: 出る！！
records.en: IT'LL COME OOOUT!!!
records.assessment: In this context the omitted first-person subject marks the speaker's imminent climax. The English instead predicts that an unspecified object will come out.
records.remedy: I'M COMING!!!

highlights.text: IT'LL COME OOOUT!!!

records.jp: 「……太一、可愛い、好き」
records.en: Taichi: "...Taichi... so cute, love you."
records.assessment: The authoritative source identifies Youko as the speaker addressing Taichi. The English labels Taichi as speaking to himself.
records.remedy: Youko:

highlights.text: Taichi:

records.jp: いや、道具、なんだと。
records.en: No, I'm an utensil, dammit.
records.assessment: The Japanese calls the speaker a tool or instrument. 'Utensil' is the wrong kind of object here and also takes the article 'a,' not 'an.'
records.remedy: a tool

highlights.text: an utensil

records.jp: 消えたい、と思うだけだ。
records.en: I think I want them to vanish, but,
records.assessment: The speaker says only that he wants to disappear. The English changes the object to an unspecified plural 'them' and adds an unfinished adversative clause.
records.remedy: All I can think is that I want to disappear.

highlights.text: I think I want them to vanish, but,

records.jp: 一度は半身とした相手だ。
records.en: This enemy was once half of my own body.
records.assessment: The Japanese calls Youko the person or partner whom Taichi once made his other half. It does not call her an enemy.
records.remedy: This person

highlights.text: This enemy

records.jp: 自分に負けたまま、振り出しに戻されるのはつらい。
records.en: It hurts to be sent to the drawing board with my self still undefeated.
comments: Cough. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is still defeated by himself. The English reverses the result and calls the self undefeated.
records.remedy: while still defeated by myself

highlights.text: my self still undefeated

records.jp: 自分に打ち克つのは克己って書くくらいで難しいんだけど……さ。
records.en: To surmount the self is nearly as difficult as pronouncing the words 'self control', but... well.
comments: PCP CCA0016
And we come back to that point again. That one scene was blatantly hallucinated; and so this... -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese remarks that the written word for self-mastery literally contains the characters for overcoming oneself. It says nothing about pronunciation, so the English invents a different and incoherent comparison.
records.remedy: hard enough that the word for self-mastery is written 'overcome oneself'

highlights.text: nearly as difficult as pronouncing the words 'self control'

records.jp: 傷つけるしかない。
records.en: I can't but wound.
comments: He got this far to avoid wounding; and yet the only way he has to get onwards is to do this again. In a sense, he's hurt them all even separating, Touko and Kiri probably hardest. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he has no choice but to hurt her. The English omits the person harmed and uses 'wound' without its required object.
records.remedy: I have no choice but to hurt her.

highlights.text: I can't but wound.

records.jp: 突いた一点から、容易に崩壊へと至る、致命的な傷だ。
records.en: A thrust at this one point will easily led towards a downfall, so it will be a fatal wound.
comments: See CCD0009. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies the single weak point as a fatal wound from which collapse will readily follow once struck. The English is grammatically malformed and changes that apposition into an unsupported causal prediction.
records.remedy: It is a fatal wound: strike that one point, and she will readily collapse from there.

highlights.text: A thrust at this one point will easily led towards a downfall, so it will be a fatal wound.

records.jp: 「……からだ、拭くから」
records.en: Youko: "...after I wipe your body."
comments: Answering his implicit question, which is "when will you leave for the hokora". -GHS
records.assessment: Youko announces that she is going to wipe Taichi's body. The English changes the statement into a subordinate 'after' clause with no main clause.
records.remedy: ...I'm going to wipe your body.

highlights.text: ...after I wipe your body.

records.jp: 「今の個体が傷むまでは……二人で同じ時を過ごせる……」
records.en: Youko: "Let us spend the same time together, the two of us... until the individuality we have now has rotten away..."
records.assessment: The Japanese refers to their present individual bodies or forms wearing out. 'Individuality' instead means a personal quality, and the English also uses the wrong participle after 'has.'
records.remedy: until our present bodies wear out

highlights.text: until the individuality we have now has rotten away

records.jp: 「それで、裏切り者」
records.en: Taichi: "And because of that, a traitor."
records.assessment: The connective continues the list with 'and' or 'also.' The English invents a causal claim that the preceding point made her a traitor.
records.remedy: And also

highlights.text: And because of that

records.jp: 「ショックで、全部どっか飛んでいったとでも？」
records.en: Taichi: "That it all had flown away somewhere because of shock?"
comments: Of her looking at him -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether Youko thought the shock had blown everything away. The English omits that matrix question and leaves an ungrammatical subordinate fragment.
records.remedy: Did you think the shock had blown it all away somewhere?

highlights.text: That it all had flown away somewhere because of shock?

records.jp: 「だから、暗黙の了解を破った」
records.en: Taichi: "And therefore, what you did was violate an unspoken agreement."
comments: That borders on the contradictory. More interesting is to remind how Taichi likes things that don't change. As he dislikes the Fall that is intrinsic into every Eden, so he ultimately can't have liked this change in their relationship. -GHS
records.assessment: In context Taichi says that he himself therefore broke their tacit agreement. The English assigns the violation to Youko.
records.remedy: I broke our unspoken agreement

highlights.text: what you did was violate an unspoken agreement

records.jp: 弱々しく震える声。
records.en: A weakly, feminine, shaking voice.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes a weak, trembling voice. The English adds that it is feminine and uses the adverb 'weakly' where an adjective is required.
records.remedy: A weak, trembling voice.

highlights.text: A weakly, feminine, shaking voice.

records.jp: 「声をかけたんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You called out to me."
comments: So did Misato. But Misato's was a religious solicitation, as said explicitly; see CCC3025 - "Youko exists in the real world". The two calls look similar, but are subtly different, and it's more Real World vs. Heaven. -GHS
records.assessment: In context Taichi says that he called out to Youko. The English reverses the speaker and recipient.
records.remedy: I called out to you.

highlights.text: You called out to me.

records.jp: 「だから、急に意識するようになったんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "And you came to realize that quickly."
records.assessment: Taichi explains that he suddenly became conscious of Youko. The English instead makes Youko the person who realized something quickly.
records.remedy: I suddenly became conscious of you

highlights.text: you came to realize that quickly

records.jp: 「二人は一心同体。切ることの出来ない絆」
records.en: Youko: "We are alter egos. It's a bond that cannot be severed."
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the pair are one in body and soul. 'Alter egos' describes alternate selves and does not convey their inseparable union.
records.remedy: one in body and soul

highlights.text: alter egos

records.jp: 「君は……誰でも良かったんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You... would've be fine with anyone, that's what."
comments: Yeah, but she had only one, and then again, that's love. So? -GHS
records.assessment: The perfect conditional requires the past participle 'been,' not the base form 'be.'
records.remedy: would've been fine

highlights.text: would've be fine

records.jp: 「……一心同体というのはさ、互いを完全に肯定しあうものだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "...but being alter egos means to assert to each other completely."
records.assessment: Taichi defines being one in body and soul as mutually affirming or accepting each other completely. 'Assert to each other' does not express that acceptance.
records.remedy: means affirming each other completely

highlights.text: means to assert to each other completely

records.jp: 「本来の曜子ちゃんなら、一人でやり遂げようとしたはずだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "The original Youko-chan would have certainly have wanted to do by herself!"
comments: The only reason I can find for her to fall for him at this point is because it's all decided in the Settei. It's sort of weak to only have a metareason, though. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the original Youko would have tried to carry the task through alone. The English duplicates the auxiliary and weakens accomplishment into merely wanting to do something.
records.remedy: would certainly have tried to see it through by herself

highlights.text: would have certainly have wanted to do by herself

records.jp: 生涯で最後の交差のため。
records.en: For the sake of the very last Crossing, without Meeting, of my entire life.
comments: And then there's this, which is so much better it makes the above look that much worse. Oh, forget it. See CCD1001 - and everything else. This ruby text doesn't seem to have comedic intent, for once. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese refers only to the final crossing or intersection of Taichi's life. The English invents 'without Meeting' and turns the simple image into an unsupported title-like construction.
records.remedy: crossing

highlights.text: Crossing, without Meeting

records.jp: 「君は何もしなかったじゃないか！」
records.en: Taichi: "You didn't do absolutely nothing, didn't you!"
records.assessment: The Japanese accuses Youko of doing nothing. The English double negative literally says that she did do something.
records.remedy: You did absolutely nothing

highlights.text: You didn't do absolutely nothing

records.jp: 「俺は君が解放されて、元に戻ってくれるだけで満足だった」
records.en: Taichi: "If only I had been released by you, and let me go back to what I was, that alone would have satisfied me."
comments: He wasn't being Strawman Saintly in a way that borders the facepalmingly dumb - even considering he's ZOMGS TEH GEESAS; he just wanted the deed done, and all to go back as it was before. In other words, he wanted something that could never ever have happened: un-Downfall. But once the current Eden has Fallen, there ain't no going back; there's only pretending that another Eden is being built, self-assurances that This Time It Will Work, and then watching the same idiocies be performed, all with the same result. This cannot be solved, in the Christian vision, until enough embrace Jesus as Lord, bringing in the end of the world itself. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he would have been satisfied if Youko were freed and returned to normal. The English reverses the beneficiary and makes Taichi the person Youko should release and restore.
records.remedy: I would have been satisfied just for you to be freed and return to normal.

highlights.text: If only I had been released by you, and let me go back to what I was, that alone would have satisfied me.

records.jp: 「君は裏切り者だ。みみ先輩なんて可愛いもんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You are the traitor. Mimi-senpai was just adorably cute."
comments: Aside from the religion/real world of above, Misato wanted to be forgiven; Youko merely wants things to go her way. For starters, she wants Taichi as he was back before Misato and the rest had their way with him. Although unfortunately largely conjecture on my part, she may want him back to the way he was before she broke him at least to ease her conscience about her responsibility in the matter. -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom says that Mimi-senpai's betrayal was mild or nothing by comparison. It is not a literal claim that Mimi-senpai was adorably cute.
records.remedy: Mimi-senpai's betrayal was nothing by comparison.

highlights.text: Mimi-senpai was just adorably cute.

records.jp: 「君みたいな頂点にいる人の、退化した愛なんか欲しくないよ」
records.en: Taichi: "People like you who exist at the very summit don't want anything as degenerate as love!"
comments: And there we come to one of the few gems in this sewer: this is laughable. Taichi has miserably failed to understand Youko; she wants love because she doesn't live anywhere near that summit, it's only in his mind that she does. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he does not want the degraded love of someone at the summit like Youko. The English instead says that people like Youko do not want love.
records.remedy: I don't want the degraded love of someone at the very top like you!

highlights.text: People like you who exist at the very summit don't want anything as degenerate as love!

records.jp: 「長い時間を投じて、俺を保持して……」
records.en: Taichi: "Tossing away long hours, preserving me..."
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko invested or devoted a long time to preserving Taichi. The English instead says that she threw those hours away.
records.remedy: Investing a long time

highlights.text: Tossing away long hours

records.jp: 「暗示そのものだ」
records.en: Taichi: "The hint was right there."
records.assessment: Taichi says that the act was suggestion or conditioning itself. The English instead calls it a clue that happened to be nearby.
records.remedy: That was suggestion itself.

highlights.text: The hint was right there.

records.jp: 「君は身動き一つ取れなくなった」
records.en: Taichi: "You were unable to make but one movement."
comments: Myotron'd? Maybe that's why he became unable to look at blood; she learned it from her. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko became unable to make even a single movement. The English construction instead suggests she could make one movement.
records.remedy: unable to make even a single movement

highlights.text: unable to make but one movement

records.jp: 「頑張ったよ。おかしくなるくらいに」
records.en: Taichi: "I gave it all! Until I became sort of weird."
comments: CCD0022A now contrasts with this. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that he worked hard enough to nearly lose his mind. Calling the result 'sort of weird' substantially weakens both the extremity and the voice.
records.remedy: Hard enough to nearly lose my mind.

highlights.text: Until I became sort of weird.

records.jp: 「そしてこれも断定できる」
records.en: Taichi: "And then, one thing we can with this conclude."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he can state this point conclusively too. The English switches to a collective subject and uses malformed word order.
records.remedy: I can state this conclusively too

highlights.text: one thing we can with this conclude

records.jp: 「なまじ優秀で強い精神力を持ってるから、一度定まった観念に逆らえない」
records.en: Taichi: "Because when you have a strong willpower and incomplete exceptionality, once fixated an idea becomes unopposable."
comments: See CCA0023. So she's stands at the absolute top, and if she continues advancing while standing at the top she can become something amazing, but she didn't, because she's not completely perfect and therefore becomes incapable of changing her ideas, like she did when she decided to fall in love with Taichi after she broke him. In short she's a chick except she's an egg and a piece who can't be resurrected as it'd take magic except there she is therefore magic but magic is a sleight of hand that also requires a viewer meaning detective authority but if Erika doesn't have it no problem she can still do everything 100% even when she can't and still fake-Beatrice can't become a player because that's impossible and therefore certain due to the fact of miracles being about low probability events making them closer to certain. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that precisely because Youko is so capable and strong-willed, she cannot defy an idea once it becomes fixed. The English invents 'incomplete exceptionality,' makes the idea itself unopposable, and is grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: Precisely because you're so capable and strong-willed, you can't defy an idea once it becomes fixed.

highlights.text: Because when you have a strong willpower and incomplete exceptionality, once fixated an idea becomes unopposable.

records.jp: 「科学的に分析された怪獣みたいだよ、それ」
records.en: Taichi: "That's like analyzing a monster scientifically, that's what it is."
comments: A monster is a thing of fantasy, so putting that under scientific analysis would reveal nothing but flaws; cringe-inducing whiplash segue aside, since Cross Channel is religious-inspired fantasy of the Tolkenian species, and all the sci-fi bits are troll for the less careful, this makes sense. Out of context. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese compares Youko to a monster that has already been scientifically analyzed. The English instead compares the situation to the act of analyzing a monster.
records.remedy: You're like a monster that's been scientifically analyzed

highlights.text: That's like analyzing a monster scientifically

records.jp: 「……太一に抵抗、したくない」
records.en: Taichi: "...I don't want to... oppose Taichi."
comments: Because the above was Taichi's will due to her making pretext and I give up. -GHS
records.assessment: The authoritative source identifies Youko as the speaker saying that she does not want to resist Taichi. The English labels the line as Taichi speaking.
records.remedy: Youko:

highlights.text: Taichi:

records.jp: 「自分の心を、他者に仮託するな！」
records.en: Taichi: "Don'tcha make other people into a pretext for your own heart!"
comments: See CCC3012A, possibly above. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi tells Youko not to project or entrust her own heart to someone else. 'Make other people into a pretext' describes using them as an excuse and changes the meaning.
records.remedy: project your own heart onto someone else

highlights.text: make other people into a pretext for your own heart

records.jp: へたり込む。
records.en: She falls hard onto the floor.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko sinks or collapses down. The English adds a hard impact with the floor that is not present.
records.remedy: sinks to the floor

highlights.text: falls hard onto the floor

records.jp: 魂の抜けたような彼女を、祠につれてきた。
records.en: I brought the dispirited girl to the hokora.
records.assessment: The Japanese uses the ordinary common noun for a small shrine. The unexplained transliteration with an English article withholds that meaning.
records.remedy: the small shrine

highlights.text: the hokora

records.en: Taichi: "...Taichi."
records.assessment: The authoritative source identifies Youko as the speaker addressing Taichi. The English incorrectly labels Taichi as speaking his own name.
records.remedy: Youko:

highlights.text: Taichi:

records.jp: 「自分にいいものを与えてくれるなにか」
records.en: Taichi: "Just a whatever that gives you something that you want yourself."
records.assessment: Taichi defines the object as something that gives Youko something good for herself. The English is grammatically malformed and changes 'good for you' into something she wants herself.
records.remedy: Just something that gives you something good.

highlights.text: Just a whatever that gives you something that you want yourself.

records.jp: 「否定するわけじゃないよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "This is not me repudiating you, OK?"
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is not rejecting the transactional conception of love he just described. The English instead says that he is not repudiating Youko herself.
records.remedy: I'm not denying that kind of love

highlights.text: This is not me repudiating you

records.jp: 「ただ、そうやってつがいになるには……俺は駄目すぎるから」
records.en: Taichi: "Just, to have become paired that way... made me totally worthless."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is far too hopeless or unfit to form a pair in that way. The English instead describes a past pairing that caused him to become worthless.
records.remedy: I'm far too hopeless to pair up that way

highlights.text: to have become paired that way... made me totally worthless

records.jp: 「どうにも、ならなかったことなの？」
records.en: Youko: "So we could never become something, no matter what?"
records.assessment: Youko asks whether there was nothing they could do about the situation. The English instead asks whether they could never become an unspecified thing.
records.remedy: Was there nothing we could do about it?

highlights.text: So we could never become something, no matter what?

records.jp: 「やっぱり、手近な俺を利用する可能性は高かった」
records.en: Taichi: "Indeed, the likelihood you'd have used what was underhand, me, was high."
records.assessment: Taichi calls himself the person who was nearby or readily at hand. 'Underhand' incorrectly characterizes him as deceitful.
records.remedy: someone close at hand

highlights.text: what was underhand

records.jp: 「だから、平気だよ」
records.en: Taichi: "And so, it'll be alright!"
records.assessment: Taichi reassures Youko that he is fine or that it does not bother him now. The English changes the subject to an unspecified situation and projects the state into the future.
records.remedy: I'm all right

highlights.text: it'll be alright

records.jp: 「私、再挑戦する」
records.en: Youko: "I would try for you again."
records.assessment: Youko states that she will try again. The English makes the action conditional and adds Taichi as its beneficiary.
records.remedy: I'll try again.

highlights.text: I would try for you again.

records.jp: 恭しく頭を下げて。
records.en: A reverent bow, down to the waist.
records.assessment: The Japanese says only that the speaker reverently lowers his head. The English adds the unsupported depth of a waist-level bow.
records.remedy: lowering my head reverently

highlights.text: down to the waist

records.jp: 「……胸、痛いんだ……失恋って……」
records.en: Youko: "...breast, hurts... it's a broken heart..."
records.assessment: In this statement about heartbreak, the Japanese word refers to Youko's chest or heart hurting. 'Breast' wrongly localizes the pain to the anatomical breast.
records.remedy: my heart hurts

highlights.text: breast, hurts

records.jp: 「カレーパンがなくなるその日まで」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Until that day when curry bread itself has finally passed."
comments: CP CCC0025
records.assessment: Sakuraba means until the day when the curry bread is gone or runs out. 'Passed' does not express the disappearance of the food.
records.remedy: the curry bread is finally gone

highlights.text: curry bread itself has finally passed

records.jp: 「レトルトのカレーでも食ってればいいじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "Wouldn't you like to eat some retort pouch curry too?"
comments: CP CCC0025
records.assessment: Taichi dismissively says that Sakuraba could just eat packaged curry. The English turns this into a polite offer or preference question and adds 'too.'
records.remedy: You could just eat some packaged curry.

highlights.text: Wouldn't you like to eat some retort pouch curry too?

records.jp: 信頼できるか。
records.en: Yeah, because I can trust you.
records.assessment: The Japanese is a skeptical rhetorical question meaning that the narrator cannot trust Sakuraba. The English reverses the polarity and directly addresses him as 'you.'
records.remedy: As if I could trust him.

highlights.text: Yeah, because I can trust you.

records.jp: 「わかってるじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "Didn't you get it?"
records.assessment: Taichi positively acknowledges that Sakuraba does understand. The English changes this into a negative question suggesting that he failed to understand.
records.remedy: See, you do get it.

highlights.text: Didn't you get it?

records.jp: 「……インポ野郎が」
records.en: Taichi: "...but yer impotent, you son of a bitch."
records.assessment: The phrase requires the contraction 'you're.' 'Yer' is a possessive dialect spelling and leaves the clause grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: you're impotent

highlights.text: yer impotent

records.jp: 考えてないわけじゃないのか。
records.en: That just means he hasn't thought through this at all, doesn't it.
comments: CP CCC4016
records.assessment: The Japanese double-negative question concludes that Sakuraba has given the matter some thought. The English removes that negation and concludes the opposite.
records.remedy: he has given this some thought

highlights.text: he hasn't thought through this at all

records.jp: 「あと足りない分はこれで補ってくれ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "And, I'll be supplementing the amount that's missing with this."
comments: CP CCC4016
records.assessment: Sakuraba hands something to Taichi and tells him to use it to make up the shortfall. The English instead says that Sakuraba himself will do the supplementing.
records.remedy: Use this to make up whatever you're short.

highlights.text: I'll be supplementing the amount that's missing with this.

records.jp: 「よし、二人で鷹になるぞ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Great, we'll become Twin Falcons."
comments: Suspecting it's this: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%81%B5%E3%81%9F%E3%82%8A%E9%B7%B9 ...unless it means Eagles, and then... -GHS
records.assessment: Sakuraba says simply that the two of them will become hawks. The English changes hawks to falcons and invents a capitalized compound name.
records.remedy: hawks together

highlights.text: Twin Falcons

records.jp: 「まあスズメでもトンビにでもなってくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, we're more like Tree Sparrow (those chatty ones) and Black Kite."
comments: Assuming it's a pun on the names of the guys above. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi dismissively tells Sakuraba that he can become a sparrow or kite for all Taichi cares. The English instead assigns both birds to the pair, adds a species gloss, and presents it as Taichi's comparison.
records.remedy: Fine, become a sparrow or a kite for all I care.

highlights.text: Well, we're more like Tree Sparrow (those chatty ones) and Black Kite.

records.jp: 「日曜までいろと言っただろうが！」
records.en: Taichi: "I told to be here until Sunday didn't I!"
comments: Can be read "live until Sunday". Since leaving the town by a route that goes by, but not through, the hokora is de-facto death... -GHS
records.assessment: The English omits the object of 'told.' Taichi says that he told Sakuraba to remain through Sunday.
records.remedy: I told you to be here until Sunday

highlights.text: I told to be here until Sunday

records.jp: 桜庭を囲った。
records.en: I fenced in Sakuraba.
comments: Though one of the meanings is "shelter a criminal". Hmmm, but that's not quite it, is it? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi kept or confined Sakuraba with him. The English literally depicts the construction of a fence around him.
records.remedy: I kept Sakuraba with me.

highlights.text: I fenced in Sakuraba.

records.jp: さて、あと数分もないだろう。
records.en: Well then, it won't be for a few more minutes I guess.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that fewer than a few minutes remain. The English instead says that an event will not occur for a few more minutes.
records.remedy: there can't be even a few minutes left

highlights.text: it won't be for a few more minutes

records.jp: ギリギリだったな。
records.en: We made it at just at the last moment, didn't we.
records.assessment: The preposition 'at' is duplicated.
records.remedy: at just

highlights.text: at just at

records.jp: 「つるむのは、もうおしまいなのか？」
records.en: Sakuraba: "We're now all done with our mate-ing, right?"
records.assessment: Sakuraba asks whether the two are finished hanging around together. The English incorrectly turns this into mating and compounds the error with a nonstandard hyphenation.
records.remedy: hanging out together

highlights.text: mate-ing

records.jp: 「けど一番ショックなことは、おまえが追いつめられているのに、何もできないことだ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "But the most shocking thing was, even though you were cornered, you couldn't do anything about it."
records.assessment: Sakuraba says that his own inability to do anything while Taichi was cornered shocked him most. The English makes Taichi both the cornered person and the one unable to act.
records.remedy: even though you were cornered, I couldn't do anything about it

highlights.text: even though you were cornered, you couldn't do anything about it

records.jp: 「おまえは自分のことだけ考えてろ。人の心配なんざ百年早いんだよ。桜庭の分際でシリアスなこと言ってんじゃない」
records.en: Taichi: "You stick to thinking about your own self. Yer a century too young to to be worrying about people! Your social class is that of someone who can't say serious stuff, Sakuraba!"
comments: It's more manga/shonen referencing. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi says that it is a hundred years too soon for Sakuraba to worry about others and rebukes him for talking seriously. The English adds a claim about social class, mistranslates the idiom as literal youth, misspells 'you're,' and duplicates 'to.'
records.remedy: It's a hundred years too soon for you to worry about other people! Don't go saying serious things when you're Sakuraba!

highlights.text: Yer a century too young to to be worrying about people! Your social class is that of someone who can't say serious stuff, Sakuraba!

records.en: Sakuraba: "...hm... sent back?"
comments: Literally knows. -GHS
records.assessment: Sakuraba wonders whether the sound is a broadcast. The English mistakes the noun for the unrelated passive action 'sent back.'
records.remedy: a broadcast?

highlights.text: sent back?

records.jp: 今時、そんなことを言うヤツがいるか。
records.en: That there would exists a guy that would blurt out that right on this occasion.
records.assessment: The Japanese is a rhetorical question asking who would say such a thing nowadays. The English removes the negative rhetorical force, changes 'nowadays' to this particular occasion, and is grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: Who would say something like that nowadays?

highlights.text: That there would exists a guy that would blurt out that right on this occasion.

records.jp: いるかよ……。
records.en: That there would exist...
records.assessment: The Japanese is a negative rhetorical answer meaning that no such person exists. The English presents existence affirmatively and leaves an unattached fragment.
records.remedy: As if anyone would...

highlights.text: That there would exist...

records.jp: 支倉曜子は部屋に戻った。
records.en: Hasekura Youko returned to her one-room apartment.
comments: It's not a "room" as intended generally in English, and it's not an "apartment" as intended in the same, so making explicit. This would be after school. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says only that Youko returned to her room. The English adds both that the room is an apartment and that it is a one-room unit.
records.remedy: room

highlights.text: one-room apartment

records.jp: 部屋に沿ってＬ字に組み合わされたラックは、見るからに手狭だ。
records.en: The rack, arranged in an L shape and set parallel to the room, is discernibly thin.
comments: L=り ri. Hum, it IS an unit of measurement, but I don't see it. 12th letter of the alphabet... plus the 3 PCs it has on and the 6 tatami room it's in, 7x3=21. But that's probably coincidence. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the L-shaped rack is visibly too cramped or insufficient for the room. The English instead describes the rack's physical thickness.
records.remedy: obviously too cramped

highlights.text: discernibly thin

records.jp: 万全の盗撮をするには三台すべてを用いるが、今はブラウジング専用機とも言える一台をのぞき使用されることはほとんどない。
records.en: While all three were utilized for a flawless stalking, now, except for one machine that could be said to be dedicated for browsing, they are almost never used.
comments: 3 whole PCs? What's she doing with them? Are peeping cameras so processor expensive? Uh, not that I don't use 2 PCs myself, but... wait that's actually three, but, uhm, you know what nevermind. Don't see numbers here. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese specifically refers to covert filming or voyeuristic surveillance using all three machines. 'Stalking' is a different act and loses the camera-based meaning.
records.remedy: thorough covert filming

highlights.text: flawless stalking

records.jp: 天井まではめ殺されている書棚には、各種の専門書が詰め込まれている。
records.en: Bookshelves are infixed in the wall, so tall they seemed to stab through the ceiling, and crammed to the brim with specialized technical books of all kinds.
comments: Now that's an use for the word 'kill' that even I didn't expect. (Though I do tend to expect words to have a sexual meaning. Often correctly.) -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the bookcases are fitted or fixed up to the ceiling. The English invents the image of their stabbing through it.
records.remedy: fixed in place all the way to the ceiling

highlights.text: so tall they seemed to stab through the ceiling

records.jp: 政治家の汚職。
records.en: Corrupted politicians,
records.assessment: The Japanese names political corruption or corruption by politicians. The English instead describes politicians who have been corrupted.
records.remedy: Political corruption

highlights.text: Corrupted politicians

records.jp: 少年犯罪。
records.en: juvenile criminals,
records.assessment: The Japanese names juvenile crime as a topic. The English changes the subject from criminal acts to the people who commit them.
records.remedy: juvenile crime

highlights.text: juvenile criminals

records.jp: その自殺についてのページから、何気なく飛んだ掲示板に、曜子の目は止まった。
records.en: An innocent forum post was flowing by on that webpage about suicide, and it's on it that Youko's eyes stopped.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko casually followed a link from the suicide page to a message board, where something caught her eye. The English instead puts an innocent post flowing past on the suicide page itself.
records.remedy: From the page about suicide, Youko casually followed a link to a message board, where her eyes stopped.

highlights.text: An innocent forum post was flowing by on that webpage about suicide, and it's on it that Youko's eyes stopped.

records.jp: ここ数日、いくつか気になる動きを見せた銘柄を、オンライントレードで調整する。
records.en: The last few days she has been making adjustment on the online trading of a number of stocks that have been showing interesting movement.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes Youko now adjusting several stocks that have shown notable movement over the last few days. The English makes the adjustments themselves a days-long activity and uses the ungrammatical singular 'adjustment.'
records.remedy: She adjusts through online trading several stocks that have shown notable movement over the last few days

highlights.text: The last few days she has been making adjustment on the online trading

records.jp: 今日もトレーニングだけは済ませてきた。
records.en: And today as well ended up being nothing but training.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that today too she at least finished her training. The English instead says that training was the only thing she did all day.
records.remedy: today too, she at least finished her training

highlights.text: today as well ended up being nothing but training

records.jp: 自分を高めて外に出る。
records.en: to make herself worthy and capable, and leave for the outside.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko would improve herself before going out into the world. The English adds the moral judgment that she must make herself worthy.
records.remedy: improve herself

highlights.text: make herself worthy and capable

records.jp: 半身の設定と、同期。
records.en: at the same time when she established she was half of a body.
comments: Can literally be read "at the exact moment when the Settei called for me to be half a body". -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese fragment describes synchronization with the setting or definition of her other half. The English instead says that Youko established herself as half of a body and adds a temporal relation.
records.remedy: in synchronization with the definition of her other half

highlights.text: at the same time when she established she was half of a body

records.jp: 未熟な伴侶を守るために、能力は磨かれるようになった。
records.en: Her skills were then being polished for the sake of protecting this inexperienced half of her.
comments: She may have "fallen" for him when she broke him. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese calls the person an inexperienced partner or mate whom Youko is to protect. The English instead identifies him as one half of Youko herself.
records.remedy: her inexperienced partner

highlights.text: this inexperienced half of her

records.jp: そして彼は失われた。
records.en: And then he went away.
comments: ...that's one big jump otherwise. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that he was lost, a stronger and more final description than his merely going away.
records.remedy: he was lost

highlights.text: he went away

records.jp: 指標さえ消えた。
records.en: All that points to him had vanished.
comments: Odd. It sounds like he was removed from the timeline entirely. Of course, since Youko still exists, that means he's occasionally showing up: when he plays Youko. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that even Youko's guiding objective or benchmark disappeared. The English turns this abstract guide into a set of things that point toward the absent person.
records.remedy: Even her guiding objective

highlights.text: All that points to him

records.jp: もうすることはない。
records.en: Other things to do she doesn't have.
records.assessment: The English uses malformed object-fronting for the simple statement that she has nothing else to do.
records.remedy: She has nothing else to do.

highlights.text: Other things to do she doesn't have.

records.jp: スイッチは入りっぱなしになっている。
records.en: She ended up leaving it switched on.
comments: THAT she leaves always on...? Shouldn't there be static? That radio is always completely silent, and it's just a metaphor for how "she" (definitely the others) still see Taichi talking to them every once in a while... whether he's too far gone to hear them, whether it's a chat that maintains the proper distance and therefore, metaphorically, indistinguishable from him not being there anymore in that perverted, if ordinarily longed for, sense. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese describes the switch's continuing state: it has been left on continuously. The English instead presents a completed action performed by Youko.
records.remedy: The switch has been left on continuously.

highlights.text: She ended up leaving it switched on.

records.jp: どれくらい経過しただろうか。
records.en: How many have even passed by now?
records.assessment: The Japanese asks how much time has passed. The English omits time, uses 'many' without a countable noun, and gives the verb no grammatical subject.
records.remedy: How much time has passed by now?

highlights.text: How many have even passed by now?

records.jp: ぽかんと口を開き、魂が抜けてしまったような顔をしている。
records.en: The face she had was with her mouth open slack-jawed, as if her ghost had just escaped from it.
comments: See CCB2009/CCD2002. Odd Touko reference. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese simile says that Youko looks as though her soul has left her. The English changes the soul to a ghost and adds its physical escape through her open mouth.
records.remedy: her soul had left her

highlights.text: her ghost had just escaped from it

records.jp: 声が聞こえなくなる。
records.en: His voice that could no longer be heard.
records.assessment: The Japanese states that his voice becomes inaudible. The English turns this into a noun fragment and changes the event to a past state.
records.remedy: His voice becomes inaudible.

highlights.text: His voice that could no longer be heard.

records.jp: 好ましかった。
records.en: It was desire.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko found him likable or was fond of him. 'Desire' incorrectly substitutes a sexualized abstract drive and removes the person she liked.
records.remedy: She was fond of him.

highlights.text: It was desire.

records.jp: 異性だった。
records.en: It was the opposite gender.
comments: Now see CCD1001: opposite gender awareness, just like Misato. Perhaps Kiri. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that he was a member of the opposite sex. The English replaces the person with impersonal 'it' and predicates a category rather than membership.
records.remedy: He was of the opposite sex.

highlights.text: It was the opposite gender.

records.jp: でも……好意は本物だった。
records.en: But... the favoritism was the real thing.

records.remedy: the affection was genuine

highlights.text: the favoritism was the real thing

records.jp: 殺戮の日、誰一人として殺せなかった弱さ。
records.en: Her weakness of not killing just even one person on the day of the massacre,
comments: She thinks that was weakness? She still got lots to go then. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese describes her weakness in being unable to kill anyone on the day of the massacre. The English uses contradictory quantifiers and recasts inability as a voluntary failure to act.
records.remedy: Her weakness in being unable to kill anyone on the day of the massacre.

highlights.text: Her weakness of not killing just even one person on the day of the massacre,

records.jp: 刃物を手に、死体の中、佇むだけの自分だった。
records.en: this self of hers that only stood stock still, knee-deep in the dead, blade in hand.
comments: Too young to die? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that she merely stood among the corpses with a blade in hand. The English adds that the bodies reached her knees and uses the malformed phrase 'this self of hers.'
records.remedy: herself, merely standing among the corpses with a blade in hand.

highlights.text: this self of hers that only stood stock still, knee-deep in the dead, blade in hand.

records.jp: 嗚咽。
records.en: Groaning.
records.assessment: The Japanese noun denotes sobbing or a choked cry of grief, not a groan.
records.remedy: Sobbing.

highlights.text: Groaning.

records.jp: 痛切のきわみ。
records.en: The height of dolorousness.
comments: Lit. "seriousness", but this should be the sense. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese means the very height of anguish or poignancy. The English uses the awkward abstract noun 'dolorousness' in a nonidiomatic construction.
records.remedy: The very height of anguish.

highlights.text: The height of dolorousness.

records.jp: 島友貴は、母方の家に同居するようになった姉・見里の、まだ未整理の私室に呼びかけた。
records.en: Shima Tomoki called out into the still unfinished private room of his sister Misato, who had come to live into the house of her mother's side.
comments: Meaning her mother has forgiven her too. No little detail! Certainly more important than how Tomoki's house isn't on the map. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Misato's private room is still unpacked or disorganized after she moved into her maternal relatives' home. 'Unfinished' implies construction, while 'live into the house of her mother's side' is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Shima Tomoki called into the still-unpacked room of his sister Misato, who had moved into their maternal relatives' home.

highlights.text: Shima Tomoki called out into the still unfinished private room of his sister Misato, who had come to live into the house of her mother's side.

records.jp: 扉は開いていた。
records.en: The door was opening,
records.assessment: The Japanese describes the door's already-open state. The English instead depicts it in the process of opening.
records.remedy: The door was open

highlights.text: The door was opening

records.jp: 中途半端な幅の視野に、見里が立ち膝の姿勢で硬直している。
records.en: and in the halfway width of his field of vision there was Misato, stiffening her posture with a knee drawn up.
records.assessment: Tomoki sees Misato through the partly open doorway. The English instead assigns an undefined halfway width to his field of vision.
records.remedy: through the partly open doorway

highlights.text: in the halfway width of his field of vision

records.jp: 上半身だけを室内に浸し、見つめる。
records.en: He dips only the upper half of his body in the room, and stares.
records.assessment: Tomoki leans his upper body into the room. The English literalizes the action as dipping his body into a liquid-like space.
records.remedy: He leans his upper body into the room

highlights.text: He dips only the upper half of his body in the room

records.jp: 友貴も、姉が見入っていたものを目にする。
records.en: And Tomoki as well witnessed his sister's stare.
comments: Ugh. More troll? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Tomoki sees the object his sister had been staring at. The English instead says that he observes the stare itself.
records.remedy: saw what his sister had been staring at

highlights.text: witnessed his sister's stare

records.jp: かつて、二人には仲間がいた。
records.en: Once, the two of time had a friend. A very good friend.
comments: Nakama is almost as strong as nanaka -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the two once had a companion. The English contains the nonsensical phrase 'two of time' and adds a separate claim that he was a very good friend.
records.remedy: Once, the two of them had a companion.

highlights.text: Once, the two of time had a friend. A very good friend.

records.jp: たまに驚かせてやろうとのぞきこむと、信じられないほど無感情な顔をしている……そんな少年だった。
records.en: On occasion, when she peered at him while going to surprise him, he showed this unbelievably expressionless face... and that was the kind of boy he was.
records.assessment: The demonstrative cannot grammatically modify the adjective phrase in this construction.
records.remedy: an unbelievably expressionless face

highlights.text: this unbelievably expressionless face

records.jp: 友人をするのは構わない。けど、自覚した上で―――
records.en: I don't care if you're his friend. But after you take notice---
records.assessment: Youko says that befriending him is fine, but Misato must do so with conscious awareness of what he is. The English sounds indifferent to an existing friendship and turns awareness into an event that occurs afterward.
records.remedy: It's fine to be his friend. But do it knowing what he is---

highlights.text: I don't care if you're his friend. But after you take notice---

records.en: Tomoki: "...what was?"
records.assessment: Tomoki asks whether they heard something just now. The English omits the deictic reference and leaves an ungrammatical question.
records.remedy: ...what was that just now?

highlights.text: ...what was?

records.en: Tomoki: "...what, is...?"
records.assessment: Tomoki asks what the sound is. The English omits the object and uses malformed word order.
records.remedy: ...w-what is this...?

highlights.text: ...what, is...?

records.jp: 「今週もやってまーす」
records.en: Taichi: "And I made this week tooo!"
records.assessment: Taichi says that the club is on the air again this week. The English instead says that he made the week.
records.remedy: We're on the air again this weeek!

highlights.text: And I made this week tooo!

records.jp: 「第何回だっけな、まあいいや」
records.en: Taichi: "This was episode number, ah who cares."
comments: Now a popular fanservice-ridden 12 episode anime! -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi wonders which numbered episode this is, then dismisses the question. The English changes the question to a malformed past-tense statement.
records.remedy: Which episode was this again? Ah, who cares.

highlights.text: This was episode number, ah who cares.

records.jp: 唖然とするほど、あっけらかんとした声だった。
records.en: His voice seemed very indifferent to what was going on around him, which left them dumbfounded.
comments: This makes perfect sense if he's standing right next to them. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says simply that his voice was astonishingly carefree. The English invents indifference to surrounding events.
records.remedy: astonishingly carefree

highlights.text: very indifferent to what was going on around him

records.jp: 「相変わらず生きていますか？　元気ですか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Have you been losing your hearts to others as usual? Are you in good spirits?"
comments: See CCC3004. It's the same pun, and that's another hint that he's talking to them directly. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi asks whether the listeners are still alive as usual. The English replaces survival with an invented image of losing their hearts to other people.
records.remedy: Are you still alive as usual?

highlights.text: Have you been losing your hearts to others as usual?

records.jp: 「……うまく折り合いをつけて、生きてます」
records.en: Taichi: "...I'm working nicely through things, and living on."
records.assessment: Taichi says that he is finding a way to come to terms with things. The English turns that emotional accommodation into efficient work.
records.remedy: I'm finding a way to come to terms with things

highlights.text: I'm working nicely through things

records.jp: 自分は太一にとって、友人と呼び交わせる存在だったのだろうかと。
records.en: that he perhaps was, for Taichi, a someone with whom there could be the reciprocal exchange of the term, "friend".
records.assessment: The indefinite article cannot precede the pronoun 'someone.'
records.remedy: someone

highlights.text: a someone

records.jp: ラジオはもう言語を投げかけてはこない。
records.en: The radio does not throw any more word at them.
records.assessment: The Japanese personifies the radio as no longer addressing them in language. The English uses a singular count noun after 'any more' and the nonidiomatic action of throwing a word at them.
records.remedy: The radio speaks no more words to them.

highlights.text: The radio does not throw any more word at them.

records.jp: 語りようがない。
records.en: There is no talking.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that there is no way to put the experience into words. The English instead says that nobody is talking.
records.remedy: There is no way to put it into words.

highlights.text: There is no talking.

records.jp: 肌の感触。髪の香り。耳元に残る息づかい。
records.en: The feeling of the skin. The scent of the hair. The breathing that remains on the edge of her ears.
records.assessment: The Japanese evokes remembered breathing lingering beside her ear. The English literalizes the location as the physical edge of the ears and turns breath into the process noun 'breathing.'
records.remedy: The breath that lingered beside her ear.

highlights.text: The breathing that remains on the edge of her ears.

records.jp: 広々とした自室で、冬子は机に突っ伏していた。
records.en: In her spacious personal room, Touko had fallen prostrate on her desk.
records.assessment: The Japanese simply places Touko slumped over the desk in her own spacious room. 'Personal room' is a calque, while 'prostrate on' depicts an unnatural bodily posture rather than伏す at a desk.
records.remedy: In her spacious room, Touko was slumped over her desk.

highlights.text: personal room
fallen prostrate on her desk

records.jp: 反面、いったん親しくなると、際限なく依存した。
records.en: On the other hand, if she became intimate for just a moment, her dependency knew no bounds.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that once Touko became close to someone, she depended on that person without limit. The English mistakes the transition marker for a brief duration.
records.remedy: once she became close to someone

highlights.text: if she became intimate for just a moment

records.jp: 相手と寄り添うために、手段を選ばずプライドも売り払ってしまう。
records.en: To snuggle up to a partner she would, by means fair or foul, even end up selling off her pride.
records.assessment: The Japanese concerns staying emotionally close to the other person. 'Snuggle up' adds a specifically cozy physical action.
records.remedy: To remain close to someone

highlights.text: To snuggle up to a partner

records.jp: 脆い面があった。
records.en: That is a fragile side of her.
records.assessment: The Japanese narration states that Touko had this vulnerable aspect. The English uses a deictic subject and shifts the established past narration into the present.
records.remedy: She had a vulnerable side.

highlights.text: That is a fragile side of her.

records.jp: そんな冬子が女子校にいたのは、適切なことだった。
records.en: As she was like this, it was appropriate for Touko to be in a girl's school.
records.assessment: The Japanese means an all-girls school. The singular possessive describes a school belonging to one girl rather than the institution type.
records.remedy: an all-girls school

highlights.text: a girl's school

records.jp: 相手に怪我をさせたことがきっかけで、冬子は悪名高い国家試験を受けることに。
records.en: On the wake of her causing injury to this partner, Touko took the infamous National Exam.
comments: Original term is not necessarily about her hurting the other girl, might just be the same with Misato and Tomoki. It is not really precise, however. -GHS
records.assessment: The English uses a malformed version of 'in the wake of' for the Japanese causal construction.
records.remedy: After

highlights.text: On the wake of

records.jp: 友達など、その事実だけで消し飛んだ。
records.en: Just because of that, friends scattered and disappeared.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the mere fact made friendship vanish. The English adds the distinct physical image of multiple friends scattering.
records.remedy: that fact alone made any friendship vanish

highlights.text: friends scattered and disappeared

records.jp: 誰か別の人間に、冬子自身の価値を見いだして欲しかった。
records.en: Touko wanted another human someone to discover her own value,
records.assessment: The Japanese means another person. The English combines two alternative noun phrases into an ungrammatical expression.
records.remedy: someone else

highlights.text: another human someone

records.jp: たとえ冬子でなく、別の何者かであっても。
records.en: so that someone else would know it, even if Touko didn't.
comments: swap around -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the value perceived could belong not to Touko herself but to some other persona or identity. The English instead makes Touko the person who fails to know her own value.
records.remedy: even if the person they found value in was not Touko herself, but someone else

highlights.text: so that someone else would know it, even if Touko didn't

records.jp: そのための対面であり、態度である。
records.en: That is the purpose of her manners, for that encounter.
comments: IOW she was looking for precisely the kind of person Taichi was. Well, she's an idiot too. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese identifies her outward presentation and attitude as serving that desire. The English invents a particular encounter and makes her manners its purpose.
records.remedy: That was what her outward presentation and attitude were for.

highlights.text: That is the purpose of her manners, for that encounter.

records.jp: 矜持も自分も投げ捨てて。
records.en: Self-respect and the self as well she threw away.
records.assessment: The English preserves Japanese constituent order so literally that the sentence is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: She cast aside both her pride and herself.

highlights.text: Self-respect and the self as well she threw away.

records.jp: 家政婦が、冬子のための夕食を持ってきたのだ。
records.en: It's the housekeeper, who has brought Touko's dinner with.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that the housekeeper brought Touko's dinner. The English adds a stranded 'with,' leaving the verb phrase incomplete.
records.remedy: has brought Touko's dinner

highlights.text: has brought Touko's dinner with

records.jp: すげなく追い返すと、再び机に伏した。
records.en: Dismissing her curtly, she once again bends onto the desk.
records.assessment: The Japanese continues past narration and says that Touko again lay face down on the desk. The English shifts to present tense and uses the nonidiomatic action 'bends onto.'
records.remedy: she once again slumped over the desk

highlights.text: she once again bends onto the desk

records.jp: 腹の虫が鳴った。
records.en: Her belly bug cried.
records.assessment: 腹の虫が鳴る is an idiom meaning that one's stomach growls. The English translates the component words as a literal insect in her belly.
records.remedy: Her stomach growled.

highlights.text: Her belly bug cried.

records.jp: 懊悩と食欲とのかねあいにべそをかきつつ食事をしていると、ラジオが鳴った。
records.en: As she was having a meal on the verge of tears due to an equilibrium of anguish and hunger, a sound came from the radio.
comments: -de beso again? -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese depicts her tearful compromise between distress and appetite. 'Equilibrium' turns that lived conflict into a technical state of balance.
records.remedy: torn between anguish and hunger

highlights.text: due to an equilibrium of anguish and hunger

records.jp: ラジオのボリュームをひねる。
records.en: She adjust the radio's volume.
records.assessment: The singular subject requires the inflected verb 'adjusts' in the chosen present tense.
records.remedy: She adjusts

highlights.text: She adjust

records.jp: 「生きていますか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Are you living?"
records.assessment: In this direct existential question, 生きていますか asks whether the listener is alive. 'Are you living?' instead sounds like a question about manner or residence.
records.remedy: Are you alive?

highlights.text: Are you living?

records.jp: 唐突に、そんなことを言った。
records.en: That is what he just said, all of a sudden.
records.assessment: The Japanese past narration says that he suddenly said that. The English shifts to present tense and inserts 'just,' which can misleadingly denote recent time.
records.remedy: He said that without warning

highlights.text: That is what he just said

records.jp: 冬子は、ラジオをへし折るような力で、握り締めていた。
records.en: Touko grasped the radio tight, with strength enough to shatter it.
records.assessment: The Japanese specifically compares her grip to the force used to bend and snap the radio. 'Shatter' substitutes a different physical action.
records.remedy: as though she meant to snap it in two

highlights.text: strength enough to shatter it

records.jp: その顔は、ずいぶんと引きつっている。
records.en: Her face cramps, very tightly.
records.assessment: The Japanese describes her face as markedly taut or contorted. The English uses 'cramps' as an intransitive facial action and shifts the surrounding past narration into present tense.
records.remedy: Her face was badly contorted.

highlights.text: Her face cramps, very tightly.

records.jp: 「生きるって……なによ……生きるって……？」
records.en: Touko: "Living on you said... what's this... living on...?"
comments: See CCX0001, refusal of suicide. Seems like a simple thing, but there's ways to live that are like death itself. Like Touko's. -GHS
records.assessment: Touko asks what 'living' is supposed to mean. The English turns the first phrase into a malformed report of something said and repeats the phrasal verb 'living on.'
records.remedy: Living... What do you mean, living...?

highlights.text: Living on you said... what's this... living on...?

records.jp: 気持ちをぶつけることもできないまま。
records.en: without being able to vent her feelings at him either.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that she cannot direct or express her feelings to him. 'Vent' adds the narrower sense of discharging anger or frustration.
records.remedy: express her feelings to him

highlights.text: vent her feelings at him

records.jp: できるはずがなかった。
records.en: She had no expectation should could manage to do that.
records.assessment: The Japanese simply says that she could not possibly do it. The English adds an expectation frame and contains the nonsensical sequence 'should could.'
records.remedy: There was no way she could do that.

highlights.text: She had no expectation should could manage to do that.

records.jp: 別の誰かを好きになるか？
records.en: Moving on to like, to love, another person?
records.assessment: The Japanese is a finite deliberative question asking whether she should fall for someone else. The English turns it into a malformed gerund fragment and adds 'moving on.'
records.remedy: Should she fall in love with someone else?

highlights.text: Moving on to like, to love, another person?

records.jp: 冬子の心は千々に乱れる。
records.en: Touko's heart disorders in thousands of ways.
records.assessment: 千々に乱れる is an idiom for being thrown into complete turmoil. The English literalizes the number and uses 'disorders' ungrammatically as an intransitive verb.
records.remedy: Touko's heart was in utter turmoil.

highlights.text: Touko's heart disorders in thousands of ways.

records.jp: 「他の人なんて、見つからないわよ……ばか」
records.en: Touko: "Another person, really! I'll never find one... dummy."
records.assessment: Touko says that there is no way she could find anyone else. The English inserts an exclamatory 'really' that makes the first phrase sound like incredulous repetition rather than rejecting the possibility.
records.remedy: As if I could find anyone else

highlights.text: Another person, really! I'll never find one

records.jp: 「あたまのおかしい女なんて、誰も好きになってくれないじゃない……」
records.en: Touko: "No one would ever end up loving this woman with her weirdness in the head..."
records.assessment: The Japanese bluntly calls her a crazy woman. The English replaces that self-description with a malformed and evasive phrase.
records.remedy: a crazy woman like me

highlights.text: this woman with her weirdness in the head

records.jp: 「会いたいよ……太一……」
records.en: Touko: "I wanna meet you... Taichi..."
comments: These 'meet' sound a little off, but they're the de-facto opposite of 'cross'. -GHS
records.assessment: 会いたい here means wanting to see an already-known person, not wanting to meet that person for the first time.
records.remedy: I want to see you

highlights.text: I wanna meet you

records.jp: 膝をつき、ゆっくりと自身の価値畳んで……床に額をつけた。
records.en: She fell to her knees, slowly folding her self-worth until it is so small it might be gone... and touched her forehead to the floor.
comments: This means somewhat 'to kill'. Which is what will happen to JAPAN ALL PEOPLE for making tatami into a verb. I won't forgive this! -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese uses the image of folding her own value inward as she lowers herself. The English adds an explicit endpoint in which that value nearly disappears.
records.remedy: slowly folding up her own worth

highlights.text: until it is so small it might be gone

records.jp: ちゃんと触れたいのだ。
records.en: I wanna be well and touched,

records.remedy: I want to truly touch someone

highlights.text: I wanna be well and touched

records.jp: ただそれだけのことを成し遂げるのに、どれくらいの時間が必要なのか。
records.en: to accomplish even merely that, how much time will it be necessary?
records.assessment: The Japanese asks how much time she will need. The English preserves Japanese question structure in an ungrammatical English construction.
records.remedy: how much time would it take?

highlights.text: how much time will it be necessary?

records.jp: お花畑から切り取った華々しい雰囲気が、さびれた古い店先に漂う。
records.en: A magnificent ambiance as if picked fresh from a field of flowers floated into the old deserted storefront.
comments: Tasaki. See CCA0004, it's deserted because the guy's always somewhere on his hobby... hey, just like Taichi! -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese likens the pair's showy atmosphere to something cut from a flower garden and says it hangs around a run-down old shopfront. The English adds freshness and changes the stationary atmosphere into movement into the shop.
records.remedy: A showy atmosphere, as though cut from a flower garden, hung around the run-down old storefront.

floated into the old deserted storefront

records.jp: 買い食いをしていた。
records.en: They were eating the sweets they had just bought.
comments: I'm sure there's a double meaning for prostitution here that I can't see... -GHS

records.remedy: They were eating snacks they had bought while out.

highlights.text: the sweets they had just bought

records.jp: 「はー、霧ちんとこーして買い食いするのも最後かぁ」
records.en: Miki: "Awww, then this buy'n'eat with you is the last, Kiri-chin!"
records.assessment: The English calques 買い食い into the invented noun 'buy'n'eat' and uses 'the last' without the required noun or time expression.
records.remedy: this is the last time we'll get snacks together

highlights.text: this buy'n'eat with you is the last

records.jp: 咎めだてる口調で、連呼した。
records.en: And that is what she kept repeating, reproach in her tone of voice.
records.assessment: The Japanese says directly that she repeated the phrase in a reproachful tone. The English adds a retrospective deictic frame and shifts the narration into present tense.
records.remedy: She kept repeating it

highlights.text: And that is what she kept repeating

records.jp: 霧は苦笑するしかない。
records.en: Kiri couldn't do anything but a forced smile.

highlights.text: a forced smile

records.jp: 社会に適応できるようになったと認められたわけである。
records.en: She had been declared as capable of conforming with society.

records.remedy: capable of adapting to society

highlights.text: capable of conforming with society

records.jp: 心中のわだかまりを、ほどいたわけではない。
records.en: It isn't that the reserves and ill feelings that exist deep in her heart had slackened.

records.remedy: the knot in her heart had come undone

highlights.text: the reserves and ill feelings that exist deep in her heart had slackened

records.jp: 今の自分を肯定できてもいない。
records.en: She cannot assert to her present self, either.
comments: This reminds me of the folOling sentence: "barf of vanilla". -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that Kiri still cannot accept or affirm who she is now. The English turns affirmation of the self into an ungrammatical assertion addressed to the self.
records.remedy: She still could not accept who she was now

highlights.text: She cannot assert to her present self

records.jp: 美希はずっと黒い感じになっている。
records.en: Miki began to always be in a dark mood,
