records.assessment: The source is an explanatory note: it identifies the extravagant phrase as the narrator's coinage and states that it means women's underwear. The English repeats only a strained rendering of the coined phrase and omits both pieces of explanation, so the note no longer performs its defining function.
records.remedy: Retain the coined phrase, then state that it is the narrator's term for women's underwear or panties.

highlights.text:
* "Passion of the reverse triangle that like
an eagle unopposably ensnares the male heart"

records.jp: そうでなければ、あの肉欲の罪過を誘引せしめる三年生女子の臀部に、俺ごときのゴザ虫が欲情を抑えられるはずもなく。
records.en: Without doing that, there would be no way for stinkbugs like I to ever restrain their sexual appetites when confronted with the offenseful carnal desires induced by this third year girl's loins.
comments: All the insect stuff means him being a stinkbug is also meant literally. Notice that this is meant in reaction to his steeling himself, not the standards changing. ...though I suspect ambiguity as both work, really. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that otherwise a lowly bedbug like the narrator could not restrain his arousal before the older student's buttocks, which invite the sin of lust. The English changes the self-deprecating insect, turns singular self-reference into plural stinkbugs, replaces buttocks with loins, and makes the girl's body appear to possess or induce carnal desires rather than provoke his.
records.remedy: Keep the narrator as the single desiring subject and preserve the comic self-abasement, the buttocks, and the conditional relation.

highlights.text: Without doing that, there would be no way for stinkbugs like I to ever restrain their sexual appetites when confronted with the offenseful carnal desires induced by this third year girl's loins.

records.jp: 「パンツ売ってくださーい！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Please sell me what you wear!!!"
comments: Please sell me what you wear! -> please bake me some bread? -> Please buy what I wear (see CCA0013) Original pun is: pantsu utte kudasai (please sell me your panties) -> pan tsukutte kudasai (please bake me some bread) -> [ore no] pantsu katte kunnai (please buy my panties). -GHS
records.assessment: The request explicitly asks her to sell him her panties. Replacing パンツ with the generic 'what you wear' removes the underwear request and destroys the audible パンツ売って／パン作って misunderstanding that produces the next reply.
records.remedy: Use an explicit underwear request and rebuild the adjacent English exchange so the mistaken bread request remains audibly motivated.

highlights.text: Please sell me what you wear!!!

records.jp: 八割方聞こえテールッ！（メキシカン調）
records.en: Seh can uhnderstand meeh at eh nearly 80% rahteh! (Mexican accent)
comments: Randomly foreign. I suppose American would be too obvious. I just fed the translation through this http://www.oddcast.com/home/demos/tts/tts_example.php?sitepal (Spanish language/Javier's voice) and transcribed. More importantly: this is an eight (80% is written hachi-wari), and she's sort of misunderstanding him. It's a very very early reading key: Eight Means Wrong. -GHS
records.assessment: The source exclaims that she can hear about eighty percent of what he says, delivered in a Mexican-style voice. The English instead says that an unspecified 'she' can understand the speaker and supplies an invented phonetic caricature, changing person, action, and delivery.
records.remedy: Keep first-person perception and the approximate eighty-percent figure, with a restrained stage direction for the stylized accent.

highlights.text: Seh can uhnderstand meeh at eh nearly 80% rahteh! (Mexican accent)

records.jp: 「言葉のアヤ子さんです」
records.en: Taichi: "Something I got from Didnotmentat Literallia-san!"
comments: Kotoba no Ayako-san, just a widespread pun, doesn't seem to have a specific origin. Since it's an anthropomorphism, of which there are a fair few (may or may not include Youko), now she's a Family Circus running gag. See CCD1001 for Tomoki using this normally. -GHS
records.assessment: The source turns 言葉の綾, 'a figure of speech,' into the woman's name Ayako as a comic excuse. The invented name does not make 'figure of speech' or 'I did not mean it literally' intelligible in English, so the line's immediate repair function and its name pun are both lost.
records.remedy: Build an English feminine-name pun whose surrounding wording clearly means that 'while I was at it' was only a figure of speech.

highlights.text: Didnotmentat Literallia-san!

records.jp: 「はい、お待たせです」
records.en: Misato: "Yes, here I am now."
records.assessment: お待たせです conventionally acknowledges that the other person has been kept waiting: 'thanks for waiting' or 'sorry to keep you waiting.' The English instead announces the speaker's arrival and omits that acknowledgment.
records.remedy: Use 'There—thanks for waiting' or an equivalent acknowledgment.

highlights.text: Misato: "Yes, here I am now."

records.jp: 脳内フォトシ○ップが立ち上がる。
records.en: Launching intracranial Photosh*p (pirated copy).
comments: HACK that addition is from the 360 version. Nice censorship, by the way. -GHS
records.assessment: The source jokes that the narrator's mental Photo○shop launches. The parenthetical claim that the copy is pirated is newly invented and changes the joke without textual support.
records.remedy: Remove the piracy parenthesis and retain only the censored mental image-editing software gag.

highlights.text: (pirated copy)

records.jp: ０．１秒で起動だ。脳内だから。
records.en: Startup completes in 0.1 seconds. That's why it's intracranial.
comments: That would still make it about 1 second. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives the mental location as the reason for the 0.1-second startup. 'That's why it's intracranial' reverses the causal direction, making the startup speed explain why the process is in his head.
records.remedy: Say that it starts in 0.1 seconds because it is running in his head.

highlights.text: Startup completes in 0.1 seconds. That's why it's intracranial.

records.jp: ついでに生肌が露出している腕と脚の部分も、先輩のものを使う。
records.en: While I'm at it, I use Senpai's tone from the exposed skin on the arms and legs.
comments: No way that "while I'm at it" is coincidental. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that for the exposed arms and legs he also uses the senior's own body parts. The English instead says he samples her skin tone, changing a component replacement into color matching.
records.remedy: Say that he uses the senior's own exposed arms and legs as well.

highlights.text: tone from the exposed skin

records.jp: 肌の色の差は、薄い黄色の新規レイヤーを重ね、描画モードをソフトラインにすることで統一した。
records.en: As for the difference in skin color, add a pale yellow into a new layer, and consolidate using Soft Line Blending Mode.
comments: That's the correct translation according to the Adobe help pages, except it should be soft LINE blending mode (ソフトライト not ソフトライン). There's no Soft Line mode documented, so either it's a typo that went unfixed as far as the 360 edition, or Taichi's talking out of his ass. Which seems likely regardless. Does he even know how to use Photoshop...? -GHS
records.assessment: The source names the image editor's Soft Light blending mode. 'Soft Line' is not that mode and gives an incorrect technical instruction, even though the new pale-yellow layer and the goal of unifying skin color are retained.
records.remedy: Use 'Soft Light blending mode.'

highlights.text: Soft Line Blending Mode

records.jp: 十年使えるエロコラ、ここに爆誕。
records.en: A sexy 'shopped image that will last decades has here its explosive birth.
comments: I can't find that word used seriously outside of the Pokemon 2000 movie, so I got the word from the Wikipedia literal translation of the title. Will recur. No, seriously, it will. Although ten isn't as recurring as 7 or 8, ten years is cross-years. -GHS
records.assessment: 十年 is specifically ten years. 'Decades' changes that comic quantitative boast to an indefinite period of twenty years or more, while the source's explosive-birth register is otherwise retained.
records.remedy: Call it an erotic composite good for ten years.

highlights.text: will last decades

records.jp: 『何も考えずにＨＤＤを捨ててください（閲覧・形見分け絶対禁止、したら全霊力をかけて呪う）』
records.en: 'Please dispose of my hard disk drive without even a single thought (inspection or utilization as memento mori are strictly forbidden, violators shall be cursed to the full extent of the powers of my soul.)'
comments: Ironically, if he's not dead, at the end he'd be a ghost of sorts... -GHS
records.assessment: 形見分け is the distribution of a deceased person's belongings as keepsakes. 'Utilization as memento mori' instead suggests using the drive as a reminder of mortality and loses the prohibition on dividing it among survivors.
records.remedy: Forbid both inspection and distribution as a keepsake, followed by the threatened curse.

highlights.text: utilization as memento mori

records.jp: 慌てて口を押さえる。
records.en: I restrain my mouth in a frenzy.
records.assessment: The source describes hurriedly covering his mouth with a hand. 'Restraining' the mouth neither specifies covering it nor clearly describes a physical gesture, and 'in a frenzy' overstates the simple hurried reaction.
records.remedy: Say that he hurriedly clapped a hand over his mouth.

highlights.text: I restrain my mouth in a frenzy.

records.jp: ちらと見やった先輩の手が、傷だらけだった。
records.en: I chanced to look closely at Senpai's hands, and they were covered with scratches.
comments: This is what she uses in replacement of the wrist slashing. -GHS
records.assessment: ちらと見やる is to cast a quick glance. 'Chanced to look closely' changes an intentional brief glance into an accidental close inspection, altering both attention and duration.
records.remedy: Say that he glanced over and saw that the senior's hands were covered in cuts or scratches.

highlights.text: chanced to look closely

records.jp: モニターひとつ持ち上げられない細腕なのに。
records.en: When her slender arms could never lift up but one of those transceivers.
comments: Although 'monitor' is technically the correct word, it makes it sound like she's carrying computer monitors around, which have very little to do with an antenna that has no video feeds whatsoever and very little apparent need for any. Someone should probably tell the guy who draws BGs before he fills the Club Room with actual--- whoops. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says her slender arms cannot lift even a single monitor. 'Could never lift up but one' conventionally means she could lift only one, reversing the scalar negative, and 'transceiver' replaces the monitor without support.
records.remedy: Say that her slender arms cannot even lift a single monitor.

highlights.text: When her slender arms could never lift up but one of those transceivers.

records.jp: 「みんな……好きなことやってるわけじゃないスよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Everybody... but they are not doing anything they like doing, you know?"
records.assessment: The Japanese says not everyone is doing what they like. The English instead makes everybody the subject of 'not doing anything they like,' changing a partial negation into the much stronger claim that no one is doing any liked activity.
records.remedy: Say 'Not everyone is doing what they like, you know.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Everybody... but they are not doing anything they like doing, you know?"

records.jp: 「実感わいてないだけじゃないですかね、きっと」
records.en: Taichi: "It is just that their true feelings are sort of not coming out in the open, definitely."
records.assessment: 実感がわく concerns gaining a felt sense of reality or having something sink in. The English invents suppressed 'true feelings' that are not coming out publicly, changing internal apprehension into emotional disclosure.
records.remedy: Say that the situation simply has not felt real to them yet.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is just that their true feelings are sort of not coming out in the open, definitely."

records.jp: 「そんな先輩はいないですよ？」
records.en: Misato: "You do know that Senpai does not exist?"
records.assessment: そんな先輩 refers to the incorrectly named kind of 'senpai' just invoked: there is no such senior. The English instead appears to tell him that Senpai herself does not exist, turning a correction of address into an ontological claim.
records.remedy: Say 'There is no such senpai, you know' or directly reject the mistaken nickname.

highlights.text: Misato: "You do know that Senpai does not exist?"

records.jp: 「ぺけくんはじゃあ、もう落ち着いちゃったわけだ」
records.en: Misato: "Then, Peke-kun, I have already calmed down."
comments: Easily forgiven. Too easily, perhaps. -GHS
records.assessment: The topic is Peke-kun: she concludes that he has already calmed down. The English changes the subject to the speaker and says that she has calmed down, reversing who the inference concerns.
records.remedy: Say 'Then that means you've already calmed down, Peke-kun.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Then, Peke-kun, I have already calmed down."

records.jp: 髪の毛を、柔らかい指先がくしゃくしゃにしていく。
records.en:
Soft fingertips rustle and ruffle the hair
My hair is rustled and ruffled by soft fingertips.
records.assessment: The source describes soft fingertips progressively tousling his hair once. The English accidentally translates the action twice in immediate succession, first actively and then passively, leaving a duplicated sentence and a missing separator.
records.remedy: Keep one sentence: 'Soft fingertips tousled my hair.'

highlights.text:
Soft fingertips rustle and ruffle the hair
My hair is rustled and ruffled by soft fingertips.

comments: Tweaked a little as it doesn't look as good with this font. Comment = "should be fine without voice" -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains a short eight-symbol pseudoformula followed by an ellipsis. The English replaces it with a much longer and differently ordered symbol string, inventing visible content rather than reproducing or equivalently abbreviating the formula.
records.remedy: Preserve the source's symbol sequence and trailing ellipsis.

records.jp: 「でも、もう始業時間過ぎてマスカラ……」
records.en: Misato: "But we cannot put mascara on the pig of it being well past opening time..."
comments: ;_; -GHS
records.assessment: The source runs the ordinary ending 過ぎてますから into マスカラ, 'mascara,' which motivates the following mime and maracas correction. The English invents a pig, changes the sentence into an inability to apply mascara, and provides no intelligible sound bridge to the ensuing maracas gag.
records.remedy: Rebuild the adjacent exchange around a fluent sentence whose ending can be misheard or extended as 'mascara,' followed by the maracas mime.

highlights.text: Misato: "But we cannot put mascara on the pig of it being well past opening time..."

records.jp: 「さぼりますか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Shall we cut?"
records.assessment: The verb means to skip or play truant here; the unqualified English verb does not express that sense.
records.remedy: Use an idiomatic invitation to skip class.

highlights.text: cut

records.jp: 「……でもそうですね」
records.en: Misato: "...but that is how it is."
comments: She's agreeing, but to what part is ambiguous. -GHS
records.assessment: In context this concedes the preceding suggestion; the rendering turns that assent into a vague statement about circumstances.
records.remedy: Render the phrase as a quiet concession such as 'but you're right.'

highlights.text: that is how it is

records.jp: 空を見て、ほうとため息をついた。
records.en: She looks at the sky and gave an audible sigh.
records.assessment: The sentence switches from present to past tense within a single coordinated action.
records.remedy: Keep the narrative tense consistent.

highlights.text: gave

records.jp: 「悪い子、ですもんね」
records.en: Misato: "Problem children, indeed so."
comments: Because of her own problems. -GHS
records.assessment: The explanatory, self-including force of the line is lost, and the resulting English phrase is not grammatical dialogue.
records.remedy: Preserve the after-all justification and the inclusive reference.

highlights.text: Problem children, indeed so

records.jp: 「といっても、日中は暑いですから……ここでの作業はしないんですよ」
records.en: Misato: "Regardless, it is hot in daytime, therefore... we should not be doing hard manual labor here."
comments: She's just pushing him away. -GHS
records.assessment: A statement that work is not done there during the hot daytime becomes a present normative claim, with 'hard manual labor' added without source support.
records.remedy: State the daytime work policy without the added characterization.

highlights.text: we should not be doing hard manual labor here

records.jp: 「ですからせっかくさぼっても、やることってないんです」
records.en: Misato: "So even if we go to all the trouble to cut, there is nothing to do."
records.assessment: The intended idea is that even taking the opportunity to skip leaves nothing to do; the English phrase is both opaque and non-idiomatic.
records.remedy: Use idiomatic language for skipping class and preserve the concessive force.

highlights.text: go to all the trouble to cut

records.jp: 「ちゃんと心の整理して、自分のやること決めてるんですから」
records.en: Misato: "Because you organize your mind as proper, and you are set on what you want to do."
comments: She's envying his tendency to be fixed. Not impossible she's envying his perfect flight into an illusory world, possibly even unaware of how ultimately imperfect it is. -GHS
records.assessment: The phrase for sorting out one's feelings is rendered as ungrammatical English, obscuring the praise that the addressee has done so properly.
records.remedy: Use idiomatic language for sorting out one's feelings and deciding what to do.

highlights.text: organize your mind as proper

records.jp: 唐突に話が戻ったらしい。
records.en: Seems that subject has returned all of a sudden.
comments: This seems odd, but it reconnects to the Mimimi sentence. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration says that the conversation has apparently returned to its earlier topic; the English is grammatically incomplete and treats the subject itself as an agent.
records.remedy: State idiomatically that she has suddenly returned to the earlier subject.

highlights.text: Seems that subject has returned

records.jp: 瓜実型の輪郭に、仄かな憂いが訪れた。
records.en: An indistinct sadness came to that melon-shaped silhouette.
comments: Still not sure whether he's talking about her face or her b-GHS
records.assessment: The fixed descriptor refers to an oval face or facial outline, not a melon-shaped silhouette; the mistranslation distorts the image and its object.
records.remedy: Describe the faint sadness crossing her oval face.

highlights.text: melon-shaped silhouette

records.jp: 泣きそうなようにも見えて、胸を締めつけられる。
records.en: Seeing something so as if to cry makes my chest tighten.
records.assessment: The source says that she looks almost ready to cry, which tightens the narrator's chest; the English removes that subject and is not grammatical.
records.remedy: Restore her as the apparent subject of crying and retain the narrator's reaction.

highlights.text: Seeing something so as if to cry

records.jp: ありきたりで、当たり前の、胸を張って誇れる……想い。
records.en: That proud, conventional, ordinary puff of the chest... an emotion.
comments: Specific: he believes himself an unemotional insect, or at least incapable of having the 'correct' emotion at the correct time: see his tears. -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes an ordinary, natural feeling one can openly take pride in; the rendering turns the idiom about holding one's chest high into a malformed noun phrase.
records.remedy: Preserve the sequence of ordinary, natural, and proudly avowable qualities as modifiers of the feeling.

highlights.text: proud, conventional, ordinary puff of the chest

records.jp: 異性としての感情かどうかはさておき、俺はこの人が好きなんだと思う。
records.en: Even setting aside whether or not these feelings are caused by her being of opposite gender, I think I really like this person.
records.assessment: The clause asks whether the feeling is attraction toward her as a member of the opposite sex; it does not frame her gender as the mechanical cause of the feeling.
records.remedy: Use idiomatic language for setting aside whether the feeling is romantic or sexual attraction.

highlights.text: caused by her being of opposite gender

records.jp: 眼前に先輩の顔がアップで迫っていた。
records.en: Senpai upped the level of proximity of her face to right under my nose.
comments: See? Random English to disarm the atmosphere he can't handle. Plus he once again stopped and went into his random thoughts. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration presents her face looming close before his eyes; the rendering mechanically expands 'close-up' into an unnatural abstraction.
records.remedy: State directly that her face had suddenly loomed close before him.

highlights.text: upped the level of proximity of her face

records.jp: 「べっくらこきました」
records.en: Taichi: "I was scary'd!"
comments: "Surprised/frightened" in Hokkaido-ben. http://www.jinsho.jimokuji.ed.jp/bunkarekisi/hagyouhougen.htm - uhm, link worked during translation but was dead last time I checked; according to the Trap School Cross Channel subsite, it should be a relatively common variant of びっくらこく which googles straight to dictionaries. -GHS
records.assessment: The comic dialectal expression means that he was startled or surprised; the invented form instead suggests that he frightened someone and is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use a playful or rustic-sounding form of 'I was surprised.'

highlights.text: scary'd

records.jp: 「ふむ、べっくら……ふむ」
records.en: Misato: "Hum, scary'd... hum."
records.assessment: Her repetition is interest in the preceding dialectal word for surprise; repeating the mistranslated invention prevents the wordplay from functioning.
records.remedy: Repeat the same playful surprise-word used in the preceding line.

highlights.text: scary'd

records.jp: 「暑くなってきたし、校舎に戻りません？」
records.en: Taichi: "It is getting hotter, will you not go back inside the building?"
records.assessment: The negative question is an inclusive suggestion to return to the school building, not a formal request for the other person alone to go back.
records.remedy: Use an inclusive suggestion such as 'shall we head back inside?'

highlights.text: will you not go back inside the building

records.jp: 「そうしますか」
records.en: Misato: "Yes, I should."
records.assessment: The response accepts a shared plan, whereas the rendering changes it to a statement about what the speaker individually ought to do.
records.remedy: Accept the shared suggestion with 'Let's do that' or equivalent.

highlights.text: I should

records.jp: 放送部の部長さんは、一度だけアンテナに視線を移した。
records.en: The President of the Broadcast Club moved her sight to the antenna, only once.
records.assessment: The action is a single glance toward the antenna; 'moved her sight' and the displaced modifier are mechanical rather than idiomatic English.
records.remedy: State directly that she glanced at the antenna once.

highlights.text: moved her sight to the antenna, only once

records.jp: この人は、そうたやすく本心を見せたりはしない。
records.en: This person here does not want to show her true feelings all that easily.
records.assessment: The source says she does not readily reveal her true feelings; the rendering adds an explicit desire not to reveal them.
records.remedy: Describe her habitual reluctance or reserve without adding a stated intention.

highlights.text: does not want to show

records.jp: だからこそ、さっきの唖然とした顔は貴重なのであり。
records.en: That is exactly why the face of mute displeasure she made earlier is so precious.
records.assessment: The adjective describes a stunned or dumbfounded expression, not mute displeasure; the emotional content is changed.
records.remedy: Describe the earlier face as stunned or dumbfounded.

highlights.text: mute displeasure

records.jp: 柔和な顔は仮面でしかないんだと、俺はわかってしまうのだ。
records.en: Her gentle face is nothing but a mask, this I completely understand.
records.assessment: The underlying realization is retained, but the comma splice and fronted demonstrative produce unidiomatic English.
records.remedy: Integrate the realization as a normal subordinate clause.

highlights.text: mask, this

records.jp: 蝉がうるさい。
records.en: The cicadas are making loud,
records.assessment: The source simply says the cicadas are loud or noisy; 'making loud' is incomplete English.
records.remedy: Use 'The cicadas are loud' or 'The cicadas are making a racket.'

highlights.text: making loud

records.jp: 「しかし」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then."
records.assessment: The conjunction marks contrast or reservation, whereas 'well then' advances to a conclusion or next action.
records.remedy: Use 'Still,' 'But,' or another contrastive discourse marker.

highlights.text: Well then

records.jp: 屋上が炎天下となると、涼める場所はさほどない。
records.en: With the rooftop under the blazing sun, that's not really a place to cool off in.
comments: The thing about Misato saying it's gonna get hot is a load; this isn't 9AM. She was just telling him that to send him away. There's no way Taichi is so damn dumb to believe her; this is a hint that the previous scene shouldn't gel with this, cicadas or not. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that with the rooftop exposed to the blazing sun there are few places available to cool off; the rendering merely excludes the roof itself and omits the scarcity of alternatives.
records.remedy: Preserve the conclusion that few cooling-off places remain.

highlights.text: that's not really a place to cool off in

records.jp: 手近な教室をのぞいてみると、案の定授業中だった。
records.en: I tried peeking inside a class nearby, sure enough, a lesson was in progress.
records.assessment: The two independent clauses are joined only by a comma; the source relation is clear but the English sentence is mechanically defective.
records.remedy: Separate the clauses or join them with a conjunction or dash.

highlights.text: nearby, sure enough

records.jp: 教職二年目。
records.en: In her second year of teaching profession.
records.assessment: The fragment means that this is her second year as a teacher; the English omits the article and uses an unnatural construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Her second year as a teacher.'

highlights.text: of teaching profession

records.jp: 俺たちと同じ年度で教師になった。
records.en:
She had became teacher for the same class
year as us.
comments: It's actually uncertain if these two flow together, I suppose intentionally because "second year" could then easily misread as meaning Taichi is a second year, when he isn't in this flashback. The hint is above in how she teaches first years, although that may only be on this particular hour on this particular day. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she became a teacher in the same academic year that the students began; it does not say she became a teacher for their class year, and the verb form is also wrong.
records.remedy: State the parallel timing of her starting as a teacher and their school year.

highlights.text:
became teacher for the same class
year as us

records.jp: 今ではすっかり女教師が板についている。
records.en:
Nowadays female teachers are something
pretty habitual,
comments: Begin Walls of Ambiguity! "Female teachers are normal these days" + "these days I'm used to female teachers so I don't molest them so much" -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom says she has now thoroughly settled into or grown into the role of female teacher; the rendering generalizes to female teachers as a habitual phenomenon.
records.remedy: Keep her as the subject and render the idiom as being fully at home in the role.

highlights.text:
female teachers are something
pretty habitual

records.jp: 罪っ子である。
records.en: Sinful to the core.
comments: Lit. "sinbaby", which sounds less silly in Japanese, but not entirely so. -GHS
records.assessment: The source coins a playful child-or-girl label from 'sin'; the rendering replaces that wordplay with an unsupported intensifier.
records.remedy: Recreate a compact playful label rather than escalating degree.

highlights.text: to the core

records.jp: その罪の多くは、シャツを内側から突き上げるふくらみに含まれていると言ってもいいだろう。
records.en:
It could probably be said that this wealth of
sins does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt from the inside.
records.assessment: The image of the swelling that pushes up her shirt from within is recognizable, but the verb placement and plural abstraction are unidiomatic and obscure the mock claim that much of her sin resides there.
records.remedy: Make the swelling the clear object in which the sins reside and use natural English word order.

highlights.text:
does include protrusions that force upwards
her shirt

records.jp: キレた１４歳の少年が手にするナイフと同じほどに危険だ。
records.en:
equally as dangerous as a knife in the
hands of a broken 14-year old boy.
comments: Except Taichi's between 15 and 16 by now, since he's 17 by the end of Summer next year (birthday would therefore be between this early Summer and September - wanna bet it's July 7?). So while it is a big hint in hindsight because this is Psychopath High, unless he got into school at that age i.e. he killed everyone at the Mansion not a year and a half before, which is impossible because he was at Gunjou at 13 for the Cultural Festival where he met Sakuraba, the true focus is the 7x2 in there. -GHS
records.assessment: The adjective describes a fourteen-year-old who has snapped or flown into a rage, not a boy who is broken.
records.remedy: Use an idiomatic phrase for an enraged or unhinged fourteen-year-old.

highlights.text: broken 14-year old boy

records.jp: 尻の割れ目に横筋が橋を張るほどにぱっつんぱっつんなスカートの中央に、カッターで縦の切れ目をスーッと入れたいと思ったことは五度や十度じゃない。
records.en:
With a stritch and a stretch the cleft of the
ass created transversal stripes stretched like
bridges in the middle of her skirt that I thought
not five nor ten times to get a cutter and
caaarefully cut them transversally.
comments: That's the specific SFX adjective for when clothes are so tight that motion causes them to create that kind of ripple, here's a pic and description (in Japanese): http://dic.pixiv.net/a/%E3%81%B1%E3%81%A3%E3%81%A4%E3%82%93%E3%81%B1%E3%81%A3%E3%81%A4%E3%82%93 This should sound creepy on reread, like the knife above. It just means "several times", but let's consider it literally, as it is often a good thing to do with Tanaka: though technically it should mean more than ten times, if he didn't think five nor ten times then seven times would be an appropriate amount. -GHS
records.assessment: The source imagines making one vertical slit down the center of the tight skirt; the rendering changes both the direction and object to cutting plural stripes transversely.
records.remedy: Keep the horizontal bridging lines as description and the desired cut as a vertical slit in the skirt.

highlights.text: cut them transversally

records.jp: 危険な女性だ。
records.en: She's a dangerous female.
records.assessment: The source calls her a dangerous woman; the nominal use of 'female' is needlessly clinical and unnatural in this narration.
records.remedy: Use 'dangerous woman.'

highlights.text: dangerous female

records.jp: 悪の校長と番長らによって、妹（同校在籍の女生徒……明るく成績優秀でスポーツ万能で男女わけへだてなく人気があったりする）の弱みをネタに脅迫され性悦の極みに堕ちていきかねない。
records.en:
Because of a wicked headmaster and his gang of
ne'er-do-wells, her little sister (female student
enrolled in the same school... brilliant academic
results, excellent at sports and popular with
both genders without distinction) became her
weak point, so that this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down into the extremes
of forced sexual ecstasy.
comments: The headmaster is sort of a character in here. I have no idea why or what, though. I suspect he used to be the villain in Taichi's Settei before Miki came in. ...I'm not actually sure who is Imouto here. I wonder if it means Taichi himself in his gender confusion, though in that case she reads like Youko, which gets a big hmmm. -GHS
records.assessment: The woman is blackmailed by villains who exploit leverage involving her younger sister and may thereby be driven into sexual degradation; the rendering makes the threatened sister the agent that casts her down.
records.remedy: Keep the villains as agents of the blackmail and the sister as the leverage used against the woman.

highlights.text:
this threatened sibling
may well be what casts her down

records.jp: 一年生の時、副担任になったまちこ先生に飽くなきセクハラを繰り返し、ついには授業中に泣かせてしまったうえ三日間無断欠勤をさせてしまったことが、未だに悔やまれる。
records.en:
As a first year student, Machiko-sensei became
our substitute homeroom teacher, and I repeatedly
and insatiably harassed her until eventually I
made her break down in tears in the middle of
class and take a three day leave from work
without permission, an event I still regret.
comments: It's around as forced as it is in the original, but that "as a first year student" is intended to recapture that said time hasn't necessarily ended. Whether he regrets his pranks or her reaction is intentionally unclear. -GHS
records.assessment: The title is assistant or deputy homeroom teacher, not a substitute temporarily replacing another teacher.
records.remedy: Use 'assistant homeroom teacher' or the locally established equivalent.

highlights.text: substitute homeroom teacher

records.jp: ……そして俺は停学を食らって、先輩に「停学君」とからかわれるようになった。
records.en:
...and then I was struck with suspension, and
Senpai began teasing me as "Suspension-kun".
comments: see CCA0002, CCC4006 and more. Uncertain if this is before or after her nickname for him. That students at Evil High would be given leaves of absence for their behavior is just stupid beyond comprehension. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator was suspended or got slapped with a suspension; 'was struck with suspension' is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'I got suspended' or an equivalently forceful idiom.

highlights.text: struck with suspension

records.jp: 以来、まちこ先生と俺との接点は消滅した。
records.en:
Ever since, the points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei have vanished.
comments: It reads sarcastically like "times at which I could grope her", but taken literally it's thematically important. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says their opportunities for contact disappeared; the plural technical phrase is a stiff calque that makes the relationship sound geometric.
records.remedy: Say that he had no further contact with her.

highlights.text:
points of contact between me
and Machiko-sensei

records.jp: 二年を待たずして副担が変わり、受け持ち授業からもいなくなった。
records.en:
Without waiting for second year the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of.
comments: But did the teacher change, or did she stop existing to Taichi due to what is possibly still a trauma for him? -GHS
records.assessment: Before his second year, the assistant homeroom assignment changed and she also ceased teaching any of his classes. The rendering again calls her a substitute and does not express whose timetable lost her.
records.remedy: State both the changed assistant-homeroom assignment and her disappearance from the narrator's classes.

highlights.text:
the substitute
changed, and she was no more even in the class
she was in charge of

records.jp: さらば青い思い出。
records.en: Fare thee well, memories of the green.
comments: See CCC3004, CCD2002 -GHS
records.assessment: The color adjective evokes youth or immaturity here; literal 'memories of the green' is not a functioning English expression.
records.remedy: Use 'youthful memories' or recreate the color metaphor idiomatically.

highlights.text: memories of the green

records.jp: セクハラ、ほどほどにしておけばよかったな。
records.en:
I just wish I had the kept sexual harassment
within moderation.
records.assessment: The intended regret about keeping the harassment within bounds is recognizable, but the English contains a basic word-order and article error.
records.remedy: Use 'I wish I'd kept the sexual harassment within reason.'

highlights.text: had the kept

records.jp: でもどうせ嫌われるならもっと揉んでおけばよかった、と考えてる時点で俺はもう終わってるんだろう人として。
records.en:
But if being hated was the result no matter what,
then I wish I had given a further once-over to
all that, though having those thoughts at this
point means that I'm all but done as a person.
comments: "I wish I had rubbed more" + "I wish I had worried about that more". 揉 will often be used in both its meanings many many times. Say Without Saying, once again. -GHS
records.assessment: The explicit counter-regret is that he should have groped or fondled more; the vague phrase removes the concrete act that makes his self-condemnation land.
records.remedy: Name the groping directly enough to preserve the joke and moral self-indictment.

highlights.text:
given a further once-over to
all that

records.jp: 完璧計画爆誕。
records.en: The explosive birth of a perfect project.
comments: See CCA0006. -GHS
records.assessment: The mock-grand phrase celebrates a perfect plan coming explosively into being; 'project' changes the immediate scheme into an organized undertaking.
records.remedy: Use 'perfect plan' while retaining the bombastic birth image.

highlights.text: perfect project

records.jp: だが無駄をはぶくためか、定食は数量限定が鉄の掟。
records.en: However, to cut back on waste or something, the set meal being available in limited number is an iron rule.
comments: The supply will not change in response to changes in demand. This is a strongly capitalist critique of this kind of behavior by state-run institutions, well in line with Tanaka's masked but fundamentally subversive and ultimately culturally anti-Japanese attitude. Just wait until below! -GHS
records.assessment: The limited-quantity rule is semantically present, but this count construction is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'available only in limited quantities.'

highlights.text: in limited number

records.jp: がらすきだった。
records.en: It was almost entirely uninhabited.
comments: "Garasuki". It will be one of the descriptions of the Cross World. -GHS
records.assessment: The place is almost empty or sparsely occupied, not literally without inhabitants or residents.
records.remedy: Use 'almost empty.'

highlights.text: uninhabited

records.jp: 「おばちゃん、エース定食」
records.en: Taichi: "Madam, set meal Ace."
comments: Unknown if this is Yusa's mom... -GHS
records.assessment: The address is a casual call to the cafeteria lady, and the named meal modifies the set-meal noun; the English is overly formal and reverses the name order.
records.remedy: Use a casual 'ma'am' or equivalent followed by 'the Ace set meal.'

highlights.text: Madam, set meal Ace

records.jp: らくちんらくちん。
records.en: Easy life mine, just an easy life.
comments: Hum, see CCA0013. -GHS
records.assessment: The repeated playful adjective means that the task was easy or easy-peasy; the rendering invents an ungrammatical claim about an easy life.
records.remedy: Use a light repeated expression such as 'Easy, easy.'

highlights.text: Easy life mine, just an easy life

records.jp: 部室に入ると、パイプ椅子に座って雑誌を読んでいた男が顔をあげた。
records.en: On entering the club room, a male who was sitting on a folding chair and reading a magazine raised his head.
comments: See CCD1001: he calls women a fairly creepy "females" back then, and see below. -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to a man; nominal 'a male' is clinical and unnatural for ordinary narrative identification.
records.remedy: Use 'a man.'

highlights.text: a male

records.jp: 「こんなところで奇遇ですな。先生もアレですか？　こっちの方もいける口で？」
records.en: Taichi: "What a coincidence finding you here. Are you doing 'that' as well, Sensei? You will offer me something to wet my lips as well?"
comments: Drinking. This is clearer with the thing below about the milk carton. Curiously the expression seems to be tied to alcohol drinking, perhaps since CCZRooftop was cut it lost this connection? -GHS
records.assessment: Together with the raised-pinky gesture, the speaker is insinuating that the other man is also interested in that sort of partner or pursuit. The rendering instead asks to be offered a drink, eliminating the insinuation and gesture-dependent joke.
records.remedy: Use an indirect but intelligible question that connects the pinky gesture to being interested in women.

highlights.text: You will offer me something to wet my lips as well

records.jp: 冴えない顔でそう応じる。
records.en: He answers with a sullen face.
comments: Tsukkomi fail. -GHS
records.assessment: The expression is dull, listless, or unenthused; 'sullen' adds resentment or petulance not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'with an unenthusiastic expression' or equivalent.

highlights.text: sullen

records.jp: 「さぼりか？　さぼりなのか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Cutting? Cutting aren't you?"
records.assessment: The repeated accusation is that he is skipping class. The bare verb 'cutting' does not carry that sense here, and the tag-like repetition is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use an idiomatic repeated accusation such as 'Skipping class? You are, aren't you?'

highlights.text: Cutting? Cutting aren't you

records.jp: 「うちのクラスは自習になったんだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Our class became self-study, 's all."
comments: See CCA0022. Is that just a free period? -GHS
records.assessment: The class was assigned a self-study period; a class cannot idiomatically 'become self-study.'
records.remedy: Use 'Our class has a self-study period.'

highlights.text: became self-study

records.jp: いいひと属性のくせしてワルぶりやがって。
records.en: That damnable vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are.
comments: "Attribute" will recur. This is specifically discussing his character archetype. Sooo very telling of Taichi more than Tomoki, isn't he? See below. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator mocks this particular nice guy for putting on a bad-boy act. The rendering turns it into a generalized vice shared by a category of people and weakens the direct sneer.
records.remedy: Keep the individual as subject: despite his nice-guy trait, he is trying to act bad.

highlights.text: vice of people with the Nice Guy Attribute of acting worse than they are

records.jp: シカトかい。
records.en: Ostracism?
comments: Ignoring him, but not the same way Touko does. シカト会 is more of an obvious misreading than an alternate one to 'is he giving me a cold shoulder?', but it's so awesome I was tempted to use it until practically the final moment. -GHS
records.assessment: The slang complaint means that he is being ignored or given the silent treatment, not socially ostracized.
records.remedy: Use a colloquial complaint such as 'Ignoring me, huh?'

highlights.text: Ostracism

records.jp: なんか気が抜けた。
records.en: That sends me down a bit.
records.assessment: The narrator feels deflated or has the wind taken out of him; 'sends me down' is vague and non-idiomatic.
records.remedy: Use 'That kind of deflated me.'

highlights.text: sends me down

records.jp: どだい放送部はキャラ的分業化が進んでいて、ツッコミ担当の友貴に悪ノリは期待できない。
records.en: The division of characterizational labor in the Broadcast Club is basically voluntary, so it can't be expected for Tomoki to get carried away when he's in charge of the Straight-Man role.
comments: Ah, these are the design docs that Tanaka interwove throughout the story. This would mean "I didn't have specific character roles in mind when designing the Club", see CCA0030. I don't think you can use "characterizational", but "division of labor" just demands that form. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the club's division of character roles is already highly developed. It says nothing about the arrangement being voluntary; that invention disrupts the reason a designated straight man cannot be expected to join the escalation.
records.remedy: State that the role-based division of labor is firmly established.

highlights.text: basically voluntary

records.jp: 窓から外を見る。
records.en: I looked outside from the window.
records.assessment: This immediate narrative action is in the present tense, while the rendering shifts it into the past amid surrounding present-tense narration.
records.remedy: Use 'I look outside through the window.'

highlights.text: looked

records.jp: 「暑いな、今日も」
records.en: Taichi: "Another hot day today, innit."
records.assessment: The source is casual but does not motivate a conspicuously British dialect tag, which imposes an unrelated regional voice.
records.remedy: Use a neutral casual tag or omit it.

highlights.text: innit

records.jp: 「もらうわ」
records.en: Taichi: "I shall be taking it, yes."
comments: Girly. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a casual 'I'll take it'; the rendering imposes conspicuous formality and adds a mannered final affirmation.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll take it.'

highlights.text: I shall be taking it, yes

records.jp: 突き出た手に小銭を落として、備え付けの冷蔵庫を開ける。
records.en: I drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator.
records.assessment: The coordinated present-tense actions are split across present and past, and the installed or provided refrigerator becomes a nonsensical 'provisions refrigerator.'
records.remedy: Keep both verbs in the same tense and describe the built-in or provided refrigerator.

highlights.text: drop coins into the proffered hand, and opened the provisions refrigerator

records.jp: クレームは無視して、パックをすすった。
records.en: Ignoring the objection, I sucked on the carton.
records.assessment: He sips the drink from its carton; the rendering makes the carton itself the object being sucked and sounds physically different.
records.remedy: Use 'I sipped from the carton.'

highlights.text: sucked on the carton

records.jp: それ以上の追求はなく、気怠い時間が流れた。
records.en: With no further pursuit of the matter, listlessly the time flowed on.
records.assessment: The source describes a languid stretch of time passing; the adverb is mechanically attached to time as though time itself behaved listlessly.
records.remedy: Use 'a languid silence settled in' or 'time passed languidly.'

highlights.text: listlessly the time flowed on

records.jp: 電源があるのをいいことに、小型冷蔵庫を置いたりゲーム機を常備したり携帯充電器が一列に並んでいたりと校内でも屈指の無法空間となっている。
records.en: It's nice that there's electricity, so there's a small refrigerator, game consoles on reserve, and cellphone chargers lined up in a row, making this into the foremost lawless space inside the school.
comments: And no one goes inside to see all this stuff. Don't clubs have supervising teachers? Compare Mammoth below. Rules in this school are applied with the same zeal as Misato does. -GHS
records.assessment: The occupants take advantage of having electrical power as license to install appliances and chargers. The rendering turns that causal criticism into a generic statement that electricity is nice.
records.remedy: Use 'Taking full advantage of the power outlets...' or equivalent.

highlights.text: It's nice that there's electricity

records.jp: 「あれ、機材の配線外れてない？」
records.en: Taichi: "My, isn't the wiring of the machine disconnected?"
comments: Specifying wiring as that's what Tomoki's good at when it comes to the antenna, also see CCX0001. -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to the equipment's wiring generally, not the wiring of a single machine.
records.remedy: Use 'Isn't the equipment disconnected?' or 'Haven't the cables been unplugged?'

highlights.text: wiring of the machine

records.jp: 見舞いに行ったときだ。
records.en: She came during visiting hours.
records.assessment: The narrator met her when he went to visit the hospitalized friend. The rendering reverses the visitor and invents a reference to visiting hours.
records.remedy: Use 'It was when I went to visit him.'

highlights.text: She came during visiting hours

records.jp: と頭をさげてきた制服の着こなしからして一味違う激キュートな生命体の出現に、ショックを受けた俺の記憶は未だおぼろげだ。
records.en: And she bowed her head, that Ultra Kyute life form so unique just in the elegant way she wore her uniform, that my memories are still vague from the shock of meeting her.
comments: He's using life-form just like with Machiko. See CCD1001 and above: beats the utterly contemptuous "female", so that's why I used the equivalent 'male' above. Also see CCD0002: he didn't always treat Tomoki with even this little respect, either. The vagueness of memories is the same as CCA0001, so his memories vaguefy from shock as well. MEMORY HUNTER!!! -GHS
records.assessment: The deliberately misspelled English coinage is unexplained and the surrounding sentence attaches multiple 'that' clauses without a stable structure, blunting the claim that even her uniform styling marked an exceptionally cute life-form.
records.remedy: Use a readable comic superlative and rebuild the sentence around the narrator's shock-blurred memory.

highlights.text: Ultra Kyute life form

records.jp: 「はい、なにが？　わけわかんざき」
records.en: Tomoki: "Huh, with what? I don't get a watch of whatcha sayin'."
comments: Just a hideous pun. Dumped something appropriately crappy in there, since that's the point. -GHS
records.assessment: The source ends an ordinary 'I don't get it' phrase with a recognizable name-like comic substitution. The English introduces 'watch' without a functioning target-language referent and collapses into malformed dialect.
records.remedy: Recreate the sentence-ending name pun with an intelligible English setup or retain the meaning and flag the wordplay.

highlights.text: I don't get a watch of whatcha sayin'

records.en: Girl: "...heheh!"
records.assessment: The source is a wordless caught-breath or suppressed reaction; explicit laughter is added without support and changes the emotional signal.
records.remedy: Use a breath, catch, or nonverbal ellipsis without specifying laughter.

highlights.text: heheh

records.jp: 「あれえ、いたんだ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Myyy, she was here?"
records.assessment: The speaker addresses the newly noticed girl directly: 'Oh, you were here?' The rendering changes the addressee into a third-person subject.
records.remedy: Use second person.

highlights.text: she was here

records.jp: 「おっす。元気？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Hail. In spirits?"
records.assessment: The source is an ordinary casual greeting and check-in; the English sounds archaic and omits the grammar needed for a question about wellbeing.
records.remedy: Use 'Hey. How are you?'

highlights.text: Hail. In spirits

records.jp: 「なんて地味っ娘なんだ」
records.en:
Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"
Taichi: "Why you so plain, why!"
comments: This sounds like there's a line feed missing, and indeed it's so in the console version, but the two saying this simultaneously is just so much funnier, so I didn't fix this one bug. -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains only the narrator's exclamation that she is an extraordinarily plain girl. A full anticipatory response by the girl is invented, and the remaining English line is itself malformed.
records.remedy: Remove the invented reply and render the single exclamation idiomatically.

highlights.text: Miyuki: "You're still gonna call me plain again are you?"

records.jp: 少女はがくがくと震えた。
records.en: The girl shook with a clattering.
comments: ...what's she even so nervous for? -GHS
records.assessment: The girl trembles violently; 'with a clattering' treats the mimetic manner as an unexplained accompanying object and suggests hard objects striking.
records.remedy: Use 'The girl shook violently.'

highlights.text: with a clattering

records.jp: 「うーん、君はなー、どーしてこう地味なのかなー。どーして君の髪どめのゴムはすごく安そうなの？　どうして眉がこんなにぽわぽわしてるの？　どうしてスカートもっと短くしないの？」
records.en: Taichi: "Yeaaah... whyyy you... whyyy you even so plain! Whyyy does the rubber of your hair bands look so cheap, hm? Why are your eyebrows all thin and faint like this? Why isn't this skirt just a little bit shorter?"
comments: Mugi (K-On!)'s the only character I found defined has having "powa-powa" eyebrows, but they don't fit Miyuki's pic now that she has one. It's not visible in these dolls, but in the 360 data files there's a set that's cut below the knee, and her skirt is the longest of all skirted characters except maybe Touko. -GHS
records.assessment: The eyebrows are described with a soft, fluffy, or fuzzy mimetic quality, not as thin and faint; the insult's concrete visual target changes.
records.remedy: Use an idiomatic description of fluffy or fuzzy eyebrows.

highlights.text: eyebrows all thin and faint

records.jp: 「もとはいいのにねぇ」
records.en: Taichi: "So the outside is fine theeen!"
records.assessment: The phrase says her underlying material or natural looks are good despite her plain styling; it does not contrast an exterior with an interior.
records.remedy: Use 'You've got good raw material' or a natural equivalent.

highlights.text: the outside

records.jp: 「もったいない、もったいない」
records.en: Taichi: "Wasteful, so wasteful!"
records.assessment: The exclamation means 'what a waste' repeated, not that the girl is wasteful as an adjective.
records.remedy: Use 'What a waste, what a waste.'

highlights.text: Wasteful, so wasteful

records.jp: 「もったいないから食ーべちゃおっと」
records.en: Taichi: "So wasteful I wanna eat it aaall!"
comments: See CCD0021. Who was it at fault? -GHS
records.assessment: Because letting her go to waste would be a shame, the speaker playfully decides to eat her up. The rendering uses an impersonal object and adds total consumption rather than directing the tease at the girl.
records.remedy: Use 'What a waste—maybe I'll just eat you up.'

highlights.text: I wanna eat it aaall

records.jp: 身をかがめて、耳にかぶりついたのでした。
records.en: I bent over her and bit into her ears.
records.assessment: The action is biting into one ear; pluralizing it changes the physical image.
records.remedy: Use singular 'ear.'

highlights.text: ears

records.jp: 女の子の香りがしました。
records.en: There it was, the smell of young girl.
comments: See Youko now. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she smelled like a girl. The English omits the needed article or possessive construction and adds a youth qualifier not present in the line.
records.remedy: Use 'She smelled like a girl' or 'I caught a girl's scent.'

highlights.text: smell of young girl

records.jp: みゆきがエクスタシーに達した（嘘）。
records.en: Miyuki peaked into ecstasy (lies).
records.assessment: The mock narration says she reached ecstasy, followed by a singular admission that this is a lie. 'Peaked into' is not idiomatic and plural 'lies' changes the aside.
records.remedy: Use 'Miyuki reached ecstasy. (Lie.)'

highlights.text: peaked into ecstasy (lies)

records.jp: 「お、なんだなんだ、彼女がいるくせにさらにロックオンか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Oh, lookie lookie, you got a girlfriend damn you but you're engaging in further Lock-On?"
records.assessment: The accusation that he is locking on to another target despite already having a girlfriend is recoverable, but the gerund construction is not grammatical natural dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'you're locking on to someone else too?'

highlights.text: engaging in further Lock-On

records.jp: ペッ、と吐き捨てる。
records.en: Pah!, I spat his way.
comments: Recurring (somehow). -GHS
records.assessment: The narration describes a contemptuous verbal delivery after the interjection; the English instead depicts physical spitting in another person's direction.
records.remedy: Use 'I spat the words out.'

highlights.text: spat his way

records.jp: 「けど俺の恋のライフルは、いつでも地味な君を狙って―――」
records.en: Taichi: "But the Rifle of my Love always and forever aimed at plain little---"
records.assessment: The intended boast is that his love rifle is always aimed at the plain girl being addressed. The English lacks the finite verb and drops the addressee after an incomplete adjective.
records.remedy: Use 'is always aimed at plain little you—'.

highlights.text: always and forever aimed at plain little

records.jp: 視線を移した瞬間、放送室の扉が閉まった。
records.en: The instant I moved my sight, the Broadcast Room door shut,
records.assessment: The source describes shifting one's gaze. 'Moved my sight' is a direct but nonidiomatic lexical transfer.
records.remedy: Use 'shifted my gaze.'

highlights.text: moved my sight

records.jp: みゆきはもういない。
records.en: Miyuki is no longer among us.
comments: Lit. "not here", but given the whole theme about presences, living and more, I'll use this as a form of Pretentiously Pretentiousness that Pretentiously Pretentious etc. etc. etc. at times. -GHS
records.assessment: The local observation is simply that Miyuki is no longer there. The English idiom conventionally announces death and imports a grave implication absent from the line.
records.remedy: Use 'Miyuki was gone.'

highlights.text: no longer among us

records.jp: 「……おまえって後輩は平気で呼び捨てるよな」
records.en: Tomoki: "...look at you perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics."
records.assessment: The source observes that he casually calls a junior by surname alone. The English explanation is grammatically strained and treats 'a junior' as a capitalized count noun.
records.remedy: Use 'You have no problem calling your juniors by name, do you?'

highlights.text: perfectly alright with calling a Kouhai without honorifics

records.jp: 「だって後輩だよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "She's a Kouhai innshe?"
records.assessment: The reply that she is a junior is retained, but the invented eye-dialect contraction is opaque and has no source basis.
records.remedy: Use 'She's my junior, isn't she?'

highlights.text: innshe

records.jp: 「……福原のクラスも自習なんだってさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...Fukuhara's class is also self-study, that's all."
records.assessment: The intended information is that Fukuhara's class also has an unsupervised study period. Equating the class itself with 'self-study' is unnatural and imprecise.
records.remedy: Use 'Fukuhara's class has study hall too.'

highlights.text: class is also self-study

records.jp: 謎がとけて興味も失せた。
records.en: With the enigma solved the interest vanished.
comments: Very telling this line. Taichi's someone who holds interest until it's all solved. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says that, once the mystery was solved, he also lost interest. The English substitutes a generic definite abstraction and obscures the experiencer.
records.remedy: Use 'Once the mystery was solved, I lost interest.'

highlights.text: the interest vanished

records.jp: 「まーた誰か弾けちゃったかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "Sooo I just repelled someone again, have I?"
records.assessment: The source wonders whether someone has snapped or gone off again. The English makes the speaker an agent who repelled another person, reversing the grammatical and causal structure.
records.remedy: Use 'Did somebody snap again, I wonder?'

highlights.text: I just repelled someone

records.jp: 「……たぶんな」
records.en: Tomoki: "...mebbe."
comments: But not him. -GHS
records.assessment: The nonstandard eye-dialect spelling invents a marked accent not present in the neutral casual Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'Probably.'

highlights.text: mebbe

records.jp: 椅子に座り直す。
records.en: He straightens his sitting posture.
records.assessment: The viewpoint narrator reseats himself in the chair. The translation supplies a third-person subject and changes the action into posture correction.
records.remedy: Use 'I sat back down in the chair.'

highlights.text: He straightens his sitting posture.

records.jp: 夏の日差しは、まだ室内には入ってこない。
records.en: The sunlight of Summer doesn't yet spread throughout the room.
comments: I think this is just because of where the room is located on the building. Guessing North? I should point out that this kind of sentences are just used to glue together scene bits that don't actually flow together and look written separately, but maybe I shouldn't unravel this thing TOO far. -GHS
records.assessment: The sunlight has not yet entered the room at all; 'doesn't spread throughout' permits partial entry and changes the spatial state.
records.remedy: Use 'The summer sunlight hadn't reached the room yet.'

highlights.text: spread throughout the room

records.jp: 「そうだね」
records.en: Tomoki: "Ain't that right."
records.assessment: The source is a low-energy affirmation, 'Yeah' or 'That's true.' The English recasts it as a tag-like demand for agreement and adds marked dialect.
records.remedy: Use 'Yeah.'

highlights.text: Ain't that right

records.jp: 「八束が死んで、真犯人は真崎だと判明した」
records.en: Taichi: "Yatsuka dies, the true culprit is proven to be Masaki."
comments: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%AB%E6%9D%9F%E7%94%BA <- hmmm. But this thing is about epic-level meta. Eight-bundle, the bundle of eights dies; the culprit is pure/true-Saki, same Saki as Tasaki. The Bundle of Eights (there's waaay lots) is killed by Tasaki when True, and the True Tasaki would be the Christian Tasaki. -GHS
records.assessment: The reported revelation is substantially correct, but 'the culprit is proven to be' is an unidiomatic passive construction for a discovery within a narrative.
records.remedy: Use 'and Masaki turned out to be the real culprit.'

highlights.text: is proven to be

records.jp: 「アンデルセン神父が味方のスパイでさらわれた依子を助けてくれた！」
records.en: Taichi: "Father Anderson rescues the kidnapped Yoriko with help from a friendly spy."
comments: Father Anderson -> http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellsing Began 1997, as with this scene. But I suspect that's just plausible deniability: the end of Japan, the land under the domain of Satan, is that a Christian priest, with assistance from a local (coughTanakacough), rescues the "dependent child" AKA mankind, see all the stuff about Alter Egos etc. for what is meant about "dependence". It only sounds like projecting without knowing that Cross Channel is a fundamentally Christian tale, then it's so blatantly obvious that you can see Tanaka giggling mad as he writes this, certain no one in the world would ever get it. -GHS
records.assessment: The source identifies Father Andersen himself as an allied spy who rescues the abducted person. The English invents a separate friendly spy who assists him.
records.remedy: Use 'Father Andersen was an allied spy, and he rescued the kidnapped Yoriko.'

highlights.text: with help from a friendly spy

records.jp: 「言論統制反対！」
records.en: Taichi: "Regulation of free speech ostracized!"
comments: This sort of spoils a later gag :-( -GHS
records.assessment: The line is a slogan opposing censorship or speech control. 'Ostracized' neither expresses opposition nor forms an idiomatic English slogan.
records.remedy: Use 'Down with censorship!'

highlights.text: Regulation of free speech ostracized

records.jp: 中扉が開いて、顔を出したみゆきが小さく叫んだ。
records.en: The inner door opens, and from Miyuki's peeking face comes a whispered shout.
records.assessment: She gives a small or quiet cry after peeking out. 'Whispered shout' is internally contradictory and turns a restrained exclamation into an impossible manner of shouting.
records.remedy: Use 'called out softly.'

highlights.text: a whispered shout

records.jp: 俺はもう廊下側から死角になる位置に身を潜め終えた。
records.en: I was already done concealing myself in a spot blind from the corridor side.
records.assessment: The narrator has hidden in a position outside the corridor's line of sight. The English renders the Japanese spatial relation as an unidiomatic 'spot blind from' construction.
records.remedy: Use 'a spot that couldn't be seen from the corridor.'

highlights.text: a spot blind from the corridor side

records.jp: 友貴はおたおたと右往左往している。
records.en: Tomoki is flapping about right and left in confusion.
records.assessment: The character is panicking and running or looking helplessly this way and that. 'Flapping' suggests wings or loose material and does not idiomatically describe the action.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki darted helplessly back and forth.'

highlights.text: flapping about right and left

records.jp: 身を低くして、友貴は放送室に逃げた。
records.en: Lowering his posture, Tomoki escapes into the Broadcast Room,
records.assessment: The source depicts crouching or keeping low while fleeing. 'Lowering his posture' is a literal but nonidiomatic rendering of bodily movement.
records.remedy: Use 'Keeping low, Tomoki fled into the broadcast room.'

highlights.text: Lowering his posture

records.jp: 扉が締まると同時に、廊下を身長１９０センチの筋肉が通りかかった。
records.en: Simultaneously with the closing of that door, 190cm of muscle happened to pass by in the corridor.
comments: Remember that this is Japan, where the Giant Schoolgirl archetype barely touches 170cm. Machiko was just defined as tall for being 173. Hmmn, 10 surely, but 9-1 is, uhm, hmmm, erm, where's the calculator... 3. -GHS
records.assessment: The timing is correct, but the nominalized construction is an unnatural calque where English requires a finite temporal clause.
records.remedy: Use 'Just as the door closed,'

highlights.text: Simultaneously with the closing of that door

records.jp: 見つかったらただではすまない。
records.en: If he finds me, this won't just go away.
records.assessment: The source says that being discovered will mean not getting off lightly. The English instead suggests that an abstract situation will persist, losing the threat of consequences to the speaker.
records.remedy: Use 'If he catches me, I won't get off easy.'

highlights.text: this won't just go away

records.jp: しかもやつの体罰は、２１世紀に適応していて侮れない。
records.en:
And this guy's corporal punishment is formidably
conforming to the 21st Century.
comments: Still doesn't contradict it being 1997. Same Conformity as the Coefficient, interestingly enough. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century and is not to be underestimated. 'Formidably conforming' is not idiomatic and conflates adaptation with obedience to a standard.
records.remedy: Use 'His corporal punishment has adapted to the twenty-first century, too, so it can't be taken lightly.'

highlights.text:
formidably
conforming to the 21st Century

records.jp: これで某婦人告訴団体ペタも恐くないって寸法さ！
records.en:
And with these measures he has nothing to fear
from that 『Women's Lawsuit Organization * PTA』!
comments: http://www6.ocn.ne.jp/~rejina/cc/motoneta.html the PTA in Japan seems to be at the forefront of this kind of stuff, and it'll be even more obvious that this is the reference in CCB2009 when the PTA starts censoring Taichi's porn via Modern Tsundere archetype Touko. (There's a sentence I didn't expect to type in my life.) -GHS
records.assessment: The source's parody organization is named Peta. The English changes the name to PTA and leaves a raw annotation marker inside the dialogue, breaking both the proper-noun joke and presentation.
records.remedy: Retain the parody name Peta and move any annotation outside the dialogue.

highlights.text: 『Women's Lawsuit Organization * PTA』

records.jp: マンモスはそれはもうピグミーマーモセット並に、恐ろしく狡猾な苦しみマッスルなのである。
records.en:
Assuredly, Mammoth has terrifyingly crafty
agony muscles on the level of pygmy marmosets.
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygmy_marmoset they... are not threating at all. Supposing his "agony muscles" are metaphorical? This seems over the top dumb even for Taichi. -GHS
records.assessment: The pygmy-marmoset comparison modifies how terrifyingly cunning Mammoth is; it does not compare the level of his muscles to the animal. The English attaches the comparison to the wrong constituent and obscures the closing muscle pun.
records.remedy: Keep the marmoset comparison with his cunning and preserve the suffering-muscle wordplay separately.

highlights.text: agony muscles on the level of pygmy marmosets

records.jp: 途中、視線を室内に向けた。
records.en: Midway, his sight turns inside the room,
records.assessment: The person turns his gaze into the room. Making 'sight' itself turn and using 'inside' as its destination is an unidiomatic transfer of the Japanese construction.
records.remedy: Use 'On the way past, he looked into the room.'

highlights.text: his sight turns inside the room

records.jp: 原始人に狩られてしまえ、と呪っておく。
records.en: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.
records.assessment: The curse's content is present, but the English joins a malformed imperative, exclamation point, comma, and reporting clause into an ungrammatical sentence.
records.remedy: Use 'May a caveman hunt you down, I cursed him.'

highlights.text: Go get hunted down by a caveman!, I curse him.

records.jp: 「あぶないあぶない」
records.en: Tomoki: "Close so close!"
records.assessment: The repeated relieved exclamation means 'That was close, that was close.' The English drops the finite structure and punctuation needed for intelligible natural dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'That was close. Way too close.'

highlights.text: Close so close

records.jp: 「禁止されてるんだよ。学校もよくわかってるよな」
records.en: Tomoki: "That was forbidden. School got wise to that already."
comments: They don't forbid them to have obviously non-club non-school related stuff in there, obvious pictures in front of the window nooo problem, but curtains? Nope, that's the line! Setting aside how they can easily be heard inside of there. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the curtains are currently prohibited. The past tense implies the prohibition no longer applies and shifts the practical reason they cannot install them.
records.remedy: Use 'That's forbidden.'

highlights.text: That was forbidden

records.jp: 「あー、諸君らが俺をどう思っているかは知っている。だがこれはつまらないギャグではなくマジでいい手なのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I know what you ladies think of me. But this isn't some annoying gag, I really think there's something we could do."
comments: He totally means to refer them both as 'ladies'. -GHS
records.assessment: The collective address means 'you people' or 'all of you' and includes the group present. The English changes it to a gendered address unsupported by the wording and local participants.
records.remedy: Use 'I know what you all think of me.'

highlights.text: you ladies

records.jp: 適当に部室で暇を潰して、教室に戻る途中。
records.en: After suitably passing time in the club room, I'm on my way back to the classroom.
records.assessment: The narrator kills time casually or aimlessly in the clubroom. 'Suitably passing time' suggests propriety or adequacy and is not idiomatic for this adverbial nuance.
records.remedy: Use 'After killing some time in the clubroom,'

highlights.text: suitably passing time

records.jp: 人気のない廊下で、処女がうずくまっていた。
records.en: A maiden was crouching in a corridor devoid of human presence.
comments: Pun not as obvious in English I'm afraid. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration bluntly labels the girl a virgin. 'Maiden' is an archaic euphemism that softens the comic directness and can mean merely an unmarried young woman.
records.remedy: Use the explicit noun 'virgin.'

highlights.text: A maiden

records.jp: 「大丈夫ですか、お嬢さん？」
records.en: Taichi: "Is everything well, ojou-san?"
comments: Formal. -GHS
records.assessment: The ordinary address 'miss' or 'young lady' is left as an unexplained romanized Japanese expression inside otherwise English dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'Are you all right, miss?'

highlights.text: ojou-san

records.jp: 「おっとぉ！」
records.en: Girl: "Woh'tt'ooo!"
records.assessment: The surprised 'Whoa!' is rendered as an opaque apostrophe-heavy spelling that supplies no readable English pronunciation or meaningful source distinction.
records.remedy: Use an elongated 'Whoa!'

highlights.text: Woh'tt'ooo

records.jp: すり足で距離を取る。
records.en: and gained distance with a suri-ashi.
comments: Specific judo technique, that is the correct English term. This is pretty clever for Miki, but still not Unreset clever. -GHS
records.assessment: The action is a sliding or shuffling step used to open distance. The untranslated technique term with an indefinite article leaves the motion inaccessible in English.
records.remedy: Use 'she slid back to put distance between us.'

highlights.text: a suri-ashi

records.jp: しかも跳ね起きると同時に、俺に一撃を加えてきた。
records.en: And, simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack on me.
comments: Rag below. Still sharp enough to mask some of her later behavior. -GHS
records.assessment: She strikes the narrator as she springs up. The nominalized timing phrase and 'inflicted an attack' are unidiomatic calques that obscure a simple simultaneous blow.
records.remedy: Use 'As she sprang up, she struck me.'

highlights.text: simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack

records.jp: 片手で受け止めた、顔面を狙って放たれた雑巾を、静かに床に落とす。
records.en: The rag that she threw towards my face fell from the one hand I had caught it with to the floor, in silence.
comments: See CCD5001. This is a move he learned from Taichi. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator deliberately and quietly drops the rag he caught. The English makes the rag fall from his hand and turns controlled action into an accidental event inside a malformed relative construction.
records.remedy: Use 'I quietly dropped the rag I'd caught in one hand.'

highlights.text: fell from the one hand I had caught it with

records.jp: 映画化された某有名ファンタジー小説のヒロインみたいな少女が、立っている。
records.en: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.
comments: I sooo wanted this not to be Hermione from Harry Potter, if only because first film is from 2001 and would mess up the dating in a way that would force me to consider that Taichi would only have read the book, despite it having been released in the US the damn same month the VN takes place in and the translation to Japanese being Dec 1999, which admittedly is one of the earliest translations... but CCZDXC confirms it. Personality-wise, it does fit in many ways, especially that part near the end of book 3. If it helps, Wikipedia reports that Hermione was named from Shakespeare, further cementing things. What Johnson has to do, however, I still only have the vaguest idea. -GHS
records.assessment: The girl is standing there and resembles the heroine of a well-known fantasy novel adapted for film. The English is grammatically malformed and changes the static description into the action of standing up.
records.remedy: Use 'A girl resembling the heroine of a famous fantasy novel turned movie stood before me.'

highlights.text: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.

records.jp: 「しばらく会ってないからって名前とか忘れてへんで？」
records.en: Taichi: "Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like?"
records.assessment: The source assures her that he has not forgotten her name merely because they have not met for a while. The English reverses this into a hypothetical confession that he did forget it.
records.remedy: Use 'It's not like I forgot your name just because we haven't seen each other for a while.'

highlights.text: Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like

records.jp: 山辺美希は涙を誘うほど乏しい胸を張った。
records.en: Yamanobe Miki stuck out a chest so unplentiful it invites tears.
comments: See CCA0009B: she DOES have boobs that he doesn't expect. This loli flatness vanishes around Kiri's route, never to return. -GHS
records.assessment: The joke describes a chest so meager it brings tears. 'Unplentiful' is an unnatural and weak adjective that obscures the blunt visual insult.
records.remedy: Use 'a chest so meager it could move you to tears.'

highlights.text: a chest so unplentiful

records.jp: 「だがそのスカートのめくれまでは……」
records.en: Taichi: "But until I flip that skirt..."
records.assessment: The fragment refers to the skirt having flipped up, continuing a bluff about what just happened. The English makes it a future deliberate action by the speaker.
records.remedy: Use 'But your skirt did flip up—'

highlights.text: until I flip that skirt

records.jp: 「めくれてません（きっぱり）」
records.en: Miki: "You shan't flip. (Decisevely)"
comments: ... (silence) -GHS
records.assessment: She firmly states that the skirt did not flip up. The English instead commands a future subject not to flip, omits the skirt, and misspells the manner note.
records.remedy: Use 'It didn't flip up. (Firmly.)'

highlights.text: You shan't flip. (Decisevely)

records.jp: 「いいだろう。今回は花を持たせておく」
records.en: Taichi: "But it's fine. For this once, I'll let you carry the flowers so that you can take credit for this."
comments: Literal and lateral due to overlap with the nickname. -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom means letting the other person have the credit or glory this time. The English retains a meaningless literal image and then redundantly explains it.
records.remedy: Use 'Fine. I'll let you have this one.'

highlights.text: carry the flowers

records.jp: うわー、抱きしめてぇ。
records.en: Waaah, hug meee!
comments: Supposing he wants to be held back. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator exclaims that he wants to hug her. The English turns that desire into a command or plea for someone else to hug him, reversing the action's direction.
records.remedy: Use 'God, I wanna hug her.'

highlights.text: hug meee

records.jp: 「自発的にかい、そいつはクールだネ！」
records.en: Taichi: "All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes!"
records.assessment: The mock-praise asks whether she did it voluntarily and calls that cool. The English is a fragment followed by an unnatural declarative tag, losing the question's shape.
records.remedy: Use 'All on your own initiative? That's very cool!'

highlights.text: All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes

records.jp: 「なんか久々ですねえー」
records.en: Miki: "Really been a long while there."
records.assessment: The casual observation that it feels like a long time is recognizable, but the English omits a subject and finite auxiliary and appends an unnatural 'there.'
records.remedy: Use 'It really has been a while, hasn't it?'

highlights.text: Really been a long while there

records.jp: 焦ってはいかん、冷静に対処するのだ。
records.en: Getting flustered is a no go, cope with this with composure.
records.assessment: The instruction to handle the situation calmly is accurate in content, but the repeated preposition and clinical 'cope' produce an unidiomatic calque.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't panic. Handle this calmly.'

highlights.text: cope with this with composure

records.jp: 「どどどどどどうしたことだ、山辺君！　そんなに嫌であれば無理に余白を潰そうなんて思わないぞ！　正直に申告するのダっ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "Wh-wh-wh-wh-wh-what is wrong, Yamanobe-kun?! If that is so disagreeable, than I shall not even think to wast that blank space! I proclaim this with honesty, see?!"
comments: Blank space of the notebook I guess. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker commands her to report her feelings honestly. The English changes the addressee's required confession into the speaker proclaiming his own honesty; surrounding spelling and conjunction errors further damage the line.
records.remedy: Use 'Tell me honestly!'

highlights.text: I proclaim this with honesty

records.jp: 声震えまくり。
records.en: My voice just shakes.
records.assessment: The source says his voice is trembling violently or all over, not merely that it shakes. The English drops the emphatic degree and shifts into an oddly generic present.
records.remedy: Use 'My voice was shaking like crazy.'

highlights.text: just shakes

records.jp: 俺もつられて泣きそう。
records.en: which carries me to tearfulness as well.
records.assessment: The narrator feels like crying in sympathy. 'Carries me to tearfulness' is an abstract and nonidiomatic rendering of emotional contagion.
records.remedy: Use 'Now I feel like crying too.'

highlights.text: carries me to tearfulness

records.jp: 冷や汗をぬぐった。
records.en: I wiped off cold sweat.
records.assessment: The action is clear, but English requires a possessive or determiner for the sweat being wiped away; the bare mass-noun construction reads as a calque.
records.remedy: Use 'I wiped the cold sweat from my brow.'

highlights.text: wiped off cold sweat

records.jp: 「じゃあ今回は王子（俺）のサインはおあずけだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, this time the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed."
records.assessment: The mock-prince persona says she will have to wait for his autograph this time. The nominalized passive and arbitrary capitalization are not natural English dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'Then you'll have to wait for your prince's autograph.'

highlights.text: the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed

records.jp: 「いります！　してください！」
records.en: Miki: "I need you in this! Do this please!"
comments: "I need it" + "put it in" & "please do it" + "please do me". This is another overreaction; Miki just doesn't seem capable of taking things in proper measure, which is why he takes Taichi's Settei so damn seriously. -GHS
