records.assessment: She says she wants the autograph and asks him to do it. The English instead says she needs him 'in this,' inventing an object relationship and producing an unintelligible request.
records.remedy: Use 'I want it! Please do it!'

highlights.text: I need you in this

records.jp: こっちがたじろぐ。
records.en: Faltering from my direction.
records.assessment: The narrator says he is the one who recoils or falters. The English removes the person as subject and substitutes a direction, leaving a sentence fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'Now I was the one who recoiled.'

highlights.text: Faltering from my direction.

records.jp: 甲高い声で『してください』と連呼される。
records.en: I'm repeatedly called to "do this please" with a shrill voice.
records.assessment: He is subjected to the shrill repetition of the quoted plea. 'Called to do this please' converts the words into an indirect summons and is not grammatical English reporting.
records.remedy: Use 'She kept shrilling, Please do it, over and over.'

highlights.text: repeatedly called to "do this please"

records.jp: 下腹部が熱くなってきた。
records.en: The lower abdomen grew hotter.
comments: See CCD0021, it's probably the clearest. -GHS
records.assessment: The contextually understood body part is the narrator's own lower abdomen. The English turns it into a generic anatomical object and loses the personal bodily reaction.
records.remedy: Use 'My lower abdomen was getting hot.'

highlights.text: The lower abdomen

records.jp: 童話調に思考しても生々しさは消えなかった。
records.en: I may have thought this in the tone of a fairy-tale, but the graphicness didn't go away.
comments: see CCA0007. Break out that On Fairy-Tales essay! -GHS
records.assessment: The contrast between fairy-tale framing and persistent visceral immediacy is retained, but 'graphicness' is an awkward abstract coinage that does not naturally express 生々しさ here.
records.remedy: Use 'the visceral reality of it didn't go away.'

highlights.text: the graphicness

records.jp: 「わ、わかった、ではアレを」
records.en: Taichi: "I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do."
comments: Break out that "On 'that' I'll do" essay! -GHS
records.assessment: The stammered acceptance and turn toward the euphemistic 'that' are visible, but the English is syntactically inverted and over-completes the source fragment with an awkward 'I'll do.'
records.remedy: Use 'O-okay. Then, that...'

highlights.text: I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do.

records.jp: 当校では身分証明書をかねるこの手帳を、そう呼ぶ。
records.en: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.
records.assessment: The source says that this notebook, which doubles as identification, is called that at the school. 'An ID booklet with a second role' reverses which function is being specified and leaves the other role unexplained.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what our school calls this notebook, which doubles as an ID.'

highlights.text: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.

records.jp: どうも本校のお歴々は、『都会』の駅裏にある人気ＮＯ１高級浴場『メイトブック』の存在を知らないようなのだ。
records.en: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.
comments: This will be one of the weirdest running gags in the VN. The MateBook will be repeatedly said to be named (or not) after a possible whorehouse, SoapLand or public bathhouse. The origin will change pretty much every time. The point, of course, is that this is part of Taichi's Settei and its origin changing constantly and without warning is the reading key to watch out for other things to. Clarified as it's not necessarily obvious in English that being behind the train station is a popular spot, not a seedy one. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the school's leading figures apparently do not know of the bathhouse. The English reverses that into a claim that none could be unaware, and also invents a 'popular spot' not present in the location phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'Apparently, the school's grandees don't know about MateBook, the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the City.'

highlights.text: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.

records.jp: スタンプを集めることによって、Ｗやトリプルなどのサービスが格安で楽しめるという寸法だ。
records.en: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.
records.assessment: Collecting stamps enables discounted access to the named services. The English instead makes the number of stamps a measure of relative cheapness, changing the mechanism into a scale.
records.remedy: Use 'Collect enough stamps and you can enjoy services like the Double or Triple at a steep discount.'

highlights.text: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.

records.jp: ……トリプルだなんて。
records.en: ...what's even a triple now.
comments: See CCC4007, though there's another in CCD3003B. -GHS
records.assessment: The fragment reacts in astonishment to a 'Triple, of all things.' The English turns that reaction into a request for the term's definition.
records.remedy: Use '...A Triple, of all things.'

highlights.text: what's even a triple now

records.jp: それはいかなる世界なのか。
records.en: What kind of world would be that?
records.assessment: The question's content is correct, but its English word order is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use 'What kind of world would that be?'

highlights.text: What kind of world would be that?

records.jp: 勃ってきました……。
records.en: I have erected...
records.assessment: The source says the speaker is becoming erect. 'I have erected' makes him the transitive agent of an unstated object and is not idiomatic English for the bodily state.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm getting hard...'

highlights.text: I have erected

records.jp: ここで安易に前傾シフトをとれば、美希にばれる。
records.en: If I take a gentle forwards Shift here, Miki will notice.
records.assessment: The risk of giving himself away by casually leaning forward is retained, but 'take a gentle forwards Shift' is an unnatural mechanical calque and the capitalization is unjustified.
records.remedy: Use 'If I casually shift forward now, Miki will notice.'

highlights.text: a gentle forwards Shift

records.jp: 美希は処女だが、男の生理には精通している。
records.en: Miki might be a literal maiden, but she is acquainted with male physiology,
records.assessment: The concessive states that she is a virgin despite knowing male physiology well. 'Might be' introduces uncertainty absent from the source, while 'literal maiden' substitutes an archaic euphemism for the factual contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'Miki may be a virgin, but she knows male physiology inside out.'

highlights.text: might be a literal maiden

records.jp: 前傾しなくともばれるだろうが、堂々としていれば、格好だけはつく。
records.en: Even if I don't lean I'll likely be spotted, but if I stay confident, I should at least look cool.
comments: No, that's never cool you damn unrepentant beta. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says brazenly acting as though nothing is wrong will at least preserve appearances. 'Stay confident' and 'look cool' turn that social cover into self-confidence and attractiveness.
records.remedy: Use 'She'll probably notice even if I don't lean forward, but if I brazen it out, I can at least keep up appearances.'

highlights.text: if I stay confident, I should at least look cool

records.jp: あ、今ちらっと見た。
records.en: Ah, she glimpsed right then.
records.assessment: The source observes that she just stole a glance. 'Glimpsed' is used transitively without an object and 'right then' weakens the immediate 'just now.'
records.remedy: Use 'Ah, she just glanced over.'

highlights.text: glimpsed right then

records.jp: 視線を窓の外に向けて、わずかにもじもじする。
records.en: She turns her gaze towards the outside via the window, and fidgets slightly.
comments: Is she embarrassed or horny? -GHS
records.assessment: The action of looking out the window and fidgeting slightly is present, but the route-like phrase 'towards the outside via the window' is not natural visual description.
records.remedy: Use 'She turns her gaze out the window and fidgets slightly.'

highlights.text: towards the outside via the window

records.jp: 羞恥のあまり、荒ぶる破壊神は鎮まっていく。
records.en: But the embarrasment is so great that this savage god of destruction grows subdued.
comments: Of course there's a god in here. -GHS
records.assessment: The metaphorical content is retained, but 'embarrassment' is misspelled in the displayed prose.
records.remedy: Correct 'embarrasment' to 'embarrassment.'

highlights.text: embarrasment

records.jp: 実戦経験がないためか、直で面すると弱いんだな。
records.en: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.
comments: His dick and Miki both. Remember, she's a Witch of Words. -GHS
records.assessment: The source infers that she is weak when confronted directly, perhaps because she lacks practical experience. The English depersonalizes her into the abstract claim that confrontation itself is a weakness and places 'perhaps' unnaturally.
records.remedy: Use 'Maybe because she has no practical experience, she's weak when faced with the real thing.'

highlights.text: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.

records.jp: というか全部、完璧に、申し分のない、痴漢行為である。
records.en: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.
records.assessment: The conclusion that all the listed acts are unequivocally molestation is present, but the stacked adverbs are unpunctuated and 'are ... molestation' is not grammatical count syntax.
records.remedy: Use 'Or rather, every last one is a perfectly unambiguous act of molestation.'

highlights.text: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.

records.jp: 「美希は手帳だいぶ使いこんでるなあ。ぼろぼろだ」
records.en: Taichi: "You've been using this notebook thoroughly, Miki. It's all worn!"
records.assessment: The source observes that she has used the notebook heavily and that it is in tatters. 'Using ... thoroughly' is an unnatural calque, and 'all worn' weakens the physical condition.
records.remedy: Use 'You've really put this notebook through its paces, Miki. It's falling apart.'

highlights.text: using this notebook thoroughly

records.jp: ページを繰ると、メモ欄にはすでに俺のサインがでかでかと書かれていた。
records.en: Flipping the pages, I see annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature.
comments: No one else's, meaning it's their game. -GHS
records.assessment: The source reveals that his signature is already written very large in the memo field. The English pluralizes the field, makes it generally filled, and uses the unnatural adjective 'large-sized.'
records.remedy: Use 'As I flipped through it, I found my signature already scrawled huge across the memo field.'

highlights.text: annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature

records.jp: 何ページにも渡っている。
records.en: I pass by several pages.
records.assessment: The source says the oversized signature extends across several pages. The English instead describes the narrator moving past pages, changing both subject and action.
records.remedy: Use 'It stretched across several pages.'

highlights.text: I pass by several pages.

records.jp: 白紙を見つけ、そこに新たなサインを書き込む。
records.en: I find a blank page and there I fill out a fresh signature.
records.assessment: The action of finding a blank page and adding a new signature is present, but English speakers write or sign a signature rather than 'fill out' one.
records.remedy: Use 'I find a blank page and write a fresh signature on it.'

highlights.text: fill out a fresh signature

records.jp: 「あのさ、今回は俺がサインしたくて美希の胸を借りたってことで……全然いじわるしようとか思ってないからね？」
records.en: Taichi: "You know, this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding... not because of mean intent, OK?"
comments: Oh dear. Word itself means "practice with a sparring partner of higher skill", with the implication of imitative behavior; this form means "to have a contest with you"/"challenge you"; and literally it's "borrowed your chest". All necessary. Left vague, because it is after all. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker proposes framing the incident as borrowing her chest because he wanted to sign, then denies intending to tease her. The English invents a shared 'game,' changes the object into padding, and turns the strained excuse into a different proposition.
records.remedy: Use 'Look, let's just say I borrowed your chest because I wanted somewhere to sign this time... I wasn't trying to be mean, okay?'

highlights.text: this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding

records.jp: 「そ、そう？」
records.en: Taichi: "You-, don't?"
records.assessment: The stammered response is simply 'R-really?' or 'I-is that so?' The English instead forces a grammatically broken negative echo of the previous sentence.
records.remedy: Use 'R-really?'

highlights.text: You-, don't?

records.jp: 美希はおだやかな顔をしていた。
records.en: Miki was making a tranquil face.
records.assessment: The calm expression is understood, but 'making a tranquil face' is an unnatural English calque for wearing or having that expression.
records.remedy: Use 'Miki wore a peaceful expression.'

highlights.text: making a tranquil face

records.jp: 確かに嫌がっている風ではない。
records.en: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.
comments: This is basically screaming the reading key for the Misato scenes, that 'wind' needs to be read 'pretense'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she certainly does not look displeased. The English instead denies any pretense of having disliked it, shifting from her apparent feeling to whether that feeling is feigned and producing the opposite logical structure.
records.remedy: Use 'She certainly doesn't look bothered.'

highlights.text: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.

records.jp: 「べ、別にそんなことで安心したりしないもん」
records.en: Taichi: "It-, it's not like you need to reassure me of such things!"
comments: Intentional -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker protests that this fact does not make him feel relieved. The English instead tells her that she does not need to reassure him, changing the subject and the force of the embarrassed denial.
records.remedy: Use 'I-it's not like that makes me feel relieved or anything!'

highlights.text: it's not like you need to reassure me of such things

records.jp: 「掃除、手伝おうか？」
records.en: Taichi: "So, cleaning, can I help you?"
records.assessment: The offer to help with the cleaning is accurate, but the topic-fronted English is fragmented and unnatural for a simple offer.
records.remedy: Use 'Want some help cleaning?'

highlights.text: So, cleaning, can I help you?

records.jp: 寄せてあげることもままならない平らな胸を張った。
records.en: She pushed out a chest that you couldn't fondle by putting your hands on it.
records.assessment: The source jokes that her chest is so flat it cannot even be pushed together and lifted for cleavage. The English replaces that visual bra-related joke with an unrelated claim that the chest cannot be fondled by hand.
records.remedy: Use 'She thrust out a chest so flat there was nothing to push together or lift.'

highlights.text: a chest that you couldn't fondle by putting your hands on it

records.jp: 自分で捨てた雑巾を拾って、汚れに向かう。
records.en: Grabbing back the rag that I had dropped earlier, I turn towards the uncleanliness.
comments: Intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he picks up the rag he himself threw away and heads for the stain. 'Dropped earlier' weakens the deliberate disposal, while 'turn towards the uncleanliness' is an abstract and unidiomatic substitute for confronting the dirty spot.
records.remedy: Use 'I picked up the rag I'd thrown away and headed for the stain.'

highlights.text: dropped earlier, I turn towards the uncleanliness

records.jp: 雑巾を顔から離す。
records.en: I unhide my face from behind the rag.
comments: Parallel to above.
records.assessment: The source simply says he lowers or moves the rag away from his face. 'Unhide my face from behind' is a cumbersome negative construction rather than natural physical description.
records.remedy: Use 'I lowered the rag from my face.'

highlights.text: unhide my face from behind the rag

records.jp: 「うー、血弱くてさ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ngggh, I'm weak to blood."
records.assessment: The meaning that he cannot handle blood is recognizable, but 'weak to blood' is a game-stat calque rather than idiomatic English for this sensitivity.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm really bad with blood.'

highlights.text: weak to blood

records.jp: 「正直、きついっす」
records.en: Taichi: "Honestly, that's harsh..."
comments: See CCA0004, he could be talking about her as well as the blood. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker says that his physical reaction is honestly rough or hard to bear. 'That's harsh' instead sounds like a response to the preceding teasing remark and shifts the line away from his condition.
records.remedy: Use 'Honestly, this is rough.'

highlights.text: that's harsh

records.jp: ちらっと見ただけで、まだ気分が悪い。
records.en: I still feel sick despite having just glimpsed at it.
comments: IOW he didn't really see if it's blood. And she wiped it away in like .3 seconds! This is ridiculous. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says even a mere glance has left him still feeling sick. 'Glimpsed at' is ungrammatical, and 'despite' weakens the causal force of the small exposure producing the reaction.
records.remedy: Use 'One little glance, and I still feel sick.'

highlights.text: despite having just glimpsed at it

records.jp: 「豚とののしってくれ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Please abuse this worthless pig..."
comments: Connection that mascara thing was unintentional, but I guess it works too. Notice the pattern: see blood -> feel sick -> desires abuse. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks her to insult him by calling him a pig. The English instead calls him a worthless pig in the narration of the request and asks for general abuse, adding the judgment and weakening the specific requested wording.
records.remedy: Use 'Call me a pig...'

highlights.text: abuse this worthless pig

records.jp: 「どうか豚と」
records.en: Taichi: "Like an oinker treat me."
records.assessment: He repeats his plea to be called a pig. 'Treat me like an oinker' substitutes treatment for naming, softens 'pig,' and uses inverted, unidiomatic syntax.
records.remedy: Use 'Please. Call me a pig.'

highlights.text: Like an oinker treat me.

records.jp: 「豚は豚箱に行け？」
records.en: Miki: "Piggy wants to pig out in the pigpen?"
comments: Lit. "Pig wants to go into the prison cell", which is written "pig-box". Using "the pigs" for cops is too out of character for Miki. This oddly connects to Misato, who's the one who has all the jail and arrest stuff around her.
records.assessment: The line tentatively insults him with a command asking whether the pig should go to the 'pig box,' slang for jail. The English invents wanting to eat excessively and replaces the jail pun with an ordinary pigpen.
records.remedy: Use 'Should the pig go back to the pigsty?' with a note preserving the jail sense if needed.

highlights.text: Piggy wants to pig out in the pigpen?

records.jp: アレンジされた上、疑問形式なのが妙にきつかった。
records.en: That arrangement being then put in the form of a question made it oddly painful.
records.assessment: The source says her improvised variation, especially being phrased as a question, struck oddly hard. The English nominalizes the whole thought into an ungainly progressive construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Her little improvisation—and the fact that she made it a question—hurt in a strangely specific way.'

highlights.text: That arrangement being then put in the form of a question

records.jp: 「豚箱より保健室いきませんか？」
records.en: Miki: "Rather than the pigpen, would you like to go the infirmary?"
comments: Is there a law that requires calling it "health room"? No, seriously, I want to know. -GHS
records.assessment: The alternative suggestion of going to the infirmary is accurate, but the English omits the required preposition 'to.'
records.remedy: Use 'Rather than the pigpen, would you like to go to the infirmary?'

highlights.text: go the infirmary

records.jp: 「……うーん」
records.en: Miki: "...uh-huh."
records.assessment: The drawn-out sound expresses hesitation or doubt. 'Uh-huh' conventionally signals agreement, reversing her response to his reassurance.
records.remedy: Use '...Hmm.'

highlights.text: uh-huh

records.jp: その提案は、後ろ髪を引きすぎる。
records.en: That proposal made the hair on the back of my head stand way up.
comments: This is supposed to be a Standard Perverted Protagonist thing, where they're all unflappable until they're actually put on the spot. In this sense, it's fairly straightforwards: he's only interested in the sport of it, the actual deed he's more than a little reluctant, understandably given his backstory.
records.assessment: The idiom says the proposal is far too tempting to leave behind. The English reads the body-part image literally and turns attraction or reluctance to depart into alarm or gooseflesh.
records.remedy: Use 'That offer was far too tempting.'

highlights.text: made the hair on the back of my head stand way up

records.jp: 「ベッドも二つありますし」
records.en: Miki: "There are at least two beds there."
records.assessment: She adds that there are two beds. 'At least' changes the exact count into a lower bound and introduces uncertainty absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use 'There are two beds there, too.'

highlights.text: at least two beds

records.jp: 微笑む少女の胸元に、自然な挙措で手が伸びた。
records.en: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.
comments: The hand did, not him. This is automatic behavior, see below. -GHS
records.assessment: The hand naturally reaches toward the smiling girl's chest. The inverted modifier 'manners nonchalant' is ungrammatical literary affectation, and making the hand the sentence's agent does not require that inversion.
records.remedy: Use 'My hand naturally reached toward the smiling girl's chest.'

highlights.text: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.

records.jp: 気がつくと、俺はおっぱいを揉んでいた。
records.en: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.
comments: He's now de-automatized. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that when he realized what he was doing, he was fondling her breasts. 'Come to notice' is unidiomatic, its tense clashes with 'was,' and the English drops the contextual possessor.
records.remedy: Use 'When I came to, I was fondling her breasts.'

highlights.text: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.

records.jp: ほとんどないと思っていたその「板」には……薄いとはいえ確かな感触が。
records.en: I flatly thought that there would be about nothing on this Chopping Board... but, weak as it may be, there is certainly that tactile sensation.
comments: OmotteITA sono ITA where ita = board... well at least that was easy to adapt. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls her a 'board' he had thought almost entirely flat, then registers a faint but definite softness. 'I flatly thought,' 'about nothing,' and 'weak tactile sensation' are malformed, while capitalizing and specifying 'Chopping Board' distorts the plain insult used for the wordplay.
records.remedy: Use 'That "board" I'd thought was almost perfectly flat... had a faint but unmistakable softness to it.'

highlights.text: I flatly thought that there would be about nothing on this Chopping Board... but, weak as it may be, there is certainly that tactile sensation.

records.jp: 笑顔のまま、口元を引きつらせる。
records.en: Still smiling, the edge of her lips begin to twitch.
records.assessment: The mouth remains smiling but starts to twitch. The English has a subject-verb disagreement and replaces the natural mouth or corners-of-the-mouth expression with the singular 'edge of her lips.'
records.remedy: Use 'Still smiling, the corners of her mouth began to twitch.'

highlights.text: the edge of her lips begin to twitch

records.jp: 「ごめん、無意識に手が」
records.en: Taichi: "Sorry, alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own."
comments: The moment when you realize that yes, that's correct, it did... -GHS
records.assessment: He apologizes that his hand moved unconsciously. Naming a neurological syndrome is an unsupported diagnostic joke added by the translation, and the appended clause overexplains the unfinished source line.
records.remedy: Use 'Sorry—my hand moved on its own...'

highlights.text: alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own

records.jp: 「あの、こんなこと俺が言うのもなんだけど……ちょっと膨らんでるね。良かったね！」
records.en: Taichi: "Uhm, I shouldn't exactly be saying this but... they've bulged out a bit. That's great!"
records.assessment: He awkwardly congratulates her on having filled out a little. 'Bulged out' suggests an abrupt protrusion or swelling rather than modest physical development, making the line harsher and less idiomatic than the source.
records.remedy: Use 'you've filled out a little.'

highlights.text: they've bulged out a bit

records.jp: 「恐縮です。いつ手を離していただけますでしょうか」
records.en: Miki: "Much obliged. When will this hand finally distance itself?"
comments: Formal here. -GHS
records.assessment: Her mock-politeness asks when he will kindly remove his hand. The English makes the hand an autonomous subject, uses the unidiomatic reflexive 'distance itself,' and loses the pointedly courteous request directed at him.
records.remedy: Use 'Much obliged. And when might you remove your hand?'

highlights.text: When will this hand finally distance itself

records.jp: 「俺は感慨深いよ。あの小さかった、いやさ、平べったかった美希が三次元的立体感を手に入れるなんて」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm deeply moved here. For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality!"
records.assessment: The mock-grand statement says that formerly tiny—or rather flat—Miki has acquired three-dimensional volume. The English is syntactically broken after 'For,' and 'tabular' and 'solid feeling of tridimensionality' are technical malapropisms rather than controlled grandiosity.
records.remedy: Use 'To think little—no, flat—Miki has finally acquired three-dimensional volume!'

highlights.text: For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality

records.jp: 嗚咽もなく、頬の曲線を滑りおちる。
records.en: with sobbing neither, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.
records.assessment: The tears slide down the curve of her cheeks without a sob. 'With sobbing neither' is not grammatical English and obscures the clean continuation from the preceding fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'without a sob, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.'

highlights.text: with sobbing neither

records.jp: 理解ができないから。
records.en: because there's no understanding.
comments: It's mostly from Taichi, but it's from both sides in the end. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives his inability to understand as the reason he stops. The impersonal 'there's no understanding' replaces that experiencer with an abstract absence and is unnatural in context.
records.remedy: Use 'because I don't understand.'

highlights.text: because there's no understanding

records.jp: やがて美希はぐっと涙をぬぐった。
records.en: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears,
records.assessment: Miki soon wipes her tears away firmly. The stray 'well and' makes the sentence ungrammatical and does not convey the decisive force of the adverb.
records.remedy: Use 'Before long, Miki firmly wiped away her tears.'

highlights.text: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears

records.jp: まぶたの上を腕が往復して、出てきたのはいつもの笑顔。
records.en: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always.
comments: 往復, see CCA0015C -GHS
records.assessment: Her arm passes back and forth over her eyelids, revealing her usual smile. The English changes one arm into plural forearms, invents a trip 'around' the eyelids, and ends with the calque 'smile of always.'
records.remedy: Use 'Her arm passed back and forth over her eyes, and out came her usual smile.'

highlights.text: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always

records.jp: 「さー、掃除掃除！」
records.en: Miki: "Sooo, to cleaning, to cleaning!"
records.assessment: She cheerfully turns back to cleaning. 'To cleaning' is not an English idiom for resuming a task and makes the energetic repetition sound malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'All right—back to cleaning, cleaning!'

highlights.text: to cleaning, to cleaning

records.jp: 腕の秘孔（二の腕の中ほどあたり）を一本拳で突かれた。
records.en: My arm's pressure point (around the center of the forearm) was struck with the exact knuckletip of a fist.
comments: Hokuto no Miki. GIS 一本拳 for what exactly it means. -GHS
records.assessment: The parenthetical locates the point around the middle of the upper arm, not the forearm. That anatomical change makes the explicit gloss factually wrong.
records.remedy: Use 'around the middle of my upper arm.'

highlights.text: forearm

records.jp: もがき苦しむ俺。
records.en: Writhing in agony go I,
records.assessment: The source is a compact fragment describing him writhing in agony. The translation adds an inverted finite construction that is neither ordinary narration nor controlled comic diction.
records.remedy: Use 'I writhed in agony,' or retain the fragment as 'Me, writhing in agony.'

highlights.text: Writhing in agony go I

records.jp: 掃除する美希。
records.en: sweeping goes Miki.
records.assessment: The fragment simply shows Miki cleaning. The subject-verb inversion is unidiomatic and adds an affected cadence absent from the plain source.
records.remedy: Use 'Miki went on sweeping.'

highlights.text: sweeping goes Miki

records.jp: 「いや、ごめん」
records.en: Taichi: "Nah, nothing."
records.assessment: He says 'No, sorry.' The English replaces the apology with a dismissal that nothing is wrong, changing both the speech act and his stance.
records.remedy: Use 'No—sorry.'

highlights.text: Nah, nothing

records.jp: 「それは胸があったから美希ではないという意味のご発言でございましょうか？」
records.en: Miki: "Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki?"
comments: This continues to sound silly, but see the end of her route: if she changes - grows old - then she stops being what she is.
records.assessment: Her deliberately formal question asks whether he means she cannot be Miki because she has breasts. 'Be to the meaning' and 'have presence of breasts' are ungrammatical pseudo-formality rather than natural ceremonious English.
records.remedy: Use 'Am I to understand that, because I have breasts, I cannot possibly be Miki?'

highlights.text: Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki

records.jp: ぺっ、と架空のツバを吐く。
records.en: Pah, I Imaginarily spat out.
comments: Meaning he didn't actually do it. -GHS
records.assessment: The present-tense narration has him mime spitting with an imaginary gob. The adverb 'Imaginarily' is malformed in this use, its capitalization is erroneous, and the translation switches tense.
records.remedy: Use 'Pah. I mimed spitting.'

highlights.text: I Imaginarily spat out

records.jp: 「何人の固定ファンを手放したか」
records.en: Taichi: "How many fixated fans did you just lose?"
comments: The reason she isn't too loli (until that new CG in Kiri Sendback that is so loli I could only name the file itself as 'loli') is because Lolicon is a Disease. The word itself isn't exactly strange, but using something that means "fixed" in this story is always suggestive, especially considering this is a metareference. -GHS
records.assessment: 固定ファン means established, loyal, or dedicated fans. 'Fixated fans' instead describes people obsessively attached and changes a marketing-style category into a psychological judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'How many dedicated fans do you think you just lost?'

highlights.text: fixated fans

records.jp: 「固定ファン？」
records.en: Miki: "Fixated fans?"
records.assessment: The repeated term refers to loyal or dedicated fans, not fans who are fixated. The error is repeated here as dialogue terminology.
records.remedy: Use 'Dedicated fans?'

highlights.text: Fixated fans

records.jp: 「たとえロリっ娘でなくとも胸がないことで、幼稚園児をその聖域とする社会不適合者の支持を受けることも不可能ではないのに……」
records.en: Taichi: "Because it's not impossible you've been receiving the endorsement of those societally nonconforming people who make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground due to your having a flat chest, even if you aren't exactly loli..."
comments: And here's more from where that Fixated came from: "noncomforming" is the PC word for "people in Gunjou". I THINK TANAKA IS SAYING SOMETHING HERE TO PEOPLE WITH LOLICON BUT I WOULDN'T KNOW WHAT. And he's still being comparatively nice than to the Big Purty Words Mean Good Writing crowd. Also, notice the unsubtle way in which Taichi puts himself in this. See CCA0013: he was trying to groom Miki as he did Yusa. -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes social misfits who treat kindergarten-aged children as their sacred domain. The English changes the children, 幼稚園児, into the institution 'the kindergarten,' materially altering the target of the grotesque joke.
records.remedy: Use 'who regard kindergarteners as their sacred domain.'

highlights.text: make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground

records.jp: 「そろそろ部活、活動再開するってさ」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm hearing that Club is going to be starting up again any time now."
comments: This is intended to be read as Misato having said this, but of course it's a lie. Left it a little ambiguous. -GHS
records.assessment: He reports that club activities will be resuming soon. 'I'm hearing that Club' treats the activity as a proper-named entity and uses a needlessly progressive reporting construction, producing malformed dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'I hear club activities are starting up again soon.'

highlights.text: I'm hearing that Club is going to be starting up again any time now

records.jp: 記憶とともに、温度もゆるくなったようだ。
records.en: The temperature seems to have become more lenient together with the recollections.
comments: He's totally starting to forget whether Misato was up there. That's the result of those flashbacks he possibly had off-screen. -GHS
records.assessment: The temperature or heat seems to have eased along with the memories. Calling temperature 'lenient' is a lexical calque, while 'together with the recollections' fails to express the parallel softening naturally.
records.remedy: Use 'The heat seemed to have softened along with the memories.'

highlights.text: more lenient together with the recollections

records.jp: 屋上から見渡せた藍色の帳は、すでに緋色に染め直されている。
records.en: The curtain of indigo blue I could see on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back into a brilliant scarlet.
comments: Supposing it's 6PM. This should be 2AM. -GHS
records.assessment: The indigo curtain visible from the rooftop has already been redyed scarlet. The English changes the rooftop into the object looked over, uses the calque 'passing my sight,' and makes the curtain intransitively dye itself.
records.remedy: Use 'The indigo curtain I had seen from the rooftop was already dyed scarlet.'

highlights.text: on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back

records.jp: 吹きつけていた突風もない。
records.en: The squall that was blowing against is gone.
comments: See CCA0006. Since the wind = the pretense, and Misato is asleep, ergo SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
records.assessment: The gusts that had been blasting across the rooftop are gone. 'Blowing against' requires an object, leaving the English clause grammatically incomplete.
records.remedy: Use 'The gusts that had been buffeting the rooftop were gone too.'

highlights.text: blowing against

records.jp: 去勢された猫のようにおとなしい、黄昏の頃。
records.en: The time of twilight is as docile as an emasculated cat.
comments: Taichi, well emasculated from soon after birth, yet struggling with a monster that repeatedly takes the form of his dick, and who can't stand the blood that is evening to the point of hallucinating that the twilasdiujdveSYMBOLISM!!1! -GHS
records.assessment: The simile specifies a castrated cat. 'Emasculated' is normally applied figuratively to people or institutions and sounds like an accidental thesaurus substitution rather than the blunt animal image.
records.remedy: Use 'Twilight was as docile as a neutered cat.'

highlights.text: emasculated cat

records.jp: アンテナが佇むのその隣で。
records.en: Neighboring the stillstanding antenna,
records.assessment: The fragment locates her beside the standing antenna. 'Neighboring' makes the subject itself adjacent as a participial action, and 'stillstanding' is not a standard compound in this use.
records.remedy: Use 'Beside the standing antenna,'

highlights.text: Neighboring the stillstanding antenna

records.jp: 「いたよ」
records.en: Taichi: "There she was."
records.assessment: Within present-tense discovery, he says 'There she is.' The past-tense English turns the immediate recognition into retrospective narration.
records.remedy: Use 'There she is.'

highlights.text: There she was

records.jp: 規則的な軽い寝息。
records.en: A light sleeper's breathing, regular.
records.assessment: The source describes light, regular sleeping breaths. 'A light sleeper's breathing' instead characterizes the person as easily awakened, while the postposed 'regular' leaves the phrase malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'Light, regular sleeping breaths.'

highlights.text: A light sleeper's breathing, regular

records.jp: 雑音に過ぎないそれは、不思議な音楽性を伴って思考を弛緩させる。
records.en: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax.
comments: See CCA0006. This is far closer to pretty than to purple, but it's still fairly overwrought. And what he's about to do isn't changing. -GHS
records.assessment: Though merely noise, the breathing has a mysterious musicality that relaxes his thoughts. The English is syntactically incoherent, recasts 'no more than noise' as failure to transcend a specific noise, and never establishes the causal relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Though it was only noise, its strange musicality relaxed my thoughts.'

highlights.text: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax

records.jp: 飾り気のない、彼女の自然体の姿。
records.en: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned.
records.assessment: The source presents her unadorned, natural self. The English's noun stack is ungrammatical, and 'natural in posture' narrows 自然体 into physical posture rather than unselfconscious being.
records.remedy: Use 'Her natural, unadorned self.'

highlights.text: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned

records.jp: 汚れもない。
records.en: filth neither.
records.assessment: The paired fragment says there is no stain or impurity either. 'Filth neither' is not grammatical English and is harsher and more concrete than the abstract moral image.
records.remedy: Use 'nor any stain.'

highlights.text: filth neither

records.jp: じっと。
records.en: Motionlessly I stare.
records.assessment: The source is the adverbial fragment 'still' or 'without moving.' The English adds the act of staring and uses the markedly unnatural adverb 'motionlessly.'
records.remedy: Use 'Motionless.' or, if the carried context requires it, 'I stared without moving.'

highlights.text: Motionlessly I stare

records.jp: 奪われた視線を、世界を包む薄暮の鮮やかさでさえ取り戻せない。
records.en: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back by the mere vividness of the dusk that clads the world.
records.assessment: His gaze has been captured, and even the vivid twilight enveloping the world cannot win it back. The apparent typo 'said' removes the gaze entirely, 'forcibly stolen' overstates 奪われた, and the passive construction obscures what cannot reclaim it.
records.remedy: Use 'Even the vivid twilight enveloping the world could not reclaim my captured gaze.'

highlights.text: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back

records.jp: すこやかな寝息はおさまり、まぶたが震えた。
records.en: A more vigorous breath the conclusion, her eyelids quivered,
records.assessment: Her peaceful sleeping breaths subside and her eyelids tremble. The English fragment is syntactically incoherent, turns healthy or sound breathing into 'more vigorous' breathing, and does not state that it stops.
records.remedy: Use 'Her peaceful breathing subsided, and her eyelids trembled.'

highlights.text: A more vigorous breath the conclusion

records.jp: 長い睫毛が小刻みに痙攣する。
records.en: her long eyelashes tremble in a quivering motion,
records.assessment: Her long eyelashes twitch in tiny movements. 'Tremble in a quivering motion' is tautological and replaces the sharper involuntary twitch with a redundant phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'her long eyelashes twitching rapidly,'

highlights.text: tremble in a quivering motion

records.jp: 「ぺけです」
records.en: Taichi: "Peke I am."
records.assessment: He corrects her with 'It's Peke.' The subject-complement inversion is not motivated by the source and gives him an affected, non-native syntax.
records.remedy: Use 'It's Peke.'

highlights.text: Peke I am

records.en: Senpai: "...hn, not nice..."
records.assessment: Her drowsy protest is 'Mm, no...' or 'I don't like that...' The bare adjective 'not nice' is childlike in a different way and does not form a natural response to the situation.
records.remedy: Use '...Mm, no...'

highlights.text: not nice

records.jp: 「寝顔見たら、いゃ……」
records.en: Misato: "Seeing my sleeping face, not nice..."
comments: Childish -GHS
records.assessment: She objects to his having seen her sleeping face. The fragment makes her own act of seeing the grammatical subject and again substitutes the malformed 'not nice' for her embarrassed refusal.
records.remedy: Use 'You saw me sleeping... no...'

highlights.text: Seeing my sleeping face, not nice

records.jp: 二の腕でいちどきに双眸を覆い、かすかに身もだえる。
records.en: She writhes slightly, both arms covering the both of her eyes.
comments: Back to purple: zero need whatsoever to use that OMFG HARD KANJI's for "pair of eyes" here. Or pretty much ever. I'd translate it to "binocular", but I have standards dammit. -GHS
records.assessment: She covers both eyes at once with one upper arm and writhes faintly. The English changes that singular upper arm into both arms, repeats 'both' ungrammatically, and obscures the specific pose.
records.remedy: Use 'She covered both eyes with one upper arm and squirmed faintly.'

highlights.text: both arms covering the both of her eyes

records.jp: 無防備な自分の姿は、誰だって隠したい。
records.en: Anyone would want to conceal their most defenseless of appearances.
records.assessment: Anyone would want to hide their unguarded self. The superlative-plus-of construction is ungrammatical and turns a general state of vulnerability into an oddly ranked appearance.
records.remedy: Use 'Anyone would want to hide such an unguarded side of themselves.'

highlights.text: most defenseless of appearances

records.jp: 「いつからいたんですかぁ？」
records.en: Misato: "How long 've you been there?"
comments: Not wholly awake. -GHS
records.assessment: The question is accurate, but the detached apostrophe before 've' is not a valid contraction and visibly corrupts the line.
records.remedy: Use 'How long have you been there?'

highlights.text: How long 've you been there

records.jp: 「今ですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Just moments."
comments: Immediate lie... or is it? See CCX0001: hours aren't seconds for him. -GHS
records.assessment: He answers 'Just now.' The plural noun phrase is incomplete English and suggests an unspecified number of moments rather than immediate arrival.
records.remedy: Use 'Just now.'

highlights.text: Just moments

records.jp: 両手をあげて、降参してみる。
records.en: I raise both hands and attempt surrender.
comments: See CCA0006, which is why he did the same there. -GHS
records.assessment: He raises both hands in a show of surrender. 'Attempt surrender' is missing the infinitive marker or nominal preposition and sounds like a failed tactical action rather than a gesture.
records.remedy: Use 'I raised both hands in surrender.'

highlights.text: attempt surrender

records.jp: 「でも、日中は寝こけないようにしないと危ないですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "But it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day!"
comments: Misato's sleep patterns are also broken. -GHS
records.assessment: He warns that it is dangerous to let herself fall asleep during the day. The nested negative 'not to ensure you do not' makes the condition difficult to parse and reverses its force on a first reading.
records.remedy: Use 'But you shouldn't fall asleep during the day. It's dangerous.'

highlights.text: it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day

records.jp: 欠伸を噛み殺す。
records.en: She kills a yawn in her teeth.
comments: Just look at that sentence! Unnecessarily using kanji that require furries for something as simple as a 'yawn', and an apparently simple sentence ("stifling e.g. a yawn") that also means "to bite do death", as well as containing the kanji for 'kill' fairly literally. Ugly in surface, evocative underneath: Touko is known to kill stuff in her mouth, for starters, as well as subject to dehydration (and starvation). -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom means that she stifles or suppresses a yawn. The English renders both halves literally and adds 'in her teeth,' producing an image and construction that do not exist in idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'She stifled a yawn.'

highlights.text: kills a yawn in her teeth

records.jp: つい手が伸びた。
records.en: Instinctively my hand stretched.
comments: Everybody dazzled from the big words above, or are you not missing this? See CCA0009B. Fixed existence... -GHS
records.assessment: His hand reaches out before he can help himself. 'My hand stretched' describes the hand lengthening or extending itself and omits the directional particle needed for the involuntary gesture.
records.remedy: Use 'My hand reached out before I knew it.'

highlights.text: my hand stretched

records.jp: 眼鏡を両手で挟み、顔を寄せて、そっと元に戻す。
records.en: With both hands I seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face.
comments: No choice, but he knows his limits. "Return to origin", see below. -GHS
records.assessment: He cups the glasses with both hands, leans his face closer, and gently puts them back in place. 'Seize' makes the touch forceful, 'return them to normal' mistakes position for condition, and 'close to the face' relocates rather than describes his approach.
records.remedy: Use 'I took her glasses between both hands, leaned close, and gently set them back in place.'

highlights.text: seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face

records.jp: 「これで、いつもの先輩」
records.en: Taichi: "And there, Senpai as always."
records.assessment: He says that this restores her usual appearance. The English is a malformed fragment that lacks the idiomatic demonstrative or copula needed to complete the thought.
records.remedy: Use 'There. Now you're the Senpai I know.'

highlights.text: And there, Senpai as always

records.jp: 「……もう、危ないなぁ」
records.en: Misato: "...really, so dangerous."
comments: Because she knows he wanted to go for her boobs... or does she? And did he? More below. -GHS
records.assessment: Her embarrassed complaint means roughly 'Honestly, that was risky.' The English supplies two unsupported intensifiers but no natural clause, making her reaction sound like a label rather than speech.
records.remedy: Use '...Honestly. That was dangerous.'

highlights.text: really, so dangerous

records.jp: 「鏡を見て考えなさい」
records.en: Misato: "Do look at a mirror and think about this."
comments: Despite the thing about the boobs, she might just not like people sneaking up to others, seeing CCA0006, CCD1001, and parts of Youko. Of course she does it herself, that's how she knows his smile is fake, see CCE0001. Sentence should refer to 長生きしたい人は鏡を見なさい, those who want a long life should look in a mirror.

The sentence, silly Misato, means external looks are a reflection of one's internal health, not simply to reflect on one's actions, so she screwed this up bad. This scene is where cross communication really starts, so pay attention. Come the Kiri route... -GHS
records.assessment: She tells him to look in a mirror and think about it. 'Look at a mirror' makes the physical object the target rather than his reflection and weakens the idiomatic rebuke.
records.remedy: Use 'Look in a mirror and think about it.'

highlights.text: look at a mirror

records.jp: うわ、泣きそうなこと言った、この人！
records.en: Bwah, this person here's just said something that makes me cry!
records.assessment: He exclaims that she said something liable to make him cry. The demonstrative-person calque is unnatural, and 'makes me cry' turns the near-tears reaction into a categorical present fact.
records.remedy: Use 'Whoa—she said something that could make me cry!'

highlights.text: this person here's just said something that makes me cry

records.jp: 「俺が不細工ってことですかぁーっ！　うわあああ、気にしてるのにー！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Is it because I am horrendooous! Bwaaaaaah, when I worry so much about thaaat!!!"
comments: The term used is literally "a poor-quality product". Ties well into him being a product of God and all. -GHS
records.assessment: He wails that he is sensitive about being ugly. 'When I worry' introduces a temporal subordinate clause with no main-clause relation and misses the idiomatic sense of being self-conscious about it.
records.remedy: Use 'And I'm already so self-conscious about it!'

highlights.text: when I worry so much about thaaat

records.jp: 「我ガ名ハクリエイター、人類ノ支配存在デアル！」
records.en: Taichi: "WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE THE BEING THAT DOMINATES MANKIND!"
comments: The stupid old ROM wouldn't really accept Western characters unless I hacked the graphics drawing program and had it insert the text manually, which isn't not very elegant due to double-byte characters in the original Japanese (technical hacking stuff, don't mind it), so it read like all centered and with lots of spaces and stuff, but then my editor (which is inexplicably a sock puppet) begged me to use the bootleg that runs on Scramble hardware (MAME joke) so that mere caps are sufficient. Stupid tween who's never been in an arcade in the 80s grumble grumble gitoffmahlawn a fie on both his house and the basement he lives in grumble. -GHS
records.assessment: The mock-archaic declaration is singular: 'My name is Creator; I am the being who rules humanity.' The English is ungrammatical and changes both singular first-person claims into plural ones.
records.remedy: Use a deliberately archaic but grammatical singular declaration.

highlights.text: WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE

records.jp: 「わ、わ、ぺけくんが二十年前のゲームのボスみたいな陳腐な創造主に！？」
records.en: Misato: "Wah, wah, Peke-kun has become an hackneyed Creator of All Life like some boss from a 20-year old videogame?!"
comments: Beware, he lives! Well, the reference is too vague, I only suspect Sinistar because of tone. Also "I hunger!" works with Taichi the Devourer of All Things (in his mind). The rest is religious, but I don't see how anyone could be stumped by a guy who was likely retrained via videogames and spouts sub-Nietzscheian nonsense at the drop of a hat thinking he's a hackneyed videogame God from the '80s after being struck in a very delicate spot. I mean, DUH. -GHS
records.assessment: She calls him a hackneyed creator like a boss from a game twenty years ago. The English uses the wrong article and adds the unsupported scope 'of All Life.'
records.remedy: Use 'a hackneyed creator' without the added domain.

highlights.text: an hackneyed Creator of All Life

records.jp: 「ナニユエ我ニ逆ラウノカ。我ノ支配ノナカニイレバ、永遠ノ平和ヲ手ニ入レルコトガデキヨウ」
records.en: Taichi: "FOR WHAT PURPOSE DO YOU OPPOSE US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL IS TO OBTAIN PEACE ETERNAL."
comments: See CCC3013 as well: the final boss of Phantasy Star II fits. Perhaps a conflation of Sinistar and PS2, actually, it would fit very well with Taichi's memory. This question is Jesus in a nutshell. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker asks why she opposes him and promises that entering his rule would let her obtain eternal peace. The English again changes singular 'me/my' to plural 'us/our' and turns the conditional promise into an abstract equation.
records.remedy: Keep the singular ruler and the conditional relation.

highlights.text: US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL

records.jp: 「ごめんなさい、やっぱいいです」
records.en: Misato: "Apologies, it is really not a problem!"
records.assessment: She apologizes and withdraws the question: 'Sorry, never mind.' The English instead reassures him that there is no problem and loses her change of mind.
records.remedy: Use 'Sorry, never mind.'

highlights.text: it is really not a problem

records.jp: 「スターバスター発射用意！」
records.en: Taichi: "COMMENCE STARBUSTER FIRING PROCEDURE!"
comments: Hum, is that something that would cause a star to go nova? http://marathongame.wikia.com/wiki/Trih_Xeem This joke actually ties to how he's supposed to be the cause of all this. It's true if considering this as a parallel universe, literally; it's true in the sense of considering Taichi a Jesus disciple/equivalent; it's true in the sense that it's all a dream, if more hallucinated than anything. -GHS
records.assessment: The command is to prepare to fire, not to commence firing. The English advances the action from readiness to execution.
records.remedy: Use 'Prepare to fire Starbuster!'

highlights.text: COMMENCE STARBUSTER FIRING PROCEDURE

records.jp: 「……はっ、ここは？」
records.en: Taichi: "...huh, where is here?"
comments: See CCZDXC again. -GHS
records.assessment: He wakes and asks 'Where am I?' The English calques the Japanese demonstrative into a non-idiomatic English location question.
records.remedy: Use 'Where am I?'

highlights.text: where is here

records.jp: 「よかった。元に戻って」
records.en: Misato: "Oh, good. He returned to normal."
comments: Compare/contrast scene & words re: her glasses above. Is Misato being hypocritical too? -GHS
records.assessment: She addresses him directly with relief that he is back to normal. The English switches to third person and presents the return as a completed report rather than her immediate reaction.
records.remedy: Use 'Thank goodness. You're back to normal.'

highlights.text: He returned to normal

records.jp: 「ぺけくんは容姿のこと気にしすぎです。人間は心ですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Peke-kun, you worry too much about appearances. Humanity is in the heart!"
records.assessment: The canonical speaker is Misato, not Taichi. She tells him that he worries too much about looks and that what matters in a person is the heart; the English label is wrong and turns the latter reassurance into an abstract statement about humanity.
records.remedy: Restore Misato as speaker and express the contrast between appearance and inner character.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Peke-kun, you worry too much about appearances. Humanity is in the heart

records.jp: 『最初に会ったときは（そのあまりの醜さに）おどろかされましたけど』
records.en: Misato: 『Certainly when we first met you[r indescribable ugliness] did give me a sort of scare.』
comments: PCP above
...remembers. No, wait, he edits memories in near-real time to make things look worse. This is so blatant -GHS
records.assessment: The parenthetical supplies the remembered cause of the shock: his extreme ugliness. The English's bracketed insertion corrupts 'you' into an editorial substitution and leaves the displayed sentence mechanically malformed.
records.remedy: Integrate the parenthetical as a grammatical aside rather than an in-word bracket substitution.

highlights.text: you[r indescribable ugliness]

records.jp: 「好きで、好きで醜く生まれてきたわけじゃ……だから、せめて清潔にはしてるし……人を不快にさせないように……ひっく……」
records.en: Taichi: "It's not-, it's not like I was born ugly by choice... so I'm trying to be virtuous, or clean at least... so I won't make others uncomfortable... sob..."
comments: 清潔 See CCC4003, apparently leaving clean does not mean 'entering' baths. There's no way that first sentence's intended to sound as anything than a negative, but Tanaka has this bad habit of meaning exactly what he says, and there's technically no negative in there sentence. After all, his ugliness was in a certain sense his choice, if we take "his birth" to be the Mansion murders. -GHS
records.assessment: He says that because he did not choose to be born ugly, he at least keeps himself clean so as not to make others uncomfortable. 'Virtuous' introduces a moral claim absent from the concrete hygiene statement.
records.remedy: Keep the concession focused on cleanliness rather than virtue.

highlights.text: virtuous, or clean at least

records.jp: そっと抱きしめてくれた。
records.en: I am gently hugged closed.
records.assessment: She gently hugs him. The English uses a malformed passive, suppresses the acting subject, and adds 'closed,' which is not a valid completion of 'hugged.'
records.remedy: Use 'She gently hugged me.'

highlights.text: I am gently hugged closed

records.jp: 埋めまくった。
records.en: submerged it fully.
records.assessment: The suffix marks doing the burying emphatically or repeatedly. 'Submerged it fully' changes the action and replaces the source's excessive iterative force with a terminal degree.
records.remedy: Express that he buries his face in it repeatedly or with abandon.

highlights.text: submerged it fully

records.jp: 果てしなく、やわっこい。
records.en: Soffness' without end.
comments: He's reminded of his URMOM, and he's finally crying in her arms. -GHS
records.assessment: The line is an emphatic fragment meaning endlessly soft. The English changes the adjective into a misspelled noun and adds a stray possessive apostrophe, leaving the fragment mechanically corrupt.
records.remedy: Use a stylized but grammatical form such as 'Endlessly soffft.'

highlights.text: Soffness' without end

records.jp: もぞもぞと動く俺の顔に、先輩はこそばゆげに喉を鳴らした。
records.en: To the tickling of my squirmingly moving head Senpai emitted throaty moans.
records.assessment: As his face moves around, she makes a sound in her throat as though tickled. The English changes face to head, makes the tickling an external agent, and inflates one throat sound into plural 'moans.'
records.remedy: Keep his moving face, her ticklish reaction, and a singular throat sound distinct.

highlights.text: tickling of my squirmingly moving head Senpai emitted throaty moans

records.jp: 「……不意に近づかれると、ドキッとしてしまうんですよ」
records.en: Misato: "...if you suddenly get close to someone, of course their hearts will go all 'badum'!"
comments: Technically it's just "I get flustered if you get close to me", but see CCB2011: it's nearly what he says to Youko word for word. This is the whole point. -GHS
records.assessment: She admits that when he suddenly comes close, her own heart skips a beat. The English generalizes the confession into what happens to unspecified people and adds 'of course,' erasing the personal subject and force of the disclosure.
records.remedy: Keep her as the person startled when he comes close.

highlights.text: if you suddenly get close to someone, of course their hearts

records.jp: 「世話が焼けますねー」
records.en: Misato: "You would just burn yourself up without the care of others!"
comments: Given big themes of the game include both him needing other people's help and stuff burning on fire due to Hell, overliteral is correct. -GHS
records.assessment: The idiom means that he is a handful or requires looking after. The English literalizes the verb 'burn,' makes him burn himself, and invents a counterfactual dependence on other people's care.
records.remedy: Use 'You really are a handful' or an equivalent care-taking idiom.

highlights.text: You would just burn yourself up without the care of others

records.jp: 焼いて焼いてー、と心の中では思う。
records.en: But in my heart of hearts my only thoughts are, "burn, buuurn!"
comments: Like he heard that thing about his looks wrong in his second attempt... interesting considering Witches, see CCD2002. Not the typical moe/burn pun, so nothing there. -GHS
records.assessment: His internal repetition asks her to keep fussing over or caring for him while extending the preceding burn-wordplay. The English retains only literal burning, so the primary care-taking desire disappears.
records.remedy: Preserve both the request for care and, if possible, the burn pun.

highlights.text: burn, buuurn!

records.jp: 「すぐに荷物まとめて、お宅にうかがいます」
records.en: Taichi: "I shall gather my luggage posthaste, and pay visit to Your house."
comments: See CCB2002, more Touko. -GHS
records.assessment: He says he will pack immediately and come to her house. The English omits the article required by 'pay a visit' and arbitrarily capitalizes 'Your,' corrupting the mock-formal register.
records.remedy: Use 'pay a visit to your house' or simply 'come to your house.'

highlights.text: pay visit to Your house

records.jp: 「実は、ずっと寂しかったんです……ありがとう、ぼくの姉さん……いや、姫ねえさまと呼ばせていただきます」
records.en: Taichi: "The truth is, I have been lonely for so long... this young boy thanks you, my nee-san... no, I shall be calling you hime-nee-sama!"
comments: See CCC0000, Ichiko. -GHS
records.assessment: He thanks his new big sister after confessing his loneliness. The English turns the first-person pronoun into an added third-person self-description, producing affected and ungrammatical narration not supported by the line.
records.remedy: Keep the direct first-person thanks before the escalating sister title.

highlights.text: this young boy thanks you

records.jp: あさっての方角を向いて、先輩は呟いた。
records.en: So muttered Senpai when faced with this derailing of thoughts.
comments: See CCA0003, CCA0027; Nanaka and Kiri also have difficulties dealing with these things. -GHS
records.assessment: She mutters while looking off in a completely unrelated direction, expressed through the idiom 'toward the day after tomorrow.' The English removes the physical action and replaces it with an abstract derailment of thoughts.
records.remedy: Describe her looking off in a random or entirely unrelated direction as she mutters.

highlights.text: So muttered Senpai when faced with this derailing of thoughts

records.jp: とかやってるうちに、そろそろ夜がやってくる。
records.en: And while chatting about this and that, soon the night will descend at our backs.
records.assessment: Night is drawing near while they are occupied with all this. The English narrows their actions to chatting and adds the unsupported spatial image that night descends behind them.
records.remedy: Say that while they are doing all this, night is beginning to fall.

highlights.text: while chatting about this and that
descend at our backs

records.jp: 「はあ」
records.en: Taichi: "Sir!"
records.assessment: The source is a subdued acknowledgement or noncommittal response. The English changes it into a crisp form of address, altering the speech act and tone.
records.remedy: Use a subdued acknowledgement such as 'Yeah' or 'Uh-huh.'

highlights.text: Sir!

records.jp: やがて先輩の顔がふっとほころぶ。
records.en: Eventually, Senpai's face puffs into the broadest of smiles.
comments: The term also means "to come apart at the seams". Three guesses. -GHS
records.assessment: Her face gently relaxes or opens into a smile. 'Puffs' gives the wrong physical motion, while 'the broadest' adds an unsupported superlative.
records.remedy: Describe her face softly relaxing into a smile without the superlative.

highlights.text: puffs into the broadest of smiles

records.jp: 「いえ、帝国軍人として当然であります」
records.en: Taichi: "'Tis nothing, ma'am, it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire."
comments: Ah, Nations of the World. -GHS
records.assessment: He mock-formally says that helping is only natural for an imperial soldier. The English uses the adjective 'ordinary' as a noun and produces an ungrammatical military-register line.
records.remedy: Use 'only natural for a soldier of the Empire' or an equivalent mock-formal expression.

highlights.text: it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire

records.jp: 「でも残念ですが、今日はもう夜になってしまうのでした」
records.en: Misato: "It is too bad, but the day has already turned to night."
records.assessment: She says that the day is about to give way to night, explaining why the activity must end. The English states that night has already arrived, changing the temporal relation.
records.remedy: Say that it is already going to be night or is getting late.

highlights.text: the day has already turned to night

records.jp: 「女は度胸です」
records.en: Misato: "Women are pluck."
records.assessment: She invokes the maxim that a woman needs courage or nerve. The literal predicate construction is unidiomatic and grammatically malformed in English.
records.remedy: Use 'A woman's got to have guts' or another idiomatic courage maxim.

highlights.text: Women are pluck

records.jp: 「じゃ男は愛ですね」
records.en: Taichi: "Then men pluck them out."
comments: From "Men are charm, women are pluck", but he took off one kanji so he said "men are love". That doesn't really make sense in English, and the closest thing to this in English (men are from Mars, women are from Venus) doesn't work here. This isn't too far anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: His reply says that men are 'love,' creating a deliberate wordplay response to the preceding maxim. The English invents an action of plucking women out and removes the love term entirely.
records.remedy: Retain the assertion that men are love, with a note or adaptive pun if necessary.

highlights.text: men pluck them out

records.jp: 「先輩、ぼかぁ、ぼかぁ―――」
records.en: Taichi: "Senpai, pwease, pwease---"
comments: Childish "boku". It's on Wikipedia and everything(tm). Gah, combo breaker -GHS
records.assessment: He breaks off while repeating a childish deformation of the first-person pronoun. The English replaces the failed self-reference with an explicit repeated plea that is not in the line.
records.remedy: Preserve the broken childish 'I—I—' rather than adding a request.

highlights.text: pwease, pwease

records.jp: 顔面を片手で突き押され、よりさらに不細工になる俺。
records.en: With one hand she squeezes on my face, turning me ever more ugly.
comments: Curiously, see CCA0030. -GHS
records.assessment: She pushes or shoves his face away with one hand. The English changes the forceful pushing action into squeezing his face.
records.remedy: Describe her pushing his face away with one hand.

highlights.text: squeezes on my face

records.jp: あさっての方角に向けて、口笛を吹く。
records.en: So I whistled when faced with this derailing of thoughts.
comments: PCP CCA0010
records.assessment: He physically turns toward a completely unrelated direction and whistles, using the idiom 'toward the day after tomorrow.' The English removes the physical direction and replaces it with an abstract derailment of thought.
records.remedy: Describe him whistling while looking off in a random or unrelated direction.

highlights.text: when faced with this derailing of thoughts

records.jp: 「オ・ト・コ・ノ・コ、なんですものねー」
records.en: Misato: "Be-ca-use-you-are-a-boooy, are you!"
comments: This is funnier considering "otokonoko" is sort of gaining traction as meaning "transvestite" in contemporary anime parlance (they have one). -GHS
records.assessment: She pointedly concludes that this is because he is a boy. The English appends an inverted interrogative tag to the already stated cause, producing the wrong syntax and rhetorical force.
records.remedy: Use an emphatic assertion such as 'Because you're a boy, after all.'

highlights.text: are you!

records.jp: 「わたしも、そのくらいの価値はある女だったってことですかね」
records.en: Misato: "Would that mean I, myself, am a woman with about that kind of value?"
comments: Misato the traitor. See below: -GHS
records.assessment: She wonders whether the past incident means she was a woman worth that much to him. The English shifts the marked past-tense reflection into a present-tense statement about her general identity.
records.remedy: Preserve the retrospective 'was a woman worth that much' framing.

highlights.text: am a woman with about that kind of value

records.jp: 「いやいやいや、虚無僧ではありますが無節操などには！」
records.en: Taichi: "NoNnoNno, I may be a Komusou, but unprincipled, really!"
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komus%C5%8D -GHS
records.assessment: He protests that although he may be a komusou, he is not indiscriminate. The ellipsis-dependent Japanese denial is not completed in English, leaving an ungrammatical phrase that can read as an admission of the accusation.
records.remedy: Complete the denial: 'I may be a komusou, but I'm not indiscriminate.'

highlights.text: but unprincipled, really

records.jp: 作業していた。
records.en: working, blue collar,
records.assessment: The source simply says that she was working. The English adds a blue-collar social or occupational characterization that is absent and does not fit the linked sentence.
records.remedy: Use only 'working' or 'still working.'

highlights.text: blue collar

records.jp: 靴の底から熱が伝わる。
records.en: The heat reports through the soles of the shoes,
records.assessment: Heat travels or is transmitted through the soles of his shoes. 'Reports' cannot take this physical-transfer sense and corrupts an otherwise simple sensory statement.
records.remedy: Use 'The heat comes through the soles of my shoes.'

highlights.text: reports

records.jp: 乾いた音がして、足下にステンレスの杖が転がってきた。
records.en: There was a dry sound, and a stainless steel crutch tumbled at his foot.
records.assessment: The stainless-steel cane comes rolling to the narrator's feet, as marked by the deictic motion toward him. The English instead places it at the fallen person's foot.
records.remedy: Say that the cane rolled to my feet.

highlights.text: his foot

records.jp: 「あ、すいません、平気です」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "Ah, thanks. I'm alright."
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "Ah, thanks. I'm alright."
records.assessment: The speaker apologizes before saying he is fine. Both conditional English branches replace that apology with thanks, changing the speech act.
records.remedy: Use 'Ah, sorry. I'm alright' in both branches.

highlights.text: thanks
thanks

records.jp: 二番目の理由は、顔とのギャップなんだろう。ちぇっ。
records.en: Reason number two it's how girly my face naturally looks. Dammit.
comments: ...when they actually caught this. -GHS
records.assessment: The second reason is presumably the contrast or mismatch between the white hair and his face. The English replaces that relational contrast with an unsupported categorical claim that his face naturally looks girly.
records.remedy: Preserve the contrast with his face without inventing a specific feminine appearance.

highlights.text: how girly my face naturally looks

records.jp: そして、お仲間、か。
records.en: And then, a close friend, maybe.
comments: Many many many meanings. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator recognizes the other person as a fellow member of the same group or category. The English instead invents a close personal friendship.
records.remedy: Use 'one of us' or 'a fellow member' without adding intimacy.

highlights.text: close friend

records.jp: 「やばいよー、鍛えろよー」
records.en: Taichi: "That's baaad! Discipline, man!"
comments: Technically "you should train it". -GHS
records.assessment: The imperative tells him to train or exercise the leg. 'Discipline' changes the requested physical action into an abstract concept.
records.remedy: Use 'Train it' or 'Exercise it.'

highlights.text: Discipline

records.jp: 「ほとんど動かないんだって。一応、手動でちょっとやってるけど」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "Told you can't really move it. I can sort of of work it on manual, let's say."
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "Told you can't really move it. I can sort of of work it on manual, let's say."
records.assessment: Both branches contain the same duplicated preposition, creating a clear mechanical grammar error in the statement that he works it manually a little.
records.remedy: Remove the duplicated 'of' in both branches.

highlights.text: sort of of
sort of of

records.jp: 「おまえ、さては自虐ネタの使い手だな」
records.en: Taichi: "You're very good at making masochistic jokes."
comments: Since Taichi is the masochist, what he actually means is easy to tell; even more so considering the joke he just made wasn't entirely at his expense. Taichi, after all, took it sorta seriously. -GHS
records.assessment: The compound identifies self-deprecating jokes made at one's own expense. 'Masochistic' substitutes a different psychological or sexual category.
records.remedy: Use 'self-deprecating jokes.'

highlights.text: masochistic

records.jp: 「なんだよそれ」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "What's that even that."
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "What's that even that."
comments: He sorta-recognizes what Taichi just said. -GHS
records.assessment: Both branches garble the simple question with a duplicated demonstrative and incorrect punctuation.
records.remedy: Use 'What even is that?' or 'What the hell is that?' in both branches.

highlights.text: What's that even that.
What's that even that.

records.jp: 「あの学校、いいとこだといいなあ」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "Be nice if that's school's nice, innit."
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "Be nice if that's school's nice, innit."
comments: Sudden change of topic again, borderline avoidance. Interestingly Nanaka-ish. -GHS
records.assessment: Both branches contain a malformed double possessive in the hope that the school is a nice place.
records.remedy: Use 'I hope that school's a nice place' in both branches.

highlights.text: that's school's nice
that's school's nice

records.jp: 「やべぇーっ、エロいかぁーっ、そりゃますますお盛んな人生が開けてきたーっ！！」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "No waaay! Lewd too! Wow, my life's getting more and more prosperous!"
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "No waaay! Lewd too! Wow, my life's getting more and more prosperous!"
comments: Ouch. -GHS
records.assessment: In both branches the neutral 'prosperous' loses the contextually sexual force of the vigorous or active life now opening before him.
records.remedy: Use a phrase such as 'a more and more active sex life' while retaining the boastful wordplay.

highlights.text: prosperous
prosperous

records.jp: 「……その前に、まちこ先生のデータくれな」
records.en:
IF $loop == 0 Boy: "...before that,, hand over that Machiko-sensei databank."
IF $loop != 0 Shinkawa: "...before that,, hand over that Machiko-sensei databank."
records.assessment: Both conditional branches contain the same duplicated comma in an otherwise accurate request for the data first.
records.remedy: Remove one comma from each branch.

records.jp: 「人種は違うが頑張ろう、ジャパニーズ」
records.en: Taichi: "Our races are different but let's do our best, you Nipponjin!"
comments: ~♪ -GHS
records.assessment: The source comically addresses the other man with the English loanword 'Japanese.' Replacing that code-switch with an untranslated Japanese noun reverses the marked register and obscures the setup for the reply.
records.remedy: Address him as 'Japanese' or 'Mr. Japanese' in English.

highlights.text: Nipponjin

records.jp: ここで赤い薔薇をさした花瓶のアップ。やがて花は根本で折れ、静かに落ちる。
records.en: Close-up of a vase containing a red rose here. Soon afterwards, cut the flower at its base, that it falls to the ground in silence.
records.assessment: The flower itself eventually breaks at the base and falls quietly. The English turns this into an instruction for someone to cut it, inventing an agent and changing the action.
records.remedy: Say that the flower breaks at the base and quietly falls.

highlights.text: cut the flower at its base

records.jp: これはゆゆしき問題ですぞ、校長！
records.en: The tips of my fingers fired towards Miki's ass with the speed of lightning, but merely grazed and couldn't seize the substance.
comments: The three lines are split on the console version anyway since the font is way bigger, so character limit's no issue here. -GHS
records.assessment: The English translates a separate prefatory comment instead of the bound source line. It entirely omits the exclamation that this is a grave matter addressed to the principal and substitutes an unrelated action.
records.remedy: Translate the bound source as a mock-formal declaration that this is a grave matter, Principal.

highlights.text: The tips of my fingers fired towards Miki's ass with the speed of lightning, but merely grazed and couldn't seize the substance.

records.jp: 『避妊するから』
records.en: Sakuraba: 『IT'S CONTRACEPTIVE!』
comments: SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker promises to use contraception or protection. The English instead applies the adjective 'contraceptive' to an unspecified thing and loses the promised action.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll use protection.'

highlights.text: IT'S CONTRACEPTIVE

records.jp: 避妊すると言いつつ肉体関係を強要してくる、桜庭自体を否認したかった。
records.en: If Sakuraba was going to force carnal relationships while saying it's contraceptive, then I wanted to reject him from the very body.
comments: 自体 means "himself" as in "Sakuraba himself", but the sarcastic undertone of the overliteral, as often in Tanaka, can't be missed. Taichi rejecting this Broken Sakuraba - who's himself in a similar Pattern to what Taichi has - is itself interesting, but there's more. I suppose the anti-gay message is sorta unsubtle, but the real point is the rejection of contraceptives as the excuse for sexual relationships. That's pretty damn Catholic, considering. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator wants to deny or reject Sakuraba himself for forcing a sexual relationship under that pretext. The English misparses 'himself' as a phrase about rejecting him from a body.
records.remedy: Say that he wanted to deny Sakuraba's very existence or reject Sakuraba himself.

highlights.text: reject him from the very body

records.jp: 日記にひどいことを書いたせいか？
records.en: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?
comments: See CCA0012, exact same word that referred to what he did to Touko. Touko's name conspicuous in its absence. He was keeping a diary BEFORE his exchange diary with Yusa, meaning it's not his exchange with her that causes this. In short, Sakakibara is most the likely source. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether this is happening because of the cruel things he wrote. The English drops the causal predicate and leaves an incomplete question about the things themselves.
records.remedy: Use 'Is it because of the mean things I wrote in my diary?'

highlights.text: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?

records.jp: そりゃ微妙に違うか？
records.en: Aren't they only slightly different?
comments: Well, they are. I hope I don't need to make tedious explanations as to why the ancient Code of Hammurabi (and its refinement of Eye for an Eye) isn't metaphorically incompatible with a Christian Divine Retribution. -GHS
records.assessment: The source singles out the immediately preceding comparison as perhaps slightly off. The English instead compares the whole plural set to one another and reverses the tentative self-correction.
records.remedy: Use 'Maybe that one's a little different?'

highlights.text: Aren't they only slightly different?

records.jp: 俺はと言うと、どこかで夢だと知りつつも、パニック状態になっていた。
records.en: Whatever it may be, while I still know it's a dream that came from somewhere, I still slip into panic mode.
comments: Interesting to notice that he's having a flashback/dream about a dream, so it's legitimate to compare this to the previous dream seen in the route with Nanaka. -GHS
records.assessment: He knows at some level that this is a dream but panics anyway. The English attaches 'somewhere' to the dream's origin, inventing a provenance instead of locating his awareness.
records.remedy: Use 'though somewhere in my mind I knew it was a dream.'

highlights.text: a dream that came from somewhere

records.jp: 一発がうまくクリーンヒット。
records.en: One of them is a skillful clean hit.
comments: See CCA0002 -GHS
records.assessment: One blow successfully lands as a clean hit. The English turns the adverb of successful contact into a claim that the hit itself is skillful.
records.remedy: Use 'One of them lands cleanly.'

highlights.text: skillful

records.jp: 仰臥して意識を失った桜庭の股間が、不意に暴発した。
records.en: Supine, his sense lost, Sakuraba's nethers unconsciously discharged.
