records.assessment: The source describes evidence that someone or something tried to bite at the wound. The English substitutes an internal desire, which the visible marks cannot establish.
records.remedy: Use 'It looked as if something had tried to bite at the wound.'

highlights.text: wanted to bite off

records.jp: 言葉にならない。
records.en: Language that doesn't become words.
records.assessment: The English is incoherent and changes the first-person inability into an abstract statement about language. The source says he cannot put it into words.
records.remedy: Use 'I can't put it into words.'

highlights.text: Language that doesn't become words

records.jp: 先輩がふっと微笑む。
records.en: Senpai puffs into a smile.
records.assessment: The source says Senpai smiles softly or suddenly. 'Puffs into' describes neither the motion nor the expression and creates an unsupported physical image.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai smiles softly.'

highlights.text: puffs into a smile

records.jp: 「軽蔑するようなことは、なにもしてませんよ、あなたは」
records.en: Misato: "You did nothing that is worthy of despise, you did not."
records.assessment: The complement is ungrammatical and the doubled ending is a literal calque. The source reassures him that he has done nothing she would despise.
records.remedy: Use 'You haven't done anything I'd despise you for.'

highlights.text: worthy of despise

records.jp: 「おりこうさんなので、不問とします」
records.en: Misato: "You are a well-behaved kid, so I shall overlooking all that."
comments: Translation: "nice doggy, I'll pretend you didn't shit on the carpet". -GHS
records.assessment: A modal auxiliary must take the base verb. The source says she will let the matter pass because he was good.
records.remedy: Use 'I shall overlook it.'

highlights.text: shall overlooking

records.jp: より上位の感情が、あったから。
records.en: Because... that high-ranking emotion was there.
records.assessment: The source describes a higher-order or more powerful emotion. 'High-ranking' incorrectly treats the feeling as occupying an official rank.
records.remedy: Use 'Because there was a higher-order emotion.'

highlights.text: high-ranking emotion

records.jp: 「くすぐったいですー」
records.en: Misato: "That tickleees!"
records.assessment: The demonstrative subject requires a third-person singular verb. The elongated spelling can preserve delivery, but the verb lacks agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'That tickleees!'

highlights.text: That tickleees

records.jp: 「ご、ごめんなさい……緊張して」
records.en: Taichi: "I, I am sorry... nervousness."
records.assessment: The English leaves an isolated noun and omits the predicate. The source apologizes and explains that he is nervous.
records.remedy: Use 'S-sorry... I'm nervous.'

highlights.text: nervousness

records.jp: 「包帯まくのへたっぴですねー」
records.en: Misato: "You are crap at making bandages are you."
comments: Slangy. Notice the old bandages aren't described as crap, so it's far from impossible the actual nurse did them. -GHS
records.assessment: The sentence is ungrammatical, and the source criticizes his skill at wrapping a bandage, not making bandages.
records.remedy: Use 'You're really bad at wrapping bandages, aren't you?'

highlights.text: crap at making bandages are you

records.jp: そんな幸せな時間が。
records.en: That hours of this blessed happiness,
records.assessment: The source refers to such a happy time in the singular. The English has incompatible demonstrative and number marking and adds an unsupported 'blessed.'
records.remedy: Use 'Such a happy time...'

highlights.text: That hours of this blessed happiness

records.jp: あったんだ―――
records.en: would even exist---
records.assessment: The source completes the recollection with the factual past 'there was.' The English changes it into a hypothetical or future-in-the-past claim.
records.remedy: Use '...really existed—'

highlights.text: would even exist

records.en: Taichi: "Ah!"
records.assessment: The canonical source assigns the exclamation to Misato. The English speaker label instead gives it to Taichi, disrupting the following exchange.
records.remedy: Assign the line to Misato.

highlights.text: Taichi:

records.jp: 思考が麻痺した。
records.en: It paralyzed thoughts.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator's thinking went numb or froze. The English invents an external 'it' as agent and uses an unnatural plural object.
records.remedy: Use 'My thoughts froze.'

highlights.text: It paralyzed thoughts

records.jp: 散乱した資材の間に、転がっていた。
records.en: It had fallen down when the pile of materials fell.
records.assessment: The source says the phone was lying among the scattered materials. The English invents a pile, a fall, and a causal time relation that the sentence does not state.
records.remedy: Use 'It was lying among the scattered materials.'

highlights.text: had fallen down when the pile of materials fell

records.jp: 俺がそうしているように、先輩もまたちっぽけな携帯電話に、大きなものを託しているのかもしれない。
records.en: Just like what I do, so Senpai might just be entrusting something great to this tiny little portable telephone.
records.assessment: The comparative construction is ungrammatical. The source says Senpai may entrust something important to her small phone just as the narrator relies on something himself.
records.remedy: Use 'Just as I do, Senpai may also be entrusting something important to that tiny phone.'

highlights.text: Just like what I do, so

records.jp: 「ご苦労様。これでチャラですね」
records.en: Misato: "I very much appreciate it. With this, your debt is forgiven."
records.assessment: The source says the exchange makes them even or wipes the slate clean. The English imposes a one-way creditor-debtor relation and has Senpai forgive his debt.
records.remedy: Use 'With this, we're even.'

highlights.text: your debt is forgiven

records.jp: 「……わかりません。可能性はありますよ」
records.en: Taichi: "...I do not know. There is the possibility."
records.assessment: The definite noun phrase is an unnatural calque. The source says recurrence is possible.
records.remedy: Use 'It's possible.'

highlights.text: There is the possibility

records.jp: 言葉を解することもないはずなのに。
records.en: But I expect I wouldn't have been able to interpret language.
records.assessment: The source says the altered or bestial state should not even understand language. The English assigns the inability to the ordinary first-person narrator and recasts comprehension as interpretation.
records.remedy: Use 'Even though that thing shouldn't have been able to understand words.'

highlights.text: I expect I wouldn't have been able to interpret language

records.jp: そうに決まってる。
records.en: That is what I decide it is.
records.assessment: The source asserts certainty that it must have been coincidence. The English instead describes a conscious personal decision to label it that way.
records.remedy: Use 'It had to be a coincidence.'

highlights.text: That is what I decide it is

records.jp: 言葉が途切れる。
records.en: Words interrupt.
records.assessment: The source says his words break off. The English uses an intransitive event with the wrong verb relation, suggesting that words interrupt something else.
records.remedy: Use 'My words break off.'

highlights.text: Words interrupt

records.jp: あまりにも静かで、部活や授業の気配さえ消えていて。
records.en: Excessively quiet, that even the signs of club activities and classes disappear.
comments: COUGH COUGH COUGH COOOOOOUGH. -GHS
records.assessment: The result construction is ungrammatical and shifts the surrounding past description into present tense. The source says it was so quiet that even signs of classes and club activity had vanished.
records.remedy: Use 'It was so quiet that even the sounds of classes and club activities had vanished.'

highlights.text: Excessively quiet, that

records.jp: 世界が黄昏に満ちているのだから、白を基調とする室内は抗うことなく従属し、胎内に抱く二つの異物を生贄とばかりに夕暮れに差し出すはずだった。
records.en: As the world was being filled by the dusk, the interior of the room with its white color as foundation would've subordinate it without a struggle, and offered to the twilight the two foreign elements held in it like would a womb, as scapegoats.
comments: Translation: "duuude we're getting colored orange due to the twilight!" This is still Taichi reflexively jumping into verbiagism as he can't handle the situation. Nice little scapegoating there, however. -GHS
records.assessment: The clause is ungrammatical and assigns no coherent subject or object. The source imagines the white room yielding to dusk and offering up the two alien presences inside it like sacrifices.
records.remedy: Recast the sentence with the room as the subject that yields to dusk and offers up its two occupants.

highlights.text: would've subordinate it

records.jp: 夕の色は、一日のどんな時間よりも印象に強い。
records.en: The color of evening leaves an impression stronger than any other time of a day.
comments: Kana Little Sister: "I walk in the sunset at Kana's pace. A slow pace. The orange glow of our surroundings feels like a different world." -GHS
records.assessment: The article and comparative time phrase are unidiomatic. The source says evening's color is more striking than that of any other time of day.
records.remedy: Use 'than any other time of day.'

highlights.text: any other time of a day

records.jp: すべてを異世界へと変えてしまう、おどろおどろしいもの。
records.en: Everything changes into a parallel world, a thing of hair-raising eeriness.
comments: Yes, that's the term. Dusk = parallel world. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls evening an eerie thing that transforms everything into another world. The English instead makes everything transform itself and leaves the following apposition malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'An eerie force that turns everything into another world.'

highlights.text: Everything changes into a parallel world

records.jp: 滅びの時間だ。
records.en: These are the hours of annihilation.
comments: Term often found to describe what happened to humanity. It's all but screamed. -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes dusk as a singular time or hour of destruction. The plural 'hours' changes the image and 'annihilation' overstates the compact noun.
records.remedy: Use 'It is the hour of destruction.'

highlights.text: hours of annihilation

records.jp: 世界が多重に見える時間。
records.en: Hours when the world can be seen in multiplex.
records.assessment: The source describes a time when the world looks layered or multiple. 'Seen in multiplex' is a technical calque that is not idiomatic visual description.
records.remedy: Use 'A time when the world appears layered.'

highlights.text: Hours when the world can be seen in multiplex

records.jp: 沈んで、翌日また何食わぬ顔でやってきた大陽が昨日のそれと同一であると、誰が保証できるのか。
records.en: After it has sunk, who can possibly ascertain whether the sun that in the next day again comes full of nonchalance on its face is identical to the one of yesterday?
comments: This used to have "sun" written with the wrong kanji. -GHS
records.assessment: The embedded relative clause has malformed English word order. The source asks whether tomorrow's nonchalantly returning sun can be guaranteed to be yesterday's.
records.remedy: Use 'the sun that returns so nonchalantly the next day.'

highlights.text: that in the next day again comes

records.jp: 毎日一回ずつ、世界が滅び去っているとしたら。
records.en: What if every day, one piece at a time, the world perishes and passes away.
comments: Cooooooooooooooooooooooooooooough, he gasped. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the world may perish once each day. The English mistakes the distributive count for gradual destruction piece by piece.
records.remedy: Use 'What if the world perishes once every day?'

highlights.text: one piece at a time

records.jp: 実際の世界と、人間の認識する世界が、同じだという保証はどこにもない。
records.en: Nowhere there is proof that the world of reality and the world that humans are aware of are one and the same.
comments: Still true because Heaven(tm). -GHS
records.assessment: The negative locative requires inversion in this construction. The source says there is no guarantee anywhere that reality and human perception coincide.
records.remedy: Use 'Nowhere is there any proof...'

highlights.text: Nowhere there is proof

records.jp: いつになく、世界が鮮明に見ていたからだ。
records.en: Because, unusually, I had seen the world so clearly.
comments: Should have something to do with his night eyes. Or the fact that it's currently like 9AM, so the orange isn't the growing twilight, it's the morning. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the world looked unusually vivid or clear at that moment. The English turns appearance into a completed act of seeing in past perfect.
records.remedy: Use 'Because the world looked unusually vivid.'

highlights.text: I had seen the world

records.jp: 「いちいち欠点や失敗を攻撃していたら、生きていけないです」
records.en: Misato: "Attacking every single fault and mistake one by one is not the way to live."
records.assessment: The source says people could not go on living if they attacked every flaw and failure. The English weakens that consequence into general advice about a preferable way to live.
records.remedy: Use 'If we attacked every flaw and mistake, we couldn't live.'

highlights.text: is not the way to live

records.jp: 涙のひとつも出れば、格好悪く格好がつくのだが。
records.en: If I shed but a single tear, I'll look as cool as a tool.
comments: He'd be unhip all the way to the hip. So uncool it heats up the room. -GHS
records.assessment: The source plays on looking uncool while nevertheless making a fitting dramatic picture. The English reverses 'uncool' to 'cool' and substitutes an unsupported rhyme with 'tool.'
records.remedy: Preserve the paradox that a tear would look pathetic but complete the scene.

highlights.text: look as cool as a tool

records.jp: 不思議と、激しい情動はなりをひそめていた。
records.en: Inexplicably, the extreme emotions have fallen silent.
comments: Because of the purple above, see CCC3025. -GHS
records.assessment: The surrounding narration is simple past, and the source says the intense emotion had curiously gone quiet. The English present perfect breaks the narrative time frame.
records.remedy: Use 'the intense emotions had fallen silent.'

highlights.text: have fallen silent

records.jp: 静かに時間がうつろう。
records.en: while hours abate in the quiet.
records.assessment: The source says time passes quietly. 'Abate' means diminish in intensity and does not describe hours moving on.
records.remedy: Use 'Time passes quietly.'

highlights.text: hours abate

records.jp: 「嫌われるのは嫌だから、傷つけたくもなく」
records.en: Taichi: "I don't want to be disliked, so I don't want to hurt anyone either."
comments: And he's learned his lesson, soon to forget it. -GHS
records.assessment: The source coordinates two personal fears: being disliked and hurting the addressee. The English makes the second a result of the first and broadens its object to anyone.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't want to be disliked, and I don't want to hurt you.'

highlights.text: so I don't want to hurt anyone

records.jp: 「……さっきのことは申し訳ないと思っていて」
records.en: Taichi: "...I think that what I did right then is unforgivable."
records.assessment: The source says he feels sorry or remorseful about what happened. Calling the act unforgivable intensifies the moral judgment and changes the confession's stance.
records.remedy: Use 'I feel terrible about what happened earlier.'

highlights.text: unforgivable

records.jp: 「でも自制する自信はなくて」
records.en: Taichi: "But I have no self-confidence in my self-control."
records.assessment: The doubled abstract noun phrase is an unnatural calque. The source says he lacks confidence that he can restrain himself.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm not confident I can control myself.'

highlights.text: no self-confidence in my self-control

records.jp: 遮って、言った。
records.en: Interjected, this she said:
records.assessment: The inversion is unidiomatic and leaves the participle without a clear subject. The source says she cut him off and spoke.
records.remedy: Use 'She cut me off and said,'

highlights.text: Interjected, this she said

records.jp: 「力仕事を手伝ってくれるんでしょう？」
records.en: Misato: "Would you help me with the heavy lifting?"
records.assessment: The source is a confident confirmation that he will help with the heavy work, not a tentative future request. The English weakens her decisive interruption.
records.remedy: Use 'You'll help me with the heavy lifting, won't you?'

highlights.text: Would you help me

records.jp: じんわりと、肋骨に包まれた胸の奥を、震わせた。
records.en: Gradually, the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver.
comments: ...aqua splash? -GHS
records.assessment: The English has number disagreement and invents a separate cage possessing ribs. The source says her words slowly made the depths of his rib-enclosed chest tremble.
records.remedy: Use 'Slowly, they made something deep inside my rib cage tremble.'

highlights.text: the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver

records.jp: 『いつもお一人なんですね』
records.en: 『You are always alone, are you.』
comments: CP CCA0016
records.assessment: The English tag question is malformed and punctuated as a statement. The source observes that he is always alone and seeks confirmation.
records.remedy: Use 'You're always alone, aren't you?'

highlights.text: are you.

records.jp: 『一緒に、部活しませんか？』
records.en: 『Will you not have club together with me?』
comments: CP CCA0016
records.assessment: The phrase is not idiomatic English and obscures the invitation to do club activities together.
records.remedy: Use 'Would you like to join me in the club?'

highlights.text: have club together

records.jp: 自分一人では解決できない悩みを、他人のたった一言が解消してしまう。
records.en: When I have worry that I cannot resolve alone, a single solitary word from another erases it.
records.assessment: The singular count noun lacks an article, and the construction needlessly turns the source's general statement into a temporal subordinate clause.
records.remedy: Use 'A single word from someone else can erase a worry I cannot solve alone.'

highlights.text: When I have worry

records.jp: そのために、人は互いに通じ合いたいと思うのだった。
records.en: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that.
records.assessment: The English is syntactically incoherent and adds a first-person belief frame. The source concludes that this is why people want to understand and connect with one another.
records.remedy: Use 'That is why people want to connect with one another.'

highlights.text: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that

records.jp: ……通信で。
records.en: ...with intercommunication.
records.assessment: The rare bureaucratic term is an unnatural choice for the source's plain 'communication' and disrupts the compact rhetorical sequence.
records.remedy: Use '...through communication.'

highlights.text: intercommunication

records.jp: 触れあおうと努力できる。
records.en: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort:
records.assessment: The source says people are capable of striving to reach or touch one another. The English changes ability and continuing effort into a desire already accomplished.
records.remedy: Use 'We can strive to reach one another.'

highlights.text: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort

records.jp: 「やっぱり組み立て、手伝ってもらうことにします」
records.en: Misato: "I knew it, I ended up needing to ask for help for the assembly."
records.assessment: The source says she has decided after all to have him help. The English recasts that choice as an externally imposed need.
records.remedy: Use 'I've decided to have you help me assemble it after all.'

highlights.text: I ended up needing to ask

records.jp: 気恥ずかしい。
records.en: I feel ashamed.
records.assessment: The source describes self-conscious embarrassment or bashfulness, not moral shame. The English gives the feeling an unjustified ethical weight.
records.remedy: Use 'I feel bashful.'

highlights.text: ashamed

records.jp: 先輩はにこにこと楽しそう。
records.en: Senpai smiles bright, looking like she's enjoying herself.
records.assessment: The verb requires an adverb in this construction. The source describes Senpai smiling brightly and looking pleased.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai smiles brightly.'

highlights.text: smiles bright

records.jp: 曜子さんは、俺のことを強力な人間だと言った。
records.en: Youko-chan said that I make for a very strong human being.
comments: Odd -san honorific changed to usual -chan in the console version, so it was another error. -GHS
records.assessment: The source uses the respectful adult address 'Youko-san.' The English changes it to the diminutive intimate suffix '-chan.'
records.remedy: Use 'Youko-san.'

highlights.text: Youko-chan

records.jp: 俺以外の人間は、えてして凄い。
records.en: Humans outside of me are so often amazing.
records.assessment: The literal spatial phrase is not idiomatic for 'people other than me.' The source says other people are often remarkable.
records.remedy: Use 'Other people are often amazing.'

highlights.text: Humans outside of me

records.jp: そんなこと……自分ではできない。
records.en: That is something... that cannot be done on one's own.
records.assessment: The source is a first-person admission that he cannot do those things himself. The English generalizes it into an impersonal universal claim.
records.remedy: Use 'I could never do those things myself.'

highlights.text: cannot be done on one's own

records.jp: そしてまだ、時間はあるのだ。
records.en: and even then, there will be time.
comments: Life After Death. -GHS
records.assessment: The source affirms that there is still time now. The English shifts it to a future after the previously named end point and adds 'even then,' reversing the temporal relation.
records.remedy: Use 'And there is still time.'

highlights.text: even then, there will be time

records.jp: 頭を下げて、
records.en: With a bow of her head,
records.assessment: The source's implicit subject is the narrator, who bows his head. The English assigns the bow to Senpai and reverses the action immediately before she touches him.
records.remedy: Use 'I bow my head,'

highlights.text: her head

records.jp: 先輩の手がぽんと置かれて、
records.en: Senpai makes her hands fall together with a pof,
records.assessment: The source says Senpai places one hand lightly on him. The English makes plural hands fall together, suggesting a clap and omitting the contact.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand comes to rest lightly on me,'

highlights.text: makes her hands fall together

records.jp: こそばゆくて、
records.en: awkwardly,
records.assessment: The source describes a ticklish, pleasantly bashful sensation. 'Awkwardly' describes manner rather than the narrator's tactile and emotional response.
records.remedy: Use 'feeling pleasantly ticklish,'

highlights.text: awkwardly

records.jp: やっと笑えて、
records.en: eventually smiling,
records.assessment: The source says the narrator was finally able to smile. The participial English omits ability and leaves the subject implicit.
records.remedy: Use 'I can finally smile,'

highlights.text: eventually smiling

records.jp: これで、もとどおり。
records.en: and with that, she is as she was.
records.assessment: The source leaves the restored state implicit: 'With that, back to normal.' The English specifically asserts that Senpai herself is restored, despite the sequence centering the narrator and their relationship.
records.remedy: Preserve the open reference with 'And with that, everything is back to normal.'

highlights.text: she is as she was

records.jp: 先輩の手が、カーテンをあける。
records.en: Senpai's hands open the curtains.
records.assessment: The source names a single hand. The English pluralizes it without support.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand opens the curtain.'

highlights.text: hands open

records.jp: 「え、結構出血が？」
records.en: Taichi: "Eh, but they're nice and bleeding?"
records.assessment: The adjective suggests approval and the progressive phrase is malformed. The source objects that the scrapes are bleeding quite a lot.
records.remedy: Use 'But they're bleeding quite a bit, aren't they?'

highlights.text: nice and bleeding

records.jp: 「幼なじみだった女の子が初潮を迎えたときって、ソレ系の恋愛漫画だったら生々しいイベントの一つや二つあったりなかったりしますよねっ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "On the occasion when a childhood friend that is to say a young girl is met by her menarche, the love manga of 'that' series might or might not have a scene or two of lurid graphicness!!!"
comments: Can't find what this series would be, and I'm even uncertain it's referring to any series in particular and it isn't just a trope of sorts. -GHS
records.assessment: The English is syntactically tangled and makes menarche an agent that meets the girl. The source jokes that romance manga about a childhood friend reaching menarche usually have one or two intimate incidents.
records.remedy: Recast the sentence with the girl as the one reaching menarche and the manga as the genre frame.

highlights.text: On the occasion when a childhood friend that is to say a young girl is met by her menarche, the love manga of 'that' series might or might not have a scene or two of lurid graphicness

records.jp: 意識が暗転する。
records.en: I theatrically part with consciousness.
records.assessment: The source simply says his consciousness goes dark and he blacks out. The English adds theatrical intent and replaces the abrupt loss with a voluntary-sounding euphemism.
records.remedy: Use 'I black out.'

highlights.text: theatrically part with consciousness

records.jp: ぱたりこ
records.en: Badump.
records.assessment: The source mimetic marks a light collapse or flop. 'Badump' conventionally suggests a heartbeat or heavy double impact and gives the wrong sound image.
records.remedy: Use a collapse sound such as 'Flop.'

highlights.text: Badump

records.jp: 寝台に寝かせられている。
records.en: I have been laid to sleep on a bed.
records.assessment: The source says the unconscious narrator has been laid on the infirmary bed. 'Laid to sleep' implies that someone deliberately induced sleep.
records.remedy: Use 'I've been laid on a bed.'

highlights.text: laid to sleep

records.jp: 「うーん」
records.en: Taichi: "Ooo-kay."
records.assessment: The source is a groan or thoughtful 'Hmm.' The English instead sounds like reluctant acceptance or a judgment that something is acceptable.
records.remedy: Use 'Hmmm.'

highlights.text: Ooo-kay

records.jp: 廊下を歩いていると、呼び止められた。
records.en: I walk down the corridor when I'm stopped by a call.
records.assessment: The passive phrase is unidiomatic, and the present tense disrupts the source's completed event. The source says someone called out and stopped him as he walked down the hall.
records.remedy: Use 'As I walked down the hall, someone called out and stopped me.'

highlights.text: I walk down the corridor when I'm stopped by a call

records.jp: 微妙な距離を置いて、ふたり。
records.en: It's a complex distance that they keep, these two.
comments: Ambiguous, but it's definitely between him and Misato. Remember he's out of the infirmary room because he knows Misato got injured. -GHS
records.assessment: The English is syntactically awkward and misreads the source's delicate or awkward interpersonal distance as a complex measurable distance.
records.remedy: Use 'The two of us keep an awkward distance between us.'

highlights.text: It's a complex distance that they keep, these two

records.jp: 「部活だったんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "I was at club 's all."
comments: He keeps eyes on Misato, so he knows where they were. -GHS
records.assessment: The clipped copular phrase is malformed even for colloquial speech. The source casually says he was at club activities.
records.remedy: Use 'I was at club, that's all.'

highlights.text: club 's all

records.jp: 「……どうしてまた？」
records.en: Tomoki: "...why again?"
comments: Odd question, in retrospect. -GHS
records.assessment: Here the source particle asks why he has started now or why this sudden return to club activities, not why he is repeating an earlier act.
records.remedy: Use 'Why now, all of a sudden?'

highlights.text: why again

records.jp: 「部活って、例の与太話？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Club activities, you mean that garbage?"
comments: Love how the term is "give fat speech", where the middle is the first kanji for Taichi. Well, now it's what he defines himself. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls it a tall tale or absurd nonsense. 'Garbage' is a harsher value judgment and loses the sense that Tomoki doubts the story's truth.
records.remedy: Use 'that tall tale' or 'that nonsense.'

highlights.text: garbage

records.jp: 群青学院放送局の開局。
records.en: The inauguration of the Gunjou Institute Broadcast Department.
records.assessment: The source names the opening of the academy's broadcasting station. The English changes the institution from an academy station to an institute department.
records.remedy: Use 'the launch of the Gunjou Academy Broadcasting Station.'

highlights.text: Gunjou Institute Broadcast Department

records.jp: 「与太じゃないよ、たぶん」
records.en: Taichi: "That wasn't garbage, maybe."
records.assessment: The source rejects the label in the present: it is not nonsense, probably. The English past tense makes the status sound concluded.
records.remedy: Use 'It's not garbage. Probably.'

highlights.text: wasn't garbage

records.jp: 「他に誰が参加してんの？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Who's else's participating?"
records.assessment: The interrogative and possessive endings are incorrectly combined.
records.remedy: Use 'Who else is participating?'

highlights.text: Who's else's

records.jp: 「部活と思えば自慰だって部活だ」
records.en: Taichi: "If I think it's club then even 'self-consolation' is club."
records.assessment: The source explicitly says masturbation for a crude joke about what can count as a club activity. The euphemism blunts the joke and changes the speaker's register.
records.remedy: Use the source's explicit term.

highlights.text: self-consolation

records.jp: 「……最近、いろいろと動いてるのは知ってたけど、部活とはね」
records.en: Tomoki: "...I only knew there's been moving about here and there of late, so it was about club."
records.assessment: The sentence is incoherent and reverses the discovery. The source says Tomoki knew Taichi had been active lately but had not realized those activities were for a club.
records.remedy: Use 'I knew you'd been busy with things lately, but I didn't realize it was club activity.'

highlights.text: I only knew there's been moving about here and there of late, so it was about club

records.jp: 「……え、意味わからん？」
records.en: Taichi: "...eh, but I don't get it?"
records.assessment: In context, Taichi asks whether Tomoki did not understand his joke. The English instead has Taichi declare that he himself does not understand.
records.remedy: Use 'What, you don't get it?'

highlights.text: I don't get it

records.jp: 「そりゃいいけど……」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, see, it's..."
records.assessment: The source concedes that joining would be fine before trailing into a reservation. The English omits that agreement and leaves a different filler fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'Sure, that's fine, but...'

highlights.text: Well, see, it's

records.jp: ぽつ、と言う。
records.en: Fragmentary, to say.
comments: ぽつぽつ. See CCA0028B. I think this refers to how he just drops it in with no context, but that script'll be different. -GHS
records.assessment: The English is not a sentence and does not convey that Tomoki says the warning quietly or abruptly in a small, isolated utterance.
records.remedy: Use 'He says it quietly.'

highlights.text: Fragmentary, to say

records.jp: 様子が変だったな。
records.en: Quite an odd behavior we had here.
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki was acting strangely. The English turns the observation into shared behavior by 'we' and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'He was acting strangely.'

highlights.text: Quite an odd behavior we had here

records.jp: 大人しかった蝉たちが、再びじわじわと鳴きはじめる。
records.en: The docile cicadas once more slowly but steadily being their cry.
comments: With the implication that the cicadas are not always crying. How much of this is to troll the first-time reader and how much of this is to troll further readers isn't so obvious, but I suspect it's strongly for the latter as well. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says cicadas that had quieted down gradually begin chirping again. 'Docile' means obedient, and 'being their cry' is grammatically incoherent.
records.remedy: Use 'The cicadas, quiet until now, gradually begin chirping again.'

highlights.text: docile cicadas once more slowly but steadily being their cry

records.jp: 「ちょいーす」
records.en: Shinkawa: "A'hoooy!"
comments: Mercifully the speaker tags are consistent with the flashback now... -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a casual contemporary greeting. The English supplies a nautical hail and changes the social flavor.
records.remedy: Use a casual greeting such as 'Yo.'

highlights.text: A'hoooy

records.jp: 「ああ、この鴻巣太一、たとえ免停になっても元気だけが取り柄だ」
records.en: Taichi: "Yup, this Kounosu Taichi here has being in spirits even in case of driving license suspension as his only redeeming feature."
comments: Continuing the driving thing from Yutaka's leg being on manual drive. -GHS
records.assessment: The English is grammatically incoherent. The source jokes that even with his license suspended, Kounosu Taichi's only virtue is that he stays cheerful.
records.remedy: Use 'Even with my license suspended, staying cheerful is my one good quality.'

highlights.text: has being in spirits even in case of driving license suspension as his only redeeming feature

records.jp: 「それを言うならこの谷崎豊だってそうだぜ？」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Ain't those the words that Tanizaki Yutaka here with his name written with the kanji for 'abundance' should be saying?"
comments: Just a bunch of seemingly tertiary characters through which run ludicrously overcomplicated overlapping metaphors that constitute significant portion of the story and themes well beyond what the characters themselves understand, pay no attention. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the same claim applies to Tanizaki Yutaka too. The English adds an unmarked kanji gloss and turns the parallel claim into a remark about who should say the words.
records.remedy: Use 'The same goes for this Tanizaki Yutaka, you know?'

highlights.text: with his name written with the kanji for 'abundance' should be saying

records.jp: 「谷崎は学校いつから来んの？」
records.en: Taichi: "So when are you coming, Tanizaki?"
records.assessment: The source asks when Tanizaki will start coming to school. The English omits the destination and can sound like a question about arriving at the current place.
records.remedy: Use 'When are you coming to school?'

highlights.text: when are you coming

records.jp: 「……ＯＫギブアップだ！　新川豊です、すいませんでした黒須さん」
records.en: Shinkawa: "...OK, it's a give-up! I'm Shinkawa Yutaka, my sincere apologies Kurosu-san!"
comments: EIGO WA TAISETSU DESU-nya!!1 because that's something they share. Anyway he's the first to break cover; is he also the first to realize what's going on? -GHS
records.assessment: The source uses the direct exclamation 'I give up.' The nominal construction is an unidiomatic calque.
records.remedy: Use 'Okay, I give up!'

highlights.text: it's a give-up

records.jp: 「こっから十分くらいかな」
records.en: Taichi: "I'd say from here ten minutes are enough."
comments: subteeext. -GHS
records.assessment: The source estimates the travel time as about ten minutes. The English treats minutes as an amount sufficient for an unstated task.
records.remedy: Use 'It's about ten minutes from here.'

highlights.text: ten minutes are enough

records.jp: 「姪がさー、やっぱ群青行くんだけどさ、いろいろ教えてやらんと」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Got a niece, ya know, 'course she goes to Gunjou, ya know, so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff."
records.assessment: The source says Shinkawa has to teach or explain various things to his niece. The English reverses the information flow and makes the niece teach him.
records.remedy: Use 'so I have to show her the ropes.'

highlights.text: so she's telling me lots and lots of stuff

records.jp: 俺の耳、
records.en: From my ears
records.assessment: The source begins a subject phrase, 'My ears...' The English changes it to a source prepositional phrase that cannot govern the continuing sentence.
records.remedy: Use 'My ears...'

highlights.text: From my ears

records.jp: 逃さない（ぐっ）。
records.en: could never run away (tahm!).
comments: See CCA0019. But doesn't ぐっ look like a mouth about to eat, teeth and all? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his ears do not miss information like that, followed by a thumbs-up gesture. The English makes the information run away and replaces the gesture with an opaque sound.
records.remedy: Complete the sequence as 'would never miss information like that. (Thumbs up.)'

highlights.text: could never run away (tahm!)

records.jp: 「マジごめん。姪、とか聞こえちゃった」
records.en: Taichi: "Seriously sorry. It seems I heard a word that sounded like 'niece'."
records.assessment: The source says he happened to hear the actual word 'niece.' The English suggests he may only have heard a similar-sounding word and adds uncertainty.
records.remedy: Use 'Sorry, I couldn't help overhearing "niece."'

highlights.text: a word that sounded like 'niece'

records.jp: 「しかしあれだ、一つ違いだと可愛いだろう」
records.en: Taichi: "But still she's gotta be cute even if there's that one thing that's off."
comments: Either because she's gotta have an ultramarine, or because of incest. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says a niece only one year younger must be cute. The English misreads the one-year age difference as a single flaw or thing that is wrong.
records.remedy: Use 'With only one year between you, she must be cute.'

highlights.text: even if there's that one thing that's off

records.jp: 「最初に言っておくと、そういう感情はないぞ。なんかそういう目で見ようとしても気色悪いだけだし」
records.en: Shinkawa: "I'm telling ya this from the start, I don't feel like that about her. Lookin' at me with those eyes you got 's just creepy."
comments: And doesn't he know about his eyes. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Shinkawa feels gross if he himself tries to look at his niece sexually. The English instead accuses Taichi of looking at Shinkawa in a creepy way.
records.remedy: Use 'Even if I try to see her that way, it just feels gross.'

highlights.text: Lookin' at me with those eyes you got 's just creepy

records.jp: 「わ、どうしたいきなり」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Wah! What's with the sudden?"
records.assessment: The adjective lacks a noun and does not form an idiomatic question. The source asks why Taichi suddenly shouted.
records.remedy: Use 'What was that all of a sudden?'

highlights.text: What's with the sudden

records.jp: 「黒須……かわいそうだが、マジなんだ」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Kurosu... maybe that's lame, but I'm serious."
records.assessment: The source expresses pity for Taichi before insisting that the statement is true. 'Lame' instead disparages the situation.
records.remedy: Use 'I feel sorry for you, Kurosu, but I'm serious.'

highlights.text: maybe that's lame

records.jp: 「本気で、妹みたいなもんなんだよ。同居してるし」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Seriously, she's kinda like a little sister, 's all. 's just cohabitation."
records.assessment: The source plainly says they live together. The formal term 'cohabitation' carries an adult-partner implication that conflicts with his insistence that she is like a sister.
records.remedy: Use 'We live together, too.'

highlights.text: cohabitation

records.jp: 同棲っ！？
records.en: Sharing the house?!
records.assessment: The source uses a loaded term for an unmarried couple living together, which drives the narrator's scandalized leap. The neutral paraphrase loses that implication.
records.remedy: Use 'Cohabiting?!' or another equivalently loaded reaction.

highlights.text: Sharing the house

records.jp: 「お、おい、そのロケーションには途轍もない何者かの意志が介在しているぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "W-, whoa, there must be the will of someone preposterous mediating in that location."
comments: God, of course, although first read is intended to be read that Taichi thinks it a miracle Yutaka has an Imouto-like being to him. Instead, it's about the miracle it'd take to turn someone like Yutaka into someone who'd be able to live with Kiri without making mincemeat of her. -GHS
records.assessment: The source imagines the will of some extraordinary being intervening in the situation. The English calls the person preposterous, uses the wrong sense of 'mediate,' and reduces the situation to a location.
records.remedy: Use 'the will of some extraordinary being is at work in that setup.'

highlights.text: someone preposterous mediating in that location

records.jp: 「今回、家ぐるみで引っ越してきたんだよ。俺の足のこともあるけど、そいつもちょっとアレでさ」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Lately, they've had to move, family and all. There's this foot of mine, 'course, and she's kinda like 'that' too."
comments: Unlike the Kiriharas, I don't think they physically moved the house, however. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the whole family moved here on this occasion. The English shifts it to an extended recent period and adds that the move was compulsory.
records.remedy: Use 'This time, the whole family moved here.'

highlights.text: Lately, they've had to move

records.jp: 一発で納得だ。
records.en: One blow and it's understood.
records.assessment: The source idiom means he understands immediately or from that single clue. The literal 'one blow' incorrectly evokes a physical strike.
records.remedy: Use 'That explains it immediately.'

highlights.text: One blow and it's understood

records.jp: 「あれ、そうするとチミは、姪子ちゃんのためにつきあいで転入みたいなもの？」
records.en: Taichi: "Ehhh, so Ol' Scratch here made a sort of a move-in for the sake of socializing with niecey-chan?"
comments: Ambiguous. Particularly that "chimi", which is just an odd 'kimi', but also means "mountain demon". Ol' Scratch should sound just as innocuous on first look, but... http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Scratch -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether Shinkawa transferred here to accompany his niece. The English invents the devilish nickname 'Ol’ Scratch' and renders the transfer and companionship relation incoherently.
records.remedy: Use 'So did you transfer here to accompany your niece?'

highlights.text: Ol' Scratch here made a sort of a move-in for the sake of socializing

records.jp: 「そうなるかな。いや、俺だって障害持ちですが」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Is that it, dunno. Nah, it's 'cause I'm disabled."
comments: This hints Taichi that Yutaka should be External Damage. -GHS
records.assessment: The source first concedes that this is roughly true, then notes that he himself also has a disability. The English turns the concession into uncertainty and the contrast into the sole cause.
records.remedy: Use 'I guess that's about right. Though I'm disabled too.'

highlights.text: Is that it, dunno. Nah, it's 'cause I'm disabled

records.jp: 「優しいお兄ちゃんだな、オイ」
records.en: Taichi: "You are a kind-hearted onii-chan, ol' one."
comments: Just an 'oi', but with "ol' scratch" up there... -GHS
records.assessment: The source ends with a rough attention-getter akin to 'hey' or 'man.' 'Ol’ one' is not an English form of address and suggests age without support.
records.remedy: Use 'You're a kind big brother, man.'

highlights.text: ol' one

records.jp: 「あの、姪の話になってから絡みっぱなしなんですけど？」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Uhm, didn't we kinda get all arguing since this turned to the niece?"
records.assessment: The source accuses Taichi alone of persistently picking at Shinkawa since the niece was mentioned. The English makes the arguing mutual and is grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'Haven't you been picking on me nonstop since my niece came up?'

highlights.text: didn't we kinda get all arguing since this turned to the niece

records.jp: 「羨望を集めるってのはそういうことだ」
records.en: Taichi: "That is what a gathering of envy is about."
records.assessment: The source says that being the object of others' envy entails this treatment. The English turns envy into something that gathers and obscures the social relation.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what happens when everyone envies you.'

highlights.text: a gathering of envy

records.jp: 「そうかあ～？　ずっと暮らしてるとさー、生理的なこととか見えてきてけっこうアレなんだぜ？」
records.en: Shinkawa: "Is it no～w? 'Cause we've been living together a long while now, so won't I have seen how she's very much 'that', on the physical level and all that?"
records.assessment: The English is incoherent and uses an inappropriate future-perfect question. The source says long cohabitation exposes bodily realities that make idealization difficult.
records.remedy: Use 'When you've lived together this long, you see all the bodily stuff, and it can be pretty off-putting.'

highlights.text: won't I have seen how she's very much 'that', on the physical level

records.jp: 「外見はいいとこもあるんだろうけど、欠点がバリバリ見えるから、たいしてきれいなモンにゃ思えないって感じか？」
records.en: Shinkawa: "For the outwards she's fine for sure, but, after those weak points tear through that nice and clean, I can't really think of 'er as something pretty can I?"
comments: See CCC3004. That's the majority of how we see her treat her precious onii-chan. Sure, she's tsundere, but, damn. -GHS
records.assessment: The clause is incoherent. The source says her good looks are offset by glaring flaws, so he cannot see her as especially beautiful.
records.remedy: Use 'She may look good, but her flaws are so obvious that I can't think of her as especially beautiful.'

highlights.text: after those weak points tear through that nice and clean

records.jp: 「食うものは食うし、出すものは―――」
records.en: Shinkawa: "What's for eating you eat, what's for expelling---"
comments: This sounds less scatological and more creepy considering the whole 'devour' metaphor. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she eats and excretes like anyone else. The English shifts to generic second person and forms neither clause idiomatically.
records.remedy: Use 'She eats, and what goes in has to come—'

highlights.text: What's for eating you eat, what's for expelling

records.jp: 「ぜひおまえとチェンジして姪子ちゃんとイチャイチャしたいものだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Wanting to completely replace you and getting all kissy-kissy with your niecey-chan, of course."
comments: It sounds like foreshadowing, until realizing Taichi doesn't believe Yutaka for one second. This is an accusation. -GHS
records.assessment: The source states Taichi's wish to switch places with Shinkawa. The English is a gerund fragment, and 'completely replace you' can imply erasing the person rather than trading roles.
records.remedy: Use 'I'd love to trade places with you and get cozy with your niece.'

highlights.text: Wanting to completely replace you

records.jp: 「現実は駄目だ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Reality is a waste..."
comments: No no no, you mean 'RIAJUU is KUSOGE-desu'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says reality is no good or unacceptable. Calling it a waste introduces a different evaluation.
records.remedy: Use 'Reality is no good...'

highlights.text: Reality is a waste

records.jp: エロ小説万歳。
records.en: Ero LN banzai.
comments: Damn straight! Fuck eroge! ...though I'm tempted to replace it with the console version's 二次元万歳 (2D banzai). This is Taichi not understanding that he's understood. It's self-troll, not troll. -GHS
records.assessment: The source celebrates erotic novels. The English narrows novels to light novels and leaves the celebratory word untranslated as Japanese apparatus.
records.remedy: Use 'Long live erotic novels.'

highlights.text: Ero LN banzai

records.jp: 「じゃまた今度にでも遊びに来てくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, maybe sometime I'll drop in to visit if you'll have me."
records.assessment: The source has Taichi invite Shinkawa to visit him another time. The English reverses visitor and host, making Taichi promise to visit Shinkawa.
records.remedy: Use 'Come visit me sometime.'

highlights.text: I'll drop in to visit

records.jp: そう言ったやつの目がテポドン級の節穴であることが、後に明らかになるのである。
records.en: How the guy who said this will be shown to have Taepodong-class knothole eyes will become clear afterwards.
comments: It's indeed the missile, which fits into the Nations of the World thing - "he has rockets big enough to threaten Japan", except it's not a sexual metaphor (somehow). but this refers to a type of creepy dolls called 'murder dolls' (殺人人形), who have eyes like knotholes. Chucky from Child's Play seems to be among the most popular, curiously. This ties to Taichi's backstory as a human doll, automatic behavior, Taichi's own eyes, and more. -GHS
records.assessment: The doubled future construction is ungrammatical and the literal 'knothole eyes' does not convey the idiom for spectacular blindness or bad judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'It would later become clear that his judgment was blind on a Taepodong scale.'

highlights.text: How the guy who said this will be shown to have Taepodong-class knothole eyes will become clear afterwards

records.jp: あれで没ってことは、どう攻めたらいいんだろう。
records.en: She failed that other one, so what is a good way of attacking now?
comments: "That one was rejected, so how do I attack this one" + "should I assault her somehow for saying that was rejected?" -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the previous script was rejected and wonders how to approach the next attempt. The English makes Senpai the person who failed, rather than the evaluator who rejected his work.
records.remedy: Use 'If that one was rejected, how should I approach the next?'

highlights.text: She failed that other one

records.jp: 手が動かない。
records.en: The hand does not move.
records.assessment: The source's implicit possessor is the narrator: his hand will not move. The definite phrase sounds like a detached or previously identified hand.
records.remedy: Use 'My hand won't move.'

highlights.text: The hand

records.jp: タンスの中から、着流しを取り出し、着替える。
records.en: Out of the dresser I produce a men's Kimono, and in Kinigashi style, casually dress with it.
comments: http://www.kimonoguide.com/dictionary/index3.html That seems to be a wearing style, not a specific type of kimono. Seems to be specifically used for "men's kimono", which are a specific type. -GHS
records.assessment: The English is ungrammatical, misspells the garment style, and treats the source's casual kimono outfit as both a separate men's kimono and a style applied afterward.
records.remedy: Use 'I take a casual kimono from the dresser and change into it.'

highlights.text: produce a men's Kimono, and in Kinigashi style, casually dress with it

records.jp: 「……文豪爆誕」
records.en: Taichi: "...the explosive birth of a master at literature."
comments: Continuing the Big Bang ref-- ehm, the metaphors. See below. -GHS
records.assessment: The source's comic proclamation is that a literary master has been born. 'Master at literature' is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'A literary master is born with a bang.'

highlights.text: master at literature

records.jp: そんなことをやっていると。
records.en: that is what I must do.
records.assessment: The source is a temporal transition, 'As I was doing that...' The English instead states an obligation and breaks the arrival sequence.
records.remedy: Use 'As I was doing that...'

highlights.text: that is what I must do

records.jp: 突如とした現れた着物の男に、友貴はびびったようだった。
records.en: Tomoki seemed to jitter in surprise at the sight of a man in Kimono materializing in front of him all of a sudden.
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki was startled by the kimono-clad man who suddenly appeared. 'Jitter' is not the reaction verb here, and 'materializing' adds a supernatural manner of arrival.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki looked startled when a kimono-clad man suddenly appeared.'

highlights.text: jitter in surprise at the sight of a man in Kimono materializing in front of him

records.jp: 「ほっとけ」
records.en: Taichi: "Vacate."
comments: Pissed at his 'face' remark. -GHS
records.assessment: The source colloquially means 'Leave me alone' or 'Shut up.' The formal command to leave a place has the wrong object and register.
records.remedy: Use 'Leave me alone.'

highlights.text: Vacate

records.jp: 「間違えた。なんて格好だ……」
records.en: Tomoki: "My mistake. I mean, what's that figure..."
comments: To be read literally, of course. -GHS
records.assessment: The source corrects 'face' to 'outfit' or 'getup.' 'Figure' refers to body shape or a person and misses the clothing joke.
records.remedy: Use 'I mean, what's with that outfit?'

highlights.text: what's that figure

records.jp: 「本当に間違いなのかそれは？」
records.en: Taichi: "Truly a mistake what you made?"
comments: Hmmm. Men's Kimono tend to be dark colors http://www.kimonoguide.com/mens/index.html so what he's seeing is dark clothes and really white hair; maybe he resembles some kind of Japanese monster? Or did he confuse him for someone else? -GHS
records.assessment: The question lacks an auxiliary and has malformed word order. The source asks whether the first remark was really a mistake.
records.remedy: Use 'Was that really a mistake?'

highlights.text: Truly a mistake what you made

records.jp: 「ジャパニーズソーセキでもある」
records.en: Taichi: "Also the habits of the Japanese Soseki."
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natsume_S%C5%8Dseki (though I can't find pictures of him in anything but the most boring Early Color Period Hollywood brown jacket) + the clothes of priesthood (general), 僧籍 souseki. He's wearing the clothes of a priest in order to get inspired to write the script for his 11AM sermon: now THAT is foreshadowing. -GHS
records.assessment: The source extends the 'Japanese kimono' phrasing into a self-identification with the literary figure Soseki. The English invents his habits and loses the speaker's comic claim.
records.remedy: Preserve the parallel as 'And Japanese Soseki, too.'

highlights.text: the habits of the Japanese Soseki

records.jp: 「ソーセキか……すごいな」
records.en: Tomoki: "Soseki then... nice pun."
comments: Making it a bit more obvious given how it's translingual and all. -GHS
records.assessment: The source merely reacts that Soseki is impressive. The English explicitly labels the preceding line a pun, adding interpretation to the dialogue.
records.remedy: Use 'Soseki, huh... impressive.'

highlights.text: nice pun

records.jp: 友貴はよりいっそう俺を尊敬したようだった。
records.en: Seems Tomoki's respect for me has further grown.
records.assessment: The surrounding narration reports a completed impression in the past. The present perfect breaks that time frame.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki seemed to respect me even more.'

highlights.text: has further grown

records.jp: 「いや……どうしたもこうしたも……これ、太一の分」
records.en: Tomoki: "Well... purpose, now, let's say, ah... here, Taichi, your part."
records.assessment: The English is incoherent. The source dismisses the question as nothing special and presents Taichi with his share.
records.remedy: Use 'Nothing special... Here, this is your share.'

highlights.text: purpose, now, let's say, ah... here, Taichi, your part

records.jp: ぐっ
records.en: Tahm!
comments: See CCA0018B. That changes things a little, considering he was less than sincere in there. -GHS
records.assessment: The source mimetic marks a forceful thumbs-up gesture completed by the following sentence. The opaque sound does not communicate that visible action.
records.remedy: Render the gesture directly, for example '(Thumbs up.)'

highlights.text: Tahm

records.jp: 「正確には倒れていた」
records.en: Tomoki: "Specifically, she has been fainting."
records.assessment: The source corrects the wording to say she was found collapsed or had collapsed. The English progressive describes an ongoing or repeated act of fainting.
records.remedy: Use 'More precisely, she was found collapsed.'

highlights.text: has been fainting

records.jp: 「あいつはハラキリ拳の使い手で、俺のカラデをもってしても倒すのは容易じゃないはずだ」
records.en: Taichi: "That one is the master of the Harakiri Fist, that even I with my Karade do not expect to make her part with her senses!"
comments: The word used here means both "to collapse" and "to [be] defeat[ed]" as in a fight. -GHS
records.assessment: The source has Taichi misunderstand 'collapsed' as 'defeated' and boast that even his Karade would struggle to defeat her. The English is ungrammatical and collapses the joke back into loss of consciousness.
records.remedy: Use 'Even with my Karade, she wouldn't be easy to defeat.'

highlights.text: that even I with my Karade do not expect to make her part with her senses

records.jp: サンダルをはいて、彼女の家に向かう。
records.en: I wear my sandals and I head towards her house.
records.assessment: The source narrates completed actions in sequence. The English shifts to simple present and uses 'wear' where 'put on' is required for the action.
records.remedy: Use 'I put on my sandals and headed for her house.'

highlights.text: I wear my sandals and I head

records.jp: 戻ってくると、まだ友貴がいた。
records.en: When I returned back, still Tomoki was there.
comments: Did he even go anywhere? -GHS
records.assessment: 'Returned back' is redundant, and the following adverbial inversion is unidiomatic. The source says Tomoki was still there when the narrator returned.
records.remedy: Use 'When I came back, Tomoki was still there.'

highlights.text: returned back, still Tomoki was there

records.jp: ないが。
records.en: That I don't have.
records.assessment: The fragment uses a demonstrative as though replying to a named object. The source adds the aside that he does not actually own a PC-98.
records.remedy: Use 'Though I don't have one.'

highlights.text: That I don't have

records.jp: 「嘘だと言ってくれよ、マイフレン」
records.en: Taichi: "Mai furendo, what you just told me must be a lie."
records.assessment: The source uses a comic English loan phrase meaning 'my friend.' The English transliterates the Japanese pronunciation rather than restoring the intelligible phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'Tell me it's a lie, my friend.'

highlights.text: Mai furendo

records.jp: パソコン少年の分際で。
records.en: When his social class is that of a PC guy!
comments: Ah, this is also recurring. -GHS
records.assessment: The source taunts him for not knowing despite being a computer kid. The English invents a social-class claim and loses the concessive rebuke.
records.remedy: Use 'And you call yourself a computer kid.'

highlights.text: social class is that of a PC guy

records.jp: 「……そういうものなのかな……いや、俺だって世代違うけど……」
records.en: Taichi: "...that you would say something like... nah I'm from the wrong generation too, but..."
records.assessment: The English trails into an incomplete complement and does not convey the narrator's wondering realization that this may simply be how things are for a different generation.
records.remedy: Use 'I guess that's just how it is... though I'm from a different generation too.'

highlights.text: that you would say something like

records.jp: 友貴はわりと恐いもの知らずだ。
records.en: Tomoki is comparatively unaffected by terror.
records.assessment: The source plainly describes Tomoki as fairly fearless. The clinical abstraction is an unnatural calque and obscures the character judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki is pretty fearless.'

highlights.text: comparatively unaffected by terror

records.jp: 寿命が縮んだ。
records.en: My life expectancy contracted.
records.assessment: The source idiom says the experience shortened his life. 'Contracted' is not the natural collocation for lifespan in this context.
records.remedy: Use 'That shortened my life.'

highlights.text: life expectancy contracted

records.jp: 「しかしあっつい」
records.en: Taichi: "But damn it's hot."
records.assessment: The source simply complains that it is hot. The English adds profanity and sharpens the voice.
records.remedy: Use 'But it's hot.'

highlights.text: damn

records.jp: 「水風呂にでも入るか」
records.en: Taichi: "Should I just take a cold bath."
comments: It's a flashback because he pretty much never does in the main story. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a question about taking a cold bath. The English closes it with a period, suppressing the interrogative force.
records.remedy: Use a question mark: “Should I take a cold bath or something?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Should I just take a cold bath."

records.jp: あまりの気持ちよさにちょっと向こう側に行っていた意識を、ドアベルが呼び戻す。
records.en: The doorbell called back an awareness that had nearly left for the pleasant comfortableness of the other side.
records.assessment: The source says extreme comfort has let his consciousness drift slightly toward the other side, before the doorbell calls it back. The English’s “pleasant comfortableness” and “awareness ... left for ... the other side” are malformed and blur that sequence.
records.remedy: Use “The doorbell called back the consciousness that had drifted slightly toward the other side in my extreme comfort.”

highlights.text: The doorbell called back an awareness that had nearly left for the pleasant comfortableness of the other side.

records.jp: 「やべ」
records.en: Taichi: "No way."
comments: Though it's not exactly an uncommon wording, here it's sorta Yutaka's catchphrase. -GHS
records.assessment: The source interjection is alarmed self-talk akin to “Oh crap.” “No way” instead expresses disbelief or refusal.
records.remedy: Use “Oh crap.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "No way."

records.jp: 着物を身につけて、玄関に。
records.en: With a Kimono over me, I head to the entryway.
records.assessment: The source says he puts on a kimono and heads to the entrance. “With a Kimono over me” is unidiomatic and treats the garment as merely draped over him.
records.remedy: Use “I put on a kimono and headed to the entryway.”

highlights.text: With a Kimono over me, I head to the entryway.

records.jp: 「その極道みたいな苗字とは裏腹にキュートな声は……遊紗ちゃん？　あいてるからどーぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"
comments: see CCA0013 -GHS
records.assessment: The contrast between the intimidating surname and unexpectedly cute voice is present, but “conversely kyute” contains a misspelling and an ungrammatical adverbial relation.
records.remedy: Use “That gangster-like surname paired with such an unexpectedly cute voice... Yusa-chan?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"

records.jp: ドアがおそるおそる開き、美少女が立っていた。
records.en: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.
records.assessment: The English shifts from present “opens” to past “stood” inside one coordinated event, producing an unsupported tense break.
records.remedy: Use “The door slowly and carefully opened, and there stood a beautiful girl.”

highlights.text: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.

records.jp: 黒々とした瞳孔に、俺の姿が映る。
records.en: The reflection of my figure on her deep dark pupils.
comments: See CCA0001 -GHS
records.assessment: The source makes her pupils the surface in which his figure is reflected. The English is only a noun fragment and leaves the reflection without a predicate.
records.remedy: Use “My figure was reflected in her deep, dark pupils.”

highlights.text: The reflection of my figure on her deep dark pupils.

records.jp: 「着物、なんですね」
records.en: Yusa: "A Kimono... yes it is."
records.assessment: The source observes that he is wearing a kimono. “A Kimono... yes it is” neither forms that observation nor identifies what “it” refers to.
records.remedy: Use “A kimono... You’re wearing one.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "A Kimono... yes it is."

records.jp: 「ソーセキが好きでね」
records.en: Taichi: "It's because I like dem Soseki."
comments: See CCA0019 for the pun. -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply says he likes Soseki. The slang determiner “dem” is unsupported, ungrammatical here, and changes the speaker’s voice.
records.remedy: Use “It’s because I like Soseki.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's because I like dem Soseki."

records.jp: 「はー」
records.en: Yusa: "Huh?"
records.assessment: The source response acknowledges the explanation, roughly “I see.” “Huh?” instead signals incomprehension.
records.remedy: Use “I see.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Huh?"

records.jp: 「そのー、お髪がお白くていらっしゃられるので……色合いとかが」
records.en: Yusa: "Well, the hair is indeed giving it some white and... it suits you, I think."
records.assessment: The source says his white hair makes various colors suit him. The English makes “the hair” give the kimono “some white,” reversing the descriptive relation and producing malformed grammar.
records.remedy: Use “Well, because your hair is white, different colors look good on you... I think it suits you.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Well, the hair is indeed giving it some white and... it suits you, I think."

records.jp: 苦笑いを浮かべ。
records.en: Rise a bitter smile to the surface.
comments: Imperative and specific, remember he molds smiles. This is pure resentment. If Yutaka isn't dead, he's about to die. -GHS
records.assessment: The source narrates a wry smile rising to his face. “Rise a bitter smile” lacks a subject and uses an unsupported imperative/base form.
records.remedy: Use “A wry smile rose to my face.”

highlights.text: Rise a bitter smile to the surface.

records.jp: 「遊紗ちゃんなんか、もっと似合うんじゃないかな」
records.en: Taichi: "Wouldn't it'd fit you a lot better, Yusa-chan?"
records.assessment: “Wouldn’t it’d” combines two incompatible auxiliary constructions. The source asks whether the kimono would suit Yusa better.
records.remedy: Use “Wouldn’t it suit you much better, Yusa-chan?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wouldn't it'd fit you a lot better, Yusa-chan?"

records.jp: 「そ、そんなっ……ひっくっ」
records.en: Yusa: "B-, but it's... hic!"
comments: And there it goes, right on cue. -GHS
records.assessment: The source begins with a flustered negative refusal before the hiccup. “But it’s” changes the polarity and leaves the clause incomplete.
records.remedy: Use “N-no... hic!”

highlights.text: Yusa: "B-, but it's... hic!"

records.jp: 声を張り上げた拍子に、しゃっくりが出た。
records.en: On the downbeat of her raising her voice, out came a hiccup.
comments: See CCA0013, exact same term. -GHS
records.assessment: The source means that a hiccup emerges just as she raises her voice. “On the downbeat” imports a musical term not licensed by the scene.
records.remedy: Use “The instant she raised her voice, a hiccup came out.”

highlights.text: On the downbeat of her raising her voice, out came a hiccup.

records.jp: 驚かせるといいんだっけ。
records.en: But it should be fine if I give are fright, right.
records.assessment: “Give are fright” is malformed, and the source tentatively wonders whether startling her might stop the hiccups rather than asserting that it should be fine.
records.remedy: Use “Maybe giving her a fright would work.”

highlights.text: But it should be fine if I give are fright, right.

records.jp: 見上げた美少女面に、顔を寄せていく。
records.en: The head of the pretty girl looks up to my approaching face.
records.assessment: The source says he brings his face close to the beautiful girl’s upturned face. The English instead makes the girl’s head look upward toward his approaching face, assigning the action to the wrong body and subject.
records.remedy: Use “I brought my face close to the beautiful girl’s upturned face.”

highlights.text: The head of the pretty girl looks up to my approaching face.

records.jp: 五センチまで接近して、囁く。
records.en: I draw near to five centimeters of distance, and whisper:
comments: See CCA0030. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he closes the distance until only five centimeters remain. “Draw near to five centimeters of distance” is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use “I moved to within five centimeters of her and whispered:”

highlights.text: I draw near to five centimeters of distance, and whisper:

records.jp: 座らせて、麦茶を出す。
records.en: I let her sit, and lay out some barley tea.
comments: So he DOES have tea in the house. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he serves barley tea after seating her. “Lay out” is the wrong collocation for serving a drink.
records.remedy: Use “I sat her down and served some barley tea.”

highlights.text: I let her sit, and lay out some barley tea.

records.jp: 複雑な事情を想像したに違いない。
records.en: She guesses complicated circumstances, no mistake.
comments: She probably guesses his host family isn't his actual family. -GHS
records.assessment: The source narrates that she must have imagined complicated circumstances. “She guesses ... no mistake” is ungrammatical and changes the completed inference into simple present.
records.remedy: Use “She must have imagined that there were complicated circumstances.”

highlights.text: She guesses complicated circumstances, no mistake.

records.jp: 「仕事が忙しい時期は社員寮に泊まりっぱなしなんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's that she always keeps staying at the company dormitory when she's busy with work."
records.assessment: The source explains that she stays at the company dormitory when work is busy. “Always keeps staying” is redundant and unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “She stays at the company dormitory whenever work gets busy.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's that she always keeps staying at the company dormitory when she's busy with work."

records.jp: 「ああ、そうですか……」
records.en: Yusa: "Ahhh, that is what..."
records.assessment: The source gives a complete acknowledgment equivalent to “Oh, I see.” “That is what...” is an unfinished clause and omits the acknowledgment.
records.remedy: Use “Oh, I see...”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Ahhh, that is what..."

records.jp: 「それで今日はどんなわくわくするようなニュースを持ってきてくれたのかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "So, what thrilling news may you be bringing me bring here on this day?"
records.assessment: The duplicated “bringing me bring” makes the question ungrammatical, while the embellished “thrilling news” adds a quality not established by the source.
records.remedy: Use “So, what brings you here today?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "So, what thrilling news may you be bringing me bring here on this day?"

records.jp: 「あの、わたし今日が誕生日なんです」
records.en: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."
comments: This seems cut from two very different parts of a take, or two takes. Unfortunately, there's been no pickups for Yusa (she has not a single line in After Story either), so this is still like this as far as the 360 version. -GHS
records.assessment: The source states that today is her birthday. “Would be” makes that fact hypothetical or conditional.
records.remedy: Use “Um, today is my birthday.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."

records.jp: 「へえ、そうだったのか」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, it was, right."
records.assessment: The response recognizes that today is the birthday. “It was, right” incorrectly places it in the past and is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “Oh, right, it is.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, it was, right."

records.jp: 包装紙に包まれたそれを無意識に受け取る俺の、頭の中は『？』で満ちた。
records.en: I unconsciously accept a something packed inside wrapping paper as "?" fill the inside my head.
comments: fucking metal gears -GHS
records.assessment: The English is syntactically incoherent: “accept a something” and “as ‘?’ fill the inside my head” do not express the source’s simultaneous acceptance and confusion.
records.remedy: Use “I unconsciously accepted the wrapped object while question marks filled my head.”

highlights.text: I unconsciously accept a something packed inside wrapping paper as "?" fill the inside my head.

records.jp: 若い頃から優しく接していれば、容姿のマイナス面は緩和できると思ったからだ。
records.en: Because, I thought, if she received gentle attention from the time of youth, then that 'minus' that is my appearance could be mitigated.
comments: OTOH, this is closer to what he really thinks his problem is. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says early kindness might mitigate the negative effect of the girl’s appearance. The English calls the narrator’s own appearance the “minus,” reversing whose appearance is under discussion.
records.remedy: Use “I thought that treating her kindly from an early age might offset the disadvantage of her appearance.”

highlights.text: Because, I thought, if she received gentle attention from the time of youth, then that 'minus' that is my appearance could be mitigated.

records.jp: 『光源氏は本当にウハウハなのか大検証』というこの企画は、今のところ順調と判断できるデータが揃いつつある。
records.en: The Super Was Hikari Genji Truly All Satisfied Smiles Experiment, as I call my plan, has presently assembled sufficient data to produce a judgment of 'favorable'.
comments: See CCA0013. -GHS
records.assessment: The coined project title asks whether Hikaru Genji was really living it up. The English changes Hikaru to Hikari and reduces the title to an ungrammatical string that does not preserve the question.
records.remedy: Use a coherent title such as “The ‘Was Hikaru Genji Really Living It Up?’ Comprehensive Investigation.”

highlights.text: The Super Was Hikari Genji Truly All Satisfied Smiles Experiment, as I call my plan, has presently assembled sufficient data to produce a judgment of 'favorable'.

records.jp: 成功したあとについてあんまり考えていなかったことには、今気づいた。
records.en: As to how I hadn't given much thought what to do after a success, I realized it just now.
comments: What does a dog do after it's caught a car? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he has only now realized he never considered what to do after succeeding. The English omits the required “to” after “thought” and tangles the temporal realization.
records.remedy: Use “I only just realized that I hadn’t given much thought to what I would do if it succeeded.”

highlights.text: As to how I hadn't given much thought what to do after a success, I realized it just now.

records.jp: 「それと、交換日記を明日提出できたらなと思ったので……」
records.en: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."
records.assessment: The source presents handing in the exchange diary tomorrow as her additional reason. “I thought, so I could” does not form a grammatical causal relation.
records.remedy: Use “And I thought this way I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow...”

highlights.text: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."

records.jp: 膝の上、なかなか落ち着こうとしない指を、懸命にあやしている。
records.en: She rocks back and forth above her lap fingers that don't wish to readily settle down.
records.assessment: The source depicts her fidgeting with restless fingers on her lap. The English makes the fingers themselves objects that do not wish to settle and gives “rocks” no coherent object structure.
records.remedy: Use “She fidgets with her restless fingers in her lap.”

highlights.text: She rocks back and forth above her lap fingers that don't wish to readily settle down.

records.jp: うつむいて、のぞく首筋がすっかり赤い。
records.en: She bows, and all but the nape of the neck is completely red.
records.assessment: The source says even the exposed nape of her neck is completely red. “All but the nape” explicitly excludes the nape, reversing the extent.
records.remedy: Use “She bows her head, and even the exposed nape of her neck is bright red.”

highlights.text: She bows, and all but the nape of the neck is completely red.

records.jp: いっぱいいっぱいのご様子。
records.en: She looks like she's full, full to the brim.
records.assessment: The repeated expression means she is completely overwhelmed and at the limit of her composure. “Full to the brim” leaves the emotional state unspecified and sounds like physical fullness.
records.remedy: Use “She looks completely overwhelmed.”

highlights.text: She looks like she's full, full to the brim.

records.jp: 遊紗ちゃんに贈れるようなもの。
records.en: Something that I could present Yusa-chan...
records.assessment: The source searches for something he could give Yusa. The English omits the verb complement after “present,” leaving a fragment that can read as introducing her rather than giving her a gift.
records.remedy: Use “Something I could give Yusa-chan...”

highlights.text: Something that I could present Yusa-chan...

records.jp: ぬいぐるみでもあればいいのに、メルヘンとは無縁なマイ部屋。
records.en: You should've had a stuffed animal or something in you, dear my room so indifferent to the Marchen.
comments: http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/364221/Marchen -GHS
records.assessment: The source wishes he had a stuffed toy and comments that his room is unrelated to fairy-tale charm. The English addresses the room as though it should contain something “in you” and is syntactically incoherent.
records.remedy: Use “If only I had a stuffed toy or something. My room has nothing remotely fairy-tale about it.”

highlights.text: You should've had a stuffed animal or something in you, dear my room so indifferent to the Marchen.

records.jp: 自分だったらなにが欲しいか考えてみる。
records.en: Let's try thinking about what I'd want if it were for me.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator tries to think what he himself would want. “Let’s try” changes the singular internal decision into a plural exhortation.
records.remedy: Use “I try to think what I would want.”

highlights.text: Let's try thinking about what I'd want if it were for me.

records.jp: 遊紗ちゃんの生パンツ。
records.en: ...Yusa-chan's just-stripped underpants...
records.assessment: The source’s expression refers directly to Yusa’s panties; it does not establish that they have just been removed. “Just-stripped” adds a specific prior action.
records.remedy: Use “...Yusa-chan’s panties...”

highlights.text: ...Yusa-chan's just-stripped underpants...

records.jp: 自然と帯をほどきだす己の手を、理性が鉄の意志力をもって引きはがす。
records.en: The self's hand that with spontaneity goes to unfasten the kimono's belt is torn off via rationality and the iron will it possesses.
comments: Reminder that it's technically not his hand. Interesting he's going for HIS kimono, isn't it? Now look at CCD0021. Whose clothes is he taking off there? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says reason and iron will pull back the hand that spontaneously starts undoing the obi. The English calls it “the self’s hand,” makes rationality possess the iron will, and says the hand is torn off.
records.remedy: Use “Reason and iron will dragged back the hand that had spontaneously started undoing my obi.”

highlights.text: The self's hand that with spontaneity goes to unfasten the kimono's belt is torn off via rationality and the iron will it possesses.

records.jp: 今まで築き上げたものを、一瞬で地平の彼方へ飛ばしてどうする。
records.en: What would I do if what was built up 'til this moment were to be cast towards the horizon in an instant?
records.assessment: The source worries that everything built up so far could be ruined in an instant. “Cast towards the horizon” is a literalized image that does not convey destruction of the accumulated relationship.
records.remedy: Use “What would I do if everything I’d built up until now were ruined in an instant?”

highlights.text: What would I do if what was built up 'til this moment were to be cast towards the horizon in an instant?

records.jp: いや、これはどうだろう。
records.en: Nah, how could I use this.
records.assessment: The source weighs the discovered object with “No, I wonder how this would be.” “How could I use this” changes tentative evaluation into a question about possible use.
records.remedy: Use “No... I wonder how this would go over.”

highlights.text: Nah, how could I use this.

records.jp: 意外性は、あるかな。
records.en: It does have that it's unpredictable, doesn't it.
records.assessment: The source notes that the idea does have an element of surprise. “It does have that it’s unpredictable” is ungrammatical and substitutes unpredictability for surprise.
records.remedy: Use “It does have the element of surprise, at least.”

highlights.text: It does have that it's unpredictable, doesn't it.

records.jp: 「ううう～ん」
records.en: Taichi: "Nnnaaa～h."
records.assessment: The source is a prolonged deliberative groan. “Naaah” reads as a casual rejection and changes the pragmatic force.
records.remedy: Use a hesitant “Hmmmm...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nnnaaa～h."

records.jp: 「あのー、たいちさーん、わたしそろそろもどらないといけない時間なんですー」
records.en: Yusa: "Uhmmm, Taichi-saaan, it's that it is just about time and I just must head back..."
records.assessment: The source is a hesitant but complete warning that it is about time for her to leave. The stacked “it’s that it is” and “just must” are ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “Um, Taichi-san, it’s about time I headed home...”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Uhmmm, Taichi-saaan, it's that it is just about time and I just must head back..."

records.jp: 箱とマニュアルを探して詰め直し、紙袋に突っ込んだ。
records.en: Search for manual and box, repackage, and cram into a paper bag.
records.assessment: The source narrates his completed rapid actions: finding the manual and box, repacking the item, and stuffing it into a paper bag. The English uses bare imperatives without a subject.
