records.remedy: Use “I found the manual and box, repacked it, and stuffed it into a paper bag.”

highlights.text: Search for manual and box, repackage, and cram into a paper bag.

records.jp: この娘は驚くと絶句する癖があるな。
records.en: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.
records.assessment: The source notes her tendency to become speechless when surprised. “Don’t she” is ungrammatical, and “bad” adds a negative judgment not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use “This young lady has a habit of losing her words when she’s surprised.”

highlights.text: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.

records.jp: さっきの倍くらいに絶句する。
records.en: Her loss of words about doubles from before.
comments: This isn't moe; this is a girl who is utterly and honestly astonished at being treated as anything but worthless. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she is left roughly twice as speechless as before. “Her loss of words about doubles” is an unidiomatic nominal construction.
records.remedy: Use “She was about twice as speechless as before.”

highlights.text: Her loss of words about doubles from before.

records.jp: 「もう夜だし、ちょっと危ない人もいるからね」
records.en: Taichi: "It's night by now, and there's kinda dangerous people out there."
comments: That would seem extraordinarily unlikely, given the difficulty of access, but considering Gunjou... -GHS
records.assessment: The source warns that there are some dangerous people around. The singular existential “there’s” does not agree with the plural “people.”
records.remedy: Use “It’s nighttime, and there are some dangerous people around.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's night by now, and there's kinda dangerous people out there."

records.jp: 「母にデスカ？」
records.en: Yusa: "But, to mother?"
comments: Suddenly tense. Possibly because her mother is partially to blame for her bullying. -GHS
records.assessment: The source merely confirms, with surprise, that he means her mother. “But” adds an opposition not present in the question.
records.remedy: Use “My mother?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "But, to mother?"

records.jp: 「……まあ、そうですねぇ」
records.en: Yusa: "...well, if you say so."
records.assessment: The response is a hesitant concession, roughly “Well, I suppose so.” “If you say so” introduces skepticism about Taichi’s claim.
records.remedy: Use “...Well, I suppose so.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "...well, if you say so."

records.jp: 「なんてことを、君はこれからの数年間を言われて過ごすんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "What are you saying, you will be so many years after this being told that!"
comments: By annoying grandmothers, given the answer above doesn't seem to imply he already says this often. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she will spend the next several years being told things like that. The English’s word order is incoherent and does not preserve who will be told what.
records.remedy: Use “You’ll spend the next few years having people say things like that to you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What are you saying, you will be so many years after this being told that!"

records.jp: 「はじめて会ったときより育ってると思うよ。俺の目から見ても」
records.en: Taichi: "You've grown up a lot since the time we first met, I think. From what I see with my eyes."
comments: Now he's ogling her. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she has grown since they first met, even in his view. “A lot” and the redundant “with my eyes” add emphasis and awkwardly literalize the viewpoint.
records.remedy: Use “I think you’ve grown since we first met, even to my eyes.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You've grown up a lot since the time we first met, I think. From what I see with my eyes."

records.jp: 「一部はまだ未発達だけど♪」
records.en: Taichi: "But one part's still undeveloped♪."
records.assessment: The source ends with a musical-note mark. Adding a period after the note produces a stray double terminal punctuation sequence.
records.remedy: Use “But one part is still undeveloped♪”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But one part's still undeveloped♪."

records.jp: 「今の自分を大切にしたまえ。肉体的に」
records.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with holding yourself more precious. Physically, I mean.."
comments: Ah, there we begin with the 'holding the self precious', see Miki route. "Gladden" is that damn running gag, see CCC0026 for payoff. -GHS
records.assessment: The source tells her to cherish her present physical self. “Gladden me with holding yourself more precious” invents the speaker’s gratification and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “Cherish who you are now—physically.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gladden me with holding yourself more precious. Physically, I mean.."

records.jp: 「あの、すみません、送ってもらって」
records.en: Yusa: "Uhm, sorry for having to take me home."
records.assessment: Yusa apologizes for making Taichi walk her home. “For having to take me home” makes her sound as though she had to escort herself and lacks a grammatical agent.
records.remedy: Use “Um, sorry for making you walk me home.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Uhm, sorry for having to take me home."

records.jp: 「きょーしゅーです」
records.en: Yusa: "Trainingful then!"
records.assessment: Her childish mispronunciation of 恐縮 is the setup for the following 強襲 joke. “Trainingful” has no relation to either sound or meaning and destroys the wordplay chain.
records.remedy: Use a sound-based mistake that can plausibly be heard as “assault.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Trainingful then!"

records.jp: 恐縮を読み間違えているんだろうなぁ。
records.en: She's really mispronounced that 'grateful'.
comments: Literally it's kyoushuu vs. kyoushuku. This is either the misreading that becomes fixed into the OH NO ME SO VIOLENT AND MAD in CCB0018, or, she's not misreading anything as practicing to be normal IS training to him. This trends heavily towards the latter, unfortunately, but it's still on the topic at least. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration identifies which polite word she has misread. “Mispronounced that ‘grateful’” is ungrammatical and does not name the Japanese sound relation driving the joke.
records.remedy: Use a concise explanation that she has mispronounced the word for being obliged or grateful.

highlights.text: She's really mispronounced that 'grateful'.

records.jp: かわええなぁ。
records.en: Sooo kyute.
records.assessment: The source is an affectionate “So cute.” “Kyute” is an unexplained misspelling rather than a meaningful voice choice.
records.remedy: Use “Sooo cute.”

highlights.text: Sooo kyute.

records.jp: 「ぜひ君のような娘に、夜の寝室で強襲されたいものだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Certainly, a Nightly Bedroom Assault is something one wishes to do to a girl like you."
comments: Cats seem to top the topic, so I'm not sure if it's a specific type of fet-- ah, dammit, forgot it's Japan. Of course it's a specific type of fetishism. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he would like to be assaulted in a nighttime bedroom by a girl like her. The English says he wishes to assault her, reversing agent and patient.
records.remedy: Use “I’d certainly like to be assaulted in a nighttime bedroom by a girl like you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Certainly, a Nightly Bedroom Assault is something one wishes to do to a girl like you."

records.jp: 「夜の寝室でですか？」
records.en: Yusa: "Why in the bedroom at night?"
records.assessment: The source echoes the location as a surprised question. “Why” adds a request for cause that is not stated.
records.remedy: Use “In a bedroom at night?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Why in the bedroom at night?"

records.jp: 「こういう、送ってもらったりするのって、小説の中だけの話かと思ってました」
records.en: Yusa: "Being walked home at night like this I thought would only happen in the story of a novel.
records.assessment: The spoken line opens a quotation mark but never closes it, leaving the dialogue structurally incomplete.
records.remedy: Add the closing quotation mark after “novel.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Being walked home at night like this I thought would only happen in the story of a novel.

records.jp: 「そお？」
records.en: Taichi: "Innit?"
records.assessment: The drawn-out source question means “Really?” or “Is that so?” “Innit?” is a tag question requiring a prior proposition and gives the speaker unsupported dialect.
records.remedy: Use “Really?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Innit?"

records.jp: 「さっきも言ったけど、当然のことだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "But I told you before, this is absolutely normal."
records.assessment: The source says escorting her is only natural. “Absolutely normal” shifts from an obligation or courtesy to statistical normality and adds emphasis.
records.remedy: Use “Like I said, it’s only natural.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But I told you before, this is absolutely normal."

records.jp: 「世の中には、大は小を決して決して兼ねないとする一派がいるからね」
records.en: Taichi: "Because in this world, there are some parties that will never, ever allow the small to coexist with the big."
comments: Remember that Taichi's not anti-loli, just anti-pure lolicons. -GHS
records.assessment: The source twists the proverb that the large can serve for the small, saying some people insist it absolutely cannot. “Allow the small to coexist with the big” changes substitution into coexistence.
records.remedy: Use “Some people insist that bigger absolutely does not serve for smaller.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because in this world, there are some parties that will never, ever allow the small to coexist with the big."

records.jp: 究極的にはどんなものでもいいものなんだ、というのがマイ哲学だ。
records.en: Ultimately, either choice is a good choice, and that is Mai Philosophy.
records.assessment: The source generalizes that ultimately anything can have merit. “Either choice” narrows that open set to two choices.
records.remedy: Use “My philosophy is that, ultimately, anything can be good in its own way.”

highlights.text: Ultimately, either choice is a good choice, and that is Mai Philosophy.

records.jp: なにかが刺激された。
records.en: Something is stimulated.
comments: There he goes... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says something in the narrator was stimulated at that moment. The English drops the experiencer and shifts the narration to present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Something in me was stimulated.”

highlights.text: Something is stimulated.

records.jp: 「え、どうしましたですっ？」
records.en: Yusa: "Eh? What is wrong with that?"
records.assessment: Yusa asks what is wrong or what happened. “With that” invents a specific object of objection and makes her defend the note-taking.
records.remedy: Use “Huh? What’s wrong?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Eh? What is wrong with that?"

records.jp: 「記録してはいけないのっ」
records.en: Taichi: "Making recordings is out of the question!"
records.assessment: In context he forbids writing the information down. “Making recordings” commonly means audio or video recording and obscures the written-note action shown by the source.
records.remedy: Use “You mustn’t write that down!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Making recordings is out of the question!"

records.jp: 今のデンジャラスワードをインターネットなどでリサーチされたりしたら！！
records.en: She wants to implement the act of Research on these Dangerous Words on the Internet etc.!!!
comments: Engrish-y = flat translation -GHS
records.assessment: The source fears what would happen if she researched the dangerous words online. The English turns the hypothetical fear into her present desire and renders it as bureaucratic nonsense.
records.remedy: Use “If she researched those dangerous words on the internet...!”

highlights.text: She wants to implement the act of Research on these Dangerous Words on the Internet etc.!!!

records.jp: 「危ない！　伏せろ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Watch out! Ambush!"
comments: Feint. Or is it? -GHS
records.assessment: 伏せろ is the command “Get down!” The English replaces the command with the noun “Ambush!”
records.remedy: Use “Watch out! Get down!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Watch out! Ambush!"

records.jp: 抱き寄せて、電柱の陰に隠れる。
records.en: I embrace her, and we hide behind an utility pole.
records.assessment: The indefinite article before “utility” must be “a,” not “an,” because the word begins with a consonant sound.
records.remedy: Use “We duck behind a utility pole.”

highlights.text: I embrace her, and we hide behind an utility pole.

records.jp: 「そるじゃー兵士！？」
records.en: Yusa: "But then, it's a soldier?!?"
records.assessment: The source incredulously repeats the intentionally redundant hybrid “soldier-soldier.” The English removes that repetition and asks only whether it is a soldier.
records.remedy: Preserve the bilingual redundancy: “A ‘soldier soldier’!?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "But then, it's a soldier?!?"

records.jp: 「ＣＩＡかＫＧＢ、あるいはＮ○Ｋという可能性もある」
records.en: Taichi: "From the CIA or the KGB, but there is the possibility of the N*K as well."
comments: That may sound like a North Korean espionage agency, but I can't find anything that's more likely than the NHK. -GHS
records.assessment: The source lists CIA, KGB, or possibly N*K as alternatives. “From ... but there is” does not form a grammatical alternative list.
records.remedy: Use “It might be the CIA, the KGB, or even N*K.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "From the CIA or the KGB, but there is the possibility of the N*K as well."

records.jp: 「どれも極めて武力的な諜報機関だ」
records.en: Taichi: "Any of them is an extraordinarily militarized intelligence agency."
records.assessment: The plural set “any of them” takes “are” in this construction, not “is.”
records.remedy: Use “Any of them could be an extremely militarized intelligence agency.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Any of them is an extraordinarily militarized intelligence agency."

records.jp: たまたま通りかかった帰宅中のサラリーマンが、怪訝な顔でこちらを見ていた。
records.en: That salaryman on his way home that we accidentally happened to pass looked at us with doubt on his face.
comments: Maybe the guy works for the NHK...? How many times has he done this? This is so Settei-like it's less uncanny and more telling. -GHS
records.assessment: “Accidentally happened” redundantly marks chance twice, and the source describes a puzzled or suspicious look rather than abstract “doubt on his face.”
records.remedy: Use “A salaryman who happened to be passing on his way home gave us a puzzled look.”

highlights.text: That salaryman on his way home that we accidentally happened to pass looked at us with doubt on his face.

records.jp: シャーペンの背についてる消しゴムで、こすこすと紙面にリセットをかける。
records.en: And with the eraser attached to the back of the pencil, scrub scrub the page is reset.
comments: Specific term. Interesting. -GHS
records.assessment: The source makes the narrator rub the page with the pencil’s eraser. The English’s “scrub scrub the page is reset” lacks an agent and joins incompatible clauses.
records.remedy: Use “Using the eraser on the end of her mechanical pencil, she rubbed the writing off the page.”

highlights.text: And with the eraser attached to the back of the pencil, scrub scrub the page is reset.

records.jp: 「いいんです。わたしが悪いんです」
records.en: Yusa: "It is all right! It is my bad!"
comments: She probably means that literally. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says “It’s my fault.” “It is my bad” is not idiomatic in this formal register and mishandles the possessive idiom.
records.remedy: Use “It’s all right. It’s my fault.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "It is all right! It is my bad!"

records.jp: 「は、はいっ！？」
records.en: Misato: "Eh, what?!"
records.assessment: The source is a startled, deferential “Y-yes!?” in response to being shouted at. “Eh, what?!” drops the acknowledgment and sounds confrontational.
records.remedy: Use “Y-yes!?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Eh, what?!"

records.jp: 「な、鳴いてないじゃないですか」
records.en: Misato: "I-, I am not making animal calls here!"
records.assessment: Misato protests that she did not cry out, directly answering the pheasant proverb. “Making animal calls” over-literalizes the pheasant image and changes her denial.
records.remedy: Use “I-I didn’t cry out!”

highlights.text: Misato: "I-, I am not making animal calls here!"

records.jp: 「ヘイ、ミス怪我人。ホワイワズイットナウ？」
records.en: Taichi: "HEI, MISU injured person. HOWAI WAZU ITTO NAU?" (Hey, Miss injured person! Why are you already at work?)
records.assessment: The source deliberately uses broken katakana English. The parenthetical fluent paraphrase is absent from the source and explains away the joke while adding a more specific work-related question.
records.remedy: Preserve only the broken-English performance without an explanatory parenthesis.

highlights.text: Taichi: "HEI, MISU injured person. HOWAI WAZU ITTO NAU?" (Hey, Miss injured person! Why are you already at work?)

records.jp: 「べ、別にこそこそやっていたわけじゃ……ただどうしても気になりまして。今朝は五時に目が覚めましたし」
records.en: Misato: "It's-, it's not like I was trying to be all sneaky... I was just very anxious. This morning I was awake at five."
comments: going with first part being less formal-ish. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she woke at five this morning. “Was awake at five” describes a state and loses the event of waking unusually early.
records.remedy: Use “I woke up at five this morning.”

highlights.text: Misato: "It's-, it's not like I was trying to be all sneaky... I was just very anxious. This morning I was awake at five."

records.jp: 弁解がましく、先輩は身振り満載でそう説明した。
records.en: So Senpai explained, adding full-extent gesticulation to improve the excuse.
comments: This is a characterization that didn't quite get used, unfortunately. -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes her excuse-laden explanation and abundant gestures. “To improve the excuse” invents a deliberate strategy and goal.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai explained defensively, gesturing profusely.”

highlights.text: So Senpai explained, adding full-extent gesticulation to improve the excuse.

records.jp: 両手をあげた。
records.en: She brought up both hands.
records.assessment: The source says she raises both hands in surrender. “Brought up both hands” is an awkward motion description and misses the idiomatic surrender gesture.
records.remedy: Use “She raised both hands.”

highlights.text: She brought up both hands.

records.jp: あ、しまった……つい。
records.en: Ah, dammit... unconscious me.
records.assessment: The source means he did it without thinking and immediately regrets it. “Unconscious me” is an ungrammatical noun phrase and suggests literal unconsciousness.
records.remedy: Use “Ah, crap... I did it without thinking.”

highlights.text: Ah, dammit... unconscious me.

records.jp: 「なんです、これ？」
records.en: Misato: "What are... these?"
records.assessment: The source asks “What is this?” The English changes the singular demonstrative to plural “these.”
records.remedy: Use “What is this?”

highlights.text: Misato: "What are... these?"

records.jp: 「こ、こここ交番に人いなくて手錠落ちてたから持って来ちゃったの……」
records.en: Taichi: "Th-, th-th-th-the police box was empty and handcuffs fell on the floor and so I brought them with..."
comments: The koban is around the train station which is waaay out of his path to school. Hum, 4 stutters of hers and 3 of his. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the police box was empty and the handcuffs were lying there. “Handcuffs fell on the floor” invents an observed falling event.
records.remedy: Use “The police box was empty, and the handcuffs were lying there, so I brought them...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Th-, th-th-th-the police box was empty and handcuffs fell on the floor and so I brought them with..."

records.jp: つん
records.en: Tsun-tsun.
comments: As expected of today's onii-chan, such technical terms are いろいろ funny/interesting, etc. and it can't be helped so I stick my brobdingnagian meat poleaxe in such a small honeypot? So. -GHS
records.assessment: The sound effect describes a small poke. “Tsun-tsun” imports an unrelated fandom label instead of representing the physical action.
records.remedy: Use a light “poke” sound or “Poke.”

highlights.text: Tsun-tsun.

records.jp: 笑みが固着した。
records.en: Her smile fixes fast.
comments: Because Fixation. But it means hardening. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says her smile froze in place. “Fixes fast” is an unidiomatic present-tense calque.
records.remedy: Use “Her smile froze in place.”

highlights.text: Her smile fixes fast.

records.jp: 「も、ものによってはＯＫデス！」
records.en: Taichi: "De-, depending on what that means that is Most OK!"
comments: -desu. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says some kinds of assault would be acceptable to him. The English repeats “that” around the predicate and never forms the conditional relation coherently.
records.remedy: Use “D-depending on the kind, I’d be okay with it!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "De-, depending on what that means that is Most OK!"

records.jp: 「あの、つい条件反射で……」
records.en: Taichi: "Uhm, via conditioned reflexes..."
comments: He's still not kidding! -GHS
records.assessment: The source apologetically attributes the response to a conditioned reflex. “Via conditioned reflexes” uses an unnatural plural and bureaucratic preposition.
records.remedy: Use “Um, it was just a conditioned reflex...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uhm, via conditioned reflexes..."

records.jp: ギリギリギリ……
records.en: GrytGrytGryt...
comments: Giri-giri. See CCC0016A, but given the SFX, works better uhmmm let's say literally. -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
records.assessment: The sound effect represents sustained grinding or squeezing. “Gryt” repeated without an established English sound convention is opaque.
records.remedy: Use a recognizable grinding sound such as “Grrrind...”

highlights.text: GrytGrytGryt...

records.jp: 「とりあえず、教室にいたらどうです？」
records.en: Taichi: "For now, how about going into a classroom?"
records.assessment: The source suggests that she wait in her classroom. “Going into a classroom” changes staying to entering and makes the room indefinite.
records.remedy: Use “For now, why don’t you wait in your classroom?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "For now, how about going into a classroom?"

records.jp: 「連行されているように見えるじゃないですか」
records.en: Misato: "Will it not look like that I am being frog-marched!"
records.assessment: The source says it will look as though she is being hauled away. “Look like that I am” is not a grammatical complement structure.
records.remedy: Use “Won’t it look as though I’m being hauled away?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Will it not look like that I am being frog-marched!"

records.jp: 「どっちかと言うと、プレイしているように見えたりして」
records.en: Taichi: "If I have to say what it is, you look like you are doing a Playact."
records.assessment: The source says the two of them may look as though they are engaging in kinky ‘play.’ The English assigns the appearance only to her and renders プレイ as generic “Playact.”
records.remedy: Use “If anything, it might look like we’re engaging in some kind of play.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "If I have to say what it is, you look like you are doing a Playact."

records.jp: そこに美希がやってきた。
records.en: Over there Miki had appeared.
records.assessment: The source narrates Miki arriving at that point. Past perfect “had appeared” incorrectly places her arrival before the current sequence.
records.remedy: Use “Miki came over just then.”

highlights.text: Over there Miki had appeared.

records.jp: 焦って手元を隠そうとした先輩は、それに失敗した。
records.en: Senpai attempted to hide the top of her hands and, flustered, failed in the act.
records.assessment: The source says she tries to hide her hands or what is at hand. “The top of her hands” incorrectly names a specific anatomical surface.
records.remedy: Use “Flustered, Senpai tried to hide her hands and failed.”

highlights.text: Senpai attempted to hide the top of her hands and, flustered, failed in the act.

records.jp: じっとしていれば良かったのに。
records.en: It would have been better if she had just sat still...
records.assessment: The source only says she should have kept still. “Sat” adds a posture not established by the line.
records.remedy: Use “She should have just kept still...”

highlights.text: It would have been better if she had just sat still...

records.jp: 「た、逮捕されてる……」
records.en: Miki: "Y-, you were arrested..."
records.assessment: Miki observes that Misato is under arrest in the present scene. “You were arrested” moves the arrest into completed past.
records.remedy: Use “Y-you’ve been arrested...”

highlights.text: Miki: "Y-, you were arrested..."

records.jp: 「違います、これは悪戯です」
records.en: Misato "I was not! This is just a prank!"
records.assessment: The speaker label lacks its required colon, unlike the surrounding dialogue records, so the line’s presentation is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “Misato: ‘No, this is just a prank!’”

highlights.text: Misato "I was not! This is just a prank!"

records.jp: 挙手をした。
records.en: She gave a military salute.
records.assessment: 挙手 means she raises her hand. A military salute is a different gesture; the actual salute is introduced later.
records.remedy: Use “She raised her hand.”

highlights.text: She gave a military salute.

records.jp: 敬礼しつつ、プレイする場所を紹介してくれた。
records.en: Bowing, she presents us a place to have our little sex playact.
comments: Maybe too explicit, but that's Miki's intent anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: The source explicitly says she salutes while suggesting a place for their ‘play.’ The English changes the salute to a bow and adds the explicit word “sex.”
records.remedy: Use “Saluting, she suggested a place for us to continue our ‘play.’”

highlights.text: Bowing, she presents us a place to have our little sex playact.

records.jp: 「おつとめご苦労様でーす」
records.en: Miki: "Thank you very much for everything!"
comments: I still think this reads closer to a *literal* "your business is much appreciated". -GHS
records.assessment: The stock phrase evokes an official or underworld send-off and extends the arrest routine. Generic “Thank you very much for everything” erases that register joke.
records.remedy: Use a service-flavored line such as “Thank you for your service!”

highlights.text: Miki: "Thank you very much for everything!"

records.jp: ぺこりと頭をさげて、僕らを見送る。
records.en: With a snappy bow of the head, she saw off this innocent young boy and his Senpai.
records.assessment: The source simply says Miki bows and sees them off. “This innocent young boy and his Senpai” adds character judgments and recasts the first-person group.
records.remedy: Use “She bowed her head and saw us off.”

highlights.text: With a snappy bow of the head, she saw off this innocent young boy and his Senpai.

records.jp: 「今の会話、よくわかりませんでした」
records.en: Misato: "I did not really understand that conversation now."
records.assessment: The source says she did not understand the conversation just now. “That conversation now” is unidiomatic temporal placement.
records.remedy: Use “I didn’t really understand that conversation just now.”

highlights.text: Misato: "I did not really understand that conversation now."

records.jp: とはいっても、こじんまりとしたものだ。
records.en: Despite how it normally is in most parts of Japan, this place is a small and cozy thing.
comments: Reminder as the front of the station is normally a popular, not seedy, spot in Japan. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that even though it is called the station-front area, it is compact. The English invents a comparison with most parts of Japan.
records.remedy: Use “Even so, it was a small, compact place.”

highlights.text: Despite how it normally is in most parts of Japan, this place is a small and cozy thing.

records.jp: なるに決まっている。
records.en: I choose for it to be.
records.assessment: The source answers that it is obviously theft. “I choose for it to be” turns an objective conclusion into the narrator’s arbitrary decision.
records.remedy: Use “Of course it counts as theft.”

highlights.text: I choose for it to be.

records.jp: しかも備品だ。
records.en: And of office supplies, as well.
records.assessment: 備品 means institutional equipment or property. “Office supplies” narrows it to stationery and does not fit the handcuffs.
records.remedy: Use “And they’re police equipment, too.”

highlights.text: And of office supplies, as well.

records.jp: 「あった」
records.en: Taichi: "Mine."
comments: grabs keys, to contrast with how he just saw it earlier. -GHS
records.assessment: The source exclaims “Found it.” “Mine” instead asserts ownership, especially damaging in a passage already discussing theft.
records.remedy: Use “Found it.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Mine."

records.jp: すぐ戻らないとな。
records.en: Gotta go back immediately, right.
records.assessment: The source resolves that he has to hurry back. The appended “right” turns the internal resolution into a request for confirmation.
records.remedy: Use “I’ve got to hurry back.”

highlights.text: Gotta go back immediately, right.

records.jp: どうなんだろう。
records.en: But would it, really.
records.assessment: The source is an open internal “I wonder” about the implications of the empty world. “But would it, really” supplies no grammatical antecedent for “it.”
records.remedy: Use “I wonder how that would work.”

highlights.text: But would it, really.

records.jp: どんな犯罪に手を染めても、誰も咎めることもなく、また咎められることもない。
records.en:
no matter what crime one has had stained their
hands with, if no one rebukes you, then there
will be no being rebuked at all.
comments: Very careful here, he does not say that a world without people to call things crimes there'd be no crime. He says that without anyone to call on crimes, there'd be nothing CALLED a crime. Remember how he decides he is still stealing from the kouban. Consider Misato vs. her father: there's a higher law than the one of men, that won't pass or miss anything even if the law of men does. -GHS
records.assessment: The source imagines that no matter what crime he commits, nobody would condemn it and he could not be condemned. The English shifts between “one,” “their,” and “you” and reduces the second relation to a tautology.
records.remedy: Use “No matter what crime I committed, no one would condemn it, and there would be no one to condemn me.”

highlights.text:
no matter what crime one has had stained their
hands with, if no one rebukes you, then there
will be no being rebuked at all.

records.jp: だけどここにいるのは自分だけなのだ。
records.en: But still, here, there is only myself.
records.assessment: The source says he is the only person in this world. “There is only myself” is not grammatical English for that existential claim.
records.remedy: Use “But I would be the only one there.”

highlights.text: But still, here, there is only myself.

records.jp: 自分だけの世界で、どんな犯罪があるだろう。
records.en: In a world of only myself, what crime even exists?
records.assessment: The reflexive “myself” cannot serve as the complement of “of” in “a world of only myself.”
records.remedy: Use “In a world belonging only to me, what crime could there be?”

highlights.text: In a world of only myself, what crime even exists?

records.jp: 人との接点がなければ、大半の罪は霧散して意味を失う。
records.en: If there are no points of tangent with people, then the majority of offenses disperse and loses meaning.
comments: That's actually nonsense even from the Nietzscheian standpoint. If all are construct of the interaction between people, what offenses remain when no one's left? Taichi's failing the basics here. OTOH, considering the Ten Commandments, only four remain if there's no people, so it'd be correct in that sense... -GHS
records.assessment: The source speaks of points of contact with other people. “Points of tangent” is the wrong mathematical term, and plural “offenses” does not agree with “loses.”
records.remedy: Use “Without contact with other people, most crimes dissipate and lose their meaning.”

highlights.text: If there are no points of tangent with people, then the majority of offenses disperse and loses meaning.

records.jp: 個であること。群を捨てるということ。
records.en: Being Individual. An abandonment of the flock.
comments: 群 gun same as in 'gunjou'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source presents individuality and abandoning the group as parallel concepts. “Being Individual” omits the article and needlessly capitalizes the adjective.
records.remedy: Use “Being an individual. Abandoning the group.”

highlights.text: Being Individual. An abandonment of the flock.

records.jp: そのために必要な能力とは何か？
records.en: What strength would be necessary for that?
comments: See CCC3025, Youko in particular. Is he inventing the character even here? At times I do wonder. The point is more of a warning to hikikomori; most of them have zero chance of actually surviving in that environment, hence suicide rates. And if Cross Channel has a 'message', it's anti-suicide. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks what ability is required for individuality. “Strength” narrows ability to power or fortitude without support.
records.remedy: Use “What ability would that require?”

highlights.text: What strength would be necessary for that?

records.jp: また、適した精神構造とは？
records.en:
And more, what kind of intrapsychical structure
would be suitable to be in it?
records.assessment: The source asks what mental structure would be suited to it. “Intrapsychical” is needlessly technical, and “suitable to be in it” is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “And what kind of mental structure would be suited to it?”

highlights.text:
And more, what kind of intrapsychical structure
would be suitable to be in it?

records.jp: 人間にはいろいろな欲望がある。
records.en: Humans have many appetites, many lusts.
comments: This is one of two somewhat-recurring terms... -GHS
records.assessment: The source states that humans have many desires. Rendering them as both “appetites” and “lusts” adds a duplicated, bodily or sexual narrowing.
records.remedy: Use “Human beings have many desires.”

highlights.text: Humans have many appetites, many lusts.

records.jp: 欲望とは何だろう。
records.en: What appetites, what lusts? What desires?
comments: That's the actual term I'll use, but since the original means all this, and it's an explanation, putting 'em all in. -GHS
records.assessment: The source poses the singular philosophical question “What is desire?” The English replaces it with a three-item list and changes the inquiry to which desires exist.
records.remedy: Use “What is desire?”

highlights.text: What appetites, what lusts? What desires?

records.jp: 知識欲。
records.en: Knowledge. Intellectuality.
records.assessment: 知識欲 is the desire or thirst for knowledge. “Knowledge. Intellectuality.” removes the motivating desire and introduces a different trait.
records.remedy: Use “The desire for knowledge.”

highlights.text: Knowledge. Intellectuality.

records.jp: 創作欲。
records.en: Creation. Creativity.
records.assessment: 創作欲 is the desire to create. Bare “Creation. Creativity.” removes the appetitive force shared by the list.
records.remedy: Use “The desire to create.”

highlights.text: Creation. Creativity.

records.jp: 征服欲。
records.en: Conquest. Overcoming.
comments: Same as with CCA0016 -GHS
records.assessment: 征服欲 is the desire to conquer. “Overcoming” is not equivalent to conquering others or things and again removes desire.
records.remedy: Use “The desire to conquer.”

highlights.text: Conquest. Overcoming.

records.jp: 前提としての他者。
records.en: Others stand as prerequisite.
records.assessment: The source is a compressed nominal statement that other people are the prerequisite. The English requires an article before “prerequisite.”
records.remedy: Use “Other people as a prerequisite.”

highlights.text: Others stand as prerequisite.

records.jp: 多くの人が価値あると認めるものを獲得することに、欲望の根元がある。
records.en:
The principle of desire lies in the acquisition of
that which many other people confer value to.
records.assessment: The source says desire is rooted in acquiring what many people recognize as valuable. “Confer value to” uses the wrong preposition and obscures that recognition.
records.remedy: Use “The root of desire lies in acquiring what many people recognize as valuable.”

highlights.text:
The principle of desire lies in the acquisition of
that which many other people confer value to.

records.jp: さしあたっての利用目的がなくとも、人はそれを欲する。
records.en:
It is what people want even if they have
no goal they need it for in their immediate.
records.assessment: The source says people desire currency even without an immediate use for it. “No goal they need it for in their immediate” is ungrammatical and substitutes a goal for a use.
records.remedy: Use “People desire it even when they have no immediate use for it.”

highlights.text:
It is what people want even if they have
no goal they need it for in their immediate.

records.jp: 人間が欲望とともに生きる時、すでに他者の意識や価値観によって世界は染まっているのであり、またその中で人格は形成されていくのだ。
records.en:
When humans live together with desires, it's in
a world already stained by the consciousness and
the sense of values of others, that their
personality is itself by those molded and shaped.
comments: This is fairly basic stuff so I don't think I need to further comment on it. Well, let's just say that if this confuses you, then you either jumped into this at this point, or you've long given up. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the world is already colored by others’ consciousness and values, and personality forms within it. The English’s passive “personality is itself by those molded” has no grammatical structure and makes “those” the molders.
records.remedy: Use “When people live with desire, the world is already colored by others’ consciousness and values, and personality takes shape within it.”

highlights.text:
When humans live together with desires, it's in
a world already stained by the consciousness and
the sense of values of others, that their
personality is itself by those molded and shaped.

records.jp: では個であったなら。
records.en: Well then, what if he was truly Individual.
records.assessment: The source asks what happens if one were an individual. “He” adds a gendered subject, while capitalizing “Individual” gives an ordinary noun unsupported emphasis.
records.remedy: Use “Then what if one were truly an individual?”

highlights.text: Well then, what if he was truly Individual.

records.jp: いや、他者がいなくなった瞬間、欲望はその定義を失って欲求へと至る。
records.en:
No, the instant others are no more, desire loses
its very definition until it has become
a mere want.
records.assessment: The source says desire loses its definition and becomes basic need. “Until it has become” incorrectly presents that transformation as an endpoint reached over time.
records.remedy: Use “The moment others disappear, desire loses its definition and becomes mere need.”

highlights.text:
No, the instant others are no more, desire loses
its very definition until it has become
a mere want.

records.jp: 自分一人の世界で、なお知識層であろうとする者が何人いるだろう？
records.en:
In a world of their own self alone, how many
people will still want to be intellectuals?
comments: "How many will desire to remain intellectual if they are all living individually separate from others", not necessarily "how big is the intellectual class if one person alone exists in the world". Since this is for the former, not the latter, though the troll is still present. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks how many would still try to be intellectuals in a world where they are alone. “Their own self alone” is an ungrammatical reflexive construction.
records.remedy: Use “In a world where each person was alone, how many would still try to be intellectuals?”

highlights.text:
In a world of their own self alone, how many
people will still want to be intellectuals?

records.jp: 一人になれば、人は変質する。
records.en:
If a person becomes Alone, the very essence of
this person alters.
records.assessment: The source says people necessarily change when alone. “Becomes Alone” needlessly capitalizes an adjective, and “this person” awkwardly repeats the subject.
records.remedy: Use “When a person is alone, they change.”

highlights.text:
If a person becomes Alone, the very essence of
this person alters.

records.jp: 突き上げるような負の感情も、マイナスではなくなる。
records.en:
The negative emotions that try to swell out of
themselves stop being a minus point.
records.assessment: The source describes surging negative emotions ceasing to count as negative. “Swell out of themselves” is malformed, and “minus point” leaves the evaluative transformation opaque.
records.remedy: Use “Even the negative emotions surging up within a person would no longer be negative.”

highlights.text:
The negative emotions that try to swell out of
themselves stop being a minus point.

records.jp: 罪も罪でない世界なら。
records.en:
It would be a society, a world, where a sin is
not a sin.
records.assessment: The source is a conditional fragment: “If it were a world where sin was not sin.” The English turns it into a full prediction and adds “society.”
records.remedy: Use “If it were a world where sin was no longer sin.”

highlights.text:
It would be a society, a world, where a sin is
not a sin.

records.jp: この『目』は、そのためにあったのだと、天啓のように思った。
records.en:
These 『eyes』 we have exist for that purpose, I
thought as if by divine revelation.
comments: He means more than just his Mystic Eyes. Or rather, it's the opposite. And in the end, Divine Revelation. -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to the narrator’s singular marked “eye” as existing for that purpose. “These eyes we have” changes number and generalizes the eye to an inclusive group.
records.remedy: Use “I felt, like a revelation, that this ‘eye’ existed for that purpose.”

highlights.text:
These 『eyes』 we have exist for that purpose, I
thought as if by divine revelation.

records.jp: 人気のない広場に、声はよく通る。
records.en: Voices carry well in this unpopulated open space.
comments: Is he still in front of the station...? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his voice carries well across the deserted plaza. Plural “Voices” generalizes away from the specific voice in the scene.
records.remedy: Use “My voice carried well across the deserted plaza.”

highlights.text: Voices carry well in this unpopulated open space.

records.jp: 「用事があるんじゃないのかな？」
records.en: Taichi: "Do you have some business with me or something?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether the follower has some other business to attend to. “With me” invents the narrator as the object of that business.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t you have something else to do?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Do you have some business with me or something?"

records.jp: 「どうかしてる」
records.en: Taichi: "You've gone mad."
comments: This is what Kiri will often tell him and her. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says there is something wrong with the follower. “Gone mad” escalates this to insanity and changes the register.
records.remedy: Use “There’s something wrong with you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You've gone mad."

records.jp: 吐き捨てて、学校方面に歩き出す。
records.en: That I spit out, then go to walk towards the school.
records.assessment: The source says he spits the words out and starts walking toward school. “Go to walk towards” is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “I spat the words out and started walking toward school.”

highlights.text: That I spit out, then go to walk towards the school.

records.jp: いちいち構っていられない。
records.en: I don't need someone to worry about every single thing.
records.assessment: The source says he cannot stop to engage with every little thing. The English instead says he does not need someone to worry, reversing the actor and action.
records.remedy: Use “I couldn’t stop to deal with every little thing.”

highlights.text: I don't need someone to worry about every single thing.

records.jp: 気配はひたひたと追尾してきた。
records.en: The presence of a pursuit continues steady and gradual.
records.assessment: The source says the sensed presence steadily follows him. “The presence of a pursuit” turns the pursuer into an abstract property and lacks a clear subject-object relation.
records.remedy: Use “The presence kept following steadily behind me.”

highlights.text: The presence of a pursuit continues steady and gradual.

records.jp: 新鮮ではあったけど、煩わしさがまさった。
records.en: There was something refreshing and sweet to it, but it's also incredibly bothersome.
comments: 新鮮=!!!NEO-AKIRA!!! -GHSolvedthepuzzle
records.assessment: The source says the experience was fresh, but the annoyance outweighed that freshness. “Sweet” and “incredibly” are additions, and the line shifts into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “It was a fresh experience, but the annoyance outweighed the novelty.”

highlights.text: There was something refreshing and sweet to it, but it's also incredibly bothersome.

records.jp: 「……あーもー、イライラした」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, really, that made me all nervous."
records.assessment: イライラ means irritation or frustration here. “Nervous” names anxiety rather than the emotion explicitly stated.
records.remedy: Use “Ah, geez, that was irritating.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, really, that made me all nervous."

records.jp: あの存在密度には。
records.en: It's that overbearing being.
records.assessment: The source attributes the goosebumps to the entity’s extraordinary density of presence. “That overbearing being” removes the density concept and recasts it as a personality trait.
records.remedy: Use “That density of presence does it.”

highlights.text: It's that overbearing being.

records.jp: 近いかも。
records.en: ...could be nearby...
comments: Still trying to avoid the 'she' -GHS
records.assessment: “Close” evaluates whether “demon” is near the truth. The English reads it spatially as though a demon might be nearby.
records.remedy: Use “That might be close.”

highlights.text: ...could be nearby...

records.jp: がるるるるるるるる
records.en: GlRlRlRlRlRlRlRlRl!
comments: This totally sounds like a creepy roar sped up... -GHS
records.assessment: The source is a sustained animal-like growl. The consonant string “GlRl...” is not a recognizable English representation of that sound.
records.remedy: Use “Grrrrrrrrr...”

highlights.text: GlRlRlRlRlRlRlRlRl!

records.jp: 腹の虫だ。
records.en: It's my belly bug.
comments: He talks about everyone being gone, then the eyes, and then he's chased by Youko, and when she leaves the belly bug takes her place. It could be random, but the flow seen here suggests it isn't so. -GHS
records.assessment: 腹の虫 is the idiom for a rumbling stomach or hunger. “Belly bug” translates its components literally and creates a nonexistent creature.
records.remedy: Use “It was my stomach growling.”

highlights.text: It's my belly bug.

records.jp: 「食べ物のにおいがする……」
records.en: Taichi: "There's smell of food..."
records.assessment: The source says he smells food. The singular count noun “smell” requires an article in this construction.
records.remedy: Use “I smell food...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's smell of food..."

records.jp: 「おー、すいとる」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, smell that!"
records.assessment: The source remarks that the place is empty or uncrowded, leading into the low guard count. “Smell that” introduces an olfactory action disconnected from the sequence.
records.remedy: Use “Oh, it’s empty.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, smell that!"

records.jp: いつもは十人くらい立ってるのに、今日は二人だ。
records.en: There are always around ten standing around, but today it's only two.
comments: Which are going to be zero in case of off-hour. -GHS
records.assessment: The source contrasts the usual ten guards with only two today. “Today it’s only two” uses a singular dummy subject for people.
records.remedy: Use “There are usually about ten of them, but today there are only two.”

highlights.text: There are always around ten standing around, but today it's only two.

records.jp: 暑くなってきて、みんな精神的にも参ってきてるせいか欠席が多い。
records.en: It's gotten hot so, maybe because everybody's mentally cracking up, there's many not attending.
comments: Should be more evident, on second reading, what exactly this means. Except, on further readings, this is even more suspect: this is a very good explanation for why there's no one around. More importantly, the guards themselves seem to be cracking up in the heat! -GHS
records.assessment: The source says many people are absent. “There’s many” has incorrect number agreement and “not attending” lacks a natural object.
records.remedy: Use “It’s gotten hot, and perhaps everyone is mentally worn down, because many people are absent.”

highlights.text: It's gotten hot so, maybe because everybody's mentally cracking up, there's many not attending.

records.jp: だから学食も、どことなく閑散としていた。
records.en: Therefore, even the cafeteria was in many ways deserted.
comments: Though it isn't totally empty. -GHS
records.assessment: どことなく means somehow or vaguely. “In many ways” changes it to multiple identifiable respects.
records.remedy: Use “As a result, the cafeteria somehow felt deserted too.”

highlights.text: Therefore, even the cafeteria was in many ways deserted.

records.jp: おかげで競争率高めのメニューにも楽にありつける。
records.en: Thanks to that, even menus with a high rate of competition can be comfortably obtained.
records.assessment: The source refers to highly sought-after menu items. “Menus with a high rate of competition” treats menus as objects acquired and calques the competition expression.
records.remedy: Use “Thanks to that, even the most sought-after dishes were easy to get.”

highlights.text: Thanks to that, even menus with a high rate of competition can be comfortably obtained.

records.jp: いや……とあるコネを使えば、簡単にありつけるのだが。
records.en: Well... using a certain 'connection', they are always easily obtained.
comments: So, would Yusa's mom have much issue being overbearing to Taichi even if her daughter isn't exactly on good terms with him anymore? From the way Yusa's grown up to be completely incapable of expecting kindness, little things like Taichi trying to push her down shouldn't be much of an obstacle. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the narrator could obtain one easily by using a certain connection. “They are always obtained” adds habitual frequency and removes his agency.
records.remedy: Use “Though I could get one easily by using a certain connection...”

highlights.text: Well... using a certain 'connection', they are always easily obtained.

records.jp: 禁断の奥義なのだ。
records.en: It is forbidden esoterica.
comments: This is how he'll describe the Parachute Death Sentence. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls it a forbidden secret technique. Bare “esoterica” names obscure knowledge, not a technique he can deploy.
records.remedy: Use “It’s a forbidden secret technique.”

highlights.text: It is forbidden esoterica.

records.jp: あーでも、遊紗ちゃんかわいいからなぁ。
records.en: Ahhh, but Yusa-chan's adorable ain't she.
records.assessment: The English uses a tag question without the comma or question mark needed to distinguish it from the statement.
records.remedy: Use “Ah, but Yusa-chan is adorable, isn’t she?”

highlights.text: Ahhh, but Yusa-chan's adorable ain't she.

records.jp: ドカン、と怒声が学食に響く。
records.en: BOOM!, that's how those harsh words echo throughout the cafeteria.
records.assessment: The source says an explosive angry shout reverberates through the cafeteria. “Those harsh words echo” substitutes lexical harshness for the voice’s physical volume.
records.remedy: Use “Her angry shout boomed through the cafeteria.”

highlights.text: BOOM!, that's how those harsh words echo throughout the cafeteria.

records.jp: 「……声が大きいよ、おばちゃん」
records.en: Taichi: "...voice's loud, madam."
records.assessment: The source says “Your voice is loud.” The English drops the possessive subject, leaving the fragment “voice’s loud.”
records.remedy: Use “Your voice is too loud, ma’am.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...voice's loud, madam."

records.jp: 巨大な、異形と称していいてのひらが、ゴウッと眼前を横切った。
records.en: The palm of an hand so gigantic one could correctly call it heteromorphic crossed right before my eyes with a 'whoff'.
records.assessment: The article must be “a hand,” and “heteromorphic” is an opaque technical substitute for the source’s description of a grotesquely huge palm.
records.remedy: Use “A palm so huge it could be called misshapen whooshed past my face.”

highlights.text: The palm of an hand so gigantic one could correctly call it heteromorphic crossed right before my eyes with a 'whoff'.

records.jp: 太一（今の）（スキンシップ？）（直撃していたら……）（死！？）
records.en: Taichi: (That now) (skinship?) (if that had been a direct hit...) (death?!)
records.assessment: The first mental fragment means “Just now,” referring to the near blow. “That now” is not an English temporal phrase.
records.remedy: Use “(Just now) (Was that skinship?) (If it had hit me...) (Death?!)”

highlights.text: Taichi: (That now) (skinship?) (if that had been a direct hit...) (death?!)

records.jp: ついつい筒井○隆の七瀬シリーズで使われたみたいな心理表現方法を用いてしまう。
records.en: All fluky-fluky I made use of a Tsutsui Yasut*ka's Nanase Series-like Process of Intrapsychical Expression.
comments: Can't source an official translation of what I assume to be Nanase's mind-reading power. Supposing the line above is also a reference. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasutaka_Tsutsui "unconsciously" is also written Tsuitsui, so it's a really crap pun. Have an odd word that's still close enough in meaning instead. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he inadvertently uses a mode of psychological narration like that in the Nanase series. “All fluky-fluky,” the possessive article, and “Process of Intrapsychical Expression” are malformed and distort the claim.
records.remedy: Use “Without thinking, I used a style of psychological narration like the one in Tsutsui Yasut*ka’s Nanase series.”

highlights.text: All fluky-fluky I made use of a Tsutsui Yasut*ka's Nanase Series-like Process of Intrapsychical Expression.

records.jp: なんつうか七瀬繋がりってあると思うし（ねぇよ）。
records.en: For some reason I think there's a connection with Nana-se (seven - currents) (there ain't).
comments: That's no lie, it's only a reference to the number seven. -GHS
records.assessment: The source makes a loose “Nanase connection” joke and immediately denies it. The English invents an explanatory “seven-currents” gloss that is not present.
records.remedy: Use “I guess there’s some kind of Nanase connection there. (No there isn’t.)”

highlights.text: For some reason I think there's a connection with Nana-se (seven - currents) (there ain't).

records.jp: ライオンに餌をやるような気持ちで、食券を差し出す。
records.en: With the same feeling as of feeding a hungry lion, I hand over the meal ticket.
comments: See CCB2002. This reminds very much of that Belly Bug scene. -GHS
records.assessment: The source compares his feeling to feeding a lion. “Same feeling as of” is ungrammatical, and “hungry” adds a state not stated.
records.remedy: Use “Feeling as though I were feeding a lion, I held out the meal ticket.”

highlights.text: With the same feeling as of feeding a hungry lion, I hand over the meal ticket.

records.jp: 「どうしたい？　ふらついて」
records.en: Yusa's mom: "Wassit now? Ya twitchin'."
records.assessment: ふらついて says he is staggering or swaying. “Twitching” describes involuntary small jerks and is the wrong motion.
records.remedy: Use “What’s wrong? You’re staggering.”

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Wassit now? Ya twitchin'."

records.jp: 「そりゃいけないね。血肉が足りないんだよ」
records.en: Yusa's mom: "Tha'ss no good is it! Ya don't have enough blood in yer meat!"
records.assessment: The source jokingly diagnoses a lack of flesh and blood or nourishment. “Blood in your meat” decomposes 血肉 into a nonsensical literal relation.
records.remedy: Use “That’s no good. You need more meat on your bones!”

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Tha'ss no good is it! Ya don't have enough blood in yer meat!"

records.jp: 「Ｓなんてあったんですか」
records.en: Taichi: "Does S even exist?"
comments: See Taichi's internal categorization. Interesting... -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether an S set meal existed. “Does S even exist?” drops the meal-set referent and reads as an abstract question about a letter.
records.remedy: Use “There was an S set meal?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Does S even exist?"

records.jp: ヒソヒソされる。
records.en: I'm being psst-psst'd about.
comments: And since everyone here knows Yusa's her daughter... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says people are whispering about him. “Psst-psst’d” turns a sound effect into a nonexistent passive verb.
records.remedy: Use “People are whispering about me.”

highlights.text: I'm being psst-psst'd about.

records.jp: 「は、どうと申されますと？」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, what could one possibly answer to that?"
comments: He goes hyperpolite 'round here. She's truly terrifying. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks what she means by “how are things.” The English instead asks what answer could possibly be given.
records.remedy: Use “W-what do you mean, ‘how’?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, what could one possibly answer to that?"

records.jp: 「ムコっ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "In law?!?!"
records.assessment: 婿 specifically means a groom or son-in-law. “In law” is incomplete and could describe any relation by marriage.
records.remedy: Use “S-son-in-law?!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "In law?!?!"

records.jp: マスヲっ！？
records.en: The trout...?!
comments: Trout hold, below. Or, "the increase", or... -GHS
records.assessment: マスヲ invokes the son-in-law character Masuo as a joke. Translating the name as the fish “trout” destroys the cultural and phonetic callback.
records.remedy: Use “Masuo?!” and preserve the name-based joke.

highlights.text: The trout...?!

records.jp: これは……賄賂！　Ｙ炉ですか？
records.en: This is... bribery! An offer I can't refuse?!
comments: Ｙ炉 'Y' + 'furnace'. It's pronounced wairo, like the actual word for bribery. Can't source the origin; maybe just a meme of sorts. -GHS
records.assessment: The source follows “bribe” with a compact Y-marked 炉 pun. “An offer I can’t refuse” replaces the wordplay with an unrelated stock phrase.
records.remedy: Preserve or annotate the Y-marked pun rather than substituting a different idiom.

highlights.text: This is... bribery! An offer I can't refuse?!

records.jp: 噂されてる！
records.en: I'm being rumor'd about!
comments: I never knew rumor was a verb! You make up something every day. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says people are gossiping about him. “Rumor’d” is not a standard English passive verb.
records.remedy: Use “They’re gossiping about me!”

highlights.text: I'm being rumor'd about!

records.jp: 俺、今すっごく噂されちゃってる！
records.en: I am reeeally being rumor'd about right now!
records.assessment: The repeated “rumor’d” remains nonstandard and obscures the escalating realization that others are talking about him.
records.remedy: Use “They’re really gossiping about me right now!”

highlights.text: I am reeeally being rumor'd about right now!

records.jp: 「アンタもいろいろあるんだろうから、難しいこと考えなくてもいいんだよ」
records.en: Yusa's Mom: "Ye look like ya got a lots of stuff on yer mind, but don'tcha think about all th' hard stuff now!"
records.assessment: The quantifier is malformed: English permits “a lot of stuff” or “lots of stuff,” not “a lots of stuff.”
records.remedy: Use “You look like you’ve got a lot on your mind...”

highlights.text: Yusa's Mom: "Ye look like ya got a lots of stuff on yer mind, but don'tcha think about all th' hard stuff now!"

records.jp: 具は薄いワカメしかないはずのみそ汁に、なぜかカニが丸ごとぶち込まれていた。
records.en: In that Wakame that one'd expect to always be thin on ingredients, somehow, a crab got tossed in whole.
comments: Must be that dreaded Myso Syrup, which is like miso soup but evil. Where'd she get a craKinoko NASUUUUU-GHS
records.assessment: The source says a whole crab has been thrown into miso soup that should contain only thin wakame. The English makes “that Wakame” the container and calls it thin on ingredients.
records.remedy: Use “A whole crab had somehow been tossed into the miso soup that should have contained nothing but thin wakame.”

highlights.text: In that Wakame that one'd expect to always be thin on ingredients, somehow, a crab got tossed in whole.

records.jp: 「天下りで……」
records.en: Voice: "Crony capitalism..."
comments: Literally "retired government officials taking lucrative jobs in the private sector", although there's something about golden parachuting it's obviously got nothing to do with this particular instance. Or, because SYMBOLISM!!!, "descent from heaven". -GHS
records.assessment: 天下り refers to officials descending into cushy private-sector posts, not the broader economic system of crony capitalism.
records.remedy: Use “Through amakudari...” or “Through bureaucratic golden parachutes...”

highlights.text: Voice: "Crony capitalism..."

records.jp: 「……参拝問題の当事者……」
records.en: Voice: "...parties related to the issue of formal visits to the shrine of..."
comments: Probably just a tone-change joke. The sentences flow into each other to an extent, but not in a way that appears obvious. -GHS
records.assessment: The source identifies someone involved in the shrine-visit controversy. The English trails off after “shrine of,” leaving the object and thought syntactically incomplete.
records.remedy: Use “...someone involved in the shrine-visit controversy...”

highlights.text: Voice: "...parties related to the issue of formal visits to the shrine of..."

records.jp: 「ん？　なんだい、これくらい食べられるだろうよ、男の子なんだから！」
records.en: Yusa's mom: "Hm? Whassat, inn'this 'bout how much ya eat, yer a man after all!"
records.assessment: The source says this amount should be edible because he is a boy. The dialect string “inn’this ’bout how much ya eat” is grammatically incoherent and loses the assertion of capacity.
records.remedy: Use “What? You can eat this much—you’re a growing boy!”

highlights.text: Yusa's mom: "Hm? Whassat, inn'this 'bout how much ya eat, yer a man after all!"

records.jp: 自重の倍ほどの重みが、俺を床に押しつけた。
records.en: The weight of about two unloaded freight trucks pushed me down to the floor.
comments: It's about the doubling of his own weight, but the term's also used for empty vehicles (when it's not about self-care and prudence?) and this is both funnier and technically not (too) incorrect. See CCD0021 yet again. So not funny in retrospect. -GHS
records.assessment: The source compares the downward force to roughly twice the woman’s own body weight. “Two unloaded freight trucks” invents a radically different comparison and scale.
records.remedy: Use “A weight about twice her own body weight drove me to the floor.”

highlights.text: The weight of about two unloaded freight trucks pushed me down to the floor.

records.jp: 遊紗ちゃん……はやく家を出ないと、太らされてしまうよ。
records.en: Yusa-chan... if you don't hurry and leave home, all fat you'll be made to become.
comments: IOW, she's pretty much certain to be overfed. So when she's pushed, what's gonna come out of her is what's been put there by his own mother... -GHS
records.assessment: The source warns that Yusa will be fattened up if she does not leave home soon. “All fat you’ll be made to become” is malformed English.
records.remedy: Use “Yusa-chan... if you don’t leave home soon, she’ll fatten you up.”

highlights.text: Yusa-chan... if you don't hurry and leave home, all fat you'll be made to become.

records.jp: 「あやかりたいもんだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "You sharing some of that fortune?"
records.assessment: Tomoki states that he would like to share in Taichi’s good fortune. The English turns this into a question asking whether Taichi is currently sharing.
records.remedy: Use “I’d like some of that good fortune.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "You sharing some of that fortune?"

records.jp: 「あやかってくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Share my fortune I do."
records.assessment: Taichi invites him to share the fortune. “Share my fortune I do” uses an unsupported inverted parody register.
records.remedy: Use “Be my guest.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Share my fortune I do."

records.jp: 「こんなに食えない」
records.en: Tomoki: "I can't eat all this."
records.assessment: Taichi is the one saying he cannot eat the oversized meal. The English labels the line as Tomoki’s, reversing the speaker.
records.remedy: Use the Taichi speaker label: “I can’t eat all this.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I can't eat all this."

records.jp: 「さっきまで桜庭とパン食ってたんだけど、足りなくてさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "I was eating bread with Sakuraba 'til like now, but that's not enough."
comments: This could mean he was eating bread earlier in the day, which fits the idea that the cafeteria is less than strict on that stuff. That's why Sakuraba's first hour is Curry Bread. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the bread eaten until just now was not enough. “’Til like now” and present “that’s not enough” mishandle the completed meal.
records.remedy: Use “I was eating bread with Sakuraba until just now, but it wasn’t enough.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I was eating bread with Sakuraba 'til like now, but that's not enough."

records.jp: 「元運動部だもんな」
records.en: Taichi: "Because you're ex-sports club."
records.assessment: The source calls Tomoki a former member of a sports club. “You’re ex-sports club” treats the club itself as an adjective and omits membership.
records.remedy: Use “You’re a former athlete, after all.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because you're ex-sports club."

records.jp: 「筋トレとかもうやってないんだけどなぁ」
records.en: Taichi: "But I'm not doing physical training or anything anymore."
records.assessment: Tomoki replies that he no longer does strength training. The English assigns his first-person reply to Taichi.
records.remedy: Use the Tomoki speaker label.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But I'm not doing physical training or anything anymore."

records.jp: 「んなバカな。余分な脂肪がつかない体質になるから、適度に筋トレはしといた方がいい」
records.en: Taichi: "Yammoron. If you got yourself a constitution that doesn't grab excess weight, it's better to only do muscle training with moderation."
comments: Wouldn't want to end up with his cut tendons on manual drive? Seriously, this is kinda random. -GHS
records.assessment: The source rejects the idea that no muscles are better and explains that moderate training builds a body less prone to excess fat. “Yammoron” is meaningless, and the conditional relation is reversed.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t be ridiculous. Moderate strength training is better, because it makes your body less likely to put on excess fat.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yammoron. If you got yourself a constitution that doesn't grab excess weight, it's better to only do muscle training with moderation."

records.jp: 「ここの学食業者のがマイフェイバリッド・カレーパンだとか言ってさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "The curry bread that the contractor of this cafeteria makes is Mai Favorite Curry Bread, he says."
comments: I wonder if Tanaka just transliterates stuff himself, as he keeps using odd uncommon spellings. More common is フェイバリット -GHS
records.assessment: The source’s deliberately off “my favorite” wording is part of Sakuraba’s quoted voice. “Mai” turns the possessive into what looks like a personal name.
records.remedy: Use a conspicuously affected form of “my favorite curry bread” without changing “my” into a name.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "The curry bread that the contractor of this cafeteria makes is Mai Favorite Curry Bread, he says."

records.jp: 「アホ舌だな」
records.en: Taichi: "Dumb tongue, yeah."
records.assessment: This second agreement that Sakuraba has a foolish palate is Tomoki’s response. The English repeats the Taichi label and erases the exchange.
records.remedy: Use the Tomoki speaker label.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Dumb tongue, yeah."

records.jp: 「くそっ、食っても食っても減らん！」
records.en: Taichi: "Dammit, I eat and I eat but it don't decrease!"
records.assessment: The thing that will not diminish is the singular pile of food, not a plural object. “It don’t decrease” has subject-verb disagreement.
records.remedy: Use “Damn it, no matter how much I eat, it doesn’t get any smaller!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Dammit, I eat and I eat but it don't decrease!"

records.jp: 「もらってくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Help I need."
records.assessment: Taichi tells Tomoki to take more food. “Help I need” instead says Taichi needs assistance and uses malformed inversion.
records.remedy: Use “Please, take some.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Help I need."

records.jp: 「どういうコネだよ……」
records.en: Tomoki: "What connection's even that, man..."
records.assessment: The source asks what kind of connection could produce a crab in soup. “What connection’s even that” is not an idiomatic interrogative construction.
records.remedy: Use “What kind of connection is that...?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "What connection's even that, man..."

records.jp: 「世界最強のサブミッション、マスヲホールド（婿固め）だ」
records.en: Taichi: "It is the World's Strongest Submission, The Trout Hold (son-in-law clampdown)."
comments: Best I can do is this: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sazae-san it's long running, likely to be widely understood in Japan, written by a person with Machiko in the name (see below for more Machiko), a character named マスオ Masuo appears, his name is explicitly trout-inspired, and is a son-in-law.

Now, the manga's gone on for like 30 years, the anime has well over 6000 (!!!!!!!!!!!!) half-hour episodes, most of which are unavailable anywhere due to the author's wishes, and though there's at least one certain and another possible reference to same, see CCC0039 and CCD2002, this might be all completely unrelated.

The only alternative joke I got is a really bad fat joke ("hold the mass" with a pun for trout in there), or the "increase in mass" above, which is equally awful. Tanaka says in the Materials Book interview that in the PS2/PSP versions this would be expanded on, but I still got nothing.

Anyway, the term means 'son-in-law consolidation', but also has the implication of 'pledge', so she's securing him as son-in-law via corruption. As holding a trout's hard, according to such reliable sources as random googling, then adapted so it fits both. -GHS
records.assessment: The move name continues the Masuo/婿 son-in-law pun. “Trout Hold” again translates Masuo as a fish and destroys the named callback.
records.remedy: Use “Masuo Hold” while preserving the parenthetical son-in-law pun.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is the World's Strongest Submission, The Trout Hold (son-in-law clampdown)."

records.jp: 「やっぱ、母親似なのかな」
records.en: Tomoki: "Really, she's gonna look like her mother right."
comments: = he doesn't know Yusa yet -GHS
records.assessment: Tomoki wonders whether Yusa resembles her mother now. “She’s gonna look like” changes resemblance into a future prediction.
records.remedy: Use “Does she take after her mother after all?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Really, she's gonna look like her mother right."

records.jp: 「いや、すっげー可愛い眼鏡っ子。俺になついてんの。言うこと全部信じるし、たまらん」
records.en: Taichi: "Nah, she's this reeeally cute meganekko. She got kinda attached to me. She believes my words to the last, it's unbearable."
comments: Japanese is to fetish term what English is to tech stuff, never forget. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she believes everything he says and that this is irresistible. “Believes my words to the last” is unidiomatic, while “unbearable” gives the delight a negative valence.
records.remedy: Use “She believes everything I tell her. I can’t get enough of it.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nah, she's this reeeally cute meganekko. She got kinda attached to me. She believes my words to the last, it's unbearable."

records.jp: 「スイス銀行に口座を持っちゃうようなアグレッシブな固ゆでジョブに就くだろう俺は、カタギのクーニャンとニャンニャンしちゃうわけにはいかんのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "I intend to ascend to an aggressive tough-simmered job the likes of which you need an account in a swiss bank, I can't afford to meow-meow with an honest frau."
comments: That's "hard-boiled" written in kanji, which is as silly as the translation. http://vndb.org/v1 (kidding, but like 95~~~ 99.999% of the words in Japanese, nyan-nyan IS an euphemism for sex). I'm assuming he wants to be an extremely well-paid author of texts with more or less philosophical and/or pretentious overtones. Reminds me of someone, but I can't tanaka who. Original term is "[honest] kuunyan", which has nothing to do with nyan and only means "unmarried woman" (or "chinese girl"). Since there's lots of fraulein 'round here, that should work. -GHS
records.assessment: The source’s comic hard-boiled persona imagines a Swiss-bank-account job and says he cannot fool around with an ordinary Chinese girl. “Tough-simmered” literalizes hard-boiled, and “frau” changes Chinese クーニャン to German.
records.remedy: Use “I’m headed for an aggressive hard-boiled job that calls for a Swiss bank account, so I can’t fool around with an ordinary civilian girl.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I intend to ascend to an aggressive tough-simmered job the likes of which you need an account in a swiss bank, I can't afford to meow-meow with an honest frau."

records.jp: 「激高。あかんです。担任もコイツやばすぎって感じで白い目してたし」
records.en: Taichi: "Frenzily high. Most hopeless. Teacher in charge stared at me with dead eyes that just said, man this guy's way dangerous."
comments: 激高 the kanji are "super" and "high", but it means "frenzied". Second is formal. -GHS
records.assessment: 激高 here means extremely high, not frenzied. “Most hopeless” is a fragment, and the teacher’s disapproving look is rendered as literal dead eyes.
records.remedy: Use “Extremely high. It’s bad. Even my homeroom teacher gave me a look like, ‘This guy is seriously dangerous.’”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Frenzily high. Most hopeless. Teacher in charge stared at me with dead eyes that just said, man this guy's way dangerous."

records.jp: 「うわ、それ偏差値だったらなぁ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Uhwah, if only those were your grades!"
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_grading_in_Japan see also CCD1001 -GHS
records.assessment: 偏差値 is a standardized deviation score, not grades generally. The joke depends on 84 being excellent as that particular kind of score.
records.remedy: Use “Wow—if only that were your deviation score.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Uhwah, if only those were your grades!"

records.jp: 「そーなのよ。まっずいよなぁ。俺、やばいことになっちゃうかも」
records.en: Taichi: "Indeeed, yeah. Sooo bad innit. Me, I might be turnin' into something real nasty I might."
records.assessment: The source worries that he himself may end up in serious trouble. “Turnin’ into something real nasty” changes an adverse situation into a transformation and repeats “I might.”
records.remedy: Use “Exactly. This is bad. I might be in serious trouble.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeeed, yeah. Sooo bad innit. Me, I might be turnin' into something real nasty I might."

records.jp: 「……だって、俺外障だし」
records.en: Tomoki: "...told ya, I'm External Damage."
comments: Gunjou lingo, though it's rarely recurring. -GHS
records.assessment: 外障 denotes an external or physical disability in this classification. “External Damage” sounds like damage to an object and misstates the status.
records.remedy: Use “I told you, I’m physically disabled.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...told ya, I'm External Damage."

records.jp: 「あー、ラバ（桜庭の蔑称）も低いんだろうな」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, Sack (disparaging nickname for Sakuraba) should also be pretty low scoring."
comments: Adapted. Original was Raba, meaning mule now it's... oh fuck... sackuraba... what have I done -GHS
records.assessment: The disparaging nickname ラバ is derived from Sakuraba’s name. “Sack” does not preserve that derivation or sound.
records.remedy: Use “Raba” or another nickname visibly derived from Sakuraba.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, Sack (disparaging nickname for Sakuraba) should also be pretty low scoring."

records.jp: 「あいつ１５だったかな」
records.en: Tomoki: "That guy was about 15 I think."
comments: Hoh, this one doesn't seem to fit. Though given Sakuraba, that'd be normal. But add all three... 116=1+1+6=8. -GHS
records.assessment: The surrounding figures are percentages from the same test. “15” omits the percent sign and leaves the measure less explicit than the source context.
records.remedy: Use “I think his was about 15 percent.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That guy was about 15 I think."

records.en: Tomoki: "...iii-dem."
comments: Matches voice. -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply means “Agreed” or “Same here.” The stretched Latin “iii-dem” is an unsupported affected register.
records.remedy: Use “...Agreed.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...iii-dem."

records.jp: 「やりにくくってしょうがない」
records.en: Taichi: "It's gonna be hard but there's no other ways."
records.assessment: Taichi says their quarrel makes things unbearably awkward for him. The English says reconciliation itself will be hard but unavoidable, changing both subject and relation.
records.remedy: Use “Their fighting makes everything too awkward for me.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's gonna be hard but there's no other ways."

records.jp: 「宮澄先輩が？」
records.en: Taichi: "Miyasumi-senpai? Her?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether Miyasumi-senpai is the one who betrayed him. The isolated “Her?” redundantly adds a second pronoun question.
records.remedy: Use “Miyasumi-senpai did?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Miyasumi-senpai? Her?"

records.jp: 友貴とみみ先輩は姉弟である。
records.en: Tomoki and Mimi-senpai are siblings,
comments: Hmmm, but CCA0027 implies he doesn't have a nickname for her yet. Maybe things were just not kept quite straight. -GHS
records.assessment: The source specifies that Tomoki and Mimi-senpai are older sister and younger brother. Generic “siblings” removes their gender and order, both relevant to the address-form exchange.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki and Mimi-senpai are sister and brother.”

highlights.text: Tomoki and Mimi-senpai are siblings,

records.jp: 「っつーか走れないんだろうに」
records.en: Taichi: "Wait, you can't run wasn't it?"
records.assessment: The source points out that Tomoki cannot run. “You can’t run wasn’t it?” combines present and past auxiliaries ungrammatically.
records.remedy: Use “Besides, you can’t run anyway.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wait, you can't run wasn't it?"

records.jp: 「帰宅部になったら、好きなだけ漫画読めると思ったのになぁ」
records.en: Tomoki: "I thought if I was in the Going Home Club, I could read aaall the manga I like."
comments: Hey, like Taichi at the end! -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he expected to read as much manga as he wanted. “All the manga I like” changes unlimited quantity into the set of titles he likes.
records.remedy: Use “I thought I could read as much manga as I wanted.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I thought if I was in the Going Home Club, I could read aaall the manga I like."

records.jp: 「なんでいまさら姉貴と仲良く部活動しなきゃなんないのよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Why do I even have to go and get all along with Aneki and have happy club activities after all that!"
comments: Supposing he means their parents' divorce due to Misato. -GHS
records.assessment: The source complains about now having to do club activities amicably with his sister. “Go and get all along” is malformed, and “happy” adds an emotional characterization.
records.remedy: Use “Why do I have to start doing club activities all buddy-buddy with my sister now?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Why do I even have to go and get all along with Aneki and have happy club activities after all that!"

records.jp: それは一年前の思い出だった。
records.en:
These were memories
from one year ago.
records.assessment: The source refers to the preceding sequence as one memory from a year ago. The English changes singular “it was a memory” to plural “these were memories.”
records.remedy: Use “That was a memory from one year ago.”

highlights.text:
These were memories
from one year ago.

records.jp: 思ったまま口にしてしまった。
records.en: Dammit, thoughts passed through the mouth!
comments: Or, "thoughts passed through my mom's mouth". May be stretching it... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he accidentally spoke exactly what he was thinking. “Thoughts passed through the mouth” is an impersonal calque that does not express his action.
records.remedy: Use “I accidentally said exactly what I was thinking.”

highlights.text: Dammit, thoughts passed through the mouth!

records.jp: 「思ったまま口にしないように」
records.en: Nanaka: "I wish you wouldn't pass thoughts through the mouth."
comments: ...then again, this seems clear enough, really. -GHS
records.assessment: Nanaka tells him not to voice every thought. Repeating “pass thoughts through the mouth” preserves the same non-English construction.
records.remedy: Use “Try not to say everything that crosses your mind.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "I wish you wouldn't pass thoughts through the mouth."

records.jp: ばれていた。
records.en: Discovered.
records.assessment: The source means she had seen through him or caught what he was doing. Bare “Discovered” does not specify what was discovered and can imply a new find.
records.remedy: Use “She saw right through me.”

highlights.text: Discovered.
