records.jp: 「あやしいんだよなー、この女。素性は不明だし。見たこと無い制服だし」
records.en: Taichi: "Suspicious, ain't she, this female. Origins and background unknown. Uniform that I have never seen."
records.assessment: The source’s suspicions form connected colloquial sentences. “This female,” “Origins and background unknown,” and “Uniform that...” are unnatural fragments with an unsupported clinical register.
records.remedy: Use “This woman is suspicious. I don’t know who she is, and I’ve never seen that uniform before.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Suspicious, ain't she, this female. Origins and background unknown. Uniform that I have never seen."

records.jp: 「……開き直って思考を言葉に仮託しないように」
records.en: Nanaka: "...I wish you wouldn't turn defiant and use thoughts as pretext for words."
records.assessment: She tells him not to get defiant and pass his thoughts off as spoken words. “Use thoughts as pretext for words” reverses the representational relation.
records.remedy: Use “And don’t get defiant and start passing your thoughts off as dialogue.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...I wish you wouldn't turn defiant and use thoughts as pretext for words."

records.jp: 「七香って名前だって本当なのかどうか」
records.en: Taichi: "Nanaka she says her name is, but is that the truth?"
records.assessment: The source questions whether Nanaka is even her real name. “Nanaka she says her name is” uses malformed inversion.
records.remedy: Use “For all I know, even the name Nanaka may be fake.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nanaka she says her name is, but is that the truth?"

records.jp: 「……うっさいわね。細かいことグダグダ言うんじゃないわよ」
records.en: Nanaka: "...shaddap you. Don't just keep fussing tediously on the details."
records.assessment: The source tells him not to ramble about petty details. “Fussing tediously on the details” uses the wrong preposition and redundant adverb.
records.remedy: Use “Shut up. Stop going on and on about every little detail.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...shaddap you. Don't just keep fussing tediously on the details."

records.jp: 「まぁねん」
records.en: Nanaka: "Yah whatev'."
comments: Unlistenable moe words. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is an easygoing “Yeah” or “I guess.” “Whatever” adds dismissal toward the conversation.
records.remedy: Use “Yeah, I guess.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Yah whatev'."

records.jp: びっしりと指さして。
records.en: She points close at me.
records.assessment: The source says she points sharply or decisively. “Points close at me” changes manner into physical proximity.
records.remedy: Use “She pointed sharply at me.”

highlights.text: She points close at me.

records.jp: 「一回一回が、大事な人生でしょうが！　調子こいてるといつまでもいつまでも無駄にしちゃって、そのうち存在自体が固定行動に固着しちゃうんだからね！」
records.en: Nanaka: "Once, just once, live like your life's precious! But you get caught in the moment and always but always waste it all, and before you know it your very existence is stuck into fixed behaviors!"
comments: This is sooort of important. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says every single occasion in life is precious, then warns repeated waste hardens existence into fixed behavior. “Once, just once, live” changes the distributive claim into a one-time command.
records.remedy: Use “Every single moment matters in a life! If you keep wasting them, your whole existence will eventually harden into fixed behavior!”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Once, just once, live like your life's precious! But you get caught in the moment and always but always waste it all, and before you know it your very existence is stuck into fixed behaviors!"

records.jp: 「可能性ってのはそーいう性質があるんだから！　ウィン○ウズだって一時キャッシュのせいでリセットしたつもりでもエラーを繰り返すことがあるでしょーに！　ことに今は―――」
records.en: Nanaka: "Because possibilities have that as their nature! It's like when you go to reset Wi***ws because of problems in the temporary cache and then you find that it has the same error over again! Especially now it's---"
comments: Nanaka's being quite inaccurate here. "一時キャッシュ" is the temporary cache... of an Internet browser. If that cache gets corrupted, then you gotta clear it, not reset the PC; then again, that's the whole point, isn't it? It works exactly like this in the time loop: he clears the RAM over and over, but the content of the hokora ain't gonna change. -GHS
records.assessment: The source analogizes possibility to errors recurring after an apparent reset because a temporary cache remains. The English says the cache caused unspecified problems before the reset, weakening the residual-cache relation.
records.remedy: Use “Even Wi***ws can repeat the same error after you think you’ve reset it, because of the temporary cache.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Because possibilities have that as their nature! It's like when you go to reset Wi***ws because of problems in the temporary cache and then you find that it has the same error over again! Especially now it's---"

records.jp: 「こんなキューティーつかまえて貴様なんて言うなあ！」
records.en: Nanaka: "Ya don't call this kyute catch a 'bastard' you DON'T!"
records.assessment: The source says not to call a cutie like her 貴様. “This kyute catch” is ungrammatical and turns つかまえて into literal catching.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t call a cutie like me ‘you bastard’!”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Ya don't call this kyute catch a 'bastard' you DON'T!"

records.jp: 高速でスピンしつつ斜めに跳ね上がり、水平になった状態で地面に叩きつけられた。
records.en: While spinning at highway speeds I am sprung diagonally, and as my status became horizontal I smacked into the ground.
comments: Highway speeds seemed somehow weirdly appropriate. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he spins at high speed, springs diagonally upward, becomes horizontal, and slams into the ground. “Highway speeds” invents a road-specific measure, and “as my status became horizontal” is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “Spinning at high speed, I flew diagonally upward, leveled out horizontally, and slammed into the ground.”

highlights.text: While spinning at highway speeds I am sprung diagonally, and as my status became horizontal I smacked into the ground.

records.jp: この娘、コミック力場を発生させることができるとは。
records.en: This girl is capable of generating Comic Force Fields.
comments: Curiously, a Comic Force Field is a contrasting definition to 'real science' in Yanagita Rikao's series of books on manga/anime physics. Unfortunately I can't source which is the origin (or if it even is either). There's relatively little in English, and no official translation I could find.
http://d.hatena.ne.jp/keyword/%A5%B3%A5%DF%A5%C3%A5%AF%CE%CF%BE%EC
http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%9F%B3%E7%94%B0%E7%90%86%E7%A7%91%E9%9B%84
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C5%ABs%C5%8D_Kagaku_Dokuho
Oh, but there IS a manga of hers translated: http://mangafox.me/manga/kuusou_kagaku_edison/ though it doesn't seem quite on this subject. -GHS
records.assessment: The source identifies one comic force field generated by the girl. The unexplained plural “Force Fields” changes the number.
records.remedy: Use “This girl can generate a Comic Force Field.”

highlights.text: This girl is capable of generating Comic Force Fields.

records.jp: ※コミック力場＝太一科学。スカラー電磁学やエーテル宇宙論、昇騰機関などと並ぶ超科学理論のひとつ。あらゆる物理現象を加速すると同時に緩和する。
records.en: * Comic Force Field = Science-Taichinism.
records.assessment: The source note continues beyond the equation: it classifies the force field among several super-scientific theories and explains that it both accelerates and moderates all physical phenomena. The English omits that entire definition.
records.remedy: Translate the complete explanatory note, including its peer theories and dual physical effect.

highlights.text: * Comic Force Field = Science-Taichinism.

records.jp: 助け起こしてもらう。
records.en: She graciously helped me to my feet.
records.assessment: The source only says she helps him up. “Graciously” adds an approving manner judgment not stated.
records.remedy: Use “She helped me to my feet.”

highlights.text: She graciously helped me to my feet.

records.jp: 「しょうがないヤツ」
records.en: Nanaka: "There are no ways for you, really."
comments: See CCX0001 -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls him a hopeless or troublesome guy. “There are no ways for you” is not an English characterization.
records.remedy: Use “You’re hopeless.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "There are no ways for you, really."

records.jp: 呆れ半分、ため息を落とす。
records.en: Half-disgusted, she lets a sigh fall.
records.assessment: 呆れ describes exasperation or disbelief here, not disgust. The English gives her a harsher emotion.
records.remedy: Use “Half exasperated, she let out a sigh.”

highlights.text: Half-disgusted, she lets a sigh fall.

records.jp: 「あ、ほっぺたに血」
records.en: Nanaka: "Ah, blood's on your cheeky."
records.assessment: The source points out blood on his cheek. “Cheeky” is an adjective or playful noun, not the anatomical noun required.
records.remedy: Use “Ah, there’s blood on your cheek.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Ah, blood's on your cheeky."

records.jp: その時、七香の顔に去来した表情を、俺はうまく表現できない。
records.en: I can't describe well those recurring expression that were on Nanaka's face at that moment.
records.assessment: The source refers to one hard-to-describe expression passing across Nanaka’s face. “Those recurring expression” has number disagreement and makes it multiple recurring expressions.
records.remedy: Use “I can’t adequately describe the expression that crossed Nanaka’s face then.”

highlights.text: I can't describe well those recurring expression that were on Nanaka's face at that moment.

records.jp: 泣きそうでもあったし、笑っているようでもあった。
records.en: There was something of the crying, there was something of the laughing.
records.assessment: The source says she looked on the verge of tears and also as though she were smiling. “Something of the crying/laughing” is ungrammatical and turns expressions into activities.
records.remedy: Use “She looked ready to cry, yet also as though she were smiling.”

highlights.text: There was something of the crying, there was something of the laughing.

records.jp: 掠れるような声が、唇から流れて。
records.en: A voice that feels roughened flows from her lips.
records.assessment: The source describes a hoarse, faint voice flowing from her lips. “A voice that feels roughened” assigns tactile feeling to the voice and is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “A faint, hoarse voice flowed from her lips.”

highlights.text: A voice that feels roughened flows from her lips.

records.jp: 潤んだ瞳とともに。
records.en: together with her damp eyes.
records.assessment: 潤んだ瞳 are moist or tear-filled eyes in an emotional context. “Damp eyes” sounds physically wet and misses the conventional emotional description.
records.remedy: Use “Along with her moist, tear-filled eyes.”

highlights.text: together with her damp eyes.

records.jp: 現実人間であるところの俺の脳は『ＫＩＳＳされる！？』というシチュ的にそれしかありえない結末を容易に予測してのけて。
records.en: Whereas this brain I have as a real human yet easily pulls off the prediction that we are in a 'chewation-like Event that has the name "I'LL BE KISSED?!" with all other conclusions impossible.
comments: "Sichu" is actually technical term, ergo 'chewation-like (and I still specified with Event). This is far funnier considering he's not so much wrong, but far too right. His too human brain has confused his mother for the osananajimi. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his real-human brain easily predicts the only situationally plausible conclusion: he is about to be kissed. The English is syntactically incoherent and invents “chewation-like Event.”
records.remedy: Use “My real-human brain easily predicted the only ending the situation allowed: ‘I’m about to be KISSED!?’”

highlights.text: Whereas this brain I have as a real human yet easily pulls off the prediction that we are in a 'chewation-like Event that has the name "I'LL BE KISSED?!" with all other conclusions impossible.

records.jp: 七香の顔が五センチに迫った時にはもう、キス後に『いかにそれっぽく振る舞うか』といった体面処理について検討していたりするわけだが。
records.en: At the moment Nanaka's face is but five centimeters away, I am yet already in the process of elaborating post-kiss face-saving responses such as "what sort of behavior is that?!"
records.assessment: Before the kiss he is already considering how to act convincingly afterward. The quoted “what sort of behavior is that?!” instead sounds like a rebuke and does not translate いかにそれっぽく振る舞うか.
records.remedy: Use “By the time her face was five centimeters away, I was already considering how to look suitably convincing after the kiss.”

highlights.text: At the moment Nanaka's face is but five centimeters away, I am yet already in the process of elaborating post-kiss face-saving responses such as "what sort of behavior is that?!"

records.jp: ……実際こっちのがリアルなのだが、世の物語にほとんど採用されていない理由は、リアルすぎて物語性とうまく親和しないんだということが素人の俺にもありありとわかった。
records.en: ...but while this of mine is realistic, the reason that in the tales of the world it is almost never employed is that stories with an overly realistic nature do not inspire much affinity, and that is something vividly understood even by an amateur such as I.
comments: Paraphrasis: Reality is Unrealistic. The irony in this thing is subtle, considering this story is altogether too realistic in a sense. -GHS
records.assessment: The source concludes that this mental process is realistic but too realistic to mesh with narrativity, which explains its absence from stories. The English says realistic stories fail to ‘inspire affinity’ and tangles the causal relation.
records.remedy: Use “This is more realistic, but even I could see that it is too real to mesh with storytelling, which is why stories almost never use it.”

highlights.text: ...but while this of mine is realistic, the reason that in the tales of the world it is almost never employed is that stories with an overly realistic nature do not inspire much affinity, and that is something vividly understood even by an amateur such as I.

records.jp: と内心うんうん頷いてたりして。
records.en: And those are the innermost thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement.
records.assessment: The source says he is inwardly nodding along with his own conclusion. “Thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement” is a heavily calqued construction.
records.remedy: Use “I nodded sagely to myself.”

highlights.text: And those are the innermost thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement.

records.jp: 舌を頬に貼りつけて舐めあげる行為を、ＫＩＳＳと称すればのことだが。
records.en: But for the act of putting a tongue on a cheek and licking up to even take the name of K-I-S-S...
records.assessment: The source conditionally says this was a kiss only if pressing a tongue to a cheek and licking upward can be called one. The English is a fragment that never completes that condition.
records.remedy: Use “That is, if pressing your tongue to someone’s cheek and licking upward can be called a KISS.”

highlights.text: But for the act of putting a tongue on a cheek and licking up to even take the name of K-I-S-S...

records.jp: 拳で側頭部を打つ、打つ、打つ！！
records.en: Fist to the side of the head and strike, strike, strike!!!
comments: SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS
records.assessment: The source explicitly says the narrator strikes his own temple with his fist again and again. The English drops the subject and possessive, reading like an instruction.
records.remedy: Use “I struck myself in the temple with my fist again and again!”

highlights.text: Fist to the side of the head and strike, strike, strike!!!

records.jp: 「自分で自分をっ！？」
records.en: Nanaka: "But, yourself, to yourself?!"
comments: So she sounds adequately confused. Not that she doesn't know who he's talking to. -GHS
records.assessment: Nanaka is shocked that he is hitting himself. “But, yourself, to yourself” does not form that reflexive action coherently.
records.remedy: Use “Y-you’re hitting yourself!?”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "But, yourself, to yourself?!"

records.jp: 「なにがリアリティか！　なにが親和か！　頭良いつもりか俺様野郎が！　人以下であることを国際的に証明されている分際で！」
records.en: Taichi: "Reality, are you kidding me! Affinity, are you kidding me! The Greatness that is I thinks he's so smart, the worthless son of a bitch! Your social standing is that of someone who has been internationally proven to be subhuman!"
comments: ore-sama-yarou. He's so specific, and he forgets so easily... this is what Fixed Behaviors are. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is self-directed abuse: he mocks his own pretensions and internationally demonstrated subhuman score. “The Greatness that is I thinks” shifts between first and third person, while “social standing” is added.
records.remedy: Use a coherent first-person self-rebuke preserving the reality, affinity, pseudo-intellectual, and test-score insults.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Reality, are you kidding me! Affinity, are you kidding me! The Greatness that is I thinks he's so smart, the worthless son of a bitch! Your social standing is that of someone who has been internationally proven to be subhuman!"

records.jp: 「いわゆるひとつの自分がゴミであることを自覚していなければならないのです」
records.en: Taichi: "This one has been making too many wrong mistakes and must therefore awaken to the reality of being garbage."
comments: That "iwayuru hitotsu no", which makes zero sense in that context, connects to a trope about http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeo_Nagashima which is sort of Japan's Yogi Berra in the sense he speaks sort of weird. Here's a book of his sayings http://www.amazon.co.jp/%E3%81%84%E3%82%8F%E3%82%86%E3%82%8B%E3%81%B2%E3%81%A8%E3%81%A4%E3%81%AE%E9%95%B7%E5%B6%8B%E8%8C%82%E9%9B%84%E8%AA%9E%E9%8C%B2-%E8%97%A4%E6%9C%AC-%E7%BE%A9%E4%B8%80/dp/4898272177 titles reads "iwayuru hitotsu no Shigeo Nagashima goroku".

It's more baseball stuff, as it recurs for reasons I guess to be simply that Tanaka likes baseball, and it's suddenly formal, so the intended effect would be humorous, i.e. Taichi's not quite accepting of this. Of course there's no official translation, so have a Yogi-ism instead. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says one must recognize that the so-called self is garbage. The English invents a history of “too many wrong mistakes” as the reason.
records.remedy: Use “One must recognize that this thing called the self is garbage.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "This one has been making too many wrong mistakes and must therefore awaken to the reality of being garbage."

records.jp: 「群青には無識者もたくさんいるから」
records.en: Taichi: "Because, there's many people who aren't really aware in Gunjou."
comments: The Experts, see CCC4009. -GHS
records.assessment: The plural existential subject requires “there are,” not “there’s.”
records.remedy: Use “There are many unaware people in Gunjou.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because, there's many people who aren't really aware in Gunjou."

records.jp: 「俺はいつもこわかったんだ。傷つけてしまわないかって」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm always living with fear. I don't want to hurt."
comments: These and the following are entirely ambiguous. It's far from clear who'd be doing the hurting here, as it should be; Taichi's a good candidate for either, given his backstory. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he has always feared that he might hurt them. “I don’t want to hurt” omits the object and changes fear of a possible act into a present preference.
records.remedy: Use “I’ve always been afraid that I might hurt them.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm always living with fear. I don't want to hurt."

records.jp: 「猫が車の前に飛び出すみたいに」
records.en: Taichi: "It's like a cat running out in front a car."
records.assessment: The source compares it to a cat darting in front of a car. The English omits “of” after “in front.”
records.remedy: Use “Like a cat darting out in front of a car.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's like a cat running out in front a car."

records.jp: 「……自制しないといけない。細心の注意でもって」
records.en: Taichi: "...having no self-control is unacceptable. You have to be meticulously careful."
records.assessment: The source says he must restrain himself with meticulous care. The English condemns lacking self-control in general, then shifts the instruction to “you.”
records.remedy: Use “I have to restrain myself—with the utmost care.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...having no self-control is unacceptable. You have to be meticulously careful."

records.jp: 不思議と、猥雑なものは感じない。
records.en: Inexplicably, I feel nothing out of order.
records.assessment: 猥雑 refers to something vulgar, obscene, or sexually sordid. “Out of order” means improper or broken and does not convey that register.
records.remedy: Use “Strangely, I felt nothing vulgar or obscene.”

highlights.text: Inexplicably, I feel nothing out of order.

records.jp: 抱かれた時の感覚が、曜子さんとは違った。
records.en: The feeling at the moment of embrace was so different from Youko-chan's.
comments: Another honorific fixed in the console version, as well as in CCC0045A. See CCC0000. This is not random in the slightest, the two characters are being directly compared. Whether they're both nonexistent, they're related in this sense. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls her 曜子さん, Youko-san. The English changes the honorific to “-chan,” altering the relationship marker.
records.remedy: Use “Youko-san.”

highlights.text: The feeling at the moment of embrace was so different from Youko-chan's.

records.jp: 知っている。
records.en: Understanding.
comments: Vague due to this part being vague. -GHS
records.assessment: The source states that she knows something. Nominal “Understanding” removes both subject and the active state of knowing.
records.remedy: Use “She knows.”

highlights.text: Understanding.

records.jp: 彼女は何かを知っている？
records.en: What does she understand?
records.assessment: The source wonders whether she knows something, not what particular proposition she understands. The English presupposes understanding and asks for its object.
records.remedy: Use “Does she know something?”

highlights.text: What does she understand?

records.jp: 知らない。
records.en: No understanding.
records.assessment: The source states “I don’t know,” referring to her identity or name. “No understanding” is an impersonal nominal fragment.
records.remedy: Use “I don’t know her.”

highlights.text: No understanding.

records.jp: じゃあどうして彼女は俺のことを？
records.en: Well then why does she... me...?
records.assessment: The source asks how she knows about him. “Why does she... me...?” omits the governing verb and never forms the relation.
records.remedy: Use “Then how does she know about me?”

highlights.text: Well then why does she... me...?

records.jp: 身を離す。
records.en: We distance from each other.
records.assessment: The source says one participant pulls their body away after the embrace. “We distance from each other” makes the action mutual and omits the required reflexive object.
records.remedy: Use “She drew away from me.”

highlights.text: We distance from each other.

records.jp: 「ばかめ」
records.en: Nanaka: "Ya dum'ass!"
records.assessment: ばかめ is a teasing “Fool” or “Idiot.” “Dum’ass” is substantially coarser and gives Nanaka unsupported vulgarity.
records.remedy: Use “You fool.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Ya dum'ass!"

records.jp: 否定してから、小首を傾げて言葉の穂を継いだ。
records.en: After the denial, she tilted her head in doubt and continued on the ear of the words she had left.
comments: "Resume the talk", but literally "inherited the ear of words", which although a set phrase in Japanese (話の穂を継ぐ), has a very similar expression in Chaucher: "an ere of [any goodly] words" http://www.sacred-texts.com/neu/eng/mect/mect63.htm so I adapted it to sorta like that, but withoute Ye Olde Englishe (fore enoewe). -GHS
records.assessment: The source idiom means she tilts her head and continues speaking. “Continued on the ear of the words she had left” literalizes components into nonsense.
records.remedy: Use “After denying it, she tilted her head slightly and continued.”

highlights.text: After the denial, she tilted her head in doubt and continued on the ear of the words she had left.

records.jp: 「……けど、そーだな。好きかもね」
records.en: Nanaka: "...but, riiight. I might just love you!"
records.assessment: 好きかも tentatively says she may like him. “Love you” selects a stronger romantic sense precisely before she explains that her meaning differs.
records.remedy: Use “...But, yeah. Maybe I do like you.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...but, riiight. I might just love you!"

records.jp: 「いねーですもん」
records.en: Taichi: "Thassnottrue!"
comments: Prolly same accent as above. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi’s retort says he did not have a mother. “That’s not true” merely denies her personality claim and removes the biographical fact.
records.remedy: Use “I didn’t have one.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Thassnottrue!"

records.jp: 「でもさ、そーいうのって、けっこう母親も嬉しいのかもよ？」
records.en: Nanaka: "But yannow, all that said, surely mother's gonna be happy too, right?"
comments: I'm not quite sure she's still talking in third person, and more sort-of reminding Taichi that she's more of a memory of his mother rather than her mother physically. After all, this script's been heavily meta VN focused, i.e. the idea she's merely a supernatural apparition in the To Heart/Key style is strong in this script. -GHS
records.assessment: The source suggests mothers may actually be rather pleased by such behavior. “Mother’s gonna be happy too” makes one mother future-certain and leaves “too” without a comparison.
records.remedy: Use “But maybe mothers are actually pretty happy about that kind of thing.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "But yannow, all that said, surely mother's gonna be happy too, right?"

records.jp: 「Ｈな悪戯がか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Of perverted sexual pranks?"
records.assessment: Taichi incredulously asks whether the sexual prank itself would please a mother. “Of perverted sexual pranks?” is not a grammatical echo question.
records.remedy: Use “The naughty prank would make her happy?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Of perverted sexual pranks?"

records.jp: 「するする、来たらするさ」
records.en: Taichi: "I will, I will, come in and I will!"
records.assessment: The source says he would do it if she came in. “Come in and I will” turns the condition into an imperative addressed to her.
records.remedy: Use “I would, I would. If you came in, I’d do it.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I will, I will, come in and I will!"

records.jp: 背後にまわって下着を見ようとする俺。
records.en: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.
records.assessment: The source says he moves around behind her to look at her underwear. “Turning to my back” reverses the direction, and “go I” is malformed inversion.
records.remedy: Use “I circled around behind her to look at her underwear.”

highlights.text: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.

records.jp: ノーコンのブルマだった。
records.en:
Buruma Out of Control*.
* Dark blue
comments: http://detail.chiebukuro.yahoo.co.jp/qa/question_detail/q1259121567 (J only), basically no control means dark blue, so going with cryptic and silly because that's actually literal. -GHS
records.assessment: The source identifies the bloomers’ dark navy color. “Out of Control” invents a meaning for ノーコン, while the footnote only partially repairs the mistranslation.
records.remedy: Use “They were dark navy bloomers.”

highlights.text:
Buruma Out of Control*.
* Dark blue

records.jp: 女性解放運動も真っ青なセクハラ体操着としてずいぶん前に絶滅したという、ブルマ！？
records.en: That deep blue gym sexual harassment-ish uniform hunted down to extinction a fair while ago by the women's lib movement, that is, buruma?!
comments: According to Wikipedia it's a "mid-90s" thing indeed, so he's just after them. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the bloomers were so harassing that even the women’s liberation movement would pale, and that they went extinct long ago. The English makes that movement the agent that hunted them down.
records.remedy: Use “Bloomers—the harassing gymwear, enough to make even the women’s liberation movement blanch, said to have gone extinct long ago!?”

highlights.text: That deep blue gym sexual harassment-ish uniform hunted down to extinction a fair while ago by the women's lib movement, that is, buruma?!

records.jp: 俺はわなわなと震えた。
records.en: I shook and trembled with fear.
records.assessment: The source says he trembles violently; it does not specify fear. The surrounding reaction may instead be shock or excitement.
records.remedy: Use “I trembled violently.”

highlights.text: I shook and trembled with fear.

records.jp: 噂によれば、そのヒップへの張りつき具合は絶品だと言う。
records.en: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.
comments: Hmmm, but he talks as if he didn't collect buruma... -GHS
records.assessment: The rumor praises how exquisitely the bloomers cling to the hips. The English calls the object itself “a superlative article” and loses the quality of the fit.
records.remedy: Use “Rumor says the way they cling to the hips is exquisite.”

highlights.text: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.

records.jp: 「アンテナ、ちゃっちゃっと組み立てちゃいなさいよね」
records.en: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"
records.assessment: The source tells him to assemble the antenna briskly. “Pretty and fast” treats ちゃっちゃっと as two separate qualities.
records.remedy: Use “Put that antenna together, and make it quick.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"

records.jp: 「それって、可能性だからさ」
records.en: Nanaka: "That is... possibilities, 's what."
records.assessment: The source identifies the antenna as a possibility in the singular conceptual sense. “That is possibilities” has number disagreement and changes the abstraction.
records.remedy: Use “Because that antenna represents possibility.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "That is... possibilities, 's what."

records.jp: チェーンが小気味よい音をたてて、まわる。
records.en: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.
records.assessment: The singular subject “chain” requires “spins.”
records.remedy: Use “The chain spins with a crisp, pleasant sound.”

highlights.text: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.

records.jp: タイヤがアスファルトを擦り、自転車が走り出す。
records.en: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.
records.assessment: The singular “tire” requires “grazes,” and a bicycle itself begins to move or roll rather than “ride forth.”
records.remedy: Use “The tire grazes the asphalt, and the bicycle rolls away.”

highlights.text: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.

records.jp: 「どうしたんですかー？」
records.en: Taichi: "What brings youuu?"
records.assessment: The source asks what happened or what brought her there. “What brings you” lacks the complement “here.”
records.remedy: Use “What brings you here?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What brings youuu?"

records.jp: 「暗くて見えませーん」
records.en: Misato: "It's too dark I cannot seee!"
records.assessment: The two independent parts require coordination or punctuation: “It’s too dark; I can’t see.”
records.remedy: Use “It’s too dark—I can’t see!”

highlights.text: Misato: "It's too dark I cannot seee!"

records.jp: 「どうしてなんでしょうねー」
records.en: Misato: "How is that possibleee!"
records.assessment: The source wonders why their visibility differs. “How is that possible” makes it sound like an astonished challenge.
records.remedy: Use “I wonder why that is.”

highlights.text: Misato: "How is that possibleee!"

records.jp: 「野生どーぶつなんで感覚鋭いんですよー」
records.en: Taichi: "I got sharp senses 'cause I'm wild animaaal!"
records.assessment: The singular count noun “animal” requires an article after “I’m.”
records.remedy: Use “I’ve got sharp senses because I’m a wild animal!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I got sharp senses 'cause I'm wild animaaal!"

records.jp: あれでけっこう幼いのだ。
records.en: That's pretty childish of her.
records.assessment: The source observes that despite appearances she is rather childlike. “That’s childish of her” judges only the immediately preceding arm motion.
records.remedy: Use “For all that, she’s actually quite childlike.”

highlights.text: That's pretty childish of her.

records.jp: 「執筆活動には雰囲気が大切なんですよ、おぜうさん」
records.en: Taichi: "Atmosphere is important to the act of Writing, my lady."
comments: Capital W because [boring explanation about minor details of Japanese no one cares about]. I sooo want to use 'hlaefdige' for that old pronunciation of ojou-san... -GHS
records.assessment: The source jokingly says atmosphere matters to writing. Capitalizing the common noun in “the act of Writing” is unsupported and overformalizes the phrase.
records.remedy: Use “Atmosphere is important when one writes, my lady.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Atmosphere is important to the act of Writing, my lady."

records.jp: ちょこんと正座。
records.en: She goes into seiza with a quiet puff.
comments: soff' -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she settles neatly and compactly into seiza. “With a quiet puff” invents a sound and misses the small, composed posture.
records.remedy: Use “She settled neatly into seiza.”

highlights.text: She goes into seiza with a quiet puff.

records.jp: 「あ、よく手伝ってくれてますから、ご飯をオゴろうかと思いまして」
records.en: Misato: "Ah, because you have been so good at helping me, I thought I would give you a treat to eat."
comments: The implication is not quite feeding the dog... not *quite*. -GHS
records.assessment: She says he has helped her often and she thought she would treat him to a meal. “Good at helping me” changes frequency to skill, and “give you a treat to eat” is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “You’ve helped me so often that I thought I’d treat you to dinner.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Ah, because you have been so good at helping me, I thought I would give you a treat to eat."

records.jp: 包みを掲げた。
records.en: She produced a package.
records.assessment: The source says she holds the package up for him to see. “Produced” only means brought it out and omits the display gesture.
records.remedy: Use “She held up a package.”

highlights.text: She produced a package.

records.jp: 「二人分作ってきたんです、一緒にどうですか？」
records.en: Misato: "I made enough for two. Is together fine?"
comments: Remember she has no pure intentions here. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether he would like to eat the two portions together with her. “Is together fine?” has no subject or action.
records.remedy: Use “I made enough for two. Would you like to eat together?”

highlights.text: Misato: "I made enough for two. Is together fine?"

records.jp: 「先輩は器用だなあ」
records.en: Taichi: "You are really skilled at this Senpai!"
records.assessment: The direct address “Senpai” must be set off with a comma; without it, the object of “this” runs into the addressee.
records.remedy: Use “You’re really skilled at this, Senpai.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You are really skilled at this Senpai!"

records.jp: 「そうなんですか？」
records.en: Misato: "Was it really?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether that is presently so. “Was it really?” incorrectly places the situation in the past.
records.remedy: Use “Is that so?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Was it really?"

records.jp: 「俺……母親、いないですから」
records.en: Taichi: "Me... my mother is not with us, that is why."
comments: But his mother never made him lunch, did she. And neither his substitute mother (Youko) and foster mother (Mutsumi) have. But Misato... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he does not have a mother, without specifying death. “Not with us” conventionally implies that she died and narrows the absence.
records.remedy: Use “I... don’t have a mother.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Me... my mother is not with us, that is why."

records.jp: 薄闇の中、見つめ合う。
records.en: Gazes meet inside this faintest of lights.
records.assessment: The source says the two look into each other’s eyes in the dimness. “Gazes meet” removes the people as agents, and “faintest of lights” changes dim darkness into light sources.
records.remedy: Use “We gazed at each other in the dimness.”

highlights.text: Gazes meet inside this faintest of lights.

records.jp: 「……だめです。男がここまで来たらもう引っ込みがつきませんよ」
records.en: Taichi: "...that is not happening. When a man has gotten this far there is no longer retreat."
comments: PCP CCA0012
Told ya it was nukige. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that once a man has gone this far he cannot back down. “There is no longer retreat” needs an article or idiomatic verb phrase.
records.remedy: Use “Once a man has come this far, there’s no backing down.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...that is not happening. When a man has gotten this far there is no longer retreat."

records.jp: 「そんなこと言われてもぉ～」
records.en: Misato: "I cannot believe you just said tha～t!"
comments: Yeah, I'll be adapting that. This seems on character. -GHS
records.assessment: The source protests helplessly, “Even if you say that...” “I cannot believe you just said that” instead expresses shock or disbelief.
records.remedy: Use “Even if you say that...”

highlights.text: Misato: "I cannot believe you just said tha～t!"

records.jp: 「一年生の時、俺が一人でいた時」
records.en: Taichi: "That time when I was a first year, that time when I was alone."
records.assessment: The source identifies the time in first year when he was alone. Repeating “that time” twice adds stilted emphasis not present.
records.remedy: Use “Back in our first year, when I was alone.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "That time when I was a first year, that time when I was alone."

records.jp: 「でも、誘ってくれたじゃないですか」
records.en: Taichi: "But did you still not invite me?"
records.assessment: The source affirms that despite the restriction she invited him. “But did you still not invite me?” tangles affirmation into a negative question.
records.remedy: Use “But you invited me anyway.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But did you still not invite me?"

records.jp: 「手もまわしてくれた。俺がちゃんと入部できるように」
records.en: Taichi: "You pulled strings for me in secret. So that I could well and properly join."
comments: Specifics unknown. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she made arrangements so he could formally join. “In secret” is not stated, and “could well and properly join” is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “You made arrangements so that I could join the club properly.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You pulled strings for me in secret. So that I could well and properly join."

records.jp: 「それは……一人で、寂しそうだったから……健全な……部活を通して……やん！」
records.en: Misato: "Because... you looked lonely all alone... being wholesome... via the club... wah!"
records.assessment: She says she acted because he looked lonely and wanted to help through wholesome club activity. “Being wholesome... via the club” is a broken fragment that does not preserve her rationale.
records.remedy: Use “It was because you looked lonely by yourself... I thought that through wholesome club activities...”

highlights.text: Misato: "Because... you looked lonely all alone... being wholesome... via the club... wah!"

records.jp: 「動かないで、外せないです」
records.en: Taichi: "Do not move, I cannot take it."
records.assessment: The source says not to move because he cannot get the item off. “Cannot take it” omits the particle “off” and changes removal into taking possession.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t move; I can’t get it off.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Do not move, I cannot take it."

records.jp: 「あ……だめ、おいたです……だめっ」
records.en: Misato: "Ah... no, no I said... you can't!"
records.assessment: おいた calls the action naughty or mischievous. “No I said” removes that characterization.
records.remedy: Use “Ah... no, that’s naughty... no.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Ah... no, no I said... you can't!"

records.jp: 「人に手を差し伸べれば……そこに関係ができます」
records.en: Taichi: "If your extend your hand to someone in help... that is where you can make a connection."
records.assessment: The source says reaching out to someone creates a relationship. “If your extend” is a typo, and “make a connection” weakens the resulting interpersonal bond.
records.remedy: Use “If you reach out a hand to someone, a relationship forms between you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "If your extend your hand to someone in help... that is where you can make a connection."

records.jp: 「感謝されたり、好意が生まれたり」
records.en: Taichi: "Gratefulness is there, the birth of goodwill is there."
records.assessment: The source lists being thanked and affection arising as possible consequences. Repeated “is there” turns both into unnatural nominal constructions.
records.remedy: Use “They may thank you, and affection may arise.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gratefulness is there, the birth of goodwill is there."

records.jp: 「俺が先輩と、したいと思うのだって……自然なことです」
records.en: Taichi: "For me to think to want to do it with Senpai is... something natural."
records.assessment: The source says his desire to do it with Senpai is natural. “Think to want to do it” stacks incompatible infinitives and obscures the proposition.
records.remedy: Use “It’s only natural that I would want to do it with you, Senpai.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "For me to think to want to do it with Senpai is... something natural."

records.jp: 「俺をもとの暗闇に戻せばいい」
records.en: Taichi: "I could just be returned to the darkness of my origin."
comments: The darkness that Crawls in his Skin, i.e. eeemo. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she can send him back into the darkness he originally inhabited. “The darkness of my origin” sounds like darkness created him and loses the return image.
records.remedy: Use “You can send me back into the darkness I came from.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I could just be returned to the darkness of my origin."

records.jp: 「繋がろうとは思いません」
records.en: Taichi: "I will not think about becoming connect."
records.assessment: The source says he will not try to form or maintain a connection. “Becoming connect” uses a verb as an adjective and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “I won’t try to stay connected to you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I will not think about becoming connect."

records.jp: 「……そういう言い方は……ずるいです……」
records.en: Misato: "...but saying it like that... so unfair..."
comments: Irrelevant. She could still tell him off if she actually wanted it to. She knew what she was getting into. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that phrasing it that way is unfair. The English omits the predicate “is” before “so unfair.”
records.remedy: Use “...Saying it that way... is unfair...”

highlights.text: Misato: "...but saying it like that... so unfair..."

records.jp: 「ええ、ずるいですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Yep, it so very unfair."
records.assessment: The English omits “is” after “it.”
records.remedy: Use “Yes, it is very unfair.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yep, it so very unfair."

records.jp: 肩ひもをとりのける。
records.en: Move away the suspenders' straps,
records.assessment: The source says he moves the garment’s shoulder straps aside. “Suspenders’ straps” names a different garment and uses an unexplained fragment.
records.remedy: Use “I moved the shoulder straps aside.”

highlights.text: Move away the suspenders' straps,

records.jp: ボタンを外す。
records.en: slip out a button.
records.assessment: The source says he unfastens a button. “Slip out a button” suggests removing the button from the garment rather than opening it.
records.remedy: Use “I unfastened a button.”

highlights.text: slip out a button.

records.jp: ボタンを外していく。
records.en: Slip out another button.
records.assessment: The source narrates continuing to unfasten buttons. “Slip out another button” again implies removing a button and uses an unsupported imperative/base form.
records.remedy: Use “I continued unfastening the buttons.”

highlights.text: Slip out another button.

records.jp: ブラウスをはだける。
records.en: I unclothe her of the blouse.
records.assessment: The source says he pulls the blouse open. “Unclothe her of the blouse” says he removes the garment entirely and is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “I pulled her blouse open.”

highlights.text: I unclothe her of the blouse.

records.jp: ブラの上に、指を置く。
records.en: I lay my fingers over her bra.
records.assessment: The source says he places one finger on the bra. The English changes the finger to plural.
records.remedy: Use “I placed a finger on her bra.”

highlights.text: I lay my fingers over her bra.

records.jp: 指をかけて、そっと真上に持ち上げる。
records.en: I push my fingers in, and slowly begin to lift them right upwards.
records.assessment: The source says he hooks his fingers onto the garment and gently lifts it straight upward. “Push my fingers in” changes the contact, and “lift them” makes the fingers themselves the lifted object.
records.remedy: Use “I hooked my fingers under it and gently lifted it straight upward.”

highlights.text: I push my fingers in, and slowly begin to lift them right upwards.

records.jp: 白さが弾けた。
records.en: Whiteness burst out,
records.assessment: The source’s image says whiteness bursts free. The English trails into a comma as though the sentence were incomplete.
records.remedy: Use “A burst of white sprang free.”

highlights.text: Whiteness burst out,

records.jp: ふたつの球体が弾む。
records.en: the springness of two spheres.
comments: That's Heaven and Earth--- uhmmm never mind -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives a full action: two spheres bounce. “The springness of two spheres” is a noun fragment and replaces motion with an abstract nonstandard quality.
records.remedy: Use “Two spheres bounced.”

highlights.text: the springness of two spheres.

records.jp: 整って、膨らんで、白くて。
records.en: Well composed, swelling, white.
records.assessment: The source describes them as well-shaped, full, and white. “Swelling” makes fullness into an ongoing action.
records.remedy: Use “Well-shaped, full, and white.”

highlights.text: Well composed, swelling, white.

records.jp: 「こ、こんなつもりじゃ……不純な……ことを……停学……」
records.en: Misato: "The-, then you intended this... so impure... this is... suspension..."
comments: Still her first nickname for him. Looks like she brings it out when flustered. -GHS
records.assessment: Misato says she did not intend this and fragments references to impurity and suspension. “Then you intended this” reverses the negation and assigns intent to Taichi.
records.remedy: Use “I-I didn’t mean for this... indecent... this could mean suspension...”

highlights.text: Misato: "The-, then you intended this... so impure... this is... suspension..."

records.jp: 両手で触れる。
records.en: I envelop them with both hands.
records.assessment: The source says he touches with both hands. “Envelop” adds a complete surrounding grasp and makes the unstated object explicit.
records.remedy: Use “I touched them with both hands.”

highlights.text: I envelop them with both hands.

records.jp: 皮膚と皮膚が密着して、しっとりと微熱を交換する。
records.en: Flesh glued to flesh, a gentle interchange of minute heat.
records.assessment: The source says skin presses tightly against skin and exchanges faint body heat. “Flesh glued to flesh” is stronger and “minute heat” mistakes slight warmth for a tiny measured quantity.
records.remedy: Use “Skin pressed close to skin, exchanging a faint, moist warmth.”

highlights.text: Flesh glued to flesh, a gentle interchange of minute heat.

records.jp: 軽く握ると、ふよふよとして、心地よくなる。
records.en: A light grasp is like floating onto a cloud, so pleasant.
records.assessment: The source says the flesh yields softly under a light squeeze and feels pleasant. The floating-on-a-cloud simile is invented and replaces the tactile description.
records.remedy: Use “When I squeezed lightly, it yielded softly and felt pleasant.”

highlights.text: A light grasp is like floating onto a cloud, so pleasant.

records.jp: 脊髄を経由し脳を刺激し、また同じ道を戻り腰骨周辺で灼熱の狭霧と化す。
records.en: They run through the spinal cord to provoke the brain, and via the same road they return to the area of the hipbone where they transform into incandescent mist.
comments: See CCD5001. Uh-oh. Last one's Kiri, but more interesting, 灼熱 shokunetsu is in the name of one of Tanaka's LNs. -GHS
records.assessment: The source makes the sensation travel through the spinal cord, stimulate the brain, and return to the pelvis. “They” most naturally refers to the fingertips, giving body parts the wrong motion.
records.remedy: Use “The sensation traveled through my spinal cord to stimulate my brain, then returned along the same path and became a burning mist around my pelvis.”

highlights.text: They run through the spinal cord to provoke the brain, and via the same road they return to the area of the hipbone where they transform into incandescent mist.

records.jp: 劣情が部分に満ちはじめる。
records.en: Carnal desires begin to fill to the brim.
records.assessment: The source says lust begins to fill a particular region of the body. “Begin to fill to the brim” omits what is being filled.
records.remedy: Use “Carnal desire began to fill that part of me.”

highlights.text: Carnal desires begin to fill to the brim.

records.jp: 夢中になって。
records.en: ending up hooked.
comments: See CCC3025. -GHS
records.assessment: 夢中になって means becoming absorbed or engrossed in the action. “Ending up hooked” reframes it as addiction.
records.remedy: Use “Completely absorbed.”

highlights.text: ending up hooked.

records.jp: いや、俺はぐにゃぐにゃしたい。
records.en: Nope, I want to squishy-squishy.
records.assessment: “Want to” requires a verb; “squishy-squishy” cannot serve as one in this construction.
records.remedy: Use “No, I want to keep squishing them.”

highlights.text: Nope, I want to squishy-squishy.

records.jp: もっとぐにゃぐにゃしたいのだった。
records.en: And I want more squishy-squishy.
records.assessment: “Want more squishy-squishy” again uses an onomatopoeic modifier as an uninflected noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use “I wanted to squish them even more.”

highlights.text: And I want more squishy-squishy.

records.jp: 両の乳首がくっつきそうになる。
records.en: The tips of the nipples squeeze into each other.
comments: See CCA0016. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the two nipples nearly touch. The English says they squeeze into one another, asserting both contact and deformation.
records.remedy: Use “The two nipples nearly touched.”

highlights.text: The tips of the nipples squeeze into each other.

records.jp: ぐっとてのひらを押しつけた。
records.en: I push the palms down, firmly.
records.assessment: The source says he firmly presses his palms against them. “Push the palms down” adds a downward direction.
records.remedy: Use “I pressed my palms firmly against them.”

highlights.text: I push the palms down, firmly.

records.jp: 扁平に潰れた乳房。しかしたいらにはならない。
records.en: The breasts smush to level. However, they never become flat.
records.assessment: The source contrasts breasts compressed flatter with their refusal to become truly flat. “Smush to level” is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use “The breasts compressed flatter, yet they never became flat.”

highlights.text: The breasts smush to level. However, they never become flat.

records.jp: 鷲づかみにしたまま。
records.en: A full grasp, like the talons of an eagle.
comments: See CCA0006 -GHS
records.assessment: The source is an adverbial continuation: he pulls while maintaining an eagle-like grip. The English turns that into a detached noun fragment.
records.remedy: Use “Still gripping them in both hands.”

highlights.text: A full grasp, like the talons of an eagle.

records.jp: 少し慌てて、俺の両手を押さえてくる。
records.en: A little frenzied, she pushes my hands back down.
records.assessment: The source says she hurriedly restrains or holds his hands. “Pushes my hands back down” invents a downward movement and changes restraint into pressure.
records.remedy: Use “A little flustered, she grabbed both my hands to stop me.”

highlights.text: A little frenzied, she pushes my hands back down.

records.jp: 先輩の手の甲に口づけをしてから、指をくわえて引きはがす。
records.en: After I pass my lips on the back of Senpai's hands they are moved off, where they look onwards, unable to do anything.
comments: You don't actually touch the back of the hand when you-- wait, we're a bit too far into this aren't we. "Slipping a finger in the mouth" also means "to look on enviously doing nothing", so putting both in. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he kisses the back of Senpai’s hand, takes a finger into his mouth, and uses it to pull her hand away. The English omits the finger action and invents hands looking onward helplessly.
records.remedy: Use “I kissed the back of Senpai’s hand, took one of her fingers into my mouth, and pulled her hand away.”

highlights.text: After I pass my lips on the back of Senpai's hands they are moved off, where they look onwards, unable to do anything.

records.jp: 「千切りませんよ」
records.en: Taichi: "They will not tear off!"
records.assessment: The source promises that he will not tear them off. “They will not tear off” removes his agency and makes it a prediction.
records.remedy: Use “I won’t tear them off.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "They will not tear off!"

records.jp: 笑う。
records.en: Smile.
records.assessment: The source says he laughs. “Smile” changes the action and uses a bare present/imperative form.
records.remedy: Use “I laughed.”

highlights.text: Smile.

records.jp: 乳房はそれぞれの方向に、自在に変形した。
records.en: The two breasts deform and mush freely in every direction independently.
comments: See CCC0041. Nice, isn't it? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the breasts deform freely in separate directions. “Mush” adds a colloquial texture judgment not stated.
records.remedy: Use “The two breasts changed shape freely, each in its own direction.”

highlights.text: The two breasts deform and mush freely in every direction independently.

records.jp: 「俺が好きなときに触れるように」
records.en: Taichi: "So they will be mine to touch whenever I like."
records.assessment: The source says he wants to be able to touch them whenever he likes. “They will be mine” adds ownership beyond access.
records.remedy: Use “So I can touch them whenever I like.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "So they will be mine to touch whenever I like."

records.jp: 額に唇を当てた。
records.en: My lips went for her forehead,
records.assessment: The source says he places his lips on her forehead. “Went for” can mean merely attempted and the trailing comma leaves the sentence incomplete.
records.remedy: Use “I pressed my lips to her forehead.”

highlights.text: My lips went for her forehead,

records.jp: メガネのつるをくわえる。外す。
records.en: fishing for her glasses, catching them in the mouth. And removing.
records.assessment: The source says he catches the temple of her glasses in his mouth and removes them. “Fishing for,” “catching,” and “And removing” form a broken sequence and obscure the precise action.
records.remedy: Use “I caught the temple of her glasses in my mouth and pulled them off.”

highlights.text: fishing for her glasses, catching them in the mouth. And removing.

records.jp: 一生飽きないと思われるが。
records.en: But to me it seemed one entire life would not be enough for that.
records.assessment: The source says he believes he would never tire of it for his entire life. “One entire life would not be enough” changes endless interest into insufficient duration.
records.remedy: Use “Though I doubt I would tire of it in my entire life.”

highlights.text: But to me it seemed one entire life would not be enough for that.

records.jp: 「手の体温が伝わったのかな、それとも先輩のおっぱいが興奮してきちゃったのかな」
records.en: Taichi: "Maybe it's heat from my hands going out, or maybe your boobs are becoming aroused, Senpai."
records.assessment: The source contrasts warmth transferred from his hands with her body becoming aroused. “Heat from my hands going out” is unidiomatic and does not state transmission to her.
records.remedy: Use “I wonder if the warmth from my hands transferred to you, or if your breasts are getting excited.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Maybe it's heat from my hands going out, or maybe your boobs are becoming aroused, Senpai."

records.jp: 「でもしっとりと汗ばんでるし、さきっちょだって」
records.en: Taichi: "But, there's some damp sweat slowly forming, right on the tips."
comments: slowly + moist -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the surface is damp with sweat and begins a further point about the tips. The English locates the sweat specifically on the tips and omits the separate implication about them.
records.remedy: Use “But they’re damp with sweat, and even the tips...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But, there's some damp sweat slowly forming, right on the tips."

records.jp: 「やだ……恥ずかしくて……死にそう……」
records.en: Misato: "No! ...so embarrassing... might die..."
records.assessment: The source says she feels as though she might die of embarrassment. “Might die” omits the first-person subject.
records.remedy: Use “No... I’m so embarrassed I could die...”

highlights.text: Misato: "No! ...so embarrassing... might die..."

records.jp: 言葉の通り、恥じらいに震える乳房だった。
records.en: The breasts, following her words, quiver in embarrassment.
comments: ... -GHS
records.assessment: The surrounding narration is past. “Quiver” shifts this completed observation into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Just as she said, her breasts quivered with embarrassment.”

highlights.text: The breasts, following her words, quiver in embarrassment.

records.jp: 軽く包んで細かに揺すってみる。
records.en: With a lighter envelopment I try to give them a minute jolt.
records.assessment: The source says he lightly cups them and tries shaking them in small, rapid motions. “A minute jolt” turns repeated fine movement into one sudden impact.
records.remedy: Use “I cupped them lightly and tried shaking them in small, rapid motions.”

highlights.text: With a lighter envelopment I try to give them a minute jolt.

records.jp: 先端が無軌道に弾む。
records.en: The cusps bounce tracklessly,
records.assessment: The source says the tips bounce erratically. “Cusps” is an anatomical or mathematical technical term, and “tracklessly” is not idiomatic motion.
records.remedy: Use “The tips bounced unpredictably.”

highlights.text: The cusps bounce tracklessly,

records.jp: 「……いやぁ……ゆれるの、恥ずかしいです……」
records.en: Misato: "...nooo... no shaking, it is embarrassing..."
records.assessment: She says it is embarrassing that they jiggle. “No shaking” changes her observation into an imperative command.
records.remedy: Use “No... it’s embarrassing when they jiggle...”

highlights.text: Misato: "...nooo... no shaking, it is embarrassing..."

records.jp: 囁いて、顔を寄せた。
records.en: That ceremonial phrase whispered, my face approached,
records.assessment: The source says he whispers and brings his face closer. The English makes his face the autonomous subject and adds a trailing comma.
records.remedy: Use “I whispered and brought my face closer.”

highlights.text: That ceremonial phrase whispered, my face approached,

records.jp: 白々とした房に、かぶりついた。
records.en: and I dug into that pale pink cluster.
comments: white-white = pink #Japanese -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes biting or latching onto a pale rounded mass. “Pink” is added, and “dug into” suggests excavation rather than the mouth action.
records.remedy: Use “I latched onto the pale rounded mass.”

highlights.text: and I dug into that pale pink cluster.

records.jp: 歯をひっこめて、粘膜全体を押し当てる。
records.en: I draw back with the teeth, and adhere with the whole of the oral mucosa.
comments: Ugh, begin Wall of Mucous Membranes... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he retracts his teeth and presses the whole lining of his mouth against it. “Draw back with the teeth” changes which thing moves and “adhere with” is malformed.
records.remedy: Use “I pulled my teeth back and pressed the entire lining of my mouth against it.”

highlights.text: I draw back with the teeth, and adhere with the whole of the oral mucosa.

records.jp: 音を立てた。
records.en: Sounds come out.
records.assessment: The source says the action made a sound. Plural “Sounds come out” changes number and tense.
records.remedy: Use “It made a sound.”

highlights.text: Sounds come out.

records.jp: 「や、やめてください……口で……そんな……ひうっ……きゃ！」
records.en: Misato: "S-, stop please... the mouth... that is... hYuh... kyah!"
records.assessment: She asks him to stop doing that with his mouth. “The mouth... that is...” is a disconnected fragment that omits the governing action.
records.remedy: Use “P-please stop... using your mouth like that...”

highlights.text: Misato: "S-, stop please... the mouth... that is... hYuh... kyah!"

records.jp: 「やっだ……だめ、です……えっち……えっちぃ」
records.en: Misato: "So wrong... you cannot... do this... pervert... perveeert!"
records.assessment: Her repeated えっち describes the act as lewd. “Pervert” directly labels the man instead, changing the target and part of speech.
records.remedy: Use “No... stop... that’s lewd... so lewd...”

highlights.text: Misato: "So wrong... you cannot... do this... pervert... perveeert!"

records.jp: 軽く咀嚼して、肉質を味わう。
records.en: A delicate mastication, to taste the fleshiness.
records.assessment: The source narrates that he lightly chews and savors the texture. “A delicate mastication” is a noun fragment rather than an action.
records.remedy: Use “I chewed lightly, savoring the texture.”

highlights.text: A delicate mastication, to taste the fleshiness.

records.jp: その通りかも知れない。
records.en: That's what I'm doing, perhaps.
records.assessment: The source says her claim that she is being eaten may be right. “That’s what I’m doing” asserts his action instead of tentatively validating her metaphor.
records.remedy: Use “She might be right.”

highlights.text: That's what I'm doing, perhaps.

records.jp: 乳房や臀部を口に含みたいというのは、本能に近い。
records.en: It is something close to that instinct, that to swallow in my mouth the breast and what is behind it.
comments: Ahhh, it's eating in the sense of vore then. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls the urge to take breasts or buttocks into one’s mouth almost instinctive. “Swallow in my mouth” is malformed, and “what is behind it” avoids and misstates the buttocks.
records.remedy: Use “The urge to take breasts or buttocks into one’s mouth is almost instinctive.”

highlights.text: It is something close to that instinct, that to swallow in my mouth the breast and what is behind it.

records.jp: 「だから、いただきますって」
records.en: Taichi: "And that is why I thanked you for the food."
records.assessment: The source explicitly recalls his earlier いただきます. “Thanked you for the food” paraphrases the phrase and weakens the repeated eating joke.
records.remedy: Use “That’s why I said, ‘Itadakimasu.’”

highlights.text: Taichi: "And that is why I thanked you for the food."

records.jp: 乳輪ごと先端を食べた。
records.en: I ate the areolas one at the time.
records.assessment: The source says he takes the singular tip together with its areola into his mouth. The English pluralizes the areola and adds “one at a time,” implying multiple separate actions.
records.remedy: Use “I took the tip and its entire areola into my mouth.”

highlights.text: I ate the areolas one at the time.

records.jp: 口の中にとらえた獲物を、舌先でつつく。
records.en: The prey, caught inside my mouth, is poked and played with the tongue.
records.assessment: The source says he prods the captured ‘prey’ with the tip of his tongue. The passive English adds “played with” and removes his agency.
records.remedy: Use “I prodded the prey in my mouth with the tip of my tongue.”

highlights.text: The prey, caught inside my mouth, is poked and played with the tongue.

records.jp: 舌を突起に巻き付けた。
records.en: The tongue wreathed on the protuberances.
records.assessment: The source says he wraps his tongue around one protrusion. “Wreathed on” uses the wrong preposition and “protuberances” changes it to plural.
records.remedy: Use “I wrapped my tongue around the protrusion.”

highlights.text: The tongue wreathed on the protuberances.

records.jp: 「ふぅんっ、ん、それ、だめ……ですっ」

records.assessment: The source says that action is no good. “That gets a no” is an unnatural evaluative phrase in her voice.

highlights.text: Misato: "Huhnn, nnh, that, gets... a no!"

records.jp: 強く吸いながら、口を抜いていく。
records.en: While sucking strongly, I release it from the mouth.
records.assessment: The source says he gradually pulls his mouth away while maintaining strong suction. “Release it from the mouth” makes the object leave the mouth and loses his withdrawal.
records.remedy: Use “Still sucking hard, I slowly pulled my mouth away.”

highlights.text: While sucking strongly, I release it from the mouth.

records.assessment: 途切れる is a finite event: her voice cuts off. The noun “Interruption” removes what was interrupted and does not form a sentence.
records.remedy: Use “Her voice cut off.”

highlights.text: Interruption,

records.jp: あらゆる関節を逆向きにしならせて、全身をうねらせた。
records.en: Every joint in the body was made to move towards the converse direction, the whole body twisting.
records.assessment: The source depicts every joint bending backward as her whole body writhes. “Move towards the converse direction” is an opaque calque and weakens the bodily arching.
records.remedy: Use “Every joint bent backward as her whole body writhed.”

highlights.text: Every joint in the body was made to move towards the converse direction, the whole body twisting.

records.jp: 俺も収縮する内部を使い、長めのストロークで愉悦を弾けさせる。
records.en: I as well, making use of the contracting depths, with one longish stroke I am also made to burst into ecstasy.
records.assessment: The source makes him the agent who uses the contracting interior and long strokes to burst into pleasure. “I am also made to burst” makes him passive and shifts the tense.
records.remedy: Use “Using her contracting depths, I burst into pleasure with longer strokes.”

highlights.text: I as well, making use of the contracting depths, with one longish stroke I am also made to burst into ecstasy.

records.jp: ねっとりと絡みつく内部から抜く。
records.en: I spurt into the twisted depths, viscously.
records.assessment: The source says he withdraws from the slick interior clinging around him. The English says he spurts into it, reversing withdrawal into ejaculation and reversing direction.
records.remedy: Use “I pulled out of the slick depths clinging around me.”

highlights.text: I spurt into the twisted depths, viscously.

records.jp: 先輩の体に、筒先をつけた。
records.en: I put a nozzle inside Senpai's body.
records.assessment: The source metaphorically says he placed the muzzle or tip against her body. “Put a nozzle inside” adds penetration and turns the metaphor into an inserted object.
records.remedy: Use “I pressed the tip against Senpai’s body.”

highlights.text: I put a nozzle inside Senpai's body.

records.jp: 普段の三倍増しで出た気がする。
records.en: It feels like it's three times the normal.
records.assessment: The source says he feels he ejaculated three times his usual amount. “It’s three times the normal” is incomplete and omits the amount.
records.remedy: Use “It felt like three times my usual amount.”

highlights.text: It feels like it's three times the normal.

records.jp: 自分の薄桃色の肌が精液で汚される光景を、先輩は陶然と見ていた。
records.en: Senpai watched, enraptured, at the sight of her pale pink skin filthied by the semen.
comments: Once again, NOT the right position for this. -GHS
records.assessment: “Watched ... at the sight” is ungrammatical, and “filthied” is not idiomatic English for 汚される here.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai watched in rapture as semen sullied her pale-pink skin.”

highlights.text: Senpai watched, enraptured, at the sight of her pale pink skin filthied by the semen.

records.jp: 開いた五指に、ねっとりとまとわりついた。
records.en: Opened, her five fingers were coiled about by it, viscously.
records.assessment: The source says the viscous fluid clung between and around her spread fingers. “Her five fingers were coiled about by it” gives the fluid a rope-like action and awkwardly makes the fingers passive.
records.remedy: Use “It clung thickly to her spread fingers.”

highlights.text: Opened, her five fingers were coiled about by it, viscously.

records.jp: 「精液……白いんですね……ん……におう……男の子のにおい……んん……」
records.en: Misato: "Sperm... it so white... nh... smells... the smell of a man... nnh..."
records.assessment: “It so white” is ungrammatical. The source says it smells like a boy, while “a man” changes the characterization.
records.remedy: Use “Semen... it’s white... it smells like a boy...”

highlights.text: Misato: "Sperm... it so white... nh... smells... the smell of a man... nnh..."

records.jp: すでに軽い寝息を立てていた。
records.en: Already a light sleeper's breathing was coming from her.
records.assessment: The source says she was already breathing softly in sleep. “A light sleeper’s breathing” instead classifies her as a light sleeper and uses an awkward existential construction.
records.remedy: Use “She was already breathing softly in her sleep.”

highlights.text: Already a light sleeper's breathing was coming from her.

records.jp: ずっと見つめていた。
records.en: I've stared at her all along.
records.assessment: The source describes what he did throughout the completed hour. “I’ve stared” is an awkward present-perfect choice against the surrounding past narration.
records.remedy: Use “I watched her the whole time.”

highlights.text: I've stared at her all along.

records.jp: 全裸の自分に狼狽え、シーツで隠す。
records.en: Flustered at her own complete nakedness, she hides behind the sheets.
records.assessment: The source says she covers herself with the sheet. “Hides behind the sheets” places the sheet as a barrier and unnecessarily pluralizes it.
records.remedy: Use “Flustered by her nakedness, she covered herself with the sheet.”

highlights.text: Flustered at her own complete nakedness, she hides behind the sheets.

records.jp: シーツの中に視線を落とした。
records.en: Her gaze falls inside the sheets.
records.assessment: The source says she lowered her gaze beneath the sheet. “Falls” shifts tense, and “inside the sheets” suggests within the fabric or between multiple sheets.
records.remedy: Use “She lowered her gaze beneath the sheet.”

highlights.text: Her gaze falls inside the sheets.

records.jp: 「う……生き恥ぃ……」
records.en: Misato: "Ngh... disgraceeed..."
records.assessment: 生き恥 is the humiliation of continuing to live in disgrace, not merely being “disgraced.” The English also distorts the utterance into a stretched adjective.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll never live this down...”

highlights.text: Misato: "Ngh... disgraceeed..."

records.jp: 「おきれいな体をしてらっしゃる」
records.en: Taichi: "Your body is merely very neat and clean."
records.assessment: The teasingly polite line compliments her beautiful body. “Neat and clean” substitutes hygiene and tidiness for beauty.
records.remedy: Use “You have such a beautiful body.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Your body is merely very neat and clean."

records.jp: 呻く。
records.en: Moaning.
records.assessment: The source narrates that she groaned. “Moaning” is a present-participle fragment.
records.remedy: Use “She groaned.”

highlights.text: Moaning.

records.jp: 階下に行って、戻る。
records.en: I go down one floor and return.
records.assessment: The source says he went downstairs and returned. The English shifts to present tense and specifies exactly one floor, which the source does not.
records.remedy: Use “I went downstairs and came back.”

highlights.text: I go down one floor and return.

records.jp: アイスバー。手製。
records.en: Popsicles. Hand made.
records.assessment: The source is a compact noun phrase, “A homemade ice pop.” “Hand made” is incorrectly split and the two fragments are needlessly disconnected.
records.remedy: Use “A homemade ice pop.”

highlights.text: Popsicles. Hand made.

records.jp: 「危機的状況に生存本能が騒いだんです」
records.en: Taichi: "That survival instinct makes uproar in a crisis-like situation."
comments: This could, of course, refer to absolutely anything. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his survival instinct clamored in the crisis. “That survival instinct makes uproar” is unidiomatic and shifts the statement into a general present tense.
records.remedy: Use “My survival instinct started clamoring in a crisis.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "That survival instinct makes uproar in a crisis-like situation."

records.jp: 「明日、海にでも行きませんか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Could we still go to the beach, tomorrow?"
records.assessment: The source simply proposes going to the beach tomorrow. “Still” adds a contrast or persistence not stated here.
records.remedy: Use “Would you like to go to the beach tomorrow?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Could we still go to the beach, tomorrow?"

records.jp: 「そーですねぇ」
records.en: Misato: "Should we, then."
records.assessment: そーですねぇ is a hesitant agreement such as “I suppose so.” “Should we, then” turns it into a malformed question.
records.remedy: Use “Hmm... I suppose so.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Should we, then."

records.jp: 部活のことを考えたのかも知れない。
records.en: She might just be thinking about what to do about club activities.
records.assessment: The source says she may have been thinking about the club. “What to do about” adds a deliberative problem not stated.
records.remedy: Use “Maybe she was thinking about the club.”

highlights.text: She might just be thinking about what to do about club activities.

records.jp: 「じゃ明日は休みにして、パーッと」
records.en: Misato: "Then tomorrow we rest, aaall out!"
records.assessment: She proposes making tomorrow a day off and cutting loose. “Tomorrow we rest, aaall out” combines rest with an incompatible modifier and omits the idea of going out for fun.
records.remedy: Use “Then let’s take tomorrow off and really cut loose.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Then tomorrow we rest, aaall out!"

records.jp: はにかむ。
records.en: Shy.
records.assessment: はにかむ describes her bashful smile or shy reaction. The isolated adjective “Shy” omits the action and does not form a sentence.
records.remedy: Use “She smiled bashfully.”

highlights.text: Shy.

records.jp: 吹っ切れたように見えて、やはり、どこかに惑いがあった。
records.en: She did look like she had left behind her past, but of course, there was still some perplexity in there,
records.assessment: 吹っ切れた means she looked as though she had put her hesitation behind her, not her entire past. “Perplexity in there” is also vague and unidiomatic for lingering uncertainty.
records.remedy: Use “She looked as though she had moved past it, but some uncertainty still lingered.”

highlights.text: She did look like she had left behind her past, but of course, there was still some perplexity in there,

records.jp: 体を重ねても、なお。
records.en: Not even with the overlap of bodies.
comments: See CCE0001. Total of 16 cross-references. Not bad. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the distance remains even after they join their bodies. “The overlap of bodies” is an unnatural nominal calque and leaves the concessive relation fragmentary.
records.remedy: Use “Even after we joined our bodies.”

highlights.text: Not even with the overlap of bodies.

records.jp: 「そして、今日というサマーデイを楽しもうとするリビドー溢れる頼もしいメンツはこいつらだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "And, the promising team members overflowing with libido who desire for enjoyment on the Summer day that is today... here they are!"
records.assessment: The source introduces the reliable group brimming with libido and eager to enjoy this summer day. “Desire for enjoyment on the Summer day that is today” is an opaque calque that does not form natural English.
records.remedy: Use “And here’s the trusty crew, bursting with libido and ready to enjoy this summer day!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "And, the promising team members overflowing with libido who desire for enjoyment on the Summer day that is today... here they are!"

records.jp: 「そろいもそろってこれから葬式でもはじめようってツラだなオイ？」
records.en: Taichi: "What's with every last one of you having mugs as if we're about to start a funeral here?"
records.assessment: The source asks why every last one of them looks as though a funeral is about to begin. “Having mugs as if” is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use “Why do all of you look like we’re about to hold a funeral?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What's with every last one of you having mugs as if we're about to start a funeral here?"

records.jp: 「あんたが人のこと騙すからでしょ！！」
records.en: Touko: "Because you swindle people that's why!!!"
comments: See CCD1001. -GHS
records.assessment: The accusation is about his having deceived everyone in this instance. “Because you swindle people that’s why” shifts to habitual present and duplicates the causal structure.
records.remedy: Use “Because you tricked us!”

highlights.text: Touko: "Because you swindle people that's why!!!"

records.jp: 「どうしてカリカリ来てるんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "What did you go all grouchy there?"
records.assessment: The source asks why she is so irritated. “What did you go all grouchy there?” is ungrammatical and frames the irritation as an object she went to.
records.remedy: Use “Why are you so worked up?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What did you go all grouchy there?"

records.jp: びんたっ！
records.en: Right in the face!
records.assessment: びんた explicitly announces a slap. “Right in the face” gives only a target and omits the striking action.
records.remedy: Use “Slap!”

highlights.text: Right in the face!

records.jp: 行為の名称に等しいオノマトペを発しつつ、的確な一撃が顎を強打した。
records.en: Inflicting an act of name equivalent to that overly literally translated onomatopoeia, my jaw was smote with one precise blow.
comments: Well, it's an overly literal onomatopoeia in the first place. -GHS
records.assessment: The source wryly says a precise blow smashed his jaw while producing an onomatopoeia identical to the act’s name. The English adds commentary about an “overly literally translated” word and turns the blow into a tangled passive construction.
records.remedy: Describe the slap and its matching sound without translator commentary.

highlights.text: Inflicting an act of name equivalent to that overly literally translated onomatopoeia, my jaw was smote with one precise blow.

records.jp: 「人間の肉体は大半が水分で構成されている。いってみりゃァ、水風船よ」
records.en:
Old Karadeka: "Majority of human body made of fluid. In other words, you a water balloon, man."
* Read in P*t Mo**ta's voice
comments: This reads too odd not to adapt in some way. And the most famous old martial artist [instructor] who speaks 'oddly' in English is... there was no other choice, really. -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains only the stylized explanation comparing the water-rich human body to a water balloon. The English appends an external performance instruction that is not in the source.
records.remedy: Remove the appended voice-performance note and retain only the dialogue.

highlights.text:
Old Karadeka: "Majority of human body made of fluid. In other words, you a water balloon, man."
* Read in P*t Mo**ta's voice

records.jp: 「その柔軟かつ強靱な平手によって叩きあげられる斜め下からの一撃。こいつァ頭蓋内の体液と同調し、通常の拳打を上回る振動を脳に与える！」
records.en:
Old Karadeka: "Strike was with flexible yet strong palm, came from bottom, worked way up, diagonal. Opponent intra-skull fluids move with sympathy, give vibration to brain greater than that of normal fist strike!"
* Read in P*t Mo**ta's voice
comments: Intracranial -> intra-skull, since that word seemed a bit too big for the broken English feel. This is not the first, and not the last time that Taichi has auditory hallucinations. It's just one of the few that are made explicit. -GHS
records.assessment: The source contains only the stylized explanation of the palm strike’s vibration. The English appends an external performance instruction absent from the source.
records.remedy: Remove the appended voice-performance note and retain only the dialogue.

highlights.text:

records.jp: 「し、信じられないこのエロ猿っ、バカじゃないのっバカじゃないのっ」
records.en: Touko: "I-, I can't believe this monkey in heat! Aren't you stupid but aren't you stupid!"
comments: Unfortunately, the connection between this "monkey in heat" and Taichi's description of Yutaka in CCC3026 is gone. Sorry, "rapist monkey" doesn't work in English. -GHS
records.assessment: The repeated バカじゃないの is an angry “Are you stupid?” or “You idiot!” “Aren’t you stupid but aren’t you stupid” is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use a natural repeated insult such as “Are you stupid? Are you stupid?!”

highlights.text: Touko: "I-, I can't believe this monkey in heat! Aren't you stupid but aren't you stupid!"

records.jp: よれた尻の部分を直しながら、ブツブツと冬子。
records.en: Touko adjusts the twisted butt parts while grumbling,
comments: Too late to ask her not to get her panties in a bunch, I guess. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Touko grumbled while fixing the bunched-up seat of her swimsuit. “Twisted butt parts” is an unnatural and inaccurate description of the fabric.
records.remedy: Use “Touko grumbled as she straightened the bunched-up seat of her swimsuit.”

highlights.text: Touko adjusts the twisted butt parts while grumbling,
