records.jp: 対人関係のトラブルに弱い先輩は、はやくもグロッキーだった。
records.en: Senpai, so weak to interpersonal relationship troubles, was already groggy.
records.assessment: The source says Senpai is poor at handling interpersonal conflict. “Weak to interpersonal relationship troubles” is an unidiomatic calque.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai, who was bad at handling interpersonal conflict, was already groggy.”

highlights.text: Senpai, so weak to interpersonal relationship troubles, was already groggy.

records.jp: 「今日はこれからー、群青学院放送部の海水浴をー、はじめるー」
records.en: Taichi: "Today and on this hour! The Gunjou Institute Broadcast Club Beach Outing! Has beguuun!"
comments: Still sargeant. -GHS
records.assessment: The source announces that the club’s beach outing is starting now. “Today and on this hour” is not supported and the split sentence mishandles the announcement.
records.remedy: Use “And now, the Gunjou Academy Broadcasting Club beach outing begins!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Today and on this hour! The Gunjou Institute Broadcast Club Beach Outing! Has beguuun!"

records.jp: 「いいかー、よく聞けよー。二度たぁー言わねぇー。貴様らはカスだ！　このステーツで最高に口の臭いブタ野郎どもだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Awww right! Listen up! I won't say this twice! You bastards are scum! You are the worst mouth-breathing sons of a halfbreed bitch in all the fifty States!"
comments: I don't think it's right to channel Gunnery Sargeant Hartman without serious swearwords, but... original was 'stinking mouth female pigs bastards'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source insults them as the pigs with the foulest breath in the States. “Mouth-breathing sons of a halfbreed bitch” substitutes different insults and adds ancestry language absent from the source.
records.remedy: Preserve the foul-breathed-pigs insult without invented slurs.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Awww right! Listen up! I won't say this twice! You bastards are scum! You are the worst mouth-breathing sons of a halfbreed bitch in all the fifty States!"

records.jp: 「貴様らのような最低最悪の生ゴミのために、国が払っている維持費は決して安かねぇ。そいつは投資だ、だがそう見返りのある賭けじゃねぇ―――」
records.en: Taichi: "For the sake of the worthless, lowest, rotting kitchen leftovers that you bastards are, the country's paying maintenance costs that are by no means cheap! Theirs is an investment, nevertheless!, this ain't a gamble that has seen any level of return---"
records.assessment: The source says their upkeep is an investment but not a bet likely to yield much return. “Theirs is an investment, nevertheless!” is ungrammatical and “has seen” wrongly implies a completed investment history.
records.remedy: Use “It’s an investment, but not one likely to pay off.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "For the sake of the worthless, lowest, rotting kitchen leftovers that you bastards are, the country's paying maintenance costs that are by no means cheap! Theirs is an investment, nevertheless!, this ain't a gamble that has seen any level of return---"

records.jp: ややうんざりとした調子で、霧が頭を垂れた。
records.en: Her words sounding somewhat fed-up, Kiri hangs her head.
comments: Interesting that Taichi is ignoring his own words in the flashback. -GHS
records.assessment: The past narration says Kiri hung her head. “Kiri hangs” shifts the action into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Kiri hung her head.”

highlights.text: Her words sounding somewhat fed-up, Kiri hangs her head.

records.jp: 「イクラ、ウニ、中トロ、時価……」
records.en: Kiri: "Salted salmon roe, sea urchin, medium-fatty tuna, what's market price..."
comments: Might also be related to the above, i.e. she's going to make Taichi pay for all the sushi she didn't eat. See CCC0041 for the long awaited return of Medium-Fatty Tuna! -GHS
records.assessment: 時価 is a clipped list item meaning market price, emphasizing expensive sushi. “What’s market price” turns it into a question.
records.remedy: Use “salmon roe, sea urchin, medium-fatty tuna, market price...”

highlights.text: Kiri: "Salted salmon roe, sea urchin, medium-fatty tuna, what's market price..."

records.jp: 「で、桐原さんはどのような経路で？」
records.en: Misato: "So, what channel did they use for you, Kirihara-san?"
comments: She IS the one who calls this "Cross Channel". -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks by what route or pretext Kirihara was brought into the plan. “What channel did they use for you” sounds like a communication medium and obscures the question.
records.remedy: Use “And how did they get you here, Kirihara-san?”

highlights.text: Misato: "So, what channel did they use for you, Kirihara-san?"

records.jp: 鉄拳が震えていた。
records.en: She was shaking her 『Iron Fist * Tekken』.
comments: This is totally a Tekken reference, isn't it. Well, there's Melty Blood, so let's just roll with it. -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply says her iron fist trembled. The English adds a bracketed external title reference and makes her deliberately shake it.
records.remedy: Use “Her iron fist trembled.”

highlights.text: She was shaking her 『Iron Fist * Tekken』.

records.jp: 「ど、どーしてあんなすごい人があんたごときゴミ蔵にちゃん呼ばわりされてんのよ！」
records.en: Touko: "Ho-, hooow does a storehouse of garbage like you get to call that amazing person with the '-chan' honorific!"
comments: Seems not to be an actual dumpster: http://www.city.tatebayashi.gunma.jp/docs/2012080700013/ not that I would've translated it in another way... -GHS
records.assessment: The line asks how a garbage heap like him gets to call such an impressive person “-chan.” The English’s “does a storehouse of garbage ... get to call” is an opaque calque and mishandles the honorific phrase.
records.remedy: Use natural English while preserving the insult and surprise at his “-chan” familiarity.

highlights.text: Touko: "Ho-, hooow does a storehouse of garbage like you get to call that amazing person with the '-chan' honorific!"

records.jp: 「言葉にオブラートかけないのも限度ってものがあるだろう」
records.en: Taichi: "Because there does exist a limit on how much bush can be beaten around with words."
comments: Lit. oblaat. It's unnecessarily obscure, though there'll be necessarily a direct reference in a new line later on. This is pretty damn mean to Youko, but given everything, that fits. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says there is a limit to how completely one should avoid sugarcoating words. The English invokes “beating around the bush,” the opposite rhetorical behavior.
records.remedy: Use “There’s a limit to how little you can sugarcoat things.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because there does exist a limit on how much bush can be beaten around with words."

records.jp: 「ミキミキです。あのう、もしかして支倉先輩と黒須先輩はおつきあいされてますか？」
records.en: Miki: "This is Miki-Miki. Uhm, could it be that Hasekura-senpai and Kurosu-senpai are in a steady and formal relationship?"
comments: This being Miki, it's hard to tell if she really meant "dating" or "in some kind of business relationship" with the slightly more formal 'otsukiai'. Considering Taichi and Youko's relationship is way more complex than simple dating and that she's the Genius Loli, her figuring out is not out of character. Plus there's how Youko may well not exist, and Miki has possibly already figured this out. Leaving this sort of vague. -GHS
records.assessment: The source politely asks whether the two are dating. “A steady and formal relationship” adds conditions of steadiness and formality not present.
records.remedy: Use “Are Hasekura-senpai and Kurosu-senpai dating?”

highlights.text: Miki: "This is Miki-Miki. Uhm, could it be that Hasekura-senpai and Kurosu-senpai are in a steady and formal relationship?"

records.jp: 「……おそろしい……世の中どうかしてる……」
records.en:
Touko: "Can't be! That absolutely can't be!"
Misato: "Hyeee～h, beauty and the beee～ast!"
Tomoki: "...terrifying... the world's gone mad..."
comments: Misato's a real bitch here. Or is she just being prophetic, once more? After all, if there's a beast in that relationship, that'd be Youko. -GHS
records.assessment: This source unit contains only one short reaction about the frightening state of the world. The English prepends two additional characters’ lines that are not bound to this source span.
records.remedy: Withhold the unbound dialogue and translate only the bound reaction.

highlights.text:
Touko: "Can't be! That absolutely can't be!"
Misato: "Hyeee～h, beauty and the beee～ast!"
Tomoki: "...terrifying... the world's gone mad..."

records.jp: 「……おまえ伏せてれば何口走ってもいいとか思ってないか？」
records.en: Taichi: "...do you think that you can run your mouth out just because you use censorship?"
comments: This meta-reference means he's chuuning. This part is likely not happening literally. And it's (p)revenge for CCA0007. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether censorship makes him think he can blurt out anything. “Run your mouth out” is not an English idiom.
records.remedy: Use “You don’t think censoring it means you can say whatever you want, do you?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...do you think that you can run your mouth out just because you use censorship?"

records.jp: 「ぐぐぐ軍曹殿ーっ、宮澄先輩が卒倒されましたーっ！」
records.en: Miki: "Sa-Sa-Sargeant-donooo! Miyasumi-senpai was made to swooon!"
records.assessment: The source reports that Miyasumi-senpai has fainted. “Was made to swoon” implies that an external agent caused a romantic swoon.
records.remedy: Use “Miyasumi-senpai has collapsed!”

highlights.text: Miki: "Sa-Sa-Sargeant-donooo! Miyasumi-senpai was made to swooon!"

records.jp: 「……あの島先輩……嘘だと思われますから、そんな海に向かって全能神に祈らなくとも……」
records.en: Kiri: "...uhm, Shima-senpai... it does look like a lie, so there is no need to pray to the God Almighty while facing towards the sea like that..."
comments: Think big scene of character at sunset facing the sea screaming 'noooo'. Further specification that the above is the Christian God. It's technically just a tsukkomi, but it's odd that Kiri would say those exact words, isn't it? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says there is no need to pray to an almighty god while facing the sea. “Facing towards” is redundant and “the God Almighty” unnaturally turns the description into a title.
records.remedy: Use “you don’t need to face the sea and pray to an almighty god.”

highlights.text: Kiri: "...uhm, Shima-senpai... it does look like a lie, so there is no need to pray to the God Almighty while facing towards the sea like that..."

records.jp: 破壊力抜群だなオイ。
records.en: Extraordinary destructive power me's got.
records.assessment: The source comments that the preceding line has tremendous destructive power. “Extraordinary destructive power me’s got” is ungrammatical and assigns that power to the narrator himself.
records.remedy: Use “Now that’s some devastating power.”

highlights.text: Extraordinary destructive power me's got.

records.jp: なんか気分いー。
records.en: I'm in good mood somehow!
records.assessment: “I’m in good mood” is missing the required article.
records.remedy: Use “I’m in a good mood somehow.”

highlights.text: I'm in good mood somehow!

records.jp: 「っさいっ！　踊るのやめなさいよ！」
records.en: Touko: "'ddap! Enough with that dancing around!"
comments: Lisp -GHS
records.assessment: っさい is a clipped angry “Shut up!” or “You’re noisy!” The corrupted fragment “’ddap!” does not convey it intelligibly.
records.remedy: Use “Shut up! Stop dancing around!”

highlights.text: Touko: "'ddap! Enough with that dancing around!"

records.jp: 「……因果、なのかな。これって」
records.en: Kiri: "...fate, perhaps. It must be."
comments: Well, with all these sevens it certainly isn't Doom. -GHS
records.assessment: 因果 here invokes cause and effect or karmic consequence. “Fate” erases that causal implication, and “It must be” overstates the tentative なのかな.
records.remedy: Use “Maybe this is karma...”

highlights.text: Kiri: "...fate, perhaps. It must be."

records.jp: 「その大砲で私と撃ちあうつもりかね？」
records.en: Taichi: "Or are you just going to scare me with that cannon?"
comments: CP Laputa English script again
records.assessment: The source asks whether she intends to exchange fire with him using that cannon. The English instead asks whether she will merely scare him, replacing combat with intimidation.
records.remedy: Use “Do you intend to trade shots with me using that cannon?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Or are you just going to scare me with that cannon?"

records.jp: 「あんたもなに言ってるのよ……」
records.en: Touko: "What are you two talking about now..."
records.assessment: The source addresses one person as also saying something strange. “What are you two talking about” changes the number and invents a second addressee.
records.remedy: Use “What are you talking about too?”

highlights.text: Touko: "What are you two talking about now..."

records.jp: 「水着、ギャル、砂浜と来たらもうビーチバレー。これ、コンボイ」
records.en: Taichi: "We got swimsuits, a sandy beach, and gyaru so let's play volleyball already. Come on, convoy!"
comments: No, I haven't found anything tying 'convoy' to volley of any sort. I admit my giveashit levels for beach volley are fairly low outside of the obvious. -GHSwimsuits
records.assessment: コンボイ here is a comic deformation or extension of “combo,” following the swimsuit-girls-beach sequence. “Come on, convoy” turns it into a vehicle convoy and loses the combination joke.
records.remedy: Preserve the “combo” wordplay rather than translating it as a convoy.

highlights.text: Taichi: "We got swimsuits, a sandy beach, and gyaru so let's play volleyball already. Come on, convoy!"

records.jp: 「そう！　やっぱさー、ビーチバレーの本懐といったらもうそれっきゃないって感じで、俺なんかわざと胸を酷使する位置にパスする気まんまんでもー―――」
records.en: Taichi: "It is! You know it, as a cherished desire Beach Volley feels it's for that'n naught more, though I normally am brimming to the brim with desire to pass on situations of purposeful chestploitation, yeeet---"
records.assessment: The source says breast-bouncing is beach volleyball’s true purpose and that he is eager to send passes designed to make breasts work hard. The English’s “cherished desire Beach Volley” and “pass on situations” are largely unintelligible.
records.remedy: Render both the declared purpose and his plan to aim passes that make breasts bounce.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is! You know it, as a cherished desire Beach Volley feels it's for that'n naught more, though I normally am brimming to the brim with desire to pass on situations of purposeful chestploitation, yeeet---"

records.jp: 「安心したまえ、美希嬢」
records.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with staying at ease, Miki-jou!"
comments: See CCC0026. -GHS
records.assessment: 安心したまえ is “Rest assured” or “Don’t worry.” “Gladden me with staying at ease” reverses who is to be reassured and is not idiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “Rest assured, Miss Miki.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gladden me with staying at ease, Miki-jou!"

records.jp: 嫌がらないから美希は好きだ。
records.en: I like Miki because there's no hate in her.
comments: She literally doesn't understand it. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he likes Miki because she does not object to or dislike this treatment. “There’s no hate in her” turns her lack of resistance into a general absence of hatred.
records.remedy: Use “I like Miki because she doesn’t mind.”

highlights.text: I like Miki because there's no hate in her.

records.jp: 照れる。
records.en: Embarrassed.
records.assessment: 照れる describes her becoming bashful or embarrassed. The adjective fragment “Embarrassed” omits the subject and event.
records.remedy: Use “She blushed.”

highlights.text: Embarrassed.

records.jp: 「俺にはわかる。君は発育する！」
records.en: Taichi: "It is clear to me. You shall experience growth!"
comments: Not the same as CCA0026, but likely the same as CCA0008. -GHS
records.assessment: The source emphatically predicts that she will develop. “Experience growth” is bureaucratic and unnatural for the comic assurance.
records.remedy: Use “I can tell. You’re going to fill out!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is clear to me. You shall experience growth!"

records.jp: 横座りに片手をつくと、しなった体にふくよかな乳房がやわっこそうに揺れた。
records.en: Sitting with legs off to one side and rising with the help of one hand her body bends, two plump breasts there swayed so soff'ly.
comments: Still soff'. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives a past-tense image of her propping herself up sideways as her supple body bends and her breasts sway. The English is a run-on that shifts from “bends” to “swayed” and awkwardly inserts “there.”
records.remedy: Use a coherent past-tense sentence preserving the pose and movement.

highlights.text: Sitting with legs off to one side and rising with the help of one hand her body bends, two plump breasts there swayed so soff'ly.

records.jp: 「先輩って、美乳ですよね」
records.en: Taichi: "Senpai got beautiful boobs, don't she!"
records.assessment: “Senpai got ... don’t she” has mismatched verb forms and is not supported as a stable dialect in the source.
records.remedy: Use “You have beautiful breasts, Senpai.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Senpai got beautiful boobs, don't she!"

records.en: Misato: "Eh-?
records.assessment: The English line is missing its closing quotation mark, leaving the dialogue structurally unterminated.
records.remedy: Close the quoted dialogue.

highlights.text: Misato: "Eh-?

records.jp: 「まるで禁断の実のようだ。アダムでなくとも、たぶらかされてしまいそうですよ」
records.en: Taichi: "So much like the Forbidden Fruit. Adam I might not be, yet, they still seduce me so!"
comments: See? Full of them. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says even someone other than Adam would be seduced by fruit like this. “Adam I might not be” makes the comparison cumbersome and attaches the plural “they” to an unstated referent.
records.remedy: Use “They’re like forbidden fruit. Even someone who isn’t Adam could be tempted.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "So much like the Forbidden Fruit. Adam I might not be, yet, they still seduce me so!"

records.jp: 「お、犯されるぅ……」
records.en: Misato: "I-, I will be defiled..."
comments: PCP CCA0026
records.assessment: 犯される here means being sexually violated or ravished in her panicked role-play. “Defiled” abstracts the physical threat into loss of purity.
records.remedy: Use language that preserves the threatened sexual violation.

highlights.text: Misato: "I-, I will be defiled..."

records.jp: 「や、やめないかキミ！」
records.en: Tomoki: "W-, won't you cut it out, you!"
records.assessment: “Won’t you cut it out, you!” is an unnatural calque of his flustered command.
records.remedy: Use “H-hey, cut it out!”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "W-, won't you cut it out, you!"

records.jp: 「ケッ、ただの冗談じゃねぇかよ、ミスターシスコン君はちょっと姉にインモラルな感情持ちすぎなんじゃねえのか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Pah, ain't this just a joke now! Mistah Siscon-kun, don't you sort of have too much Immoral feelings for your own sister now!?"
comments: Immoral capitalized as it's his nickname. -GHS
records.assessment: “Too much Immoral feelings” has number disagreement and unnecessary capitalization.
records.remedy: Use “don’t you have a few too many immoral feelings for your own sister?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Pah, ain't this just a joke now! Mistah Siscon-kun, don't you sort of have too much Immoral feelings for your own sister now!?"

records.jp: 「誰がシスコンだ誰がっ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Who's the siscon who!"
records.assessment: The repeated 誰が is an emphatic denial, “Who are you calling a siscon?” “Who’s the siscon who” is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “Who are you calling a siscon?!”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Who's the siscon who!"

records.jp: しかし少し焦っている。
records.en: And still he lost his patience a bit.
records.assessment: 焦っている means he is somewhat flustered or panicked. “Lost his patience” instead describes anger or impatience.
records.remedy: Use “But he looked a little flustered.”

highlights.text: And still he lost his patience a bit.

records.jp: 「カ、カラダはいやぁ～」
records.en: Misato: "My-, my body you caaa～n't!"
comments: PCP CCA0012 and 13
records.assessment: The source is a panicked “N-not my body!” The English “My body you can’t” is incomplete and does not state the refusal intelligibly.
records.remedy: Use “N-not my body!”

highlights.text: Misato: "My-, my body you caaa～n't!"

records.jp: 「あのっ、失礼しますしますしますっ！！！！」
records.en: Girl: "A-uhm, if I maying may may mayyyyyy!!!!!!"
comments: She doesn't say desu-masu, but... adapted so it fits with "to payback you", see CCA0013 -GHS
records.assessment: 失礼します is an interruption or polite “excuse me.” “If I maying may may” is not intelligible English and does not reproduce the stuttered interruption.
records.remedy: Use a stuttered “E-excuse me!”

highlights.text: Girl: "A-uhm, if I maying may may mayyyyyy!!!!!!"

records.jp: 「ゆ、遊紗です。おおおお忙しいところ、申し訳ないです」
records.en: Yusa: "I-, I am Yusa. You-You-You-You are so very busy, it is inexcusable yes!"
comments: ~moe kyun~ -GHS
records.assessment: She apologizes for interrupting while they are busy. The English tells them “You are so very busy” and calls that state inexcusable, shifting what she is apologizing for.
records.remedy: Use “I-I’m Yusa. I’m sorry to interrupt when you’re so busy.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "I-, I am Yusa. You-You-You-You are so very busy, it is inexcusable yes!"

records.jp: 「あ、あの、本日はお招きネキネキ……いたっ」
records.en: Yusa: "Ah, ah-uhm, for inviting me this day-ay-ay... bwah!"
records.assessment: The source begins thanking them for today’s invitation before she bites her tongue. “For inviting me this day” is an unnatural calque.
records.remedy: Use “Th-thank you for inviting me today—ow!”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Ah, ah-uhm, for inviting me this day-ay-ay... bwah!"

records.jp: ざわっ
records.en: Whisper!
comments: SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS
records.assessment: ざわっ is the sudden rustle or murmur of the whole group reacting. The singular command-like “Whisper!” does not convey that collective reaction.
records.remedy: Use “A murmur ran through the group.”

highlights.text: Whisper!

records.jp: 「……今の限りなくマイナスに振り切れた空気はどういう意味だ？」
records.en: Taichi: "...what is the meaning of this temperature that's boundlessly swinging back towards sub-zero?"
records.assessment: The source speaks of the atmosphere plunging infinitely into the negative. “Temperature ... swinging back towards sub-zero” substitutes a literal temperature and adds a return motion.
records.remedy: Use “What was that atmosphere plunging straight into the negatives just now?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...what is the meaning of this temperature that's boundlessly swinging back towards sub-zero?"

records.jp: 「黒須君の、オトモダチなんですか？」
records.en: Misato: "Kurosu-kun's... is this a 'friend' of yours?"
comments: veeery off. -GHS
records.assessment: “Kurosu-kun’s... is this a ‘friend’ of yours?” duplicates the possessive construction.
records.remedy: Use “Is she a ‘friend’ of yours, Kurosu-kun?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Kurosu-kun's... is this a 'friend' of yours?"

records.jp: 「彼女です。同棲してます」
records.en: Taichi: "Girlfriend. We are sharing house."
comments: See CCA0018 -GHS
records.assessment: “We are sharing house” is missing an article or the idiomatic verb for living together.
records.remedy: Use “She’s my girlfriend. We live together.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Girlfriend. We are sharing house."

records.jp: 「どう」
records.en: Miki: "Sharing."
records.assessment: The source splits the first sound of 同棲 across two speakers. Translating どう as the semantic word “Sharing” destroys the audible completion gag.
records.remedy: Preserve the first syllable of the split word.

highlights.text: Miki: "Sharing."

records.jp: 「せい？」
records.en: Touko: "House?"
records.assessment: The source supplies the second sound of 同棲. Translating せい as “House” gives a semantic gloss rather than completing the spoken wordplay.
records.remedy: Preserve the second syllable so the two lines audibly form “dousei.”

highlights.text: Touko: "House?"

records.jp: 遊紗ちゃんに直接語りかける。
records.en: Yusa-chan is addressed directly.
records.assessment: The source says Misato directly addresses Yusa. The passive “Yusa-chan is addressed” omits the acting speaker and weakens the transition.
records.remedy: Use “She addressed Yusa-chan directly.”

highlights.text: Yusa-chan is addressed directly.

records.jp: 「とまあ、これくらい素直な女の子なわけです。よろしく」
records.en: Taichi: "And well, you see how obedient this girl is. Treat her well!"
records.assessment: 素直 here describes Yusa as candid, straightforward, or guileless. “Obedient” recasts it as compliance to authority.
records.remedy: Use “That’s how straightforward a girl she is.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "And well, you see how obedient this girl is. Treat her well!"

records.jp: 「遊紗ちゃんと言うですか。わたし、山辺美希です」
records.en: Miki: "You're Yusa-chan, you said then. I am Yamanobe Miki!"
records.assessment: The source asks or confirms that her name is Yusa-chan. “You said then” adds an unsupported report and is not grammatical in context.
records.remedy: Use “So your name is Yusa-chan? I’m Yamanobe Miki.”

highlights.text: Miki: "You're Yusa-chan, you said then. I am Yamanobe Miki!"

records.jp: こ、この寝取り野郎……遊紗ちゃんを……俺の遊紗ちゃんをっ？
records.en: Y-, you netori bastard... he, Yusa-chan... MY Yusa-chan?
records.assessment: The internal outburst is broken by “he, Yusa-chan,” which introduces an unclear pronoun and fails to connect the accusation to Tomoki.
records.remedy: Use a coherent jealous outburst identifying Tomoki as the target.

highlights.text: Y-, you netori bastard... he, Yusa-chan... MY Yusa-chan?

records.jp: 「曜子ちゃん、ちゃんと送ってくれた？」
records.en: Taichi: "Was Youko-chan nice when she took you here?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether Youko properly brought or escorted her there. “Was ... nice” asks about her demeanor instead of whether the transport was completed.
records.remedy: Use “Did Youko-chan bring you here all right?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Was Youko-chan nice when she took you here?"

records.jp: 「にゃー」
records.en: Taichi: "You meown't say..."
records.assessment: The source is only a catlike “meow.” “You meown’t say” invents a full response and changes the utterance’s function.
records.remedy: Use a simple “Meow.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You meown't say..."

records.jp: 「で、本人は？」
records.en: Taichi: "So, and the person herself?"
records.assessment: 本人 asks where Youko herself is. “And the person herself?” is an unnatural fragment that does not clearly ask her location.
records.remedy: Use “So where is she?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "So, and the person herself?"

records.jp: どっかにいるな。
records.en: Where could she be.
records.assessment: The source confidently infers that she is somewhere nearby. “Where could she be” turns that conclusion into an open question.
records.remedy: Use “She must be around here somewhere.”

highlights.text: Where could she be.

records.jp: 一応、一緒に海水浴に『参加』してはくれたわけだ。
records.en: Seems like that, tentatively, she has decided to "participate" in our beachside outing.
comments: It totally means she's out there observing, not that she's Taichi. Yu-up. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she has, at least technically, joined the outing. “Has decided to participate” adds a decision and uses a tentative construction absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use “At least she had technically ‘joined’ our beach outing.”

highlights.text: Seems like that, tentatively, she has decided to "participate" in our beachside outing.

records.jp: 「さて、遊紗ちゃんも来てくれたところで遊ぶか」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, since Yusa-chan's here, how about we get to some playing!"
comments: Note that Yusa's name uses the kanji 遊 for play. -GHS
records.assessment: “Get to some playing” is an unnatural nominal calque of the invitation to start playing.
records.remedy: Use “Now that Yusa-chan is here, let’s play.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then, since Yusa-chan's here, how about we get to some playing!"

records.jp: 「男の先輩二人はそれぞれ別れてください」
records.en: Miki: "The two male Senpai will split up, please!"
records.assessment: The instruction is for the two male seniors to go onto separate teams, one on each side. “The two male Senpai will split up” is ambiguous about simply leaving and mishandles the plural title.
records.remedy: Use “The two male senpai should be on separate teams.”

highlights.text: Miki: "The two male Senpai will split up, please!"

records.jp: 思い出せなかった。
records.en: We didn't remember.
records.assessment: 思い出せなかった means they could not recall it, not simply that they did not remember as a completed choice.
records.remedy: Use “We couldn’t remember.”

highlights.text: We didn't remember.

records.jp: 揺らすー。揺らしちゃるー。
records.en: Jiiiggle, sooo much jiggle!
records.assessment: The source expresses his intention to make the breasts bounce. “Jiggle, so much jiggle” omits both his agency and the future action.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll make them bounce. Just you wait.”

highlights.text: Jiiiggle, sooo much jiggle!

records.jp: 俺は宮澄先輩のお素敵おっぱいに思いを馳せた。
records.en: Thoughts gallop towards Miyasumi-senpai's most wonderful oppai.
comments: No powaru? And he keeps calling her by last name in his mind. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he thought of her wonderful breasts. “Thoughts gallop” is a subjectless fragment in context and adds an unsupported racing metaphor.
records.remedy: Use “My thoughts turned to Miyasumi-senpai’s wonderful breasts.”

highlights.text: Thoughts gallop towards Miyasumi-senpai's most wonderful oppai.

records.jp: 「はよう言わぬか」
records.en: Taichi: "Early and wordlessly!"
comments: How long has he stood there like an idiot? -GHS
records.assessment: はよう言わぬか is a comic demand to have told him sooner. “Early and wordlessly” means neither that demand nor a coherent response.
records.remedy: Use “Why didn’t you tell me sooner?!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Early and wordlessly!"

records.jp: あいつか。
records.en: Her I guess.
records.assessment: “Her I guess” uses unnatural word order for his recognition that she threw it.
records.remedy: Use “So it was her.”

highlights.text: Her I guess.

records.jp: ボールを手に立ち上がる。
records.en: I toss the ball up.
records.assessment: The source says he stands up with the ball in his hand. The English says he tosses the ball upward, inventing a different action.
records.remedy: Use “I stood up with the ball in hand.”

highlights.text: I toss the ball up.

records.jp: 「我が米軍はとうの昔にその情報をゲットしてたんだよ！」
records.en: Taichi: "But our American military performed an Information Get on that a long time ago!"
comments: Let's not pretend he's not going insane, please. -GHS
records.assessment: The source boasts that the American forces got the information long ago. “Performed an Information Get” is not intelligible English.
records.remedy: Use “But our American forces got that intel ages ago!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But our American military performed an Information Get on that a long time ago!"

records.jp: アタック。
records.en: ~ATTAKU~
comments: Same. -GHS
records.assessment: The source is the English loanword “attack” used as narration. Rendering it as decorative romanized Japanese leaves the word untranslated and changes the presentation.
records.remedy: Use “Attack.”

highlights.text: ~ATTAKU~

records.jp: ちっ、さすが元運動部。
records.en: Tsk, of course, the ex-sports club.
records.assessment: The source notes that he is a former sports-club member. “The ex-sports club” incorrectly makes the club itself former.
records.remedy: Use “Of course—he used to be on a sports team.”

highlights.text: Tsk, of course, the ex-sports club.

records.jp: 再びやってきた玉を、今度は宮澄先輩に戻す。
records.en: I have the ball once again, and this time I return it towards Miyasumi-senpai.
records.assessment: The source is past narration: he returned the ball that came to him again toward Miyasumi-senpai. “I have the ball” shifts to present possession and makes the two clauses temporally uneven.
records.remedy: Use “When the ball came back to me, I returned it toward Miyasumi-senpai.”

highlights.text: I have the ball once again, and this time I return it towards Miyasumi-senpai.

records.jp: おたおたと右往左往する。
records.en: Left and right and confused and left and speechless and right.
records.assessment: The source says she flusteredly scurries this way and that. “Left and right and confused and left and speechless and right” is not a sentence and adds speechlessness.
records.remedy: Use “She scurried back and forth in a panic.”

highlights.text: Left and right and confused and left and speechless and right.

records.jp: レシーブした玉が、桐原冬子の後頭部に当たった。
records.en: Her receive makes the ball hit Kirihara Touko right in the back of the head.
records.assessment: The source says the ball she received hit Touko in the back of the head. “Her receive makes the ball hit” uses a noun as an action, changes tense, and overstates direct causation.
records.remedy: Use “The ball she received hit Kirihara Touko in the back of the head.”

highlights.text: Her receive makes the ball hit Kirihara Touko right in the back of the head.

records.jp: 「るさいっ！　笑わないでよ！」
records.en: Touko: "'ddap! Don't you laugh!"
comments: Lisp -GHS
records.assessment: るさい is a clipped angry “Shut up!” The corrupted fragment “’ddap!” does not convey it intelligibly.
records.remedy: Use “Shut up! Don’t laugh!”

highlights.text: Touko: "'ddap! Don't you laugh!"

records.jp: あかん、宮澄先輩と大差ないスペックだ。
records.en: No good, her specs are not much different from Miyasumi-senpai!
comments: The youngins may be cute... see CCX0001, but it's all but the subtext between the two. -GHS
records.assessment: スペック humorously compares her overall athletic capability to Miyasumi-senpai’s. “Her specs” sounds like technical specifications rather than ability in natural English.
records.remedy: Use “No good—she’s about as athletic as Miyasumi-senpai.”

highlights.text: No good, her specs are not much different from Miyasumi-senpai!

records.jp: 運動神経の良さそうな佐倉霧に、目で合図を送る。
records.en: I send a signal with the eyes to Great Motor Reflexes Sakura Kiri.
comments: Watch him use his eyes to hallucinate an entire dialogue.
records.assessment: The source describes Kiri as looking athletic and says he signals her with his eyes. “Great Motor Reflexes Sakura Kiri” converts that description into an invented title or name.
records.remedy: Use “I signaled Sakura Kiri, who looked athletic, with my eyes.”

highlights.text: I send a signal with the eyes to Great Motor Reflexes Sakura Kiri.

records.jp: 俺の妄想かもしれないが。
records.en: Or maybe that was how my delusion did.
comments: Don't spoil it! -GHS
records.assessment: The source adds that the entire exchange may have been his imagination. “Or maybe that was how my delusion did” is ungrammatical and treats the delusion as an unspecified action.
records.remedy: Use “Though maybe I imagined the whole exchange.”

highlights.text: Or maybe that was how my delusion did.

records.jp: 「あっ、くるっ、くるるっ？」
records.en: Yusa: "Ah, this way, this wayay?"
records.assessment: She stammers that the ball is coming. “This way, this wayay?” changes the incoming-ball warning into a spatial direction and invents a word.
records.remedy: Use a stammered “I-it’s coming?”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Ah, this way, this wayay?"

records.jp: くるるとか言ってる。
records.en: Wayay is among the things she's saying.
records.assessment: The narration explicitly repeats her odd sound くるる. Translating it as the invented semantic word “wayay” breaks the audible echo with the preceding line.
records.remedy: Repeat the same stammered sound used in the preceding translation.

highlights.text: Wayay is among the things she's saying.

records.jp: 走る（すべる）。
records.en: And she runs (I mean, slips),
comments: Kinnikuman reference http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cUOegCG3v1A there doesn't seem to be an official English translation, and the only people seemingly translating the series are MuscleSubs, so this is a riff on their translation. -GHS
records.assessment: The parenthesis corrects “runs” to “slips”: she tries to run but slips. “Runs (I mean, slips)” reads as a narrator revising vocabulary rather than the comic action correction.
records.remedy: Use “She runs—no, slips.”

highlights.text: And she runs (I mean, slips),

records.jp: 見事に（転ぶ）。
records.en: beautifully (then she falls).
records.assessment: The source completes the comic action in present-tense shorthand, but “beautifully (then she falls)” adds sequence filler and awkwardly nests the action in parentheses.
records.remedy: Use “and goes down spectacularly.”

highlights.text: beautifully (then she falls).

records.jp: 顔面から突っ込んだ美希の、こぶりな尻にボールは落ちた。
records.en: Miki having plunged face-first, the ball bounces on her undersized butt.
records.assessment: The source says the ball landed on Miki’s small butt after she dove face-first. “Bounces” changes the event, while “undersized” adds a disparaging judgment absent from 小ぶり.
records.remedy: Use “The ball landed on Miki’s small butt as she lay face-down.”

highlights.text: Miki having plunged face-first, the ball bounces on her undersized butt.

records.jp: 「心に愛があったことだけは認めよう」
records.en: Taichi: "I only concede that there was love in my heart!"
comments: See CCD2002, ouch. -GHS
records.assessment: The line acknowledges that Miki at least had love in her heart when trying to help. “There was love in my heart” assigns that motive to the speaker instead.
records.remedy: Use “At least I’ll admit your heart was in the right place.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I only concede that there was love in my heart!"

records.jp: 顔をあげた美希の顔が赤い。
records.en: She had raised her head and Miki's head is red.
comments: Intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Miki’s face is red when she lifts it. The English duplicates “head,” shifts between past and present, and makes the modifier structurally unclear.
records.remedy: Use “Miki raised her head; her face was red.”

highlights.text: She had raised her head and Miki's head is red.

records.jp: 砂浜になにか切れる破片がまざっていたんだ。
records.en: Something that had cut off and splintered mixed in the sand of the beach.
records.assessment: The source says some sharp fragment capable of cutting her was mixed into the sand. “Something that had cut off and splintered mixed” misreads 切れる and omits a finite verb.
records.remedy: Use “There must have been a sharp fragment mixed into the sand.”

highlights.text: Something that had cut off and splintered mixed in the sand of the beach.

records.jp: 背筋がゾワゾワ来る。
records.en: A bizarre shivering up and down the muscles along the spine.
records.assessment: The source says a crawling shiver runs up his spine. The English is a verbless noun phrase about “muscles along the spine.”
records.remedy: Use “A shiver crawled up my spine.”

highlights.text: A bizarre shivering up and down the muscles along the spine.

records.jp: 「やだ、割けてる！」
records.en: Kiri: "Oh no, it's a cut!"
comments: Where did she even hit her head? -GHS
records.assessment: 割けてる says the skin is split or gashed open. “It’s a cut” weakens the visible extent of the injury.
records.remedy: Use “Oh no, it’s split open!”

highlights.text: Kiri: "Oh no, it's a cut!"

records.jp: 「ご、ごめんなさいわたしのせいで……」
records.en: sYusa: "So-, sorryit'sallmyfauuult..."
comments: Compressed -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker label is corrupted as “sYusa,” and the apology is run together into an unreadable word string.
records.remedy: Restore the speaker label and readable spacing.

highlights.text: sYusa: "So-, sorryit'sallmyfauuult..."

records.jp: 血を見ないよう、お茶を差しだす。
records.en: I put the tea between us, to not see the blood.
records.assessment: The source says he holds out the tea so he will not have to look at the blood. “Put the tea between us” invents a barrier between people and obscures his avoidance.
records.remedy: Use “I held out the tea, trying not to look at the blood.”

highlights.text: I put the tea between us, to not see the blood.

records.jp: 「えと、どうすんの、こんなとき……あれ？」
records.en: Kiri: "Uhm, what to do at times like this... but?"
comments: panicky -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks what to do in this situation, then reacts “huh?” “But?” introduces an unsupported contrast and leaves the question malformed.
records.remedy: Use “Um, what do you do at a time like this... huh?”

highlights.text: Kiri: "Uhm, what to do at times like this... but?"

records.jp: 「ぼ、僕にできることは？　ねえ、僕にできること？」
records.en: Tonoki: "Wh-, what can I do? Hey! What can I do?"
records.assessment: The speaker label misspells Tomoki as “Tonoki,” corrupting the named speaker attribution.
records.remedy: Correct the speaker label to Tomoki.

highlights.text: Tonoki: "Wh-, what can I do? Hey! What can I do?"

records.jp: こいつはこいつで健常なくせに！
records.en: He asks, HE, when he's all normal!
comments: getting really angry now -GHS
records.assessment: The source protests that he is able-bodied himself yet is also asking what to do. “He asks, HE, when he’s all normal” is not idiomatic and loses the contrast with everyone else’s panic.
records.remedy: Use “And he’s perfectly able-bodied, too!”

highlights.text: He asks, HE, when he's all normal!

records.jp: 何人かが泣きだして、何人かがおろおろとして。
records.en: Some people are crying, some people are all shook up,
comments: Which we're supposed to take as being because They Are Abnormal. But this isn't all that abnormal. -GHS
records.assessment: The surrounding narration is past tense, but “are crying” and “are all shook up” shift the group reaction into the present.
records.remedy: Use “Some started crying, while others panicked.”

highlights.text: Some people are crying, some people are all shook up,

records.jp: 俺も血を見たくなくてグダグダで。
records.en: and I was boiling over because I didn't want to see blood.
records.assessment: The source says he too becomes useless and incoherent because he cannot bear to see blood. “Boiling over” normally suggests mounting anger and changes the reaction.
records.remedy: Use “I was falling apart too because I couldn’t stand looking at the blood.”

highlights.text: and I was boiling over because I didn't want to see blood.

records.jp: プルタブのあく音。
records.en: The sound of the pulltab.
records.assessment: The source specifically identifies the sound of the can’s pull tab opening. “The sound of the pulltab” omits the opening action.
records.remedy: Use “The sound of the pull tab opening.”

highlights.text: The sound of the pulltab.

records.jp: 「……緑茶に含まれるカテキンに殺菌効果があるんだよ～」
records.en: Taichi: "...because green tea includes Catechin that has sterilization effects, duh～!"
comments: still a bit angry. Effect seems true, too, but that's just... an odd thing and weird thing to up and do, doesn't it? -GHS
records.assessment: 殺菌効果 is an antibacterial or germ-killing effect. “Sterilization effects” overstates it as complete sterilization, and the added “duh” is unsupported.
records.remedy: Use “The catechins in green tea have an antibacterial effect.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...because green tea includes Catechin that has sterilization effects, duh～!"

records.jp: 「俺の鞄にハンカチあるから、それあてて」
records.en: Taichi: "There's a handkerchief in my bag, go get it."
comments: But he had the tea lying right there? -GHS
records.assessment: The source tells them to use the handkerchief in his bag as a compress on the wound. “Go get it” stops at retrieval and omits applying it.
records.remedy: Use “There’s a handkerchief in my bag—press it against the cut.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's a handkerchief in my bag, go get it."

records.jp: 目を開ける。
records.en: I open my eyes,
records.assessment: The narration is past tense, but “I open my eyes” shifts the action to present.
records.remedy: Use “I opened my eyes.”

highlights.text: I open my eyes,

records.jp: ちょうど見里先輩が、ハンカチをあてがっていた。
records.en: just as Misato-senpai applied a handkerchief.
comments: Guessing cold war, but it's still odd. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Misato-senpai was holding the handkerchief against the injury. “Applied a handkerchief” omits what it was applied to and sounds like a completed placement rather than maintained pressure.
records.remedy: Use “Misato-senpai was pressing the handkerchief to her forehead.”

highlights.text: just as Misato-senpai applied a handkerchief.

records.jp: 「美希、いたむ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Hurts, Miki?"
records.assessment: “Hurts, Miki?” is an unidiomatic truncation of the question.
records.remedy: Use “Does it hurt, Miki?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hurts, Miki?"

records.jp: 「お茶、よく気づいたね。誰なの？」
records.en: Taichi: "At least someone realized about the tea. Who was it?"
records.assessment: The source praises whoever thought of using the tea and asks who it was. “At least” adds a dismissive contrast, while “realized about the tea” is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “Good thinking with the tea. Who was that?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "At least someone realized about the tea. Who was it?"

records.jp: 「混乱してる時に、視界のはしに誰かいたような」
records.en: Misato: "When it was all bustling, I maybe saw someone with the corner of my eyes."
records.assessment: “With the corner of my eyes” has number and preposition errors for catching someone at the edge of her vision.
records.remedy: Use “In the confusion, I thought I saw someone out of the corner of my eye.”

highlights.text: Misato: "When it was all bustling, I maybe saw someone with the corner of my eyes."

records.jp: そんなスーパー忍者みたいな意識読解技術を持つ人間と言ったら……。
records.en: If we're talking about a human possessing a Super Ninja-like Awareness Comprehension Technique...
records.assessment: The source describes a person with super-ninja-like skill at reading awareness or intentions. The capitalized phrase “Awareness Comprehension Technique” is an opaque literal calque.
records.remedy: Use “Someone with super-ninja-level mind-reading skills...”

highlights.text: If we're talking about a human possessing a Super Ninja-like Awareness Comprehension Technique...

records.jp: 周囲を見渡したが、姿はない。
records.en: I look over the surrounding, but her figure's nowhere.
records.assessment: The source is past tense, but “I look” shifts to present; “the surrounding” is also the wrong noun form.
records.remedy: Use “I looked around, but she was nowhere to be seen.”

highlights.text: I look over the surrounding, but her figure's nowhere.

records.jp: 当たり前か。
records.en: As expectable, then.
comments: Of course. She doesn't exist. -GHS
records.assessment: “As expectable” is not idiomatic English for the narrator’s “Of course.”
records.remedy: Use “Of course.”

highlights.text: As expectable, then.

records.jp: 全員が同時にぐったりとした。
records.en: All club members grew exhausted simultaneously.
records.assessment: The source says everyone sagged or went limp at once, a shared release or deflation. “Grew exhausted” substitutes fatigue as a developing state.
records.remedy: Use “Everyone sagged at the same time.”

highlights.text: All club members grew exhausted simultaneously.

records.jp: 「ずっとオチャオチャ叫んでたから」
records.en: Miki: "Because you were all screaming 'the tea, the tea'."
records.assessment: The source tells one person that he kept yelling “tea.” “You were all screaming” turns the single speaker into the whole group.
records.remedy: Use “Because you kept shouting ‘Tea! Tea!’”

highlights.text: Miki: "Because you were all screaming 'the tea, the tea'."

records.jp: 「……そうか」
records.en: Taichi: "...well then."
records.assessment: そうか is an acknowledgment such as “I see.” “Well then” instead signals a transition or consequence.
records.remedy: Use “I see.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...well then."

records.jp: 「ういやつじゃ」
records.en: Taichi: "Lov'ble 'un ye."
records.assessment: The attempted archaic English “Lov’ble ’un ye” is not grammatically intelligible and obscures the playful “What a dear girl.”
records.remedy: Use a readable playful-archaic line such as “What a sweet lass.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Lov'ble 'un ye."

records.jp: 「私、つき添います。先輩がたは帰ってて結構ですから」
records.en: Kiri: "I am going to follow. If you Senpai wish to go home, that will be fine."
records.assessment: The source says the seniors may go home because she will accompany Miki. “If you Senpai wish” is ungrammatical and adds desire as a condition.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll go with her. You senpai can head home.”

highlights.text: Kiri: "I am going to follow. If you Senpai wish to go home, that will be fine."

records.jp: 「そうはいくまいよ。のう？」
records.en: Taichi: "Sooo do we. No?"
comments: TL Note: "nou" means "no". Or brain. But that was "ou nou". Wait, that's worry never mind. -GHS
records.assessment: そうはいくまい says they cannot simply do that or leave it to her. “Sooo do we” instead appears to agree and does not express the refusal.
records.remedy: Use “We can’t very well do that. Right?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sooo do we. No?"

records.jp: 「うむ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Nah."
records.assessment: うむ is affirmative, “Indeed” or “Right.” “Nah” gives the opposite polarity.
records.remedy: Use “Right.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Nah."

records.jp: 不器用に一礼して、美希を追った。
records.en: After an awkward bow she chases after Miki.
records.assessment: The source says she bowed awkwardly and followed Miki. “Chases” shifts the completed action into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “After an awkward bow, she hurried after Miki.”

highlights.text: After an awkward bow she chases after Miki.

records.jp: 「遊紗ちゃん、あいつらかーいーだろ」
records.en: Taichi: "Yusa-chan, those girls' so kyuuute ain't 'em?"
records.assessment: “Those girls’ so kyuuute ain’t ’em?” has both possessive/verb confusion and pronoun disagreement.
records.remedy: Use “Yusa-chan, those girls are cute, aren’t they?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yusa-chan, those girls' so kyuuute ain't 'em?"

records.jp: 「え？　そ、そうですか？　大人っぽい人たちで……なんか……わたしひとり子供で」
records.en: Yusa: "Eh? The-, they are? They are so adult-like... but I... I am an only child..."
comments: She's a year under them, and she IS an only child. IOW, she's lonely. Watch out. -GHS
records.assessment: わたしひとり子供 means she feels like the only child among adults. “I am an only child” instead says she has no siblings.
records.remedy: Use “They’re so grown-up... and I’m the only kid here.”

highlights.text: Yusa: "Eh? The-, they are? They are so adult-like... but I... I am an only child..."

records.jp: ちゃん呼ばわりかよ。
records.en: You are using -chan.
records.assessment: The source is his internal surprise that Tomoki is already calling her “-chan.” “You are using -chan” supplies a vague addressee and omits the earliness of that familiarity.
records.remedy: Use “He’s already calling her ‘-chan’?”

highlights.text: You are using -chan.

records.jp: こいつもしかして、天然寝取り属性か？
records.en: Could this guy be, maybe, have a Natural Netori Character Attribute?
records.assessment: The source wonders whether Tomoki naturally has a girlfriend-stealing trait. “Could this guy be, maybe, have” is ungrammatical, and “Character Attribute” is an opaque literal label.
records.remedy: Use “Does this guy naturally have a girlfriend-stealing streak?”

highlights.text: Could this guy be, maybe, have a Natural Netori Character Attribute?

records.jp: やっぱ要注意だな。
records.en: Definitely requires attention.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator must keep an eye on him. “Definitely requires attention” omits both the watcher and the person being watched.
records.remedy: Use “I definitely needed to keep an eye on him.”

highlights.text: Definitely requires attention.

records.jp: 心中、友貴の監視レベルを１つあげた。
records.en: In my hearts of hearts, the surveillance level of Tomoki increased by one.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator privately raises Tomoki’s surveillance level by one. The English makes the level rise by itself and uses the malformed plural “hearts of hearts.”
records.remedy: Use “Inwardly, I raised Tomoki’s surveillance level by one.”

highlights.text: In my hearts of hearts, the surveillance level of Tomoki increased by one.

records.jp: 「同じ釜の飯を食う者同士の結束力さ。うらやましいかい？」
records.en: Taichi: "It's the strength of the cohesiveness of people close enough to eat out of the same pot. Are you jealous?"
comments: Adapted a bit because the meaning is likely not instantly obvious in English. At least "eating out of the same pot" doesn't seem to indicate the same level of lesb~ les~~~ lesb~~~~~ """friendship""" it seems to do in Japanese. And here we go: see the final question? It's basically "are you lonely?" in this context. Taichi is having a real bad reaction post-blood. -GHS
records.assessment: The proverb refers to the bond among people who eat from the same pot. “Strength of the cohesiveness” is redundant and unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “That’s the bond between people who eat from the same pot.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's the strength of the cohesiveness of people close enough to eat out of the same pot. Are you jealous?"

records.jp: 「キミもじきに仲間入りさ」
records.en: Taichi: "You'll soon find a group to join, too."
comments: Awwww shit x2 -GHS
records.assessment: 仲間入り says she will soon join their circle. “Find a group to join, too” changes the promised group from this group to some unspecified future group.
records.remedy: Use “You’ll be one of us soon enough.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You'll soon find a group to join, too."

records.jp: 「ほんとは……私立の付属校に行く予定だったんですけど」
records.en: Yusa: "Truth is... I was planning to attend a private elevator school, but..."
comments: Likely in the big City. -GHS
records.assessment: 付属校 is an affiliated private school with an internal progression route. “Elevator school” is a Japanese calque that is not intelligible to most English readers.
records.remedy: Use “a private affiliated school” or explain the internal progression naturally.

highlights.text: Yusa: "Truth is... I was planning to attend a private elevator school, but..."

records.jp: 「……適応試験でやっちゃって……」
records.en: Yusa: "...then I had the Conformity Test..."
comments: Still curiously uncertain whether it's compulsory, it sounds like it wasn't for Touko. Sooo what's her score? It can't be that of a normal person. -GHS
records.assessment: やっちゃって implies that something went badly on the aptitude or placement test. “Then I had the Conformity Test” merely states that she took it and omits the failure or mishap.
records.remedy: Use “but I messed up the aptitude test...”

highlights.text: Yusa: "...then I had the Conformity Test..."

records.jp: 「安心したまえ。我々もだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with being at ease. 'Tis the same for us."
comments: See CCC0026. -GHS
records.assessment: 安心したまえ means “Rest assured” or “Don’t worry.” “Gladden me with being at ease” reverses who is being reassured and is not idiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t worry. The same thing happened to us.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gladden me with being at ease. 'Tis the same for us."

records.jp: 「ちょっと、この子が入ってくる頃には私たちいないんじゃないの？」
records.en: Touko: "Hold it, when this girl came around none of us were there weren't we?"
comments: This line is odd. Of course everyone was there when they entered, if she goes to Gunjou from this year. I suspect this is when Youko brought her in. And with this line, the correct spelling would be "Youko" -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that by the time this girl enters the school, they will no longer be there. The English changes that future absence into a past claim that they were not there when she arrived.
records.remedy: Use “Won’t we be gone by the time she starts here?”

highlights.text: Touko: "Hold it, when this girl came around none of us were there weren't we?"

records.jp: 「浪漫を解さぬ輩は海の家でまずいラーメンでも食ってろ」
records.en: Taichi: "The fellows that Romance understand naught may go chow down tasteless Ramen at the House on the Sea."
comments: The ramen/romance thing sorta recurs, capitalized so maybe it's more obvious. Seems to be nothing but a bad pun, as even in Kanji 'romance' is pronounced Roman (and Rouman and Rooman). -GHS
records.assessment: The source tells anyone who cannot appreciate romance to eat bad ramen at a beach hut. “The fellows that Romance understand naught” is ungrammatical and “House on the Sea” mistranslates 海の家.
records.remedy: Use “Anyone who can’t appreciate romance can go eat lousy ramen at a beach hut.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "The fellows that Romance understand naught may go chow down tasteless Ramen at the House on the Sea."

records.jp: 「なによ」
records.en: Touko: "What's even that!"
comments: A very good question. This entire thing with Touko is just sorta off. Perhaps intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: “What’s even that!” is not idiomatic for her curt “What?”
records.remedy: Use “What?”

highlights.text: Touko: "What's even that!"

records.jp: 「なんだよー」
records.en: Taichi: "What's even now!"
records.assessment: “What’s even now!” is not idiomatic for his answering “What?”
records.remedy: Use “What?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What's even now!"

records.jp: おいおい、ナイト気取りかこいつ。
records.en: My my, putting on airs of a white knight this guy.
records.assessment: “Putting on airs of a white knight this guy” has broken word order and does not form a sentence.
records.remedy: Use “Oh, is this guy playing the white knight now?”

highlights.text: My my, putting on airs of a white knight this guy.

records.jp: 監視レベルは３になった。４になったら寝取りハザードだぞ。
records.en: Surveillance level rises to 3. If it gets to 4, we have a Netori Hazard for sure.
comments: It never does, at least explicitly. 3+4 mentioned =7. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration states that the surveillance level became three. “Rises” unnecessarily shifts to present tense.
records.remedy: Use “His surveillance level rose to three.”

highlights.text: Surveillance level rises to 3. If it gets to 4, we have a Netori Hazard for sure.

records.jp: 友貴の海パンに手をかける。
records.en: I grab on to Tomoki's slips.
comments: TL Note: literally "Sea Bread" (kai pan). Actually trunks, but see below. -GHS
records.assessment: 海パン means swim trunks. “Slips” refers to undergarments or mistakes and obscures what he grabs.
records.remedy: Use “I grabbed Tomoki’s swim trunks.”

highlights.text: I grab on to Tomoki's slips.

records.jp: 最終進化過程をすでに迎えブロントサウルスにも似た迫力を兼ね備えているその器官が、いたいけな少女の眼前にずるむけにされた（二重に）。
records.en: This organ that possesses an impact and a strength similar to that of a brontosaurus that has already welcomed the final stage of its evolution is presented to the eyes of this innocent girl via the slips (both meanings).
comments: Sort of funny I guess, but the sentence itself is borderline nonsensical. 'zuru' means a cheat, but also the SFX of slipping down, see above. Now it's slip as in swimming trunks and slip as SFX, given the 'cheat' is Taichi's anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: The source’s parenthetical signals a double exposure or double meaning in ずるむけ. “Via the slips (both meanings)” invents an English “slips” mechanism that does not express the Japanese action or pun.
records.remedy: Describe the organ being laid fully bare and handle the parenthetical without an invented “slips” gloss.

highlights.text: This organ that possesses an impact and a strength similar to that of a brontosaurus that has already welcomed the final stage of its evolution is presented to the eyes of this innocent girl via the slips (both meanings).

records.jp: 父親を知らない清純派少女は、ゆっくりと、顔色ひとつ変えず、悲鳴さえあげず……気を失って倒れた。
records.en: This girl so pure who's never known her father, gently, as her complexion changes color not, as she emits a loud scream not... parts with consciousness and falls down.
comments: First and only time we hear Yusa doesn't have a father. Uhm, maybe given her mother it shouldn't be too odd? BTW, Tanaka either has no father, or his father was a non-entity compared to his mother. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the girl faints slowly without changing expression or even screaming. “As her complexion changes color not” and “emits a loud scream not” are distorted negative calques.
records.remedy: Use natural parallel negatives: “without a change in expression, without even a scream.”

highlights.text: This girl so pure who's never known her father, gently, as her complexion changes color not, as she emits a loud scream not... parts with consciousness and falls down.

records.jp: 口うるさいくせに軟弱者である。
records.en: That damn nitpicker got her own weaknesses.
comments: See Youko. But it's odd, isn't it? See CCD2002. The reason is that she's just a hypocrite. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls Touko a coward despite how loudly she nags. “Got her own weaknesses” generalizes that specific contradiction into unspecified flaws.
records.remedy: Use “For all her nagging, she’s a coward.”

highlights.text: That damn nitpicker got her own weaknesses.

records.jp: 気絶した遊紗ちゃんは、宮澄先輩が介抱した。
records.en: Miyasumi-senpai is looking after poor fainted Yusa-chan.
records.assessment: The source says Miyasumi-senpai looked after the unconscious Yusa. The English shifts to present progressive and adds the evaluative “poor.”
records.remedy: Use “Miyasumi-senpai looked after the unconscious Yusa-chan.”

highlights.text: Miyasumi-senpai is looking after poor fainted Yusa-chan.

records.jp: 終われ終われ。
records.en: Do be finished, do be!
records.assessment: The narrator spitefully echoes “Be finished, be finished” at Tomoki. “Do be finished, do be” sounds like a polite request and loses the blunt repetition.
records.remedy: Use “Good. Be finished. Be finished.”

highlights.text: Do be finished, do be!

records.jp: 「落ち込むなよ、卒業まで俺たちはチェリーボーイズでいるって誓いを忘れたか」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't toss yourself down! Did you forget the vow we've made to remain Cherry BoyZ until graduation?"
comments: Going a little literal to recall CCA0016 more. The Z in BoyZ is necessar'ly always capitalized, this is a grammaticanal rule as iron as the prularlization of 千配, check the dictSee CCD0002 -GHS
records.assessment: 落ち込むな means “Don’t get depressed,” not “Don’t toss yourself down.” “Cherry BoyZ” also adds decorative spelling absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t get depressed. Have you forgotten our vow to stay virgins until graduation?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't toss yourself down! Did you forget the vow we've made to remain Cherry BoyZ until graduation?"

records.jp: 「つきあおう」
records.en: Taichi: "I'll go with."
records.assessment: The source says he will accompany Tomoki. “I’ll go with” is missing its object in standard English.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll go with you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'll go with."

records.jp: 「俺はずっと気になっていたのだが」
records.en: Taichi: "That thing that was on my mind before."
records.assessment: The source introduces something he has been wondering about all along. “That thing that was on my mind before” turns it into an old, completed concern and does not ask or state it clearly.
records.remedy: Use “There’s something I’ve been wondering this whole time.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "That thing that was on my mind before."

records.jp: 「……うーむ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...ye-ep."
records.assessment: うーむ is a doubtful or contemplative “Hmm.” “Yep” turns hesitation into affirmative certainty.
records.remedy: Use “Hmm...”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...ye-ep."

records.jp: 「馬鹿な海水浴だなあ、これ」
records.en: Tomoki: "A dumb beach outing, wasn't this."
records.assessment: The speaker is summing up the outing that has just happened. “Wasn’t this” is awkwardly tagged and places the whole scene at an unnecessary distance.
records.remedy: Use “This was one stupid beach outing.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "A dumb beach outing, wasn't this."

records.jp: 言うと、友貴は嘆息しつつも、首肯を返してきた。
records.en: To my words, Tomoki gave a sigh while still returning his agreement.
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki sighed but nodded back. “Returning his agreement” is an abstract and unidiomatic substitute for the visible nod.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki sighed, but nodded.”

highlights.text: To my words, Tomoki gave a sigh while still returning his agreement.

records.jp: 楽しい海水浴はこれでおしまい。
records.en: Our fun beach outing has with this concluded.
records.assessment: “Has with this concluded” is an unnatural literal construction.
records.remedy: Use “And with that, our fun beach outing was over.”

highlights.text: Our fun beach outing has with this concluded.

records.jp: 美希の傷は、ほんの少しだけ跡が残りそうだった。
records.en: As for Miki's cut, it only left behind a very small scar.
records.assessment: The source says the wound looked likely to leave only a faint scar. “It only left” presents the future possibility as an already completed certainty.
records.remedy: Use “Miki’s wound looked as though it would leave only a faint scar.”

highlights.text: As for Miki's cut, it only left behind a very small scar.

records.jp: それでも帰り道、本人は晴れ晴れとした顔をしていた。
records.en: Nevertheless, on the way back, said Miki had the most bright and cheerful face on her,
records.assessment: “Said Miki had the most bright ... face on her” is unidiomatic and uses the wrong superlative form.
records.remedy: Use “Even so, Miki wore a bright, cheerful expression on the way home.”

highlights.text: Nevertheless, on the way back, said Miki had the most bright and cheerful face on her,

records.jp: 「宮澄せんぱい以外には言わないですよねー？」
records.en: Miki: "He doesn't say that about anyone but you, Miyasumi-senpai, do you know?"
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki directs remarks like that only to Miyasumi-senpai. “Doesn’t say that about anyone but you” changes the remarks from speech addressed to her into claims about her.
records.remedy: Use “He only talks like that to you, Miyasumi-senpai.”

highlights.text: Miki: "He doesn't say that about anyone but you, Miyasumi-senpai, do you know?"

records.jp: 顔を見合わせてくすくす笑う。
records.en: They exchange glances and laugh in a giggle.
records.assessment: “Laugh in a giggle” is redundant and unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “They exchanged glances and giggled.”

highlights.text: They exchange glances and laugh in a giggle.

records.jp: 海水浴……か。
records.en: A beach outing... then.
records.assessment: The source’s reflective “A beach outing... huh” contains no “then.” The added transition implies a conclusion not present.
records.remedy: Use “A beach outing... huh.”

highlights.text: A beach outing... then.

records.jp: 思い出は、心を豊かにしてくれる。
records.en: Memories become the abundance of the heart.
comments: 豊 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says memories enrich the heart. “Become the abundance of the heart” is an unnatural nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use “Memories enrich the heart.”

highlights.text: Memories become the abundance of the heart.

records.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
records.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
comments: "Stomach it" heee heee me so crubler- clevsder- cruller. Mmmh hungry nau. What were we talking about again? -GHS
records.assessment: The source allows that there may be things she dislikes. “Can’t really stomach it” intensifies this into strong disgust.
records.remedy: Use “There may be things you don’t like, but why not try coming to club tomorrow?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"

records.jp: 困惑と戸惑いを貼りつけて、彼女は伏していた顔をあげた。
records.en: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.
comments: From the desk. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she lifts her downturned face with confusion and bewilderment written across it. “Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment” combines the emotions with each other, while “prostrate head” wrongly suggests full bodily prostration.
records.remedy: Use “Confusion and bewilderment on her face, she looked up.”

highlights.text: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.

records.jp: 憔悴したその面差しが、緋色に色づけされてどこか悲壮な印象を与えた。
records.en: Her emaciated features turned a bright scarlet, and left me with an impression in some respects tragic.
records.assessment: 憔悴 describes a haggard or exhausted look, not physical emaciation. The English also awkwardly says the features themselves “left” an impression.
records.remedy: Use “Her haggard features flushed scarlet, giving her a strangely tragic look.”

highlights.text: Her emaciated features turned a bright scarlet, and left me with an impression in some respects tragic.

records.jp: アンテナと土台の鉄塔を見あげる。
records.en: I look up at the steel tower that makes up the infrastructure of the antenna.
records.assessment: The source says he looks up at the antenna and the steel tower supporting its base. “Infrastructure of the antenna” abstracts the physical support and does not identify the base.
records.remedy: Use “I looked up at the antenna and the steel tower supporting its base.”

highlights.text: I look up at the steel tower that makes up the infrastructure of the antenna.

records.jp: 確かにこれは……一人で行う作業じゃないな。
records.en: This is... certainly not a job that can be performed alone, isn't it.
records.assessment: The sentence is a firm realization, but ends with the mismatched tag “isn’t it” after “This is.”
records.remedy: Use “This really wasn’t a job for one person.”

highlights.text: This is... certainly not a job that can be performed alone, isn't it.

records.jp: 波長と指向性の怪物みたいな姿になっていた。
records.en: Its shape became like that of a monster of wavelength and directionality.
comments: Oh c'mon, it still makes sense so far. -GHS
records.assessment: The antenna already had the monstrous form produced by its wavelength and directional properties. “Its shape became like” suggests an observed transformation and is an awkward calque.
records.remedy: Use “It looked like a monster of wavelength and directionality.”

highlights.text: Its shape became like that of a monster of wavelength and directionality.

records.jp: とはいえ、専門知識などないに等しい。
records.en: Or so I do, with my specific technical knowledge approximable to nonexistent.
records.assessment: The source says he has virtually no specialist knowledge. “My specific technical knowledge approximable to nonexistent” is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use “That said, I had practically no technical knowledge.”

highlights.text: Or so I do, with my specific technical knowledge approximable to nonexistent.

records.jp: 見里先輩にそれとなく探りを入れて聞きだしてある。
records.en: I have asked Misato-senpai using indirect investigative methods.
comments: Translation: "I sorta looked at what she was doing". -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he subtly sounded Misato-senpai out and extracted the necessary information. “Asked ... using indirect investigative methods” is needlessly clinical and omits that he obtained answers.
records.remedy: Use “I had casually sounded Misato-senpai out and gotten the details.”

highlights.text: I have asked Misato-senpai using indirect investigative methods.

records.jp: 黒須太一、文明の利器にはちと弱め。
records.en: Kurosu Taichi: slightly weakened by the conveniences of civilization.
records.assessment: The source says Kurosu Taichi is not very good with modern technology. “Slightly weakened by the conveniences of civilization” describes the technology harming him instead.
records.remedy: Use “Kurosu Taichi: not so good with modern technology.”

highlights.text: Kurosu Taichi: slightly weakened by the conveniences of civilization.

records.jp: 「いや、こうやって作業進めておけばぺけくんすごいです大感動です濡れちゃいますブチューッ……みたいな。よっ、友貴先生」
records.en: Taichi: "'Wow, the work has progressed this much, Peke-kun sugoi!, Prezy super deeply moved, Prezy sooo wet, kissy-kissy!'... or words to that effect. That is my goal. Hail, Tomoki-Sensei."
comments: Should be obvious from context what he means? As if I cared! Random Japanese is funny in its own way. 'buchuu' sounds close to 'buchou', so tweaked to fit both, because... -GHS
records.assessment: The source imagines a breathless compliment from Peke-kun and then greets Tomoki as his teacher. The English leaves “sugoi” untranslated, inserts the unexplained name “Prezy,” and adds a separate “That is my goal.”
records.remedy: Render the imagined praise and kiss joke without unbound names or untranslated Japanese.

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Wow, the work has progressed this much, Peke-kun sugoi!, Prezy super deeply moved, Prezy sooo wet, kissy-kissy!'... or words to that effect. That is my goal. Hail, Tomoki-Sensei."

records.jp: 「ブチューはないだろう」
records.en: Tomoki: "Prezy-kiss ain't happening though."
comments: Ick. See CCA0015B for the first time this pun came 'round. He's wrong, see CCC4019 for the payoff to this. -GHS
records.assessment: ブチュー is the exaggerated smooching sound from the prior fantasy. “Prezy-kiss” invents an unexplained name and changes the joke.
records.remedy: Use “The big smooch isn’t happening.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Prezy-kiss ain't happening though."

records.jp: 友貴は気怠げに地べたに座る。
records.en: Languidly Tomoki sits on the bare ground.
records.assessment: The setting is the rooftop surface, not bare earth. “Bare ground” suggests soil.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki sat down listlessly on the rooftop.”

highlights.text: Languidly Tomoki sits on the bare ground.

records.jp: 「お、マジ質問青春風味」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, it's Seriously Questioning Adolescent flavored!"
comments: The juice. -GHS
records.assessment: The source jokingly labels it a serious question with a flavor of youth. “Seriously Questioning Adolescent flavored” is grammatically malformed and changes the noun relationships.
records.remedy: Use “Whoa, a serious question with a youthful flavor.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, it's Seriously Questioning Adolescent flavored!"

records.jp: 「わけワカメだよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "That don't seaweed into sense."
comments: S/b Segue. -GHS
records.assessment: The English tries to preserve the わけワカメ seaweed pun, but “That don’t seaweed into sense” has broken agreement and an opaque verb.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical nonsense/seaweed pun.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That don't seaweed into sense."

records.jp: 「おいおい、おまえ自分でこんなモノ寄こしておいてはぐらかすなや」
records.en: Tomoki: "Come on, come on, you hand over this stuff my way by your own, don't go dodging it!"
records.assessment: Tomoki says Taichi sent him this item and should not evade the question now. “You hand over this stuff my way by your own” is ungrammatical and changes the completed sending into a present handoff.
records.remedy: Use “You sent me this yourself, so don’t dodge the question.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Come on, come on, you hand over this stuff my way by your own, don't go dodging it!"

records.jp: 「寄こしたというか、人間の手で投函したんだけどな」
records.en: Taichi: "Handed over, or should you say, posted by human hands don't you."
comments: Meaning he put them in their mailboxes manually. Whether the mailman delivers or not is actually irrelevant. See CCC3017. -GHS
records.assessment: Taichi quibbles that he did not hand it over but posted it by human hand. “Posted by human hands don’t you” is ungrammatical and loses the contrast.
records.remedy: Use “I didn’t hand it over—I mailed it, with human hands.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Handed over, or should you say, posted by human hands don't you."

records.jp: 「……どうして部活なん？」
records.en: Tomoki: "...why activities now?"
comments: This ends with a Kansai ~nan. -GHS
records.assessment: The source repeats the question “Why the club?” The English omits the club and replaces it with vague “activities now.”
records.remedy: Use “Why are you so set on the club?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...why activities now?"

records.jp: 「まーまー、待ちたまえよ。ロマンは一日にして成らずだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Waiiit, waiiit, gladden me with holding on! Romance wasn't built in a day!"
comments: ...and see CCA0023, CCA0027, CCC0026. He's trying to repeat the Beach even here. Rome will return, with its SEVEN hills. -GHS
records.assessment: 待ちたまえ means “wait.” “Gladden me with holding on” is an unrelated and unidiomatic command.
records.remedy: Use “Now, now, wait. Rome wasn’t built in a day.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Waiiit, waiiit, gladden me with holding on! Romance wasn't built in a day!"

records.jp: 「気を抜いてくれてありがとう太一くん」
records.en: Tomoki: "Thank you for making me waste some time, Taichi-kun."
records.assessment: Tomoki sarcastically thanks Taichi for letting him lower his guard after presenting the question as serious. “Making me waste some time” changes relief or lowered vigilance into lost time.
records.remedy: Use “Thanks for letting me drop my guard, Taichi-kun.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Thank you for making me waste some time, Taichi-kun."

records.jp: 「つまりあれだよ。ほら、目的があった方が生き甲斐が出るだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "I mean this thing here! Come on, isn't having an objective the way to gaining something to live for?"
comments: Antenna, club activities, AND Misato. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says having a goal gives a person something to live for. “The way to gaining something” uses the wrong construction.
records.remedy: Use “Having a goal gives you something to live for, right?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I mean this thing here! Come on, isn't having an objective the way to gaining something to live for?"

records.jp: 「けど生きる糧があるならそういうのもいいけどさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "But once you have food to live, that'd be good to have, though."
comments: Double but. Leaving it a tad ambiguous. After all, they don't exactly have much in the way of provisions. -GHS
records.assessment: 生きる糧 is figurative sustenance or a reason that sustains life. “Food to live” literalizes it and leaves the comparison unclear.
records.remedy: Use “If it gives you something to live on, I suppose that’s fine.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "But once you have food to live, that'd be good to have, though."

records.jp: 「青春群像グラフティー」
records.en: Taichi: "Vitelloni Graffitea."
comments: 青春群像 is a word meaning just that, but oddly enough, it's also the Japanese title of a seminal 1950s Fellini movie http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Vitelloni I suspect this may be a reference to that and not just the word because of the second part; that's a not-uncommon transliteration for Graffiti, which, regardless of movies, with the first word suggests American Graffiti. Which was set just a few years later than Vitelloni, though it's newer by two decades, so the two fit the tone. Plus the odd tweak at the end to make a flavor of tea, in both languages, there it is. Well, that, or I dunno at all. Oh, and it means what goes on in CCA0030, especially. -GHS
records.assessment: The source names a “youth ensemble graffiti” ideal, setting up the following sound-based tea joke. “Vitelloni” imports an unbound foreign title and replaces the ensemble-youth phrase.
records.remedy: Preserve the youth-ensemble-graffiti phrase while enabling the following sound joke.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Vitelloni Graffitea."

records.jp: 友貴は立ち上がり、アンテナの周囲をまわった。
records.en: Tomoki gets up, and walks around the perimeter of the antenna.
records.assessment: The past narration says Tomoki got up and walked around the antenna. The English shifts both actions into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki got up and walked around the antenna.”

highlights.text: Tomoki gets up, and walks around the perimeter of the antenna.

records.jp: 「それで……それだけで？」
records.en: Tomoki: "With this... just with this thing?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether that is all. “With this thing” adds an object and obscures the skeptical follow-up.
records.remedy: Use “And... that’s all?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "With this... just with this thing?"

records.jp: 「することがあるのはいいもんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, if you have something to do yourself that's fine too."
records.assessment: The source says it is good simply to have something to do. “Something to do yourself that’s fine too” introduces a contrast and a second-person subject absent from the statement.
records.remedy: Use “It’s good to have something to do.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if you have something to do yourself that's fine too."

records.jp: 「……あるじゃん。別に。物資探すとか、さ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...to do, hmmm. Not really. Looking for goods and materials, maybe."
records.assessment: Tomoki says there are other things to do, such as searching for supplies. “Not really” denies that existence and reverses his point.
records.remedy: Use “There are other things to do, though. Like searching for supplies.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...to do, hmmm. Not really. Looking for goods and materials, maybe."

records.jp: 「どうしてそんな楽しそうなんだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Why're you looking like you're having fun now."
records.assessment: The source asks why he looks so happy. “Now” adds a temporal contrast not stated.
records.remedy: Use “Why do you look like you’re having so much fun?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Why're you looking like you're having fun now."

records.jp: 友貴は腕で目元をぬぐった。
records.en: Tomoki wiped his undereye with his arm.
