records.assessment: 目元 is the area around his eyes. “His undereye” is an unnatural singular anatomical label.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki wiped his eyes with his arm.”

highlights.text: Tomoki wiped his undereye with his arm.

records.jp: 「とっとと頼む」
records.en: Taichi: "Then help you whelp!"
comments: not so much aggressive as sorta curt -GHS
records.assessment: とっとと頼む means “Hurry up; I’m counting on you” or “Get to it.” “Then help you whelp” has the wrong object, adds an insult, and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “Then hurry up and help me.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then help you whelp!"

records.jp: 「ばか、内心泣いてるっての。号泣だっての。泣き感動路線だっての」
records.en: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"
comments: Tsundere Mode! Girly, for starters, which needs much broader strokes in English. Baka works well for strawman tsundere (is that a term well it is now). That last one is "weeping emotional route", which is, well. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he is crying and sobbing inwardly and calls it a tearjerker route. The English inserts “baka” twice and leaves “utsuge” untranslated.
records.remedy: Use natural English for the internal sobbing and tearjerker-route joke without added Japanese insults.

highlights.text: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"

records.jp: 「男同士でジメジメしたって寒いだけだ、そーいうイベントは貴様のねーちゃんと起こすわい」
records.en: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"
comments: Curiously, this sentence ends with 'wai', which Secret Information (dictionary) reports as 'mainly male, signifying emotion'. I guess the point is the vaguely contradictory nature? -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he will trigger that sentimental event with Tomoki’s sister instead. “Go trigger that event” orders Tomoki to do it, reversing the agent.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll save that kind of event for your sister.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"

records.jp: 「さあ、そうと決まったらとっとと働け！　放送予定日は明日じゃい」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast is scheduled for tomorrow ya know."
comments: Half-mirroring above -GHS
records.assessment: そうと決まったら means “Now that that’s settled.” “If that’s your decision” makes the plan conditional and assigns the decision to Tomoki alone.
records.remedy: Use “Now that that’s settled, get to work.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast is scheduled for tomorrow ya know."

records.jp: 校舎に戻る足を止め、友貴。
records.en: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki stops on his way back into the school building. “A leg inside the school building” places part of him inside already and does not form a grammatical sentence.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki stopped on his way back into the school.”

highlights.text: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.

records.jp: 「いや、姉弟喧嘩なんてごくまっとうな人生じゃん。止めんよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."
records.assessment: The narrator says sibling quarrels are normal and that he will not stop theirs. “Don’tcha stop” tells Tomoki not to stop, changing the speaker’s policy into a command.
records.remedy: Use “Sibling quarrels are perfectly normal. I’m not going to interfere.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."

records.jp: 「要するに俺様を手伝えということだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."
records.assessment: “The greatness that is I” uses the wrong pronoun case and awkwardly expands 俺様.
records.remedy: Use “In short, you’re here to help the great me.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."

records.jp: 胸を張る。
records.en: Puff that chest with pride!
records.assessment: The source narrates that he puffs out his chest. “Puff that chest with pride!” changes narration into a command addressed to someone else.
records.remedy: Use “I puffed out my chest.”

highlights.text: Puff that chest with pride!

records.jp: 「……おまえ大物」
records.en: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."
records.assessment: 大物 means Tomoki is calling him an impressive piece of work or a big character. “What’re you a VIP” is ungrammatical and turns it into a question about status.
records.remedy: Use “You really are something.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."

records.jp: 「適応係数８０オーバーのオーバーロードですから」
records.en: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."
comments: 8 and 0, the Error and the loop. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he is an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient above eighty. The English makes him ruler “of all those” above eighty, adding a hierarchy and other people.
records.remedy: Use “I’m an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient over eighty.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."

records.jp: 「そういうの、嫌いじゃないから」
records.en: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."
comments: See CCA0007. -GHS
records.assessment: そういうの refers to that sort of attitude or behavior. “That of you” is ungrammatical and narrows it into a trait possessed by Taichi.
records.remedy: Use “I don’t dislike that sort of thing.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."

records.jp: さっと校舎内に消えた。逃げるように。
records.en: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.
records.assessment: The past narration says he quickly disappeared into the building. “Vanishes” shifts into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “He quickly disappeared into the school building, as if fleeing.”

highlights.text: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.

records.jp: そう言った友貴は、一瞬で人類の限界まで赤面しきっていた。
records.en: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.
comments: awww they do love each o--wait waIT WAAAAAIT -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki flushed to the human limit in an instant. The pluperfect “had instantly reddened up” is unnecessarily tangled and misaligned with the simple past sequence.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki instantly flushed as red as humanly possible.”

highlights.text: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.

records.jp: 楽しい部活ごっこ。
records.en: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.
records.assessment: “Fun pretend-a-club-activities” is a malformed mixture of singular modifier and plural noun.
records.remedy: Use “Our fun game of playing club.”

highlights.text: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.

records.jp: ありがとうと、思うため。
records.en: For the sake of thinking... thank you.
comments: See CCX0001. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives a compact motive: so that he can someday think “thank you.” “For the sake of thinking... thank you” is an unnatural calque.
records.remedy: Use “So that someday I can feel grateful.”

highlights.text: For the sake of thinking... thank you.

records.jp: 俺は戦っている。
records.en: I will be fighting.
records.assessment: The source is a present declaration: “I am fighting.” “I will be fighting” shifts it into an ongoing future.
records.remedy: Use “I am fighting.”

highlights.text: I will be fighting.

records.jp: 先輩は少し、ぼっとしていた。
records.en: Senpai was a bit... absent,
comments: It also literally reads "botlike". -GHS
records.assessment: ぼっとしていた means she seemed dazed or absent-minded. Ending the sentence on the adjective “absent” creates a fragment and can mean physically missing.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai seemed a little dazed.”

highlights.text: Senpai was a bit... absent,

records.jp: だから俺は告げた。
records.en: therefore, I proclaimed this:
records.assessment: 告げた simply means he told her. “Proclaimed” adds ceremonial force not present in the scene.
records.remedy: Use “So I told her.”

highlights.text: therefore, I proclaimed this:

records.jp: 「この放送局を、ずっと維持していかないと」
records.en: Taichi: "This Broadcast Channel must always be subject to improvement."
comments: Paraphrasis: "dinnae be depress'd ya wee lass, woak be not ovah!" -GHSuddenlyScottish
records.assessment: 維持していかないと means they must keep the broadcasting station running. “Must always be subject to improvement” replaces maintenance with improvement.
records.remedy: Use “We have to keep this broadcasting station running.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "This Broadcast Channel must always be subject to improvement."

records.jp: 「そうですね」
records.en: Misato: "It will."
records.assessment: そうですね agrees with his statement: “You’re right.” “It will” predicts the station’s future behavior and changes the subject.
records.remedy: Use “You’re right.”

highlights.text: Misato: "It will."

records.jp: 先輩は工具をまとめて脇に置き、アンテナを見あげた。
records.en: Senpai had gathered and set aside all equipment, so that we can look up at the antenna.
records.assessment: The source says Senpai gathered the tools, put them aside, and looked up at the antenna. The English invents a purpose “so that we can” and changes the sole observer into both of them.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai gathered the tools, set them aside, and looked up at the antenna.”

highlights.text: Senpai had gathered and set aside all equipment, so that we can look up at the antenna.

records.jp: ただ動いていたかっただけなのだから。
records.en: Because this has been only a want to move and nothing more.
records.assessment: The source says all he wanted was to keep moving or doing something. “This has been only a want to move” is ungrammatical and replaces the narrator with an abstract “this.”
records.remedy: Use “All I had wanted was to keep moving.”

highlights.text: Because this has been only a want to move and nothing more.

records.jp: 何かしていなければ、心の均衡が取れなかっただけ。
records.en: If one does not have something to do, the balance of the heart can just never be attained.
records.assessment: The source says he could not maintain his emotional balance unless he kept doing something. The English turns this into a universal present claim about attaining balance and changes maintenance into achievement.
records.remedy: Use “If I wasn’t doing something, I couldn’t keep my mind in balance.”

highlights.text: If one does not have something to do, the balance of the heart can just never be attained.

records.jp: 「ぺけくん、原稿はできましたか？」
records.en: Misato: "Peke-kun, did you manage with that script?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether the script is finished. “Did you manage with that script?” asks generally about coping with it instead.
records.remedy: Use “Peke-kun, is the script finished?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Peke-kun, did you manage with that script?"

records.jp: だって原稿、白紙なんだから。
records.en: After all, this script is sort of almost entirely blank.
records.assessment: The source says the script is blank. “Sort of almost entirely blank” adds hedging and implies some content exists.
records.remedy: Use “Because the script is completely blank.”

highlights.text: After all, this script is sort of almost entirely blank.

records.jp: 適当にでっちあげねば。
records.en: I'd have to come up with a suitable cover story otherwise.
records.assessment: 適当にでっちあげる means he must improvise or make something up on the spot. “Come up with a suitable cover story” invents concealment and a cover story.
records.remedy: Use “I’d have to improvise something.”

highlights.text: I'd have to come up with a suitable cover story otherwise.

records.jp: やってきた友貴が、先輩を一瞥する。
records.en: Having finally turned up, Tomoki glances towards Senpai.
records.assessment: The source says the arriving Tomoki glances at Senpai. “Finally” adds a delay or impatience not stated.
records.remedy: Use “Tomoki arrived and glanced at Senpai.”

highlights.text: Having finally turned up, Tomoki glances towards Senpai.

records.jp: 視線がそれる。
records.en: The gazes become divergent.
records.assessment: The source says their gazes turn away from each other. “Become divergent” is an abstract, unnatural description of eye movement.
records.remedy: Use “Their eyes slid away from each other.”

highlights.text: The gazes become divergent.

records.jp: 以前ほど刺々しくはない。
records.en: There isn't the same sharp thorniness of before.
records.assessment: The source says the atmosphere is not as prickly as before. “There isn’t the same sharp thorniness of before” is an unnatural nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use “It wasn’t as prickly as before.”

highlights.text: There isn't the same sharp thorniness of before.

records.jp: これから、どうしたって顔をあわせて生きていくことになるんだから。
records.en: Because after this, no matter what, they are going to have to be living face-to-face.
records.assessment: The source says they will inevitably have to keep seeing each other as they live on. “Be living face-to-face” suggests constant physical confrontation and is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “They would have to keep seeing each other, no matter what.”

highlights.text: Because after this, no matter what, they are going to have to be living face-to-face.

records.jp: 屋上でモニターするためだ。
records.en: so as to be monitoring from the rooftop.
comments: Not actual PC Monitors, as usual. -GHS
records.assessment: The purpose clause should say they carried the equipment up to monitor on the roof. “So as to be monitoring from” is a progressive calque and leaves the object implicit.
records.remedy: Use “We carried the equipment so we could monitor the broadcast from the rooftop.”

highlights.text: so as to be monitoring from the rooftop.

records.jp: 「ラバのヤツ、こんな時でも豪快にサボりやがる」
records.en: Taichi: "Damn that Sack, even at times like this did he have to be a stupidly cheerful slacker!"
records.assessment: The source says Sakuraba is brazenly skipping out even at a time like this. “Stupidly cheerful slacker” substitutes cheerfulness for brazen scale and treats it as a stable identity.
records.remedy: Use “That damn Sakuraba—skipping out in style even at a time like this.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Damn that Sack, even at times like this did he have to be a stupidly cheerful slacker!"

records.jp: 「……今にはじまったことだろうか」
records.en: Tomoki: "...didn't he just start?"
comments: Unclear, but it sounds like Tomoki actually knew he was there. -GHS
records.assessment: 今にはじまったことだろうか means “Is that anything new?” The English “didn’t he just start?” asks whether his behavior began moments ago, reversing the implication.
records.remedy: Use “As if that’s anything new.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...didn't he just start?"

records.jp: ぐっ
records.en: Tahm!
comments: CP CCA0019
records.assessment: ぐっ marks the firm thumbs-up gesture or its emphatic beat. “Tahm!” is an invented sound with no intelligible relation to the action.
records.remedy: Use a gesture cue such as “Thumbs up.”

highlights.text: Tahm!

records.jp: 冬子たちが来ていた。
records.en: Touko and the rest have come.
records.assessment: The past narration says Touko and the others had arrived. “Have come” shifts to present perfect.
records.remedy: Use “Touko and the others had arrived.”

highlights.text: Touko and the rest have come.

records.jp: 元気に両手をあげて、叫んだ。
records.en: She rose both hands energetically and shouted.
records.assessment: She raised both hands. “Rose both hands” uses the intransitive verb instead of “raised.”
records.remedy: Use “She raised both hands energetically and shouted.”

highlights.text: She rose both hands energetically and shouted.

records.jp: その大声に霧が、眉を寄せて肩をすくめる。
records.en: To that loud voice Kiri furrows her brows and shrugs.
records.assessment: The past narration says Kiri furrowed her brow and hunched or shrugged at the loud voice. The English shifts both actions into present.
records.remedy: Use “At the loud voice, Kiri furrowed her brow and hunched her shoulders.”

highlights.text: To that loud voice Kiri furrows her brows and shrugs.

records.jp: 「まー、ちょいと手を打ったです」
records.en: Taichi: "Welll, I made a deal or so."
records.assessment: 手を打った means he took measures or made arrangements. “Made a deal or so” introduces a bargain or counterparty not stated.
records.remedy: Use “I pulled a few strings.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Welll, I made a deal or so."

records.jp: 「スーパーディレクターですから、そこはうまく」
records.en: Taichi: "For I am the Supah Directah, and that is my success!"
comments: screw it *chug* -GHS
records.assessment: The source boasts that, as Super Director, he handled that part skillfully. “That is my success” is an unnatural result claim and omits the handling.
records.remedy: Use “I’m the Super Director. I handled it.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "For I am the Supah Directah, and that is my success!"

records.jp: 「全員集合、ですね」
records.en: Misato: "A whole club assembly, then."
records.assessment: 全員集合 means everyone is assembled. “A whole club assembly” adds the formal idea of a club meeting.
records.remedy: Use “Everyone’s here.”

highlights.text: Misato: "A whole club assembly, then."

records.jp: 「ＹＥＳ、ＢＯＳＳ」
records.en:
Taichi: "HAI, BUCHOU!"
/screw it *chug* -GHS
records.assessment: The source is already English: “YES, BOSS.” The translation replaces it with Japanese “HAI, BUCHOU” and appends an unbound translator aside.
records.remedy: Retain “YES, BOSS” and remove the translator aside.

highlights.text:
Taichi: "HAI, BUCHOU!"
/screw it *chug* -GHS

records.jp: 全員集合。
records.en: A whole club assembly.
records.assessment: 全員集合 says everyone is gathered. “A whole club assembly” again adds a formal assembly not present.
records.remedy: Use “Everyone together.”

highlights.text: A whole club assembly.

records.jp: いや、この結束をこれから維持していけばいいのだ！
records.en: No, improving on this union from here on out will be enough!
comments: Should recall line about 'broadcast channel'. -GHS
records.assessment: 維持 means maintain or preserve this unity. “Improving on this union” changes preservation into enhancement.
records.remedy: Use “No—we just have to keep this bond intact from now on!”

highlights.text: No, improving on this union from here on out will be enough!

records.jp: 今だけに。
records.en: because this is only the now,
records.assessment: The fragments lead to making a memory of the present moment. “Because this is only the now” is ungrammatical and adds an explicit causal clause not present in this unit.
records.remedy: Use “Just for now—”

highlights.text: because this is only the now,

records.jp: 思い出を。
records.en: I will make it into a memory.
records.assessment: The source’s fragment calls for a memory of this moment. “I will make it into a memory” supplies an explicit actor and singular object, flattening the deliberate fragment structure.
records.remedy: Use “a memory.”

highlights.text: I will make it into a memory.

records.jp: 片手をあげて皆に呼びかける。
records.en: Raising one hand, I call attention to everyone.
records.assessment: 皆に呼びかける means he calls out to everyone. “Call attention to everyone” means making everyone the object of attention.
records.remedy: Use “I raised one hand and called out to everyone.”

highlights.text: Raising one hand, I call attention to everyone.

records.jp: 「では放送部の再集結を祝って、これよりパン屋を再襲撃します」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, to celebrate the re-gathering of the Broadcast Club, we shall after this re-assault a bakery."
comments: re- in both cases. Hum, so they did this once? -GHS
records.assessment: The announcement says they will now raid the bakery again. “We shall after this re-assault” is an unnatural sequence and postpones the action beyond “now.”
records.remedy: Use “we will now raid the bakery again.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then, to celebrate the re-gathering of the Broadcast Club, we shall after this re-assault a bakery."

records.jp: 「嘘つくな」
records.en: Tomoki: "Don't toss lies around!"
records.assessment: “Toss lies around” is an unnatural expansion of the curt command “Don’t lie.”
records.remedy: Use “Don’t lie.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Don't toss lies around!"

records.jp: 「あなたも本気で検討しない」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't you give this serious thought as well."
records.assessment: The source tells her not to seriously consider the absurd plan too. “Don’t you give this serious thought as well” is awkwardly formed like either a question or admonition and obscures the “you too” reaction.
records.remedy: Use “Don’t you start seriously considering it too.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't you give this serious thought as well."

records.jp: 「でも揃うのは確かに久しぶりだね」
records.en: Tomoki: "But really, being all here, 's been a while."
records.assessment: “Being all here, ’s been a while” is missing a subject and uses unnatural word order.
records.remedy: Use “It really has been a while since we were all together.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "But really, being all here, 's been a while."

records.jp: 「それは貴様が部活に全然出ようとしない裏切り者だからだ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Because you're a traitorous bastard who never ever comes to club."
comments: ...and by Tomoki's signature 'traitor' he seems to be quoting. Interactions between Tomoki and Touko are more unique than rare. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls her a traitor who never tries to attend club. “Bastard” adds a gendered insult absent from the line.
records.remedy: Use “Because you’re a traitor who never even tries to come to club.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Because you're a traitorous bastard who never ever comes to club."

records.jp: 殺傷力の高い一本拳によるツッコミ（暴力）が時間差で入る。
records.en: Two High Bloodshed Power Single Fist Straight Man Ripostes (literal meaning) strike with a time lag.
comments: Tsukkomi does have a violent meaning beyond the more usual comedic one (plus at least a sexual one, like every other word in Japanese). -GHS
records.assessment: 一本拳 is a one-knuckle-fist strike, not a “Single Fist Straight Man” attack. The English also inserts “literal meaning” commentary and turns the delayed comic retorts into opaque capitalized jargon.
records.remedy: Describe the delayed one-knuckle-fist retorts without translator commentary.

highlights.text: Two High Bloodshed Power Single Fist Straight Man Ripostes (literal meaning) strike with a time lag.

records.jp: 無言で桜庭は沈んだ。
records.en: Sakuraba sinks wordlessly.
records.assessment: The past narration says Sakuraba sank wordlessly. “Sinks” shifts the action into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Sakuraba sank wordlessly.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba sinks wordlessly.

records.jp: ちなみに男三人衆の役割分担は、
records.en: By the way, the division of characterizational labor of this three-man team ended up becoming:
comments: See CCA0007 -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply introduces the division of roles among the three men. “Division of characterizational labor ... ended up becoming” is inflated and ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “For reference, the roles among the three men were divided as follows:”

highlights.text: By the way, the division of characterizational labor of this three-man team ended up becoming:

records.jp: 「彼女の心を解きほぐしたのは俺だ。愛の力なのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "I shall be the one to disentangle her heart. With the power of love!"
comments: As it'll start soon becoming obvious, this script is obviously composed of scenes more or less elegantly stitched together. Maybe it's just Taichi dreaming (<- fanwanking). -GHS
records.assessment: The source claims he was the one who already loosened or opened her heart. “I shall be the one” changes that completed boast into a future promise.
records.remedy: Use “I’m the one who opened her heart. It was the power of love.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I shall be the one to disentangle her heart. With the power of love!"

records.jp: 「……本気で嫌がってるよ？」
records.en: Tomoki: "...don't her voice seem to be seriously saying no?"
comments: See CCA0012 -GHS
records.assessment: The source observes that she is genuinely resisting or hates it. “Don’t her voice seem to be seriously saying no” is ungrammatical and narrows the evidence to her voice.
records.remedy: Use “She seriously hates this, you know?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...don't her voice seem to be seriously saying no?"

records.jp: 「でも体は正直なんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "But her body here has evidence!"
comments: PCP CCA0012
records.assessment: 体は正直 is the trope “her body is honest.” “Her body ... has evidence” changes honesty into unspecified proof.
records.remedy: Use “But her body is honest.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But her body here has evidence!"

records.jp: 「煮るわよ！」
records.en: Touko: "Go stand in a fire!"
comments: Lit. "go boil", but 煮 = 火 fire + 者 person ergo SCIENCE! -GHS
records.assessment: 煮るわよ means “I’ll boil/cook you!” “Go stand in a fire” changes the threatened action and its agent.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll boil you alive!”

highlights.text: Touko: "Go stand in a fire!"

records.jp: オクターブ高い悲鳴があがる。
records.en: She makes a high octave scream.
records.assessment: The source says a scream rises an octave higher. “A high octave scream” treats octave as an adjective and loses the comparison.
records.remedy: Use “Her scream shot up an octave.”

highlights.text: She makes a high octave scream.

records.jp: 美希は尻をもみしだく。
records.en: Miki thoroughly rubs her butt.
comments: Doesn't match picture either. -GHS
records.assessment: もみしだく means she thoroughly kneads or mauls Touko’s butt. “Rubs” weakens the force and hand action.
records.remedy: Use “Miki kneaded her butt vigorously.”

highlights.text: Miki thoroughly rubs her butt.

records.jp: 「や、やめてよ山辺！」
records.en: Touko: "You-, not you too Yamanobe!"
comments: Too many Ys. -GHS
records.assessment: The source directly orders Yamanobe to stop. “Not you too” changes the command into surprise at her participation.
records.remedy: Use “S-stop it, Yamanobe!”

highlights.text: Touko: "You-, not you too Yamanobe!"

records.jp: 「セクハラ集団だな」
records.en: Tomoki: "Mass sexual harassment innit."
records.assessment: セクハラ集団 calls them a sexual-harassment gang or group. “Mass sexual harassment” describes the scale of acts rather than identifying the group.
records.remedy: Use “What a sexual-harassment gang.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Mass sexual harassment innit."

records.jp: 「民事不介入だぜ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Neutrality in civilian affairs, ma'am."
comments: Official Japanese police policy. Unsure if there's an official translation of the term. -GHS
records.assessment: The line parodies the police doctrine of nonintervention in civil disputes. “Neutrality in civilian affairs” changes nonintervention into neutrality and loses the police phrasing.
records.remedy: Use “Police don’t intervene in civil disputes.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Neutrality in civilian affairs, ma'am."

records.jp: 「桐原さん、体調の方はもういいんですか？」
records.en: Misato: "Kirihara-san, have your physical conditions improved now?"
comments: Likely asking about how she had been fainting. This flows with the scene sooo well, doesn't it. -GHS
records.assessment: “Have your physical conditions improved” unnaturally pluralizes her overall health.
records.remedy: Use “Kirihara-san, are you feeling better now?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Kirihara-san, have your physical conditions improved now?"

records.jp: 「でもその子たち本能で生きてるのでどうにもなりませんから」
records.en: Misato: "But those poor things are living on instinct, there is nothing we can do to change that."
records.assessment: The source calls them “those kids” living by instinct. “Those poor things” adds sympathy not present in the dry joke.
records.remedy: Use “But those kids live entirely by instinct, so there’s nothing we can do.”

highlights.text: Misato: "But those poor things are living on instinct, there is nothing we can do to change that."

records.jp: 慌てて離れる。
records.en: Confused, we release her.
comments: See CCC0009B. Miki's totally only stopping because Taichi does. -GHS
records.assessment: 慌てて means they hurriedly or in alarm let her go. “Confused” substitutes lack of understanding for sudden panic.
records.remedy: Use “We hurriedly let her go.”

highlights.text: Confused, we release her.

records.jp: 「てんそ（天然素材）なんだって」
records.en: Tomoki: "Natural Raw (Natural airhead as Raw materials) innhe."
comments: http://ts.revinx.net/project/dic/crossc.htm confirms that TenSo is a portmanteu of Tennen Sozai, Natural Materials (but the 'natural' also means 'airhead', used around Sakuraba back in CCA0002 for example). Not sure why there isn't a * interjection, maybe because, like everything Tomoki, it's sort of obvious and lame. -GHS
records.assessment: The source explains the clipped pun てんそ as 天然素材, “natural material,” while also invoking an airhead. “Natural Raw ... as Raw materials” is ungrammatical and fails to preserve either phrase cleanly.
records.remedy: Use a readable abbreviation joke linking “natural airhead” and “natural material.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Natural Raw (Natural airhead as Raw materials) innhe."

records.jp: 平手で背中を叩かれた。
records.en: I was smacked in the back with the flat of a hand.
records.assessment: “Smacked in the back” uses the wrong preposition for a blow landing on his back.
records.remedy: Use “I was smacked on the back with an open palm.”

highlights.text: I was smacked in the back with the flat of a hand.

records.jp: 鞭みたいな痛さだった。
records.en: It hurt like it was a whip.
comments: It's... too late, yeah. But see CCA0002. -GHS
records.assessment: The source compares the pain to a whip. “It hurt like it was a whip” suggests the prior slap itself might literally be one.
records.remedy: Use “The pain was like a whip.”

highlights.text: It hurt like it was a whip.

records.jp: 霧がそっぽを向いて、ため息をついた。
records.en: Kiri disdainfully turned away and exhaled a sigh.
records.assessment: The source says Kiri turned away and sighed. “Disdainfully” adds an explicit attitude not stated in the action.
records.remedy: Use “Kiri looked away and sighed.”

highlights.text: Kiri disdainfully turned away and exhaled a sigh.

records.jp: 顎をつかんで、強引に飴を押し込む。指ごと。
records.en: Grabbing her chin, I cram the candy down her throat. Fingers and all.
records.assessment: The source says he forces the candy into her mouth, fingers and all. “Down her throat” intensifies the depth and danger beyond the stated mouth.
records.remedy: Use “I grabbed her chin and forced the candy into her mouth, fingers and all.”

highlights.text: Grabbing her chin, I cram the candy down her throat. Fingers and all.

records.jp: 「ママの味をくらうがよい」
records.en: Taichi: "Have a taste, it's like your mommy used to make!"
comments: Pseudo-recurring. Made it into some kind of ad slogan, I think it's intended (if it's not a parody of one that I can't source). Literal is "you should eat mother's flavor", but written sorta bookishly/old-fashioned. Actually a lot creepier considering the 'mom' is Youko. -GHS
records.assessment: ママの味 is the candy slogan “the taste of mama.” “Like your mommy used to make” converts it into homemade food and adds her personal childhood.
records.remedy: Use “Taste the flavor of mama.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Have a taste, it's like your mommy used to make!"

records.jp: 逃げようとするが、顎をつかんで離さない。
records.en: She wants to escape, but I catch her chin tight and don't let her gain distance.
records.assessment: The source says she tries to escape while he keeps hold of her chin. “Wants to escape” weakens the attempt, and “gain distance” is an unnatural substitute for his not letting go.
records.remedy: Use “She tried to escape, but I held her chin and wouldn’t let go.”

highlights.text: She wants to escape, but I catch her chin tight and don't let her gain distance.

records.jp: 「ひとーつ、ふたーつ……さあて、この可愛らしい穴にいくつ入るかな～？」
records.en: Taichi: "And ooone, and twooo... weeell, how many will this adorable hole be able to take, nooo～ one knows!"
records.assessment: The source asks how many pieces will fit. “No one knows” adds a teasing conclusion absent from the question.
records.remedy: Use “Now, how many will fit in this cute little hole?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "And ooone, and twooo... weeell, how many will this adorable hole be able to take, nooo～ one knows!"

records.jp: 「イヤだったら、指ごと噛みきってもいいんだぞ？」
records.en: Taichi: "If you disliked this, you could just bite the fingers you know?"
comments: See CCE0001. Indeed, when it comes to food, her body has evidence. This is why I believe CCA0012 was intended to be about force-feeding, not rape. It's gangrape used as allegory for eating food instead of letting oneself die, not viceversa. This thing is just so classy. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she may bite them off, his fingers along with the candy. “Bite the fingers” omits the severing result and also needs an object marker.
records.remedy: Use “If you hate it, you can bite them off—my fingers and all.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "If you disliked this, you could just bite the fingers you know?"

records.jp: が、口内をかきまわし、舌を絡め取って引っ張ると、ぎゅっとまぶたを閉じた。
records.en: but, as I churn her oral cavity, entwining and pulling on tongue, her eyelids shut tightly.
records.assessment: “Churn her oral cavity” is clinically jarring, and “pulling on tongue” omits the possessive article.
records.remedy: Use “I stirred inside her mouth, caught her tongue, and pulled until she squeezed her eyes shut.”

highlights.text: but, as I churn her oral cavity, entwining and pulling on tongue, her eyelids shut tightly.

records.jp: 根本まで押し込んで蹂躙を尽くす。
records.en: I push down to the root, utterly trampling it down.
comments: Totally a sex scene. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he pushes them in to their base and thoroughly ravages her mouth. “Trampling it down” leaves the object singular and unclear after “the root.”
records.remedy: Use “I shoved them in to the base and thoroughly ravaged her mouth.”

highlights.text: I push down to the root, utterly trampling it down.

records.jp: 「た、たいちぃ、そんなことしたらダメだよぅ、えっちすぎるよぅ（小児化）」
records.en: Tomoki: "Ta-, Taichin! That is a bad thing to do, it's way too dirty! (infantilized)"
comments: I added Taichin, but it's too good to resist. -GHS
records.assessment: The source’s childish pronunciation stretches “Taichi,” while “Taichin” changes the name by adding a consonant.
records.remedy: Use a childlike but recognizable “Taichiii.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Ta-, Taichin! That is a bad thing to do, it's way too dirty! (infantilized)"

records.jp: 「だ、だから……この人は危険だって……わたしは……」
records.en: Kiri: "Th-, that's why... this person is dangerous... I'm always..."
records.assessment: The source trails off after “I...” The English adds “always,” supplying a habitual claim not present in the unfinished line.
records.remedy: End on the same incomplete “I...”

highlights.text: Kiri: "Th-, that's why... this person is dangerous... I'm always..."

records.jp: 「俺的にはギブミーキャンディの一点、それだけだ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "To me it's part of a Give-Me-Candy, nothing more."
comments: Odd sentence this. Don't think he's rating him. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his sole concern is “give me candy.” “It’s part of a Give-Me-Candy” turns the demand into one component of an unspecified larger thing.
records.remedy: Use “All I care about is: give me candy.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "To me it's part of a Give-Me-Candy, nothing more."

records.jp: 謝るつもりがイジメになってる！？
records.en: My intent of apology turned into bullying?!
records.assessment: The source asks whether his attempt to apologize has turned into bullying. “My intent of apology” is an unnatural nominal phrase.
records.remedy: Use “Did my attempt to apologize turn into bullying?!”

highlights.text: My intent of apology turned into bullying?!

records.jp: 「まーとにかく、糖分を摂取して元気に生きてくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Weeell anyway, sugar intake means you can go living energetically."
records.assessment: The source commands Touko to consume some sugar and live energetically. “Sugar intake means you can” converts that imperative into a general causal claim.
records.remedy: Use “Anyway, get some sugar in you and live with energy.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Weeell anyway, sugar intake means you can go living energetically."

records.jp: しばしぼんやりとしていたが、我に返ってキッと俺を睨んだ。
records.en: She was disoriented for a while, but on return to her senses, she gives me an audibly sharp glare,
records.assessment: The source says she came to her senses and glared sharply. “Audibly sharp glare” adds an impossible sound quality, and “gives” shifts the action to present tense.
records.remedy: Use “She came to her senses and fixed me with a sharp glare.”

highlights.text: She was disoriented for a while, but on return to her senses, she gives me an audibly sharp glare,

records.jp: リスみたいに口をあめ玉でいっぱいにしながら。
records.en: while her mouth is filled to the brim with candy, like a squirrel.
comments: See CCB2010. -GHS
records.assessment: The narration is past tense, but “her mouth is filled” shifts the image into present.
records.remedy: Use “her mouth stuffed with candy like a squirrel’s.”

highlights.text: while her mouth is filled to the brim with candy, like a squirrel.

records.jp: 「言い返せないですね」
records.en: Miki: "No talk back there!"
comments: Both sides. -GHS
records.assessment: 言い返せないですね observes that there is no comeback to the accusation. “No talk back there!” turns it into an order not to answer.
records.remedy: Use “You can’t exactly argue with that.”

highlights.text: Miki: "No talk back there!"

records.jp: 「はいはい、レクリエーションはそこまで」
records.en: Misato: "Yes, yes, recreation extends no further than this!"
records.assessment: “Recreation extends no further than this” is a stiff literal boundary rather than the natural command that playtime is over.
records.remedy: Use “All right, that’s enough fooling around.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Yes, yes, recreation extends no further than this!"

records.jp: パンパンと手を叩く先輩。
records.en: Clap-clap claps Senpai.
records.assessment: “Clap-clap claps Senpai” redundantly combines an onomatopoeia with the verb and uses broken word order.
records.remedy: Use “Senpai clapped her hands twice.”

highlights.text: Clap-clap claps Senpai.

records.jp: スルーされた。
records.en: And her words just fall through.
records.assessment: The source simply says Touko was ignored. “Her words just fall through” invents a spatial metaphor, changes tense, and shifts the grammatical subject.
records.remedy: Use “They ignored her.”

highlights.text: And her words just fall through.

records.jp: 「せっかくですから、改めて一緒にどうですか？」
records.en: Misato: "We have gone to so much effort, how about letting us be together one more time?"
records.assessment: The source says that since they have this chance, the two should join the club activity again. “We have gone to so much effort” invents labor, while “be together one more time” sounds like a romantic reunion.
records.remedy: Use “Since we have the chance, why not join us again?”

highlights.text: Misato: "We have gone to so much effort, how about letting us be together one more time?"

records.jp: 二人は互いに、軽く目線を交差させた。
records.en: Two gazes that were made to loosely cross each other.
records.assessment: The source says the two lightly exchange glances. “Two gazes that were made to ... cross” is a passive fragment and removes the two women as agents.
records.remedy: Use “The two exchanged a brief glance.”

highlights.text: Two gazes that were made to loosely cross each other.

records.jp: 「わたしは」
records.en: Kiri: "I have..."
records.assessment: The source is the incomplete start “As for me...” “I have...” adds an auxiliary that presupposes a different completion.
records.remedy: Use “I...”

highlights.text: Kiri: "I have..."

records.jp: 「……美希が帰るまで同行するだけです」
records.en: Kiri: "...I will be accompanying Kiri until she leaves, no more."
records.assessment: Kiri says she will accompany Miki until Miki leaves. The English says she will accompany Kiri, making her accompany herself.
records.remedy: Use “I’m only staying with Miki until she leaves.”

highlights.text: Kiri: "...I will be accompanying Kiri until she leaves, no more."

records.jp: 空気が緩和する。片方だけ。
records.en: The mood relieved. One half of it only.
comments: See CCC3012A. Except there, the first level is [Y]ouko and the second Kiri. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the atmosphere relaxes, but only on one side. “The mood relieved” uses the wrong intransitive form and makes mood an agent.
records.remedy: Use “The tension eased—on one side, at least.”

highlights.text: The mood relieved. One half of it only.

records.jp: もう片方はと言うと、なお渋面のまま止まったまま。
records.en: This other half, however, is still stopped in a still grimace.
comments: Intentionally intentional -GHS
records.assessment: The other person remains frozen with a sour expression. “Still stopped in a still grimace” is redundant and unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “The other remained frozen, still scowling.”

highlights.text: This other half, however, is still stopped in a still grimace.

records.jp: あめ玉が詰められた口を手で押さえて、言葉を紡ぐ。
records.en: She holds down with a hand her mouth stuffed with candy and spins words.
records.assessment: The source says she covers her candy-stuffed mouth and pieces together words. “Holds down” suggests restraint, while “spins words” is an unnatural literal metaphor here.
records.remedy: Use “Covering her candy-stuffed mouth, she managed to form the words.”

highlights.text: She holds down with a hand her mouth stuffed with candy and spins words.

records.jp: 「止めないの？」
records.en: Tomoki: "Won't this stop?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether they are not going to stop the two fighters. “Won’t this stop?” makes the quarrel itself the subject and asks whether it will end autonomously.
records.remedy: Use “Aren’t you going to stop them?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Won't this stop?"

records.jp: 「部長が止めるしかないような気がします」
records.en: Kiri: "It feels like this will continue until the President stops it."
records.assessment: The source says it seems only the club president can stop them. “This will continue until” changes exclusive capability into a prediction of duration.
records.remedy: Use “I think only the president can stop them.”

highlights.text: Kiri: "It feels like this will continue until the President stops it."

records.jp: 「効果０とお見受けします」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Effect visible is 0."
comments: SYMBOLISM!!! for the situation doesn't progress ergo circle ergo time loop. Also it's people talking different languages see CCZAS ergo SYMBOLISM!!! again. -GHS
records.assessment: “Effect visible is 0” uses unnatural word order and treats お見受けします as literal visibility.
records.remedy: Use “I judge its effectiveness to be zero.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Effect visible is 0."

records.jp: 「だからこれからも仲良くケンカしようじゃないか」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore, can we have the these friendly fights from now on, how about?"
records.assessment: “Can we have the these friendly fights ... how about?” contains a duplicated article and two competing question frames.
records.remedy: Use “So let’s keep having friendly fights from now on.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore, can we have the these friendly fights from now on, how about?"

records.jp: 肯定と理解。
records.en: Asserted and understood.
records.assessment: The source gives two nouns—affirmation and understanding—describing what he reads in her response. “Asserted and understood” changes them into mismatched past-participle actions.
records.remedy: Use “Affirmation, and understanding.”

highlights.text: Asserted and understood.

records.jp: 「隊長、なんとかかんとか、失われた日常の再現に成功いたしました」
records.en: Taichi: "Commander, by one mean or by another, the restoration of that ordinary that was lost has met with success!"
records.assessment: The source reports successfully recreating their lost everyday life somehow. “The restoration of that ordinary ... has met with success” turns “everyday life” into an adjective used as a noun and is needlessly bureaucratic.
records.remedy: Use “Captain, somehow or other, we have successfully recreated our lost everyday life.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Commander, by one mean or by another, the restoration of that ordinary that was lost has met with success!"

records.jp: 釈然としない顔。
records.en: Not a fully satisfied face.
comments: See CCA0011A -GHS
records.assessment: 釈然としない means she looks unconvinced or unable to accept the explanation. “Not a fully satisfied face” weakens that stance and is not a natural noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use “She looked unconvinced.”

highlights.text: Not a fully satisfied face.

records.jp: 当然か。彼女たちにはそれぞれ、また異なる視点があるのだから。
records.en: Of course. Because those girls still have their own personal differences in viewpoints.
comments: I can't read this as anything but a creepy "because they are still individuals". Maybe intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: “Personal differences in viewpoints” is redundant and less direct than the source’s point that each woman has a different perspective.
records.remedy: Use “Of course. Each of them had her own perspective.”

highlights.text: Of course. Because those girls still have their own personal differences in viewpoints.

records.jp: 「ぺけくん、準備お願いしてもいいですか？」
records.en: Misato: "Peke-kun, do you mind if we leave things to you?"
comments: After mucous membranes and equipment, we have these mysterious unspecific 'preparations'. I can't seriously think of this as some sort of gag. This is also contradicted after the toilet scene. -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks Peke-kun to handle the preparations. “Leave things to you” generalizes the task beyond preparations.
records.remedy: Use “Peke-kun, could I ask you to handle the preparations?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Peke-kun, do you mind if we leave things to you?"

records.jp: 「その前に、トイレに行って小さい方を」
records.en: Taichi: "But before that, I have to go to the toilet for the small one."
records.assessment: 小さい方 is a euphemism meaning urination. “For the small one” is an opaque literal calque in English.
records.remedy: Use “Before that, I need to go take a leak.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But before that, I have to go to the toilet for the small one."

records.jp: あとでまたハラスメントしてやる。
records.en: I will help her to more harassment afterwards.
records.assessment: The narrator says he will harass her again later. “I will help her to more harassment” makes him an assistant and her the beneficiary or actor.
records.remedy: Use “I’ll harass her again later.”

highlights.text: I will help her to more harassment afterwards.

records.jp: 「あとでハラスメントして気をハラスとか思っているな？」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Were you just refreshed by a harass of thoughts about later harassment?"
comments: HARASUmento + ki wo HARASU. -GHS
records.assessment: The source puns on ハラスメント and 気を晴らす, accusing him of planning harassment to vent his feelings. “Refreshed by a harass of thoughts” is grammatically incoherent and loses both halves of the pun.
records.remedy: Use a readable harassment/venting pun or explain the wordplay without gibberish.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Were you just refreshed by a harass of thoughts about later harassment?"

records.jp: 「そ、そこまで思ってへんっ！」
records.en: Taichi: "T-, thinking that far's weird!"
records.assessment: The source denies having thought that far. “Thinking that far’s weird” calls the thought strange instead of denying it.
records.remedy: Use “I-I wasn’t thinking that far!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "T-, thinking that far's weird!"

records.jp: 腹いせに女子トイレを使ってやったわ。
records.en: So in retaliation I used the women's toilet, neh.
comments: Still trying to get Taichi to sound girly at times like this. Unfortunately, English is not collaborating even after repeatedly smacking it with a pipe wrench and sticking bamboo shoots under the fingernails. But if violence doesn't work then there's nothing that can! -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he used the women’s restroom in retaliation. The sentence-final “neh” is added Japanese-flavored discourse not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use “Out of spite, I used the women’s restroom.”

highlights.text: So in retaliation I used the women's toilet, neh.

records.jp: 「ふふん」
records.en: Taichi: "Hoooh hoh hoh!"
comments: Noblewoman's laugh? Going with that. -GHS
records.assessment: ふふん is a smug little snort or hum. “Hoooh hoh hoh!” turns it into a prolonged aristocratic laugh.
records.remedy: Use “Hmph-heh.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hoooh hoh hoh!"

records.jp: 鏡に、彼女が映っていた。
records.en: In the mirror she was reflected.
comments: Possibly intended to be Touko on start. Instead it's Tou--, Youko. Close enough. -GHS
records.assessment: “In the mirror she was reflected” uses unnatural inversion and passive voice.
records.remedy: Use “She was there in the mirror.”

highlights.text: In the mirror she was reflected.

records.jp: 手が止まる。
records.en: Hands stop.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator’s hands stop. “Hands stop” omits the possessor and sounds like a general stage direction.
records.remedy: Use “My hands stopped.”

highlights.text: Hands stop.

records.jp: 「部活ごっこ、楽しい？」
records.en: Youko: "Pretend-a-club, having fun?"
records.assessment: “Pretend-a-club, having fun?” is a fragment with no explicit subject or finite verb.
records.remedy: Use “Having fun playing club?”

highlights.text: Youko: "Pretend-a-club, having fun?"

records.jp: 返答があるとは思ってなかったので、驚いた。
records.en: I did not think there would be any reply, which surprised me.
comments: Of course it would. It's just himself. Split personalities aren't supposed to answer. But is she one? -GHS
records.assessment: He is surprised because she replies despite his expectation of silence. “There would be any reply, which surprised me” can make the absence of a reply the surprising fact and weakens the causal sequence.
records.remedy: Use “I hadn’t expected her to answer, so the reply surprised me.”

highlights.text: I did not think there would be any reply, which surprised me.

records.jp: 「……部活ごっこじゃなくて部活だけど」
records.en: Taichi: "...but this isn't pretend-a-club, this is club."
records.assessment: “This is club” lacks an article or natural phrase for real club activity.
records.remedy: Use “It isn’t playing club. It is the real club.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...but this isn't pretend-a-club, this is club."

records.jp: 「たいそう意味があることだよ。俺のためにも、みんなのためにも」
records.en: Taichi: "There's practical meaning. For my sake, and for everyone's sake as well."
comments: Taisou is both 'exaggerated' and 'calisthenics'. Given CCA0020/CCB0018, I suspect the pun is intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: たいそう means there is great or considerable meaning in it. “Practical meaning” changes magnitude into utility.
records.remedy: Use “It means a great deal—to me, and to everyone.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's practical meaning. For my sake, and for everyone's sake as well."

records.jp: 「家でじっとしてられない性格なんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Who's even got a personality capable of staying still at home here!"
comments: Both of them, really. It's why True Solitude is unachievable by Taichi, and why what he sees of that in her is false. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he personally has a personality that cannot sit still at home. “Who’s even got a personality capable...” turns it into a rhetorical question about an unspecified person.
records.remedy: Use “I’m just not the type who can sit quietly at home.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Who's even got a personality capable of staying still at home here!"

records.jp: 「皮肉なんて……言ってない……」
records.en: Youko: "Sarcastically... I didn't mean it that way..."
records.assessment: Youko says she was not making a sarcastic remark. “Sarcastically... I didn’t mean it that way” labels her delivery sarcastic and changes denial of the utterance into denial of intent.
records.remedy: Use “I wasn’t... being sarcastic...”

highlights.text: Youko: "Sarcastically... I didn't mean it that way..."

records.jp: 「せっかくだし参加してく？」
records.en: Taichi: "You went to all that effort, you participating?"
records.assessment: The invitation asks whether she wants to join since she came all this way. “You participating?” is a verbless present-progressive fragment.
records.remedy: Use “Since you came all this way, want to join us?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You went to all that effort, you participating?"

records.jp: 「部活だよ。これから放送するんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "This is club! We're gonna broadcast right after this."
records.assessment: これから means they are about to broadcast now. “Right after this” adds an intervening event.
records.remedy: Use “It’s the club. We’re about to broadcast.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "This is club! We're gonna broadcast right after this."

records.jp: 「俺がお願い参加してってすがりついたら？」
records.en: Taichi: "What if I hugged you while begging you to participate?"
records.assessment: すがりつく means cling to her while begging. “Hugged you” substitutes an embrace and weakens the pleading dependence.
records.remedy: Use “What if I begged you to join while clinging to you?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "What if I hugged you while begging you to participate?"

records.jp: 彼女はスカートの中に手を入れた。
records.en: She puts her hands under her skirt.
records.assessment: The source says she put one hand under her skirt. The English shifts to present tense and pluralizes the hand.
records.remedy: Use “She slipped a hand under her skirt.”

highlights.text: She puts her hands under her skirt.

records.jp: 「あー、やっぱいーや」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I knew it, donnn't!"
comments: See below for specific type of frustration he's having here. -GHS
records.assessment: やっぱいーや means “Never mind after all.” “I knew it, don’t” incorrectly adds prior knowledge and does not form a natural retraction.
records.remedy: Use “Ah, never mind after all.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, I knew it, donnn't!"

records.jp: 彼女の動きが止まる。
records.en: She stops all motions.
records.assessment: The source says her movement stops. “All motions” intensifies this into total bodily stillness beyond the singular phrasing.
records.remedy: Use “She stopped moving.”

highlights.text: She stops all motions.

records.jp: 鬼畜ゲームの主人公ですか俺は。
records.en: What am I now, the protagonist of a platform hell game?
comments: 鬼畜ゲーム Kichiku geemu, lit. Brute Game. Sounds like it's a porn game, doesn't it? Instead, top representative is I Wanna Be The Guy and all games of that style. Given she's quick to obey his orders and he has to be quick to stop her, platform hell actually makes more sense than hardcore porn. ...annnd there goes another one of those sentences. -GHS
records.assessment: 鬼畜ゲーム is a cruel or sadistic adult game, whose protagonist mistreats characters. “Platform hell game” instead names an extremely difficult platformer genre and loses the moral joke.
records.remedy: Use “What am I, the protagonist of some sadistic game?”

highlights.text: What am I now, the protagonist of a platform hell game?

records.jp: 「じゃあ……遠くでいいから、見ていきなよ。君は人間嫌いなんだろうけどさ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well... keeping your distance is fine, just look in. You're a misanthrope after all, aren't you."
records.assessment: 見ていきな asks her to stay and watch, even from far away. “Just look in” sounds like a brief glance through an opening.
records.remedy: Use “You can keep your distance, but stay and watch.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well... keeping your distance is fine, just look in. You're a misanthrope after all, aren't you."

records.jp: 「嫌いじゃない……興味ないだけ」
records.en: Youko: "Not hate mine... just disinterest."
comments: Don't forget your etymologies now. hmmm that starts with the same letters as EThanol for some reason. I knew it! It's about aliens! -GHS
records.assessment: She says she does not hate people; she is merely uninterested. “Not hate mine... just disinterest” is ungrammatical and introduces an unexplained possessive.
records.remedy: Use “I don’t hate them... I’m just not interested.”

highlights.text: Youko: "Not hate mine... just disinterest."

records.jp: 淡々と言う。
records.en: So she says, dispassionate.
records.assessment: “So she says, dispassionate” uses an adjective where an adverb is required.
records.remedy: Use “she said dispassionately.”

highlights.text: So she says, dispassionate.

records.jp: 「でもせっかくのイベントなんだから、一緒に参加してってもいいだろう？」
records.en: Taichi: "But this has been an Event hard to organize, so how about we just participate together?"
comments: vs. her just staying afar and looking on? Maybe her previous assent was just sarcastic. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that since this is a special event, she could stay and participate with them. “Hard to organize” adds production difficulty, and “we ... participate” shifts the invitation’s subject from her to the group.
records.remedy: Use “But it’s a special event. You could stay and join us.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But this has been an Event hard to organize, so how about we just participate together?"

records.jp: 女子トイレに入ったって、よく気づいたな……。
records.en: I had gone into the girls' toilet, but how quick she noticed...
comments: As if she was always there with him. -GHS
records.assessment: The source marvels that she noticed he had entered the women’s restroom. “How quick she noticed” uses the wrong adjective form and construction.
records.remedy: Use “She did well to notice I’d gone into the women’s restroom.”

highlights.text: I had gone into the girls' toilet, but how quick she noticed...

records.jp: さすがスーパーくの一。
records.en: What else from our Super Kunoichi.
records.assessment: “What else from our Super Kunoichi” is a fragment and does not express “As expected.”
records.remedy: Use “Just what I’d expect from a super kunoichi.”

highlights.text: What else from our Super Kunoichi.

records.jp: 「ところで女って字を分解して『くの一』って呼ぶってご存じでしたか？」
records.en: Taichi: "By the way, did you know that if you disassemble the kanji for Woman, you can get the 'ku', 'no', and 'ichi' to make kunoichi? They're hiragana, katakana and kanji respectively, tho."
comments: Curse, double curse, and triple curse the lack of kanji display. 女 = く+ノ+一. But also a point here is that it's written くの + 一, as the last one's kanji and is just like Taichi's name. -GHS
records.assessment: The source only mentions decomposing the character 女 into ku-no-ichi. The English appends an unbound technical explanation of three script systems.
records.remedy: Remove the added script-system explanation and retain the stated character-decomposition fact.

highlights.text: Taichi: "By the way, did you know that if you disassemble the kanji for Woman, you can get the 'ku', 'no', and 'ichi' to make kunoichi? They're hiragana, katakana and kanji respectively, tho."

records.jp: とすれ違いにトイレに入っていく。
records.en: Our path cross but don't meet as she goes inside the toilet.
comments: See CCD5001, same term furry'd after the "for the sake of..." bit. IOW: SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
records.assessment: The source says they pass each other as she enters the restroom. “Our path cross but don’t meet” is ungrammatical and contradicts the encounter inherent in passing.
records.remedy: Use “She passed me and went into the restroom.”

highlights.text: Our path cross but don't meet as she goes inside the toilet.

records.jp: 「あの……女子トイレに入ってたことはどうかナイショに」
records.en: Taichi: "Uhm... me going in the girls' toilet you keep a secret, OK?"
records.assessment: “Me going in ... you keep a secret” has broken word order and lacks a request marker.
records.remedy: Use “Please keep it secret that I went into the women’s restroom.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uhm... me going in the girls' toilet you keep a secret, OK?"

records.jp: 「そーですねー、どーしようかなー」
records.en: Miki: "Wooon't I nooow, whaaat should I dooo..."
records.assessment: Her teasing “Hmm, what should I do?” weighs whether to keep the secret. “Won’t I now” is an opaque negative construction.
records.remedy: Use “Hmm, what should I do?”

highlights.text: Miki: "Wooon't I nooow, whaaat should I dooo..."

records.jp: 我が校屈指の二大冷血女じゃないですか。
records.en: They are the two most pre-emenint cold-blooded females at this school of ours, are they not?
comments: Only in their tsun part I guess. -GHS
records.assessment: “Pre-emenint” is misspelled, and the heavy tag construction is needlessly awkward.
records.remedy: Use “They’re two of the coldest women at our school.”

highlights.text: They are the two most pre-emenint cold-blooded females at this school of ours, are they not?

records.jp: 「それじゃあこの口はペペラペラと開いてしまいそうですなぁ～」
records.en: Miki: "Well then, seems this mouth here will be opening and go all Pepe le Pew with wooo～rds!"
comments: Seems to be just a cutesy variation on perapera (fluent, talkative), but it sounds like Pepe le Pew was mixed in to that so here's another unsound effect for the pile. -GHS
records.assessment: ペラペラ refers to her mouth flapping and spilling words. “Go all Pepe le Pew” substitutes an unrelated cartoon name and destroys the chatter pun.
records.remedy: Use a readable loose-lips or flapping-mouth joke.

highlights.text: Miki: "Well then, seems this mouth here will be opening and go all Pepe le Pew with wooo～rds!"

records.jp: 「はーい、三流コントはそのくらいにして、とっとと始めましょうね」
records.en: Misato: "Okaaay, that third rate sketch ends there, so let us begin on the double!"
comments: Considering a consistent translation of 'とっとと' (see CCA0029) ... ... ... reconsidered. -GHS
records.assessment: とっとと means promptly. “On the double” is possible but “that third rate sketch ends there” uses unnatural tense for the command to stop.
records.remedy: Use “All right, enough of the third-rate skit. Let’s get started.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Okaaay, that third rate sketch ends there, so let us begin on the double!"

records.jp: 男衆はのたくたと動き出す。
records.en: Lethargically the male troupe begins to move.
records.assessment: 男衆 simply means the men. “Male troupe” adds a theatrical group identity not present.
records.remedy: Use “The men sluggishly started moving.”

highlights.text: Lethargically the male troupe begins to move.

records.jp: 孤立している彼女は、美希がいないと所在なげだ。
records.en: Solitary as she is, in Miki's absence she seems bored.
records.assessment: 所在なげ means she looks ill at ease or does not know where to place herself without Miki. “Bored” substitutes lack of stimulation.
records.remedy: Use “Isolated as she was, without Miki she looked lost.”

highlights.text: Solitary as she is, in Miki's absence she seems bored.

records.jp: ごく自然に、霧のそばに立つ。
records.en: Extremely naturally she goes to stand next to Kiri.
records.assessment: “Extremely naturally she goes to stand” is an awkward adverb stack and shifts the action into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Without a second thought, she stood beside Kiri.”

highlights.text: Extremely naturally she goes to stand next to Kiri.

records.jp: 霧の方が保護者のように見えて、その実、美希が中心になっている。
records.en: Kiri looks and acts very much like a guardian, and that is fact, Miki is important to her.
records.assessment: The source says Kiri appears to be the guardian, but Miki is actually the center of their relationship. The English merely says Miki is important to Kiri, omitting the reversal of dependence and centrality.
records.remedy: Use “Kiri looked like the guardian, but in truth Miki was the center of the pair.”

highlights.text: Kiri looks and acts very much like a guardian, and that is fact, Miki is important to her.

records.jp: その支配性を感じさせる構図に。
records.en: That composition, that felt of dominance,
records.assessment: “That composition, that felt of dominance” is an ungrammatical fragment and uses “felt” as a noun.
records.remedy: Use “That arrangement suggested a kind of dominance.”

highlights.text: That composition, that felt of dominance,

records.jp: 心がざわついた。
records.en: was in my heart as a morass of chatter.
comments: These three are pretty ambiguous, I suppose they only explain that Miki's in control here. -GHS
records.assessment: 心がざわついた means his heart stirred uneasily. “Was in my heart as a morass of chatter” literalizes ざわつく into audible chatter and creates a different metaphor.
records.remedy: Use “It made my heart stir uneasily.”

highlights.text: was in my heart as a morass of chatter.

records.jp: 原稿も初期稿しかないし。
records.en: This script is no more than an introduction.
comments: How long before the rest was this first week written? -GHS
records.assessment: 初期稿 means an initial draft. “Introduction” means an opening section and changes the state of the script.
records.remedy: Use “And all I had was the initial draft.”

highlights.text: This script is no more than an introduction.

records.jp: そういえば、曜子ちゃんの姿が見えない。
records.en: Speaking of not-quite-things, Youko-chan's profile is nowhere to be seen.
records.assessment: そういえば means “Come to think of it.” “Speaking of not-quite-things” is unrelated, while “profile” means a view or account rather than her physical presence.
records.remedy: Use “Come to think of it, Youko-chan was nowhere to be seen.”

highlights.text: Speaking of not-quite-things, Youko-chan's profile is nowhere to be seen.

records.jp: 参加すると言ったからには、どこかにいるはずだ。
records.en: As she said she would join in, I expect her to be somewhere.
records.assessment: The source concludes she must be somewhere because she promised to join. “I expect” weakens this necessity into a personal prediction.
records.remedy: Use “Since she said she’d join, she had to be somewhere nearby.”

highlights.text: As she said she would join in, I expect her to be somewhere.

records.jp: ただその先に、かすかな違和感がある。
records.en: Just beyond that there's a vague sense of physical discomfort.
comments: This term means "a moral or physical disturbance at seeing something that mismatches". It will be used to describe Nanaka, as well as Youko and more, hinting that what's being seen may not be actually there. -GHS
records.assessment: 違和感 is a faint anomaly or sense that something is off. “Physical discomfort” relocates the feeling into the narrator’s body.
records.remedy: Use “But just beyond them, I sensed a faint anomaly.”

highlights.text: Just beyond that there's a vague sense of physical discomfort.

records.jp: 「いた」
records.en: Taichi: "There she was."
records.assessment: The immediate discovery is “There she is.” “There she was” unnecessarily distances it into the past.
records.remedy: Use “There she is.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "There she was."

records.jp: 案の定というか、給水塔の上に潜んでいた。
records.en: As I should've thought, that is to say, she was lurking on top of the water tower.
comments: Seems like ninjas like that spot. -GHS
records.assessment: “As I should’ve thought, that is to say” is a tangled calque of “as expected.”
records.remedy: Use “Sure enough, she was hiding atop the water tower.”

highlights.text: As I should've thought, that is to say, she was lurking on top of the water tower.

records.jp: だがわずかでも動があれば、俺にはわかった。
records.en: but if there is even just the smallest of movements, I can tell.
records.assessment: The source says he could detect even the slightest movement in that moment. “I can tell” shifts the capability into a general present.
records.remedy: Use “But if anything moved even slightly, I could tell.”

highlights.text: but if there is even just the smallest of movements, I can tell.

records.jp: 「ほんと興味ないんだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Really uninterested, innit."
records.assessment: “Really uninterested, innit” omits the person who lacks interest and uses a tag that does not agree with an unstated subject.
records.remedy: Use “You really aren’t interested, are you?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Really uninterested, innit."

records.jp: 「さー放送放送」
records.en: Taichi: "Sooo broadcast, to broadcast."
records.assessment: “Broadcast, to broadcast” does not naturally reproduce his call to get on with the broadcast.
records.remedy: Use “All right, time to broadcast.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sooo broadcast, to broadcast."

records.jp: 「恐怖地獄放送局」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Hell and Dismay Broadcast Relay."
comments: Doesn't seem to be a specific reference...? -GHS
records.assessment: 恐怖地獄放送局 is “Terror Hell Broadcasting Station.” “Hell and Dismay Broadcast Relay” changes terror to dismay and station to relay.
records.remedy: Use “Terror Hell Broadcasting Station.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Hell and Dismay Broadcast Relay."

records.jp: 「いたいぜ～」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Hurts, yes～."
records.assessment: The source simply says it hurts. “Yes” is an added affirmation with no prompt.
records.remedy: Use “It hurts...”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Hurts, yes～."

records.jp: 「じゃあ適当にバンバン言ってみるか」
records.en: Taichi: "Let's do like machine guns and just fire off some suitable ones."
comments: See CCA0015 -GHS
records.assessment: The source suggests rapidly blurting out random names. The machine-gun simile is not present and makes the wording more elaborate than the casual proposal.
records.remedy: Use “Then let’s just rattle off random ideas.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Let's do like machine guns and just fire off some suitable ones."

records.jp: 「放送倶楽部」
records.en: Tomoki: "Broadcast bu."
records.assessment: 放送倶楽部 means “Broadcasting Club.” “Broadcast bu” leaves the final Japanese morpheme untranslated and is not intelligible English.
records.remedy: Use “Broadcasting Club.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Broadcast bu."

records.jp: 「くるくるぱー放送局」
records.en: Miki: "Kenneth Broadcast Channel!"
comments: Kurukurupa originally a much worse word http://japan-cc.com/slang.htm http://oshiete.goo.ne.jp/qa/2664417.html Since it refers to insanity, that's probably the real reason why it's so chastised here. Replaced with something appropriate. -GHS
records.assessment: くるくるぱー is a childish “crazy/idiot” expression. “Kenneth” is an unrelated proper name and removes the joke’s direction.
records.remedy: Use a title such as “Loony Broadcasting Station.”

highlights.text: Miki: "Kenneth Broadcast Channel!"

records.jp: その場にいた全員が、事務的かつ義務的に美希をこづいた。
records.en: All members in the proximity of her location poked Miki in manners businesslike and clerical.
records.assessment: The source says everyone present poked Miki in a businesslike, obligatory manner. “In the proximity of her location” is redundant, and “manners businesslike and clerical” is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “Everyone present dutifully gave Miki a businesslike poke.”

highlights.text: All members in the proximity of her location poked Miki in manners businesslike and clerical.

records.jp: 「いたた……しどい……」
records.en: Miki: "OwChCh... meeniesh..."
comments: Intentional -GHS
records.assessment: しどい is a childish slurring of “cruel/awful.” “Meeniesh” changes the adjective into a plural noun and adds a different speech defect.
records.remedy: Use a childish “That’s sho mean...”

highlights.text: Miki: "OwChCh... meeniesh..."

records.jp: 「不謹慎禁止」
records.en: Misato: "Imprudences forbidden."
records.assessment: 不謹慎禁止 prohibits inappropriate or irreverent remarks. “Imprudences forbidden” is both unnatural and semantically about poor judgment rather than impropriety.
records.remedy: Use “No inappropriate jokes.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Imprudences forbidden."

records.jp: 「それがイチオシなのか……」
records.en: Tomoki: "That's getting a lot of votes ain't it..."
records.assessment: イチオシ asks whether that is his number-one recommendation. “Getting a lot of votes” turns one person’s favorite into group popularity.
records.remedy: Use “Is that your top pick?”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That's getting a lot of votes ain't it..."

records.jp: 「町娘を斬る」
records.en: Taichi: "Slays a girl raised in the town."
comments: All these are of course gender ambiguous, but it's obviously Youko. She's even literally referred as a Super Ninja in CCA0027 (but a Super Kunoichi above, because Tanaka's a bastard like that). -GHS
records.assessment: 町娘 is a stock “town maiden/commoner girl,” not specifically a girl who was raised in a town.
records.remedy: Use “He cuts down a town maiden.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Slays a girl raised in the town."

records.jp: 「少しは加工しなよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Give it some elaboration!"
comments: Could be to either. -GHS
records.assessment: 加工しなよ asks him to modify or work the idea at least a little. “Give it some elaboration” is an awkward noun phrase and narrows modification to adding detail.
records.remedy: Use “At least rework it a little.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Give it some elaboration!"

records.jp: 「マイナス方向から離れてくださーい」
records.en: Misato: "Distance yourselves from that negative direction pleeease."
comments: Probably both negativity and, uhm, 'weird stuff'. -GHS
records.assessment: “Distance yourselves from that negative direction” is a spatially literal and unnatural rendering of the request to move away from negative ideas.
records.remedy: Use “Please move away from all the negativity.”

highlights.text: Misato: "Distance yourselves from that negative direction pleeease."

records.jp: 「うーん」
records.en: Taichi: "Yeah!"
records.assessment: うーん is a thoughtful or doubtful “Hmm.” “Yeah!” changes hesitation into enthusiastic agreement.
records.remedy: Use “Hmm...”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yeah!"

records.jp: 美しい中段の正拳であった。
records.en: A beautiful Straight Punch to the Midsection it was.
records.assessment: “A beautiful Straight Punch to the Midsection it was” uses inverted word order and unnecessary title capitalization.
records.remedy: Use “It was a beautiful straight punch to the midsection.”

highlights.text: A beautiful Straight Punch to the Midsection it was.

records.jp: 「下品なのはいけませんのでありましょう？」
records.en: Misato: "Vulgarities are not to be, is that clear?"
records.assessment: “Vulgarities are not to be, is that clear?” is a stiff and incomplete prohibition.
records.remedy: Use “No vulgarity, understood?”

highlights.text: Misato: "Vulgarities are not to be, is that clear?"

records.jp: 「ギャルであるべきだ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Girls are a must have."
comments: Tough words from Mr. Yaoi here. -GHS
records.assessment: The source insists the DJ should be a gal, singular. “Girls are a must have” pluralizes the subject and changes the role requirement into general possession.
records.remedy: Use “It has to be a girl.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Girls are a must have."

records.jp: 「ふっ……相変わらず、手厳しい」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Hu! ...as always, firm of hand."
comments: The 'hu' laugh will return. -GHS
records.assessment: 手厳しい means harsh or severe. “Firm of hand” suggests physical firmness and is not the idiom used here.
records.remedy: Use “As harsh as ever.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Hu! ...as always, firm of hand."

records.jp: 「チヌって何だ？」
records.en: Taichi: "A porgy, what's that?"
comments: He doesn't know this. It's very interesting he wouldn't. -GHS
records.assessment: “A porgy, what’s that?” has unnatural apposition and word order.
records.remedy: Use “What’s a chinu?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "A porgy, what's that?"

records.jp: 「もきーっ、あの小娘ーっ」
records.en: Taichi: "MokYYYYY, that puss!!!"
records.assessment: 小娘 is “little brat/girl.” “Puss” is a sexualized English insult with different connotations and force.
records.remedy: Use “That little brat!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "MokYYYYY, that puss!!!"

records.jp: 「オラ、なんか疲れてきたぞ」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Me somewhat tired now."
comments: He's all but officially a chimpanzee anyway. -GHS
records.assessment: The source’s rustic first person can sound rough, but “Me somewhat tired now” is telegraphic to the point of broken English.
records.remedy: Use a readable rustic line such as “I’m gettin’ kinda tired.”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Me somewhat tired now."

records.jp: プチ人格破綻者たちの交流なんてこんなもんです。
records.en: This is but an intermingling of petite failures of character, after all.
records.assessment: プチ人格破綻者 calls them minor or pint-sized cases of personality breakdown. “Petite failures of character” turns psychological dysfunction into moral shortcomings and makes “petite” describe the people.
records.remedy: Use “That’s what interaction among a bunch of minor personality disasters looks like.”

highlights.text: This is but an intermingling of petite failures of character, after all.

records.jp: 「いちおう部員なんだし、何か言えこのスベタ」
records.en: Taichi: "As far as it goes you're a club member, aren't you, so say something you curtana!"
comments: Sword + bitch. Curt-ana is a valid alternate spelling of Cortana, which is good because Halo references here are a bit lacking. (Cortana is now a Halo reference FOREVER, by the way.) (also ana is hole fnarr^2) -GHS
records.assessment: スベタ is a derogatory term for a woman, such as “shrew.” “Curtana” is the name of a ceremonial sword and is unrelated.
records.remedy: Use an appropriate insulting address such as “you shrew.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "As far as it goes you're a club member, aren't you, so say something you curtana!"

records.jp: 「……馬鹿'S（おバカちゃんたち）」
records.en: Touko: "...o-baka-chan-tachi (The Idiots)"
comments: Proposal. Literal is Baka's (sic). -GHS
records.assessment: The source presents the hybrid label “Idiot’S” and glosses it as “you little idiots.” Leaving the Japanese phrase o-baka-chan-tachi untranslated makes the punchline inaccessible.
records.remedy: Translate the gloss while preserving the affected label.

highlights.text: Touko: "...o-baka-chan-tachi (The Idiots)"

records.jp: 「おのれ！　ちょっと金持ちだという分際でよくも馬鹿にしてくれるものだ！」
records.en: Sakuraba: "I take offense to that last one! How dare you ridicule others as idiots just because your social class is of the somewhat wealthy!"
comments: High class twit. This is another thing that gets used in CCX0001. -GHS
records.assessment: The source mocks her for being merely a little rich. “Your social class is of the somewhat wealthy” adds class-analysis language and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “How dare you mock us just because you’re a little rich!”

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "I take offense to that last one! How dare you ridicule others as idiots just because your social class is of the somewhat wealthy!"

records.jp: 「おまえだよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "You're the same."
records.assessment: おまえだよ means “He means you” or “You’re the idiot.” “You’re the same” instead claims equivalence with someone else.
records.remedy: Use “He means you.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "You're the same."

records.jp: 「おまえだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "You're the same."
records.assessment: The repeated おまえだよ again identifies Sakuraba as the idiot. “You’re the same” does not convey that correction.
records.remedy: Use “He means you.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "You're the same."

records.jp: 同時に同等のツッコミ（暴力）が、桜庭をマットに沈めた。
records.en: Same time and same style of riposte (literal meaning) sinks Sakuraba to the mat.
comments: stop spanking the monkey dammit -GHS
records.assessment: The source says two equivalent delayed comic retorts, explicitly violent, sink Sakuraba. The English adds “literal meaning” translator commentary and uses a singular ungrammatical subject.
records.remedy: Describe the simultaneous matching retorts and violence without meta commentary.

highlights.text: Same time and same style of riposte (literal meaning) sinks Sakuraba to the mat.

records.jp: 「しかもおまえ金持ちでバカじゃないか。そのままだ」
records.en: Tomoki: "And anyway, you're stupid because you have money don't you. So stay like that."
records.assessment: Tomoki says Sakuraba is rich and stupid, exactly matching Touko’s label. “Stupid because you have money” invents causation, and “stay like that” is unrelated.
records.remedy: Use “Besides, you’re rich and stupid. She described you perfectly.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "And anyway, you're stupid because you have money don't you. So stay like that."

records.en: Sakuraba: "...pologi's...
comments: Intentional -GHS
records.assessment: The English dialogue is missing its closing quotation mark, and the clipped apology is corrupted into an unclear form.
records.remedy: Close the quote and use a readable stylized apology.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "...pologi's...

records.jp: 「……そうですね」
records.en: Misato: "...does seem unlikely."
records.assessment: Misato’s そうですね begins her own consideration, “Let’s see.” “Does seem unlikely” instead agrees with Miki’s pessimistic forecast and changes the function.
records.remedy: Use “Let’s see...”

highlights.text: Misato: "...does seem unlikely."

records.jp: 「しかも気になるアイツの名前がついてて激キュート！」
records.en: Miki: "Also, it including the name of that guy that I so like is Ultra Kyute!"
