records.assessment: “It including the name ... is Ultra Kyute” has a non-finite subject clause and distorted word order.
records.remedy: Use “And it has the name of that guy I like—super cute!”

highlights.text: Miki: "Also, it including the name of that guy that I so like is Ultra Kyute!"

records.jp: 「……と霧ちんがわたしの耳に熱く囁いたのでした」
records.en: Miki: "...or so Kiri-chin murmured hot and bothered in my ear."
comments: ...she's trying for a save on her de-facto confession, doesn't she. -GHS
records.assessment: 熱く means passionately or fervently here. “Hot and bothered” specifically suggests sexual arousal, adding a stronger implication.
records.remedy: Use “Kiri-chin whispered passionately in my ear.”

highlights.text: Miki: "...or so Kiri-chin murmured hot and bothered in my ear."

records.jp: 遠くで怒る霧。
records.en: Kiri's angry at a distance.
records.assessment: The narration says Kiri got angry in the distance. “Kiri’s angry” shifts into present tense.
records.remedy: Use “Kiri shouted angrily from a distance.”

highlights.text: Kiri's angry at a distance.

records.jp: 「くそう、本音を隠して俺を萌えさせるそんな貴様にデートを申し込むぞ、佐倉霧！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Dammit, hiding your true thoughts and finding me moe! You're challenged to a date, Sakura Kiri, you bastard!!!"
records.assessment: The source accuses Kiri of hiding her true feelings and making him feel moe. “Finding me moe” reverses who experiences the moe response.
records.remedy: Use “You hide your true feelings and make me swoon—so I’m asking you on a date, Sakura Kiri!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Dammit, hiding your true thoughts and finding me moe! You're challenged to a date, Sakura Kiri, you bastard!!!"

records.jp: 先輩に話しかけられて、一瞬友貴は戸惑う。
records.en: Addressed by Senpai, Tomoki goes flustered instantly.
records.assessment: The past narration says Tomoki was briefly flustered when Senpai addressed him. “Goes flustered instantly” shifts tense and is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use “When Senpai addressed him, Tomoki faltered for a moment.”

highlights.text: Addressed by Senpai, Tomoki goes flustered instantly.

records.jp: 複雑な顔のまま。
records.en: Mixed feelings remain on his face.
records.assessment: The source only says the complex expression remains. “Mixed feelings remain on his face” shifts tense and explicitly interprets the expression as feelings.
records.remedy: Use “The complicated look remained on his face.”

highlights.text: Mixed feelings remain on his face.

records.jp: 「小生めの名を冠していただき、恐悦至極」
records.en: Taichi: "The use of this worthless servant's appellation as prefix is something to be extremely and humbly delighted of."
records.assessment: The mock-formal line expresses profound honor that the station bears his name. “Appellation as prefix ... delighted of” is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use mock-formal but readable English: “I am deeply honored that it bears my humble name.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "The use of this worthless servant's appellation as prefix is something to be extremely and humbly delighted of."

records.jp: 「なんだね同志ムッツリーニ。よもやこのお素敵ネーミングにクレームをつけようというムッツリした魂胆ではあるまいな？」
records.en: Taichi: "What is it now, Camerata Muttsolini! Surely there is no secret plot within you to mutt-er a most morose complaint to this wonderful naming?"
comments: Backing away veeery slooowly here. But I suppose if we'll have Mein Third Reich, might's well have him. -GHS
records.assessment: 同志 means “comrade,” while “Camerata” imports an unbound foreign term. The added “mutt-er” pun is not present in the source’s ムッツリ wordplay.
records.remedy: Preserve “Comrade Muttsolini” and the hidden-lecher joke without invented English puns.

highlights.text: Taichi: "What is it now, Camerata Muttsolini! Surely there is no secret plot within you to mutt-er a most morose complaint to this wonderful naming?"

records.jp: 「ＣＲＯＳＳ　ＣＨＡＮＮＥＬではなくＣＲＯＳＳ†ＣＨＡＮＮＥＬがいい」
records.en: Sakuraba: "Not Cross Channel, but Cross†Channel is better." (reading does not change)
comments: It's commented out, but I assume that's just a writing oversight, that's obviously part of the line. Also, this is Sakuraba's most explicit contribution to the storyline: adding the actual Christian Cross to the story. It doesn't get much blunter, frankly.. -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives the preferred title with the dagger. The parenthetical “reading does not change” is an unbound translator note embedded in dialogue.
records.remedy: Remove the appended translator note.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Not Cross Channel, but Cross†Channel is better." (reading does not change)

records.jp: 「わからない……本当にこいつはわからない……」
records.en: Tomoki: "I don't get him... seriously, this guy I just don't get him..."
records.assessment: “Seriously, this guy I just don’t get him” duplicates the object and produces a run-on.
records.remedy: Use “I don’t understand him... I really don’t understand this guy.”

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I don't get him... seriously, this guy I just don't get him..."

records.jp: 「いいな、それ」
records.en: Taichi: "Niiice that one."
records.assessment: “Niiice that one” uses unnatural word order.
records.remedy: Use “That’s nice.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Niiice that one."

records.jp: 群青学院放送局・ＣＲＯＳＳ†ＣＨＡＮＮＥＬの開局だった。
records.en: Gunjou Institute Broadcast Station Cross†Channel has officially been inaugurated.
records.assessment: The source marks the station’s opening as a past narrative event. “Has officially been inaugurated” shifts to present perfect.
records.remedy: Use “And so the Gunjou Academy Broadcasting Station, Cross†Channel, opened.”

highlights.text: Gunjou Institute Broadcast Station Cross†Channel has officially been inaugurated.

records.jp: 「よし友貴、放送だ！　ボイラーに火を入れろ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then Tomoki, it's to broadcasting! Put some fire into that boiler!"
comments: They should be using dynamite. ...of course they'd have some, it's post-apocalyptic Japan, the only thing odd here is how they're not drowning in the ammunition and medkits that they will find in every locker. They're certainly drowning in crossbows and bolts. -GHS
records.assessment: “It’s to broadcasting” is not grammatical English for the command to start the broadcast.
records.remedy: Use “All right, Tomoki, time to broadcast! Fire up the boiler!”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then Tomoki, it's to broadcasting! Put some fire into that boiler!"

records.jp: 苛立たしげに呟く。
records.en: An irritated muttering.
records.assessment: The source says Touko muttered irritably. “An irritated muttering” is a noun fragment and omits her as the speaker.
records.remedy: Use “Touko muttered irritably.”

highlights.text: An irritated muttering.

records.jp: 「馬鹿じゃなけりゃ、少なくともここに全員は揃わなかったさ」
records.en: Taichi: "If it wasn't for the dumb, then this would've been less than a complete club gathering wouldn't it."
comments: Seems like a subtle insult. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that if they were not idiots, at least they would not all have gathered there. “If it wasn’t for the dumb” makes stupidity an external cause and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use “If we weren’t idiots, at least we never would’ve all gathered here.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "If it wasn't for the dumb, then this would've been less than a complete club gathering wouldn't it."

records.jp: 「本当に全員……だったら良かったのに」
records.en: Misato: "Being really all here... it would be great if we were."
comments: Now isn't this odd. -GHS
records.assessment: The wistful “If only everyone were really here” is broken into “Being really all here ... it would be great if we were,” with duplicated subjects.
records.remedy: Use “If only everyone were really here...”

highlights.text: Misato: "Being really all here... it would be great if we were."

records.jp: ほ、と大きく憂鬱玉を吐き出す先輩。
records.en: A great ball of gloom leaves Senpai by the mouth with a 'hoh'.
records.assessment: The playful image is a great ball of gloom leaving her with a sigh. “Leaves Senpai by the mouth” is an unnatural anatomical calque.
records.remedy: Use “With a long ‘hoh,’ Senpai breathed out a great ball of gloom.”

highlights.text: A great ball of gloom leaves Senpai by the mouth with a 'hoh'.

records.jp: 「とにかく桐原、せっかく来たんだから俺の流ちょうなトークに濡れていきなよ」
records.en: Taichi: "By the way, Kirihara, you went the effort to come here so do get all wet because of this flowing speech I'm gonna make, OK?"
records.assessment: The source says that since Kirihara came all this way, she should let his fluent talk soak her. "Went the effort" is ungrammatical, while "flowing speech" substitutes a literal flow image for fluency and adds future framing.
records.remedy: Use "Since you came all this way, let my smooth talk soak you.".

highlights.text: Taichi: "By the way, Kirihara, you went the effort to come here so do get all wet because of this flowing speech I'm gonna make, OK?"

records.jp: 向こうを向いて、冬子は飴玉を口に放り込んだ。
records.en: Directing herself in the other direction, Touko keeps tossing candy in her mouth.
comments: So now she has reserves? -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes Touko turning away and tossing one piece of candy into her mouth. "Keeps tossing candy" changes the completed single action into an ongoing repeated action and removes the singular object.
records.remedy: Use "Touko turns away and tosses a piece of candy into her mouth.".

highlights.text: Directing herself in the other direction, Touko keeps tossing candy in her mouth.

records.jp: バリバリと噛み砕く。
records.en: Crunch-crunch she chews down.
records.assessment: The source says she crunches or bites the candy to pieces. "Chews down" is not idiomatic English for this action.
records.remedy: Use "She crunches it up.".

highlights.text: Crunch-crunch she chews down.

records.jp: 下方から顔をのぞきこむ。唇間の距離は五センチ。
records.en: I peer into her face, coming from below. Distance between her lips and mine: five centimeters.
records.assessment: The intended action is peering up into her face from below. "I peer into her face, coming from below" uses a dangling directional phrase and makes the physical staging needlessly unclear.
records.remedy: Use "I peer up into her face from below.".

highlights.text: I peer into her face, coming from below. Distance between her lips and mine: five centimeters.

records.jp: 「きゃいやーーーーーーーっ！？」
records.en: Touko: "KIYOOOOOOOOH?!"
records.assessment: The source scream fuses the sounds of kyaa and iya. "KIYOOOOOOOOH" does not preserve either recognizable component, so the fusion explicitly explained by the following line disappears.
records.remedy: Use a fused scream such as "KYAIYAAAAAA?!".

highlights.text: Touko: "KIYOOOOOOOOH?!"

records.jp: 「映像出ないメディアで良かったですね」
records.en: Miki: "So very lucky for us that this is not a media that transmits images."
comments: Trolllllllll -GHS
records.assessment: The source says they are fortunate this medium does not transmit images. "A media" treats the plural or mass form media as a singular count noun.
records.remedy: Use "this is not a medium that transmits images.".

highlights.text: Miki: "So very lucky for us that this is not a media that transmits images."

records.jp: 気が引き締まる。
records.en: Tension rises.
records.assessment: 気が引き締まる describes the narrator becoming braced, focused, or mentally alert. "Tension rises" turns that internal change of state into an ambient increase in tension.
records.remedy: Use "I pull myself together.".

highlights.text: Tension rises.

records.jp: 「ぺけくん……が？」
records.en: Misato: "Peke-kun... you...?
records.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation mark but never closes it, leaving the displayed line malformed.
records.remedy: Add the closing quotation mark after the question mark.

highlights.text: Misato: "Peke-kun... you...?

records.jp: どうしようもない欺瞞でありながら。
records.en: full of deceits about which absolutely nothing can be done about.
comments: See CCC3004. This may be another arc word.
records.assessment: The source calls it a hopeless or irredeemable deception. The English pluralizes it into unspecified deceits and contains the ungrammatical doubled construction "about which ... about.".
records.remedy: Use "while still being a hopeless deception.".

highlights.text: full of deceits about which absolutely nothing can be done about.

records.jp: 「いいんですって、そーいう本音みたいなことは」
records.en: Taichi: "I said it's fine, that's something that sounds very like a true intent."
records.assessment: The source dismisses noble-sounding statements that resemble sincere motives: there is no need for that kind of true-feeling talk. The English instead positively labels the preceding statement as something resembling a true intent, reversing the reply's function.
records.remedy: Use "I told you, we don't need that kind of sincere-sounding motive.".

highlights.text: Taichi: "I said it's fine, that's something that sounds very like a true intent."

records.jp: そんなものが、この世界に生きる俺たちの寿命を、心の崩壊までのリミットを、少しだけ延ばしてくれる。
records.en: And for us who live in this world that will become a tiny elongation of our lifespan, of the limit before the downfall of our hearts.
records.assessment: The source says that such wreckage slightly extends the lives of those in this world, postponing emotional collapse. The English makes "this world" the subject that becomes an elongation and leaves the causal and temporal relation ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use "Something like that extends our lives in this world just a little, pushing back the limit before our hearts collapse.".

highlights.text: And for us who live in this world that will become a tiny elongation of our lifespan, of the limit before the downfall of our hearts.

records.jp: 美希が口を閉じ、指を一本ずつ減らしていく。
records.en: Miki closes her mouth, and decreases the fingers one by one.
records.assessment: The source says Miki lowers her raised fingers one by one during the countdown. "Decreases the fingers" suggests reducing their number rather than folding or lowering them.
records.remedy: Use "Miki closes her mouth and lowers one finger at a time.".

highlights.text: Miki closes her mouth, and decreases the fingers one by one.

records.jp: こういう他愛ない部活動、普通のガクセーらしい日常を。
records.en: About this kind of silly innocent club activities, about an ordinary life as if an ordinary student.
records.assessment: This is the object of the preceding "I had dreamed": trivial club activities like these and an ordinary student's everyday life. The English begins an unattached "About," repeats "ordinary," and changes student-like daily life into life merely resembling an ordinary student.
records.remedy: Use "Trivial club activities like these—an ordinary student's everyday life.".

highlights.text: About this kind of silly innocent club activities, about an ordinary life as if an ordinary student.

records.jp: 満足だ―――
records.en: I will be satisfied---
records.assessment: 満足だ states present satisfaction. "I will be satisfied" postpones that state into the future.
records.remedy: Use "I'm satisfied—".

highlights.text: I will be satisfied---

records.jp: 息を吸う。
records.en: Draw in a breath,
records.assessment: The source is first-person narration: the narrator inhales. "Draw in a breath" reads as an imperative because its subject is omitted.
records.remedy: Use "I draw in a breath,".

highlights.text: Draw in a breath,

records.jp: 原稿を手放す。
records.en: release the script from the grasp,
records.assessment: The source says the narrator lets go of the script. The English continues an imperative-like subjectless construction and adds the awkward phrase "from the grasp.".
records.remedy: Use "I release the script,".

highlights.text: release the script from the grasp,

records.jp: 夏の香りを含んだ夕風が、悪戯する手つきでそれをさらっていく。
records.en: and an evening wind that still captured that scent of Summer kidnaps it with a mischievous sleight of hand.
comments: see CCX0001, this needs to work with or without the script line. -GHS
records.assessment: The evening breeze carries the scent of summer and mischievously snatches the script away. "Still captured that scent" reverses the relation by making the wind capture the scent and is grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: Use "and the evening breeze, carrying the scent of summer, mischievously snatches it away.".

highlights.text: and an evening wind that still captured that scent of Summer kidnaps it with a mischievous sleight of hand.

records.jp: 原稿は連なって飛び立ち、千々に乱れて中空に散った。
records.en: The manuscript pages took flight, one by one, and in pieces disordered they scattered and spread in the air.
records.assessment: The pages take flight in a connected stream and then scatter chaotically through the air. "One by one" changes that connected motion, while "in pieces disordered" suggests torn pieces and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use "The pages take flight in a stream, then break formation and scatter through the air.".

highlights.text: The manuscript pages took flight, one by one, and in pieces disordered they scattered and spread in the air.

records.jp: さあ放送だ。
records.en: So, to broadcast.
records.assessment: さあ放送だ announces that it is time for the broadcast. "So, to broadcast" is an incomplete infinitive phrase rather than an announcement.
records.remedy: Use "Now for the broadcast.".

highlights.text: So, to broadcast.

records.jp: そして俺は、力強く言葉を押し出した。
records.en: And then, I pushed out these forceful words:
records.assessment: The source says the narrator forcefully pushes the words out. The English instead calls the words themselves forceful, shifting the force from delivery to content.
records.remedy: Use "And then I forcefully pushed the words out.".

highlights.text: And then, I pushed out these forceful words:

records.jp: 俺たち一年生が進級し、幸せな三年生が引退して。
records.en:
Among us the freshmen are being promoted,
while the happy third years are retiring.
comments: Hum. Japan school year starts in Spring, and there isn't much to say that Gunjou is any different. Taichi is halfway through second year by the Camp scene, so I can't make this make much sense outside of really blatant trolling. Unless he's actually a delayed First Year, it's the norm at Gunjou. Same for the third years: Misato (and Youko FWIW) should be dropping club to focus on graduation and university entrance exams. There's never been mention of there ever having been any member in the Broadcast Club outside of the eight except for Miyuki. See CCC3004. -GHS
records.assessment: The source narrates the first-years advancing a grade and the third-years retiring as linked completed transitions. "Among us the freshmen are being promoted" is ungrammatical and changes the sequence to present progressive actions.
records.remedy: Use "We first-years moved up a grade, and the happy third-years retired.".

highlights.text:
Among us the freshmen are being promoted,
while the happy third years are retiring.

records.jp: 彼女は……どうせ呼べばすぐにやってくる。
records.en: Her... after all, she'll turn up quick if called.
records.assessment: The source's topic is "she": if called, she will come right away anyway. "Her" uses the object form as the subject, and "turn up quick" is grammatically nonstandard here.
records.remedy: Use "She... would come right away if we called her, anyway.".

highlights.text: Her... after all, she'll turn up quick if called.

records.jp: 支払った代価は安くない。
records.en: there was no cheap price to pay.
records.assessment: The source says the price paid to gather seven people was not small. "There was no cheap price to pay" is an unnatural negative construction that fails to state clearly that a steep price was actually paid.
records.remedy: Use "the price we paid was not small.".

highlights.text: there was no cheap price to pay.

records.jp: そりゃもう大騒ぎさ。
records.en: That is, it was already an uproar.
records.assessment: そりゃもう emphatically introduces the scale of the commotion. "That is, it was already" misreads the idiomatic discourse phrase as explanatory and temporal wording.
records.remedy: Use "It caused one hell of a commotion.".

highlights.text: That is, it was already an uproar.

records.jp: 学院には内緒のオチャメ。
records.en: a mischief kept away from the Institute.
records.assessment: The source calls it a bit of mischief kept secret from the academy. "A mischief kept away from the Institute" changes secrecy into physical separation and uses an unnatural count noun.
records.remedy: Use "a little mischief kept secret from the academy.".

highlights.text: a mischief kept away from the Institute.

records.jp: 公になれば、ちょっとした騒ぎになる。
records.en:
If this was turned public, it
would become quite the uproar.
records.assessment: The source says that if it became public, it would cause a minor commotion. "If this was turned public" is ungrammatical and imposes an external passive agent not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use "If it became public, it would cause a bit of a commotion.".

highlights.text:
If this was turned public, it
would become quite the uproar.

records.jp: そうして、合宿が終わり。
records.en: Finally, the Training Camp is ending.
records.assessment: The source says "and so the training camp ended." "Is ending" changes the completed event to an ongoing one, and "Finally" adds a culmination marker not present in the sentence.
records.remedy: Use "And so the training camp ended.".

highlights.text: Finally, the Training Camp is ending.

records.jp: 七人は帰路に着いた。
records.en: Seven people reached the way of return.
records.assessment: 帰路に着いた means the seven set out on the journey home. "Reached the way of return" is an unidiomatic literal construction and can imply that they arrived at a road rather than departed.
records.remedy: Use "The seven of us set out for home.".

highlights.text: Seven people reached the way of return.

records.jp: 何時間も。
records.en: A countless number of hours.
comments: 6.5 isn't "countless", though since Taichi never reaches that answer, nor cares... -GHS
records.assessment: 何時間も means many hours or hours on end. "A countless number of hours" exaggerates the duration into something literally innumerable.
records.remedy: Use "For hours and hours.".

highlights.text: A countless number of hours.

records.jp: 空気までも冷たく感じさせる。
records.en: A chilling sensation made by the mood alone,
records.assessment: The source says the eerie quiet made even the air feel cold. The English replaces the air with a generic "chilling sensation" produced by mood alone, removing the concrete sensory image.
records.remedy: Use "It made even the air feel cold,".

highlights.text: A chilling sensation made by the mood alone,

records.jp: 夏だというのに。
records.en: when however it is Summer.
records.assessment: The source supplies a concessive fragment: despite it being summer. "When however it is Summer" is ungrammatical and uses a temporal connector instead of a clean concessive relation.
records.remedy: Use "even though it was summer.".

highlights.text: when however it is Summer.

records.jp: 人類は滅亡していた。
records.en: Mankind had fallen.
comments: Literally it's closer to extinction, but it follows in the sense of downfall, of a clan a family etc. - the sense is pretty much that of the actual Fall of Mankind. Curiously, 人類は滅亡しました (jinrui wa metsubou shimsashita) googles to Jintai. No autocorrections or "did you mean", googl that with quotes around it and it literally googles to Jintai, big banner on the right about the series included. -GHS
records.assessment: 滅亡していた states that humanity had become extinct. "Had fallen" can mean defeat or decline and does not communicate extinction.
records.remedy: Use "Humanity had gone extinct.".

highlights.text: Mankind had fallen.

records.jp: 「はいはいはいはい！」
records.en: Taichi: "QuickQuickQuickQuick!"
records.assessment: The repeated はい is a rapid string of acknowledgments such as "yes" or "okay." "Quick" turns it into a command about speed.
records.remedy: Use "Okay, okay, okay, okay!".

highlights.text: Taichi: "QuickQuickQuickQuick!"

records.jp: 勢いよく家を飛び出した。
records.en: I flew out of the house with vigorous swiftness.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator burst energetically out of the house. "With vigorous swiftness" is a redundant and unidiomatic adverbial phrase.
records.remedy: Use "I burst energetically out of the house.".

highlights.text: I flew out of the house with vigorous swiftness.

records.jp: 扉の内側でスタンバッてパワーをたくわえていた甲斐があり、上々の上方っぷり。
records.en: The result of this storage of power while on standby inside of the door is an uppermost elevation in the most highest of styles.
comments: Beautiful quasi-nonsense (it's about his till-now gloomy mood that he's faking out as cheerful). Last part may well be "I have a hard-on". -GHS
records.assessment: The source jokes that waiting inside the door and storing up power paid off in an excellent upward leap or trajectory. The English is syntactically broken and renders 上々の上方っぷり as the opaque "uppermost elevation in the most highest of styles.".
records.remedy: Use "Waiting inside the door and storing up power paid off: a splendid upward launch.".

highlights.text: The result of this storage of power while on standby inside of the door is an uppermost elevation in the most highest of styles.

records.jp: いつもだったら、ここで羞恥プレイ。
records.en: If it was as always, this'd be a shameful playact.
records.assessment: The source says that normally this would be a public-humiliation routine. "If it was as always" is ungrammatical, and "shameful playact" weakens the imposed humiliation into something the narrator merely performs.
records.remedy: Use "Normally, this would be the point where I humiliated myself.".

highlights.text: If it was as always, this'd be a shameful playact.

records.jp: 集団登校中の玄孫ギャルたち。
records.en: great-great-granddaughter gyaru in a group going to (pre)school.
comments: 玄孫ギャル seems to be コギャル with waaay younger girls. See CCB2012 for why I left it. -GHS
records.assessment: The source identifies a group of 玄孫ギャル on their way to school. The parenthetical "(pre)" is unsupported, and the singular compound "great-great-granddaughter gyaru" does not agree with the plural group.
records.remedy: Remove the unsupported preschool gloss and make the English phrase agree with the plural group.

highlights.text: great-great-granddaughter gyaru in a group going to (pre)school.

records.jp: まだまだ決まったわけではない。
records.en: Still not the time to surrender to this sight.
records.assessment: The source says that nothing has been decided yet. "Not the time to surrender to this sight" replaces that proposition with an invented command about surrender and adds a visual object absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use "Nothing has been decided yet.".

highlights.text: Still not the time to surrender to this sight.

records.jp: 口を押さえる。
records.en: I hold down the mouth.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator covers or holds a hand over his mouth. "Hold down the mouth" uses the wrong article and suggests restraining the mouth physically.
records.remedy: Use "I cover my mouth.".

highlights.text: I hold down the mouth.

records.jp: 人類滅亡だなんて！
records.en: Mankind had fallen!
records.assessment: 人類滅亡だなんて reacts to the idea of humanity's extinction. "Mankind had fallen" changes extinction to defeat and presents it as an already completed fact.
records.remedy: Use "Humanity going extinct?!".

highlights.text: Mankind had fallen!

records.jp: たいへん笑えた。
records.en: A disaster of laughter.
comments: Forcing himself to laugh + suppressing a laugh + laughing out loud. -GHS
records.assessment: たいへん笑えた says it was very funny or that the narrator laughed hard. "A disaster of laughter" treats たいへん as a noun meaning disaster and does not express the successful laughter.
records.remedy: Use "I laughed hard.".

highlights.text: A disaster of laughter.

records.jp: 今時、人類滅亡ネタはないだろう。
records.en: These days, the Fall of Mankind is beneath stories and jokes alike.
records.assessment: The source says a humanity-extinction gag is too clichéd for the present day. "Beneath stories and jokes alike" invents a comparison between stories and jokes and obscures the judgment that the trope is dated.
records.remedy: Use "An extinction-of-humanity gag is passé these days.".

highlights.text: These days, the Fall of Mankind is beneath stories and jokes alike.

records.jp: 「さてと」
records.en: Taichi: "That aside."
records.assessment: さてと is a transition meaning 'well then/now then.' 'That aside' instead says the previous topic is being dismissed.
records.remedy: Use 'Well then.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "That aside."

records.jp: 周囲に人がいないのに騒いでも虚しいだけだ。
records.en: When surrounded by an absence of people, making uproar is only futility.
records.assessment: The source says making a commotion is merely empty when nobody is around. 'Surrounded by an absence of people' and 'is only futility' are unidiomatic calques.
records.remedy: Use 'Making a fuss when nobody is around just feels empty.'

highlights.text: When surrounded by an absence of people, making uproar is only futility.

records.jp: 近所に住む激プリティ小娘の顔を見ずして、一日ははじまらない。
records.en: Without the sight of that Ultra Pretty Little Girl who nearby dwells, the day has not begun.
records.assessment: The source jokes that a day cannot begin without seeing the extremely pretty little girl who lives nearby. 'Who nearby dwells' is malformed inverted syntax, and 'has not begun' disrupts the habitual construction.
records.remedy: Use 'My day doesn't start until I've seen the ultra-pretty little girl who lives nearby.'

highlights.text: Without the sight of that Ultra Pretty Little Girl who nearby dwells, the day has not begun.

records.jp: 堂島家に訪れる。近い。
records.en: I visit Doujima residence. It's close.
records.assessment: The source says he visits the Doujima household. 'I visit Doujima residence' omits the possessive or article required in English.
records.remedy: Use 'I visit the Doujima residence. It's close by.'

highlights.text: I visit Doujima residence. It's close.

records.jp: 電気が止まっているのだった。
records.en: Because the power supply had been interrupted.
comments: Not because you can't hear it from outside of the house. -GHS
records.assessment: The source independently realizes that the electricity has been cut off. Beginning with 'Because' leaves an unattached subordinate clause and falsely presents it as an explicit reason clause.
records.remedy: Use 'The electricity had been cut off.'

highlights.text: Because the power supply had been interrupted.

records.jp: 掃除機も冷蔵庫も。
records.en: No vacuuming, no refrigerating.
records.assessment: The source lists the vacuum cleaner and refrigerator among the powerless appliances. 'No vacuuming, no refrigerating' replaces the appliances with activities.
records.remedy: Use 'The vacuum cleaner and refrigerator, too.'

highlights.text: No vacuuming, no refrigerating.

records.jp: 何もかも。
records.en: Nothing of nothing.
records.assessment: 何もかも means everything or absolutely everything in the ongoing list. 'Nothing of nothing' is ungrammatical and does not express the inclusive scope.
records.remedy: Use 'Everything.'

highlights.text: Nothing of nothing.

records.jp: 「お嬢さんをいただきにきましたー！」
records.en: Taichi: "I have come to help myself to Ojou-saaan!"
records.assessment: お嬢さん here means the listener's daughter and supports the mock marriage-request joke. Leaving it as 'Ojou-san' removes that relationship for an English reader.
records.remedy: Use 'I've come to take your daughter!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I have come to help myself to Ojou-saaan!"

records.en: Taichi: Yu...sa..."
records.assessment: The dialogue has a closing quotation mark but no opening quotation mark, leaving the displayed line malformed.
records.remedy: Add the opening quotation mark before 'Yu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: Yu...sa..."

records.jp: 叩きつけた拳が、ほつれて落ちた。
records.en: The fist I slam in, but there is only fraying and falling.
comments: Him and the punches. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the fist he had been pounding with went limp and dropped. 'The fist I slam in' has the wrong tense, while 'only fraying and falling' mistranslates the metaphor and leaves the sentence syntactically broken.
records.remedy: Use 'The fist I'd been pounding with went limp and dropped.'

highlights.text: The fist I slam in, but there is only fraying and falling.

records.jp: 犬小屋はカラだった。
records.en: The dog house was a shed skin.
comments: And not a mention of the collar and the chain that he would've left behind if he had been Taken, rather than if he had simply uprooted it and left. -GHS
records.assessment: カラ means the doghouse was empty. 'A shed skin' assigns an unrelated sense of shell or husk and changes the concrete observation completely.
records.remedy: Use 'The doghouse was empty.'

highlights.text: The dog house was a shed skin.

records.jp: そういえば、一匹の猫も見ていない。
records.en: Now that I say it, I did not see even just one cat.
records.assessment: そういえば means 'come to think of it.' 'Now that I say it' is an incorrect calque, and 'did not see even just one cat' is needlessly malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'Come to think of it, I haven't seen a single cat.'

highlights.text: Now that I say it, I did not see even just one cat.

records.jp: 「うーんうーん」
records.en: Taichi: "Yeeeah, yeeeah."
records.assessment: うーんうーん is a repeated thoughtful or troubled hum. 'Yeah, yeah' turns it into repeated agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'Hmm, hmm.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yeeeah, yeeeah."

records.jp: 夢なら夢でも構わなかった。
records.en: If it's a dream then no need for concern, it's a dream.
records.assessment: The source says he would not mind even if it were a dream. The English substitutes 'no need for concern,' repeats 'it's a dream,' and fails to state his willingness clearly.
records.remedy: Use 'I didn't mind if it was a dream.'

highlights.text: If it's a dream then no need for concern, it's a dream.

records.jp: 「学校行くか」
records.en: Taichi: "Should I go to school, then."
records.assessment: 学校行くか is a self-directed volitional decision, roughly 'guess I'll go to school.' 'Should I go' turns it into a question about what he ought to do.
records.remedy: Use 'Guess I'll go to school.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Should I go to school, then."

records.jp: 「切っておきたかったなー……」
records.en: Taichi: "Awww, and I wanted to cut 'em..."
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: The source says he had wanted to get his bangs cut beforehand. 'I wanted to cut 'em' can make him the person doing the cutting and loses the beforehand aspect.
records.remedy: Use 'I wanted to get them cut beforehand...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Awww, and I wanted to cut 'em..."

records.jp: 鬱陶しい。
records.en: How gloomy.
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: 鬱陶しい describes the bangs as annoying or bothersome. 'Gloomy' assigns an emotional atmosphere instead of physical irritation.
records.remedy: Use 'They're annoying.'

highlights.text: How gloomy.

records.jp: 色のせいもあるけど、あまり自分の髪は好きじゃない。
records.en: I don't really like my hair, although it's a bit the color's fault.
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: The source says their color is one reason he dislikes his hair. 'Although it's a bit the color's fault' is grammatically malformed and weakens the causal relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Partly because of the color, I don't really like my hair.'

highlights.text: I don't really like my hair, although it's a bit the color's fault.

records.jp: 前髪をいじりながら坂だらけの通学路、通称『通学坂』に出た。
records.en: As I played with my bangs I began on the hill-infested road to school, common nickname: The Hills to School.
comments: PCP CCA0003, CCA0002
records.assessment: The source says he reaches the hill-filled school route nicknamed School Hill while playing with his bangs. 'Began on' is ungrammatical, 'hill-infested' adds hostile imagery, and 'The Hills to School' changes the singular nickname.
records.remedy: Use 'Playing with my bangs, I reach the hilly school route nicknamed School Hill.'

highlights.text: As I played with my bangs I began on the hill-infested road to school, common nickname: The Hills to School.

records.jp: ドカーン！
records.en: Thump!
comments: SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
records.assessment: ドカーン is a loud explosive crash. 'Thump' substantially reduces the force and volume of the collision.
records.remedy: Use 'KABOOM!' or another forceful crash effect.

highlights.text: Thump!

records.jp: 俺は卍みたいな形になって回転した。
records.en: I went rotating in the fylfot shape of a swastika.
comments: Just for ners. As usual, no kanjis or 卍 would get in. Swastikas, as we all know and accept universally, only exclusively mean Nazism and have nothing to do with Buddhism. Nah, it's a troll, the swastikas are him being a good Nietzscheian, they have zero to do with Buddhism because this story doesn't, in the slightest. -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply compares the rotating body to a manji shape. 'The fylfot shape of a swastika' redundantly names the same symbol twice and makes the comparison cumbersome.
records.remedy: Use 'I spun around in the shape of a manji.'

highlights.text: I went rotating in the fylfot shape of a swastika.

records.jp: 「ブレーキブレーキ！」
records.en: Nanaka: "BREEEAKING BREEEAKING!"
records.assessment: ブレーキ means 'brakes' or 'brake.' 'Breaking' is the wrong English word and changes the shouted instruction.
records.remedy: Use 'BRAKES! BRAKES!'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "BREEEAKING BREEEAKING!"

records.jp: 「この処女が」
records.en: Taichi: "This damn maiden..."
records.assessment: 処女 explicitly means 'virgin.' 'Maiden' euphemizes the recurring crude insult and removes its sexual bluntness.
records.remedy: Use 'You damn virgin.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "This damn maiden..."

records.jp: ペッと吐き捨てる。
records.en: Pah! I spat her way.
comments: PCP CCA0007
records.assessment: The source says he spits the words out contemptuously. 'I spat her way' instead suggests physically spitting toward the girl.
records.remedy: Use 'I spit the words out.'

highlights.text: Pah! I spat her way.

records.jp: 「うひ」
records.en: Nanaka: "Owieee."
records.assessment: うひ is a startled or sheepish squeak, not an expression of physical pain. 'Owie' invents an injury reaction.
records.remedy: Use a brief squeak such as 'Eep.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Owieee."

records.jp: 「人をプロペラみたいに回転させやがって」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't go turning people into propellerish things dammit!"
records.assessment: The source complains that she spun a person around like a propeller. 'Turning people into propellerish things' changes the simile into transformation, pluralizes the victim, and uses a malformed adjective.
records.remedy: Use 'You spun me around like a propeller, damn it.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't go turning people into propellerish things dammit!"

records.jp: ホコリを払い落とし、学校に向かう。
records.en: Dusting off clothes and pride, I turn back towards school.
comments: 誇り+埃 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he brushes off the dust and heads toward school. 'Clothes and pride' adds an unsupported joke, while 'turn back' asserts a reversal not stated in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'I brush off the dust and head for school.'

highlights.text: Dusting off clothes and pride, I turn back towards school.

records.jp: 並んで、自転車に飛び乗る。
records.en: Lining up to me, she hops back onto the bike.
records.assessment: The source says she draws alongside him and hops onto the bicycle. 'Lining up to me' is not idiomatic and does not express catching up or riding abreast.
records.remedy: Use 'She pulls alongside me and hops back onto her bike.'

highlights.text: Lining up to me, she hops back onto the bike.

records.jp: 「うん。今回も落ち着いていて結構結構」
records.en: Nanaka: "Yep! You calmed down nice an' nice this time as well."
comments: Likely from the panic attack he was having above. -GHS
records.assessment: The source praises him for being calm again. 'You calmed down nice an' nice' is grammatically broken and turns the repeated 結構 into an invented dialectal repetition.
records.remedy: Use 'Good, good. You're calm again this time.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Yep! You calmed down nice an' nice this time as well."

records.jp: 「太一は偉いなあ」
records.en: Nanaka: "Taichi's extraordinary, innit."
comments: Great + awful. -GHS
records.assessment: 偉い here praises Taichi as admirable or good. 'Extraordinary' overstates the compliment as exceptional ability or status.
records.remedy: Use 'Taichi, you're really admirable.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Taichi's extraordinary, innit."

records.jp: ＤＡＮＧＥＲＯＵＳ？
records.en: DAI KIKEN?
comments: Guessing, these kanjis don't sound familiar. -GHS
records.assessment: The source itself displays the English word DANGEROUS. Replacing it with romanized Japanese both mistranslates and erases the deliberate English presentation.
records.remedy: Use 'DANGEROUS?'

highlights.text: DAI KIKEN?

records.jp: つうか、俺たち全員か。
records.en: No, more like, all us are.
records.assessment: The source concludes that all of them are dangerous. 'All us are' omits the required preposition and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'More like all of us are.'

highlights.text: No, more like, all us are.

records.jp: 「……ったく」
records.en: Taichi: "...'sly."
comments: Seriously -GHS
records.assessment: ったく is an exasperated 'jeez' or 'honestly.' The fragment ''sly' is unrelated and unintelligible in context.
records.remedy: Use '...Jeez.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...'sly."

records.jp: 笑えん。
records.en: Laugh on.
records.assessment: 笑えん means 'I can't laugh' or 'this isn't funny.' 'Laugh on' reverses the negative statement into an imperative to continue laughing.
records.remedy: Use 'This isn't funny.'

highlights.text: Laugh on.

records.jp: しかしこの処女は何者だ？
records.en: However, who or what is this maiden?
records.assessment: 処女 again explicitly means 'virgin.' 'Maiden' removes the crude sexual wording that drives the repeated characterization.
records.remedy: Use 'But who is this virgin?'

highlights.text: However, who or what is this maiden?

records.jp: 「新学期、月曜日、新しい出会い、別れ」
records.en: Nanaka: "New school term, Monday, new meetings, farewells."
records.assessment: 出会い means encounters or people one meets. 'Meetings' suggests scheduled gatherings and misses the paired life-event sense alongside farewells.
records.remedy: Use 'new encounters, farewells.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "New school term, Monday, new meetings, farewells."

records.jp: 「そして祠」
records.en: Nanaka: "And then, the Hokora."
records.assessment: 祠 is the common noun 'shrine.' Leaving it as 'Hokora' turns it into an unexplained apparent proper name.
records.remedy: Use 'And then, the shrine.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "And then, the Hokora."

records.jp: ほこら？
records.en: Ho-ko-ra?
records.assessment: The narration repeats the common noun ほこら in puzzlement. Splitting its romanization into 'Ho-ko-ra' with no translation withholds the meaning rather than conveying the puzzled echo.
records.remedy: Use 'A shrine?'

highlights.text: Ho-ko-ra?

records.jp: 「このシーンが終わったら祠に行く選択肢が出るように」
records.en: Nanaka: "When you complete this chapter, the choice to go to the Hokora will appear."
comments: As "scene" is explicitly used to refer to chapters in the Xbox 360 version achievements. So she is perfectly correct (provided you actually complete the routes). -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that when this scene ends, an option to go to the shrine should appear. 'Chapter' changes the game unit, and 'Hokora' leaves the destination untranslated.
records.remedy: Use 'When this scene ends, the option to go to the shrine should appear.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "When you complete this chapter, the choice to go to the Hokora will appear."

records.jp: 「どうしてあんな山まで行かないといかんのよ。学校あるしさ」
records.en: Taichi: "Why do I just have to go all the way up that mountain! I got school too!"
records.assessment: The source asks why he has to go all the way to that mountain and notes that he has school. 'Why do I just have to' is malformed and makes 'just' modify obligation rather than distance.
records.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to go all the way to that mountain? I have school.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Why do I just have to go all the way up that mountain! I got school too!"

records.jp: 「学校って、人いないじゃん」
records.en: Nanaka: "'Cause there's nobody at school."
records.assessment: The source counters that there is nobody at school, phrased as an expectation-seeking observation. Starting with ''Cause' invents an explicit causal relation to the preceding line.
records.remedy: Use 'But there's nobody at school, right?'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "'Cause there's nobody at school."

records.jp: 「いや、人類滅亡してますし」
records.en: Nanaka: "Nope, mankind has fallen."
records.assessment: 人類滅亡 means humanity is extinct. 'Mankind has fallen' can mean defeat or decline and does not state extinction.
records.remedy: Use 'Humanity has gone extinct.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Nope, mankind has fallen."

records.jp: 「いや、実際そうですし」
records.en: Nanaka: "Nope, seems like it's reality."
records.assessment: 実際そうです says that is in fact the case. 'Seems like it's reality' weakens certainty to appearance and changes the proposition into generic reality.
records.remedy: Use 'No, that's actually what happened.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Nope, seems like it's reality."

records.jp: 「はいはい、その話はおしまい！」
records.en: Taichi: "There, there, that topic is now all done!"
records.assessment: はいはい is a dismissive 'yeah, yeah' before ending the topic. 'There, there' is a soothing formula with the wrong interpersonal function.
records.remedy: Use 'Yeah, yeah, end of discussion!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There, there, that topic is now all done!"

records.jp: 「……毎回毎回、違う精神状態なんだよね、太一は」
records.en: Nanaka: "...every time but every time, always in a different mental state, aren't you Taichi."
records.assessment: The source says Taichi is in a different mental state every single time. 'Every time but every time' is malformed, and the tag question lacks required punctuation and word order.
records.remedy: Use 'Every single time, you're in a different state of mind, Taichi.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...every time but every time, always in a different mental state, aren't you Taichi."

records.jp: 処女は大きくため息をついた。
records.en: The maiden exhaled a very big sigh.
records.assessment: 処女 explicitly means 'virgin.' 'Maiden' euphemizes the recurring crude description.
records.remedy: Use 'The virgin heaved a huge sigh.'

highlights.text: The maiden exhaled a very big sigh.

records.jp: 「妙に平然としているかと思えば、現実を拒絶してたり」
records.en: Nanaka: "If you're thinking you're oddly calm, you're rejecting reality."
records.assessment: The source contrasts occasions when he seems strangely calm with occasions when he rejects reality. The English makes Taichi think he is calm and turns rejection into the result of that thought.
records.remedy: Use 'One time you seem strangely calm; the next, you're rejecting reality.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "If you're thinking you're oddly calm, you're rejecting reality."

records.jp: 「でも特定の傾向だけに固着してないってことは、強さかもしれない……」
records.en: Nanaka: "But just that you're not fixed to one specific tendency, maybe it's a strength..."
records.assessment: The source says not being fixed on only one particular tendency may be a kind of strength. 'But just that you're not fixed' is grammatically malformed and obscures what may constitute strength.
records.remedy: Use 'But maybe it's a strength that you aren't stuck in one particular pattern.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "But just that you're not fixed to one specific tendency, maybe it's a strength..."

records.jp: 「祠行けよ、行ってくれよ！」
records.en: Nanaka: "Go to the Hokora, please, just go!"
records.assessment: 祠 is the common noun 'shrine.' Leaving it as the apparent proper name 'Hokora' withholds the destination's meaning.
records.remedy: Use 'Go to the shrine—please, just go!'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Go to the Hokora, please, just go!"

records.jp: 「祠行くか？」
records.en: Nanaka: "Will you go to the Hokora?"
records.assessment: The question again uses the common noun 祠, not a proper name. 'Hokora' leaves it untranslated.
records.remedy: Use 'Will you go to the shrine?'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Will you go to the Hokora?"

records.jp: 苦しい……死ぬる。
records.en: Agonizing... dying...
records.assessment: 死ぬる is a deliberately comic or archaic form of 'die.' Plain 'dying' loses that marked voice.
records.remedy: Use a marked line such as 'The agony... I perish.'

highlights.text: Agonizing... dying...

records.jp: こくこくと頷く。
records.en: Bob bob steady nod.
records.assessment: The source says he nods repeatedly and vigorously. 'Bob bob steady nod' is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'I nod vigorously over and over.'

highlights.text: Bob bob steady nod.

records.jp: 「よかろう」
records.en: Nanaka: "Goody."
records.assessment: よかろう is a lofty or authoritative 'very well.' 'Goody' is childish approval with the opposite register.
records.remedy: Use 'Very well.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Goody."

records.jp: 逆らわない方が良さそうだ。
records.en: Non-disobedience appears best.
records.assessment: The source says it seems best not to resist her. 'Non-disobedience appears best' is an unnatural nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use 'It seems best not to resist.'

highlights.text: Non-disobedience appears best.

records.jp: 「けどどうして祠……」
records.en: Taichi: But, why the hokora..."
records.assessment: The dialogue is missing its opening quotation mark, and 祠 is left as romanized 'hokora' instead of 'shrine.'
records.remedy: Add the opening quote and use 'But why the shrine...?'

highlights.text: Taichi: But, why the hokora..."

records.jp: 「もんのすごい御利益があるわけさ」
records.en: Nanaka: "He's got this amazing graciousness, y'know."
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: 御利益 means a deity or shrine's miraculous blessing or benefit. 'He's got amazing graciousness' assigns a personality trait to the god instead.
records.remedy: Use 'It grants incredible blessings.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "He's got this amazing graciousness, y'know."

records.jp: 「いや、笑いたくなるのはごもっともですよ。あたしだって人からンなこと真顔で言われたら笑うわ」
records.en: Nanaka: "Naaah, wanting to ridicule it is totally natural. If some guy saidd'at to me with a really straight face I'd laugh too."
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: 笑いたくなる means wanting to laugh. 'Wanting to ridicule it' adds a hostile target and changes laughter into mockery.
records.remedy: Use 'It's only natural you'd want to laugh.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Naaah, wanting to ridicule it is totally natural. If some guy saidd'at to me with a really straight face I'd laugh too."

records.jp: 「だから俺を笑かすために真顔だったのだろうに」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore you just said that to me with a straight face to make me laugh, have you."
comments: CP CCA0003
records.assessment: The source asserts that she kept a straight face precisely to make him laugh. The English is syntactically broken and ends with the wrong question tag.
records.remedy: Use 'That's why you said it with a straight face—to make me laugh.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore you just said that to me with a straight face to make me laugh, have you."

records.jp: 「大切なことだよ」
records.en: Nanaka: "This is something precious!"
records.assessment: 大切 here means important. 'Precious' changes practical or serious importance into sentimental value.
records.remedy: Use 'It's important.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "This is something precious!"

records.jp: 「なぜに？」
records.en: Taichi: "In what way?"
records.assessment: なぜに asks 'why?' 'In what way?' asks for a manner or dimension instead of a reason.
records.remedy: Use 'Why?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "In what way?"

records.jp: 「とにかく大切なことなの！」
records.en: Nanaka: "Whatever, this is something p-r-e-c-i-o-u-s!"
records.assessment: The source insists that it is important, whatever the reason. 'Whatever' dismisses the topic, 'precious' changes the key word, and spelling it out adds emphasis not in the text.
records.remedy: Use 'Anyway, it's important!'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Whatever, this is something p-r-e-c-i-o-u-s!"

records.jp: たまに写真を見せびらかされるが、ちっとも楽しくない。
records.en: Occasionally he did flaunt one of his photos at me, but that didn't seem really interesting.
records.assessment: The source states habitually that he sometimes shows off the photos and the narrator finds it no fun at all. The English shifts to sporadic past and weakens certainty to 'didn't seem really interesting.'
records.remedy: Use 'Sometimes he shows them off to me, but I don't enjoy it at all.'

highlights.text: Occasionally he did flaunt one of his photos at me, but that didn't seem really interesting.

records.jp: こっちは電車に抱く幻想など持ち合わせない今っ子なのだ。
records.en: For this boy right now, fantasies to be entertained on trains are a product out of stock.
records.assessment: The narrator calls himself a modern kid who has no romantic fantasies about trains. 'Fantasies to be entertained on trains' changes the object of fantasy into its location and is syntactically opaque.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm a modern kid with no romantic fantasies about trains.'

highlights.text: For this boy right now, fantasies to be entertained on trains are a product out of stock.

records.jp: 店は店主不在時もあいている。
records.en: A shop open even with shopkeeper absent.
records.assessment: The source states that the shop remains open even when its owner is absent. 'A shop open even with shopkeeper absent' omits required articles and the finite verb.
records.remedy: Use 'The shop stays open even when the owner is away.'

highlights.text: A shop open even with shopkeeper absent.

records.jp: 道楽的な無人商店だ。
records.en: A clerk-less store that smells of profligacy.
records.assessment: 道楽的 describes the unmanned shop as an indulgent hobby operation. 'Smells of profligacy' adds a moralized accusation of wasteful vice.
records.remedy: Use 'It's an unmanned shop run more as a hobby.'

highlights.text: A clerk-less store that smells of profligacy.

records.jp: 遺産以外の何が、元暴走族の粗暴な鉄オタを善人に変えうるというのか。
records.en: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.
comments: CP CCA0004
records.assessment: The source rhetorically says nothing but inheritance could have turned the rough former biker-gang railfan into a good man. The English claims something outside the inheritance did so and changes his combined traits into a comparison between them.
records.remedy: Use 'What but an inheritance could turn a rough former biker-gang railfan into a good man?'

highlights.text: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.

records.jp: とにかく目先の現金にだけはありあまっている氏の店は、近隣の住人に対してはいくらでもツケてくれる希有な地元密着型店舗なのである。
records.en: Anyway, the store owned by this man with more than enough cash underhand is one of those very rare, local-contact type stores that allows an unlimited tab for those who live around it.
comments: PCP CCA0004
records.assessment: 目先の現金 means ready cash on hand. 'Cash underhand' suggests illicit money, adding corruption absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use 'this man with more ready cash than he knows what to do with.'

highlights.text: Anyway, the store owned by this man with more than enough cash underhand is one of those very rare, local-contact type stores that allows an unlimited tab for those who live around it.

records.jp: そういえば、ちょっと喉が渇いたな。
records.en: Speaking of which, my throat is a bit parched.
records.assessment: そういえば means 'come to think of it.' 'Speaking of which' incorrectly treats the previous subject as a conversational segue.
records.remedy: Use 'Come to think of it, I'm a little thirsty.'

highlights.text: Speaking of which, my throat is a bit parched.

records.jp: 店の奥に行って、緑茶のボトルを一本取ってくる。
records.en: I go into the depths of the store, and take out one bottle of green tea.
records.assessment: 店の奥 is the back of the store. 'The depths of the store' adds exaggerated spatial imagery.
records.remedy: Use 'I go to the back of the store and take a bottle of green tea.'

highlights.text: I go into the depths of the store, and take out one bottle of green tea.

records.jp: メモ帳を取り出し、ペンを走らせる。
records.en: Taking out a notebook, I make the pen run.
comments: Same, notes don't seem provided. -GHS
records.assessment: ペンを走らせる simply means he writes quickly. 'Make the pen run' is an opaque literal calque.
records.remedy: Use 'I take out a notepad and start writing.'

highlights.text: Taking out a notebook, I make the pen run.

records.jp: 『９／７、大緑茶、１３０円……黒須太一』
records.en:
9/7
Green King Tea
130￥
Kurosu Taichi
comments: CP CCA0004
records.assessment: The product name 大緑茶 is 'Great/Big Green Tea.' 'Green King Tea' replaces the defining character with an unsupported royal title.
records.remedy: Use 'Great Green Tea.'

highlights.text:
9/7
Green King Tea
130￥
Kurosu Taichi

records.jp: 見ると、もう何枚ものメモが張ってある。
records.en: Looking closer, there are several of these memos are up already.
comments: CP CCA0004
records.assessment: 'There are several of these memos are up' contains two competing finite constructions and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'Looking closer, several memos are already posted there.'

highlights.text: Looking closer, there are several of these memos are up already.

records.jp: 合宿中はいろいろ買いにきてたんだっけ。
records.en: Seems we came here several times to buy things during the Training Camp.
records.assessment: いろいろ says they came to buy various things during camp. 'Several times' changes variety of purchases into frequency of visits.
records.remedy: Use 'We came here to buy all sorts of things during camp.'

highlights.text: Seems we came here several times to buy things during the Training Camp.

records.jp: 皆、麻痺していた。
records.en: All of us simply paralyzed.
records.assessment: The source says everyone was numb or paralyzed. 'All of us simply paralyzed' omits the finite verb and narrows everyone to the narrator's group.
records.remedy: Use 'Everyone was numb.'

highlights.text: All of us simply paralyzed.

records.jp: 棚上げするには重すぎる感情のやりとりが、直前にあったからだ。
records.en: It shelved the exchange of depressing sentiments that was there just moments before.
records.assessment: The source explains that immediately beforehand they had exchanged emotions too weighty to set aside. The English says an unspecified 'it' shelved the exchange and reduces the weight to depressing sentiment.
records.remedy: Use 'Just before that, we'd had an emotional exchange too heavy to put aside.'

highlights.text: It shelved the exchange of depressing sentiments that was there just moments before.

records.jp: 遮断されていた人の気配が溢れて、さらりと頬を撫でた。
records.en: The presence of a blockade of a person overflows and smoothly brush my cheeks.
records.assessment: The source says the pent-up presence of people spills out and lightly brushes his cheek. 'The presence of a blockade of a person' treats 遮断 as a blockade belonging to one person and fails subject-verb agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'The pent-up presence of people spills out and lightly brushes my cheek.'

highlights.text: The presence of a blockade of a person overflows and smoothly brush my cheeks.

records.jp: 立て肘をついて座っている少女が、ちらと一瞥をよこす。
records.en: there sat a girl, with her elbow on the table, sends a single peeking glance my way.
comments: CP CCA0004
records.assessment: The source says a seated girl with her elbow propped gives him a fleeting glance. The English mixes 'there sat' with present 'sends' and adds a table not specified.
records.remedy: Use 'A girl sits with her elbow propped and flicks a glance my way.'

highlights.text: there sat a girl, with her elbow on the table, sends a single peeking glance my way.

records.jp: それは神経質なほどの手入れによって保たれている、危うい整然。
records.en: A systematicness that speaks of insecurity, maintained through a care at the limits of neurosis.
records.assessment: The source calls the order of her hair precarious, maintained by almost neurotically meticulous care. 'Systematicness that speaks of insecurity' changes precarious order into psychological insecurity and uses unnatural abstractions.
records.remedy: Use 'A precarious order maintained by almost neurotically meticulous care.'

highlights.text: A systematicness that speaks of insecurity, maintained through a care at the limits of neurosis.

records.jp: 触れると軽く、指で梳けばさらさらと砂のように流れる。
records.en: Hers is a hair that with the lightest of touches sinks and slides through the fingers as if sand.
records.assessment: The source says the hair feels light and flows like sand when fingers comb through it. 'With the lightest of touches sinks' invents sinking and does not express the hair's lightness.
records.remedy: Use 'It feels light, and when I comb it with my fingers it flows like sand.'

highlights.text: Hers is a hair that with the lightest of touches sinks and slides through the fingers as if sand.

records.jp: 近寄りがたい雰囲気という、見えない甲冑。
records.en: A mood of difficult approachability that turned into helmet and armor unseen.
records.assessment: The source apposes an invisible suit of armor: her unapproachable air. The English says a mood turned into armor, adds a helmet, and uses the unnatural phrase 'difficult approachability.'
records.remedy: Use 'An invisible suit of armor made of an unapproachable air.'

highlights.text: A mood of difficult approachability that turned into helmet and armor unseen.

records.jp: 理由はいろいろあったのだろう。
records.en: A variety of reasons, of course.
records.assessment: The source says there were probably various reasons. The fragment 'A variety of reasons, of course' omits the uncertainty and supplies unwarranted certainty.
records.remedy: Use 'There were probably all sorts of reasons.'

highlights.text: A variety of reasons, of course.

records.jp: ここが群青学院であること。
records.en: What we have here, at Gunjou Institute,
records.assessment: This is one item in the list of reasons: that this place is Gunjou Academy. 'What we have here, at Gunjou Institute' changes the proposition and produces a broken continuation into the next line.
records.remedy: Use 'The fact that this was Gunjou Academy.'

highlights.text: What we have here, at Gunjou Institute,

records.jp: まともに会話が成立する者など、数えるほどしかいない。
records.en:
The ones who can even establish the most basic
and upfront of conversations are but a handful.
comments: See CCA0011C -GHS
records.assessment: まともに means properly or coherently. 'The most basic and upfront of conversations' adds a superlative and an unrelated claim of frankness.
records.remedy: Use 'Only a handful of people could hold a coherent conversation.'

highlights.text:
The ones who can even establish the most basic
and upfront of conversations are but a handful.

records.jp: 屍の山に、ゼンマイ仕掛けの玩具を放り込んだが如く、悪辣な世界観。
records.en:
It's a horrifying view of the world, that
resembles a wind-up toy's as released into
a mountain of corpses.
records.assessment: The source calls the worldview vicious, like throwing a wind-up toy into a mountain of corpses. 'Horrifying' changes the judgment, and 'a wind-up toy's as released' is syntactically broken.
records.remedy: Use 'A vicious worldview, like a wind-up toy tossed onto a mountain of corpses.'

highlights.text:
It's a horrifying view of the world, that
resembles a wind-up toy's as released into
a mountain of corpses.

records.jp: 適応係数４６、桐原冬子がその中で生きるには、残された５４％を守るものが必要だった。
records.en: With a Conformity Coefficient of 46, for Kirihara Touko to live in that midst, defending the remaining 54% is a necessity.
comments: 46+54=100 I AM ON TO SOMETHING I JUST DON'T KNOW WHAT -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Touko needed something to protect the remaining fifty-four percent. 'Defending the remaining 54% is a necessity' removes Touko as the experiencer and is awkwardly nominal.
records.remedy: Use 'Touko needed something to protect the remaining fifty-four percent.'

highlights.text: With a Conformity Coefficient of 46, for Kirihara Touko to live in that midst, defending the remaining 54% is a necessity.

records.jp: 他者を疎外することで、保たれる自意識。
records.en: A preservation of self-consciousness maintained through the alienation from others.
records.assessment: The source says her self-awareness is preserved by her alienating other people. 'Alienation from others' can instead mean that others alienate her, erasing her agency.
records.remedy: Use 'A sense of self preserved by shutting others out.'

highlights.text: A preservation of self-consciousness maintained through the alienation from others.

records.jp: それが桐原冬子という人物の全てと言えた。
records.en: Those were all the words that could be said about the personality that is Kirihara Touko.
records.assessment: The source says those traits could be called everything there was to Kirihara Touko as a person. The English changes that claim into one about all words that could be said about her personality.
records.remedy: Use 'That could be said to be everything Kirihara Touko was.'

highlights.text: Those were all the words that could be said about the personality that is Kirihara Touko.

records.jp: 視線が窓の外に投じられる。
records.en: Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window,
records.assessment: The source says she directs her gaze outside the window. 'Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window' substitutes the faculty of sight and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'She casts her gaze out the window,'

highlights.text: Her eyesight is thrown to outside of the window,

records.jp: そらぞらしいほどのタイミングで。
records.en: with a timing that is hypocritically false.
records.assessment: そらぞらしい describes timing so pointedly feigned or artificial that it is obvious. 'Hypocritically false' assigns moral hypocrisy and does not describe the staged timing.
records.remedy: Use 'with almost comically artificial timing.'

highlights.text: with a timing that is hypocritically false.

records.jp: 無視する気まんまんだ。
records.en: Full to the brim with a desire to ignore.
comments: Intentional desire to act all tsun-tsun, rather than simply ignoring to protect herself. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says she is plainly intent on ignoring him. 'Full to the brim with a desire to ignore' is an over-literal, incomplete construction without an object.
records.remedy: Use 'She is clearly determined to ignore me.'

highlights.text: Full to the brim with a desire to ignore.

records.jp: 「しかもまた私服通学か」
records.en: Taichi: "And yet you came to school in normal clothes again?"
comments: CP CCA0004
records.assessment: 私服 means personal or casual clothes in contrast to a school uniform. 'Normal clothes' misses that institutional contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'And you're commuting in casual clothes again?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And yet you came to school in normal clothes again?"

records.jp: 学生が自らを律する必要などない。
records.en: There is no need for students to regulate, judge, or decide for themselves.
comments: expanding. -GHS
records.assessment: 自らを律する means students disciplining themselves. 'Regulate, judge, or decide for themselves' adds two unrelated activities.
records.remedy: Use 'There is no need for students to discipline themselves.'

highlights.text: There is no need for students to regulate, judge, or decide for themselves.

records.jp: だから制服着用という決まり事は、まるで意味をなさない。
records.en: Therefore, the regulatory standard mandating the use of uniforms is entirely ignorable.
records.assessment: The uniform rule is said to have no meaning at all. 'Entirely ignorable' instead says a meaningful rule exists but can be disregarded.
records.remedy: Use 'So the rule requiring uniforms is completely meaningless.'

highlights.text: Therefore, the regulatory standard mandating the use of uniforms is entirely ignorable.

records.jp: いかに天下群青とはいえ、年頃の少女をひんむいて制服に着替えさせるわけにはいかないからだ。
records.en: In this lone Gunjou under the heavens, to force a girl of that age back into the uniform she took off is hopeless beyond all effort.
comments: See CCA0013. -GHS
records.assessment: Even at Gunjou they cannot strip a teenage girl and force her into uniform. The English invents a uniform she previously took off and calls the task hopeless rather than impermissible.
records.remedy: Use 'Even at freewheeling Gunjou, they can't strip a teenage girl and force her into uniform.'

highlights.text: In this lone Gunjou under the heavens, to force a girl of that age back into the uniform she took off is hopeless beyond all effort.

records.jp: うーん。
records.en: Yee-ep.
records.assessment: うーん is a thoughtful or doubtful hum. 'Yep' turns it into agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'Hmm.'

highlights.text: Yee-ep.

records.jp: 冬子はこんな状態でいるのが、もっとも絵になるわけで。
records.en: The more Touko stays just like this, the more like a picture she becomes.
comments: See CCA0014B, CCA0023, the fact that this is a CG -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Touko is most picturesque in this state. 'The more she stays ... the more' invents a progressive comparative relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Touko is at her most picturesque like this.'

highlights.text: The more Touko stays just like this, the more like a picture she becomes.

records.jp: 俺は隣に座って、じっと横顔を見つめた。
records.en: I sat her neighbor, and motionlessly gazed at her profile.
records.assessment: The source says he sits beside her. 'I sat her neighbor' is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'I sat beside her and gazed steadily at her profile.'

highlights.text: I sat her neighbor, and motionlessly gazed at her profile.

records.jp: 飽くことなく、ずっと。
records.en: Insatiably, for a long time.
comments: See CCA0010 -GHS
records.assessment: 飽くことなく means without tiring or ever growing bored. 'Insatiably' suggests appetite or desire rather than sustained attention.
records.remedy: Use 'Without ever tiring, for a long time.'

highlights.text: Insatiably, for a long time.

records.jp: いきり立った。
records.en: The rage shoots upwards.
records.assessment: The source says she bristled or became furious. 'The rage shoots upwards' is an unnatural literal image and shifts to present.
records.remedy: Use 'She bristled.'

highlights.text: The rage shoots upwards.

records.jp: 「こら、芸術品が喋るな」
records.en: Taichi: "Come on, paintings should not be talking."
records.assessment: Taichi calls Touko an artwork, singular. 'Paintings should not be talking' changes the object and number.
records.remedy: Use 'Hey, artworks aren't supposed to talk.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Come on, paintings should not be talking."

records.jp: 「おまえは語尾が～だわ、とか～ですわ、とかオバサン臭いんだからあんま喋るなよイメージが崩れる」
records.en: Taichi: "You always drop in affectations like 'shan't' or 'mayhap' that stink of grandmother, so don't talk too much or your image will crumble."
comments: Intentionally literal for imagery. FWIW, she'll use a ～だわ in CCD2002, and the only ～ですわ so far was in his hallucination in CCA0002 (plus the one below). -GHS
records.assessment: He mocks her feminine sentence endings だわ and ですわ as sounding like an older woman. 'Shan't' and 'mayhap' are unrelated archaic vocabulary, and 'grandmother' exaggerates オバサン.
records.remedy: Use equivalent affected feminine or old-fashioned sentence endings without changing the words' content.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You always drop in affectations like 'shan't' or 'mayhap' that stink of grandmother, so don't talk too much or your image will crumble."

records.jp: 「ぬぁんですってーっ！？」
records.en: Touko: "WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID?!?"
comments: lisp + angrish = plausibility (or at least plausible deniability) -GHS
records.assessment: 'WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID' is not grammatical English and does not form the intended slurred 'What did you say?!'
records.remedy: Use a distorted but intelligible 'WHAAAT DID YOU SAAAAY?!'

highlights.text: Touko: "WHAASSS'D YOU SAAAAID?!?"

records.jp: ダメだこりゃ。
records.en: It's deeead.
records.assessment: ダメだこりゃ means 'this is hopeless/no good.' 'It's dead' assigns literal death instead.
records.remedy: Use 'This is hopeless.'

highlights.text: It's deeead.

records.jp: ぬぁんですってーとか言い出したよ。
records.en: She actually uttered "whas'd you said".
records.assessment: The narration quotes her distorted 'What did you say?' The embedded 'whas'd you said' is ungrammatical beyond the source's phonetic distortion.
records.remedy: Use an intelligible distorted form of 'what did you say.'

highlights.text: She actually uttered "whas'd you said".

records.jp: 芸術の終焉だった。
records.en: This is the demise of a work of fine arts.
records.assessment: The source says it was the end of art. The English changes to present and adds 'a work of fine arts.'
records.remedy: Use 'It was the end of art.'

highlights.text: This is the demise of a work of fine arts.

records.jp: 「フー、興ざめだな」
records.en: Taichi: "Awww, whatta killjoy."
records.assessment: 興ざめ describes the mood being spoiled or a turnoff. 'Whatta killjoy' labels Touko herself as a person who spoils fun.
records.remedy: Use 'What a turnoff.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Awww, whatta killjoy."

records.jp: 世界正義という強圧的な概念とともにキレイさっぱり根絶されたであろう米国人のように、肩をすくめてみせた。
records.en: I made display of a shrug similar to that of an American that fears himself thoroughly eradicated alongside the coercive concept known as the righteousness of the world.
comments: This doesn't make much sense...? PS2 version calls it simply "exaggerated". -GHS
records.assessment: The source compares his shrug to an American who would have been eradicated along with coercive 'world justice.' The English says the American merely fears his own eradication and is syntactically tangled.
records.remedy: Use 'I shrugged like an American who would have been wiped out along with the coercive idea of world justice.'

highlights.text: I made display of a shrug similar to that of an American that fears himself thoroughly eradicated alongside the coercive concept known as the righteousness of the world.

records.jp: 「おまえに芸術の破壊者という二つ名を与える」
records.en: Taichi: "I bestow you the second name of, Destroyer of Arts."
records.assessment: 二つ名 means an epithet or sobriquet, not a literal second name. 'Bestow you' also lacks the required preposition.
records.remedy: Use 'I bestow on you the epithet Destroyer of Art.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I bestow you the second name of, Destroyer of Arts."

records.jp: 「よかったな。ピカソもそんなこと言われてたぞ。またすごいのとならんだな」
records.en: Taichi: "It's to be happy, too. Picasso himself was called the same. No finer thing on the same level as it."
comments: http://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1988/06/picasso-creator-and-destroyer/305715/?single_page=true as far as I could find this is the only instance. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Picasso was called the same thing and congratulates her on joining another great figure. The English is syntactically incoherent and does not express the comparison.
records.remedy: Use 'Good for you. Picasso was called that too. You're in distinguished company again.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's to be happy, too. Picasso himself was called the same. No finer thing on the same level as it."

records.jp: 「こわいですわ～」
records.en: Taichi: "Giving a fright shan't we～!"
records.assessment: Taichi mockingly imitates her with 'How scary, desuwa.' 'Giving a fright shan't we' changes both the proposition and the mocked ending.
records.remedy: Use an affected 'How frightening, indeed.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Giving a fright shan't we～!"

records.jp: 「ですわなんて言ってないでしょっ！！」
records.en: Touko: "I do not say 'shan't' you know!!!"
records.assessment: Touko protests that she never says ですわ. Translating that ending as the lexical verb 'shan't' makes her deny a word she never used.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't say “desuwa”!' or an equivalent denial of the affected ending.

highlights.text: Touko: "I do not say 'shan't' you know!!!"

records.jp: 「そうエクスクラメイションマークを二つセットでばかり使うなよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't just use sets of three exclamation marks!"
comments: Adapted because two exclamation marks don't look right in English. This is true because of the following: !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!, whereas !=what I said is true. -GHS
records.assessment: The source explicitly says she keeps using exclamation marks in pairs of two. The English says sets of three.
records.remedy: Use 'Stop using exclamation marks two at a time.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't just use sets of three exclamation marks!"

records.jp: 「ぷっぷくぷー」
records.en: Taichi: "Pffft heheheheh..."
records.assessment: ぷっぷくぷー is a comic trumpet-like vocal sound. 'Pffft heheheheh' turns it into laughter and loses the sound effect.
records.remedy: Use a playful trumpet sound such as 'Pup-puku-puu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Pffft heheheheh..."

records.jp: 「バカにしてんのっ！？　バカにしてるのよね！　バカにしてーーーーーっ！！」
records.en: Touko: "You making fun of me?! You making fun of me! YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN!!!"
records.assessment: The final repetition still means 'You're making fun of me.' 'YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN' drops the required object and preposition.
records.remedy: Use 'YOU'RE MAKING FUN OF MEEEE!'

highlights.text: Touko: "You making fun of me?! You making fun of me! YOU MAKING FUUUUUUN!!!"

records.jp: 「よく燃える」
records.en: Taichi: "Look who's burning."
comments: vs. 'yoku iu' -GHS
records.assessment: よく燃える observes that she flares up or burns very well. 'Look who's burning' omits the evaluative よく.
records.remedy: Use 'You flare up so well.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Look who's burning."

comments: Unfortunately, the audio file seems too compressed to recover. -GHS
records.assessment: The source ends the symbol string with repeated small-ts characters, representing a choked consonant. Replacing them with ordinary exclamation marks removes that vocal effect.
records.remedy: Preserve a repeated cut-off consonant before the exclamation marks.

records.jp: うっとりと耳を傾けていると。
records.en: Spellbound I lend my ear to listen closely.
records.assessment: 'Lend my ear to listen closely' redundantly combines two listening idioms and lacks the comma after the fronted modifier.
records.remedy: Use 'As I listen, spellbound,'

highlights.text: Spellbound I lend my ear to listen closely.

records.jp: 冬子の右手が霞んだ。
records.en: Touko's right hand had grown blurry.
records.assessment: Her hand blurs from sudden motion in the narrative moment. 'Had grown blurry' makes it an earlier completed visual state rather than rapid movement.
records.remedy: Use 'Touko's right hand blurred.'

highlights.text: Touko's right hand had grown blurry.

records.jp: 叩き倒される。
records.en: Strike-induced fall.
records.assessment: The source says he is struck and knocked down. 'Strike-induced fall' replaces the event and victim with a clinical noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'The blow knocks me down.'

highlights.text: Strike-induced fall.

records.jp: 座る者のない机と椅子を巻き込んで、盛大にすっ転んだ。
records.en: A grand, magnificent fall that drags in even unoccupied chairs and desks.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator tumbles spectacularly, taking desks and chairs with him. The English is a noun fragment whose 'fall' performs the dragging.
records.remedy: Use 'I tumble spectacularly, taking empty desks and chairs with me.'

highlights.text: A grand, magnificent fall that drags in even unoccupied chairs and desks.

records.jp: 「るさいっ！」
records.en: Touko: "'addap!"
comments: Lisp -GHS
records.assessment: るさい is a clipped 'shut up/noisy.' ''addap' is not intelligible English.
records.remedy: Use a clipped 'Shaddap!'

highlights.text: Touko: "'addap!"

records.jp: 顔がひきつった。
records.en: Her face cramped.
records.assessment: 顔がひきつった says her face twitched or stiffened. 'Cramped' describes a muscle spasm and is not idiomatic for facial reaction.
records.remedy: Use 'Her face twitched.'

highlights.text: Her face cramped.

records.jp: 「あ、あ、あ……あんたが……それを……言うわけ？」
records.en: Touko: "Y-, y-, y-... you've really... said... that?"
records.assessment: The source incredulously asks whether Taichi, of all people, is saying that to her. 'You've really said that' loses the accusatory contrast between speaker and statement.
records.remedy: Use 'Y-you... you're the one saying that to me?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Y-, y-, y-... you've really... said... that?"

records.jp: 低くくぐもった声で。
records.en: In a lowering tone of voice.
records.assessment: The source specifies a low, muffled voice. 'A lowering tone' describes a changing pitch and omits muffling.
records.remedy: Use 'In a low, muffled voice.'
