highlights.text: In a lowering tone of voice.

records.jp: 「遙かなる次元を越えて……」
records.en: Touko: "That is just... on a dimension of vulgarity that surpasses..."
comments: Parallel, of course. -GHS
records.assessment: The line says 'crossing far-distant dimensions...' and leads into her command. The English invents a dimension of vulgarity not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'Across dimensions vast and distant...'

highlights.text: Touko: "That is just... on a dimension of vulgarity that surpasses..."

records.jp: めでたく叩き出された。
records.en: Oh joyous forceful expulsion.
comments: her and him -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he was duly or happily thrown out. 'Oh joyous forceful expulsion' is a subjectless noun phrase and drops the completed action.
records.remedy: Use 'And with that, I was cheerfully thrown out.'

highlights.text: Oh joyous forceful expulsion.

records.jp: そこにはきっと、彼女がいるだろう。
records.en: And there I know she will be, for certain.
records.assessment: きっと...だろう expresses strong expectation but retains supposition. 'I know ... for certain' removes that uncertainty.
records.remedy: Use 'She'll surely be there.'

highlights.text: And there I know she will be, for certain.

records.jp: 失敗するとわかっていた合宿。
records.en: The training camp had failed, that I understood.
records.assessment: The source calls it a camp he had known would fail before it happened. 'The training camp had failed, that I understood' relocates the knowledge after the failure.
records.remedy: Use 'A training camp I knew would fail.'

highlights.text: The training camp had failed, that I understood.

records.jp: 無理を言って先輩を駆り出した。
records.en: I asked a big favor, roped in Senpai.
records.assessment: 無理を言って says he made an unreasonable request, not merely a large favor. The English softens his acknowledged imposition.
records.remedy: Use 'I made an unreasonable request and dragged Senpai into it.'

highlights.text: I asked a big favor, roped in Senpai.

records.jp: それが彼女を傷つけることさえ、予想していた。
records.en: That is something, I expected, that would have even wounded her.
records.assessment: He had predicted even that it would hurt her. 'Would have even wounded' introduces a counterfactual perfect and inserts disruptive commas.
records.remedy: Use 'I had even expected that it would hurt her.'

highlights.text: That is something, I expected, that would have even wounded her.

records.jp: 予想していたけど、考えないようにして。
records.en: Expected, but not really thought about.
records.assessment: The source says he expected it but deliberately tried not to think about it. The subjectless passive 'not really thought about' omits his intentional avoidance.
records.remedy: Use 'I expected it, but tried not to think about it.'

highlights.text: Expected, but not really thought about.

records.jp: そして今また、彼女……先輩を利用しようとしている。
records.en: And now, again, she... Senpai's going to be used.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator is now trying to use Senpai again. 'Senpai's going to be used' removes his agency and changes an ongoing intention into passive future fate.
records.remedy: Use 'And now I'm trying to use her—Senpai—again.'

highlights.text: And now, again, she... Senpai's going to be used.

records.jp: 己が心の平安のために。
records.en: For the sake of the peace of a heart.
records.assessment: 己が心 means his own heart or mind. 'A heart' removes the reflexive ownership central to his selfish motive.
records.remedy: Use 'For my own peace of mind.'

highlights.text: For the sake of the peace of a heart.

records.jp: 今さらどの面さげて、と思いもする。
records.en: And I also thought, how could one do this after all that?
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: どの面さげて expresses shameful nerve: how can he show his face now? 'How could one do this' generalizes the subject and changes shame into ability.
records.remedy: Use 'I wonder how I can show my face now.'

highlights.text: And I also thought, how could one do this after all that?

records.jp: 少し気になってしまった。
records.en: That was a little bit worrying.
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: The source says he found himself a little concerned about what she would think. 'That was ... worrying' makes the external fact the worrying thing and loses his involuntary concern.
records.remedy: Use 'I found myself a little concerned.'

highlights.text: That was a little bit worrying.

records.jp: ノブをひねって、鉄扉を押し出す。
records.en: Turning the handle, I push out the iron door.
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: He pushes the metal door open. 'Push out the iron door' suggests moving the door outward as an object rather than opening it.
records.remedy: Use 'I turn the knob and push open the metal door.'

highlights.text: Turning the handle, I push out the iron door.

records.jp: ちょうど踏み出た瞬間に。
records.en: on the exact instant I stepped outside.
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: 'On the exact instant' uses the wrong preposition for a point in time.
records.remedy: Use 'at the exact moment I stepped outside.'

highlights.text: on the exact instant I stepped outside.

records.jp: 目線の先、広々とした給水塔が階段とは別にあって、その土台を共有して、大きなアンテナが立っていた。
records.en: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: The source places the water tower apart from the stairs and the antenna on the same base. The English makes the water tower be 'on the staircase' and tangles which structures share the foundation.
records.remedy: Use 'Ahead, apart from the stairs, stood a broad water tower; a large antenna rose from the same base.'

highlights.text: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.

records.jp: 彼女はそれらを前向きな気持ちでもって補いながら、少しずつ形にしてきた。
records.en: Yet little by little it was taking shape, as that insufficiency was being supplemented by proactive feelings,
comments: PCP CCA0006
records.assessment: The source says she actively compensated for missing parts and knowledge with optimism and gradually gave the antenna form. The passive English removes her agency and calls her feelings merely 'proactive.'
records.remedy: Use 'She made up for what was missing with optimism and gradually brought it into shape.'

highlights.text: Yet little by little it was taking shape, as that insufficiency was being supplemented by proactive feelings,

records.jp: 後ろ向きの気持ち、なのかもしれない。
records.en: They might just be pessimistic feelings, perhaps.
records.assessment: 後ろ向きの気持ち corrects the preceding positive feelings to possibly negative ones. 'They' can refer to the missing parts and knowledge, obscuring the corrected subject.
records.remedy: Use 'Or perhaps those feelings were negative.'

highlights.text: They might just be pessimistic feelings, perhaps.

records.jp: そういうことは、往々にしてあるのだから。
records.en: Because that is is something that happens from time to time.
records.assessment: 'That is is' duplicates the finite verb.
records.remedy: Use 'Because that sort of thing often happens.'

highlights.text: Because that is is something that happens from time to time.

records.jp: 部活はその逃避する最後の砦だったことを、俺は知っている。
records.en: Club activities have always been the final stronghold of her flight, this I know.
records.assessment: The club was her final refuge for escape. 'Stronghold of her flight' uses flight as physical fleeing and obscures psychological refuge.
records.remedy: Use 'I know the club was her last refuge from reality.'

highlights.text: Club activities have always been the final stronghold of her flight, this I know.

records.jp: そして今また、部活は逃避の砦のままである。
records.en: And now, again, here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities.
records.assessment: The source says the club remains a refuge for escape even now. 'Here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities' is syntactically broken and fails to identify club activities.
records.remedy: Use 'And even now, the club remains her refuge.'

highlights.text: And now, again, here she is in the stronghold of her flight that are activities.

records.jp: 呼びかけると、扇状の毛髪が大きくうねる。
records.en: I called out to her, and the fan shape of her twisted about grandiosely.
comments: PCP CCA0006
I'm not sure what's the proper name for this hairstyle. The one time the exhaustive traits in VNDB would've been useful... *grumble*. Notice the lack of black hair now. Hmmm. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says her fan-shaped hair billows dramatically when he calls. The English omits 'hair' after 'fan shape of her' and substitutes twisting for billowing.
records.remedy: Use 'When I call out, her fan-shaped hair billows broadly.'

highlights.text: I called out to her, and the fan shape of her twisted about grandiosely.

records.jp: 耳を澄ませば、彼女だけが呼ぶ俺の名が届く。
records.en: If I strain my ears towards all that she is, the nickname for her only personal use is conveyed,
comments: dat if. Also 耳+澄 = mimi + second character of her last name. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that if he listens closely, the name only she calls him reaches his ears. 'Towards all that she is' is invented, and 'nickname for her only personal use is conveyed' is an opaque calque.
records.remedy: Use 'Listening closely, I hear the name only she uses for me.'

highlights.text: If I strain my ears towards all that she is, the nickname for her only personal use is conveyed,

records.jp: 幸せな錯覚というやつだ。
records.en: It's something of a delusion of happiness.
records.assessment: 幸せな錯覚 is a happy or fortunate illusion. 'A delusion of happiness' makes happiness the illusion's content instead of its quality.
records.remedy: Use 'It was a happy illusion.'

highlights.text: It's something of a delusion of happiness.

records.jp: そのたもとに歩み寄る。
records.en: I step nearer to the infrastructure.
records.assessment: そのたもと means he walks to her side or nearby base. 'Infrastructure' is an unrelated technical sense and removes the person he approaches.
records.remedy: Use 'I walk over to her side.'

highlights.text: I step nearer to the infrastructure.

records.jp: 俺も自然、ほころぶ。
records.en: I too, naturally, begin to discompose the edges of the lips.
comments: See CCE0001, his smile and hers are equally fake. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he naturally breaks into a smile too. 'Begin to discompose the edges of the lips' is unintelligible and does not state smiling.
records.remedy: Use 'I naturally break into a smile too.'

highlights.text: I too, naturally, begin to discompose the edges of the lips.

records.jp: 視線が睦み合うほどに継がれる。
records.en: The glances inherit harmoniousness.
comments: Suspiciously purple... -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes their gazes meeting and remaining joined in mutual warmth. 'The glances inherit harmoniousness' assigns an unrelated inheritance relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Our gazes meet and linger in mutual affection.'

highlights.text: The glances inherit harmoniousness.

records.jp: こういうのが一番たまらないよ！
records.en: That is the most unbearable of all!
records.assessment: たまらない is positive here: this is the most irresistible or exciting kind of glimpse. 'Unbearable' can mean intolerably unpleasant and reverses the enthusiasm.
records.remedy: Use 'This is the most irresistible kind!'

highlights.text: That is the most unbearable of all!

records.jp: パンチランド共和国、建国万歳！
records.en:
Banzai for the founding of the Commonwealth of
Panchiralandia!
records.assessment: The invented state is the Republic of Punchland. 'Commonwealth' changes the form of government and 'Panchiralandia' replaces the source's place-name joke.
records.remedy: Use 'Long live the founding of the Republic of Punchland!'

highlights.text:
Banzai for the founding of the Commonwealth of
Panchiralandia!

records.jp: 素晴らしき国！
records.en: A wonderful country that one!
records.assessment: 'A wonderful country that one' lacks the punctuation and word order needed for the emphatic afterthought.
records.remedy: Use 'What a wonderful country!'

highlights.text: A wonderful country that one!

records.jp: しまった、また意識が飛んでしまった。
records.en: Dammit, again my awareness damnably flew away.
comments: shimatta x2 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his consciousness slipped away again. Repeating 'dammit/damnably' adds emphasis and 'my awareness flew away' is an awkward calque.
records.remedy: Use 'Damn, I zoned out again.'

highlights.text: Dammit, again my awareness damnably flew away.

records.jp: その方がええです。
records.en: And that is most fine.
records.assessment: その方がええです means it is better that way. 'That is most fine' is unnatural and changes a comparative judgment into generic approval.
records.remedy: Use 'That's probably for the best.'

highlights.text: And that is most fine.

records.jp: 「あ、わかりました。サボりですね」
records.en: Misato: "Ah, I understand. Cutting are you!"
records.assessment: She realizes he is skipping class. 'Cutting are you' is ungrammatical and omits the object needed by 'cutting.'
records.remedy: Use 'Ah, I understand. You're cutting class.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Ah, I understand. Cutting are you!"

records.jp: なんてこった。
records.en: What even the hell.
records.assessment: なんてこった is 'what a mess/what the hell.' 'What even the hell' is malformed and adds an unsupported discourse filler.
records.remedy: Use 'What the hell.'

highlights.text: What even the hell.

records.jp: いつもの彼女だった。
records.en: That was the her of always.
records.assessment: The source says she was her usual self. 'The her of always' is an opaque nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use 'She was her usual self.'

highlights.text: That was the her of always.

records.jp: 正気に、常軌を。
records.en: In the proper course of soundness of her mind,
records.assessment: Together with the next fragment, the source says she had strayed from sanity and the ordinary course. 'In the proper course of soundness of her mind' instead places her within sanity and is syntactically incomplete.
records.remedy: Use 'From sanity, from the ordinary course,'

highlights.text: In the proper course of soundness of her mind,

records.jp: 逸していた。
records.en: there was a derailment.
records.assessment: 逸していた completes that she had strayed. 'There was a derailment' replaces her action/state with an abstract event.
records.remedy: Use 'she had strayed.'

highlights.text: there was a derailment.

records.jp: 彼女が漏らした言葉から受けた印象は、当たった。
records.en: the impression that I got out of the words that came out of her was correct.
records.assessment: The source says the impression he received from her words was correct. 'Got out of the words that came out of her' is redundant and unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use 'The impression I'd taken from her words was correct.'

highlights.text: the impression that I got out of the words that came out of her was correct.

records.jp: 『明日、部活がありますから』
records.en: Misato: 『Tomorrow we do have club activities.』
records.assessment: The English quotation retains Japanese corner brackets instead of the dialogue quotation style used by the translation.
records.remedy: Use English quotation marks around the recalled line.

highlights.text: Misato: 『Tomorrow we do have club activities.』

records.jp: 「夏休みも終わって新学期、気が抜けたコ○コーラみたいな気持ちを引きずっていてはいけません」
records.en: Misato: "This is a new term right after the end of Summer break, you cannot trail behind feeling like a C**a Cola with all the bubbles gone!"
records.assessment: The source warns against dragging along a flat-cola-like feeling into the new term. 'Trail behind feeling like a cola' reverses what trails what and is grammatically malformed.
records.remedy: Use 'You mustn't drag that flat-cola feeling into the new term.'

highlights.text: Misato: "This is a new term right after the end of Summer break, you cannot trail behind feeling like a C**a Cola with all the bubbles gone!"

records.jp: 「うまずたゆまず姿勢を正して授業にそして課外活動に励むのが、日本男児の美徳というものでありましょう」
records.en: Misato: "Tirelessly persist in maintaining a straightened self and approach curricular and extracurricular activities with zeal, for those are the virtues of a Son of Japan!"
records.assessment: 姿勢を正して means straighten one's posture or attitude. 'Maintaining a straightened self' is an unnatural abstraction, and the sentence mishandles the exhortation's syntax.
records.remedy: Use 'Tirelessly straighten your posture and devote yourself to classes and extracurricular activities.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Tirelessly persist in maintaining a straightened self and approach curricular and extracurricular activities with zeal, for those are the virtues of a Son of Japan!"

records.jp: 呆けた者が、傍目の印象に反して幸福であるように。
records.en: Engrossed to the point of befuddlement, as if repelling all views from the outside made only happiness remain.
records.assessment: The source compares her to an absent-minded person who is happy despite how they look to others. The English instead says repelling outside views causes happiness and substitutes engrossment for vacant befuddlement.
records.remedy: Use 'Like a vacant fool who is happy despite how they look to others.'

highlights.text: Engrossed to the point of befuddlement, as if repelling all views from the outside made only happiness remain.

records.jp: 「とはいえ、初日に授業があるわけでもありませんし、これくらいにしておいてあげます」
records.en: Misato: "Having said that, as in the very first day classes are not held, I will leave the reprimand with this."
comments: So now it's not half day, it's no day at all. I wonder if classes are not actually held on Monday. Not that it matters if it's like 1AM. -GHS
records.assessment: She says there are no classes on the first day, so she will let him off at that. 'As in the very first day' is ungrammatical, and 'the reprimand' is an added noun.
records.remedy: Use 'Still, there aren't classes on the first day, so I'll let you off with that.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Having said that, as in the very first day classes are not held, I will leave the reprimand with this."

records.jp: 誰彼にとって望む自分が、常に高潔であるとは限らない。
records.en: The self desired by so many is not necessarily confined to someone of a consistent pure nobility.
records.assessment: The source says the self any given person desires is not always noble. 'Desired by so many' changes individual variation into mass popularity and 'confined to someone' obscures the predicate.
records.remedy: Use 'The self each person desires is not always noble.'

highlights.text: The self desired by so many is not necessarily confined to someone of a consistent pure nobility.

records.jp: 価値観を人にを強いるほど、俺が偉いわけでもない。
records.en: The degree of force used to impose values on other is not what makes me great.
comments: See CCD1001 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he is not so superior that he can impose his values on others. The English instead says the amount of force used does not make him great and uses the ungrammatical singular 'other.'
records.remedy: Use 'I'm not so great that I can force my values on other people.'

highlights.text: The degree of force used to impose values on other is not what makes me great.

records.jp: 許容して、協力しよう。
records.en: I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate,
records.assessment: The source resolves to accept and help with her escape. 'I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate' makes acceptance an act of permission and changes cooperation into a mutual future action.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll accept it and help her escape.'

highlights.text: I shall permit it, and we shall cooperate,

records.jp: 彼女の逃避に。
records.en: in her flight of escape.
records.assessment: The source's 逃避 is psychological escape. 'Flight of escape' is redundant and suggests physical fleeing.
records.remedy: Use 'with her escape.'

highlights.text: in her flight of escape.

records.jp: 「それに、実はわたしもサボリです」
records.en: Misato: "Still, the truth is that I am cutting too."
records.assessment: サボリ means she is skipping or playing hooky too. 'I am cutting too' omits the object 'class' and is incomplete.
records.remedy: Use 'Actually, I'm playing hooky too.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Still, the truth is that I am cutting too."

records.jp: 先輩は小さく舌を出す。
records.en: Senpai thrust a little tongue out in a cute teh-heh fashion.
records.assessment: The source only says she sticks out her tongue slightly. 'In a cute teh-heh fashion' adds an explicit performance and judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai sticks out her tongue a little.'

highlights.text: Senpai thrust a little tongue out in a cute teh-heh fashion.

records.jp: 俺は渾身の意志で、己に命じた。
records.en: This is a command to the self, that I give with all the might of my volition:
records.assessment: The source says the narrator commanded himself with all his will. 'This is a command to the self, that I give' shifts to present and is syntactically cumbersome.
records.remedy: Use 'With all my will, I commanded myself:'

highlights.text: This is a command to the self, that I give with all the might of my volition:

records.jp: 「ぎゃふんっ」
records.en: Taichi: "Mine is the silence of agreement."
comments: That's what that means. -GHS
records.assessment: ぎゃふん is a comic cry of defeat or being silenced. 'Mine is the silence of agreement' replaces the utterance with a formal abstract declaration.
records.remedy: Use a comic defeated cry such as 'Gyaffun!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Mine is the silence of agreement."

records.jp: 先輩は目を細くする。
records.en: Senpai smiles 'till her eyes squint.
records.assessment: The source says Senpai narrows her eyes. The English adds that she smiles and makes the squint the result of that smile.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai narrows her eyes.'

highlights.text: Senpai smiles 'till her eyes squint.

records.jp: いつもの笑顔。
records.en: The smile of always.
records.assessment: The source simply identifies her usual smile. 'The smile of always' is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'Her usual smile.'

highlights.text: The smile of always.

records.jp: 「ちょっとお待ちください」
records.en: Misato: "Please be patient some more."
comments: PCP CCA0006
Not shouted, because, uhm, how does she stay above and still talk, and, uhm SYMBOLISM? -GHS
records.assessment: ちょっとお待ちください asks him to wait a moment. 'Please be patient some more' implies he has already waited and requests an attitude rather than a brief pause.
records.remedy: Use 'Please wait a moment.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Please be patient some more."

records.jp: 彼女の爪先が床を踏む頃には、もとどおりの二人。
records.en: By the time the tip of her toes had touched the floor, it was as normal for us both.
comments: Curiously, no version has any graphical change at this point whatsoever. -GHS
records.assessment: By the time her toes touch the floor, the two of them are back to their usual selves. 'It was as normal for us both' is ungrammatical and fails to state restoration.
records.remedy: Use 'By the time her toes touch the floor, we're back to our usual selves.'

highlights.text: By the time the tip of her toes had touched the floor, it was as normal for us both.

records.jp: 先輩も何かわけのわからない構えを取る。
records.en: Senpai also takes the stance of something with a meaning I couldn't comprehend.
comments: dat also. See CCA0016, CCA0019. What a nice family portrait. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Senpai also adopts some incomprehensible stance. 'The stance of something with a meaning' changes the stance itself into an object belonging to something.
records.remedy: Use 'Senpai assumes some equally incomprehensible stance.'

highlights.text: Senpai also takes the stance of something with a meaning I couldn't comprehend.

records.jp: 「スク水からアンスコまで、黒須太一はあなたの部活ライフをいやらしくサポートします！」
records.en: Taichi: "From school swimsuits 'till the plain underwear worn over panties in sports (bloomers), Kurosu Taichi will offer his disgustingly lascivious support to your Club Activity Life!"
comments: http://d.hatena.ne.jp/keyword/%A5%A2%A5%F3%A5%B9%A5%B3 -GHS
records.assessment: アンスコ is a compact term for athletic undershorts. The English inserts a long explanatory parenthesis into spoken dialogue, calls them plain underwear over panties, and disrupts the boast's rhythm.
records.remedy: Use a concise term such as 'athletic undershorts' without an in-dialogue gloss.

highlights.text: Taichi: "From school swimsuits 'till the plain underwear worn over panties in sports (bloomers), Kurosu Taichi will offer his disgustingly lascivious support to your Club Activity Life!"

records.jp: 「想像するだにめまいがしますね！」
records.en: Misato: "I am getting the giddies from imagining that!"
comments: 'giddies' seems so wrong -GHS
records.assessment: The source says merely imagining it makes her dizzy. 'The giddies' is not standard English and can suggest excitement rather than vertigo.
records.remedy: Use 'Just imagining it makes me dizzy!'

highlights.text: Misato: "I am getting the giddies from imagining that!"

records.jp: 「恐悦！」
records.en: Taichi: "A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I!"
comments: Visuals -GHS
records.assessment: 恐悦 is a terse, mock-formal 'I am delighted/honored.' 'A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I' is ungrammatical and misreads the first character as terror.
records.remedy: Use 'I am honored!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "A terrifying rejoice of delight is in I!"

records.jp: 「誉めているように聞こえましたか！」
records.en: Misato: "Did you hear that as a compliment now!"
records.assessment: The source asks whether that sounded like praise. 'Did you hear that as a compliment now' is awkward and adds an unsupported 'now.'
records.remedy: Use 'Did that sound like a compliment to you?!'

highlights.text: Misato: "Did you hear that as a compliment now!"

records.jp: 「さあ、オイル塗りからバストマッサージ、野いちご狩りまで幅広くこなすこの愛肉奴隷めに、なんなりとお命じください」
records.en: Taichi: "Indeed, from a oil-coated bust massage to wild strawberry hunting, your worthless meat-love slave has a wide range of uses, so order however you please!"
comments: Misato's nipples, see CCA0016 -GHS
records.assessment: The source lists oiling, bust massage, and wild-strawberry picking as separate services. 'From a oil-coated bust massage' combines the first two and uses the wrong article.
records.remedy: Use 'From oiling to bust massage to wild-strawberry picking...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeed, from a oil-coated bust massage to wild strawberry hunting, your worthless meat-love slave has a wide range of uses, so order however you please!"

records.jp: 幸いなることに、先輩はにっこり微笑んだ。
records.en: Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling broadly.
records.assessment: The source says fortunately Senpai smiled. 'Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling' is an ungrammatical present-tense exclamation.
records.remedy: Use 'Fortunately, Senpai smiled brightly.'

highlights.text: Oh joyful event then, that Senpai is just smiling broadly.

records.jp: 「ここからいなくなれ」
records.en: Misato: "Be ye forever gone from this place!"
records.assessment: The source bluntly says 'Get out of here.' 'Be ye forever gone' adds permanence and an archaic biblical register not present in her line.
records.remedy: Use 'Get out of here.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Be ye forever gone from this place!"

records.jp: 「中国株に手を出したのが凋落のはじまりだったーっ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "The moment I put my hands on that Chinese stock was the start of my life's ruiiin!!!"
comments: Number one in a series that I shall name, "Taichi the Failed Speculator" -GHS
records.assessment: 中国株 is Chinese stocks as a category. 'That Chinese stock' invents one particular share.
records.remedy: Use 'Getting into Chinese stocks was the beginning of my downfall!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The moment I put my hands on that Chinese stock was the start of my life's ruiiin!!!"

records.jp: フェンスの向こうに広がる無垢なる青空に生々しいことを叫んだ。
records.en: I make my rawly graphic shout towards that everexpanding everpure blue sky on the other side of the fence.
records.assessment: The source says he shouted something painfully real or vulgar at the pure sky. The English shifts to present, invents repeated 'ever' modifiers, and uses the nonstandard 'rawly.'
records.remedy: Use 'I shouted that painfully real thing at the pure blue sky beyond the fence.'

highlights.text: I make my rawly graphic shout towards that everexpanding everpure blue sky on the other side of the fence.

records.jp: 「アンテナ、だいぶ形になりましたね」
records.en: Taichi: "The antenna seems to have mostly taken shape, has it."
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: The source observes that the antenna has taken shape considerably. The tag 'has it' after 'seems' is malformed and weakens the direct observation.
records.remedy: Use 'The antenna has really taken shape.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The antenna seems to have mostly taken shape, has it."

records.jp: 世界が滅亡したくらいでは壊れません。
records.en: Even with the Fall of the World it did not break.
comments: See at the top. The end of all people is not exactly at the top of the list of reasons it would break. This is another transparent contradiction. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says even the world ending would not break their bond. 'Did not break' makes it a completed past test, while 'Fall of the World' turns destruction into an abstract title.
records.remedy: Use 'Even the end of the world won't break it.'

highlights.text: Even with the Fall of the World it did not break.

records.jp: 「……まだ全然なんですよ、これが」
records.en: Misato: "...not at all yet, it is not."
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: 'Not at all yet, it is not' duplicates the negative predicate and uses broken inversion.
records.remedy: Use '...Not even close yet.'

highlights.text: Misato: "...not at all yet, it is not."

records.jp: 「専門家じゃありませんし、だましだまし組み立ててます」
records.en: Misato: "I am not a specialist, but by hook or by crook I am putting it together."
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: だましだまし means coaxing the work along or improvising. 'By hook or by crook' suggests unscrupulous means.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm no specialist, so I'm feeling my way through the assembly.'

highlights.text: Misato: "I am not a specialist, but by hook or by crook I am putting it together."

records.jp: 「本体はいいとしても、配線や調整は手つかずですし」
records.en: Misato: "The frame may be fine, but I have not laid hand on the wiring or the tuning."
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: 'Have not laid hand on' needs an article or idiomatic plural and is unnatural for untouched technical work.
records.remedy: Use 'I haven't touched the wiring or adjustments yet.'

highlights.text: Misato: "The frame may be fine, but I have not laid hand on the wiring or the tuning."

records.jp: なでっこなでっこ
records.en: Sooooftly, sooooftly.
records.assessment: なでっこなでっこ represents repeated patting or stroking. 'Softly, softly' preserves only manner and omits the action.
records.remedy: Use 'Pat, pat.'

highlights.text: Sooooftly, sooooftly.

records.jp: 頭をなでっこされる。
records.en: My head is sooooftly caressed.
comments: I'm just gonna slooowly back away now. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says his head is patted or stroked. 'Caressed' makes the contact more sensual and does not echo the playful なでっこ.
records.remedy: Use 'She pats my head.'

highlights.text: My head is sooooftly caressed.

records.jp: 喉が鳴る。
records.en: A note from the throat.
records.assessment: The source says his throat makes a sound, suggesting a pleased purr. 'A note from the throat' is a verbless abstraction.
records.remedy: Use 'My throat rumbles contentedly.'

highlights.text: A note from the throat.

records.jp: 「よしよし」
records.en: Misato: "Good boy good."
records.assessment: よしよし is repeated soothing praise, 'good, good.' 'Good boy good' adds 'boy' and reverses the second phrase's word order.
records.remedy: Use 'Good, good.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Good boy good."

records.jp: 「すっごい即物的な俺になっちゃいそうです！」
records.en: Taichi: "I shall become that so very matter-of-factly yes I will!"
records.assessment: 即物的 means crudely materialistic or literal, not matter-of-fact. 'I shall become that so very matter-of-factly yes I will' is also syntactically incoherent.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll turn into an incredibly shallow, materialistic version of myself!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I shall become that so very matter-of-factly yes I will!"

records.jp: 「大衆なんてっ、嫌いっ！」
records.en: Taichi: "General public, blech!"
records.assessment: The source explicitly says 'I hate the masses.' 'General public, blech' conveys disgust but omits the statement of hatred.
records.remedy: Use 'I hate the masses!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "General public, blech!"

records.jp: ちらと見やった先輩の手が、傷だらけなことに気づく。
records.en: I chanced to look closely at Senpai's hands, and they were covered with scratches.
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: 傷だらけ says her hands are covered in wounds or injuries. 'Scratches' narrows and softens the damage.
records.remedy: Use 'I glance at Senpai's hands and notice they are covered in wounds.'

highlights.text: I chanced to look closely at Senpai's hands, and they were covered with scratches.

records.jp: 「みんなでやった方がよくありません？」
records.en: Taichi: "Is the idea of doing it with everybody problematic?"
comments: Well of course it is, the poor lady, group sex proposals so early... -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks whether it would be better to do the work together. 'Is ... problematic?' reverses the polarity and asks whether collaboration is a problem.
records.remedy: Use 'Wouldn't it be better if everyone worked on it together?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Is the idea of doing it with everybody problematic?"

records.jp: 「ホラ、部活ですし。その方が感じ出るかなって」
records.en: Taichi: "Come on, this is club! Would that way not feel better?"
records.assessment: He says it is a club activity and doing it together would make it feel more like one. 'This is club' is ungrammatical, while 'feel better' changes authenticity into comfort.
records.remedy: Use 'It's a club activity, after all. Doing it together would make it feel more like one.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Come on, this is club! Would that way not feel better?"

records.jp: 「で、でもですね、それはさすがにきついのではないかと」
records.en: Misato: "B-, but, now, doing that would indeed be so very hard would it not."
records.assessment: The source tentatively says that would be rather difficult. 'Would indeed be so very hard would it not' piles two predicate structures together.
records.remedy: Use 'B-but wouldn't that be rather difficult?'

highlights.text: Misato: "B-, but, now, doing that would indeed be so very hard would it not."

records.jp: 「やりようですね。そいつを攻略するのにもっとも適切な駒を使えばいいだけのことでありましょう」
records.en: Taichi: "There are ways. Capturing those guys merely requires making use of the most suitable pieces."
comments: Very specific term for Capture. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says it depends on the approach and one need only use the most suitable piece to overcome the target. 'Capturing those guys' pluralizes and personalizes the target without support.
records.remedy: Use 'It depends how you do it. Just use the piece best suited to overcoming the target.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There are ways. Capturing those guys merely requires making use of the most suitable pieces."

records.jp: 「三すくみにおけるナメクジを擁したカエルが蛇をも使役するに至ること示唆しているのと同じく、的確な人材によって急所を突くことが人間社会においては肝要であるわけでして」
records.en: Taichi: "The same way that, in a three-way standoff, the frog that is home to a snail can then make it influence the snake into cooperation, it is of crucial importance inside human society to have the precise skills to strike at vital points."
comments: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E4%B8%89%E3%81%99%E3%81%8F%E3%81%BF "Frog is home to a snail": http://dic.nicovideo.jp/oekaki/612042.png -GHS
records.assessment: The three-way-deadlock analogy has a frog armed with a slug go on to command the snake. 'Home to a snail' and 'influence the snake into cooperation' change both possession and control.
records.remedy: Use 'Just as a frog with a slug at its disposal can come to command the snake in a three-way deadlock...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The same way that, in a three-way standoff, the frog that is home to a snail can then make it influence the snake into cooperation, it is of crucial importance inside human society to have the precise skills to strike at vital points."

records.jp: 「理論的には、自分が支払える代価で手に入る駒をもっとも友好に使える局面に冷静にぶつけていけば制覇は成立しうるわけですから」
records.en: Taichi: "Because, theoretically speaking, if the pieces one has in hand because their price can be paid are employed with calm quietness to strike at the position most exploitable for a friendship, conquest must come into being."
comments: Possibly about how certain routes can unlock others? How certain friends/nonessential characters can help with reaching the capture with a certain heroine? I think it's about fixed patterns, actually, but it's filtered through so much half-understood pseudo-nihilism that it's almost impossible to understand. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says deploy affordable pieces calmly where they can be used most effectively. The English misreads effective use as 'exploitable for a friendship' and tangles acquisition, position, and conquest.
records.remedy: Use 'In theory, calmly deploy the pieces you can afford in the situations where they are most effective, and conquest becomes possible.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because, theoretically speaking, if the pieces one has in hand because their price can be paid are employed with calm quietness to strike at the position most exploitable for a friendship, conquest must come into being."

records.jp: 「無論、チャートが進むに従って管理の煩雑さと管理者の育成・配置といった新しい要素も混入してくるわけですが」
records.en: Taichi: "Of course, following the progress of the chart, as management grows more complex, the situation demands the addition of a new element: the rearing and stationing of a supervising administrator."
comments: As the design (flow)chart gets messy, one needs a project supervisor? -GHS
records.assessment: The source lists new factors such as training and deploying managers as the chart advances. The English collapses those plural functions into one 'supervising administrator.'
records.remedy: Use 'As the chart advances, new factors enter, including increasingly complex management and the training and placement of managers.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Of course, following the progress of the chart, as management grows more complex, the situation demands the addition of a new element: the rearing and stationing of a supervising administrator."

records.jp: 「ここいらになってくるとマキャベリズムにも触れる必要が出てきます」
records.en: Taichi: "However, as we proximate to this area, it becomes a necessity to touch upon Machiavellism."
records.assessment: 'As we proximate to this area' is not idiomatic English, and the established term is Machiavellianism rather than 'Machiavellism.'
records.remedy: Use 'At this point, we also need to touch on Machiavellianism.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "However, as we proximate to this area, it becomes a necessity to touch upon Machiavellism."

records.jp: 「ぺけくんがすっごく邪悪っぽいです……」
records.en: Misato: "Peke-kun got so very evilish..."
comments: Third person, see CCA0010. The content's different, but the behavior isn't. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Peke-kun seems extremely evil. 'Got so very evilish' changes appearance into a past transformation and uses a malformed adjective.
records.remedy: Use 'Peke-kun seems incredibly evil...'

highlights.text: Misato: "Peke-kun got so very evilish..."

records.jp: しもうた。
records.en: Condemn it!
comments: Weirdly formal -GHS
records.assessment: しもうた is a rueful 'I messed up/whoops.' 'Condemn it' is an unrelated imperative.
records.remedy: Use 'Whoops.'

highlights.text: Condemn it!

records.jp: 先輩の前では、素直な僕でいいのに！
records.en: When in front of Senpai I should be a most upfront manservant!
comments: Boku wa manservanto de aru de ari-desu-nya. -GHS
records.assessment: 僕 here is the narrator's humble 'me.' 'Manservant' assigns a servant role absent from the source and changes his wish to be his honest self.
records.remedy: Use 'I can just be my honest self in front of Senpai!'

highlights.text: When in front of Senpai I should be a most upfront manservant!

records.jp: ということで誤魔化すことにした。
records.en: And for that purpose, I've decided to swindle her.
comments: You just gotta love a guy that just decides to take his own words and systematically stab himself in the gut with them. -GHS
records.assessment: 誤魔化す means cover it up or bluff his way past it. 'Swindle' implies deliberate fraud, often for money, and overstates the act.
records.remedy: Use 'So I decided to bluff my way out of it.'

highlights.text: And for that purpose, I've decided to swindle her.

records.jp: 「ああっ、頭痛がっ！」
records.en: Taichi: "AHH! My head...!"
records.assessment: 頭痛 explicitly means a headache. 'My head...' leaves the symptom incomplete.
records.remedy: Use 'Ahh, my headache!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "AHH! My head...!"

records.jp: 「ああ、しっかり！」
records.en: Misato: "Ahhh, steadfast!"
comments: See CCA0016 -GHS
records.assessment: しっかり is an exhortation to hold on or pull oneself together. 'Steadfast' is an isolated adjective and not a natural rescue cry.
records.remedy: Use 'Hold on!'

highlights.text: Misato: "Ahhh, steadfast!"

records.jp: 「なんか今へんな外宇宙の超知性存在オムルスがエッセネ派の叡智をもってエルゴ領域を越え並列的宇宙史観を浸食してきたんですー！」
records.en: Taichi: "I do not know how, but right now the queer Outer Space Hyper Intelligent Being OMRUS has eroded the parallel universe history across the Ergosphere via the wisdom of the Essenese!"
comments: Might be a horrible portmanteu of Omurice with Ormus, or just a weird mistransliteration of the latter. Ormus, AKA Ahura Mazda, leads back to the ol' stuff about the templars and all that Dan Brown stuff. Essenese confirmed by author. The "wisdom of the Essenese" could be the Dead Sea Scrolls, but it's difficult to tell. "Proper" term for parallel universe would be 並行宇宙. Considering how an Ergosphere messes about with spacetime, and that the diaries are de-facto history as seen from the viewpoint of parallel, simultaneous universes, this sounds suspiciously like "burning up the diaries stored in the hokora".

Alternative reading, but this is more conjecture than the Psychoman thing, is that this odd alien being (see CCA0002) is actually God, which is seen as a monster by Taichi's erroneous POV, the wisdom of the Essenese, although largely pseudo-theology, would be Jesus, and the whole parallel universe thing would be, well, this. IOW, God, via Jesus, is wrecking the idea of Cross Channel being about MWI and sci-fi. It works, but I admit it's more of a guess than inference. -GHS
records.assessment: エッセネ派 refers to the Essenes, not 'the Essenese,' and エルゴ領域 is the Ergo domain rather than an asserted scientific 'Ergosphere.'
records.remedy: Use 'the wisdom of the Essenes' and 'the Ergo domain.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I do not know how, but right now the queer Outer Space Hyper Intelligent Being OMRUS has eroded the parallel universe history across the Ergosphere via the wisdom of the Essenese!"

records.jp: 「出て行けー、僕の中から出て行けー！」
records.en: Taichi: "Get ooout, leave this poor boy and get ooout!"
comments: See CCB0004C. This still works with the above: he's pushing this out because it's too hard to accept, see CCA0003. It doesn't matter, he'll live it even if he explicitly doesn't accept it. -GHS
records.assessment: He orders it to get out from inside him. 'Leave this poor boy' adds self-pity and omits the crucial internal location.
records.remedy: Use 'Get out—get out of me!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Get ooout, leave this poor boy and get ooout!"

records.jp: 「すごく早い展開で助かります」
records.en: Misato: "You were saved by some really rapid developments."
comments: fucking 20 hours of nothing and then all the plot at the end amirite amirite. Slightly more seriously, of course: the bad guy was the good guy all along. -GHS
records.assessment: Misato says the very rapid development is helpful to her. 'You were saved by ... developments' makes Taichi the beneficiary and treats the speed as his rescue mechanism.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm grateful this is wrapping up so quickly.'

highlights.text: Misato: "You were saved by some really rapid developments."

records.jp: 「すこしふしぎ……」
records.en: Misato: "Somewhat freaky..."
comments: SF, see CCC0016A. The above is therefore a valid explanation. ...but you see why I left this in the script, I hope. -GHS
records.assessment: すこしふしぎ means 'a little mysterious' and evokes an SF abbreviation joke. 'Somewhat freaky' changes mystery into disturbing strangeness and loses the wordplay.
records.remedy: Use 'A little mysterious...'

highlights.text: Misato: "Somewhat freaky..."

records.jp: 「そんなわけでいつもの太一です」
records.en: Taichi: "And with that, here is the Taichi of always!"
records.assessment: The source says he is back to his usual self. 'The Taichi of always' is an unnatural nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use 'And with that, I'm back to my usual self!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And with that, here is the Taichi of always!"

records.jp: 「ええ。他には特に」
records.en: Misato: "Yes. No particular issues with the rest."
records.assessment: 他には特に means there is nothing else in particular she needs. 'No particular issues with the rest' changes requested tasks into problems or issues.
records.remedy: Use 'Yes. Nothing else in particular.'

highlights.text: Misato: "Yes. No particular issues with the rest."

records.jp: 「そんなことないですよ。ただ……わたしが個人でやっていることですし」
records.en: Misato: "That, no, never! Just... this is something I have to do individually."
records.assessment: She says it is something she is doing on her own. 'Have to do individually' adds obligation and suggests a rule requiring solitude.
records.remedy: Use 'It's just something I'm doing on my own.'

highlights.text: Misato: "That, no, never! Just... this is something I have to do individually."

records.jp: 押し黙る。
records.en: Continuing silence.
records.assessment: 押し黙る says she falls abruptly silent. 'Continuing silence' describes an already ongoing state and omits her action.
records.remedy: Use 'She falls silent.'

highlights.text: Continuing silence.

records.jp: 「みんな……好きなことやってるわけじゃないスよ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Everybody... but they are not doing anything they like doing, you know?"
comments: CP CCA0006
records.assessment: The source says not everyone is doing what they like, not that everyone does nothing they enjoy. The English makes the negation absolute.
records.remedy: Use 'Not everyone is doing what they like, you know?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Everybody... but they are not doing anything they like doing, you know?"

records.jp: 冒険も探求もできない。
records.en: Adventures or quests we can't do.
records.assessment: 探求 means inquiry, investigation, or pursuit of knowledge. 'Quests' turns it into another adventure genre term.
records.remedy: Use 'We can't go adventuring or investigating.'

highlights.text: Adventures or quests we can't do.

records.jp: 心は麻痺するものだからだ。
records.en: Because our hearts are something paralyzed.
comments: That's also a bit of cough-cough handwaving as to why these people won't leave, or change their behavior, in a sense. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says hearts become numb. 'Are something paralyzed' is ungrammatical and treats numbness as a fixed classification.
records.remedy: Use 'Because our hearts go numb.'

highlights.text: Because our hearts are something paralyzed.

records.jp: 群青の者は、特にそう。
records.en:
For us, the Ultramarines of Gunjou, that
is especially true.
comments: expanded, same as CCA0016. -GHS
records.assessment: 群青の者 means people at Gunjou. Calling them 'the Ultramarines of Gunjou' invents a named faction and duplicates the color meaning.
records.remedy: Use 'Especially people at Gunjou.'

highlights.text:
For us, the Ultramarines of Gunjou, that
is especially true.

records.jp: ……はて？
records.en: ...what even...?
records.assessment: はて is a puzzled 'hmm/wait.' 'What even' is an unfinished colloquial question with no object.
records.remedy: Use '...Hmm?'

highlights.text: ...what even...?

records.jp: わからない。
records.en: I don't get that.
records.assessment: The source simply says 'I don't know.' 'I don't get that' adds a specific object and frames it as comprehension.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't know.'

highlights.text: I don't get that.

records.jp: わかるのは。
records.en: What I get is,
records.assessment: わかるのは means 'what I do know is.' 'What I get is' suggests comprehension or acquisition and is awkward before the continuation.
records.remedy: Use 'What I do know is...'

highlights.text: What I get is,

records.jp: 曜子ちゃんと似ているような、別物のような。
records.en: she's something like Youko-chan, a special case.
records.assessment: The source says the girl seems similar to Youko yet also seems like something different. 'A special case' removes that similarity-versus-difference tension.
records.remedy: Use 'She seemed like Youko-chan, yet also like something entirely different.'

highlights.text: she's something like Youko-chan, a special case.

records.jp: そんな違和感だけだ。
records.en: There's just that sense of physical discomfort.
records.assessment: 違和感 is a general sense of incongruity or something being off. 'Physical discomfort' incorrectly narrows it to bodily sensation.
records.remedy: Use 'That faint sense that something was off was all I had.'

highlights.text: There's just that sense of physical discomfort.

records.jp: 俺はことさら相好を崩した。
records.en: I was letting my face deliberately fall into an especially beaming smile.
comments: Visuals -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he deliberately breaks into a broad smile. 'Was letting my face ... fall into' is progressive and physically awkward.
records.remedy: Use 'I deliberately broke into a broad smile.'

highlights.text: I was letting my face deliberately fall into an especially beaming smile.

records.jp: 「あとハラキリ冬子も来てましたよ」
records.en: Taichi: "Also, Harakiri Touko has come in as well."
records.assessment: The source says Touko was there too. 'Has come in as well' uses an awkward present-perfect arrival construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Harakiri Touko was here too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Also, Harakiri Touko has come in as well."

records.jp: 「あいつらはなんだかんだいって健全に近いんで」
records.en: Taichi: "Say what you like, but those guys are close to that wholesome healthiness."
records.assessment: The source says they are close to healthy or normal. 'Close to that wholesome healthiness' is redundant and oddly deictic.
records.remedy: Use 'For all their quirks, they're pretty close to normal.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Say what you like, but those guys are close to that wholesome healthiness."

records.jp: 鉄扉をこじあけて校舎に入る。
records.en: closing the iron door and reentering the school building.
records.assessment: The source says he pries the metal door open and enters the building. 'Closing the iron door' states the opposite action.
records.remedy: Use 'I pry open the metal door and enter the school building.'

highlights.text: closing the iron door and reentering the school building.

records.jp: 振り返ると、彼女はずっと見送ってくれていた。
records.en: I look back and I can see that she has been watching me leave all along.
records.assessment: The source is past narration: he looked back and saw she had watched him leave. The English shifts the first two actions to present.
records.remedy: Use 'I looked back and saw that she had been watching me leave all along.'

highlights.text: I look back and I can see that she has been watching me leave all along.

records.jp: 蝉がうるさい。
records.en: The cicadas are making loud,
comments: CP CCA0007
records.assessment: 'The cicadas are making loud' uses an adjective as the object of 'making' and is incomplete.
records.remedy: Use 'The cicadas are loud,'

highlights.text: The cicadas are making loud,

records.jp: 「しかし」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then."
comments: CP CCA0007
records.assessment: しかし means 'however/but,' introducing a contrast. 'Well then' instead marks a transition or decision.
records.remedy: Use 'However...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then."

records.jp: 屋上が炎天下となると、涼める場所はさほどない。
records.en: With the rooftop under the blazing sun, that's not really a place to cool off in.
comments: CP CCA0007
records.assessment: The source says that with the rooftop in blazing sun there are not many places available to cool off. The English instead says only that the rooftop itself is not such a place, changing the quantification and spatial relation.
records.remedy: Use 'With the rooftop baking under the sun, there aren't many places where I can cool off.'

highlights.text: With the rooftop under the blazing sun, that's not really a place to cool off in.

records.jp: 一年Ｅ組では、まちこ先生が授業をしていた。
records.en: First Year Class E, the class that was being taught by Machiko-sensei.
comments: PCP CCA0007 2 merged lines & tense -GHS
records.assessment: The English is a sentence fragment with a doubled clause structure; it never supplies a grammatical predicate for 'First Year Class E.'
records.remedy: Use 'Machiko-sensei was teaching Class 1-E.'

highlights.text: First Year Class E, the class that was being taught by Machiko-sensei.

records.jp: 友貴が漫画雑誌を読んでいた。
records.en: Tomoki kept reading that manga magazine.
records.assessment: The source states that Tomoki was reading a manga magazine. 'Kept reading that' adds persistence and a previously identified object that the Japanese does not specify.
records.remedy: Use 'Tomoki was reading a manga magazine.'

highlights.text: Tomoki kept reading that manga magazine.

records.jp: 軽く会話をかわす。
records.en: A light conversation bounces off.
comments: Exchange + deflect, see CCA0007 -GHS
records.assessment: 会話をかわす means to exchange a few words. 'A conversation bounces off' is not an English rendering of that reciprocal action.
records.remedy: Use 'We exchanged a few words.'

highlights.text: A light conversation bounces off.

records.jp: 「禁止されてるんだよ。学校もよくわかってるよな」
records.en: Tomoki: "That was forbidden. School got wise to that already."
comments: CP CCA0007
records.assessment: 禁止されてる describes a standing prohibition. The simple past 'was forbidden' incorrectly presents it as a completed past state.
records.remedy: Use 'It's prohibited. The school knows what it's doing.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That was forbidden. School got wise to that already."

records.jp: 「あー、諸君らが俺をどう思っているかは知っている。だがこれはつまらないギャグではなくマジでいい手なのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I know what you ladies think of me. But this isn't some annoying gag, I really think there's something we could do."
comments: CP CCA0007
records.assessment: 諸君ら addresses the people present without marking them as women. 'You ladies' misgenders a mixed group and changes the taunt's target.
records.remedy: Use 'I know what you people think of me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, I know what you ladies think of me. But this isn't some annoying gag, I really think there's something we could do."

records.jp: 「という感じでどうだ」
records.en: Taichi: "How's this feel then!"
records.assessment: という感じでどうだ proposes the demonstrated arrangement: 'How about something like this?' 'How's this feel' asks about a sensation rather than judging the plan.
records.remedy: Use 'How about something like this?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "How's this feel then!"

records.jp: フルカラー印刷した『無人の室内』画像を、窓ガラスの内側に貼り付けた。
records.en: A full-color print titled Unoccupied Interior was affixed to the windowpane on the inside.
records.assessment: The Japanese quotes a descriptive image of an empty room; it does not give the print a formal title. 'Titled Unoccupied Interior' invents that status.
records.remedy: Use 'We taped a full-color printout of an empty room to the inside of the window.'

highlights.text: A full-color print titled Unoccupied Interior was affixed to the windowpane on the inside.

records.jp: 「わはは」
records.en: Taichi: "Wahaha!
records.assessment: The English dialogue is missing its closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Close the quotation after the exclamation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wahaha!

records.jp: 「ハンカチで手をふきふきしながら戻ってくれば誰だってわかるわい！」
records.en: Taichi: "If you come back going all wipey-wipey on your hands with a towel, anyone could tell where you've been!"
comments: I still think it should be butterbur-butterbur -GHS
records.assessment: ハンカチ is a handkerchief, not a towel. The substituted object changes the visible clue described by the source.
records.remedy: Use 'If you come back wiping your hands with a handkerchief, anyone can tell!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If you come back going all wipey-wipey on your hands with a towel, anyone could tell where you've been!"

records.jp: 「だからさ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Really, I told you..."
records.assessment: だからさ means 'that's what I told you' or 'that's why,' depending on the carried context. 'Really' is added, and the ellipsis invents a trailing hesitation.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what I told you.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Really, I told you..."

records.jp: 俺は愕然とした。
records.en: An appalling sensation pervaded me.
records.assessment: 愕然とした directly means that the narrator was stunned or appalled. 'An appalling sensation pervaded me' turns a reaction into an external sensation and is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'I was appalled.'

highlights.text: An appalling sensation pervaded me.

records.jp: 「な、なんてふしだらなことを」
records.en: Taichi: "W-, why you slovenly-!"
records.assessment: ふしだら here condemns impropriety or shamelessness. 'Slovenly' means untidy and misses the moral register driving the mock outrage.
records.remedy: Use 'H-how shameless of you!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "W-, why you slovenly-!"

records.jp: 怯えるみゆき。
records.en: frightening her.
records.assessment: 怯えるみゆき presents Miyuki as frightened. 'Frightening her' converts the description into an action performed by the narrator and supplies a causal relation not stated in this unit.
records.remedy: Use 'Miyuki cowers.'

highlights.text: frightening her.

records.jp: くそう、地味なやつめ。
records.en: Damn this lame plain girl!
records.assessment: 地味 calls her plain or unassuming. 'Lame' adds a separate disparaging judgment and changes the comic register.
records.remedy: Use 'Damn it, you incurably plain girl.'

highlights.text: Damn this lame plain girl!

records.jp: とスカートをゆっくりめくっていく。
records.en: Via a slow flip of that skirt.
records.assessment: The source explicitly says that the narrator slowly lifts Miyuki's skirt. 'Via a slow flip of that skirt' is a verbless fragment that suppresses both actor and progressive action.
records.remedy: Use 'I slowly begin lifting her skirt.'

highlights.text: Via a slow flip of that skirt.

records.jp: 「もし毛糸のパンツをはいていたら、汝の罪は許されるであろう」
records.en: Taichi: "Should you be presenting Us with traditional underwear of knitting wool made, then thy sins shall be forgiven, woman!"
comments: Visuals. I think he just wants good ol' bloomers. 汝 is woman + water, and is a 'you' that's either archaic ("thou") or vulgar ("blockhead"). -GHS
records.assessment: The source condition is simply that she be wearing woolen bloomers. The English invents 'traditional underwear,' adds 'woman,' and becomes syntactically incoherent.
records.remedy: Use 'If you are wearing woolen bloomers, your sins shall be forgiven.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Should you be presenting Us with traditional underwear of knitting wool made, then thy sins shall be forgiven, woman!"

records.jp: 「しかーし、もし薄手のショーツなどを生意気にも着用しているようであればぁ」
records.en: Taichi: "But, supposing you are impertinently under-wearing short panties of a thin make..."
records.assessment: 薄手のショーツ means thin or flimsy panties. 'Under-wearing short panties of a thin make' is not grammatical English and misparses ショーツ as an adjective meaning short.
records.remedy: Use 'But if you have the nerve to wear flimsy panties...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But, supposing you are impertinently under-wearing short panties of a thin make..."

records.jp: 背後からの踵落としですかそうですか。
records.en: Could that be a drop-kick from behind perhaps indeed that is so.
records.assessment: 踵落とし is a heel drop or axe kick. A drop-kick is a different technique and is not what the Japanese names.
records.remedy: Use 'An axe kick from behind. Of course.'

highlights.text: Could that be a drop-kick from behind perhaps indeed that is so.

records.jp: ギロッという感じの視線が、俺を射竦める。
records.en: The feeling of a sight using me as a guiro, pinning me down.
comments: That's a musical instrument. -GHS
records.assessment: ギロッ is the mimetic force of a sharp glare. The English mistakes it for the musical instrument 'guiro' and consequently destroys the sentence's action.
records.remedy: Use 'A razor-sharp glare pins me in place.'

highlights.text: The feeling of a sight using me as a guiro, pinning me down.

records.jp: 「ほ、先生とな。どの先生に泣きつくつもりかな、おぜうさん？」
records.en: Taichi: "Huh, teachers. Which teacher are you planning on going to cry to, my dear lady?
comments: See CCC0024 -GHS
records.assessment: The English dialogue is missing its closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Close the quotation after 'lady?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Huh, teachers. Which teacher are you planning on going to cry to, my dear lady?

records.jp: 「誰にでも」
records.en: Kiri: "Any is fine."
records.assessment: 誰にでも means 'anyone' or 'whoever.' 'Any is fine' treats a person as an omitted selectable item and is unidiomatic.
records.remedy: Use 'Any of them.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "Any is fine."

records.jp: 「気にするなマイフレン、人徳のなすわざだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Worry not about it, my friend, 'tis a technique born of natural virtues!"
records.assessment: 人徳のなすわざ means that the result is due to the speaker's personal virtue or character. 'A technique born of natural virtues' changes a cause into a technique.
records.remedy: Use 'Think nothing of it, my friend. It's all thanks to my sterling character.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Worry not about it, my friend, 'tis a technique born of natural virtues!"

records.jp: 「へえ。偉いんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ehhh, aren't I awesome."
comments: Think he's talking about himself. -GHS
records.assessment: 偉いんだ is directed at the other speaker: 'Oh, so you're important/impressive.' The English reverses the subject and has Taichi praise himself.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh? So you're a big shot.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ehhh, aren't I awesome."

records.jp: 「……単に反応を愉しみたかったダゲァ！？」
records.en: Tomoki: "...'cause you simply wanted to relish her reaction, what eAHLS?!"
comments: "Else". More pretentious tanoshii -GHS
records.assessment: The source is an interrupted retort. The English's 'what eAHLS' is not intelligible as either the intended clause or a legible interruption effect.
records.remedy: Use an intelligible interrupted line such as '...You just wanted to enjoy her reaction—agh?!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...'cause you simply wanted to relish her reaction, what eAHLS?!"

records.jp: 「のう、友貴よ？」
records.en: Taichi: "Is that a no, Tomoki-yo?"
comments: Tone change. That's a literal "nou" used as "no", so it recurring is justified. -GHS
records.assessment: The sentence-final のう is a theatrical request for confirmation, equivalent here to 'right, Tomoki?' It is not the noun or response 'no.'
records.remedy: Use 'Isn't that right, Tomoki?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Is that a no, Tomoki-yo?"

records.jp: 正拳側上段突き。
records.en: Direct Upper Straight Punch
comments: PCP above
records.assessment: The English sentence lacks terminal punctuation while neighboring attack labels are presented as complete captions.
records.remedy: Add a period.

highlights.text: Direct Upper Straight Punch

records.jp: ポケットに手をつっこみ、瞑想するかのように目を閉じ、名悪役の物腰で、
records.en: A hand thrust in the pocket, the eyelids lowered as if meditating, all with the bearing of famous villains.
records.assessment: 名悪役 is a singular archetype, a great or famous villain. 'The bearing of famous villains' changes the number and leaves the opening participial sequence without a stable subject.
records.remedy: Use 'With one hand in my pocket and my eyes closed as if in meditation, I assume the bearing of a great villain.'

highlights.text: A hand thrust in the pocket, the eyelids lowered as if meditating, all with the bearing of famous villains.

records.jp: 語尾とともにくわっと開眼した。
records.en: On the trail of the last words shock zoom and sharp sound effect as I opened my eyes.
comments: Not graphic enough in English otherwise. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that his eyes snap open with the end of the line. 'Shock zoom and sharp sound effect' are new production directions not stated in the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'As I finish the line, my eyes snap open.'

highlights.text: On the trail of the last words shock zoom and sharp sound effect as I opened my eyes.

records.jp: 「群青学院にはいじめはないって聞いてたのに……」
records.en: Kiri: "And they told me that there's no bullying at the Gunjou Institute..."
records.assessment: Under the source-critical terminology record and standard Hepburn, 群青学院 is Gunjō Academy. 'Gunjou Institute' uses non-Hepburn romanization and shifts the established institution type.
records.remedy: Use 'Gunjō Academy.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "And they told me that there's no bullying at the Gunjou Institute..."

records.jp: 「僕だって違う！」
records.en: Tomoki: "I got nothing to do with this!"
records.assessment: 僕だって違う answers 'Neither am I' to the charge of hypocrisy. 'I got nothing to do with this' changes the proposition from denying a trait to denying involvement.
records.remedy: Use 'Neither am I!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I got nothing to do with this!"

records.jp: 「やるかー！」
records.en: Taichi: "You so dooo!"
comments: Children. -GHS
records.assessment: やるか is a challenge to fight. 'You so do' answers the prior denial instead and loses the escalation into a scuffle.
records.remedy: Use 'You wanna fight?!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You so dooo!"

records.jp: 「低学歴低収入！」
records.en: Tomoki: "Inferior education means poor remuneration!"
comments: Still concerning the stocks -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
records.assessment: 低学歴低収入 is a paired insult, 'low education, low income.' The English invents a causal claim that one means the other.
records.remedy: Use 'Low education, low income!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Inferior education means poor remuneration!"

records.jp: 「株の敗残者！」
records.en: Tomoki: "Stocks market loser!"
comments: Part 2, Taichi the Failed Speculator -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent CG shake -GHS
records.assessment: 'Stocks market' is an ungrammatical noun phrase; the Japanese simply calls him a defeated stock trader.
records.remedy: Use 'Stock-market loser!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Stocks market loser!"

records.jp: 「おまえだって人のこと、シスコンオナニーのプロとかあちこちで吹聴しただろ！」
records.en: Tomoki: "You went and told everybody left and right of how some people are 'pro-level siscon onanists', didn't you!"
comments: clarified a bit what he's referring to -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that Taichi spread the claim that Tomoki himself was a professional siscon masturbator. 'Some people' removes the directly targeted person and weakens the accusation.
records.remedy: Use 'You went around telling everyone I was a professional siscon masturbator!'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "You went and told everybody left and right of how some people are 'pro-level siscon onanists', didn't you!"

records.jp: 「……そしてあなたたちも、悪なんて美意識のあるものじゃないことがわかった」
records.en: Kiri: "...furthermore, you have understood that evil has no sense of beauty."
comments: I think she's referring to the sad spectacle they just gave, not generally. -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker says she has realized that the two people before her are not even something as aesthetically principled as evil. The English instead says that they have understood a general claim that evil lacks beauty, reversing subject and evaluative relation.
records.remedy: Use '...And now I see that neither of you possesses enough aesthetic sense even to qualify as evil.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "...furthermore, you have understood that evil has no sense of beauty."

records.jp: 「ぼ、僕は関係ないのに。太一のせいで僕まで……」
records.en: Tomoki: "I-, I have nothing to do with this! It's Taichi's fault, always making me..."
records.assessment: The source trails off after saying that Taichi has dragged him into it too. 'Always making me' adds habitual frequency not present here.
records.remedy: Use 'I had nothing to do with this. Because of Taichi, now I'm...'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I-, I have nothing to do with this! It's Taichi's fault, always making me..."

records.jp: 「いいもう。引きこもる」
records.en: Tomoki: "Had enough. Hikikomori now."
comments: Will recur. ...of course. -GHS
records.assessment: 引きこもる is a first-person decision to shut himself away. 'Hikikomori now' changes the verb into a clipped identity label and leaves the action unstated.
records.remedy: Use 'That's it. I'm shutting myself away.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Had enough. Hikikomori now."

records.jp: しくしく泣き出す。
records.en: Sobbing and weeping tears flow out.
records.assessment: しくしく describes quiet, plaintive crying. 'Sobbing and weeping tears flow out' both overstates the manner and splices an action to an incompatible subject.
records.remedy: Use 'He begins to whimper.'

highlights.text: Sobbing and weeping tears flow out.

records.jp: 「そこまで……」
records.en: Miyuki: "Pushed that far..."
records.assessment: そこまで is a shocked reaction to the extent of his collapse. 'Pushed that far' supplies an external agent and leaves the response as an unclear fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'That badly...?'

highlights.text: Miyuki: "Pushed that far..."

records.jp: 「この子もいいって言うし、その無様さに免じて今回だけは見逃してあげます」
records.en: Kiri: "If the girl also says it's fine, then in deference to this unpresentable event, I will overlook things this time."
records.assessment: 無様さ refers to the target's pathetic or undignified state. 'This unpresentable event' turns that personal condition into a generic event and misses the contempt.
records.remedy: Use 'Since she says it's fine, I'll let you off this once out of pity for that pathetic state.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "If the girl also says it's fine, then in deference to this unpresentable event, I will overlook things this time."

records.jp: 教室に戻る途中、処女がうずくまっていた。
records.en: I met a crouching maiden while on my way back to the classroom.
comments: PCP CCA0008
Actually had to change quite a bit since the two fragments don't seem to flow. -GHS
records.assessment: 処女 explicitly means 'virgin' and is the narrator's deliberately inappropriate label. 'Maiden' euphemizes and changes that pointed diction.
records.remedy: Use 'On my way back to class, I found a virgin crouched in the hall.'

highlights.text: I met a crouching maiden while on my way back to the classroom.

records.jp: 素早い挙動。
records.en: Very sudden behavior.
comments: Very suspicious, too. -GHS
records.assessment: 素早い挙動 describes swift movement. 'Very sudden behavior' replaces physical speed with unexpected conduct.
records.remedy: Use 'A quick movement.'

highlights.text: Very sudden behavior.

records.jp: いつもと変わる風でもない美希だ。
records.en: Miki's style is an ever unchanging, bluff-less thing.
comments: See CCA0008, more reading key for the wind (now gone). -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Miki does not seem different from usual. 'An ever unchanging, bluff-less style' introduces unsupported qualities and is not a coherent rendering of いつもと変わる風でもない.
records.remedy: Use 'Miki doesn't seem any different from usual.'

highlights.text: Miki's style is an ever unchanging, bluff-less thing.

records.jp: 少し違和感。
records.en: A vague sense of physical discomfort.
comments: Specific recurring term -GHS
records.assessment: 違和感 is a sense that something is off or incongruous. 'Physical discomfort' incorrectly makes it a bodily symptom.
records.remedy: Use 'Still, something feels slightly off.'

highlights.text: A vague sense of physical discomfort.

records.jp: もともと素質はあったようだが、一回りも二回りもたくましくなったような。
records.en: That quality was there from the start, yes, but it feels she has gone around the block once or twice with regards to strength of willpower.
comments: Lit. "incomparably [stronger] than before", but keeping closer to the original since it hints about her not resetting. -GHS
records.assessment: 一回りも二回りもたくましく is figurative size language meaning markedly tougher or more robust. 'Gone around the block once or twice' imports an unrelated English idiom about experience.
records.remedy: Use 'She always had the makings of it, but now she seems one or two sizes tougher.'

highlights.text: That quality was there from the start, yes, but it feels she has gone around the block once or twice with regards to strength of willpower.

records.jp: 「俺もやったぞ、そーじ」
records.en: Taichi: "What a coincidence, I'm scrubbing."
comments: Adaptation Hell begins! -GHS
records.assessment: 俺もやったぞ、そーじ says that the narrator also did sōji and sets up the following homophone joke. 'What a coincidence, I'm scrubbing' invents coincidence and commits to one lexical reading before the joke lands.
records.remedy: Use 'I did sōji too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "What a coincidence, I'm scrubbing."

records.jp: 「表面的な言葉遊びで送辞と相似とか言いますか？」
records.en: Miki: "Is that a superficial wordplay with your idea of my physical characteristics and your parentage?"
comments: farewell+resemblance+cleaning -> cleaning+she's flat+he's a bastard -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese explicitly anticipates superficial puns linking the sound sōji with 送辞 and 相似. The English about physical characteristics and parentage has no support in either word and eliminates the metalinguistic joke.
records.remedy: Recast the line around the three-way sōji homophony, with a brief unobtrusive gloss if the edition permits one.

highlights.text: Miki: "Is that a superficial wordplay with your idea of my physical characteristics and your parentage?"

records.jp: 「……言いません！」
records.en: Taichi: "...it is not!"
comments: Suddenly formal -GHS
records.assessment: The reply denies an intended future move, 'I wasn't going to.' 'It is not' has neither the correct subject nor the intended temporal relation.
records.remedy: Use '...I wasn't going to!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...it is not!"

records.jp: たくましかった。
records.en: Stronger willpower.
comments: Same as above. -GHS
records.assessment: たくましかった is a complete retrospective judgment that she had gotten tougher. 'Stronger willpower' is a verbless noun phrase and narrows the quality to willpower.
records.remedy: Use 'She really had gotten tougher.'

highlights.text: Stronger willpower.

records.jp: う、なんか強い？
records.en: Ugh, so strong, but how?
records.assessment: なんか強い asks in surprise whether she is unexpectedly strong. 'So strong, but how?' asserts the degree and invents a question about cause.
records.remedy: Use 'Huh? Is she kind of strong?'

highlights.text: Ugh, so strong, but how?

records.jp: カラデをおさめたこの俺を。
records.en: To hit I, the Master of Karade!
records.assessment: The line is a mock-heroic object fragment referring back to the previous blow: even the narrator who has mastered 'Karade.' 'To hit I' is ungrammatical and obscures that construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Even me, a master of Karade.'

highlights.text: To hit I, the Master of Karade!

records.jp: ちょっぴり本気になる。
records.en: It got just a smidgen serious.
records.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator gets a little serious. 'It got ... serious' removes the acting subject and turns his decision into a change in the situation.
records.remedy: Use 'I get just a little serious.'

highlights.text: It got just a smidgen serious.

records.jp: 軸足を払ってやろうと思ったが、白パンツが垣間見えた。
records.en: I was thinking how to sweep off the leg she uses as axle, but through the gap, I saw panties.
comments: Recurring term. Unfortunately more than a bit forced here. "White" removed in the console version not for censorship (for once), but because, well, they're definitely not. -GHS
records.assessment: 軸足 is the planted or pivot leg, not an 'axle' leg, and 白 explicitly says the briefly seen panties are white. The English both calques the martial term and omits the color.
records.remedy: Use 'I consider sweeping her planted leg, but catch a glimpse of white panties.'

highlights.text: I was thinking how to sweep off the leg she uses as axle, but through the gap, I saw panties.

records.jp: 攻撃中止。
records.en: Attack suspension.
records.assessment: The source is the clipped but verbal declaration that the attack is called off. 'Attack suspension' is an unnatural bureaucratic noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'Attack aborted.'

highlights.text: Attack suspension.

records.jp: 男太一、眼前に供えられたパンツを見ないなどという惰弱な選択肢はない。
records.en: To Taichi the Man not looking at panties sacrificed to his sight is an effeminate choice that does not exists.
comments: Intended to be ironic given his gender issues. -GHS
records.assessment: 惰弱 means cowardly or feeble, not specifically effeminate, and 'does not exists' is ungrammatical. The sentence's mock-heroic self-designation is also left syntactically stranded.
records.remedy: Use 'For Taichi the Man, cowardly refusal to look at panties offered before his eyes is no option at all.'

highlights.text: To Taichi the Man not looking at panties sacrificed to his sight is an effeminate choice that does not exists.

records.jp: 腰を落として視線を下げた。
records.en: I dropped my gaze to below the hips.
records.assessment: The narrator lowers his stance and then lowers his gaze. 'I dropped my gaze to below the hips' omits the bodily movement and invents a spatial object for the gaze.
records.remedy: Use 'I lower my stance and drop my gaze.'

highlights.text: I dropped my gaze to below the hips.

records.jp: カラデによる中段受けにて備える。
records.en: As per Karade, I steady myself to take it in the mid-section.
records.assessment: 中段受け is a middle-level block. The English says he prepares to take the kick in his midsection, reversing defense into receiving the blow.
records.remedy: Use 'I brace with a Karade middle-level block.'

highlights.text: As per Karade, I steady myself to take it in the mid-section.

records.jp: 「はっ？」
records.en: Taichi: Huh?"
records.assessment: The English dialogue is missing its opening quotation mark.
records.remedy: Open the quotation before 'Huh?'

highlights.text: Taichi: Huh?"

records.jp: 「あ、よかった。気がつきましたか？」
records.en: Miki: "Ah, I'm so glad! Did you recover now?"
comments: That can mean 'did you come back to senses?' just as much as 'have you realized now?'. -GHS
records.assessment: 気がつきましたか asks whether he regained consciousness. 'Did you recover now?' is broader, awkward, and does not identify the observed return to awareness.
records.remedy: Use 'You're awake?'

highlights.text: Miki: "Ah, I'm so glad! Did you recover now?"

records.jp: 膝を打った。
records.en: I pound my lap.
comments: ...I actually think that's intended to sound dirty... -GHS
records.assessment: 膝を打つ here is to slap one's knee. 'Pound my lap' names a different body area and a more violent action.
records.remedy: Use 'I slap my knee.'

highlights.text: I pound my lap.

records.jp: 「ライブで見る素人娘がリアルに着用しているパンツ、だよ、君」
records.en: Taichi: "For the live show of 'serious' panties worn by an amateur girl, that's what!"
comments: Since they're sex panties... -GHS
records.assessment: リアル modifies the fact that the underwear is really being worn and viewed live. The English turns it into 'serious panties,' which has no support in the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'Panties actually being worn by an amateur girl you're watching live, my boy.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "For the live show of 'serious' panties worn by an amateur girl, that's what!"

records.jp: 「違うとも。このように―――」
records.en: Taichi: "So true. Like THIS!---"
records.assessment: 違うとも emphatically agrees that the proposed equivalence is different before demonstrating how. 'So true' reverses that reply into a denial of Miki's objection.
records.remedy: Use 'Different indeed. Like this—'

highlights.text: Taichi: "So true. Like THIS!---"

records.jp: チョキで、しっかと挟まれているっ！
records.en: And a scissor of fingers cleanly pushes them away!
records.assessment: The source says the skirt hem is firmly caught between a scissors-shaped pair of fingers. 'A scissor of fingers ... pushes them away' changes both the grip and its direction.
