records.remedy: Use 'Only to be caught fast between two fingers held like scissors!'

highlights.text: And a scissor of fingers cleanly pushes them away!

records.jp: 横たわって膝を抱え、エビチリみたいに丸くなった。
records.en: I grab back my stretched-out knees, and hug them until I look as round as a fried shrimp.
comments: See CCB0006 -GHS
records.assessment: エビチリ is chili shrimp, not fried shrimp, and the narrator lies down and curls up while hugging his knees. 'Grab back my stretched-out knees' does not describe that posture.
records.remedy: Use 'I lie down, hug my knees, and curl up like a chili shrimp.'

highlights.text: I grab back my stretched-out knees, and hug them until I look as round as a fried shrimp.

records.jp: 「で、俺はもう引退しゆ」
records.en: Taichi: "Then it's an oily good time for me to retire."
comments: Shrimp + shiyu (fatty oil) = fried shrimp. -GHS
records.assessment: The line is a babyish slip from 引退する into 引退しゆ. 'An oily good time' invents an English oil pun that is not present in the malformed ending.
records.remedy: Preserve the childish slip without adding a new lexical pun, for example 'I'm wetiring now.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then it's an oily good time for me to retire."

records.jp: 「しゆとか言うし……」
records.en: Miki: "Oily, you sayly..."
comments: And here it is. -GHS
records.assessment: The response points out the speaker's malformed しゆ ending. 'Oily, you sayly' continues an invented oil pun rather than calling attention to that speech slip.
records.remedy: Echo the same childish deformation used in the preceding line.

highlights.text: Miki: "Oily, you sayly..."

records.jp: ゆさゆさと揺すられる。
records.en: I was shaken and quaked like a certain too yu-ng girl.
comments: Yusa-yusa is actually an SFX. -GHS
records.assessment: ゆさゆさ is a repeated rocking or shaking motion. The reference to 'a certain too yu-ng girl' invents a new English/Japanese pun with no source basis.
records.remedy: Use 'She rocks me back and forth.'

highlights.text: I was shaken and quaked like a certain too yu-ng girl.

records.jp: 「ししょー、元気出してくださいよ」
records.en: Miki: "Shishou, please stay strong!"
records.assessment: If the Japanese address term is retained rather than translated, standard Hepburn requires shishō, not 'Shishou.'
records.remedy: Use 'Master' or the consistently romanized 'shishō.'

highlights.text: Miki: "Shishou, please stay strong!"

records.jp: 「いい。引きこもる」
records.en: Taichi: "'s fine. Hikikomori now."
comments: See CCB0006 -GHS
records.assessment: 引きこもる is the speaker's decision to shut himself away. 'Hikikomori now' converts the action into a clipped identity label.
records.remedy: Use 'Fine. I'm shutting myself away.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "'s fine. Hikikomori now."

records.jp: 「それはもう、せんぱいのプレッシャーみたいっぽいやつに当てられて、小心者の美希はビビリまくりなわけですよ」
records.en: Miki: "That's because, when affected by Senpai's straining at the mental pressure, cowardly little Miki just jumps all into the jitter-jitters."
comments: Third person -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Miki is being overwhelmed by something like pressure emanating from Senpai. 'Senpai's straining at the mental pressure' makes him the person under strain and misassigns the relation.
records.remedy: Use 'Something like your pressure is getting to timid little Miki, so she's scared stiff.'

highlights.text: Miki: "That's because, when affected by Senpai's straining at the mental pressure, cowardly little Miki just jumps all into the jitter-jitters."

records.jp: うーむ、ポワワとしてしまうではないか。
records.en: Ye-ep, let's just puff those cheeks and give a good smile, won't we.
comments: Although the console version seems to relate this to powaru (sexual delusions), ポワワ keeps returning as ポワワーン, which means the above. Maybe he's just trying to ignore suspicions, seems to fit. -GHS
records.assessment: ポワワ describes the narrator going soft, dreamy, or warmly fuzzy in response. Puffing cheeks and deliberately producing a smile are actions invented by the English.
records.remedy: Use 'Hmm. She's making me go all soft and fuzzy.'

highlights.text: Ye-ep, let's just puff those cheeks and give a good smile, won't we.

records.jp: 拳を打つ。
records.en: I make a fist as if throwing rock.
comments: That's what it also means. Well, she DID play scissors before... -GHS
records.assessment: 拳を打つ here is a compact fist gesture in the certification routine. 'As if throwing rock' introduces a rock-paper-scissors comparison absent from the source.
records.remedy: Render the fist gesture directly without the added comparison.

highlights.text: I make a fist as if throwing rock.

records.jp: 当校では身分証明書をかねるこの手帳を、『都会』の駅裏にある人気ＮＯ１高級浴場『メイトブック』にちなんでそう呼ぶ。
records.en: So is called this intra-school ID booklet with a second role, named after the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station, MateBook.
comments: PCP CCA0008
records.assessment: The source explains that the handbook doubles as school ID and is jokingly named after a popular high-end bathhouse behind the station in the City. The English's clause structure is ungrammatical and invents an additional 'popular spot.'
records.remedy: Use 'At our school, this handbook doubles as ID; we call it the Matebook after the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the City.'

highlights.text: So is called this intra-school ID booklet with a second role, named after the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station, MateBook.

records.jp: 「……すんっ」
records.en: Miki: "...sob."
records.assessment: すんっ is a sniff or suppressed sob. Rendering the sound as the descriptive word 'sob' changes the audible beat into narration.
records.remedy: Use a brief sound such as '...sniff.'

highlights.text: Miki: "...sob."

records.jp: 微妙なためがあった。
records.en: There was a subtle effect.
comments: On her, I guess? Though technically there were advantages for him in a sense, it doesn't flow either way. -GHS
records.assessment: ため here is a pause or hesitation in the response. 'A subtle effect' selects an unrelated sense and removes the conversational timing.
records.remedy: Use 'There is a slight pause.'

highlights.text: There was a subtle effect.

records.jp: 「そうですね、そうかも」
records.en: Miki: "So it did, so it seems."
records.assessment: そうですね、そうかも means 'Yes, maybe so.' 'So it did, so it seems' invents a completed event and does not express tentative agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'Yes... maybe so.'

highlights.text: Miki: "So it did, so it seems."

records.jp: 「もう１３歳とか１５歳の新じゃがならぬ新処女と出会う機会はなくなったわけだよなぁ」
records.en: Taichi: "Now, all opportunities to meet Unnew Potatoes New Virgins of 13 or 15 years of age are all gone."
comments: See CCB2002 for New Potatoes. Seems to mean "new first graders of Junior and High school". Going by Wiki, he picked the earliest age where one should be out of elementary school, and the youngest for being in High. That's why it's not 12 and 15. Of course 3+5=8 and 2+5=7; he's making the usual 7 vs. 8 mistake due to him being messy about the timeline of things. Uncertain of the potato comparison, actually. -GHS
records.assessment: The source parodies 新じゃが, 'new potatoes,' by replacing it with 新処女, 'fresh virgins.' 'Unnew Potatoes New Virgins' is not grammatical and does not communicate the substitution joke.
records.remedy: Use a legible substitution such as 'fresh virgins—like new potatoes, only thirteen or fifteen years old.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Now, all opportunities to meet Unnew Potatoes New Virgins of 13 or 15 years of age are all gone."

records.jp: 「そっちかい」
records.en: Miki: "That's the point then."
comments: Bit disdainful. -GHS
records.assessment: そっちかい is a sharp comic rebuke meaning 'That's what you care about?!' 'That's the point then' flattens both the challenge and its target.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what you're upset about?!'

highlights.text: Miki: "That's the point then."

records.jp: 何ページにも渡っている。
records.en: I pass by several pages.
comments: CP CCA0008
records.assessment: 何ページにも渡っている says the signature exercise extends across many pages. 'I pass by several pages' makes the narrator the subject of an unrelated action.
records.remedy: Use 'It goes on for pages.'

highlights.text: I pass by several pages.

records.jp: いつ頃からかはじまった、俺たちのお遊びだ。
records.en: How long ago it was when we began to play?
comments: See CCC3004. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls this a harmless game of theirs that began at some point. The English turns it into a question about elapsed time and omits the game.
records.remedy: Use 'It's a little game of ours that started somewhere along the way.'

highlights.text: How long ago it was when we began to play?

records.jp: ちょっとあふれた涙を、ぬぐってやりもする。
records.en: Copying that, I go and wipe those tears now overflowing.
comments: Mosuru -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator also wipes away the small spill of tears. 'Copying that' has no source basis, while 'now overflowing' exaggerates the deliberately limited ちょっとあふれた.
records.remedy: Use 'I wipe away the few tears that have spilled over.'

highlights.text: Copying that, I go and wipe those tears now overflowing.

records.jp: わ、俺って紳士。
records.en: Wah, me gentleman.
comments: Girly? -GHS
records.assessment: The mock self-congratulation is a complete exclamation, 'Wow, I'm such a gentleman.' 'Me gentleman' is ungrammatical without reproducing a source-language distortion.
records.remedy: Use 'Wow, I'm such a gentleman.'

highlights.text: Wah, me gentleman.

records.jp: 「なに」
records.en: Taichi: "For what."
records.assessment: In response to thanks, なに dismisses the matter: 'Don't mention it' or 'It's nothing.' 'For what' instead asks a question and changes the social move.
records.remedy: Use 'It's nothing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "For what."

records.jp: 廊下を見渡す。
records.en: I pass my gaze on the corridor.
records.assessment: 見渡す means to look over or scan the corridor. English does not say 'pass my gaze on' a place.
records.remedy: Use 'I look down the corridor.'

highlights.text: I pass my gaze on the corridor.

records.jp: 「しかし、掃除とはね」
records.en: Taichi: "So anyway, cleaning are you."
records.assessment: The Japanese is a lightly surprised 'Cleaning, huh.' 'So anyway, cleaning are you' is ungrammatical and adds a discourse transition.
records.remedy: Use 'Cleaning, huh.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "So anyway, cleaning are you."

records.jp: 「体動かしていた方が落ち着くかなって」
records.en: Miki: "When the body is moving there is relaxation, it's said."
comments: That quoting particle って, with Miki, is all but a nuclear weapon, see CCB0012. -GHS
records.assessment: Miki says she thought moving her body might help her settle down. The English turns this personal, tentative motive into a generic assertion that movement produces relaxation.
records.remedy: Use 'I thought moving around might help me calm down.'

highlights.text: Miki: "When the body is moving there is relaxation, it's said."

records.jp: 手ひどく、容赦なく、一片の同情さえなく。
records.en: No technique, no pity, not one slice of sympathy.
records.assessment: 手ひどく means harshly or severely. 'No technique' is an unrelated sense and breaks the escalating series 'harshly, mercilessly, without a shred of sympathy.'
records.remedy: Use 'Harshly, mercilessly, without a shred of sympathy.'

highlights.text: No technique, no pity, not one slice of sympathy.

records.jp: ０．５秒で奈落に叩き戻した。
records.en: In 0.5" it was beaten back to the hell it came from.
comments: Or the theater basement, apparently there's no difference. ...man, the Japanese must really hate lesb--thespians. -GHS
records.assessment: 奈落 is the abyss into which the suspicion is immediately struck down. 'The hell it came from' adds both a theological location and an origin not specified in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'In half a second, I knock it back into the abyss.'

highlights.text: In 0.5" it was beaten back to the hell it came from.

records.jp: 美希だぞ。
records.en: This is Miki dammit.
records.assessment: The source is simply the self-reminder 'This is Miki.' 'Dammit' adds irritation absent from that corrective beat.
records.remedy: Use 'This is Miki.'

highlights.text: This is Miki dammit.

records.jp: 「ごもっともですのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Quite plausible, I would say."
comments: See below. -GHS
records.assessment: ごもっとも agrees that the reason is entirely fair or reasonable. 'Quite plausible' only judges possibility and weakens the concession.
records.remedy: Use 'Entirely reasonable, I would say.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Quite plausible, I would say."

records.jp: 「それは確かに苦労ですのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "This certainly looks like some work, I would say."
comments: See below. -GHS
records.assessment: 苦労 describes hardship or difficulty, not merely an unspecified amount of work that 'looks like' something.
records.remedy: Use 'That certainly would be difficult, I would say.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "This certainly looks like some work, I would say."

records.jp: 「伝染してますよ」
records.en: Miki: "I've infected you!"
comments: There you go. -GHS
records.assessment: 伝染してます says the speech habit is rubbing off on him. 'I've infected you' adds an explicit agent and turns the playful observation into a claim of deliberate transmission.
records.remedy: Use 'It's rubbing off on you.'

highlights.text: Miki: "I've infected you!"

records.jp: 全人類に足蹴にされることを運命づけられた不幸なる大地と床だけが覗き見ることを許される、秘儀たる領域。
records.en: It is a territory worthy of being called a Sancta Sanctorum this, which is allowed to be peeked only by what is predestined to the misfortune of being stepped upon by all mankind, the ground and the floor.
records.assessment: Although the ornate register is intentional, the English's stacked relative clauses and 'a Sancta Sanctorum this' do not form a grammatical sentence or preserve the source's controlled rhetorical syntax.
records.remedy: Retain the mock-grandiose register in grammatical English, with the ground and floor as the only permitted witnesses.

highlights.text: It is a territory worthy of being called a Sancta Sanctorum this, which is allowed to be peeked only by what is predestined to the misfortune of being stepped upon by all mankind, the ground and the floor.

records.jp: 「ごめん、無意識に手が」
records.en: Taichi: "Sorry, alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own."
comments: CP CCA0009B
records.assessment: The source apologizes that the speaker's hand moved unconsciously. 'Alien hand syndrome' is a specific medicalizing joke added by the translation.
records.remedy: Use 'Sorry—my hand moved without me realizing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sorry, alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own."

records.jp: 「あの、こんなこと俺が言うのもなんだけど……そのランジェリー、とってもセクシーだね。お兄ちゃんちょっびっくりしてる。いい意味で」
records.en: Taichi: "Uhm, I shouldn't exactly be saying this but... that lingerie is veeery sexy innit. Onii-chan is hyyyper surprised. In a good sense."
comments: PCP CCA0009B
records.assessment: If お兄ちゃん is retained as Japanese rather than translated, standard Hepburn requires onī-chan. 'Onii-chan' is nonstandard romanization.
records.remedy: Use an English equivalent or standard Hepburn 'onī-chan.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uhm, I shouldn't exactly be saying this but... that lingerie is veeery sexy innit. Onii-chan is hyyyper surprised. In a good sense."

records.jp: 「恐縮です。いつ手を離していただけますでしょうか」
records.en: Miki: "Much obliged. When will this hand finally distance itself?"
comments: CP CCA0009B
records.assessment: Miki politely asks when the narrator will let go. 'When will this hand finally distance itself?' transfers agency to the hand and changes a direct request into an odd self-movement.
records.remedy: Use 'Much obliged. When might you let go?'

highlights.text: Miki: "Much obliged. When will this hand finally distance itself?"

records.jp: 「そ、その、その下着は、美希の清楚な、下着っ、デルタが、清楚な、体は正直っ、色がっ、しっとり包んでっ、こうっ、子猫ちゃんがっ」
records.en: Taichi: "Th-, that, that underwear, pure and clean Miki, underwear, the delta, pure and clean, body has evidence, the color, gracefully enclosed, like this, that little kitten...!"
records.assessment: The source intentionally fragments under agitation, but key fragments still carry recognizable content. 'Body has evidence' mistranslates 体は正直, and the English sequence loses rather than reproduces the semantic fragments.
records.remedy: Keep the broken syntax while retaining each recoverable fragment, including 'the body is honest' and the enclosing color and texture images.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Th-, that, that underwear, pure and clean Miki, underwear, the delta, pure and clean, body has evidence, the color, gracefully enclosed, like this, that little kitten...!"

records.jp: 「いや、とても無理だ。この手は我が手ではないかのように石化してしまった。鍵っ子が自宅の鍵をキーピックするみたいに気軽に解除することはできない」
records.en: Taichi: "Nope, totally impossible. This hand is as if it were no longer a hand of mine, petrified as it got. Like a young child entrusted with the keys to home yet picking said home's lock, there is no possibility of simple interruption."
comments: Best guess it's about pussy (oh, really, no, you don't say), coming out of one -> latchkey kid, going back into another = picking the lock. Ergo, lockpick is now also a word for dick. You're welcome. See CCC0011C (maybe) -GHS
records.assessment: 解除する means release or undo the petrified grip. 'Simple interruption' neither names the hand's release nor completes the lock-picking analogy.
records.remedy: Use 'I can't release it as casually as a latchkey kid picking the lock to his own house.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nope, totally impossible. This hand is as if it were no longer a hand of mine, petrified as it got. Like a young child entrusted with the keys to home yet picking said home's lock, there is no possibility of simple interruption."

records.jp: 「は、ありがたきお言葉。そろそろお離しいただければ幸いです」
records.en: Miki: "Ah, my appreciation for your courteous words. I would be happy if I could be granted your slow but steady distancing."
records.assessment: Miki says she would appreciate him letting go soon. 'Slow but steady distancing' invents a manner, while 'if I could be granted' obscures who must release whom.
records.remedy: Use 'I appreciate the compliment. I would also appreciate it if you let go now.'

highlights.text: Miki: "Ah, my appreciation for your courteous words. I would be happy if I could be granted your slow but steady distancing."

records.jp: 「ひぃぃぃぃぃぃっ、本気の目ですね！？」
records.en: Taichi: "HyYyYyYy, what's with those serious eyes?!"
comments: Regression into bad translation. If blah blah ぃx7. -GHS
records.assessment: 本気の目ですね asks in alarm whether the look means she is serious about the threat. 'What's with those serious eyes?' notices the eyes but loses that confirmation of intent.
records.remedy: Use 'Those eyes say you mean it, don't they?!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "HyYyYyYy, what's with those serious eyes?!"

records.jp: 「あ、でもずいぶん大人っぽいのを履いてらっしゃるんですね、そのう」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, but, those are some extremely adult things you've come to wear, most assuredly."
records.assessment: 大人っぽい describes the underwear as mature or grown-up in style. 'Adult things' is vague and can imply an entirely different product category.
records.remedy: Use 'Those are rather grown-up panties you're wearing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, but, those are some extremely adult things you've come to wear, most assuredly."

records.jp: 少し赤面して美希。
records.en: Miki grows a bit embarrassed.
records.assessment: 赤面 states the visible action of blushing. 'Grows embarrassed' substitutes an inferred internal state and omits the visual beat.
records.remedy: Use 'Miki blushes slightly.'

highlights.text: Miki grows a bit embarrassed.

records.jp: けどどうしよう、教えた方がいいのかな。
records.en: So, what to do, how should I tell her this?
records.assessment: The narrator wonders whether he should tell her. 'How should I tell her' presupposes that he will and changes a yes-or-no decision into a question of method.
records.remedy: Use 'But what should I do? Should I tell her?'

highlights.text: So, what to do, how should I tell her this?

records.jp: 「あのね、それって玩具下着なんだよ。オープンショーツとかホーニーショーツとか言う」
records.en: Taichi: "say now, those'd be sorta totally play underwear. Open Shorts, or Horny Shorts, they're called."
comments: still girly -GHS
records.assessment: 玩具下着 is adult novelty underwear. 'Play underwear' is not an established English term and obscures the product category that the following explanation depends on.
records.remedy: Use 'They're novelty underwear—what they call open-crotch panties or horny panties.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "say now, those'd be sorta totally play underwear. Open Shorts, or Horny Shorts, they're called."

records.jp: つんつんと指先を見合わせる。
records.en: My fingertips bounce off of each other in the manner of someone aloof and easily irritated.
comments: Tsun-tsun. -GHS
records.assessment: The source shows the speaker touching her index fingertips together in a bashful gesture. The English invents aloofness and irritability, assigning the gesture the opposite social affect.
records.remedy: Use 'I tap my index fingertips together.'

highlights.text: My fingertips bounce off of each other in the manner of someone aloof and easily irritated.

records.jp: ダダダダダダダダダッ
records.en: TrampleTrampleTrample!
records.assessment: The repeated ダ marks rapid running footsteps. 'Trample' describes stepping on or crushing something and gives the sound the wrong action.
records.remedy: Use a rapid footstep effect such as 'DADADADADADA!'

highlights.text: TrampleTrampleTrample!

records.jp: 「俺もよく利用してまーす」
records.en: Taichi: "It is my favorite shop in Kamisaka!"
comments: This seems intended to sound like a testimonial, so even if it's sooorta old-memeish this should work as intended. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says only that the narrator also shops there often. 'Favorite shop in Kamisaka' invents both a superlative preference and a place name absent from the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'I shop there all the time too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is my favorite shop in Kamisaka!"

records.jp: 美希は股間を押さえて、もじもじ脚をすりあわせた。
records.en: Continuing to hold her nethers down she starts rubbing her knees together with a nervous twitch.
records.assessment: 脚 means her legs, which she rubs together. The English narrows the contact to her knees and therefore alters the described movement.
records.remedy: Use 'Holding herself, Miki fidgets and rubs her legs together.'

highlights.text: Continuing to hold her nethers down she starts rubbing her knees together with a nervous twitch.

records.en: Taichi: "...but then."
records.assessment: さて opens a new move as 'now then.' 'But then' introduces an adversative relation that the source does not express.
records.remedy: Use '...Now then.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...but then."

records.jp: 「……ミキミキがこぉんなＨな下着を履いているなんて。不潔」
records.en: Taichi: "...that Miki-Miki would wear something this perverted under her skirt. Filthy!"
records.assessment: The source says only that Miki-Miki is wearing such lewd underwear. 'Under her skirt' adds a location not stated in the line.
records.remedy: Remove 'under her skirt.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...that Miki-Miki would wear something this perverted under her skirt. Filthy!"

records.jp: 「それだけはー！」
records.en: Miki: "But that's insaaane!"
comments: PCP CCA0015
records.assessment: それだけは means 'Anything but that!' or 'Not that!' The English 'that's insane' comments on reasonableness instead of pleading against the threatened consequence.
records.remedy: Use 'Anything but that!'

highlights.text: Miki: "But that's insaaane!"

records.jp: 「いいだろう。では命じる」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't worry. So, this is my command!"
records.assessment: いいだろう accepts the condition: 'Very well.' 'Don't worry' reassures the listener and is a different speech act.
records.remedy: Use 'Very well. Then I command you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't worry. So, this is my command!"

records.jp: 嫌がらない。
records.en: there's no hate.
records.assessment: 嫌がらない says Miki does not resist or show dislike. 'There's no hate' removes her as the experiencer and turns a behavioral beat into an abstract statement.
records.remedy: Use 'She doesn't pull away.'

highlights.text: there's no hate.

records.en: Miki: "...{ae}h?"
comments: Alternative: "I HAVE READ YOUR DIARIES, TAICHI" -GHS
records.assessment: The archaic kana ゑ supplies an intentionally odd 'we/eh?' sound. The literal encoding artifact '{ae}h' is not readable English dialogue.
records.remedy: Use a legible odd reaction such as '...Wha?' while preserving its marked quality.

highlights.text: Miki: "...{ae}h?"

records.jp: 「掃除か、まふまふかだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Cleaning, or Mof Mof!"
records.assessment: The source coinage is まふまふ. If retained as Japanese sound symbolism, standard Hepburn is mafu-mafu; 'Mof Mof' changes both vowels.
records.remedy: Use one consistent English coinage or standard Hepburn 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cleaning, or Mof Mof!"

records.jp: 「まふまふとは？」
records.en: Miki: "And Mof Mof is...?"
records.assessment: This repetition refers to the established coinage まふまふ. 'Mof Mof' is not its standard Hepburn form.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering, such as 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Miki: "And Mof Mof is...?"

records.jp: 「うむ、まふまふとは……」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, Mof Mof would be..."
records.assessment: This repetition refers to the established coinage まふまふ. 'Mof Mof' is not its standard Hepburn form.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering, such as 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, Mof Mof would be..."

records.jp: 「脚と脚の間に顔をつっこんで、まふまふ、まふまふ……」
records.en: Taichi: "You thrust the head in the space between left leg and right leg, then Mof Mof, Mof Mof..."
records.assessment: Both repetitions represent まふまふ. 'Mof Mof' changes the source vowels rather than translating or standardly romanizing the coined sound.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering twice, such as 'mafu-mafu, mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You thrust the head in the space between left leg and right leg, then Mof Mof, Mof Mof..."

records.jp: 「ペッティングっす！」
records.en: Miki: "That's heavy petting!"
records.assessment: ペッティング is 'petting.' The modifier 'heavy' is added and changes the named sexual category.
records.remedy: Use 'That's petting!'

highlights.text: Miki: "That's heavy petting!"

records.jp: 「まふまふとか可愛く称してもだめっす！　ペッティングっす！」
records.en: Miki: "You can't just stick a cute name like Mof Mof to it! It's heavy petting!"
records.assessment: The rebuttal repeats まふまふ and identifies it as ペッティング. 'Mof Mof' is nonstandard romanization, while 'heavy petting' adds a degree absent from the identification.
records.remedy: Use the established rendering of まふまふ and 'petting' without the added modifier.

highlights.text: Miki: "You can't just stick a cute name like Mof Mof to it! It's heavy petting!"

records.jp: 「したいなー、まふまふ」
records.en: Taichi: "Wanna dooo it yeees, Mof Mof..."
records.assessment: The closing まふまふ repeats the established coined term. 'Mof Mof' is not standard Hepburn and breaks the required terminology form.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering, such as 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wanna dooo it yeees, Mof Mof..."

records.jp: 「いやーーーっ、まふまふはいやーーーーーっ！！」
records.en: Miki: "NoOoO! Mof Mof gets a nOOOooo!!!"
comments: ーx3+ーx5=8 -GHS
records.assessment: Both occurrences refer to the established まふまふ coinage. 'Mof Mof' changes the vowels rather than translating or standardly romanizing it.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering in both positions, such as 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Miki: "NoOoO! Mof Mof gets a nOOOooo!!!"

records.jp: 「霧に嫌われるか、それともまふまふか！　開戦か、和平か！」
records.en: Taichi: "Being hated by Kiri, or Mof Mof! Outbreak of war, or maintaining the peace!"
records.assessment: The alternative again uses まふまふ. 'Mof Mof' is not standard Hepburn and should match the established term exactly.
records.remedy: Use the same established rendering, such as 'mafu-mafu.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Being hated by Kiri, or Mof Mof! Outbreak of war, or maintaining the peace!"

records.jp: 「ほれ、モップだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Come one, here's the mop."
records.assessment: 'Come one' is a typographical substitution for the imperative 'Come on.'
records.remedy: Use 'Come on, here's the mop.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Come one, here's the mop."

records.jp: 「モッププレイを？」
records.en: Miki: "Mop playacting?"
records.assessment: プレイ in this context asks about a sexualized 'mop play.' 'Playacting' instead means pretending to perform a role.
records.remedy: Use 'Mop play...?'

highlights.text: Miki: "Mop playacting?"

records.jp: 「掃除してたんだろう？」
records.en: Taichi: "Weren't you cleaning?
records.assessment: The English dialogue is missing its closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Close the quotation after the question mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Weren't you cleaning?

records.jp: 「では、すみやかに掃除を続けたまえ」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore, gladden me with a most prompt continuation of cleaning!"
comments: See CCC0026. -GHS
records.assessment: The command is to continue cleaning promptly. 'Gladden me' adds an emotional purpose not present in the Japanese and distorts the mock-formal order.
records.remedy: Use 'Then promptly continue your cleaning.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore, gladden me with a most prompt continuation of cleaning!"

records.jp: 「望むままにだ」
records.en: Taichi: "That is my desire."
records.assessment: 望むままに means 'as you wished' and refers to Miki's stated desire to clean. 'That is my desire' reverses whose wish is being granted.
records.remedy: Use 'Just as you wished.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "That is my desire."

records.jp: なんのことはない。
records.en: I didn't do enough to cause her problems.
records.assessment: なんのことはない means that it was nothing remarkable. The English invents a claim about not doing enough to cause her problems.
records.remedy: Use 'It was nothing, really.'

highlights.text: I didn't do enough to cause her problems.

records.jp: 自分ではたき落として自分で引き上げただけだ。
records.en: She struck down herself, then she raised back up by herself.
comments: Erroneous reaction to a pattern that was expected but did not occur, continuing the idea that this unreset Miki doesn't yet understand that Taichi's a variable, not a constant. This stuff'd have been so much more obvious if there'd been more choices... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says that he himself knocked her down and then pulled her back up. The English makes Miki perform both actions on herself, reversing the actor.
records.remedy: Use 'I was the one who knocked her down, then pulled her back up.'

highlights.text: She struck down herself, then she raised back up by herself.

records.jp: 「どうしても心がきつくなったら、顔を出してみるといい」
records.en: Taichi: "If your heart grows hard no matter what you do, please show face."
records.assessment: 心がきつくなる means that things become emotionally hard to bear. 'Your heart grows hard' instead suggests becoming callous, while 'show face' calques 顔を出す rather than expressing a visit.
records.remedy: Use 'If it ever becomes too much to bear, try dropping by.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If your heart grows hard no matter what you do, please show face."

records.jp: 誰と話すでもない。
records.en: She has no one to talk to,
records.assessment: 誰と話すでもない says that she is not talking to anyone. 'She has no one to talk to' changes her present action into a claim that no conversational partner is available.
records.remedy: Use 'She isn't talking to anyone.'

highlights.text: She has no one to talk to,

records.jp: 部活に参加するでもない。
records.en: no club activities to join,
comments: These are true for her regardless of whether there's anyone else. -GHS
records.assessment: 部活に参加するでもない says that she is not participating in club activities. 'No club activities to join' instead claims the activities do not exist.
records.remedy: Use 'Nor is she taking part in any club activities.'

highlights.text: no club activities to join,

records.jp: 慣性をもって自らの動力とするしかない。
records.en: There's no point denying that the only motive power left inside is inertia.
records.assessment: The source says that the only option is to use inertia as one's own motive power. 'There's no point denying' adds a rejected act and recasts necessity as an argument about acknowledgment.
records.remedy: Use 'All one can do is turn inertia into one's motive power.'

highlights.text: There's no point denying that the only motive power left inside is inertia.

records.jp: まともな人間たちが全員そろって滅び去り、俺たちだけが生き残った。
records.en: All normal people have perished, all hands lost, and only we have survived.
records.assessment: The source says that every normal person perished. 'All hands lost' adds a maritime idiom and repeats the loss in a register absent from the line.
records.remedy: Remove 'all hands lost.'

highlights.text: All normal people have perished, all hands lost, and only we have survived.

records.jp: 「なんなのよもーっ！」
records.en: Touko: "What's it even now!"
records.assessment: なんなのよもう is an exasperated 'What is it already?!' 'What's it even now' is not grammatical English and does not reproduce the complaint naturally.
records.remedy: Use 'What is it already?!'

highlights.text: Touko: "What's it even now!"

records.jp: ……にゅ？
records.en: ...whyat?
records.assessment: にゅ is a deliberately odd vocalization, not the English interrogative 'what' distorted as 'whyat.' The translation invents a lexical pun.
records.remedy: Use a consistent sound rendering such as '...nyu?'

highlights.text: ...whyat?

records.jp: 身振りをまじえて力説する。
records.en: With major gesticulation mixed in for emphasis.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator argues emphatically while mixing in gestures. The English is a verbless prepositional fragment and omits the act of arguing.
records.remedy: Use 'I make my case emphatically, gestures and all.'

highlights.text: With major gesticulation mixed in for emphasis.

records.jp: 「……必要ない」
records.en: Taichi: "...unneeded."
records.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the speaker of '...No need.' The English labels the line as Taichi, assigning the reply to the wrong character.
records.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...unneeded."

records.jp: 「対話なくして成立しないのだぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "Without dialogue you don't even come to exist!"
records.assessment: 対話なくして成立しない says that the relevant relationship or situation cannot be sustained without dialogue. 'You don't even come to exist' makes the addressee's literal existence depend on it.
records.remedy: Use 'This can't work without dialogue.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Without dialogue you don't even come to exist!"

records.jp: 「話しかけないでよ」
records.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me!"
comments: PCP CCA0013
records.assessment: The source says only 'Don't talk to me.' 'Stay back' adds a demand for physical distance.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't talk to me.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me!"

records.jp: 「キレイな桐原は好きさ」
records.en: Taichi: "I like clean purty Kirhara."
records.assessment: キレイ means pretty or beautiful here, not physically clean. The surname is also misspelled as 'Kirhara.'
records.remedy: Use 'I like pretty Kirihara.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I like clean purty Kirhara."

records.jp: 「アレが！　好きな相手にすることっ！？」
records.en: Touko: "There we go! You just want to be around someone you like, now?!"
records.assessment: The source challenges the preceding conduct: 'That's what you do to someone you like?!' The English instead claims that he now wants to be around someone he likes, replacing the accusation entirely.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what you do to someone you like?!'

highlights.text: Touko: "There we go! You just want to be around someone you like, now?!"

records.jp: 話しかけないでと辛口に言われると、話しかけたくなる。
records.en: When I'm told in harsh tones not to approach or talk, I end up wanting to get close and talk.
comments: CP CCA0013
records.assessment: 話しかける means to speak to someone. The English repeatedly adds physical approach and closeness not stated in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'When I'm sharply told not to talk to her, it makes me want to talk to her.'

highlights.text: When I'm told in harsh tones not to approach or talk, I end up wanting to get close and talk.

records.jp: 話しかけると、また、話しかけないでと辛口に言われる。
records.en: I get close and talk to her, but once more she harshly tells me to stay away and not to talk to her.
comments: CP CCA0013
records.assessment: The source describes speaking to her and being told again not to. 'Get close' and 'stay away' add a separate physical-distance exchange.
records.remedy: Use 'When I do talk to her, she sharply tells me again not to.'

highlights.text: I get close and talk to her, but once more she harshly tells me to stay away and not to talk to her.

records.jp: 『夕食あるかも』
records.en: 『There's dinner perhaps』
comments: CP CCA0012
records.assessment: The English memo retains Japanese corner brackets rather than the edition's English quotation treatment.
records.remedy: Use the established English styling for a written note.

highlights.text: 『There's dinner perhaps』

records.jp: こうしてぼんやりと揺らめく炎を見ていると、心が囚われて、いつまでもいつまでもまどろんでいることができた。
records.en: When I looked at the flickering flame swaying so absentmindedly, my heart was enraptured and I could just doze off endlessly, endlessly.
comments: CP CCA0012
records.assessment: ぼんやり describes the flame's dim, soft appearance or the viewer's hazy absorption. 'The flame swaying absentmindedly' assigns a human mental state to the flame.
records.remedy: Use 'As I gaze at the softly flickering flame...'

highlights.text: When I looked at the flickering flame swaying so absentmindedly, my heart was enraptured and I could just doze off endlessly, endlessly.

records.jp: 以前、それで前髪を焦がしたこともある。
records.en: Once, I even singed my bangs in it because of that.
comments: CP CCA0012
records.assessment: One singes one's bangs on or over a flame, not 'in it.'
records.remedy: Use 'I once even singed my bangs on one.'

highlights.text: Once, I even singed my bangs in it because of that.

records.jp: 泣きそう。
records.en: It's to cry.
comments: CP CCA0012
records.assessment: 泣きそう is the first-person reaction 'I could cry.' 'It's to cry' is ungrammatical and removes the experiencer.
records.remedy: Use 'I could cry.'

highlights.text: It's to cry.

records.jp: 桜庭に押し倒される夢を見た。

comments: CP CCA0013
records.assessment: 押し倒される says the narrator dreams of being pushed or pinned down. 'Pushing himself on me' adds the idiomatic implication of a sexual advance rather than reporting the physical action.
records.remedy: Use 'I dreamed that Sakuraba pinned me down.'

highlights.text: I dreamed of Sakuraba pushing himself on me.

records.jp: ぽかんと、見つめる冬子。
records.en: Touko gazes at it, flabbergasted.
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: ぽかんと describes a blank or dumbfounded stare. 'Flabbergasted' overstates the reaction and omits the visually blank quality.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko stares at it blankly.'

highlights.text: Touko gazes at it, flabbergasted.

records.jp: 「んなわけないでしょ！！　サンドイッチでしょ！」
records.en: Touko: "'s not that at all you know!!! It's a sandwich you know!"
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: The repeated 'you know' and missing subject in ''s not that' are not motivated by the Japanese. The line is an emphatic but ordinary correction.

highlights.text: Touko: "'s not that at all you know!!! It's a sandwich you know!"

records.jp: 手を払われる。
records.en: a swat of her hands,
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: 手を払われる says that the narrator's hand is slapped aside. 'A swat of her hands' changes whose body is struck, pluralizes the hand, and leaves a fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'She slaps my hand away.'

highlights.text: a swat of her hands,

records.jp: 拾う。
records.en: recovered.
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: 拾う is the narrator's present action of picking the sandwich up. 'Recovered' is a subjectless past participle and can mean that the sandwich itself recuperated.
records.remedy: Use 'I pick it up.'

highlights.text: recovered.

records.jp: そっぽを向く。
records.en: Uncooperative.
comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: そっぽを向く describes her physically turning her face away. 'Uncooperative' replaces the visible action with a generalized judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'She turns away.'

highlights.text: Uncooperative.

records.jp: 「自分しか、自分の心配をしてくれる人間がいないのは、つらいだろ？」

highlights.text: Taichi: "Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you... it's painful, right?"

records.jp: 「何言ってるのかわからない」

comments: CP CCA0014A
records.assessment: The English splices a question and 'I don't know' without a conjunction or punctuation. The source simply says she does not understand what he is talking about.

highlights.text: Touko: "What's that even mean I don't know."

records.jp: よろめく。
records.en: Staggering.

records.remedy: Use 'I stagger.'

highlights.text: Staggering.

records.jp: 目頭を押さえて、青い顔をしている。

records.remedy: Use 'She presses the inner corner of her eye, her face pale.'

records.jp: 「冬子！」
records.en: Taichi: "TOUKO!"
records.assessment: If the given name is romanized, standard Hepburn is Tōko. The all-caps 'TOUKO' uses nonstandard vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'TŌKO!' or the edition's normal capitalization with 'Tōko.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "TOUKO!"

records.jp: ぞっとする。

records.assessment: ぞっとする is the narrator's reaction of feeling a chill or horror. 'She's shivering' assigns a visible physical action to Tōko instead.
records.remedy: Use 'A chill runs through me.'

highlights.text: She's shivering.

records.jp: 「気持ち悪い。ふらふらする……吐きそう」

records.assessment: 'Like to throw up' is not grammatical after 'I feel.'
records.remedy: Use 'I feel nauseated and dizzy... I think I'm going to throw up.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I feel nauseous. I feel dizzy... like to throw up."

records.jp: 促す。
records.en: Urgently.
records.assessment: 促す is the narrator's action of urging her. 'Urgently' is an adverb fragment and changes the action into a manner.
records.remedy: Use 'I urge her to.'

highlights.text: Urgently.

records.jp: 冬子は抵抗しなかった。
records.en: Touko had no resistance.
records.assessment: 冬子は抵抗しなかった means that Tōko did not resist. 'Had no resistance' is an unnatural nominal recasting.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko did not resist.'

highlights.text: Touko had no resistance.

records.jp: 失明かな。

comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypotension looks legit -GHS

records.remedy: Use 'Could it be blindness?'

records.jp: 重篤な疾患や、臓器におよぶ大怪我よりはマシだ。

records.assessment: 大怪我 is a major injury, not 'external damage.' The source compares blindness with grave disease or injury extending to the organs.

records.jp: 「冷静にね。パニックにならないで」
records.en: Taichi: "Stay composed, OK? Don't you dare panic."
records.assessment: The source calmly tells her not to panic. 'Don't you dare' adds a threatening or scolding force inconsistent with that instruction.
records.remedy: Use 'Stay calm. Don't panic.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Stay composed, OK? Don't you dare panic."

records.jp: 「目に劇薬を浴びたとか」
records.en: Taichi: "Did you get some powerful medicine or something poisonous on the eyes?"
comments: Accidentally, maybe, but given it's her... -GHS
records.assessment: 劇薬 is a powerful caustic or dangerous chemical. 'Powerful medicine or something poisonous' splits it into vague alternatives and weakens the specific exposure question.
records.remedy: Use 'Did you splash any caustic chemical in your eyes?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Did you get some powerful medicine or something poisonous on the eyes?"

records.jp: 「じゃあ貧血だな」
records.en: Taichi: "Then this was just anemia."
records.assessment: The source tentatively concludes 'Then it's anemia.' 'Just' adds minimization not present in the diagnosis.
records.remedy: Use 'Then it's anemia.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then this was just anemia."

records.jp: 「そういう症状が出ることがあるんだ。気持ち悪いのもそのせいだな」
records.en: Taichi: "The symptoms seem to be all there. It should also cause your feeling of nausea."
records.assessment: The source says anemia can produce symptoms like these and that it also explains the nausea. 'The symptoms seem to be all there' instead claims a complete diagnostic checklist is present.
records.remedy: Use 'Anemia can cause symptoms like that. It would explain the nausea too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The symptoms seem to be all there. It should also cause your feeling of nausea."

records.jp: 「……夏はいつもないの」
records.en: Touko: "...never in Summer."
records.assessment: The omitted topic is appetite: she says she never has one in summer. 'Never in Summer' is an incomplete fragment that does not state what is absent.
records.remedy: Use '...I never have an appetite in summer.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...never in Summer."

records.jp: 「でも貧血が起きるのはまずいよ、先生」
records.en: Taichi: "But an attack of anemia is bad, Sensei!"
comments: As she's a martial artist as well. And in pretty much the same sense he is (not at all). -GHS
records.assessment: If 先生 is retained rather than functionally translated, standard Hepburn is sensei in lowercase, not the capitalized unglossed 'Sensei.'
records.remedy: Use a functional joking address such as 'doctor' or consistent standard Hepburn.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But an attack of anemia is bad, Sensei!"

records.jp: 由来＆語源主義的な浅薄スノッブ連中がだまされそうなナイスガセである。
records.en: A most nice bit of nonsense to deceive the shallow etymologies & legends snobs.
comments: Do keep thinking this is about Purty Words, my dear illiterates. -GHS
records.assessment: 由来＆語源主義的 describes shallow snobs obsessed with origins and etymologies. 'Etymologies & legends snobs' is ungrammatical and changes the first category to legends.
records.remedy: Use 'A fine piece of nonsense for fooling shallow origin-and-etymology snobs.'

highlights.text: A most nice bit of nonsense to deceive the shallow etymologies & legends snobs.

records.jp: 「目はどう？」
records.en: Taichi: "How's the eyes?"
records.assessment: The singular possessive subject calls for 'your eyes,' not 'the eyes' with singular agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'How are your eyes?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "How's the eyes?"

records.jp: ツッコミにも力がない。
records.en: Even her straight-man has no strength.
records.assessment: ツッコミ is her retort or straight-man response. 'Her straight-man' incorrectly labels the person and omits the response itself.
records.remedy: Use 'Even her retort is feeble.'

highlights.text: Even her straight-man has no strength.

records.jp: 「朝のだからな」
records.en: Taichi: "They're this morning's."
comments: Hour is undetermined. Possibly nearing noon. -GHS
records.assessment: The singular sandwich was made that morning. 'They're this morning's' changes the number and leaves the intended explanation unnatural.
records.remedy: Use 'I made it this morning.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "They're this morning's."

records.jp: 「ぐじ」
records.en: Touko: "Sob."
records.assessment: ぐじ is a wet sniffle or choked sob sound. The descriptive word 'Sob' does not render the uttered sound.
records.remedy: Use a sound such as 'Snff.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Sob."

records.jp: 口元を押さえた。
records.en: She clamps down her mouth.
records.assessment: 口元を押さえる means to cover or press a hand to one's mouth. 'Clamps down her mouth' describes forcibly closing the mouth itself.
records.remedy: Use 'She covers her mouth.'

highlights.text: She clamps down her mouth.

records.jp: 首を振る。
records.en: Shake of the head.
records.assessment: 首を振る is a complete action by Tōko. 'Shake of the head' is an unattached noun fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'She shakes her head.'

highlights.text: Shake of the head.

records.jp: 喉が隆起して、水分を摂取する。旺盛に。
records.en: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.
comments: HOLY SHIT SHE'S A TRAP -GHS
records.assessment: The source describes her throat bobbing as she drinks vigorously. 'Giving protuberance as water passes through' is ungrammatical and substitutes an anatomical abstraction for the visible action.
records.remedy: Use 'Her throat bobs as she drinks, voraciously.'

highlights.text: Her throat giving protuberance as water passes through. Vigorously.

records.jp: 「……水分くらい補給してるわけ？」
records.en: Taichi: "...you're not replenishing your fluids regularly?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether she is at least keeping hydrated. The negative English question presupposes that she is not and changes the question's stance.
records.remedy: Use '...You are at least keeping hydrated, aren't you?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...you're not replenishing your fluids regularly?"

records.jp: 「帰る途中で転んで、坂の下に全部落ちた」
records.en: Touko: "They fell on the way home, and rolled all the way to the bottom of a hill."
comments: See CCA0004. I guess they broke too? -GHS
records.assessment: Tōko says that she fell on the way home and dropped everything down the hill. 'They fell' omits her fall and assigns the entire event to the supplies.
records.remedy: Use 'I fell on the way home and dropped everything down the hill.'

highlights.text: Touko: "They fell on the way home, and rolled all the way to the bottom of a hill."

records.jp: 「不器用ちゃんか、おまえは」
records.en: Touko: "Clumsy-chan I'm gonna call ya."
records.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Taichi as the speaker. The English labels the teasing line as Tōko.
records.remedy: Attribute the line to Taichi.

highlights.text: Touko: "Clumsy-chan I'm gonna call ya."

records.jp: 泣きそうになる。
records.en: She became as if to cry.
records.assessment: 泣きそうになる means that she looks or begins to feel as though she may cry. 'Became as if to cry' is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'She looks ready to cry.'

highlights.text: She became as if to cry.

records.jp: 「はー、桐原先生、そりゃ呆けすぎですぜ」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, Kirihara-sensei, you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!"
records.assessment: 呆けすぎ criticizes her as far too absent-minded or foolish. The English forces a comedy-duo 'funny man' explanation into the line and then repeats 'you are.'
records.remedy: Use 'Kirihara-sensei, that was far too absent-minded.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, Kirihara-sensei, you are acting too much like the funny man in a comedy duo you are!"

records.jp: 「人がいなくなったら、そんな価値観は消える」
records.en: Taichi: "If there's no people anymore, then the recognition of values like that disappears."
comments: See CCA0021 -GHS
records.assessment: 価値観 means the values themselves. 'The recognition of values' adds a perceiving act and changes what disappears.
records.remedy: Use 'Once people are gone, values like that disappear.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If there's no people anymore, then the recognition of values like that disappears."

records.jp: 冬子にそれがあるとは思えない。
records.en: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.
records.assessment: それ refers to the strength to live named immediately before, not to the earlier desires. 'Those wants were in Tōko' binds the pronoun to the wrong concept.
records.remedy: Use 'I can't imagine Tōko possesses that strength.'

highlights.text: I didn't think those wants were in Touko.

records.jp: とうに、わかっていたことだ。
records.en: They are something that I discovered, long ago.
records.assessment: The source says 'I had known it for a long time.' 'They are something that I discovered' invents a plural subject and changes settled knowledge into discovery.
records.remedy: Use 'I had known it for a long time.'

highlights.text: They are something that I discovered, long ago.

records.jp: 「世界は人を塗りつぶした。俺たちだけが、『互い』だ」
records.en: Taichi: "This world has painted out all people. We alone are... reciprocal."
comments: Awww don't spoil iiit! -GHS
records.assessment: 俺たちだけが『互い』だ says that the survivors are now one another's only others or counterparts. 'We alone are reciprocal' is not idiomatic and fails to communicate that human relation.
records.remedy: Use 'We are all each other has.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "This world has painted out all people. We alone are... reciprocal."

records.jp: 関わったのだ。望んで。
records.en: There was involvement. A wish for it.
comments: Here with Touko, but also before at the hokora. -GHS
records.assessment: 関わったのだ。望んで states that the narrator chose to become involved. 'There was involvement. A wish for it' removes the acting and choosing subject.
records.remedy: Use 'I got involved because I wanted to.'

highlights.text: There was involvement. A wish for it.

records.jp: この壊れかけの少女を、放置するという選択はない。
records.en: ...the choice to abandon this broken girl to herself will never appear.
comments: Meanwhile, in inaccessible scripts... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says leaving this damaged girl alone is not an option. 'The choice ... will never appear' turns the narrator's decision into an event that may or may not materialize.
records.remedy: Use 'Leaving this damaged girl alone is not an option.'

highlights.text: ...the choice to abandon this broken girl to herself will never appear.

records.jp: 冬子ルートとも言うべき流れに乗って、際まで行って、そこで全てが崩壊したとしても。
records.en: Even if I ride this flow that ought be called the Touko Route, even if I go all the way to the edge, even if nothing is there but Downfall...
comments: Name drop. x2. -GHS
records.assessment: 全てが崩壊した says that everything may collapse at the end. 'Nothing is there but Downfall' changes the event into an abstract destination and adds capitalization.
records.remedy: Use '...even if everything collapses when I reach the end.'

highlights.text: Even if I ride this flow that ought be called the Touko Route, even if I go all the way to the edge, even if nothing is there but Downfall...

records.jp: 今度はその終焉までつきあわないといけない。
records.en: This time, not going together to that demise will be impossible.
records.assessment: The narrator says he must see it through with her to its end. The English's double negative makes that commitment opaque.
records.remedy: Use 'This time, I have to stay with her until the very end.'

highlights.text: This time, not going together to that demise will be impossible.

records.jp: 爛熟という苦痛に苛まれながら。
records.en: While being hailed torment by the agony that is this over-ripeness.
comments: So he can spell "sainamu" as well, see CCA0015C. I'm guessing it's their relationship going spoiled (in more ways than one). -GHS
records.assessment: 苛まれながら means while being tormented by the pain called over-ripeness. 'Being hailed torment' has no grammatical or semantic relation to that construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Tormented all the while by the pain of overripeness.'

highlights.text: While being hailed torment by the agony that is this over-ripeness.

records.jp: 敏感に冬子が反応した。
records.en: Touko's response is sensible.
records.assessment: 敏感に means that Tōko reacts keenly or sensitively. 'Her response is sensible' evaluates its rationality instead.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko reacts at once.'

highlights.text: Touko's response is sensible.

records.jp: 「……どうしても、何？」
records.en: Taichi: "...whatever I do, what?"
records.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the speaker asking him to finish the conditional. The English assigns the line to Taichi.
records.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...whatever I do, what?"

records.jp: 「どうして、人は滅びたんだと思う？」
records.en: Taichi: "What do you think annihilated humanity?"
records.assessment: The source asks why she thinks humanity perished. 'What annihilated humanity' instead asks her to identify an external agent or cause.
records.remedy: Use 'Why do you think humanity perished?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "What do you think annihilated humanity?"

records.jp: 「滅んだんじゃないわ」
records.en: Touko: "This isn't annihilation, no."
records.assessment: Tōko says that humanity did not perish. 'This isn't annihilation' changes the subject from the people to an undefined present situation.
records.remedy: Use 'They didn't perish.'

highlights.text: Touko: "This isn't annihilation, no."

records.jp: 「あ、あの、堂島です」
records.en: Yusa: "Ah, uhm, it's Doujima!"
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 堂島 as Dōjima. 'Doujima' uses a nonstandard vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Dōjima.'

highlights.text: Yusa: "Ah, uhm, it's Doujima!"

records.jp: 「その極道みたいな苗字とは裏腹にキュートな声は……遊紗ちゃん？　あいてるからどーぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: The line misspells 'cute' as 'kyute,' and the retained Japanese given name 遊紗 requires standard Hepburn Yūsa rather than 'Yusa.' The opening noun phrase is also ungrammatically attached.
records.remedy: Use standard Hepburn for the proper name and grammatical English for the contrast.

highlights.text: Taichi: "A gangster-like surname associated with a conversely kyute voice... Yusa-chan? It's open, do come in!"

records.jp: ドアがおそるおそる開き、美少女が立っていた。
records.en: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: The source presents two past actions in sequence. The English shifts from present 'opens' to past 'stood' within one sentence.
records.remedy: Use one consistent tense.

highlights.text: Slowly and carefully the door opens, and there stood a beautiful girl.

records.jp: 「あの、わたし今日が誕生日なんです」
records.en: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."
comments: CP CCA0020
WHYYY would you want anyone to hear this obvious miscut thing twice?! -GHS
records.assessment: The source directly states that today is her birthday. 'Today would be my birthday' introduces an unsupported conditional mood.
records.remedy: Use 'Today is my birthday.'

highlights.text: Yusa: "Uhm, it's that today would be my birthday."

records.jp: 「へえ、そうだったのか」
records.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, it was, right."
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: 'It was, right' is not an idiomatic response to learning the fact.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh, is that right?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, it was, right."

records.jp: 「それと、交換日記を明日提出できたらなと思ったので……」
records.en: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: The source says she hoped she could submit the exchange diary tomorrow. The English leaves 'I thought, so I could' as an incomplete causal construction.
records.remedy: Use 'And I was hoping I could turn in the exchange diary tomorrow...'

highlights.text: Yusa: "And also, I thought, so I could hand in the exchange diary tomorrow..."

records.jp: この娘は驚くと絶句する癖があった。
records.en: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.
comments: PCP CCA0020
Another older revision, this was slightly more formal. -GHS
records.assessment: The source neutrally says she has a habit of becoming speechless when surprised. 'Bad habit' adds disapproval, and 'don't she' is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'She has a habit of falling speechless whenever she is surprised.'

highlights.text: This young lady has the bad habit of losing words when surprised, don't she.

records.jp: 「その質問、毎回しますよね、太一さん？」
records.en: Yusa: "That question... you just ask me that every time, right Taichi-san?"
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: The vocative needs punctuation, and 'you just ask me that every time' has unnatural adverb placement.
records.remedy: Use 'You ask that every time, don't you, Taichi?'

highlights.text: Yusa: "That question... you just ask me that every time, right Taichi-san?"

records.jp: 「きょーしゅーです」
records.en: Yusa: "Trainingful then!"
comments: CP CCA0020
records.assessment: きょーしゅー represents the sound of 教習, training or instruction. 'Trainingful' is not an English word.
records.remedy: Use a legible first member of the sound chain, such as 'Training.'

highlights.text: Yusa: "Trainingful then!"

records.jp: きょーしゅー。
records.en: Calisthenics.
comments: Oh dear, adapting. Should now tie to CCA0030, as well as many themes of the story, as likely intended. Except, see CCA0020: this is just her misreading becoming fixed. -GHS
records.assessment: The repeated きょーしゅー continues the same broad sound. 'Calisthenics' narrows it to physical exercise and weakens the pivot to the following homophones.
records.remedy: Keep the same sound-linked rendering used in the preceding line.

highlights.text: Calisthenics.

records.jp: 郷愁？
records.en: To reduce homesickness?
comments: Another homonym, but as the term fits strongly in the religious sense, overadapted. -GHS
records.assessment: 郷愁 is nostalgia. 'To reduce homesickness?' invents an action and purpose rather than naming the homophone.
records.remedy: Use 'Nostalgia?'

highlights.text: To reduce homesickness?

records.jp: 強襲。
records.en: Violence.
records.assessment: 強襲 means an assault or raid. 'Violence' is broader and loses the exact homophone in the sequence.
records.remedy: Use 'Assault.'

highlights.text: Violence.

records.jp: 強襲。
records.en: Violence.
records.assessment: The repeated 強襲 again means assault or raid, not generic violence.
records.remedy: Repeat the established rendering 'Assault.'

highlights.text: Violence.

records.jp: そう、強襲。
records.en: Training in violence.
records.assessment: 強襲 means assault or raid and resolves the preceding homophone chain. 'Training in violence' combines two earlier mistranslations and does not name the word.
records.remedy: Use 'Yes. Assault.'

highlights.text: Training in violence.

records.jp: 激しく、攻めること。
records.en:
Intense, turbulent, or furious
and often destructive action.
comments: PCP Merriam-Webster
records.assessment: The source immediately glosses the word as attacking fiercely. The English substitutes a generic dictionary-style definition of intense or destructive action and omits the attack.
records.remedy: Use 'To attack fiercely.'

highlights.text:
Intense, turbulent, or furious
and often destructive action.

records.jp: 俺はこの言葉が、好きだな。
records.en: I really love those words, don't I!
records.assessment: この言葉 is singular, 'this word.' 'Those words' changes the number, while 'don't I' adds self-confirmation.
records.remedy: Use 'I like that word.'

highlights.text: I really love those words, don't I!

records.jp: 夢の中で嗤う。
records.en: I laugh so hard within my dream.
comments: Context is below so didn't go too specific on this. -GHS
records.assessment: 嗤う is a derisive laugh or sneer. 'Laugh so hard' describes intensity rather than scorn and adds a degree absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use 'I sneer in my dream.'

highlights.text: I laugh so hard within my dream.

records.jp: 殺さば殺す。
records.en: If killing needs be, killing it will be.
comments: ...though the figure of speech seems closer to "I defy you". See CCZAS. Aliens are enemy, even if aliens are Miki. -GHS
records.assessment: 殺さば殺す is retaliatory: if the enemy kills, kill in return. 'If killing needs be' changes that conditional relation into a general judgment of necessity.
records.remedy: Use 'If they kill, kill them.'

highlights.text: If killing needs be, killing it will be.

records.jp: 教室に顔を出すと、冬子がいた。
records.en: When I showed face in the classroom, Touko was there.
records.assessment: 教室に顔を出す means to drop by or look into the classroom. 'Showed face' is a literal calque rather than idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'When I dropped by the classroom, Tōko was there.'

highlights.text: When I showed face in the classroom, Touko was there.

records.jp: 髪の毛もほつれて。
records.en: Hair frayed as well.
records.assessment: Her hair is disheveled or coming loose. Hair itself is not 'frayed' like fabric or rope.
records.remedy: Use 'Her hair was disheveled too.'

highlights.text: Hair frayed as well.

records.jp: 関心ない様子で机に顔を伏せる。
records.en:
She lays her face on the desk, looking
disinterested.
records.assessment: 机に顔を伏せる means to lower or bury one's face against the desk. 'Lays her face on the desk' is not idiomatic for that posture.
records.remedy: Use 'She lowers her face to the desk, apparently indifferent.'

highlights.text:
She lays her face on the desk, looking
disinterested.

records.jp: 冬子は誰にも触れないまま、朽ちていくのだろうか。
records.en:
Seems Touko has stayed like this, not touching
nor touched by anybody, rotting away.
records.assessment: 誰にも触れないまま says she may decay without ever reaching or touching anyone. 'Nor touched by anybody' adds a passive reciprocal condition not expressed in the line.
records.remedy: Use 'Will Tōko rot away without ever reaching anyone?'

highlights.text:
Seems Touko has stayed like this, not touching
nor touched by anybody, rotting away.

records.jp: 困惑と戸惑いを貼りつけて、彼女は伏していた顔をあげた。
records.en: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.
comments: CP CCA0028
records.assessment: The source figuratively says she raises her lowered face wearing confusion and bewilderment. 'Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment' incorrectly makes one emotion adhere to another.
records.remedy: Use 'Wearing an expression of confusion, she raises her lowered face.'

highlights.text: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.

records.en: Taichi: "No?"
records.assessment: The tag question な seeks agreement or gently urges acceptance: 'Right?' 'No?' reverses its polarity.
records.remedy: Use 'Right?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "No?"

records.jp: 机に水筒とサンドイッチの包みを置いた。
records.en: I put a bundle of sandwiches and the canteen on her desk,
records.assessment: サンドイッチの包み is one wrapped sandwich or sandwich package. 'A bundle of sandwiches' changes the quantity and object.
records.remedy: Use 'I set the wrapped sandwich and canteen on her desk.'

highlights.text: I put a bundle of sandwiches and the canteen on her desk,

records.jp: 掠れた声。
records.en: A husked voice.
records.assessment: 掠れた声 is a hoarse or rasping voice. 'Husked voice' uses the wrong participle.
records.remedy: Use 'A hoarse voice.'

highlights.text: A husked voice.

records.jp: ゆっくりと手が伸びる。
records.en: Slowly she reaches with her hands,
records.assessment: The Japanese subject is one hand. 'Her hands' changes the number and leaves the clause hanging into the next line.
records.remedy: Use 'A hand slowly reaches out.'

highlights.text: Slowly she reaches with her hands,

records.jp: 小さく、囓る。
records.en: and gives tiny gnaws.
records.assessment: 小さく囓る means to take a small nibble. 'Gives tiny gnaws' is not idiomatic English and pluralizes the single action.
records.remedy: Use 'She takes a tiny bite.'

highlights.text: and gives tiny gnaws.

records.jp: 振り払われる。
records.en: Shaken off.
records.assessment: 振り払われる says the narrator's intervention or hand is brushed away. 'Shaken off' omits both actor and object and reads as an unattached participle.
records.remedy: Use 'She brushes me off.'

highlights.text: Shaken off.

records.jp: 挙措は弱々しかったが、拒絶の意志は確かだった。
records.en: Her behavior is feeble, but there is also an intent of rejection, definitely.
records.assessment: The source contrasts her weak movements with a definite will to reject him. The English's 'there is also ... definitely' is ungrammatical and weakens that contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'Her movements were feeble, but her rejection was unmistakable.'

highlights.text: Her behavior is feeble, but there is also an intent of rejection, definitely.

records.jp: 「これ、もらうわ」
records.en: Touko: "I'll... take this yes."
records.assessment: The source simply says 'I'll take this.' The appended 'yes' has no source basis and produces unnatural syntax.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll take this.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I'll... take this yes."

records.jp: 「家で食べるから」
records.en: Touko: "So I'll eat it home."
records.assessment: English requires 'eat it at home,' not 'eat it home.'
records.remedy: Use 'I'll eat it at home.'

highlights.text: Touko: "So I'll eat it home."

records.jp: 「そう……なのか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Will you... you sure?"
records.assessment: そうなのか is a hesitant acknowledgment, 'I see' or 'Is that so?' 'Will you ... you sure?' invents a question about future certainty and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'I see...?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Will you... you sure?"

records.jp: 「それが、新しい部活なんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Those will be new club activities, then."
records.assessment: それ refers to the SOS-broadcasting activity as the new club activity. 'Those' incorrectly points back to multiple settings and changes the number.
records.remedy: Use 'That will be the new club activity.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Those will be new club activities, then."

records.jp: 「……そうね」
records.en: Touko: "...I'd say."
records.assessment: そうね gives agreement: 'Yes' or 'I suppose so.' 'I'd say' is an incomplete attribution without a proposition.
records.remedy: Use '...I suppose so.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...I'd say."

records.jp: 一瞬で。
records.en: For a moment.
records.assessment: 一瞬で means that the object was destroyed in an instant. 'For a moment' describes duration and loses the speed of destruction.
records.remedy: Use 'In an instant.'

highlights.text: For a moment.

records.jp: 彼女は破壊された尖塔の足下にいた。
records.en: She was standing underfoot the wrecked spire.
records.assessment: 尖塔の足下 means at the foot of the ruined spire. 'Standing underfoot the spire' reverses the spatial relation and is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'She stood at the foot of the ruined spire.'

highlights.text: She was standing underfoot the wrecked spire.

records.jp: 肩に触れるはずだった手が空を切る。
records.en: My hand that expected to touch a shoulder cuts empty air.
records.assessment: The narrator's hand, which was about to touch her shoulder, meets empty air. The English makes the hand 'expect' the touch and uses an indefinite shoulder.
records.remedy: Use 'The hand I meant to place on her shoulder cuts through empty air.'

highlights.text: My hand that expected to touch a shoulder cuts empty air.

records.jp: 押し出すように言った。
records.en: Words that felt like they were shoving me away.
records.assessment: The source says she forces or pushes the words out. The English instead makes the words themselves feel as if they are shoving the narrator away, adding him as an object.
records.remedy: Use 'She forces the words out.'

highlights.text: Words that felt like they were shoving me away.

records.jp: 胸が軋んだ。
records.en: The heart creaks,
records.assessment: 胸 is the narrator's chest or heart in this moment, and the narration is past tense. 'The heart creaks' makes it generic and shifts tense.
records.remedy: Use 'My heart creaked.'

highlights.text: The heart creaks,

records.jp: 三人の視線が、先輩に向く。
records.en: Three sightlines turn to Senpai.
records.assessment: 視線 means the three people's gazes. 'Sightlines' is a technical spatial term rather than their act of looking.
records.remedy: Use 'All three gazes turn toward Senpai.'

highlights.text: Three sightlines turn to Senpai.

records.jp: 「……私なわけないじゃないですか」
records.en: Misato: "...it cannot be me can it now?"
records.assessment: The denial requires normal interrogative punctuation and word order. 'It cannot be me can it now' is ungrammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'It couldn't have been me, could it?'

highlights.text: Misato: "...it cannot be me can it now?"

records.jp: 「……自分で作って、自分で壊す人がいるわけないでしょう？」
records.en: Misato: "...there are no people who would build something themselves, then tear it down themselves you know?"
records.assessment: The source's rhetorical question ends with でしょう. Appending 'you know' adds a conversational tag and produces clumsy English.
records.remedy: Use 'No one would build something themselves and then destroy it, would they?'

highlights.text: Misato: "...there are no people who would build something themselves, then tear it down themselves you know?"

records.jp: そういう人もいたが。
records.en: There would have been people that act like that,
records.assessment: The source concedes that people like that did exist. 'There would have been people that act' mixes a past conditional with present tense.
records.remedy: Use 'There were people like that, though.'

highlights.text: There would have been people that act like that,

records.jp: いや？
records.en: Well then?
records.assessment: いや？ marks a reconsideration: 'Wait?' or 'Or...?' 'Well then?' instead advances the discussion and loses the self-correction.
records.remedy: Use 'Wait.'

highlights.text: Well then?

records.jp: 可能性はあるのか。
records.en: That possibility seems to exist.
records.assessment: 可能性はあるのか is a question about whether the possibility exists. 'That possibility seems to exist' changes it into an assertion.
records.remedy: Use 'Is that possible?'

highlights.text: That possibility seems to exist.

records.jp: 「完成したら、逃避先がなくなるから」
records.en: Tomoki: "Because once it's completed, there's nowhere ahead to escape to."
records.assessment: 逃避先 is a refuge or place to escape to. 'Nowhere ahead' adds a directional idea absent from the source.
records.remedy: Use 'Because once it was finished, you'd have nowhere left to escape to.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because once it's completed, there's nowhere ahead to escape to."

records.jp: そういうこともあり得る。
records.en: That is something that can be.
records.assessment: あり得る means that such a thing is possible. 'Something that can be' is an unnatural nominal calque.
records.remedy: Use 'That is possible.'

highlights.text: That is something that can be.

records.jp: 特に先輩は。群青の人間だから。
records.en: Especially with Senpai. Because she's one of the ultramarines of Gunjou.
comments: The word 'human' will be seeing you later. -GHS
records.assessment: 群青の人間 identifies her as a person of Gunjō, the established institution. 'One of the ultramarines of Gunjou' mistakes the proper institutional shorthand for the color noun and uses nonstandard romanization.
records.remedy: Use 'Especially Senpai, since she's one of Gunjō's.'

highlights.text: Especially with Senpai. Because she's one of the ultramarines of Gunjou.

records.jp: 「ちょっと待って。いくらなんでもそんな……」
records.en: Misato: "Wait a second! Things might be somewhat like that but this..."
records.assessment: いくらなんでもそんな rejects the accusation as going too far. 'Things might be somewhat like that but this' partially concedes it and is not grammatical.
records.remedy: Use 'Wait. Even so, that's going too far...'

highlights.text: Misato: "Wait a second! Things might be somewhat like that but this..."

records.jp: 「……げ、三馬鹿」
records.en: Touko: "...yuck, the three stooges."
comments: CP CCA0030
Nice consistency with her route, here. Budget problems? Eh, let's take it to mean the usual: plus ca change... -GHS
records.assessment: 三馬鹿 is simply 'the three idiots.' 'The Three Stooges' imports a specific American comedy allusion absent from the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use '...ugh, the three idiots.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...yuck, the three stooges."

records.jp: 「壊されたんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "It's been broken."
records.assessment: The passive 壊された states that someone deliberately destroyed it. 'It's been broken' can describe an accidental state and weakens the agentive contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'Someone destroyed it.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's been broken."

records.jp: 冬子の眉根が寄る。
records.en: The gap between Touko's eyebrows grows tighter.
records.assessment: 眉根が寄る means her brows knit. 'The gap between her eyebrows grows tighter' awkwardly describes geometry rather than the expression.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko's brows knit.'

highlights.text: The gap between Touko's eyebrows grows tighter.

records.jp: 「それって」
records.en: Touko: "But then..."
records.assessment: それって introduces an unfinished inference: 'You mean...' 'But then' supplies an adversative transition not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'You mean...'

highlights.text: Touko: "But then..."

records.jp: 「そうですよ、愉快なわけない……自分で壊すなんて……ありえない……」
records.en: Misato: "It is not, not pleasant at all... that I would have broken it... cannot be..."
records.assessment: The fragmented Japanese remains a first-person denial that she could have destroyed it herself. The English's 'that I would have broken it ... cannot be' is grammatically broken and obscures the denied action.
records.remedy: Use 'Of course it isn't pleasant... But there's no way I destroyed it myself...'

highlights.text: Misato: "It is not, not pleasant at all... that I would have broken it... cannot be..."

records.jp: 「絶対、違います」
records.en: Misato: "It is... absolutely mistaken."
records.assessment: 絶対、違います is an emphatic denial: 'It absolutely wasn't me' or 'That's absolutely wrong.' 'It is absolutely mistaken' sounds like an abstract classification and weakens the personal denial.
records.remedy: Use 'It absolutely wasn't me.'

highlights.text: Misato: "It is... absolutely mistaken."

records.jp: 「そうでしょう、先輩？」
records.en: Taichi: "Is that right, Senpai?"
records.assessment: そうでしょう seeks confirmation of the assertion just made: 'That's right, isn't it?' 'Is that right?' instead presents the speaker as unsure of the fact.
records.remedy: Use 'That's right, isn't it, Senpai?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Is that right, Senpai?"

records.jp: 「それが先輩にとっての部活動だった」
records.en: Taichi: "These were club activities as far as Senpai is concerned."
records.assessment: それ is the singular project or activity and the source describes what it was for Senpai. 'These were club activities' changes both number and aspect.
records.remedy: Use 'That was Senpai's club activity.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "These were club activities as far as Senpai is concerned."

records.jp: 「あながち逃避とも言えない。先があるからな」
records.en: Taichi: "It can't be said it was entirely flight. Because there's also a destination."
records.assessment: 先がある says the activity has a future or something beyond the present. 'There is also a destination' turns that temporal possibility into a physical endpoint.
records.remedy: Use 'You can't simply call it escapism. It was aimed at a future.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It can't be said it was entirely flight. Because there's also a destination."

records.jp: 「あまり思い詰めないで」
records.en: Taichi: "Do not concern yourself too much about this."
records.assessment: 思い詰める means to brood, become obsessed, or work oneself into a state. 'Concern yourself' is much milder and misses that escalation.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't brood over it too much.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Do not concern yourself too much about this."

records.jp: 「ちょっと、なにどさくさにまぎれて耳触ってるのよ！」
records.en: Touko: "Wait, what are you whispering niceties in her ears under the cover of all this confusion!"
comments: Although I still want to read 耳触 (touching her ears) literally, because, well, Mimi-senpai. -GHS
records.assessment: 耳触ってる explicitly accuses him of touching her ear. 'Whispering niceties in her ears' replaces the physical act with speech and invents its content.
records.remedy: Use 'Hey! Why are you taking advantage of the confusion to touch her ear?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Wait, what are you whispering niceties in her ears under the cover of all this confusion!"

records.jp: 「こうすると落ち着くんだよ」
records.en: Taichi: "To make her calm down of course."
records.assessment: The source states that doing this calms her. 'To make her calm down of course' recasts it as a purpose phrase and adds 'of course.'
records.remedy: Use 'This calms her down.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "To make her calm down of course."

records.jp: 冬子に目線を送る。
records.en: I send eye signals to Touko.
records.assessment: 目線を送る means to give or shoot Tōko a meaningful look. 'Send eye signals' is an unnatural technical calque.
records.remedy: Use 'I shoot Tōko a look.'

highlights.text: I send eye signals to Touko.

records.jp: 「どうして怒られないといけないわけ……」
records.en: Touko: "What is it that you even have to get angry for now..."
records.assessment: Tōko asks why she has to be scolded. 'Why you have to get angry' changes the subject to Taichi and reframes the complaint as a question about his emotion.
records.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to get yelled at...?'

highlights.text: Touko: "What is it that you even have to get angry for now..."

records.jp: 「ＯＫ、犯人捜しはもうやめだ！　さってと皆の衆、こいつをチャチャッと修理すればＳＯＳでヒューマンドラマだぞ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Okay, culprit search stops here!"
comments: HACK split line, does look better like this. -GHS
