records.assessment: 階下に is a direction fragment equivalent to 'Downstairs.' 'To downstairs' is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'Downstairs.'

highlights.text: To downstairs.

records.jp: 戸棚類をあさる。
records.en: I rustle in the cupboard.
records.assessment: 戸棚類をあさる means rummaging through the cupboards or cabinets. 'Rustle in the cupboard' names a sound or slight movement and incorrectly narrows the plural storage furniture.
records.remedy: Use 'I rummage through the cupboards.'

highlights.text: I rustle in the cupboard.

records.jp: コショウがあった。
records.en: There was a pepperful of exaggeration.
comments: "There were some peppers" + "that was exaggerated". -GHS
records.assessment: The source simply finds pepper. 'A pepperful of exaggeration' invents a pun and an abstract quantity unrelated to the item discovered.
records.remedy: Use 'There is pepper.'

highlights.text: There was a pepperful of exaggeration.

records.jp: ジャガイモもあったぞ。
records.en: There was some Solanum Tuberosum (potatoes), too!
records.assessment: The source finds potatoes. Adding the Latin binomial 'Solanum Tuberosum' invents mock-scientific narration not present in the Japanese and disrupts the inventory sequence.
records.remedy: Use 'There are potatoes too!'

highlights.text: There was some Solanum Tuberosum (potatoes), too!

records.jp: 机の上に、それらを並べる。
records.en: I line them up over the table.
records.assessment: Objects are arranged 'on' a table in English. 'Over the table' suggests suspension above it.
records.remedy: Use 'I arrange them on the table.'

highlights.text: I line them up over the table.

records.jp: 剃毛する時にも似た音を立て、塩ふり生ジャガイモを齧る。
records.en: Unable to resist the appeeling sound of the act, I add salt on a potato I had a-peeled and took a bite.
comments: Originally: "similarly to the peeling sound", which is sho-ri (vs. salt shiori). Replaced with a pun that should be about as awful. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he bites a salted raw potato, producing a sound like shaving. The English instead says he peels it because the sound is 'appeeling,' invents repeated English puns, and changes the described action sequence.
records.remedy: Use 'Making a sound like shaving, I bite into the salted raw potato.'

highlights.text: Unable to resist the appeeling sound of the act, I add salt on a potato I had a-peeled and took a bite.

records.jp: 「ほー、これが新ジャガの風味かぁ、んがぐぐ……適度に固くて、まるで石のよう……」
records.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, this is the taste of a tiny little New Potato then, mnghmngh... so moderately adamantine, almost at the levels of a rock..."
comments: I don't think the term New Potato is as evident as 新ジャガ is. also hungry nau. んがぐぐ seems to be a reference to Sazae-san, like (possibly) the one in CCA0022. See CCD2002. ...seriously, the stuff I google... -GHS
records.assessment: 新ジャガ is a new-season potato, not necessarily 'tiny little.' 'Almost at the levels of a rock' is also an ungrammatical degree comparison.
records.remedy: Use 'So this is what a new potato tastes like... Firm enough to be almost like a rock.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, this is the taste of a tiny little New Potato then, mnghmngh... so moderately adamantine, almost at the levels of a rock..."

records.jp: 「って、食えるかこんなモン！　なめんな！」
records.en: Taichi: "Wait, is this crap even edible?! Don't be pulling my leg!"
comments: Belly bug talking now, see above.
records.assessment: なめんな means 'Don't mess with me' or 'Don't underestimate me.' 'Don't be pulling my leg' instead accuses an interlocutor of joking or deceiving him.
records.remedy: Use 'Like I can eat this! Don't mess with me!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wait, is this crap even edible?! Don't be pulling my leg!"

records.jp: 投げつけた。
records.en: I tossed it.
records.assessment: 投げつける is to hurl or fling something forcefully. 'Tossed' weakens the sudden violent rejection.
records.remedy: Use 'I hurl it away.'

highlights.text: I tossed it.

records.jp: 「ペッペッ、芽まで囓っちまった！　毒なのに！（本当）」
records.en: Taichi: "Pah! pah! I gnawed it to the bud! This stuff's poisonous! (Seriously.)"
comments: See Higurashi 1, the "needle in the food" scene. Interesting. -GHS
records.assessment: 芽 is the potato sprout or eye, not a flower bud. He says he bit even that toxic part; 'gnawed it to the bud' instead describes reaching a destination.
records.remedy: Use 'Ptooey! I even bit into a sprout—and those are poisonous! (True.)'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Pah! pah! I gnawed it to the bud! This stuff's poisonous! (Seriously.)"

records.jp: 愕然とする。
records.en: Terror ensues.
records.assessment: 愕然とする is the narrator becoming stunned or appalled. 'Terror ensues' turns his reaction into an abstract event and overstates its emotional quality.
records.remedy: Use 'I am stunned.'

highlights.text: Terror ensues.

records.jp: そのくらいの度量が民にもいるってことだね。
records.en: That's how much magnanimity people have, don't they.
records.assessment: The source says the people need that much generosity or tolerance. 'That's how much magnanimity people have' changes necessity into a claim about what they already possess.
records.remedy: Use 'The people need at least that much generosity of spirit.'

highlights.text: That's how much magnanimity people have, don't they.

records.jp: 電話をかける。
records.en: I pick up the telephone.
records.assessment: 電話をかける means to place a telephone call. 'Pick up the telephone' only describes lifting the receiver and omits the call.
records.remedy: Use 'I make a call.'

highlights.text: I pick up the telephone.

records.jp: 人生後悔だらけ。
records.en: The life of a human is filled with regrets.
records.assessment: 人生後悔だらけ is a first-person comic lament that his life is full of regrets. 'The life of a human' universalizes it into a general philosophical claim.
records.remedy: Use 'My life is full of regrets.'

highlights.text: The life of a human is filled with regrets.

records.jp: 「そうか、じゃがいもがあるんだった」
records.en: Taichi: "Well then, I only got potatoes."
records.assessment: The narrator remembers that he has potatoes. 'Only' adds scarcity emphasis, and 'got' shifts the standing possession into acquisition.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh, right—I have potatoes.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then, I only got potatoes."

records.jp: ジャガイモに一人一人名前をつける。
records.en: Baptize the potatoes one by one.
records.assessment: The recipe says to give each potato a name. 'Baptize' adds a specifically religious naming ceremony and changes the comic instruction's register.
records.remedy: Use 'Give each potato a name.'

highlights.text: Baptize the potatoes one by one.

records.jp: ホイルに包んだジャガイモを断腸の思いで石に放り込む（風味が増す）。
records.en:
Toss the tinfoil into which the potatoes are
wrapped onto the stones while reminiscing of
your broken heart (improves the taste).
records.assessment: 断腸の思いで means throwing them in with heart-rending reluctance. 'While reminiscing of your broken heart' changes immediate emotion into second-person recollection and is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'With a heavy heart, throw the foil-wrapped potatoes onto the stones. (Improves the flavor.)'

highlights.text:
Toss the tinfoil into which the potatoes are
wrapped onto the stones while reminiscing of
your broken heart (improves the taste).

records.jp: 待つのをやめ。
records.en: Cease thy waiting.
records.assessment: The source is a plain recipe-like imperative to stop waiting. 'Thy' invents an archaic second-person register.
records.remedy: Use 'Stop waiting.'

highlights.text: Cease thy waiting.

records.jp: 腹の虫を止め。
records.en: Stop thy belly bug.
comments: Just for rhyme-ish-ing-sorta. -vaguely. -GHS
records.assessment: The source continues the plain parallel instructions. 'Thy' again adds archaic diction not present in the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'Silence the creature in your belly.'

highlights.text: Stop thy belly bug.

records.jp: 食す。
records.en: Devour.
records.assessment: 食す is a formal or mock-formal 'eat.' 'Devour' adds speed and voracity not contained in the verb.
records.remedy: Use 'Eat.' or a comparably mock-formal English verb.

highlights.text: Devour.

records.jp: 生きてるなぁ、俺。
records.en: Alive aren't I, me.
records.assessment: 生きてるなぁ、俺 is a complete reflective exclamation: 'I'm alive.' 'Alive aren't I, me' duplicates the subject and uses malformed inversion.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm alive, all right.'

highlights.text: Alive aren't I, me.

records.jp: 桐原冬子その人だった。
records.en: The person in question was Kirihara Touko.
records.assessment: If the given name 冬子 is romanized, standard Hepburn is Tōko. 'Touko' uses an unmarked long-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Kirihara Tōko.'

highlights.text: The person in question was Kirihara Touko.

records.jp: 「しゃべった」
records.en: Taichi: "It spoke!"
comments: See CCB2013. -GHS
records.assessment: しゃべった means that the woman spoke. 'It spoke' replaces the human subject with an inanimate pronoun and adds a dehumanizing implication not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'She spoke.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It spoke!"

records.jp: つらそうである。
records.en: Appears in pain.
records.assessment: The source gives a complete observation that she appears to be suffering. 'Appears in pain' omits the subject and leaves an English fragment.
records.remedy: Use 'She looks as though she is in pain.'

highlights.text: Appears in pain.

records.jp: 「どうした？」
records.en: Touko: "What're you here for?"
records.assessment: どうした asks what is wrong with the person. 'What're you here for?' instead asks her purpose in coming and omits concern for her condition.
records.remedy: Use 'What's wrong?'

highlights.text: Touko: "What're you here for?"

records.jp: 「ふむ。その匂いをたどってここまで？」
records.en: Taichi: "Hoh. You followed said smell to here then?"
records.assessment: The source asks whether she followed the smell this far. 'Said smell' is unsupported legalistic diction, and 'to here' is not idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'Hm. You followed the smell all the way here?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hoh. You followed said smell to here then?"

records.jp: 反応がなくなった。
records.en: She no longer is capable of a response.
comments: "There was no response" + "The response was dying". -GHS
records.assessment: 反応がなくなった says she stopped responding. 'No longer is capable of a response' adds a claim of incapacity and switches into an awkward present state.
records.remedy: Use 'She stops responding.'

highlights.text: She no longer is capable of a response.

records.jp: 俺は三つ目のじゃがいもを食べ終わってから、冬子の体を引き起こした。
records.en: Once I finished eating my third potato, I dragged Touko's body over.
comments: WHAT'S HE GONNA DO TO THIS POOR CADAVER NOOOOO -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator pulls Tōko's body upright after finishing the potato. 'Dragged ... over' changes the direction to horizontal relocation and makes the action sound like moving a corpse.
records.remedy: Use 'After finishing my third potato, I pull Tōko upright.'

highlights.text: Once I finished eating my third potato, I dragged Touko's body over.

records.jp: 冬子がじゃがいもを貪り食う。
records.en: Touko most greedily devours potatoes.
comments: Annnd graphics failure again. She should be eating a potato no bigger than her eyes FFS. -GHS
records.assessment: 貪り食う already means to devour greedily. 'Most greedily' adds a superlative degree not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko greedily devours the potatoes.'

highlights.text: Touko most greedily devours potatoes.

records.jp: 調味料もかけずに。
records.en: Without adding any flavoring.
records.assessment: 調味料 means seasoning or condiment, not generic 'flavoring.'
records.remedy: Use 'Without adding any seasoning.'

highlights.text: Without adding any flavoring.

records.jp: 咀嚼してない時間があってはならないとばかりに。
records.en: Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew.
records.assessment: The source says she eats as if she cannot allow even a moment when she is not chewing. 'Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew' says the opposite: that she lacks time for chewing.
records.remedy: Use 'As though she could not permit a single moment without chewing.'

highlights.text: Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew.

records.jp: 猛然と、勇猛果敢に、徹底して、食べる。
records.en: A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating.
comments: See CCB0008 (I guess) -GHS
records.assessment: The source piles adverbs onto the woman's act of eating. 'A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating' turns the action into an ungrammatical abstract noun phrase and removes the eater.
records.remedy: Use 'She eats ferociously, fearlessly, relentlessly.'

highlights.text: A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating.

records.jp: こんな様子は珍しい。
records.en: This thing now is a rarity.
records.assessment: こんな様子 is this sight or behavior. 'This thing now is a rarity' uses a vague object noun and unnatural word order.
records.remedy: Use 'It is a rare sight.'

highlights.text: This thing now is a rarity.

records.jp: 「……さっきから何なのよ？」
records.en: Touko: "...what's that you keep talking about now?"
records.assessment: The source asks what he has been saying for a while. 'What's that you keep talking about now' has broken interrogative structure and adds 'now.'
records.remedy: Use '...What have you been going on about?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...what's that you keep talking about now?"

records.jp: 「おまえの血肉になった新じゃがの無辜なる民たちだ」
records.en: Taichi: "The blameless, innocent people of the New Potato Republic that have now become your flesh and blood."
comments: Step 4. Also part of the Country Founding/immigration subtheme. -GHS
records.assessment: The source calls the new potatoes innocent citizens. 'New Potato Republic' invents a state name, while 'blameless, innocent' duplicates the same quality.
records.remedy: Use 'The innocent citizens of the new potatoes who have become your flesh and blood.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The blameless, innocent people of the New Potato Republic that have now become your flesh and blood."

records.jp: じゃがいものかけらを頬につけて、冬子は怪訝な顔をした。
records.en: With bits of potato stuck to her cheek, Touko made a puzzled face.
records.assessment: 怪訝な顔をした means she looked puzzled or suspicious. 'Made a puzzled face' is a literal collocation.
records.remedy: Use 'With bits of potato stuck to her cheek, Tōko looks puzzled.'

highlights.text: With bits of potato stuck to her cheek, Touko made a puzzled face.

records.jp: 合掌。
records.en: Press hands together in prayer.
comments: Not the Western one. -GHS
records.assessment: 合掌 is the narrator's clipped present action of pressing his palms together. 'Press hands together in prayer' changes narration into an imperative and omits the acting subject.
records.remedy: Use 'I press my palms together in prayer.'

highlights.text: Press hands together in prayer.

records.jp: 四肢が引きつる。
records.en: Limbs stiffen.
comments: Is she coming??? -GHS
records.assessment: 引きつる describes the limbs twitching or convulsively contracting. 'Stiffen' changes the involuntary spasm into rigid immobility.
records.remedy: Use 'Her limbs twitch.'

highlights.text: Limbs stiffen.

records.jp: 飲み干す。
records.en: She chugs down.
records.assessment: 飲み干す means she drinks the bottle dry. 'Chugs down' lacks the object required by the English phrasal verb and does not express completion.
records.remedy: Use 'She drains it.'

highlights.text: She chugs down.

records.jp: 「はふはふ」
records.en: Touko: "MnchMnch."
records.assessment: はふはふ is a breathy panting or hot-food vocalization. 'MnchMnch' turns it into the sound of chewing.
records.remedy: Use a breathy rendering such as 'Hah, hah.'

highlights.text: Touko: "MnchMnch."

records.jp: また食い出す。
records.en: She wolfs down once again.
records.assessment: また食い出す says she starts eating again. 'Wolfs down' adds voracious speed already conveyed elsewhere rather than translating this neutral resumption.
records.remedy: Use 'She starts eating again.'

highlights.text: She wolfs down once again.

records.jp: 大人びて見えるけど、年相応に子供なんだよな、こいつ……。
records.en: She looks all grown up, but she has the mannerism of a child, this one...
records.assessment: The source says that despite looking mature, she is still a child her own age. 'Has the mannerism of a child, this one' uses an unnatural singular trait and a demonstrative calque.
records.remedy: Use 'She may look mature, but she is still a child her own age...'

highlights.text: She looks all grown up, but she has the mannerism of a child, this one...

records.jp: 七個か八個もたいらげて、ようやく冬子は一息ついた。
records.en: After having flattened seven or eight, finally Touko takes a breather.
comments: Casual numbers. -GHS
records.assessment: たいらげる means to polish off or finish eating food. 'Flattened seven or eight' literalizes the verb into a physical action on the potatoes.
records.remedy: Use 'After polishing off seven or eight, Tōko finally pauses for breath.'

highlights.text: After having flattened seven or eight, finally Touko takes a breather.

records.jp: 「そりゃ何より」
records.en: Taichi: "Welll, that's what's important."
records.assessment: そりゃ何より is the social response 'Glad to hear it.' 'That's what's important' instead states a priority judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'Glad to hear it.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Welll, that's what's important."

records.jp: 俯いて、上目づかいに俺を見る。
records.en: With her head hung in shame, she rolls up her eyes to look at me.
records.assessment: 上目づかい means looking upward from beneath lowered brows, not rolling the eyes. 'In shame' also supplies an emotion not explicitly stated by 俯いて.
records.remedy: Use 'With her head lowered, she looks up at me through her lashes.'

highlights.text: With her head hung in shame, she rolls up her eyes to look at me.

records.jp: じっと見る。
records.en: Staring fixed.
records.assessment: じっと見る is a complete present action. 'Staring fixed' is an unattached participle with a nonstandard adjective where an adverb is required.
records.remedy: Use 'I stare.'

highlights.text: Staring fixed.

records.jp: 「い、いやなに。そっちがメンチを切るからつい」
records.en: Taichi: "N-,no I wasn't! I only glanced that way unconsciously!"
comments: regression to tsundere -GHS
records.assessment: メンチを切る is to glare at or stare someone down. 'I only glanced that way unconsciously' changes the other person's deliberate stare into the narrator's accidental glance and removes the idiom's force.
records.remedy: Use 'N-no, it was only because you were glaring at me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "N-,no I wasn't! I only glanced that way unconsciously!"

records.jp: 「お礼言おうとしてたのっ！」
records.en: Touko: "I'm trying to say something polite here!"
comments: !!TSUNDERE FIGHT!! -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker says she was trying to thank him. 'Trying to say something polite' weakens the specific act of gratitude and shifts the tense to the present.
records.remedy: Use 'I was trying to thank you!'

highlights.text: Touko: "I'm trying to say something polite here!"

records.jp: ぎこちなかった。
records.en: So very awkwardly.
records.assessment: ぎこちなかった is a complete past judgment that the attempt was awkward. 'So very awkwardly' is an adverb fragment with no verb or subject.
records.remedy: Use 'It was awkward.'

highlights.text: So very awkwardly.

records.jp: 「家に食料なかったとですか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Was it because there was no food in the house?"
records.assessment: The mock-dialect question asks whether there was no food at her house. 'Was it because' invents a causal frame and removes the dialectal comic coloration.
records.remedy: Use 'Weren't there no food at home?' or another controlled comic dialect form.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Was it because there was no food in the house?"

records.jp: 「どう調理していいかわからなくて」
records.en: Touko: "I don't really know how to prepare it."
records.assessment: She explains that she did not know how to prepare the food she had. The English present tense makes it a standing inability rather than the cause of the completed starvation.
records.remedy: Use 'I didn't know how to cook it.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I don't really know how to prepare it."

records.jp: 「あれ、だって昔弁当とか作って……」
records.en: Taichi: "Then, those bentos you had weren't made..."
comments: See CCD2002. But shouldn't he know? -GHS
records.assessment: The interrupted question recalls the lunches she used to make. 'The bentos you had weren't made' changes her role from maker to possessor and prematurely supplies a negative passive continuation.
records.remedy: Use 'But what about the lunches you used to make...?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then, those bentos you had weren't made..."

records.jp: 「お手伝いさんが作ったのを私が作ったってことにして」
records.en: Touko: "The maid made them and I just made it look like I made them."
comments: There mayd be something wrong with how I made this sentence, but I seem unable to figure out what unaided... -GHS
records.assessment: The helper made the lunches and Tōko passed them off as her own. 'Made it look like I made them' mismatches singular and plural objects and weakens the deliberate attribution.
records.remedy: Use 'The maid made them, and I pretended I had.'

highlights.text: Touko: "The maid made them and I just made it look like I made them."

records.jp: 「……おばちゃん弁当に……俺は……ときめいて……」
records.en: Taichi: "...my heart fluttered... for the bento... prepared by an old bag..."
comments: I wonder if THIS is what pisses him off. -GHS
records.assessment: おばちゃん is a familiar, mildly disparaging middle-aged lady or auntie. 'Old bag' adds a much harsher contemptuous insult not supported by the line.
records.remedy: Use 'My heart fluttered over a middle-aged lady's lunch...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...my heart fluttered... for the bento... prepared by an old bag..."

records.jp: 「リアリーっ！？」
records.en: Taichi: "MAJIII!?"
comments: screw it *chug* see CCC4016, it returns so keeping it like this. -GHS
records.assessment: The source writes the English loanword 'really' in katakana for the reaction. 'MAJIII' substitutes a different Japanese slang word and leaves it as untranslated romanization.
records.remedy: Use 'REALLY?!' while preserving the marked comic delivery.

highlights.text: Taichi: "MAJIII!?"

records.jp: 缶詰の存在を知らないっ？
records.en: She doesn't even know of the existence of canned food!?"
records.assessment: The English thought ends with an unmatched quotation mark after the exclamation and question marks.
records.remedy: Remove the stray closing quotation mark.

highlights.text: She doesn't even know of the existence of canned food!?"

records.jp: 缶詰という単語を知らない？
records.en: She doesn't know the words 'canned food'?
records.assessment: 缶詰という単語 is the singular word or term 'canned food.' 'The words' incorrectly pluralizes the lexical item.
records.remedy: Use 'She doesn't know the term canned food?'

highlights.text: She doesn't know the words 'canned food'?

records.jp: エンサイクロペディア冬子には缶詰の二文字がない？
records.en: Do those two words never appear together in the Encyclopedia Touka?
comments: lit. "does the two-kanji word 缶詰 not appear". -GHS
records.assessment: The nickname is Encyclopedia Tōko, using her correctly romanized given name. 'Touka' changes the final vowel and uses nonstandard long-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Does Encyclopedia Tōko have no entry for canned food?'

highlights.text: Do those two words never appear together in the Encyclopedia Touka?

records.jp: 「キャビアって缶詰に入ってるんじゃないの？」
records.en: Taichi: "Doesn't your caviar come in a can?!"
records.assessment: The source asks whether caviar comes in cans. 'Your caviar' adds personal possession before the following answer explains its delivery.
records.remedy: Use 'Doesn't caviar come in cans?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Doesn't your caviar come in a can?!"

records.jp: わなわな震えながら問う。
records.en: A question while I shake and tremble with fear.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator asks while trembling with agitation. 'A question while I shake and tremble with fear' is a noun fragment, redundantly doubles the motion, and adds fear as its cause.
records.remedy: Use 'I ask, trembling.'

highlights.text: A question while I shake and tremble with fear.

records.jp: 「ビンよ。毎週木箱に詰められて外国から送られてくるの」
records.en: Touko: "It's in jars. Every week, jam-packed in a wooden box sent from overseas."
comments: Even the most expensive caviar in the world comes in a tin: http://most-expensive.net/caviar-world As a crate like that would run likely $100,000+ a WEEK, I'm leaving this as a rich girl joke. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says jars arrive from abroad every week packed in a wooden crate. 'Jam-packed' adds an English food pun and makes the packing relation ambiguous.
records.remedy: Use 'Jars. Every week they arrive from abroad packed in a wooden crate.'

highlights.text: Touko: "It's in jars. Every week, jam-packed in a wooden box sent from overseas."

records.jp: 「キャビー！　こんなありがたみのわからない女に食われて！　おうおう！」
records.en: Taichi: "CAVIEEE! Eaten by this woman of all values ignorant! All the time!"
records.assessment: ありがたみのわからない女 is a woman who does not appreciate the caviar's value. 'Woman of all values ignorant' is not grammatical, while おうおう is mock weeping rather than 'all the time.'
records.remedy: Use 'Cavvy! Eaten by a woman who doesn't appreciate you! Boo-hoo!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "CAVIEEE! Eaten by this woman of all values ignorant! All the time!"

records.jp: 擬人化して哀れんだ。
records.en: I pity that anthropomorphism.
comments: "Cavie" -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator anthropomorphizes the caviar and pities it. 'I pity that anthropomorphism' instead makes the rhetorical device itself the object of pity.
records.remedy: Use 'I anthropomorphize it and mourn its fate.'

highlights.text: I pity that anthropomorphism.

records.jp: 「泣かれても」
records.en: Touko: "Crying, really now."
records.assessment: 泣かれても means that his crying leaves her at a loss or will not help. 'Crying, really now' is a fragment and does not state her response to being cried at.
records.remedy: Use 'Crying won't help...'

highlights.text: Touko: "Crying, really now."

records.jp: 「だから！　ご自慢のキャビアはどうしたのか訊いたんだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Therefore! I now ask what happened to this proud caviar!"
records.assessment: だから is an emphatic 'I'm asking you,' not the formal connective 'Therefore.' ご自慢 means prized or vaunted, not 'proud,' and the question concerns what happened to it.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm asking what happened to your precious caviar!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore! I now ask what happened to this proud caviar!"

records.jp: 「先週は全然食べなくて未開封だったけれど……捨ててしまったわ。傷むもの」
records.en: Touko: "Last week we didn't eat any of it and it was still sealed, but... I threw it all away. It's perishable."
comments: Odd, isn't it? Touko wasn't at home for most of that time, because of the Training Camp. Is she the only one who eats it there? Did they just stop ordering it since she wasn't eating it? -GHS
records.assessment: 先週は全然食べなくて says Tōko did not eat any of it last week. 'We didn't eat any' changes the subject and introduces other household members.
records.remedy: Use 'I didn't eat any last week, so it was still sealed, but... I threw it away. It spoils.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Last week we didn't eat any of it and it was still sealed, but... I threw it all away. It's perishable."

records.jp: 「イクッ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "BNK!!!"
comments: Lit. "I'm coming". Going with vapor lock. -GHS
records.assessment: イクッ is the climactic cry 'I'm coming!' used as an exaggerated reaction. 'BNK' substitutes an unexplained impact sound and removes the sexualized joke.
records.remedy: Use a controlled equivalent of the climactic cry.

highlights.text: Taichi: "BNK!!!"

records.jp: 俺はぴーんと反った。
records.en: I push out my chest and start to bend backwards,
records.assessment: ぴーんと反った says the narrator's body snaps into a rigid backward arch. 'Push out my chest and start to bend backwards' adds a deliberate chest action and weakens the sudden full-body motion.
records.remedy: Use 'My body snaps backward into an arch.'

highlights.text: I push out my chest and start to bend backwards,

records.jp: そのまま地面に倒れる。
records.en: until the back of my head hits the ground.
records.assessment: The source says he falls to the ground in that posture. The English adds a specific impact of the back of his head and turns the fall into a gradual endpoint.
records.remedy: Use 'Still like that, I fall to the ground.'

highlights.text: until the back of my head hits the ground.

records.jp: 「支離滅裂でもう何がなにやら……」
records.en: Touko: "What are you doing with all this incoherent and illogical nonsense..."
comments: Been asking that myself for about 18 months now. -GHS
records.assessment: Tōko says his speech is so incoherent that she can no longer tell what is what. 'What are you doing with ... nonsense' changes confusion about meaning into a question about an action.
records.remedy: Use 'This is so incoherent I can't even tell what you're talking about anymore...'

highlights.text: Touko: "What are you doing with all this incoherent and illogical nonsense..."

records.jp: 「だから金持ちは！」
records.en: Taichi: "Why you over-rich...!"
records.assessment: だから金持ちは is the exasperated generalization 'That's rich people for you!' 'Why you over-rich' is not grammatical and changes it into a direct accusation of excess wealth.
records.remedy: Use 'That's rich people for you!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Why you over-rich...!"

records.jp: 冬子は顔を伏せた。
records.en: Touko's face looks downcast.
records.assessment: The source says Tōko lowers her face. 'Tōko's face looks downcast' makes the face the subject and substitutes an inferred emotion for the physical action.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko lowers her head.'

highlights.text: Touko's face looks downcast.

records.jp: 「……お金なんて、もう意味ないじゃない」
records.en: Touko: "...rich you say, but now it's all meaningless."
records.assessment: The source says money no longer has any meaning. 'Rich you say' invents a reply to the prior label and makes wealth, rather than money, the explicit topic.
records.remedy: Use '...Money doesn't mean anything anymore.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...rich you say, but now it's all meaningless."

records.jp: 「そらそーだが」
records.en: Taichi: "Sure, suuure, but!"
records.assessment: そらそーだが concedes once that this is true before qualifying it. 'Sure, suuure' adds dismissive repetition not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'That's true, but...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sure, suuure, but!"

records.jp: 「料理って言うか、焼いただけだけど」
records.en: Taichi: "Cooking, now, it's just roasting something I rustled up."
comments: tadakedakedo -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker qualifies the act as merely roasting rather than cooking. 'Now' and 'something I rustled up' are additions, and the opening 'Cooking, now' is not a stable English clause.
records.remedy: Use 'Cooking? All I did was roast them.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cooking, now, it's just roasting something I rustled up."

records.jp: 普通できるだろう。
records.en: Should be normal to be capable of it.
records.assessment: 普通できるだろう means that anyone should be able to do it. 'Should be normal to be capable of it' is a literal nominal construction that omits the general human subject.
records.remedy: Use 'Anyone should be able to do that.'

highlights.text: Should be normal to be capable of it.

records.jp: さいとうた○をの力添えもあるけど。
records.en: Though I have had the help of Saitou Ta**o.
comments: Can't source the Golgo 13 chapter this comes from, if any. -GHS
records.assessment: The deliberately censored creator name should still use standard Hepburn: Saitō Ta**o. 'Saitou' is nonstandard, and the present assistance is needlessly shifted into present perfect.
records.remedy: Use 'Though I did have some help from Saitō Ta**o.'

highlights.text: Though I have had the help of Saitou Ta**o.

records.jp: 冬子お嬢様だ。
records.en: That's why Touko's an Ojou-sama.
records.assessment: The line calls her young mistress or Lady Tōko. 'Touko' uses nonstandard long-vowel spelling, while 'Ojou-sama' is left untranslated.
records.remedy: Use 'That makes her Lady Tōko.'

highlights.text: That's why Touko's an Ojou-sama.

records.jp: つまり、自分で何かしなくとも自動的に生きてこられたわけだ。
records.en: In other words, she was maintained alive automatically even without doing anything herself.
records.assessment: The source says she has automatically been able to stay alive without doing anything herself. 'Was maintained alive automatically' is an unnatural passive calque that implies an external maintenance process.
records.remedy: Use 'In other words, she has always stayed alive automatically without doing anything herself.'

highlights.text: In other words, she was maintained alive automatically even without doing anything herself.

records.jp: 「……るさい」
records.en: Touko: "...'ddap."
comments: Lisp -GHS
records.assessment: The clipped うるさい is a weakened 'Shut up.' The spelling ''ddap' is not a legible or systematically motivated representation of that interruption.
records.remedy: Use '...Shut up.' with controlled weakening if required.

highlights.text: Touko: "...'ddap."

records.jp: 力ない反論が肯定だった。
records.en: A feeble refutation that was an affirmation.
records.assessment: The source states that her feeble rebuttal amounted to an admission. 'A feeble refutation that was an affirmation' is an unattached noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'Her feeble rebuttal amounted to an admission.'

highlights.text: A feeble refutation that was an affirmation.

records.jp: 「自動的なやつめ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Damn automatic people..."
records.assessment: 自動的なやつ addresses one automatic person or creature. 'Automatic people' pluralizes the target and produces an unnatural insult.
records.remedy: Use 'You automatic creature...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Damn automatic people..."

records.jp: 「……ここに住んだらだめ？」
records.en: Touko: "...me staying here, can't I?"
records.assessment: The source is a hesitant request for permission to live here. 'Me staying here, can't I?' uses a dislocated object-like gerund and malformed question syntax.
records.remedy: Use '...Could I stay here?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...me staying here, can't I?"

records.jp: 本気で弱ってるな、コイツ。
records.en: She's seriously impaired, this one.
records.assessment: 弱ってる describes her as seriously weakened or vulnerable. 'Impaired' is clinical and can imply disability rather than her present depleted condition.
records.remedy: Use 'She's seriously weakened.'

highlights.text: She's seriously impaired, this one.

records.jp: ううううう（懊悩）。
records.en: Ngggggh (anguish) (pronounced oh no)
comments: See CCA0016, it's one of the few furrys that have been repeating so it's totally intentional. -GHS
records.assessment: The parenthetical explicitly labels the groan as anguish. Adding '(pronounced oh no)' invents an English sound pun not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use the groan followed only by the anguish label.

highlights.text: Ngggggh (anguish) (pronounced oh no)

records.jp: 「ウエイツ！（待て！）」
records.en: Taichi: "Matte! (Wait!)"
comments: Same as CCB2002. -GHS
records.assessment: The source comically uses the English loan 'waits' and then glosses it as 待て. The translation replaces that English with Japanese 'Matte,' reversing the language joke.
records.remedy: Use 'WAIT! (Wait!)' or another rendering that preserves the English-loan-plus-gloss structure.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Matte! (Wait!)"

records.jp: 冬子は地面にキスした。
records.en: Touko implemented a kiss with the ground.
comments: See CCA0002 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Tōko kissed the ground. 'Implemented a kiss with the ground' is bureaucratic, unidiomatic English and obscures the physical gag.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko kissed the ground.'

highlights.text: Touko implemented a kiss with the ground.

records.jp: 本音で接した。
records.en: I directly contacted my true intentions.
comments: Should be ambiguous enough, see CCX0001. -GHS
records.assessment: 本音で接した means the narrator dealt with her honestly or spoke from the heart. 'Contacted my true intentions' turns sincerity into an object contacted and is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'I spoke from the heart.'

highlights.text: I directly contacted my true intentions.

records.jp: 「しかも羞恥さえ見せない……」
records.en: Taichi: "And you don't even show any shyness..."
records.assessment: 羞恥 is shame or embarrassment in the compromising situation. 'Shyness' weakens it into a general personality trait.
records.remedy: Use 'And you aren't even showing any shame...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And you don't even show any shyness..."

records.jp: 「おまえは、人のことをポンポン殴る勝ち気娘なんだけど鑑賞面においては俺に妙に都合の良い追従的なヒロインであれよっ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "You, you're always that unyielding spirit that punches people left and right, but in terms of artistic appreciation you're a heroine that finds an oddly convenient subservience in me!!!"
comments: See CCE0001 -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator demands that although she is a strong-willed girl who hits people, for viewing purposes she should be a heroine conveniently compliant with him. 'Finds ... subservience in me' reverses who is compliant with whom and is not coherent English.
records.remedy: Use 'You may be a headstrong girl who hits people at every turn, but for my viewing pleasure, be a heroine conveniently submissive to me!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You, you're always that unyielding spirit that punches people left and right, but in terms of artistic appreciation you're a heroine that finds an oddly convenient subservience in me!!!"

records.jp: 「……意味がわからないわ」
records.en: Touko: "...I don't get what you're saying, no."
records.assessment: The source simply says she does not understand what he means. The final 'no' invents a verbal tag not characteristic of the line.
records.remedy: Use '...I don't understand what you're saying.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...I don't get what you're saying, no."

records.jp: ふぁさぁっと後ろ髪をはらった。
records.en: With a 'fwasah' I sweeped my bangs.
comments: PCP CCB0009
records.assessment: 後ろ髪 is the hair at the back of her head, not the narrator's bangs. 'Sweeped' is also not the past tense of 'sweep.'
records.remedy: Use 'With a soft swish, she brushes back her hair.'

highlights.text: With a 'fwasah' I sweeped my bangs.

records.jp: 「さっきまで殊勝だったのに！」
records.en: Taichi: "When you were so very admirable until moments ago!"
comments: I think it means he likes 'em tsun and not dere. -GHS
records.assessment: 殊勝 here means meek, contrite, or commendably submissive in conduct. 'Admirable' loses the contrast with her now abandoning the meek performance.
records.remedy: Use 'You were acting so meek until a moment ago!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "When you were so very admirable until moments ago!"

records.jp: 「言質を取ったらもうしおらしくする必要なんてないでしょ」
records.en: Touko: "Once I got your commitment, being all meek is not necessary anymore is it."
records.assessment: The source gives a coherent rhetorical question. 'Being all meek is not necessary anymore is it' needs normal clause order and punctuation.
records.remedy: Use 'Now that I have your word, I don't need to act meek anymore, do I?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Once I got your commitment, being all meek is not necessary anymore is it."

records.jp: あの妖刀ハラキリ丸を我が家に！？
records.en: The Demon Blade Harakiri, in my house!?
records.assessment: The weapon name is 妖刀ハラキリ丸, the demonic sword Harakiri-maru. 'Demon Blade Harakiri' omits the name-forming suffix -maru.
records.remedy: Use 'That demonic sword Harakiri-maru—in my house?!'

highlights.text: The Demon Blade Harakiri, in my house!?

records.jp: そうでした！
records.en: Indeed there wasn't!
records.assessment: そうでした is the narrator's immediate realization, 'That's right!' 'Indeed there wasn't' recasts it as a formal past-tense confirmation.
records.remedy: Use 'That's right!'

highlights.text: Indeed there wasn't!

records.jp: 「だいたい、よく考えたらこれは正当な権利じゃない」
records.en: Touko: "Besides, thinking hard about it, this is no unwarranted privilege."
records.assessment: よく考えたら means 'when I think about it,' not that she thinks hard. 正当な権利 is a legitimate right; 'no unwarranted privilege' substitutes a double-negative legal category.
records.remedy: Use 'Besides, now that I think about it, this is my legitimate right.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Besides, thinking hard about it, this is no unwarranted privilege."

records.jp: 「『隣に住むＨな妹１８歳』ならもう返却済みだ……」
records.en: Taichi: "I've already returned 'My Neighbor Is An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto'..."
comments: Fetishistic archetype in this case. -GHS
records.assessment: The mock title describes an eighteen-year-old sexy younger sister living next door. 'An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto' has incorrect age-compound grammar and leaves both descriptive nouns untranslated.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical English mock title such as 'My Sexy Eighteen-Year-Old Little Sister Next Door.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I've already returned 'My Neighbor Is An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto'..."

records.jp: 大きく頷いた。
records.en: A very big nod.
records.assessment: The source is the narrator's complete action of nodding broadly. 'A very big nod' is a subjectless noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'I nod broadly.'

highlights.text: A very big nod.

records.jp: 「痴呆なのあなたは！？」
records.en: Taichi: "Have you got dementia, you?!"
records.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the person demanding whether he has dementia. The English labels the line as Taichi, assigning the insult to its target.
records.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Have you got dementia, you?!"

records.jp: 「鼓膜を張り替えろーっ！！」
records.en: Touko: "Reupholster your eardruuums!!!"
comments: Hence he has no ears that can hear. -GHS
records.assessment: 鼓膜を張り替えろ tells him to replace his eardrums. 'Reupholster' applies 張り替える as though an eardrum were furniture and produces the wrong English action.
records.remedy: Use 'Get your eardrums replaced!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Reupholster your eardruuums!!!"

records.jp: 「とにかく住むの！　住みまくるの！　住みこんで住みあげて……住みぬくの！　もう決定！　可決！」
records.en: Touko: "Anyway, I'll be staying! Recklessly staying! Diving into staying to granting you my staying... thoroughly staying! Already decided! Ratified!"
comments: sumuNUKU -GHS
records.assessment: The source comically piles multiple forms of 住む, 'live/stay,' into an escalating declaration. 'Diving into staying to granting you my staying' is not grammatical and fails to keep the repeated verb as the organizing device.
records.remedy: Rebuild the escalation around repeated forms of 'live' or 'stay' in grammatical English.

highlights.text: Touko: "Anyway, I'll be staying! Recklessly staying! Diving into staying to granting you my staying... thoroughly staying! Already decided! Ratified!"

records.jp: 「すぐに荷物持ってきてやるんだから！」
records.en: Touko: "So I'll be bringing over my luggage right quick!"
records.assessment: The source says she will bring her luggage immediately. 'So' adds a logical connector and 'right quick' adds marked dialect.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll bring my luggage over right away!'

highlights.text: Touko: "So I'll be bringing over my luggage right quick!"

records.jp: きびすを返す。
records.en: She spins back on a heel.
records.assessment: きびすを返す is the idiom 'turn on one's heel.' 'Spins back on a heel' combines a different action and the wrong preposition.
records.remedy: Use 'She turns on her heel.'

highlights.text: She spins back on a heel.

records.jp: 「まだ何か？」
records.en: Touko: "Something else now?"
records.assessment: まだ何か asks whether there is anything else. 'Now' adds impatience as a temporal tag not present in the source.
records.remedy: Use 'Something else?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Something else now?"

records.jp: やむを得ないか。
records.en: Is this unavoidable?
records.assessment: やむを得ないか is a resigned conclusion that it cannot be helped. 'Is this unavoidable?' leaves the decision as an open information question.
records.remedy: Use 'I suppose it can't be helped.'

highlights.text: Is this unavoidable?

records.jp: 「……なんとか……その線で納得してもらって……うん、よし」
records.en: Taichi: "...it's just... getting consent with that line... yes, got it."
records.assessment: The narrator mutters about somehow getting her to accept that line of reasoning. 'Getting consent with that line' changes persuasion into formal consent and leaves the clause without a subject.
records.remedy: Use '...Somehow get her to accept that reasoning... Yeah, good.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...it's just... getting consent with that line... yes, got it."

records.jp: 「ＯＫ、君の入国を認めよう」
records.en: Taichi: "Okieh, I will recognize your immigration."
comments: Literal for reasons that should be obvious, otherwise u dont get CC lol kill yourself. -GHS
records.assessment: The mock-border metaphor grants her entry into the narrator's territory. 'Recognize your immigration' describes official acknowledgment of a migration process, not permission to enter.
records.remedy: Use 'Okay. I hereby grant you entry.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Okieh, I will recognize your immigration."

records.jp: 「部屋の掃除だってしないとならんし」
records.en: Taichi: "I gotta clean out the room at least, after all."
records.assessment: The source adds that the room also needs cleaning. 'At least' invents a minimum contrast.
records.remedy: Use 'I have to clean the room too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I gotta clean out the room at least, after all."

records.jp: 「明日だったら、俺も荷物運ぶの手伝ってやるから」
records.en: Taichi: "If we do this tomorrow, I can help you carry over the bags."
records.assessment: 荷物 is luggage or belongings in this moving context. 'Bags' narrows it to containers and can imply only hand baggage.
records.remedy: Use 'If it is tomorrow, I'll help you carry your things.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If we do this tomorrow, I can help you carry over the bags."

records.jp: ぱっと点灯する冬子スマイル。
records.en: Touko smiles with the suddenness of a light bulb turned on.
records.assessment: The source metaphorically says Tōko's smile switches on at once. 'With the suddenness of a light bulb' invents a specific object rather than preserving the lighting verb.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko's smile lights up at once.'

highlights.text: Touko smiles with the suddenness of a light bulb turned on.

records.jp: 俺の芸術が……。
records.en: My poor work of art...
comments: See CCA0004C, but likely what's going on near the start of the script. -GHS
records.assessment: 俺の芸術 is simply 'my art' in the narrator's trailing thought. 'My poor work of art' adds pity and turns the abstraction into a countable artwork.
records.remedy: Use 'My art...'

highlights.text: My poor work of art...

records.jp: 「んだね」
records.en: Taichi: "So you do."
records.assessment: んだね is an agreeing 'Yeah' or 'Right.' 'So you do' makes the addressee's action the focus of a newly discovered proposition.
records.remedy: Use 'Yeah.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "So you do."

records.jp: いそいそ。
records.en: With alacrity.
records.assessment: いそいそ describes cheerful, eager bustle. 'With alacrity' is stiff formal diction and loses the visible eagerness.
records.remedy: Use 'She bustles off eagerly.'

highlights.text: With alacrity.

records.jp: 「じゃあ明日ね。普通に学校に行くから」
records.en: Touko: "See you tomorrow then. Since I'll be going to school as normal."
records.assessment: The speaker gives two sequential statements: see you tomorrow, and she will come to school normally. 'Since' falsely makes attending school the reason for the farewell.
records.remedy: Use 'See you tomorrow. I'll come to school as usual.'

highlights.text: Touko: "See you tomorrow then. Since I'll be going to school as normal."

records.jp: 俺はいつまでもゆるゆると手を振っていた。
records.en: I kept constantly, loosely, slowly waving a hand.
comments: See CCA0011B -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he kept waving languidly for a long time. 'Kept constantly, loosely, slowly' stacks incompatible adverbs and redundantly expresses duration.
records.remedy: Use 'I kept waving lazily for a long time.'

highlights.text: I kept constantly, loosely, slowly waving a hand.

records.jp: 厄介なことになったなぁ……。
records.en: This has become awkward, didn't it...
comments: Actually problematic + problematic as in 'guest is staying over'. -GHS
records.assessment: 厄介 means troublesome or difficult here. 'Awkward' narrows it to social discomfort, and the tag 'didn't it' has incorrect tense agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'This has become troublesome...'

highlights.text: This has become awkward, didn't it...

records.jp: 駆け寄ってくる。
records.en: She came running over to me,
records.assessment: The source uses present narration and forms a complete action. 'Came running' shifts to past and leaves the line hanging on a comma.
records.remedy: Use 'She comes running over.'

highlights.text: She came running over to me,

records.jp: お風呂にするそれともご飯、とでも言いそうな勢いと態度だ。
records.en: As if wanting to ask me if I would prefer a bath, or dinner, or perhaps...
comments: damn waifus. -GHS
records.assessment: The stock domestic line contains two choices, bath or dinner. 'Or perhaps...' adds a suggestive unnamed third option not stated by the Japanese.
records.remedy: Use 'She looks ready to ask, Would you like a bath or dinner?'

highlights.text: As if wanting to ask me if I would prefer a bath, or dinner, or perhaps...

records.jp: 「風呂に入りながらご飯を食べゆ」
records.en: Taichi: "I'll be taking a bath while I have dinner."
comments: ゆ。 -GHS
records.assessment: 食べゆ is a deliberate babyish slip from 食べる. The English renders an ordinary grammatical 'have dinner' and removes the malformed comic ending.
records.remedy: Preserve a controlled childish slip in the final verb.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'll be taking a bath while I have dinner."

records.jp: 「そりゃ来るわよ」
records.en: Touko: "Seems like I did, yes!"
records.assessment: そりゃ来るわよ emphatically says 'Of course I came.' 'Seems like I did' turns certainty into a tentative inference.
records.remedy: Use 'Of course I came.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Seems like I did, yes!"

records.en: Taichi: "...the bags?"
records.assessment: 荷物 is her luggage or belongings for the move. 'Bags' narrows it to specific containers.
records.remedy: Use '...Where is your luggage?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...the bags?"

records.jp: 「へーい」
records.en: Taichi: "Lee-et's."
records.assessment: へーい is the narrator's casual acknowledgment, 'Okay.' 'Let's' instead proposes a joint action and leaves the verb omitted.
records.remedy: Use 'Okaaay.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Lee-et's."

records.jp: 「荷物、なに持って行こうかなーって思っていろいろ探したの」
records.en: Touko: "For the baggages, I was wondering, oh what should I bring with, so I went searching all over."
records.assessment: 'Baggage' is uncountable in this sense, 'bring with' lacks an object, and the nested 'I was wondering, oh' is not grammatical reported thought.
records.remedy: Use 'I looked through all kinds of things, wondering what luggage I should bring.'

highlights.text: Touko: "For the baggages, I was wondering, oh what should I bring with, so I went searching all over."

records.jp: 「そしたら古い写真が出てきたのよ？」
records.en: Touko: "And guess whose old photos turned up?"
comments: rethronical. Also rethorical, but that's not a real word. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that some old photos then turned up. 'Guess whose' invents a question about ownership that the line does not ask.
records.remedy: Use 'Then I found some old photographs.'

highlights.text: Touko: "And guess whose old photos turned up?"

records.jp: 「ほう、古い写真とな」
records.en: Taichi: "Huh, old pictures aren't they."
records.assessment: The archaic とな is a quotative reaction, 'Old photos, you say.' 'Old pictures aren't they' forms an unrelated tag question.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh? Old photographs, you say.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Huh, old pictures aren't they."

records.jp: 驚いてみせる。
records.en: I display astonishment.
records.assessment: 驚いてみせる says the narrator puts on a show of surprise. 'Display astonishment' presents the emotion as genuine and uses stiff diction.
records.remedy: Use 'I feign surprise.'

highlights.text: I display astonishment.

records.jp: 展開早っ！
records.en: Evolving too faaast!
records.assessment: 展開早っ comments that events are moving fast. 'Evolving' suggests developmental transformation rather than rapid plot progression.
records.remedy: Use 'This is moving fast!'

highlights.text: Evolving too faaast!

records.jp: くそう、やっぱりこの女は……。
records.en: Dammit, I knew it, this female...
comments: Creepier -GHS
records.assessment: この女 is a disparaging but human 'this woman.' 'This female' uses clinical or dehumanizing nominal diction.
records.remedy: Use 'Damn it, I knew it—this woman...'

highlights.text: Dammit, I knew it, this female...

records.jp: 俺は道具袋からアイテムを取り出す。
records.en:
I extract an [ITEM] from the tools bag.
* Tools bag = Taichian promotional item, called the Taichi
Bag. It comes in the shape of a canvas back-pack.
Within, many secret implements are found.
comments: Lines merged. Together with the Taichi Doll, the guy seems really trying to sell his image or something. He must've misunderstood, though, they sell figurines/dakimakuras/stuff of THE HEROINES of eroge, not of the protagonists. See CCC3004 -GHS
records.assessment: The source only says the narrator takes an item from his tool bag. The appended multi-line explanation invents a promotional Taichi Bag and its physical design and contents.
records.remedy: Use only 'I take an item from my tool bag.'

highlights.text:
I extract an [ITEM] from the tools bag.
* Tools bag = Taichian promotional item, called the Taichi
Bag. It comes in the shape of a canvas back-pack.
Within, many secret implements are found.

records.jp: 「腕章？」
records.en: Touko: "An arm band?"
records.assessment: The standard English compound is 'armband,' not the separated 'arm band' in this sense.
records.remedy: Use 'An armband?'

highlights.text: Touko: "An arm band?"

records.jp: 「……ばかっぷる……はんたい……」
records.en: Touko: "...syrupples... ostracized..."
comments: Syrup + couples. Terms should be tough enough that it sounds vaguely credible she'd strain a bit to read them. -GHS
records.assessment: The armband says opposition to バカップル, obnoxiously lovey-dovey couples. 'Syrupples ostracized' converts political opposition into social exclusion and obscures the label.
records.remedy: Use a consistent functional coinage followed by 'opposed' or 'no.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...syrupples... ostracized..."

records.jp: 「バカップル反対」
records.en: Touko: "Syrupples ostracized."
records.assessment: The clear reading again states opposition to lovey-dovey couples. 'Syrupples ostracized' repeats the changed relation rather than the armband's slogan.
records.remedy: Use the established English slogan for 'No lovey-dovey couples.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Syrupples ostracized."

records.jp: 変換する冬子。
records.en: So finally reads Touko.
comments: (overliteral translation with tongue-in-cheek TL note excised... THIS TIME.) -GHS
records.assessment: 変換する describes Tōko mentally converting or deciphering the obscured text. 'So finally reads Tōko' uses broken inversion and merely reports reading.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko deciphers it.'

highlights.text: So finally reads Touko.

records.jp: 「そうだ。俺はバカップルが及ぼす環境への重大な影響を重く見て、毅然とした態度でその規制ならびに抑制に努める立場なのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Indeed. I have gravely seen the enormity of the impact of Syrupples on the environment, and with manners most firm, I now strive for the position to regulate and furthermore curb said impact."
comments: See CCD2002 -GHS
records.assessment: The mock-policy statement says he takes the environmental harm seriously and therefore stands firm in working to regulate and restrain such couples. The English's 'strive for the position' makes the office itself his goal and is syntactically unstable.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical mock-policy declaration preserving impact, firm stance, regulation, and restraint.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeed. I have gravely seen the enormity of the impact of Syrupples on the environment, and with manners most firm, I now strive for the position to regulate and furthermore curb said impact."

records.jp: 「腕組みやめ」
records.en: Taichi: "Cease this arm linking!"
records.assessment: 腕組みやめ is a clipped command to stop linking arms. 'Cease this arm linking' uses a non-idiomatic action noun.
records.remedy: Use 'Stop linking arms with me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cease this arm linking!"

records.jp: 「い、いつものことながら……なに言ってるのかわからないんだけど」
records.en: Touko: "It-, it's always like this I know but... what are you even saying, I don't understand."
records.assessment: The source is a coherent hesitant complaint. 'It's always like this I know but' and 'what are you even saying, I don't understand' repeat and splice the clauses.
records.remedy: Use 'I-it's the same as always... I have no idea what you're talking about.'

highlights.text: Touko: "It-, it's always like this I know but... what are you even saying, I don't understand."

records.jp: 「人前での没頭的な愛情表現は慎むべし」
records.en: Taichi: "One ought to be most discreet in immersive displays of affections in front of people."
records.assessment: 没頭的な愛情表現 means absorbed or uninhibited displays of affection. 'Immersive displays of affections' uses the wrong collocation and incorrectly pluralizes the mass noun.
records.remedy: Use 'Refrain from uninhibited displays of affection in public.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "One ought to be most discreet in immersive displays of affections in front of people."

records.jp: 「人って、もういない……」
records.en: Touko: "People, but there's no more..."
records.assessment: The speaker says there are no people anymore. 'People, but there's no more' is a fragment and uses singular agreement with the plural noun.
records.remedy: Use 'But there aren't any people anymore...'

highlights.text: Touko: "People, but there's no more..."

records.jp: 不満げである。
records.en: Appears to be frustrated.
records.assessment: 不満げ describes dissatisfaction or displeasure. 'Frustrated' instead attributes thwarted effort.
records.remedy: Use 'She looks dissatisfied.'

highlights.text: Appears to be frustrated.

records.jp: 「桐原、おまえが反転型の勝ち気娘なのはいい」
records.en: Taichi: "Kirihara, you are the reversible model of overcompetitive girl, and this is fine."
comments: Tsundere again. See CCA0014A
records.assessment: 反転型の勝ち気娘 is a reversed or inverted strong-willed-girl type in the narrator's character-archetype framing. 'Reversible model of overcompetitive girl' suggests a mechanism and changes 勝ち気 from spirited to excessive competition.
records.remedy: Use 'Kirihara, being an inverted strong-willed-girl type is fine.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kirihara, you are the reversible model of overcompetitive girl, and this is fine."

records.jp: 「けどちょっと甘くしたらベタってしすぎるよ！　水気が多すぎだよ！　もっと徹底して勝ち気っぽく行こうよ！　照れる時は厳選。その方が萌え……桐原のためなんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "But if you get this sweet, you'll also be far too hackneyed! There's too much dampness! Let's be more consistently unyielding! Select carefully when to show shyness. Someone like that is moe... be that, Kirihara!
comments: Don't think he means that beta as in betabeta. -GHS
records.assessment: ベタベタ means overly clingy or syrupy, not hackneyed, and the extended character-direction monologue culminates in a lie that this is for Kirihara's sake. The English becomes incoherent at 'Someone like that is moe... be that,' omits that pivot, and lacks a closing quotation mark.
records.remedy: Rebuild the monologue around excessive sweetness, emotional dampness, consistent assertiveness, selective embarrassment, and the final claim that it is for Kirihara's sake; close the quotation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But if you get this sweet, you'll also be far too hackneyed! There's too much dampness! Let's be more consistently unyielding! Select carefully when to show shyness. Someone like that is moe... be that, Kirihara!

records.jp: 「一長一短なんだ。そのことをわかっておくれ、私の素敵な淑女よ」
records.en: Taichi: "You have shortcomings and strong points. This is what this one would like to have you understand, oh my fair lady."
records.assessment: 一長一短 means that something has both strengths and weaknesses or pros and cons. 'Shortcomings and strong points' reverses the fixed ordering and is followed by stiff third-person self-reference.
records.remedy: Use 'Everything has its pros and cons. Please understand that, my fair lady.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You have shortcomings and strong points. This is what this one would like to have you understand, oh my fair lady."

records.jp: 「よくわからないけど、わかったわ」
records.en: Touko: "I don't really get it but, I get it, yes."
records.assessment: The source says that although she does not really understand, she accepts it. The final 'yes' adds an unsupported verbal tic.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't really understand, but all right.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I don't really get it but, I get it, yes."

records.jp: 「……太一、恥ずかしいんだ。人前でベタベタするの」
records.en: Touko: "...Taichi, you're embarrassed. Of being all sticky-sticky in front of people that is."
records.assessment: The source is one inference that Taichi is embarrassed to be clingy in public. The English breaks the predicate into a sentence fragment beginning 'Of being.'
records.remedy: Use '...Taichi, you're embarrassed to be all clingy in public.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...Taichi, you're embarrassed. Of being all sticky-sticky in front of people that is."

records.jp: あまりにもズレた理解に、お兄ちゃんの同義語にも聞こえかねない反問が、口をついて出る。
records.en: Her understanding shifted so far that even a flat English translation of onii-chan wasn't unlikely to slip my mouth in reply.
comments: Heee heee snort -GHS
records.assessment: The narration says the wildly misaligned reply could be heard as a synonym for 'big brother.' It invents meta-commentary about 'a flat English translation' and introduces non-Hepburn 'onii-chan' instead of standard onī-chan.
records.remedy: Use 'Her understanding is so far off that a retort sounding like another word for big brother slips from my mouth.'

highlights.text: Her understanding shifted so far that even a flat English translation of onii-chan wasn't unlikely to slip my mouth in reply.

records.jp: 萌えられてる？
records.en: Have I just been thought moe?
records.assessment: 萌えられてる asks whether she is finding him endearingly moe. 'Thought moe' is not grammatical English and does not state her active response.
records.remedy: Use 'Does she find me cute?' or a consistently established rendering of moe.

highlights.text: Have I just been thought moe?

records.jp: この醜形恐怖症でならした黒須太一ともあろうものが、萌えられているっ！？
records.en: This chronically dysmorphophobic Kurosu Taichi here, of all people, thought moe?!
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_dysmorphic_disorder "features a suicidal ideation rate of 80 percent". Perhaps coincidental - perhaps. -GHS
records.assessment: The boast identifies the narrator as someone renowned for dysmorphophobia and asks whether even he is being found cute. 'This chronically dysmorphophobic ... thought moe' is not a grammatical question.
records.remedy: Use 'Even Kurosu Taichi, renowned for his dysmorphophobia, is being found cute?!'

highlights.text: This chronically dysmorphophobic Kurosu Taichi here, of all people, thought moe?!

records.jp: 許すのか、それを？
records.en: Should I let it go, should I?
records.assessment: The source asks once whether he can allow this. 'Should I let it go, should I?' duplicates the question as a malformed tag.
records.remedy: Use 'Can I allow this?'

highlights.text: Should I let it go, should I?

records.jp: 否！
records.en: Never!
records.assessment: 否 is the categorical answer 'No!' 'Never!' changes negation of the present question into a temporal absolute.
records.remedy: Use 'No!'

highlights.text: Never!

records.jp: おでこだった。
records.en: It was on the middle of the forehead.
records.assessment: The source specifies that the kiss landed on his forehead. 'The middle of' adds needless anatomical precision.
records.remedy: Use 'It was on my forehead.'

highlights.text: It was on the middle of the forehead.

records.jp: あどけなく笑う。
records.en: Cherubic laughing.
records.assessment: The source says she laughs innocently. 'Cherubic laughing' is a subjectless noun phrase and replaces innocent manner with an angelic visual judgment.
records.remedy: Use 'She laughs innocently.'

highlights.text: Cherubic laughing.

records.jp: 抱きしめてしまった。
records.en: I totally hugged her.
comments: See CCA0008 -GHS
records.assessment: The source says he ended up hugging her. 'Totally' adds modern emphatic slang rather than the involuntary-result nuance of しまった.
records.remedy: Use 'I end up hugging her.'

highlights.text: I totally hugged her.

records.jp: くっ、不覚を取った。
records.en: Gah, that was complete defeat.
records.assessment: 不覚を取った means he was caught off guard or suffered an embarrassing lapse. 'Complete defeat' turns it into the result of a contest.
records.remedy: Use 'Damn, she caught me off guard.'

highlights.text: Gah, that was complete defeat.

records.jp: そんなオノマトペごときでこの俺様がぁっ！
records.en: Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeiaaa!
comments: See CCA0025B. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator protests that the great him cannot be overcome by mere onomatopoeia. 'Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeia' uses the wrong pronoun case, misspells 'onomatopoeia,' and does not state the action resisted.
records.remedy: Use 'As if mere onomatopoeia could overcome the great me!'

highlights.text: Not the Greatness that is I, not by that onomatopeiaaa!

records.jp: 冬子が猫を真似て、胸元をひっかく。
records.en: Imitating a cat, Touko scratches my belly.
records.assessment: 胸元 is the chest or breast area. 'Belly' moves the scratching to a different part of the body.
records.remedy: Use 'Imitating a cat, Tōko scratches at my chest.'

highlights.text: Imitating a cat, Touko scratches my belly.

records.jp: とろけきっていた。
records.en: I melted into her charms.
comments: Figurative and literal -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the narrator was completely melted or overcome. 'Into her charms' supplies a causal object not stated by the line.
records.remedy: Use 'I had melted completely.'

highlights.text: I melted into her charms.

records.jp: バカップルここに爆誕。
records.en:
A Syrupple has here
its explosive birth.
comments: See CCA0006, CCA0007, CCA0019. Now it harmonizes with Shinkawa and Kiri. -GHS
records.assessment: The line announces the explosive birth of a バカップル at this spot. 'A Syrupple has here its explosive birth' uses an opaque coinage and broken English word order.
records.remedy: Use the established functional term in a grammatical announcement, such as 'Thus a hopelessly lovey-dovey couple is born.'

highlights.text:
A Syrupple has here
its explosive birth.

records.jp: 友貴に遭遇した。
records.en: I had a random encounter with Tomoki.
comments: PCP CCA0015
records.assessment: 遭遇した simply says the narrator encountered Tomoki. 'Random encounter' adds explicit video-game terminology.
records.remedy: Use 'I run into Tomoki.'

highlights.text: I had a random encounter with Tomoki.

records.jp: 「わはは、授業さぼってしまったよ。授業中の廊下って独特の世界って感じだよな」
records.en: Taichi: "Wahahah, we're totally cutting classes! You can just feel the uniqueness of the world that is a school corridor while classes are in session!"
records.assessment: The narrator says he himself skipped class. 'We're totally cutting classes' makes Tomoki jointly responsible and changes a completed lapse into a shared ongoing action.
records.remedy: Use 'Ha ha, I ended up skipping class.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wahahah, we're totally cutting classes! You can just feel the uniqueness of the world that is a school corridor while classes are in session!"

records.jp: 「虚しいからやめよう……」
records.en: Tomoki: "It's pointless, just drop it..."
comments: Look at that, it's totally afterschool! -GHS
records.assessment: 虚しい describes the performance as hollow or dispiriting. 'Pointless' instead judges its utility.
records.remedy: Use 'It's depressing, so stop...'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "It's pointless, just drop it..."

records.jp: 「空転してこそ今時の僕らだ」
records.en: Taichi: "We're just revving those engine these days, us young boys."
comments: Still the driving metaphor, it'll get a bit more use in this route. -GHS
records.assessment: 空転 is the metaphor of spinning one's wheels. 'Revving those engine' has incorrect number agreement, while 'us young boys' adds a gendered self-label absent from the line.
records.remedy: Use 'Spinning our wheels is what people our age do.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "We're just revving those engine these days, us young boys."

records.jp: 「気楽だなー、太一は」
records.en: Tomoki: "Easygoing aren't you, Taichi."
records.assessment: The direct address requires normal question punctuation and clause order. 'Easygoing aren't you' omits the comma and question mark.
records.remedy: Use 'You're carefree, aren't you, Taichi?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Easygoing aren't you, Taichi."

records.jp: 「もうサイコマンの続きは読めないんだぞ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Now I can never read how Psychoman continues no more."
comments: It ends with "they all lived happily ever after, except the non-Christians (sorry, but you were warned)". -GHS
records.assessment: The source says they can no longer read the continuation. 'Can never ... no more' uses a double negative that can reverse the meaning.
records.remedy: Use 'We'll never get to read the rest of Psychoman now.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Now I can never read how Psychoman continues no more."

records.jp: 乾いた笑い。
records.en: A parched laugh.
records.assessment: 乾いた笑い is a dry, mirthless laugh. 'Parched' ordinarily describes extreme thirst and is not the established English emotional collocation.
records.remedy: Use 'A dry laugh.'

highlights.text: A parched laugh.

records.jp: 「……そうか」
records.en: Tachi: "...so it seems."
records.assessment: The speaker label misspells Taichi as 'Tachi.'
records.remedy: Use 'Taichi.'

highlights.text: Tachi: "...so it seems."

records.jp: 「で、何しに学校に？」
records.en: Tomoki: "So, school, what'cha dying to do here?"
comments: nani SHINI gakkou ni... -GHS
records.assessment: The source asks what brings him to school. 'Dying to do' adds eagerness and asks what activity he wants rather than his reason for coming.
records.remedy: Use 'So, what brings you to school?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "So, school, what'cha dying to do here?"

records.jp: 「十代の先鋭的な部分ばかりにとらわれた思想だね」
records.en: Tomoki: "That's an idea that's all slave of a teenager's radicalist module."
comments: "It's all chuunibyou, dude". -GHS
records.assessment: The source critiques a worldview fixated only on the cutting-edge or radical aspects of adolescence. 'All slave of a teenager's radicalist module' is ungrammatical and invents a mechanistic module.
records.remedy: Use 'That worldview is fixated only on adolescence's most radical edge.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "That's an idea that's all slave of a teenager's radicalist module."

records.jp: 「まだ熱血甲子園君だっていっぱいいるんだよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "There's still lots of Hot Blooded Koshien-kun out there, you know."
comments: "People still exist damn you". http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school_baseball_in_Japan seems to be taken in contrast to the revolutionaristicoid pretentious pseudo-nihilism of above (and more). -GHS
records.assessment: The baseball-archetype label should use standard Hepburn Kōshien. 'Koshien' leaves the long vowel unmarked, and singular 'kun' conflicts with the many people referenced.
records.remedy: Use 'There are still plenty of hot-blooded Kōshien types out there.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "There's still lots of Hot Blooded Koshien-kun out there, you know."

records.jp: 「あ、彼らはポストモダンとか言ってる連中のなかでは観察価値のある人間って見なされてないから」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, but among those of us who use words such as 'postmodern', they would not be considered as humans with any observational worth."
comments: "I am so damn pretentious I'm acting as if certain people don't exist", with "oh wait there's no one anymore" as the implied subtext, but being actually a double troll. -GHS
records.assessment: The source refers to people who talk about postmodernism from the outside. 'Those of us' makes the speaker a member of that group, while 'humans with observational worth' is an unidiomatic recasting of people worth observing.
records.remedy: Use 'Among the people who talk about postmodernism, they aren't considered worth observing.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, but among those of us who use words such as 'postmodern', they would not be considered as humans with any observational worth."

records.jp: ぱたぱたと手を振る。
records.en: Flapping wave of the hand.
records.assessment: The source gives the narrator's dismissive hand wave as an action. 'Flapping wave of the hand' is a subjectless noun phrase.
records.remedy: Use 'I wave a hand dismissively.'

highlights.text: Flapping wave of the hand.

records.jp: 「わはははは、だろー」
records.en: Taichi: "Wahahahahah, can I!"
records.assessment: だろー seeks agreement: 'Right?' 'Can I!' instead asks about the speaker's ability and is punctuated as an exclamation.
records.remedy: Use 'Right?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wahahahahah, can I!"

records.jp: 毒舌な友貴は好むのだ。
records.en: Sharp-tongued Tomoki's favorite.
comments: "The favorite of Tomoki, who's sharp-tongued" + "I prefer Tomoki when he's sharp-tongued". Of course, Tomoki's no harmless young boy... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says sharp-tongued Tomoki likes black jokes. 'Sharp-tongued Tomoki's favorite' is a possessive noun fragment and omits the act of liking.
records.remedy: Use 'Sharp-tongued Tomoki enjoys that kind of thing.'

highlights.text: Sharp-tongued Tomoki's favorite.

records.jp: 「太一のおかげで久しぶりに笑ったよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while, Taichi."
comments: A little bit off... -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Tomoki laughed for the first time in a while thanks to Taichi. 'Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while' says Taichi has prevented or failed to cause laughter.
records.remedy: Use 'Thanks to you, I laughed for the first time in ages.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Haven't laughed thanks to you in a while, Taichi."

records.jp: 「つまみ食い大王が参加してないおかげで順調だよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "Thanks to the non-participation of the Great King of Foodsnatchers, fine."
records.assessment: The source is a complete reply that things are going smoothly because the Great King of Snacking is absent. The English ends with the detached adjective 'fine.'
records.remedy: Use 'It's going smoothly, thanks to the Great King of Snacking not taking part.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Thanks to the non-participation of the Great King of Foodsnatchers, fine."

records.jp: 暑苦しい笑顔、白い歯、立てた親指をガッとぶつけあう。
records.en: A lively exchange with a sweltering smile, white teeth, and raised thumb.
records.assessment: The source describes the pair forcefully bumping their raised thumbs together amid exaggerated smiles and white teeth. 'A lively exchange' omits that central contact action, and singular 'thumb' conflicts with the pair.
records.remedy: Use 'With overheated smiles and flashing white teeth, we smack our raised thumbs together.'

highlights.text: A lively exchange with a sweltering smile, white teeth, and raised thumb.

records.jp: 「いや、つまみ食い大王だから参加拒否されたじゃん……おまえに」
records.en: Taichi: "Nah, being the Great King of Foodsnatchers means my participation was rejected wasn't it... by you."
records.assessment: The source gives a coherent reminder that Tomoki rejected his participation. 'My participation was rejected wasn't it... by you' lacks the comma and question structure needed to attach the delayed agent.
records.remedy: Use 'No. You rejected me because I'm the Great King of Snacking, remember?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nah, being the Great King of Foodsnatchers means my participation was rejected wasn't it... by you."

records.jp: 寸刻、言いよどむ。
records.en: Words stagnate but for a moment.
records.assessment: 寸刻、言いよどむ says he hesitates for a brief moment. 'Words stagnate' turns speech hesitation into stationary language and uses an unnatural collocation.
records.remedy: Use 'He hesitates for a moment.'

highlights.text: Words stagnate but for a moment.

records.jp: 「……屋上の方だよ」
records.en: Tomoki: "...the one on the rooftop's."
comments: you mean the friendly ghosts who want to establish a yuritopia? -GHS
records.assessment: The source means the club on the rooftop. 'The one on the rooftop's' ends with a possessive marker but supplies nothing possessed.
records.remedy: Use '...I mean the one on the rooftop.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...the one on the rooftop's."

records.jp: 「あー、あんま出てないなぁ……いろいろあって」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, I ain't really showing up... many reasons."
records.assessment: The explanation is that he has not attended much because various things happened. 'Many reasons' is a detached noun phrase rather than a causal clause.
records.remedy: Use 'Ah, I haven't been going much... Various things came up.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, I ain't really showing up... many reasons."

records.jp: 「ま、その方がいいかもな」
records.en: Tomoki: "Well, that should be for the best, should it."
records.assessment: The source tentatively says that may be for the best. 'That should be for the best, should it' uses a malformed tag question with reversed polarity.
records.remedy: Use 'Well, maybe that's for the best.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Well, that should be for the best, should it."

records.jp: 「……いいよ、うん」
records.en: Tomoki: "...best, yes."
records.assessment: いいよ、うん is a self-reassuring 'It's fine. Yeah.' 'Best, yes' incorrectly carries the adjective from the preceding translation into this separate line.
records.remedy: Use '...It's fine. Yeah.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...best, yes."

records.jp: 様子が変だったな。
records.en: Quite an odd behavior we had here.
comments: CP CCA0018
records.assessment: The narrator observes that Tomoki was acting strangely. 'Quite an odd behavior we had here' makes the behavior shared, uses the wrong article, and removes Tomoki as its subject.
records.remedy: Use 'He was acting strangely.'

highlights.text: Quite an odd behavior we had here.

records.jp: 耳元で怒鳴られて、我に返る。
records.en: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.
records.assessment: 耳元 means right by one ear or at the narrator's ear. 'Right in the ears' uses an unnatural plural and omits the acting subject.
records.remedy: Use 'She shouts right into my ear, bringing me back to myself.'

highlights.text: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.

records.jp: 「ぼーっとしてた。無視してた。傷ついた」
records.en: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"
records.assessment: The source uses three clipped but complete accusations: he was spacing out, ignoring her, and hurt her. 'All spacing out' is not grammatical, and 'That hurts' changes the completed hurt into a present general effect.
records.remedy: Use 'You were spacing out. Ignoring me. It hurt.'

highlights.text: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"

records.jp: 「俺にはぼーっとする権利もないのですか？」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't I even have the privilege of spacing out now?"
records.assessment: 権利 is his right, not a privilege conferred by someone, and 'now' adds a temporal contrast absent from the complaint.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't I even have the right to space out?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't I even have the privilege of spacing out now?"

records.jp: 「……宮澄先輩のこと考えてたりとかして」
records.en: Touko: "...were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai maybe."
records.assessment: The tentative question needs normal English interrogative punctuation and order. 'Maybe' is left after the object and the line ends with a period.
records.remedy: Use '...Were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai, maybe?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai maybe."

records.jp: 「おとこぉ……やだ……そんなの……（赤面）」
records.en: Touko: "A guy... but no... that's so... (blushing)"
comments: SHE'S INTO BL RUN -GHS
records.assessment: The embarrassed reaction rejects the idea: 'A man...? No... I don't want that...' 'That's so' leaves the final objection unfinished without preserving its actual predicate.
records.remedy: Use 'A man...? No... I don't want that...'

highlights.text: Touko: "A guy... but no... that's so... (blushing)"

records.jp: 「なんてこった」
records.en: Taichi: "The hell's that!"
