records.assessment: なんてこった is the narrator's dismayed 'What a mess' or 'Good grief.' 'The hell's that' instead asks what an object is and adds profanity.
records.remedy: Use 'Good grief.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The hell's that!"

records.jp: 最悪だった。
records.en: That was really mean.
records.assessment: 最悪だった judges the situation or outcome the worst. 'That was really mean' instead makes it an interpersonal act of cruelty.
records.remedy: Use 'This was the worst.'

highlights.text: That was really mean.

records.jp: しかもあながち外れじゃない。
records.en: And still it's not like it's all that strange.
comments: Her reaction and him thinking about a guy. -GHS
records.assessment: あながち外れじゃない says the imagined interpretation is not entirely off the mark. 'Not all that strange' judges unusualness rather than accuracy.
records.remedy: Use 'And it wasn't entirely wrong, either.'

highlights.text: And still it's not like it's all that strange.

records.jp: 「……３馬鹿もいつもそんな感じだったら、ちょっとは夢があるのにね」
records.en: Touko: "...well, since you three stooges always gave that impression, of course there's a bit of a dream."
comments: ... -GHS
records.assessment: The source gives a conditional: if the three fools were always like that, there would be at least a little room to dream. 'Since' and 'of course' turn the hypothetical into an asserted cause and result.
records.remedy: Use '...If you three idiots were always like that, there might be something to dream about.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...well, since you three stooges always gave that impression, of course there's a bit of a dream."

records.jp: あの二人を相手に純愛ラブストーリーなんて。
records.en: A Pure Love Story with one of those two, really!
records.assessment: あの二人を相手に means imagining a pure-love story involving both of those two as the relevant counterparts. 'One of those two' arbitrarily selects only one.
records.remedy: Use 'A pure-love story with those two...'

highlights.text: A Pure Love Story with one of those two, really!

records.jp: ぞぞぞぞぞっ！
records.en: ShaaakeShakeShakeShakeShake!
records.assessment: The repeated shudder is presented as one run-on compound with inconsistent capitalization: 'ShaaakeShake.'
records.remedy: Use a consistent repeated shudder such as 'Shiver, shiver, shiver!'

highlights.text: ShaaakeShakeShakeShakeShake!

records.jp: 「気色悪いないでしょー。少なくとも３馬鹿って、みてくれはそれっぽく見えるもの」
records.en: Touko: "That's not disgusting! At least, as far as outwards you three stooges can be looked at."
comments: ...shouldn't this mean "that's what you three stooges look like [gay]?" But below... -GHS
records.assessment: The speaker denies that the thought is creepy and says the three fools at least look the part outwardly. 'That's not disgusting' uses a different quality, while 'as far as outwards ... can be looked at' is not grammatical English.
records.remedy: Use 'It's not creepy. At least you three idiots look the part.'

highlights.text: Touko: "That's not disgusting! At least, as far as outwards you three stooges can be looked at."

records.jp: 自虐ネタにしてどうにか保ってるんだ。
records.en: My self-deprecating routine is there to cover for it somehow.
comments: Best explained in the ending. ...not that Taichi gets it himself... -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator says he barely holds himself together by turning the issue into self-deprecating material. 'Cover for it' instead suggests concealing evidence or providing an excuse.
records.remedy: Use 'I only manage to hold myself together by turning it into a self-deprecating joke.'

highlights.text: My self-deprecating routine is there to cover for it somehow.

records.jp: わかっていても、意識改革なんてそう簡単にはできん。
records.en: I can understand that as much as I like, but completely changing one's way of thinking is not so simple.
records.assessment: The source concedes that even knowing the truth does not make reforming one's self-image easy. 'Understand that as much as I like' changes knowledge into a voluntary amount of understanding.
records.remedy: Use 'Even knowing that, changing how I see myself isn't easy.'

highlights.text: I can understand that as much as I like, but completely changing one's way of thinking is not so simple.

records.jp: そんなオノマトペがどこからか聞こえた。
records.en: That's the onomatopoeia that was audible from someplace.
comments: Since there's serious possibilities that Taichi is having auditory hallucinations, and this is almost certainly one of them regardless, can't specify more. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says an onomatopoeic cry seemed to come from somewhere. 'That's the onomatopoeia that was audible' is a deictic noun clause and removes the perception's uncertainty.
records.remedy: Use 'An onomatopoeic cry seems to come from somewhere.'

highlights.text: That's the onomatopoeia that was audible from someplace.

records.jp: スカートのはしをつかんだまま、頭上に固定する。
records.en: I seize the hem of the skirt, and affix it to her head.
comments: I think they sell glue in Japan for that -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator holds the skirt hem fixed above her head. 'Affix it to her head' says the fabric is attached directly onto the head and removes the elevated position.
records.remedy: Use 'Keeping hold of the skirt hem, I pin it above her head.'

highlights.text: I seize the hem of the skirt, and affix it to her head.

records.jp: 今、冬子の辱められっぷりは、並じゃない！
records.en: Now, the shaming of Touko is at levels incomparable!
records.assessment: The source exclaims that Tōko's degree of humiliation is extraordinary. 'At levels incomparable' is an ungrammatical literal degree construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko's humiliation is off the charts!'

highlights.text: Now, the shaming of Touko is at levels incomparable!

records.jp: さあ、どうする冬子！
records.en: So, what shall you do Touko!
records.assessment: The direct address requires a comma before the name.
records.remedy: Use 'Now, what will you do, Tōko?'

highlights.text: So, what shall you do Touko!

records.jp: ジト目で、俺を見るばかり。
records.en: I am but stared at by reproachful eyes.
records.assessment: The source actively says she merely looks at him with narrowed, reproachful eyes. 'I am but stared at by reproachful eyes' makes the eyes the agent and uses a stilted passive.
records.remedy: Use 'She only stares at me with narrowed eyes.'

highlights.text: I am but stared at by reproachful eyes.

records.jp: 軽く朱色に染まったりなんかしちゃって。
records.en: Her face dyes a light vermilion, that's it.
records.assessment: The source lightly describes her becoming flushed. 'Her face dyes' makes the face act on itself, and 'that's it' adds a minimizing conclusion.
records.remedy: Use 'She even flushes a faint vermilion.'

highlights.text: Her face dyes a light vermilion, that's it.

records.jp: 申し訳程度におさえた手に、本気でスキャンティをガードしようという意志はない。
records.en: Holding down her hand as if in apology, there is no serious volition of guarding her Scanties.
comments: http://www.weblio.jp/content/%E3%82%B9%E3%82%AD%E3%83%A3%E3%83%B3%E3%83%86%E3%82%A3 http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/scanties -GHS
records.assessment: The hand is perfunctorily holding the skirt down and shows no serious intent to guard the underwear. 'Holding down her hand' reverses hand and object, while capitalized 'Scanties' is an invented product-like label.
records.remedy: Use 'The hand holding it down for form's sake shows no real intention of guarding her panties.'

highlights.text: Holding down her hand as if in apology, there is no serious volition of guarding her Scanties.

records.jp: つうかモロ見えてるし。
records.en: But very much all of her frankness is visible.
records.assessment: モロ見えてる says the intimate view is fully and plainly exposed. 'All of her frankness is visible' mistakes モロ for emotional candor and removes the physical meaning.
records.remedy: Use 'I mean, everything is completely visible.'

highlights.text: But very much all of her frankness is visible.

records.jp: 「そうじゃないだろう！？」
records.en: Taichi: "That's not true you know?!"
records.assessment: そうじゃないだろう rejects the premise or point: 'That's not the issue!' 'That's not true' instead disputes the factual truth of her observation.
records.remedy: Use 'That's not the point!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "That's not true you know?!"

records.jp: 「どうしてめくった方が怒るの？」
records.en: Touko: "Why would a skirt flip make me angry now?"
records.assessment: The speaker asks why the person who flipped the skirt is the one getting angry. 'Why would a skirt flip make me angry' changes the human agent into the event and makes her anger the questioned effect.
records.remedy: Use 'Why is the person who flipped it the one getting angry?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Why would a skirt flip make me angry now?"

records.jp: 「そこはガーンと行くところだろう？」
records.en: Taichi: "Shouldn't there have been a 'dun-dun-dunnn' there?"
comments: May have termed the inversions. -GHS
records.assessment: ガーンと行く calls for a forceful retaliatory blow or explosive response. 'Dun-dun-dunnn' turns it into a dramatic musical sting.
records.remedy: Use 'This is where you strike back with a bang, isn't it?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Shouldn't there have been a 'dun-dun-dunnn' there?"

records.jp: 「さあ、おまえの技を見せてくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "Well, show me some your techniques!"
records.assessment: 'Some your techniques' uses two incompatible determiners.
records.remedy: Use 'Now, show me one of your techniques.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, show me some your techniques!"

records.jp: 「ポッって……」
records.en: Taichi: "Flushed..."
records.assessment: The line comments on the preceding blush sound itself, equivalent to 'She went pop...' or 'That little blush...' 'Flushed' changes it into a past-tense adjective and loses the quoted sound.
records.remedy: Use 'That little pop...' with a consistent blush rendering.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Flushed..."

records.jp: こく、と少女はうなずく。
records.en: Bob and the girl gives a nod.
records.assessment: The source says the girl gives a small nod. 'Bob and the girl gives a nod' invents an unexplained name or sound and uses incorrect subject-verb agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'The girl gives a small nod.'

highlights.text: Bob and the girl gives a nod.

records.jp: 冬子は死んだ、と。
records.en: "Touko is dead."
comments: This line is so not funny on the second time through. -GHS
records.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 冬子 as Tōko. 'Touko' uses an unmarked long-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko is dead.'

highlights.text: "Touko is dead."

records.jp: 否。
records.en: Nay.
records.assessment: 否 is a direct rhetorical 'No.' 'Nay' adds an archaic English register not otherwise present in the narration.
records.remedy: Use 'No.'

highlights.text: Nay.

records.jp: 冬子という個が死んだのではない。
records.en: Touko, the individual, has not died.
records.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 冬子 as Tōko. 'Touko' uses an unmarked long-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'It is not the individual called Tōko who died.'

highlights.text: Touko, the individual, has not died.

records.jp: 冬子に見立てられていた、手の早い勝ち気娘という、大いなる最大公約数的価値観が喪失せしめられたのである。
records.en:
In the analysis of Touko's character, the
quarrelsome, unyielding spirit that acts as an
enormous maximum common denominator for her values
had now been forcefully removed from her.
records.assessment: The lost thing is a broad projected value or archetype—the quick-to-hit, strong-willed girl that had been read into Tōko. The English calls it part of an analysis and says the trait was removed from her, treating the projection as an actual possession.
records.remedy: Use 'What was lost was the great common-denominator ideal projected onto Tōko: the quick-to-hit, strong-willed girl.'

highlights.text:
In the analysis of Touko's character, the
quarrelsome, unyielding spirit that acts as an
enormous maximum common denominator for her values
had now been forcefully removed from her.

records.jp: 冬子はリアルになってしまった。また。
records.en: Touko became completely realistic. Again.
comments: Hint hint. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says Tōko became real again. 'Completely' adds degree, and 'Touko' is nonstandard long-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko had become real again.'

highlights.text: Touko became completely realistic. Again.

records.jp: けど俺は、いつもカリカリしている冬子が好きなんだけどなぁ。
records.en:
But me, I like the Touko that is always
irritably edgy.
records.assessment: 'But me, I like' is dislocated and redundant, while standard Hepburn is Tōko rather than 'Touko.'
records.remedy: Use 'But I like Tōko when she is always prickly.'

highlights.text:
But me, I like the Touko that is always
irritably edgy.

records.jp: だって、それが一番安定してる。
records.en: Because that's the most equilibrated.
records.assessment: 安定してる means stable or consistent in behavior. 'Equilibrated' is technical process vocabulary and implies an achieved physical equilibrium.
records.remedy: Use 'Because that version of her is the most stable.'

highlights.text: Because that's the most equilibrated.

records.jp: 「禁断の奥義をば」
records.en: Taichi: "Time for Forbidden Esoterica!"
comments: See CCA0022 -GHS
records.assessment: 奥義 is a secret or ultimate technique. 'Esoterica' means obscure knowledge or artifacts and does not name an action.
records.remedy: Use 'Time for the forbidden secret technique.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Time for Forbidden Esoterica!"

records.jp: 「もうはなしてよー……スースーして落ち着かないわ」
records.en: Touko: "Lemme go alreadyyy... it's all breezy and it won't stop."
comments: See CCA0015B -GHS
records.assessment: スースーして落ち着かない means the breezy exposure makes her unable to settle down. 'It won't stop' instead makes an unspecified thing continue acting.
records.remedy: Use 'Let go already... The draft is making me restless.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Lemme go alreadyyy... it's all breezy and it won't stop."

records.jp: 「もっとスースーするようにしてやる。パンツを脱いだりナプキンを押さえたりできなくしてやる」
records.en: Taichi: "I will make it more breezy-breezy. Otherwise it's impossible for me to take off the panties or make you wear a sanitary napkin!"
comments: STILL on about her being on her period. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator threatens to make her more exposed and unable to remove her panties or hold a sanitary pad in place. The English makes those actions things he cannot do and changes holding a pad to making her wear one.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll make it even breezier. I'll make it impossible for you to take off your panties or hold a pad in place.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I will make it more breezy-breezy. Otherwise it's impossible for me to take off the panties or make you wear a sanitary napkin!"

records.jp: 「……ちょっと、このまま引っ張るつもりじゃないでしょうね―――」
records.en: Touko: "...wait, you can't exactly yank them off when I'm like this---"
records.assessment: このまま引っ張る asks whether he intends to drag her along while keeping her in that state. 'Yank them off' changes the action to removing a plural garment.
records.remedy: Use '...You aren't planning to drag me along like this, are you—'

highlights.text: Touko: "...wait, you can't exactly yank them off when I'm like this---"

records.jp: 下着をおろした。
records.en: The underwear down slides.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator lowered the underwear. 'The underwear down slides' makes the garment move by itself and uses inverted, ungrammatical word order.
records.remedy: Use 'I pull down her underwear.'

highlights.text: The underwear down slides.

records.jp: 足首まで。
records.en: Until the ankle.
records.assessment: 足首まで means down to both ankles in the carried sentence. 'Until the ankle' uses the wrong preposition and singular number.
records.remedy: Use 'All the way to her ankles.'

highlights.text: Until the ankle.

records.jp: おっともうかかってたか、さすがに仕事がはやいぜ！
records.en: Hoh, it already took. As typical, it works so fast!
records.assessment: The narrator notices the censor mosaic has already been applied and praises the speed of that work. 'It already took' and 'it works so fast' treat the mosaic as an effect taking hold or a mechanism operating.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh, it is already on. They work fast!'

highlights.text: Hoh, it already took. As typical, it works so fast!

records.jp: 得意のフランス語を駆使して、俺は冬子の陰部を絶賛した。
records.en: Freely using most skilled French, I present great admiration to Touko's genitalia.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator uses his specialty French to lavish praise on Tōko's genitals. 'Using most skilled French' and 'present great admiration to' are not grammatical collocations, and 'Touko' is nonstandard Hepburn.
records.remedy: Use 'Employing my best French, I lavish praise on Tōko's genitals.'

highlights.text: Freely using most skilled French, I present great admiration to Touko's genitalia.

records.jp: 『こんのぉ』と言っている。
records.en: She's saying "reallyyy",
comments: PCP CCA0002
records.assessment: The narration explicitly says she is trying to say the distorted sound こんのぉ. Rendering it as 'reallyyy' substitutes a different lexical item and disconnects the explanation from the prior cry.
records.remedy: Use a consistent distorted rendering of kono across the cry and explanation.

highlights.text: She's saying "reallyyy",

records.jp: 舌っ足らずなのだろう。
records.en: so that had to have been her lisp.
comments: PCP CCA0002
Technically it's identical, but the original line doesn't have the kanji in 'tarazu'. -GHS
records.assessment: The narrator tentatively attributes the distortion to her tongue-tied speech. 'Had to have been her lisp' overstates certainty and frames the lisp as a possessed object.
records.remedy: Use 'Her tongue must not be cooperating.'

highlights.text: so that had to have been her lisp.

records.jp: キスするとよくわかる。
records.en: It's easily understood when kissing:
records.assessment: The source says that the narrator can tell clearly when he kisses her. 'It's easily understood when kissing' turns his direct perception into an impersonal passive and leaves the action without participants.
records.remedy: Use 'You can really tell when you kiss her.'

highlights.text: It's easily understood when kissing:

records.jp: ちょっと舌を吸うと、アップアップするから。
records.en: suck a bit on her lip, and she flounders as if drowning, up, up, up.
comments: アップアップ sometimes the Japanese have an actually clever sense of humor. -GHS
records.assessment: 舌 is her tongue, not her lip. The English moves the intimate action to a different body part.
records.remedy: Use 'When I suck lightly on her tongue, she flounders as if she is drowning.'

highlights.text: suck a bit on her lip, and she flounders as if drowning, up, up, up.

records.jp: どかーん！
records.en: Bokan!
comments: Well, why not. -GHS
records.assessment: どかーん is an explosive crash or boom. 'Bokan' substitutes the title word from the preceding reference instead of rendering the impact sound.
records.remedy: Use 'Boom!'

highlights.text: Bokan!

records.jp: 「これこれーーーーーーっ！！」
records.en: Taichi: "Helpy heeeeeeeeelp!!!"
comments: Response to Scapontan? Without even a video... -GHS
records.assessment: これこれ is the narrator's excited approving or demonstrative cry in response to the referenced bit. 'Helpy help' invents a plea for rescue and reverses the utterance's function.
records.remedy: Use a context-consistent cry such as 'That's it!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Helpy heeeeeeeeelp!!!"

records.jp: もういない、新川豊という男のことを。
records.en: about Shinkawa Yutaka, the man that was no more.
records.assessment: The personal name 新川豊 should be presented in standard Hepburn as Yutaka Shinkawa in ordinary English name order. 'Shinkawa Yutaka' retains Japanese order without an edition-wide reason.
records.remedy: Use 'of Yutaka Shinkawa, the man who was no longer here.'

highlights.text: about Shinkawa Yutaka, the man that was no more.

records.jp: きゃつはそう言った。
records.en: the gal went and said.
records.assessment: きゃつ is a contemptuous or mock-archaic 'that knave/fellow.' 'The gal' identifies sex but loses the narrator's pointedly derisive register.
records.remedy: Use 'the wretch said.'

highlights.text: the gal went and said.

records.jp: リヤカーにして三台分ほどあった。
records.en: There were about three bike trailer loads,
comments: They load the stuff on the RV, so he's guesstimating I think. The question is why: the answer, they never take the RV. -GHS
records.assessment: A リヤカー is a two-wheeled handcart. 'Bike trailer' specifies a bicycle-towed vehicle and changes the object used for the three-load estimate.
records.remedy: Use 'There were about three handcart-loads in all.'

highlights.text: There were about three bike trailer loads,

records.jp: 走り屋マンガで学んだからだ。
records.en: because I've studied racing mangas.
comments: Well, see CCB2002. -GHS
records.assessment: 'Mangas' uses a nonstandard English plural for manga in this sentence.
records.remedy: Use 'because I learned from racing manga.'

highlights.text: because I've studied racing mangas.

records.jp: いろいろあったが、とりあえず冬子はトラウマになった。
records.en: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.
records.assessment: The source says only that various things happened and that, in any case, Tōko was traumatized. 'The main of which' invents a ranking and makes the trauma one event in a relative-clause list.
records.remedy: Use 'A lot happened, but in any case Tōko was traumatized.'

highlights.text: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.

records.jp: 二度と俺の車には乗らないとまで言った。
records.en: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.
records.assessment: 俺の車 is the narrator's car. 'A vehicle with me driving' generalizes her vow to every vehicle he might drive.
records.remedy: Use 'She even said she would never ride in my car again.'

highlights.text: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.

records.jp: いやー、シートベルトしていて本当に良かった。
records.en: Welll, it was a good thing we had seatbelts.
records.assessment: 'Welll' contains an unintended extra letter rather than a controlled marked-vowel spelling.
records.remedy: Use 'Well, it was a good thing we were wearing seat belts.'

highlights.text: Welll, it was a good thing we had seatbelts.

records.jp: とにかく『黒須家近所までは車を使えた』ので、あとはそこから移動すればよかった。
records.en: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.
records.assessment: The source says they were able to use the vehicle as far as the neighborhood of the Kurosu residence and only had to move the load from there. 'Walk away from the plan' says that they abandoned the plan and omits the successful transport stage.
records.remedy: Say that the car got them as far as the Kurosu neighborhood, leaving only the move from there.

highlights.text: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.

records.jp: 俺と冬子はリヤカーを探した。
records.en: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.
comments: I.e. they don't have them now. -GHS
records.assessment: 'Me and Touko' uses the object pronoun as the subject of the sentence.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko and I searched for a handcart.'

highlights.text: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.

records.jp: 冬子などはご令嬢であるためかリヤカーというものをフロントにカゴのついたママチャリだと勘違いしていたので、貧乏人代表として怒りの乳揉みをしてやった。
records.en: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.
comments: I think I read somewhere that even ojisans like granny bikes. That's very important information! -GHS
records.assessment: The English begins with the ungrammatical article sequence 'an young,' calls the mamachari a 'granny bike,' and weakens the narrator's aggressive 胸揉み from groping or kneading her breasts to a neutral massage.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical sentence that identifies the basket-equipped mamachari and preserves the deliberately improper breast-groping action.

highlights.text: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.

records.jp: で、俺が探し出したリヤカーで三往復。
records.en: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.
comments: That's 6, plus the attempt with the RV. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that the narrator found the handcart. 'We found' changes the finder to the pair.
records.remedy: Use 'Then I made three round trips with the handcart I found.'

highlights.text: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.

records.jp: 疲労困憊。
records.en: Fatigue at extreme levels.
comments: ...but he managed to make three round trips on a bike with a trailer in these hilly roads without dying. -GHS
records.assessment: 疲労困憊 is the complete state of being utterly exhausted. 'Fatigue at extreme levels' is an abstract degree fragment rather than an idiomatic account of the narrator's condition.
records.remedy: Use 'I was completely exhausted.'

highlights.text: Fatigue at extreme levels.

records.jp: 「……なに、この物置？」
records.en: Touko: "...what's even this storeroom?"
comments: But she should know Taichi's bedroom... all too well, in fact, see CCD2002. Let's go with minor plot hole. -GHS
records.assessment: 'What's even this storeroom?' is not grammatical English question order and does not naturally convey the dismissive なに、この construction.
records.remedy: Use '...What is this, a storeroom?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...what's even this storeroom?"

records.jp: 怒りのまま、冬子にクレームをつける。
records.en: Anger remains, so I file a complaint to Touko.
records.assessment: 怒りのまま says the narrator complains while still angry. 'Anger remains, so' turns the state into an explicit cause, while English files a complaint with or against someone rather than 'to' them.
records.remedy: Use 'Still angry, I lodge a complaint with Tōko.'

highlights.text: Anger remains, so I file a complaint to Touko.

records.jp: 「だいたいおまえは武道家のはしくれなんだから力仕事くらいできるだろうが！　カマトトぶりやがってもう底は見えてるんだよ！　すぺぺぺぺっ！」
records.en: Taichi: "Aren't you some leftover of a martial artist or something, you can do some physical labor too you know! I can see all through to the bottom of your feigned ignorance by the way! Ner-nernerner!"
comments: Most references to that sort of line tend to flow into this: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E5%A4%A7%E4%B8%80%E7%9B%B4%E7%B7%9A can't see from the description of the gag how that'd fit here, can't find any scans from the manga with examples, and no official English translation seems to exist. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6fXIXAHr_mg this video may elucidate... maybe. Maybe. Nope. -GHS
records.assessment: 武道家のはしくれ means even a lowly or novice martial artist, not a leftover. カマトトぶる means to feign innocence, while 'some leftover of' and 'all through to the bottom' are not coherent English renderings.
records.remedy: Say that even a novice martial artist can handle physical work and that he sees through her feigned innocence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Aren't you some leftover of a martial artist or something, you can do some physical labor too you know! I can see all through to the bottom of your feigned ignorance by the way! Ner-nernerner!"

records.jp: 「……女の細腕に何させようってのよ。馬鹿じゃないの」
records.en: Touko: "...what do you want a woman's thin arms to do! Aren't you stupid."
records.assessment: The English splices an exclamation onto 'what do you want ... to do' and then punctuates the following direct insult as a statement. The source contains two coherent challenges.
records.remedy: Use 'What are you trying to make these slender arms do? Are you stupid?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...what do you want a woman's thin arms to do! Aren't you stupid."

records.jp: ちょっと気分を害した様子。
records.en: There was a little bit of offense in that.
records.assessment: The source observes that Tōko seems slightly offended. 'There was ... offense in that' turns her reaction into an abstract property of the prior speech.
records.remedy: Use 'She seems a little offended.'

highlights.text: There was a little bit of offense in that.

records.jp: 冬子は雪だから優しくするとすぐトロトロとけるので、絶対甘い顔は見せないと決めた。
records.en: Touko, written with the kanji for Winter and Child, is snow; therefore, when treated warmly she soon melts into a sticky syrupy mess. That is why she decided to absolutely never show her sweet side.
records.assessment: The narrator decides that he must never show Tōko indulgence because she melts when treated gently. The English makes Tōko the one who decides never to show her sweet side, reversing the acting subject and the lesson drawn from the snow metaphor.
records.remedy: Say that because Tōko melts when treated gently, the narrator resolves never to go easy on her.

highlights.text: Touko, written with the kanji for Winter and Child, is snow; therefore, when treated warmly she soon melts into a sticky syrupy mess. That is why she decided to absolutely never show her sweet side.

records.jp: ぱっと顔が輝く。
records.en: Bam, her face shined.
records.assessment: ぱっと describes her face suddenly lighting up. 'Bam' supplies an impact sound rather than the rapid brightening.
records.remedy: Use 'Her face lights up at once.'

highlights.text: Bam, her face shined.

records.jp: 「……そんな贅沢できるか。水は貴重品だぞ」
records.en: Taichi: "...but can we afford luxuries? Water is a valuable thing now."
records.assessment: The narrator states that water is precious and presents the luxury objection he would make. 'Can we afford luxuries?' changes that assertion into a question about shared means.
records.remedy: Use '...We can't afford a luxury like that. Water is precious.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...but can we afford luxuries? Water is a valuable thing now."

records.jp: 「と言いたいところだが、入れるのだ」
records.en: Taichi: "That's what I'd like to say, but we should take a bath."
records.assessment: 入れるのだ announces that they can take a bath despite the preceding objection. 'We should take a bath' changes ability and permission into advice.
records.remedy: Use 'That's what I'd like to say, but you can take one.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "That's what I'd like to say, but we should take a bath."

records.jp: 「スメルマニアとして、確認させてもらおうか」
records.en: Taichi: "As a Smell Fetishist, I wonder if I can confirm it?"
records.assessment: 確認させてもらおうか is a mock-threatening proposal to let him verify it. 'I wonder if I can' turns that pressure into a private, tentative question.
records.remedy: Use 'As a smell fetishist, allow me to check.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "As a Smell Fetishist, I wonder if I can confirm it?"

records.jp: 「ちょっ、ウソでしょ、やめてよ、来ないでっ！」
records.en: Touko: "Wha-, that's false, stop it, don't get closer!"
records.assessment: ウソでしょ is an alarmed 'You can't be serious' or 'You're kidding,' not the factual declaration 'that's false.'
records.remedy: Use 'W-wait, you're kidding! Stop! Don't come any closer!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Wha-, that's false, stop it, don't get closer!"

records.jp: 鬼畜笑いを浮かべて、俺は獲物を部屋のすみに追いつめていく。
records.en: Surfacing the laugh of a brute of a man, I drive my prey into the corner of the room.
records.assessment: 鬼畜笑い is a sadistic or fiendish laugh that the narrator puts on. 'Surfacing the laugh of a brute of a man' is not grammatical or idiomatic English.
records.remedy: Use 'With a sadistic laugh, I drive my prey into a corner of the room.'

highlights.text: Surfacing the laugh of a brute of a man, I drive my prey into the corner of the room.

records.jp: 整った容貌が、青ざめて歪む。
records.en: Her well-ordered features distort into paleness.
comments: Ugh, this sentence. -GHS
records.assessment: 整った容貌 is her finely formed face and 青ざめて歪む says it pales and twists. 'Well-ordered features distort into paleness' treats pallor as a shape and uses unnatural collocations.
records.remedy: Use 'Her finely formed face pales and twists.'

highlights.text: Her well-ordered features distort into paleness.

records.jp: 「来ると、どうなのかね？　無力な婦女子ひとり、どう抗おうというのだね？　この生けるカラデ道・マス黒須を相手に」
records.en: Taichi: "If I do, what then? What opposition could a helpless young fujoshi of a woman, alone, pose? As an opponent of the 『Living Karadeka * 'The Trout' Kurosu』, even!"
comments: Of course he means fujoshi in the nice way, heheheh. See CCA0022, still no idea what the hell Tanaka was even thinking. -GHS
records.assessment: 婦女子 means a woman or girl, not 腐女子, a fujoshi. The English imports the unrelated fandom label and leaves the mock-heroic challenge in broken prepositional syntax.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical challenge addressed to one helpless woman and preserve the narrator's mock title.

highlights.text: Taichi: "If I do, what then? What opposition could a helpless young fujoshi of a woman, alone, pose? As an opponent of the 『Living Karadeka * 'The Trout' Kurosu』, even!"

records.jp: 変態紳士口調で冬子に問いかける。
records.en: So ask Touko with the tone of a gentlemen and a pervert.
records.assessment: The source says the narrator asks Tōko in the manner of a perverted gentleman. 'So ask Touko with the tone of a gentlemen' has the wrong tense, lacks its subject, and mismatches singular 'a' with plural 'gentlemen.'
records.remedy: Use 'I ask Tōko in the tones of a gentlemanly pervert.'

highlights.text: So ask Touko with the tone of a gentlemen and a pervert.

records.jp: 鯉口を切る音がした。
records.en: The sound of the hilt of a sword being disconnected from the mouth of its scabbard.
comments: ...though it doesn't fit the actual sound effect *sigh*. -GHS
records.assessment: 鯉口を切る is the practiced action of loosening a sword in its scabbard, producing a click. 'The mouth of its scabbard' literalizes the Japanese term and 'disconnected' describes the wrong mechanical relation.
records.remedy: Use 'I hear the click of a sword being loosened in its scabbard.'

highlights.text: The sound of the hilt of a sword being disconnected from the mouth of its scabbard.

records.jp: 「斬る」
records.en: Touko: "Slay."
records.assessment: The speaker's clipped threat is still a first-person action: she will cut him. The bare imperative-like 'Slay' omits both actor and target.
records.remedy: Use 'I'll cut you.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Slay."

records.jp: 「そ、それは妖刀　ハラキリ丸！？」
records.en: Taichi: "Is-, is that the Demon Blade Harakiri?!"
records.assessment: ハラキリ丸 is the invented full sword name Harakiri-maru. 'Harakiri' drops the name-forming suffix and presents it as an ordinary noun.
records.remedy: Use 'I-is that the demon sword Harakiri-maru?!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Is-, is that the Demon Blade Harakiri?!"

records.jp: 「……愛刀・今虎徹よ」
records.en: Touko: "...it's my 『Favored Sword * Ima Kotetsu』!"
comments: See CCA0030. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagasone_Kotetsu Seems to be just named after him. Oddly, one of the name pronunciations for 今 ima "now" is Yakiniku - roast meat. It's either incredibly odd or someone is trolling EDICT. -GHS
records.assessment: 今虎徹 is a single coined sword name, Imakotetsu. 'Ima Kotetsu' incorrectly splits it into two name elements.
records.remedy: Use '...It is my beloved blade, Imakotetsu.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...it's my 『Favored Sword * Ima Kotetsu』!"

records.jp: 「無双直伝英信流……段位なし」
records.en: Touko: "Muso Jikiden Eishin-ryu... no dan."
comments: Most popular Iaido style. Not the best romanization, but this googles faster. -GHS
records.assessment: 段位なし means that she holds no rank. Leaving 'dan' untranslated obscures the joke for an English reader.
records.remedy: Use 'Musō Jikiden Eishin-ryū... no rank.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Muso Jikiden Eishin-ryu... no dan."

records.jp: 「取れるわけないでしょ！！」
records.en: Touko: "Because I'm forbidden from taking any you know!!!"
comments: People in Gunjou wouldn't exactly be allowed weapons, especially someone like her with a history. -GHS
records.assessment: 取れるわけない says there is no way she could obtain a rank. 'I'm forbidden from taking any' invents an external prohibition and leaves the object of 'any' unclear.
records.remedy: Use 'There is no way I could earn one!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Because I'm forbidden from taking any you know!!!"

records.jp: 「でも刀はいいから良く切れる！」
records.en: Touko: "But the sword is good and will cut you nicely!"
records.assessment: 良く切れる praises how well the sword cuts. 'Will cut you nicely' adds the listener as a threatened object and introduces an incongruously pleasant adverb.
records.remedy: Use 'But it is a good sword, so it cuts well!'

highlights.text: Touko: "But the sword is good and will cut you nicely!"

records.jp: 「居合いの理念に反するんじゃないのかそれは！」
records.en: Taichi: "Isn't what you just did against the philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai!"
records.assessment: The line asks whether her behavior violates the philosophy of iai. 'The philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai' is not grammatical English and replaces the discipline with an improvised procedure label.
records.remedy: Use 'Doesn't that violate the philosophy of iai?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Isn't what you just did against the philosophy of unsheathe-cut-sheathe of the Iai!"

records.jp: 居合とは、人に斬られず人斬らず、己を責めて平らかの道……。
records.en: Iai is a peaceful way of self-criticism where no man is slain and is slain by no man...
records.assessment: 己を責めて describes disciplining or mastering oneself on a peaceful path. 'Self-criticism' reduces it to fault-finding, while the doubled passive obscures the balanced injunction neither to cut nor be cut.
records.remedy: Use 'Iai is a peaceful path: cut no one, be cut by no one, and discipline the self.'

highlights.text: Iai is a peaceful way of self-criticism where no man is slain and is slain by no man...

records.jp: 「生き恥をかくぐらいならば、いっそもろとも！」
records.en: Touko: "If a life of disgrace is what awaits, then this is better for all of us!"
comments: Doesn't seem to be a quote. See sendback route. Much nastier than it seems. -GHS
records.assessment: いっそもろとも threatens to take both of them down together rather than live in disgrace. 'This is better for all of us' turns mutual destruction into a beneficial collective outcome.
records.remedy: Use 'Rather than live in disgrace, I'll take us both down!'

highlights.text: Touko: "If a life of disgrace is what awaits, then this is better for all of us!"

records.jp: 「ウエイツ！　ウエイツ！」
records.en: Taichi: "UEITSU! UEITSU!"
records.assessment: ウエイツ is the deliberately Japanized sound of the English plea 'Wait,' leading into the narrator's temporary-American joke. 'UEITSU' merely retransliterates the katakana and leaves the plea unintelligible.
records.remedy: Use 'Wait! Wait!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "UEITSU! UEITSU!"

records.jp: 「ＯＫわかった、悪戯はやめだ。そっちもその物騒なのをしまってくれ」
records.en: Taichi: "OKIEH, I geddit, I'ma stop with the kidding. So please, drop the danger on your side too!"
comments: Capeesh? -GHS
records.assessment: しまってくれ asks her to put the dangerous sword away. 'Drop the danger on your side' instead suggests discarding an abstract danger and does not express sheathing or stowing the weapon.
records.remedy: Use a faux-American but intelligible request for her to put the dangerous thing away.

highlights.text: Taichi: "OKIEH, I geddit, I'ma stop with the kidding. So please, drop the danger on your side too!"

records.jp: 冬子はギラギラした目をしていた。
records.en: Touko's eyes sparkled and dazzled,
records.assessment: ギラギラした目 are fierce, glaring eyes in this armed standoff. 'Sparkled and dazzled' gives them a bright or attractive quality and reverses the threatening affect.
records.remedy: Use 'Tōko's eyes were glaring wildly.'

highlights.text: Touko's eyes sparkled and dazzled,

records.jp: まさにキチ○イに刃物。
records.en: as if a lu**tic with a cutting implement.
comments: See CCA0007. -GHS
records.assessment: The source invokes the fixed image of a mad person holding a blade. 'As if a lu**tic with a cutting implement' is a verbless comparison and loses the idiom's warning that the combination is dangerous.
records.remedy: Use 'She was the very picture of a madwoman with a blade.' while preserving the source's censorship policy.

highlights.text: as if a lu**tic with a cutting implement.

records.jp: 後ろ向きにじりじりと廊下に出て、そのまま右にスライドしていく。
records.en: Inching and inching she moves backwards and exits to the corridor, and with the same, she slides towards the right.
comments: HER right, you idiots. -GHS
records.assessment: そのまま says she continues directly from backing into the hall to sliding right. 'With the same' is not an English connective for an unchanged motion or posture.
records.remedy: Use 'Still inching backward, she enters the hall and slides off to the right.'

highlights.text: Inching and inching she moves backwards and exits to the corridor, and with the same, she slides towards the right.

records.jp: ジト目が廊下に消えた。
records.en: Scornful eyes disappeared down the hallway.
records.assessment: ジト目 is Tōko's reproachful sideways glare. 'Scornful eyes disappeared' detaches the expression from its owner and uses the eyes themselves as the moving subject.
records.remedy: Use 'Her reproachful glare disappears down the hall.'

highlights.text: Scornful eyes disappeared down the hallway.

records.jp: 殺気も一緒に洗い落としたのか、ぺたぺた身を寄せてきた。
records.en: Washed off together with the rest her bloodlust, I'm flattened flat by this sticky housemate.
comments: she's more like tsundepetta, except when she's PTA. -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that, perhaps having washed off her murderous aura too, Tōko pads over and presses close to the narrator. The English instead says the narrator is flattened by a 'sticky housemate,' replacing her approach and affectionate physical action.
records.remedy: Use 'Perhaps she washed away her murderous aura too; she pads over and snuggles against me.'

highlights.text: Washed off together with the rest her bloodlust, I'm flattened flat by this sticky housemate.

records.jp: 「やだ、太一ちょっと汗くさい！」
records.en: Touko: "But no, you stink of sweat Taichi!"
records.assessment: The direct address requires a comma before Taichi.
records.remedy: Use 'Oh no, Taichi, you smell sweaty!'

highlights.text: Touko: "But no, you stink of sweat Taichi!"

records.jp: 「……俺はフェチっ子だからフェチ娘に手はあげないがセクハラはするぞコラ」
records.en: Taichi: "...I am a fetishist therefore on a fetishette I shan't lay hand but sexual harassment will ensue so stop it!"
records.assessment: The source contrasts not hitting a fellow fetishist with still sexually harassing her. 'On a fetishette I shan't lay hand' is malformed inversion, and the passive 'harassment will ensue' removes the narrator's agency.
records.remedy: Use 'I'm a fetishist, so I won't hit a fetish girl—but I will sexually harass you, damn it.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...I am a fetishist therefore on a fetishette I shan't lay hand but sexual harassment will ensue so stop it!"

records.jp: 「怒らいでか！」
records.en: Taichi: "Because I was made angry, what do you think?!"
records.assessment: 怒らいでか is the rhetorical 'How could I not be angry?' 'Because I was made angry' changes the construction into a causal answer and adds an external causer.
records.remedy: Use 'How could I not be angry?!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because I was made angry, what do you think?!"

records.jp: 「……も、いい。水浴びしてくる」
records.en: Taichi: "...bah, it's fine. I will take this bath."
records.assessment: 水浴び is the narrator's decision to go wash or bathe in cold water. 'Take this bath' introduces a demonstrative bath and loses the motion away to do it.
records.remedy: Use '...Forget it. I'm going to wash off.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...bah, it's fine. I will take this bath."

records.jp: 戻ってくると、部屋が整頓されていた。
records.en: On returning, my room was completely tidied up.
records.assessment: The source says that the room had been put in order. 'My room' adds possession not stated in this line.
records.remedy: Use 'When I came back, the room had been tidied.'

highlights.text: On returning, my room was completely tidied up.

records.jp: 「二人で暮らすんだもの。片づけておいたの」
records.en: Touko: "Two are living together now. Things must be settled and ordered."
comments: multiple meanings, duh -GHS
records.assessment: The source says that because the two of them will be living together, Tōko went ahead and tidied the room. 'Two are living together' drops the participants, while 'Things must be settled' changes her completed action into an impersonal obligation.
records.remedy: Use 'We'll be living together, so I went ahead and tidied up.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Two are living together now. Things must be settled and ordered."

records.jp: 「睦美おばさんみたいなことをしてくれる……」
records.en: Taichi: "This something so like what Mutsumi-obasan would do..."
records.assessment: The narrator says that she is doing something Mutsumi-obasan would do. 'This something so like' is not grammatical English and omits the acting subject.
records.remedy: Use 'You're doing the sort of thing Mutsumi-obasan would do...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "This something so like what Mutsumi-obasan would do..."

records.jp: ふぁさーっとお嬢様式後ろ髪払いを繰り出した。
records.en: In the manners of a young noblewoman, she repeatedly sweeped her long bangs with a fwasaaah,
records.assessment: The source describes one sweeping toss of her back hair in a young-lady style. The English says she 'repeatedly sweeped' her bangs, inventing repetition, naming the wrong section of hair, and using a nonexistent past tense.
records.remedy: Use 'With a fwoosh, she gives her hair a young lady's backward toss.'

highlights.text: In the manners of a young noblewoman, she repeatedly sweeped her long bangs with a fwasaaah,

records.jp: 『よくってよ』とか言いそうなオーラが満ちた。
records.en: filled with an aura that seemed to say, 'wasn't this well done then!'
records.assessment: 『よくってよ』 is the stereotypically aristocratic assent 'Very well' or 'You may.' 'Wasn't this well done then' turns it into self-congratulation about the cleaning.
records.remedy: Use 'She radiates an aura that seems ready to say: Very well.'

highlights.text: filled with an aura that seemed to say, 'wasn't this well done then!'

records.jp: まず見たのは、机の上だった。
records.en: She must first have seen the ones above the desk.
records.assessment: The narrator says the first place he looked was on top of the desk. 'She must first have seen' changes the subject to Tōko, the action from looking to seeing, and certainty into conjecture.
records.remedy: Use 'The first place I looked was on top of the desk.'

highlights.text: She must first have seen the ones above the desk.

records.jp: えてして女というものは、そういうことをする。
records.en: These things called women will sometimes act like that.
records.assessment: えてして女というものは says that women are often apt to do such things. 'These things called women' objectifies the noun through a literal demonstrative construction and 'sometimes act like that' weakens the claimed tendency.
records.remedy: Use 'Women are often apt to do that sort of thing.'

highlights.text: These things called women will sometimes act like that.

records.jp: だが、ない。
records.en: But, there's none.
records.assessment: The carried object is the narrator's plural books. 'There's none' uses singular agreement and an existential construction instead of stating that they are absent.
records.remedy: Use 'But they aren't there.'

highlights.text: But, there's none.

records.jp: 「おい桐原、こ、ここにあった俺のヌードデッサン用の書物はどうした？」
records.en: Taichi: "Hey, Kirihara, the nu-, nude design reference books that were here, what happened to them?"
records.assessment: ヌードデッサン means drawing the nude figure. 'Nude design' substitutes commercial design for figure drawing and weakens the narrator's transparent cover story.
records.remedy: Use 'Hey, Kirihara, what happened to the books on nude figure drawing that were here?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hey, Kirihara, the nu-, nude design reference books that were here, what happened to them?"

records.jp: 姑息な俺だった。
records.en: I was just temporizing.
records.assessment: 姑息 here judges the narrator's excuse as cowardly or underhanded. 'Temporizing' instead means delaying a decision or buying time and does not express that self-condemnation.
records.remedy: Use 'I was a coward.'

highlights.text: I was just temporizing.

records.jp: 「ああ、写真の載ってた本？」
records.en: Taichi: "Ah, those books with all the photos?"
records.assessment: The source speaker is Tōko, answering the narrator's question. The English labels the line as Taichi and makes him answer himself.
records.remedy: Label the reply as Tōko: 'Oh, the books with photographs?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ah, those books with all the photos?"

records.jp: 俺はびーんと一直線になったまま倒れた。
records.en: I straightened like a beam and fell down.
records.assessment: びーんと一直線 describes his whole body going rigidly straight. 'Like a beam' introduces a building object and does not idiomatically describe the comic collapse.
records.remedy: Use 'My body goes ramrod-straight and topples over.'

highlights.text: I straightened like a beam and fell down.

records.jp: 「なんか……見てたらそうしなくちゃっていう気持ちになって……」
records.en: Touko: "There's... there was this feeling, that the instant I saw them, I had to do it."
records.assessment: The English begins with the false start 'There's... there was' and makes the feeling arise the instant she saw the books. The source says that as she kept looking, she came to feel she had to act.
records.remedy: Use 'I don't know... As I looked at them, I started feeling that I had to do it...'

highlights.text: Touko: "There's... there was this feeling, that the instant I saw them, I had to do it."

records.jp: 「学術書を焼くだなんて！　おまえは秦の始皇帝か！　第三帝国か！」
records.en: Taichi: "You burned school textbooks! You are the First Emperor of the Qin dynasty! The Third Reich!"
records.assessment: 学術書 means scholarly or academic books, not school textbooks. The substitution narrows the narrator's mock defense to classroom materials.
records.remedy: Use 'You burned academic books!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You burned school textbooks! You are the First Emperor of the Qin dynasty! The Third Reich!"

records.jp: 「でもベッドの下に押しやられていたから、いらないのかなって……それになんか俗っぽい本ばかりだったし……その……女の人のハダカとか……」
records.en: Touko: "But I thought that if you hide them under the bed, then you don't need them... and also... it seemed sort of like a vulgar book... with those... those women all naked..."
records.assessment: The books had merely been shoved under the bed; 'if you hide them' makes that an intentional recurring condition. The English also shifts the plural books to singular 'a vulgar book' and repeats demonstratives without stable agreement.
records.remedy: Use 'But they had been shoved under the bed, so I thought you didn't need them... And they were all such vulgar books... with naked women...'

highlights.text: Touko: "But I thought that if you hide them under the bed, then you don't need them... and also... it seemed sort of like a vulgar book... with those... those women all naked..."

records.jp: 「だからそれが学術だというのだ！」
records.en: Taichi: "I'm telling you, they were study books!"
records.assessment: The mock claim is specifically that the books are academic or scholarly. 'Study books' merely suggests books used for studying and weakens the register carried from 学術書.
records.remedy: Use 'That's exactly why I call them academic books!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm telling you, they were study books!"

records.jp: 「人間の根元たる美を肉体に求めずしてミロヴィーが語れるか！　自らの彫った彫像の娘に恋してしまったいにしえのフィギュアオタクのことでも学んで恥じるがいい！」
records.en: Taichi: "Could you talk about the Venus de Milo without the pursuit of the human fundamental of beauty that is in the body?! Learn of the Bishoujo Figurine Otakus of ancient times, who fell in love with the girls they themselves sculpted, and be ashamed!"
records.assessment: The source invokes the singular ancient figure enthusiast who fell in love with a statue he carved. The English invents 'Bishoujo,' pluralizes both enthusiasts and girls, and leaves the Venus clause in broken syntax.
records.remedy: Use a grammatical line about seeking fundamental human beauty in the body, then tell her to learn from the ancient statue enthusiast who loved the woman he carved.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Could you talk about the Venus de Milo without the pursuit of the human fundamental of beauty that is in the body?! Learn of the Bishoujo Figurine Otakus of ancient times, who fell in love with the girls they themselves sculpted, and be ashamed!"

records.jp: 「そしておまえは後悔するんだ。書物が自然発火する華氏４５１度の世界でな。つまり焦熱地獄に堕ちるってことだ！　学術書を焼くってのはそういうことだ！　人類の敵め！」
records.en: Taichi: "And now you shall repent. In the world of 451 Fahrenheit, where books spontaneously combust! In other words you are to be condemned into the fires of hell! That is the reward for roasting books of learning! You damn enemy of mankind!"
records.assessment: The referenced title and temperature are Fahrenheit 451, not '451 Fahrenheit.' 後悔する says she will regret it, not repent, and 'condemned into' and 'roasting books' break the mock-serious argument's grammar and register.
records.remedy: Use 'And you'll regret it in the world of Fahrenheit 451, where books spontaneously combust. In other words, you'll fall into a scorching hell!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And now you shall repent. In the world of 451 Fahrenheit, where books spontaneously combust! In other words you are to be condemned into the fires of hell! That is the reward for roasting books of learning! You damn enemy of mankind!"

records.jp: くるくるターンを切りながら、幾度となく冬子に指をつきつけた。
records.en: I thrust the finger at Touko so many times while I spin it round and round.
records.assessment: The narrator repeatedly points at Tōko while he performs spinning turns. The English instead spins one finger around and removes the narrator's full-body turns.
records.remedy: Use 'Executing turn after turn, I repeatedly thrust a finger at Tōko.'

highlights.text: I thrust the finger at Touko so many times while I spin it round and round.

records.jp: 「なんでも、俗世間にはエロ本なるものがあるって聞くわ」
records.en: Touko: "I've heard around that in the outside world there are things known as 'pornographic books'."
records.assessment: 俗世間 is ordinary society or the worldly realm. 'The outside world' invents a spatial separation from the speaker's present location.
records.remedy: Use 'I hear ordinary society has things called pornographic books.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I've heard around that in the outside world there are things known as 'pornographic books'."

records.jp: 「どき」
records.en: Taichi: "*heartbeat skip*"
records.assessment: どき is the sound or sensation of one alarmed heartbeat. 'Heartbeat skip' specifically asserts a missed beat rather than the source's thump.
records.remedy: Use a single startled heartbeat such as '*thump*.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "*heartbeat skip*"

records.jp: 「どきどき」
records.en: Taichi: "*heartbeat skip* *heartbeat skip*"
records.assessment: The doubled どきどき represents a pounding heartbeat, not two explicitly skipped beats.
records.remedy: Use a repeated heartbeat such as '*thump thump*.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "*heartbeat skip* *heartbeat skip*"

records.jp: 「ひとりで納得するなよ……」
records.en: Taichi: "Don't agree with yourself you..."
records.assessment: The English adds a dangling final 'you' after the complete imperative and provides no punctuation that makes it a coherent vocative.
records.remedy: Use 'Don't reach an agreement all by yourself...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't agree with yourself you..."

records.jp: 「ちぇ、しょうがないな」
records.en: Taichi: "Tsk, well, no ways around this then."
comments: See CCX0001 -GHS
records.assessment: 'No ways around this' has incorrect number in the fixed expression.
records.remedy: Use 'Tch. It can't be helped.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Tsk, well, no ways around this then."

records.jp: 見たところ、クローゼットにあるコスプレ衣装コレクションには手がつけられていないようだ。
records.en: It appears that no hand has touched the cosplay collection that is in the closet.
comments: Shouldn't it be in Youko's room, next door? -GHS
records.assessment: The source says the cosplay collection appears untouched. 'No hand has touched' is a literal passive image that makes an isolated hand the agent rather than describing the collection's condition.
records.remedy: Use 'It looks as though the cosplay-costume collection in the closet is untouched.'

highlights.text: It appears that no hand has touched the cosplay collection that is in the closet.

records.jp: つまり冬子のペタ能力は、まだまだ拙いものだと言える。
records.en:
Meaning Touko's PTA Power can still be called shoddy as well as lacking, still.
* PTA Power = Taichian for the skill of ceremonially
perceiving unwholesomeness, found in guardians
as well as teachers.
comments: Merged lines again. See CCA0007. Fits in with that Buddhist training ritual where you have to clear your mind or you get caned. It would certainly require PTA powers. -GHS
records.assessment: The glossed ペタ ability is judged still unskilled. 'Shoddy as well as lacking, still' redundantly supplies two adjectives, misplaces the temporal adverb, and does not form natural English.
records.remedy: Use 'In other words, Tōko's PTA ability is still amateurish.'

records.jp: 女性ものの下着類は、今はあるじなきおねえちゃん部屋のタンスの中。
records.en: The underclothes for female uses are in the closet of my onee-chan's currently masterless room.
comments: That should be Youko's room, see CCC0003A. -GHS
records.assessment: The source locates women's underwear in the dresser in the currently ownerless room of the narrator's older sister. 'Underclothes for female uses' is ungrammatical, and 'closet' changes the furniture from a chest of drawers.
records.remedy: Use 'The women's underwear is in the dresser in my now-ownerless big sister's room.'

highlights.text: The underclothes for female uses are in the closet of my onee-chan's currently masterless room.

records.jp: 木の葉を隠すならなんとやらだ。
records.en: When you want to hide a tree leaf, what better place.
comments: Adapted a bit. Correct proverb should be 木を隠すなら森の中 -GHS
records.assessment: 木の葉を隠すなら is the opening of the proverb 'If you want to hide a leaf, hide it in a forest.' 'What better place' omits the forest that completes both the proverb and the narrator's concealment logic.
records.remedy: Use 'If you want to hide a leaf, hide it in a forest.'

highlights.text: When you want to hide a tree leaf, what better place.

records.jp: 見よ、壁に偽装された驚愕の隠し金庫を！！
records.en: Behold, disguised in the wall, the shocking presence of a hidden safe!!!
comments: Avoiding camouflage because of CCB0006 and CCC3009. -GHS
records.assessment: The safe is disguised as part of the wall. 'Disguised in the wall' merely locates an otherwise visible object inside it and loses the concealment mechanism.
records.remedy: Use 'Behold the astonishing hidden safe disguised as the wall itself!'

highlights.text: Behold, disguised in the wall, the shocking presence of a hidden safe!!!

records.jp: 以前、曜子ちゃんに誘われて外貨で一儲けした時、そのあがりで作ったのだ。
records.en: Previously, I had been making money on foreign goods on Youko-chan's advice, and in those ascendant times I had this made.
comments: Part 5, Taichi the Failed Speculator. Specifically 'goods'. -GHS
records.assessment: 外貨 means foreign currency, not foreign goods, and あがり is the profit from that venture. 'In those ascendant times' turns the proceeds used to build the safe into a vague period of success.
records.remedy: Use 'I had it made with the profit from a foreign-currency windfall Yōko-chan once tipped me off about.'

highlights.text: Previously, I had been making money on foreign goods on Youko-chan's advice, and in those ascendant times I had this made.

records.jp: すると金庫の入り口が。
records.en: And there, the front of the safe.
records.assessment: すると金庫の入り口が is a reveal: sliding the panel exposes the safe's entrance. 'And there, the front of the safe' is a verbless fragment and does not say that it appears.
records.remedy: Use 'The entrance to the safe appears.'

highlights.text: And there, the front of the safe.

records.jp: すなわち、かのルパンであっても調査不可能というわけだ。
records.en: In other words, even if that famed Lupin were to come and search the place, there would be no chance for him.
comments: See CCA0021. Oddly, CCC4010 hints it's Lupin the 3rd, when given the style I'd have also guessed the original. Hmmm, Touko-Fuyuko-Fujiko? -GHS
records.assessment: 調査不可能 specifically says the code would be impossible to investigate or deduce, even for Lupin. 'There would be no chance for him' leaves the impossible task unstated.
records.remedy: Use 'Even the famed Lupin would be unable to work it out.'

highlights.text: In other words, even if that famed Lupin were to come and search the place, there would be no chance for him.

records.assessment: カチリ is the small click of the lock opening. 'Clank' describes a louder metallic impact.
records.remedy: Use 'Click. The lock opens.'

highlights.text: Clank, resounds the lock as it is released.

records.jp: この数字は、太一という名前からつけた。
records.en: This number is derived by my name, Taichi.
records.assessment: A number is derived 'from' a name, not 'by' it.
records.remedy: Use 'I derived this number from the name Taichi.'

highlights.text: This number is derived by my name, Taichi.

records.jp: 太＝多い、ということで桁の上限である９９９。＋太一の一で１。
records.en: The 'Ta' can be read as 'many', and the farthest ends of that would of course be 999. Plus the 'ichi' in Ta-ichi, that is 1.
records.assessment: 桁の上限 identifies 999 as the upper limit for the chosen digits. 'The farthest ends of that' is not meaningful English and obscures the numerical construction.
records.remedy: Use 'Ta means many, so I take the maximum for those digits: 999. Then the ichi in Taichi gives 1.'

highlights.text: The 'Ta' can be read as 'many', and the farthest ends of that would of course be 999. Plus the 'ichi' in Ta-ichi, that is 1.

records.jp: とんちがまじっている分、誕生日よりは解析が難しいはずだ。

records.remedy: Use 'With that bit of wordplay mixed in, it should be harder to crack than a birthday.'

highlights.text: So much wit is mixed there, that it should be much more difficult to derive than from a birthday.

records.assessment: Here よく expresses amazement at how she can bear such warm-looking clothing, not frequency. The English inserts 'often' and leaves 'hot-looking' open to a different sense instead of describing an outfit that looks stifling.

records.jp: 生存への本能は強い方だ。
records.en: The instinct to exist is very strong.
records.assessment: 生存への本能 is the established concept 'survival instinct.' 'Instinct to exist' is an awkward literal paraphrase.

highlights.text: instinct to exist

records.jp: それに、霧が向けてくる憎悪が、俺にははかりかねた。
records.en: Besides, the hatred that came from Kiri was something I didn't really know what to do with.
records.assessment: はかりかねた means that he could not fathom or gauge the hatred directed at him. The English instead says he did not know how to respond to or handle it.

highlights.text: didn't really know what to do with

records.jp: 絶望しかないのに。
records.en: there's nothing but despair, so,
records.assessment: The repeated のに is concessive: even though there is nothing but despair. 'So' makes despair the cause of the adjoining obligation and reverses the relation.

highlights.text: so

records.jp: 笑っていかねばならないのに。
records.en: I should just laugh, yet...
records.assessment: 笑っていかねばならない means that he nevertheless must go on smiling. The English reduces this sustained stance to merely laughing and adds 'just.'

highlights.text: I should just laugh

records.jp: 「今は、殺し合ってる場合じゃないだろ？」
records.en: Taichi: "This here, isn't it just a case of mutual murder?"
comments: It was all settled above. This is just perfunctory. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese says that now is not the time for them to kill each other. The English instead affirms that the situation is simply a case of mutual murder.

highlights.text: isn't it just a case of mutual murder?

records.jp: 「それにお互いのためにならない。君だって危険なんだ」
records.en: Taichi: "Besides, this won't be good for each other. Even you're in danger."
records.assessment: 君だって means that Kiri is in danger too. 'Even you' marks her inclusion as surprising rather than adding her to the shared risk.

highlights.text: Even you're in danger.

records.jp: つい、踏み込みすぎた。
records.en: Accidentally, I treaded too far into her territory.
records.assessment: The Japanese says figuratively that he went too far. The English uses the nonstandard past 'treaded' and invents a literal territory.

highlights.text: I treaded too far into her territory

records.jp: しくじった。
records.en: Fail.
comments: LOLFail. -GHS
records.assessment: しくじった is a finite admission that he made a mistake or screwed up. The English uses a bare internet-style label or command.

highlights.text: Fail.

records.jp: 撃たれたというショックから、その場に座り込む。
records.en: I fell down sitting on the spot from the shock that was being struck.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that he sits down from the shock of having been shot. The English substitutes being struck, makes the shock itself progressive, and forms no grammatical causal phrase.

highlights.text: the shock that was being struck

records.jp: 苦痛がない。
records.en: Agony there isn't.
comments: However... see CCC3022. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese plainly says there is no pain. The English raises it to agony and uses an unnatural existential inversion.

highlights.text: Agony there isn't.

records.jp: 死が近いとも感じられない。
records.en: I cannot even feel if death is coming closer.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that he cannot feel death drawing near. The English instead says he cannot determine whether it is approaching.

highlights.text: cannot even feel if death is coming closer

records.jp: まいったな、これは……苦しむぞ？
records.en: Oh, I give up, is this... suffering?
records.assessment: Taichi recognizes that this is bad and anticipates suffering. The English says he gives up and then asks whether the present situation itself is 'suffering.'

highlights.text: Oh, I give up, is this... suffering?

records.jp: ……ああ、いやだ。
records.en: ...ahhh, that's bad.
records.assessment: いやだ expresses that he does not want this or cannot bear it. The English merely evaluates the situation as bad.

highlights.text: that's bad

records.jp: 気がつくと、呼吸が恐ろしく浅くなっている。
records.en: When I come to notice, my breath is becoming frightfully shallow.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that when he notices, his breathing has already become frighteningly shallow. The English uses malformed present narration and changes the completed change into an ongoing one.

highlights.text: When I come to notice, my breath is becoming

records.jp: ガラスの割れる音。
records.en: The sound of glass being cracked.
comments: Possibly something was flung at the window, which caused the guards to intervene. See CCD1001: Youko, on being revealed, shatters like glass. -GHS
records.assessment: The Japanese gives the sound of glass breaking. 'Being cracked' suggests a crack forming without the glass necessarily breaking apart.

highlights.text: glass being cracked

records.jp: 視界の外、何かが、肉に、食いこんだ。
records.en: Out of sight... something had... eaten down... into flesh.
comments: Catfight? See CCA0017A, someone likes to bite indeed. See CCA0003 as well -GHS
records.assessment: 食いこむ means that something bites or digs into flesh. The English literalizes the verb as eating and uses past perfect for the immediate event.

highlights.text: had... eaten down... into flesh

records.jp: 唐突に呼吸が停止した。
records.en: Suddenly the breathing came to a halt.
records.assessment: The Japanese says that his breathing abruptly stops. The English removes the embodied possessor and uses a stilted nominal predicate.

highlights.text: the breathing came to a halt

records.jp: 眼球が濁ったかのように、暗くなっていく。
records.en: Eyeballs went dark, as if covered with mud.
records.assessment: 眼球が濁ったかのように means as though his eyes themselves had clouded over. The English misreads 濁る literally as being coated in mud.

highlights.text: as if covered with mud
